shloka_text: प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य राक्षसानां वधे कृते । आजग्मुर्ऋषयः सर्वे राघवं प्रतिनन्दितुम् ।। 7.1.1 ।।
transliteration: prāptarājyasya rāmasya rākṣasānāṃ vadhe kṛte | ājagmurṛṣayaḥ sarve rāghavaṃ pratinanditum || 7.1.1 ||
translation: प्राप्तराज्यस्य of one who has attained the kingdom, रामस्य of Rama, राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas (demons), वधे upon the destruction, कृते having been accomplished, आजग्मुः came, ऋषयः sages, सर्वे all, राघवं to Raghava (Rama), प्रतिनन्दितुम् to congratulate
explanation: After Rama had attained his kingdom and the destruction of the Rakshasas was accomplished, all the sages came to congratulate Raghava.
comments: After Rama's victory and coronation, the sages led by Agastya come to congratulate him on slaying Ravana and the rakshasas -- they especially extol the death of Indrajit, conqueror of Indra -- puzzled why Indrajit is praised above Ravana and Kumbhakarna, Rama asks Agastya to recount Indrajit's prowess, how Ravana conquered Indra and won his boons, and the origin of the rakshasas.

shloka_text: कौशिको ऽथ यवक्रीतो गार्ग्यो गालव एव च । कण्वो मेधातिथेः पुत्रः पूर्वस्यां दिशि ये श्रिताः ।। 7.1.2 ।।
transliteration: kauśiko 'tha yavakrīto gārgyo gālava eva ca | kaṇvo medhātitheḥ putraḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ye śritāḥ || 7.1.2 ||
translation: कौशिको Kaushika (Vishwamitra), अथ and, यवक्रीतो Yavakrita, गार्ग्यो Gargya, गालव Galava, एव च and also, कण्वो Kanva, मेधातिथेः of Medhatithi, पुत्रः the son, पूर्वस्यां in the eastern, दिशि direction, ये who, श्रिताः resided
explanation: Kaushika, Yavakrita, Gargya, Galava, and Kanva, the son of Medhatithi, who resided in the eastern direction, also arrived.

shloka_text: स्वस्त्यात्रेयो ऽथ भगवान्नमुचिः प्रमुचिस्तथा । आजग्मुस्ते सहागस्त्या ये श्रिता दक्षिणां दिशम् ।। 7.1.3 ।।
transliteration: svastyātreyo 'tha bhagavānnamuciḥ pramucistathā | ājagmuste sahāgastyā ye śritā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam || 7.1.3 ||
translation: स्वस्त्यात्रेयो Svastyatreya, अथ and, भगवान् the revered, नमुचिः Namuchi, प्रमुचिस्तथा and Pramuchi, आजग्मुस्ते they came, सहागस्त्या with Agastya, ये who, श्रिता resided, दक्षिणां in the southern, दिशम् direction
explanation: Svastyatreya, the revered Namuchi, and Pramuchi, along with Agastya, who resided in the southern direction, also came.

shloka_text: नृषद्गुः कवषो धौम्यो रौद्रेयश्च महानृषिः । ते ऽप्याजग्मुः सशिष्या वै ये श्रिताः पश्चिमां दिशम् ।। 7.1.4 ।।
transliteration: nṛṣadguḥ kavaṣo dhaumyo raudreyaśca mahānṛṣiḥ | te 'pyājagmuḥ saśiṣyā vai ye śritāḥ paścimāṃ diśam || 7.1.4 ||
translation: नृषद्गुः Nṛṣadgu, कवषो Kavaṣa, धौम्यो Dhaumya, रौद्रेयश्च and Raudreya, महानृषिः the great sage, ते they, अपि also, आजग्मुः came, सशिष्या with their disciples, वै indeed, ये who, श्रिताः resided, पश्चिमां in the western, दिशम् direction
explanation: Nṛṣadgu, Kavaṣa, Dhaumya, and the great sage Raudreya, who resided in the western direction, also came with their disciples.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठः कश्यपो ऽथात्रिर्विश्वामित्रः सगौतमः । जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजस्ते ऽपि सप्तर्षयस्तथा ।। 7.1.5 ।।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapo 'thātrirviśvāmitraḥ sagautamaḥ | jamadagnirbharadvājaste 'pi saptarṣayastathā || 7.1.5 ||
translation: वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, कश्यपो Kashyapa, अथ and, अत्रिर् Atri, विश्वामित्रः Vishwamitra, सगौतमः with Gautama, जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजस् Jamadagni and Bharadvaja, ते they, अपि also, सप्तर्षयस्तथा and the Saptarshis (seven sages)
explanation: Vasishtha, Kashyapa, Atri, Vishwamitra with Gautama, Jamadagni, and Bharadvaja, who are also known as the Saptarshis, were among those who arrived.

shloka_text: उदीच्यां दिशि सप्तैते नित्यमेव निवासिनः ।। 7.1.6 ।।
transliteration: udīcyāṃ diśi saptaite nityameva nivāsinaḥ || 7.1.6 ||
translation: उदीच्यां in the northern, दिशि direction, सप्तैते these seven, नित्यमेव always indeed, निवासिनः residents
explanation: These seven sages are permanent residents in the northern direction.

shloka_text: सम्प्राप्य ते महात्मानो राघवस्य निवेशनम् । विष्टिताः प्रतिहारार्थं हुताशनसमप्रभाः । वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषो नानाशास्त्रविशारदाः ।। 7.1.7 ।।
transliteration: samprāpya te mahātmāno rāghavasya niveśanam | viṣṭitāḥ pratihārārthaṃ hutāśanasamaprabhāḥ | vedavedāṅgaviduṣo nānāśāstraviśāradāḥ || 7.1.7 ||
translation: सम्प्राप्य having reached, ते those, महात्मानो great souls, राघवस्य of Rama, निवेशनम् abode, विष्टिताः stood, प्रतिहारार्थं for the purpose of guarding the gate, हुताशनसमप्रभाः having a luster like fire, वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषो knowing the Vedas and Vedangas, नानाशास्त्रविशारदाः skilled in various scriptures
explanation: Having arrived at Rama's palace, those great souls, shining like fire, knowledgeable in the Vedas, Vedangas, and various scriptures, stood at the gate as guards.

shloka_text: द्वाःस्थं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः । निवेद्यतां दाशरथेर्ऋषीनस्मान्समागतान् ।। 7.1.8 ।।
transliteration: dvāḥsthaṃ provāca dharmātmā agastyo munisattamaḥ | nivedyatāṃ dāśaratherṛṣīnasmānsamāgatān || 7.1.8 ||
translation: द्वाःस्थं to the doorkeeper, प्रोवाच spoke, धर्मात्मा the righteous-souled, अगस्त्यो Agastya, मुनिसत्तमः the best among sages, निवेद्यतां let it be announced, दाशरथेः to Dasharatha's son (Rama), ऋषीन् us sages, अस्मान् who, समागतान् have arrived
explanation: The righteous Agastya, the best of sages, spoke to the doorkeeper, instructing him to announce their arrival to Rama, the son of Dasharatha.

shloka_text: प्रतीहारस्ततस्तूर्णमगस्त्यवचनाद्द्रुतम् । समीपं राघवस्याशु प्रविवेश महात्मनः ।। 7.1.9 ।।
transliteration: pratīhārastatastūrṇamagastyavacanāddrutam | samīpaṃ rāghavasyāśu praviveśa mahātmanaḥ || 7.1.9 ||
translation: प्रतीहारः the doorkeeper, ततः then, तूर्णम् quickly, अगस्त्य of Agastya, वचनात् from the words, द्रुतम् swiftly, समीपम् to the presence, राघवस्य of Rama, आशु quickly, प्रविवेश entered, महात्मनः of the great-souled one
explanation: Then, the doorkeeper, swiftly and quickly, entered the presence of the great-souled Rama, following Agastya's words.

shloka_text: नयेङ्गितज्ञः सद्वृत्तो दक्षो धैर्यसमन्वितः । स रामं दृश्य सहसा पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभम् ।। 7.1.10 ।।
transliteration: nayeṅgitajñaḥ sadvṛtto dakṣo dhairyasamanvitaḥ | sa rāmaṃ dṛśya sahasā pūrṇacandrasamaprabham || 7.1.10 ||
translation: नयेङ्गितज्ञः knowing policy and gestures, सद्वृत्तः of good conduct, दक्षः skillful, धैर्यसमन्वितः endowed with courage, सः he, रामम् Rama, दृश्य having seen, सहसा suddenly, पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभम् having a luster like the full moon
explanation: He, who was skilled in policy and gestures, of good conduct, efficient, and endowed with courage, immediately saw Rama, who shone like the full moon.

shloka_text: अगस्त्यं कथयामास सम्प्राप्तमृषिभिः सह ।। 7.1.11 ।।
transliteration: agastyaṃ kathayāmāsa samprāptamṛṣibhiḥ saha || 7.1.11 ||
translation: अगस्त्यम् Agastya, कथयामास told, सम्प्राप्तम् arrived, ऋषिभिः with sages, सह with
explanation: He informed (Rama) that Agastya had arrived along with other sages.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु बालसूर्यसमप्रभान् । प्रत्युवाच ततो द्वास्स्थं प्रवेशय यथासुखम् ।। 7.1.12 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā prāptānmunīṃstāṃstu bālasūryasamaprabhān | pratyuvāca tato dvāssthaṃ praveśaya yathāsukham || 7.1.12 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, प्राप्तान् arrived, मुनींस्तांस्तु those sages, बालसूर्यसमप्रभान् having the radiance equal to the morning sun, प्रत्युवाच replied, ततो then, द्वास्स्थम् to the doorkeeper, प्रवेशय let them enter, यथासुखम् comfortably
explanation: Having heard that those sages, radiant like the morning sun, had arrived, Rama then replied to the doorkeeper, instructing him to admit them comfortably.

shloka_text: तान् सम्प्राप्तान् मुनीन् दृष्ट्वा प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः । पाद्यार्घ्यादिभिरानर्च गां निवेद्य च सादरम् ।। 7.1.13 ।।
transliteration: tān samprāptān munīn dṛṣṭvā pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ | pādyārghyādibhirānarca gāṃ nivedya ca sādaram || 7.1.13 ||
translation: तान् those, सम्प्राप्तान् arrived, मुनीन् sages, दृष्ट्वा having seen, प्रत्युत्थाय having risen to greet, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, पाद्यार्घ्यादिभिः with water for feet and other offerings, आनर्च worshipped, गाम् a cow, निवेद्य having offered, च and, सादरम् respectfully
explanation: Having seen those arrived sages, Rama rose to greet them with folded hands, honored them with water for their feet and other offerings, and respectfully presented a cow.

shloka_text: रामो ऽभिवाद्य प्रयत आसनान्यादिदेश ह । तेषु काञ्चनचित्रेषु महत्सु च वरेषु च ।। 7.1.14 ।।
transliteration: rāmo 'bhivādya prayata āsanānyādideśa ha | teṣu kāñcanacitreṣu mahatsu ca vareṣu ca || 7.1.14 ||
translation: रामः Rama, अभिवाद्य having saluted, प्रयत attentive, आसनानि seats, आदिदेश ordered, ह indeed, तेषु on those, काञ्चनचित्रेषु adorned with gold, महत्सु great, च and, वरेषु excellent, च and
explanation: Rama, having saluted them with a composed mind, indeed offered them seats that were great, excellent, and adorned with gold.

shloka_text: कुशान्तर्धानदत्तेषु मृगचर्मयुतेषु च । यथार्हमुपविष्टास्ते आसनेष्वृषिपुङ्गवाः ।। 7.1.15 ।।
transliteration: kuśāntardhānadatteṣu mṛgacarmayuteṣu ca | yathārhamupaviṣṭāste āsaneṣvṛṣipuṅgavāḥ || 7.1.15 ||
translation: कुशान्तर्धानदत्तेषु provided with kusha grass underneath, मृगचर्मयुतेषु furnished with deer skins, च and, यथार्हम् appropriately, उपविष्टाः sat, ते they, आसनेषु on the seats, ऋषिपुङ्गवाः the foremost among sages
explanation: The foremost among sages then sat appropriately on those seats, which were provided with kusha grass underneath and furnished with deer skins.

shloka_text: रामेण कुशलं पृष्टाः सशिष्याः सपुरोगमाः । महर्षयो वेदविदो रामं वचनमब्रुवन् ।। 7.1.16 ।।
transliteration: rāmeṇa kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭāḥ saśiṣyāḥ sapurogamāḥ | maharṣayo vedavido rāmaṃ vacanamabruvan || 7.1.16 ||
translation: रामेण by Rama, कुशलं welfare, पृष्टाः asked, सशिष्याः with their disciples, सपुरोगमाः with their prominent members, महर्षयः the great sages, वेदविदः knowers of the Vedas, रामं to Rama, वचनम् words, अब्रुवन् spoke.
explanation: When Rama inquired about their well-being, the great sages, who were knowers of the Vedas and accompanied by their disciples and prominent members, spoke these words to him.

shloka_text: कुशलं नो महाबाहो सर्वत्र रघुनन्दन । त्वां तु दिष्ट्या कुशलिनं पश्यामो हतशात्रवम् ।। 7.1.17 ।।
transliteration: kuśalaṃ no mahābāho sarvatra raghunandana | tvāṃ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṃ paśyāmo hataśātravam || 7.1.17 ||
translation: कुशलं well-being, नः our, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, सर्वत्र everywhere, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghu dynasty, त्वां you, तु but, दिष्ट्या fortunately, कुशलिनं well, पश्यामो we see, हतशात्रवम् with enemies slain.
explanation: The sages replied that they were well everywhere, O mighty-armed Rama, and they were fortunate to see him safe and with his enemies slain.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राजन्रावणो लोकरावणः । न हि भारः स ते राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान् ।। 7.1.18 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā tvayā hato rājanrāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | na hi bhāraḥ sa te rāma rāvaṇaḥ putrapautravān || 7.1.18 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, त्वया by you, हतः slain, राजन् O King, रावणः Ravana, लोकरावणः who made the worlds weep, न not, हि indeed, भारः a burden, सः that, ते to you, राम O Rama, रावणः Ravana, पुत्रपौत्रवान् with sons and grandsons.
explanation: O King, it is fortunate that you have slain Ravana, who tormented the worlds, for indeed, even with his sons and grandsons, he was no match for you, O Rama.

shloka_text: सधनुस्त्वं हि लोकांस्त्रीन्विजयेथा न संशयः । दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राम रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।। 7.1.19 ।।
transliteration: sadhanustvaṃ hi lokāṃstrīnvijayethā na saṃśayaḥ | diṣṭyā tvayā hato rāma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ || 7.1.19 ||
translation: सधनुः with your bow, त्वं you, हि indeed, लोकान् worlds, त्रीन् three, विजयेथा would conquer, न no, संशयः doubt, दिष्ट्या fortunately, त्वया by you, हतः slain, राम O Rama, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: There is no doubt that you, with your bow, could indeed conquer the three worlds, and it is fortunate, O Rama, that you have slain Ravana, the lord of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या विजयिनं त्वाद्य पश्यामः सह सीतया । लक्ष्मणेन च धर्मात्मन्भ्रात्रा त्वद्धितकारिणा ।। 7.1.20 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā vijayinaṃ tvādya paśyāmaḥ saha sītayā | lakṣmaṇena ca dharmātmanbhrātrā tvaddhitakāriṇā || 7.1.20 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, विजयिनं victorious, त्वा you, अद्य today, पश्यामः we see, सह with, सीतया Sita, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, च and, धर्मात्मन् O righteous one, भ्रात्रा by brother, त्वद्धितकारिणा who acts for your welfare.
explanation: O righteous one, it is fortunate that today we see you victorious, accompanied by Sita and by Lakshmana, your brother who always acts for your welfare.

shloka_text: मातृभिर्भ्रातृसहितं पश्यामो ऽद्य वयं नृप । दिष्ट्या प्रहस्तो विकटो विरूपाक्षो महोदरः । अकम्पनश्च दुर्धर्षो निहतास्ते निशाचराः ।। 7.1.21 ।।
transliteration: mātṛbhirbhrātṛsahitaṃ paśyāmo 'dya vayaṃ nṛpa | diṣṭyā prahasto vikaṭo virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ | akampanaśca durdharṣo nihatāste niśācarāḥ || 7.1.21 ||
translation: मातृभिः with mothers, भ्रातृसहितम् together with brothers, पश्यामः we see, अद्य today, वयम् we, नृप O King, दिष्ट्या fortunately, प्रहस्तः Prahasta, विकटः Vikata, विरूपाक्षः Virupaksha, महोदरः Mahodara, अकम्पनः Akampana, च and, दुर्धर्षः Durdharsha, निहताः killed, ते those, निशाचराः demons.
explanation: O King, we are fortunate to see you today with our mothers and brothers, and it is by good fortune that those demons Prahasta, Vikata, Virupaksha, Mahodara, Akampana, and Durdharsha have been killed.

shloka_text: यस्य प्रमाणाद्विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते । दिष्ट्या ते समरे राम कुम्भकर्णो निपातितः ।। 7.1.22 ।।
transliteration: yasya pramāṇādvipulaṃ pramāṇaṃ neha vidyate | diṣṭyā te samare rāma kumbhakarṇo nipātitaḥ || 7.1.22 ||
translation: यस्य whose, प्रमाणात् than the measure, विपुलम् greater, प्रमाणम् measure, न not, इह here, विद्यते exists, दिष्ट्या fortunately, ते by you, समरे in battle, राम O Rama, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, निपातितः struck down.
explanation: O Rama, it is by good fortune that you have struck down Kumbhakarna in battle, whose immense size has no equal in this world.

shloka_text: त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ । दिष्ट्या ते निहता राम महावीर्या निशाचराः ।। 7.1.23 ।।
transliteration: triśirāścātikāyaśca devāntakanarāntakau | diṣṭyā te nihatā rāma mahāvīryā niśācarāḥ || 7.1.23 ||
translation: त्रिशिराः Trishira, च and, अतिकायः Atikaya, च and, देवान्तकनरान्तकौ Devantaka and Narantaka, दिष्ट्या fortunately, ते by you, निहताः killed, राम O Rama, महावीर्याः very powerful, निशाचराः demons.
explanation: O Rama, it is by good fortune that you have killed those extremely powerful demons Trishira, Atikaya, Devantaka, and Narantaka.

shloka_text: कुम्भश्चैव निकुम्भश्च राक्षसौ भीमदर्शनौ । दिष्ट्या तौ निहतौ राम कुम्भकर्णसुतौ मृधे ।। 7.1.24 ।।
transliteration: kumbhaścaiva nikumbhaśca rākṣasau bhīmadarśanau | diṣṭyā tau nihatau rāma kumbhakarṇasutau mṛdhe || 7.1.24 ||
translation: कुम्भः Kumbha, च and, एव indeed, निकुम्भः Nikumbha, च and, राक्षसौ two demons, भीमदर्शनौ of terrible appearance, दिष्ट्या fortunately, तौ those two, निहतौ killed, राम O Rama, कुम्भकर्णसुतौ sons of Kumbhakarna, मृधे in battle.
explanation: O Rama, it is by good fortune that you have killed Kumbha and Nikumbha, the two sons of Kumbhakarna who were of terrible appearance, in battle.

shloka_text: युद्धोन्मत्तश्च मत्तश्च कालान्तकयमोपमौ । यज्ञकोपश्च बलवान्धूम्राक्षो नाम राक्षसः ।। 7.1.25 ।।
transliteration: yuddhonmattaśca mattaśca kālāntakayamopamau | yajñakopaśca balavāndhūmrākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ || 7.1.25 ||
translation: युद्धोन्मत्तः Yuddhonmatta, च and, मत्तः Matta, च and, कालान्तकयमोपमौ like Kala and Yama, यज्ञकोपः Yajnakopa, च and, बलवान् powerful, धूम्राक्षः Dhumraksha, नाम named, राक्षसः demon.
explanation: This shloka continues the list of formidable demons, including Yuddhonmatta and Matta who were like Kala and Yama, along with Yajnakopa and the powerful demon named Dhumraksha, whose defeat is being celebrated.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तः कदनं घोरमेते शस्त्रास्त्रपारगाः । अन्तकप्रतिमैर्बाणैर्दिष्ट्या विनिहतास्त्वया ।। 7.1.26 ।।
transliteration: kurvantaḥ kadanaṃ ghoramete śastrāstrapāragāḥ | antakapratimairbāṇairdiṣṭyā vinihatāstvayā || 7.1.26 ||
translation: कुर्वन्तः doing, कदनं slaughter, घोरम् terrible, एते these, शस्त्रास्त्रपारगाः masters of weapons and missiles, अन्तकप्रतिमैः resembling Yama, बाणैः with arrows, दिष्ट्या fortunately, विनिहताः killed, त्वया by you.
explanation: Fortunately, these masters of weapons and missiles, who were causing terrible slaughter, have been killed by you with arrows resembling those of Yama.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रेण द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः । देवतानामवध्येन विजयं प्राप्तवानसि ।। 7.1.27 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā tvaṃ rākṣasendreṇa dvandvayuddhamupāgataḥ | devatānāmavadhyena vijayaṃ prāptavānasi || 7.1.27 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, त्वं you, राक्षसेन्द्रेण with the king of Rakshasas, द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् a duel, उपागतः engaged in, देवतानाम् for the gods, अवध्येन by the invincible one, विजयं victory, प्राप्तवानसि you have obtained.
explanation: Fortunately, you engaged in a duel with the king of Rakshasas, who was invincible even to the gods, and you have achieved victory.

shloka_text: सङ्ख्ये तस्य न किञ्चित्तु रावणस्य पराभवः । द्वन्द्वयुद्धमनुप्राप्तो दिष्ट्या ते रावणिर्हतः ।। 7.1.28 ।।
transliteration: saṅkhye tasya na kiñcittu rāvaṇasya parābhavaḥ | dvandvayuddhamanuprāpto diṣṭyā te rāvaṇirhataḥ || 7.1.28 ||
translation: सङ्ख्ये in battle, तस्य his, न not, किञ्चित् any, तु but, रावणस्य of Ravana, पराभवः defeat, द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् a duel, अनुप्राप्तः engaged in, दिष्ट्या fortunately, ते by you, रावणिः Ravana's son, हतः killed.
explanation: There was no defeat for Ravana in battle, but fortunately, having engaged in a duel, Ravana's son (Indrajit) has been killed by you.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या तस्य महाबाहो कालस्येवाभिधावतः । मुक्तः सुररिपोर्वीर प्राप्तश्च विजयस्त्वया ।। 7.1.29 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā tasya mahābāho kālasyevābhidhāvataḥ | muktaḥ surariporvīra prāptaśca vijayastvayā || 7.1.29 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, तस्य from him, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, कालस्य of death, इव like, अभिधावतः rushing, मुक्तः freed, सुररिपोः from the enemy of gods, वीर O hero, प्राप्तः obtained, च and, विजयः victory, त्वया by you.
explanation: O mighty-armed hero, fortunately, you have been freed from that enemy of the gods who was rushing like death itself, and victory has been achieved by you.

shloka_text: अभिनन्दाम ते सर्वे संश्रुत्येन्द्रजितो वधम् । सो ऽवध्यः सर्वभूतानां महामायाधरो युधि ।। 7.1.30 ।।
transliteration: abhinandāma te sarve saṃśrutyendrajito vadham | so 'vadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ mahāmāyādharo yudhi || 7.1.30 ||
translation: अभिनन्दाम we congratulate, ते you, सर्वे all, संश्रुत्य having heard, इन्द्रजितः of Indrajit, वधम् the killing, सः he, अवध्यः invincible, सर्वभूतानाम् by all beings, महामायाधरः master of great illusion, युधि in battle.
explanation: All of us congratulate you upon hearing of Indrajit's death, for he was invincible to all beings and a master of great illusion in battle.

shloka_text: विस्मयस्त्वेष चास्माकं तच्छ्रुत्वेन्द्रजितं हतम् ।। 7.1.31 ।।
transliteration: vismayastveṣa cāsmākaṃ tacchrutvendrajitaṃ hatam || 7.1.31 ||
translation: विस्मयः wonder, तु indeed, एषः this, च and, अस्माकम् our, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, इन्द्रजितम् Indrajit, हतम् killed.
explanation: This is indeed our great wonder, having heard that Indrajit was killed.

shloka_text: एते चान्ये च बहवो राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः । दिष्ट्या त्वया हता वीरा रघूणां कुलवर्द्धन ।। 7.1.32 ।।
transliteration: ete cānye ca bahavo rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ | diṣṭyā tvayā hatā vīrā raghūṇāṃ kulavarddhana || 7.1.32 ||
translation: एते these, च and, अन्ये others, च and, बहवः many, राक्षसाः demons, कामरूपिणः form-changing, दिष्ट्या fortunately, त्वया by you, हताः killed, वीराः valiant ones, रघूणाम् of the Raghus, कुलवर्द्धन enhancer of the family.
explanation: Fortunately, O enhancer of the Raghu lineage, these and many other valiant form-changing demons have been slain by you.

shloka_text: दत्त्वा पुण्यामिमां वीर सौम्यामभयदक्षिणाम् ।। दिष्ट्या वर्धसि काकुत्स्थ जयेनामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.1.33 ।।
transliteration: dattvā puṇyāmimāṃ vīra saumyāmabhayadakṣiṇām || diṣṭyā vardhasi kākutstha jayenāmitrakarśana || 7.1.33 ||
translation: दत्त्वा having given, पुण्याम् sacred, इमाम् this, वीर O hero, सौम्याम् benevolent, अभयदक्षिणाम् gift of fearlessness, दिष्ट्या fortunately, वर्धसि you prosper, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, जयेन by victory, अमित्रकर्शन destroyer of enemies.
explanation: O hero, destroyer of enemies, having granted this sacred and benevolent gift of fearlessness, you fortunately prosper with victory, O Kakutstha.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु तेषां वचनमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम् । विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रामः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् ।। 7.1.34 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu teṣāṃ vacanamṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām | vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā rāmaḥ prāñjalirabravīt || 7.1.34 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, तेषाम् their, वचनम् words, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, भावितात्मनाम् of pure souls, विस्मयम् wonder, परमम् great, गत्वा having attained, रामः Rama, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard the words of those pure-souled sages, Rama, filled with great astonishment, spoke with folded hands.

shloka_text: भगवन्तः कुम्भकर्णं रावणं च निशाचरम् । अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यौ किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.35 ।।
transliteration: bhagavantaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ ca niśācaram | atikramya mahāvīryau kiṃ praśaṃsatha rāvaṇim || 7.1.35 ||
translation: भगवन्तः O revered ones, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, रावणम् Ravana, च and, निशाचरम् night-wanderer, अतिक्रम्य having surpassed, महावीर्यौ of great valor, किम् why, प्रशंसथ you praise, रावणिम् Ravana's son.
explanation: O revered ones, having overcome the greatly valorous Kumbhakarna and the night-wandering Ravana, why do you praise Ravana's son (Indrajit)?

shloka_text: महोदरं प्रहस्तं च विरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम् । मत्तोन्मत्तौ च दुर्धर्षौ देवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।
transliteration: mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasam | mattonmattau ca durdharṣau devāntakanarāntakau ||
translation: महोदरं Mahodara, प्रहस्तं Prahasta, च and, विरूपाक्षं Virupaksha, च and, राक्षसम् the demon, मत्तोन्मत्तौ Matta and Unmatta, च and, दुर्धर्षौ the invincible ones, देवान्तकनरान्तकौ Devantaka and Narantaka.
explanation: This shloka lists several powerful demons: Mahodara, Prahasta, Virupaksha, Matta, Unmatta, Devantaka, and Narantaka, all of whom are formidable.

shloka_text: अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान् किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.36 ।।
transliteration: atikramya mahāvīryān kiṃ praśaṃsatha rāvaṇim || 7.1.36 ||
translation: अतिक्रम्य having overlooked, महावीर्यान् the greatly valorous ones, किं why, प्रशंसथ do you praise, रावणिम् Ravana's son (Indrajit).
explanation: The speaker questions why they are praising Indrajit, having overlooked other greatly valorous warriors.

shloka_text: अतिकायं त्रिशिरसं धूम्राक्षं च निशाचरम् । अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान्किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.37 ।।
transliteration: atikāyaṃ triśirasaṃ dhūmrākṣaṃ ca niśācaram | atikramya mahāvīryānkiṃ praśaṃsatha rāvaṇim || 7.1.37 ||
translation: अतिकायं Atikaya, त्रिशिरसं Trishiras, धूम्राक्षं Dhumraksha, च and, निशाचरम् the night-ranger (demon), अतिक्रम्य having overlooked, महावीर्यान् the greatly valorous ones, किं why, प्रशंसथ do you praise, रावणिम् Ravana's son (Indrajit).
explanation: The speaker wonders why they praise Indrajit, having disregarded other mighty demons like Atikaya, Trishiras, and Dhumraksha.

shloka_text: कीदृशो वै प्रभावो ऽस्य किं बलं कः पराक्रमः । केन वा कारणेनैष रावणादतिरिच्यते ।। 7.1.38 ।।
transliteration: kīdṛśo vai prabhāvo 'sya kiṃ balaṃ kaḥ parākramaḥ | kena vā kāraṇenaiṣa rāvaṇādatiricyate || 7.1.38 ||
translation: कीदृशो what kind, वै indeed, प्रभावो influence/power, अस्य of him, किं what, बलं strength, कः what, पराक्रमः valor/prowess, केन by what, वा or, कारणेन by reason, एष this one (Indrajit), रावणात् than Ravana, अतिरिच्यते excels/surpasses.
explanation: The speaker asks about Indrajit's power, strength, and prowess, and by what reason he is considered superior to Ravana himself.

shloka_text: शक्यं यदि मया श्रोतुं न खल्वाज्ञापयामि वः । यदि गुह्यं न चेद्वक्तुं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम् ।। 7.1.39 ।।
transliteration: śakyaṃ yadi mayā śrotuṃ na khalvājñāpayāmi vaḥ | yadi guhyaṃ na cedvaktuṃ śrotumicchāmi kathyatām || 7.1.39 ||
translation: शक्यं possible, यदि if, मया by me, श्रोतुं to hear, न not, खलु indeed, आज्ञापयामि I command, वः you, यदि if, गुह्यं secret, न not, चेत् if, वक्तुं to speak, श्रोतुमिच्छामि I wish to hear, कथ्यताम् let it be told.
explanation: The speaker states that if it is possible for him to hear, he is not commanding them, but if it is not a secret to be spoken, he wishes to hear it, so it should be told.

shloka_text: शक्रो ऽपि विजितस्तेन कथं लब्धवरश्च सः । कथं च बलवानन्पुत्रो न पिता तस्य रावणः ।। 7.1.40 ।।
transliteration: śakro 'pi vijitastena kathaṃ labdhavaraśca saḥ | kathaṃ ca balavānanputro na pitā tasya rāvaṇaḥ || 7.1.40 ||
translation: शक्रो Indra, अपि even, विजितः conquered, तेन by him (Ravana), कथं how, लब्धवरः obtained boons, च and, सः he (Ravana), कथं how, च and, बलवान् powerful, अयं पुत्रो this son (Ravana), न not, पिता father, तस्य his, रावणः Ravana
explanation: Rama asks how Ravana conquered Indra and obtained boons, and how this powerful son (Ravana) is not like his father (in terms of power or nature).

shloka_text: कथं पितुश्चाभ्यधिको महाहवे शक्रस्य जेता हि कथं स राक्षसः । वराश्च लब्धाः कथयस्व मे ऽद्य तत्पृच्छतश्चास्य मुनीन्द्र सर्वम् ।। 7.1.41 ।।
transliteration: kathaṃ pituścābhyadhiko mahāhave śakrasya jetā hi kathaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ | varāśca labdhāḥ kathayasva me 'dya tatpṛcchataścāsya munīndra sarvam || 7.1.41 ||
translation: कथं how, पितुः than his father, च and, अभ्यधिकः superior, महाहवे in great battle, शक्रस्य of Indra, जेता conqueror, हि indeed, कथं how, सः that, राक्षसः Rakshasa, वराः boons, च and, लब्धाः obtained, कथयस्व tell, मे to me, अद्य today, तत् that, पृच्छतः asking, च and, अस्य this, मुनीन्द्र O chief of sages, सर्वम् all
explanation: Rama further inquires how that Rakshasa (Ravana) became superior to his father, how he conquered Indra in a great battle, and how he obtained boons, requesting the sage to explain everything to him who is asking. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः ।। 1 ।। Thus ends the first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः । कुम्भयोनिर्मिहातेजा राममेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.1 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ | kumbhayonirmihātejā rāmametaduvāca ha || 7.2.1 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनं word, श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवस्य of Rama, महात्मनः of the great-souled, कुम्भयोनिः Agastya, महातेजाः greatly effulgent, रामम् to Rama, एतत् this, उवाच said, ह indeed
explanation: Having heard those words of the great-souled Rama, the greatly effulgent sage Agastya then spoke this to Rama.
comments: Agastya begins the account of Ravana's lineage -- the sage Pulastya, son of Brahma, disturbed in his penance by maidens, curses that any maiden he sees shall conceive -- the daughter of the royal sage Trnabindu is thus afflicted and given by her father to Pulastya -- pleased by her service, the sage grants her a son, Vishravas, born endowed with fame and righteousness.

shloka_text: शृणु राम कथावृत्तं तस्य तेजोबलं महत् । जघान शत्रून्येनासौ न च वध्यः स शत्रुभिः ।। 7.2.2 ।।
transliteration: śṛṇu rāma kathāvṛttaṃ tasya tejobalaṃ mahat | jaghāna śatrūnyenāsau na ca vadhyaḥ sa śatrubhiḥ || 7.2.2 ||
translation: शृणु listen, राम O Rama, कथावृत्तं the story, तस्य his, तेजोबलं might and power, महत् great, जघान killed, शत्रून् enemies, येन by which, असौ he, न च and not, वध्यः to be killed, सः he, शत्रुभिः by enemies
explanation: O Rama, listen to his story, his great might and power, by which he killed his enemies and could not be killed by them.

shloka_text: तावत्ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव । वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते ।। 7.2.3 ।।
transliteration: tāvatte rāvaṇasyedaṃ kulaṃ janma ca rāghava | varapradānaṃ ca tathā tasmai dattaṃ bravīmi te || 7.2.3 ||
translation: तावत् then, ते to you, रावणस्य of Ravana, इदं this, कुलं lineage, जन्म birth, च and, राघव O Raghava, वरप्रदानं granting of boons, च and, तथा thus, तस्मै to him, दत्तं given, ब्रवीमि I will tell, ते to you
explanation: O Raghava, I will now tell you about Ravana's lineage, his birth, and the boons that were granted to him.

shloka_text: पुरा कृतयुगे राम प्रजापतिसुतः प्रभुः । पुलस्त्यो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षादिव पितामहः ।। 7.2.4 ।।
transliteration: purā kṛtayuge rāma prajāpatisutaḥ prabhuḥ | pulastyo nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣādiva pitāmahaḥ || 7.2.4 ||
translation: पुरा formerly, कृतयुगे in the Krita Yuga, राम O Rama, प्रजापतिसुतः son of Prajapati, प्रभुः the powerful one, पुलस्त्यो नाम named Pulastya, ब्रह्मर्षिः a Brahmarshi, साक्षादिव as if directly, पितामहः the grandfather (Brahma).
explanation: O Rama, formerly in the Krita Yuga, there was a powerful Brahmarshi named Pulastya, the son of Prajapati, who was verily like Brahma himself.

shloka_text: नानुकीर्त्या गुणास्तस्य धर्मतः शीलतस्तथा । प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः ।। 7.2.5 ।।
transliteration: nānukīrtyā guṇāstasya dharmataḥ śīlatastathā | prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṃ śakyaṃ hi nāmataḥ || 7.2.5 ||
translation: न not, अनुकीर्त्या to be fully described, गुणाः qualities, तस्य his, धर्मतः in terms of righteousness, शीलतः in terms of character, तथा and, प्रजापतेः of Prajapati, पुत्रः son, इति thus, वक्तुं to say, शक्यं possible, हि indeed, नामतः by name.
explanation: His qualities, in terms of righteousness and character, could not be fully described; indeed, it was only possible to refer to him by name as the son of Prajapati.

shloka_text: प्रजापतिसुतत्वेन देवानां वल्लभो हि सः । हृष्टः सर्वस्य लोकस्य गुणैः शुभ्रैर्महामतिः ।। 7.2.6 ।।
transliteration: prajāpatisutatvena devānāṃ vallabho hi saḥ | hṛṣṭaḥ sarvasya lokasya guṇaiḥ śubhrairmahāmatiḥ || 7.2.6 ||
translation: प्रजापतिसुतत्वेन by virtue of being the son of Prajapati, देवानां of the gods, वल्लभः beloved, हि indeed, सः he, हृष्टः pleased, सर्वस्य of all, लोकस्य the world, गुणैः by qualities, शुभ्रैः pure, महामतिः the great-minded one.
explanation: Indeed, by virtue of being the son of Prajapati, he was beloved by the gods and, being great-minded, he gladdened all the world with his pure qualities.

shloka_text: स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः । तृणविन्द्वाश्रमं गत्वा न्यवसन्मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.2.7 ।।
transliteration: sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ | tṛṇavindvāśramaṃ gatvā nyavasanmunipuṅgavaḥ || 7.2.7 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, धर्मप्रसङ्गेन for religious purposes, मेरोः of Mount Meru, पार्श्वे on the side, महागिरेः of the great mountain, तृणविन्द्वाश्रमं to the hermitage of Tṛṇavindu, गत्वा having gone, न्यवसत् resided, मुनिपुङ्गवः the foremost among sages.
explanation: Indeed, for religious purposes, that foremost sage went to the hermitage of Tṛṇavindu on the side of the great Mount Meru and resided there.

shloka_text: तपस्तेपे स धर्मात्मा स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः । गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.8 ।।
transliteration: tapastepe sa dharmātmā svādhyāyaniyatendriyaḥ | gatvāśramapadaṃ tasya vighnaṃ kurvanti kanyakāḥ || 7.2.8 ||
translation: सः he, धर्मात्मा the righteous-souled one, स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः with senses controlled by Vedic study, तपः तेपे performed penance, गत्वा having gone, आश्रमपदं to the hermitage, तस्य his, विघ्नं disturbance, कुर्वन्ति they make, कन्यकाः maidens.
explanation: That righteous-souled sage, with his senses controlled by Vedic study, performed severe penance, but maidens would go to his hermitage and create disturbances.

shloka_text: देवपन्नगकन्याश्च राजर्षितनयाश्च याः । क्रीडन्त्यो ऽप्सरसश्चैव तं देशमुपपेदिरे ।। 7.2.9 ।।
transliteration: devapannagakanyāśca rājarṣitanayāśca yāḥ | krīḍantyo 'psarasaścaiva taṃ deśamupapedire || 7.2.9 ||
translation: देवपन्नगकन्याश्च daughters of gods and serpents, राजर्षितनयाश्च and daughters of royal sages, याः who, क्रीडन्त्यो playing, अप्सरसश्चैव and Apsaras too, तं that, देशम् place, उपपेदिरे reached.
explanation: Daughters of gods, serpents, and royal sages, along with Apsaras, arrived at that place to play.

shloka_text: सर्वर्तुषृपभोग्यत्वाद्रम्यत्वात्काननस्य च । नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.10 ।।
transliteration: sarvartuṣṛpabhogyatvādramyatvātkānanasya ca | nityaśastāstu taṃ deśaṃ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ || 7.2.10 ||
translation: सर्वर्तुषृपभोग्यत्वात् due to being enjoyable in all seasons, रम्यत्वात् due to beauty, काननस्य च and of the forest, नित्यशस्तास्तु always, तं that, देशम् place, गत्वा having gone, क्रीडन्ति play, कन्यकाः maidens.
explanation: Because the forest was beautiful and enjoyable in all seasons, these maidens always went to that place to play.

shloka_text: देशस्य रमणीयत्वात्पुलस्त्यो यत्र स द्विजः । गायन्त्यो वादयन्त्यश्च लासयन्त्यस्तथैव च । मुनेस्तपस्विनस्तस्य विघ्नं चक्रुरनिन्दिताः ।। 7.2.11 ।।
transliteration: deśasya ramaṇīyatvātpulastyo yatra sa dvijaḥ | gāyantyo vādayantyaśca lāsayantyastathaiva ca | munestapasvinastasya vighnaṃ cakruraninditāḥ || 7.2.11 ||
translation: देशस्य of the place, रमणीयत्वात् due to beauty, पुलस्त्यो Pulastya, यत्र where, स he, द्विजः brahmin, गायन्त्यो singing, वादयन्त्यश्च and playing instruments, लासयन्त्यस्तथैव च and dancing thus, मुनेः of the sage, तपस्विनस्तस्य of that ascetic, विघ्नं obstruction, चक्रुः caused, अनिन्दिताः blameless (maidens).
explanation: Due to the beauty of the place where the brahmin Pulastya resided, the blameless maidens, by singing, playing instruments, and dancing, caused an obstruction to that ascetic sage.

shloka_text: अथ क्रुद्धो महातेजा व्याजहार महामुनिः । या मे दर्शनमागच्छेत्सा गर्भं धारयिष्यति ।। 7.2.12 ।।
transliteration: atha kruddho mahātejā vyājahāra mahāmuniḥ | yā me darśanamāgacchetsā garbhaṃ dhārayiṣyati || 7.2.12 ||
translation: अथ then, क्रुद्धो angered, महातेजा greatly effulgent, व्याजहार spoke, महामुनिः the great sage, या whoever, मे my, दर्शनम् sight, आगच्छेत् comes, सा she, गर्भं a fetus, धारयिष्यति will bear.
explanation: Then, the greatly effulgent great sage, being angered, declared, "Whoever comes into my sight will conceive a child."

shloka_text: तास्तु सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्य वाक्यं महात्मनः । ब्रह्मशापभयाद्भीतास्तं देशं नोपचक्रमुः ।। 7.2.13 ।।
transliteration: tāstu sarvāḥ pratiśrutya tasya vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ | brahmaśāpabhayādbhītāstaṃ deśaṃ nopacakramuḥ || 7.2.13 ||
translation: तास्तु but they, सर्वाः all, प्रतिश्रुत्य having heard, तस्य his, वाक्यं words, महात्मनः of the great soul, ब्रह्मशापभयात् from fear of the brahmin's curse, भीताः frightened, तं that, देशं place, न not, उपचक्रमुः approached.
explanation: But all of them, having heard the words of that great soul, were frightened by the brahmin's curse and no longer approached that place.

shloka_text: तृणबिन्दोस्तु राजर्षेस्तनया न शृणोति तत् ।। 7.2.14 ।।
transliteration: tṛṇabindostu rājarṣestanayā na śṛṇoti tat || 7.2.14 ||
translation: तृणबिन्दोः of Tṛṇabindu, तु indeed, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, तनया daughter, न not, शृणोति hears, तत् that
explanation: But the daughter of the royal sage Tṛṇabindu did not hear that.

shloka_text: गत्वाश्रमपदं तत्र विचचार सुनिर्भया । न सापश्यत्स्थिता तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् ।। 7.2.15 ।।
transliteration: gatvāśramapadaṃ tatra vicacāra sunirbhayā | na sāpaśyatsthitā tatra kāñcidabhyāgatāṃ sakhīm || 7.2.15 ||
translation: गत्वा having gone, आश्रमपदम् to the hermitage, तत्र there, विचचार she wandered, सुनिर्भया very fearlessly, न not, सा she, अपश्यत् saw, स्थिता present, तत्र there, काञ्चित् any, अभ्यागताम् arrived, सखीम् friend
explanation: Having gone to the hermitage, she wandered there very fearlessly, but she did not see any friend present or arrived there.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्काले महातेजाः प्राजापत्यो महानृषिः । स्वाध्यायमकरोत्तत्र तपसा भावितः स्वयम् ।। 7.2.16 ।।
transliteration: tasminkāle mahātejāḥ prājāpatyo mahānṛṣiḥ | svādhyāyamakarottatra tapasā bhāvitaḥ svayam || 7.2.16 ||
translation: तस्मिन् in that, काले time, महातेजाः greatly effulgent, प्राजापत्यः son of Prajāpati, महानृषिः great sage, स्वाध्यायम् self-study, अकरोत् he performed, तत्र there, तपसा by penance, भावितः purified, स्वयम् himself
explanation: At that time, the greatly effulgent great sage, son of Prajāpati, purified by his own penance, was performing self-study of the Vedas there.

shloka_text: सा तु वेदश्रुतिं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा वै तपसो निधिम् । अभवत्पाण्डुदेहा सा सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा ।। 7.2.17 ।।
transliteration: sā tu vedaśrutiṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā vai tapaso nidhim | abhavatpāṇḍudehā sā suvyañjitaśarīrajā || 7.2.17 ||
translation: सा she, तु but, वेदश्रुतिम् the sound of the Vedas, श्रुत्वा having heard, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वै indeed, तपसः of penance, निधिम् the treasure, अभवत् she became, पाण्डुदेहा pale-bodied, सा she, सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा with clearly manifested bodily signs
explanation: But she, having heard the sound of the Vedas and indeed having seen the repository of penance, became pale-bodied with clearly manifested bodily signs.

shloka_text: वभूव च समुद्विग्ना दृष्ट्वा तद्दोषमात्मनः । इदं मे किन्त्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वा ऽ ऽश्रमे स्थिता ।। 7.2.18 ।।
transliteration: vabhūva ca samudvignā dṛṣṭvā taddoṣamātmanaḥ | idaṃ me kintviti jñātvā piturgatvā ' 'śrame sthitā || 7.2.18 ||
translation: वभूव she became, च and, समुद्विग्ना agitated, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तत् that, दोषम् fault, आत्मनः of herself, इदम् this, मे to me, किन्तु what (is this), इति thus, ज्ञात्वा having known, पितुः of her father, गत्वा having gone, आश्रमे in the hermitage, स्थिता she stayed
explanation: And she became agitated, having seen that fault in herself, and understanding "what is this that has happened to me?", she went and stayed in her father's hermitage.

shloka_text: तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतां तृणविन्दुरथाब्रवीत् । किं त्वमेतत्त्वसदृशं धारयस्यात्मनो वपुः ।। 7.2.19 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtāṃ tṛṇavindurathābravīt | kiṃ tvametattvasadṛśaṃ dhārayasyātmano vapuḥ || 7.2.19 ||
translation: तां her, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तथाभूतां in that state, तृणविन्दुः Tṛṇabindu, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, किं why, त्वम् you, एतत् this, त्वसदृशं unbefitting you, धारयसि bear, आत्मनः your own, वपुः body.
explanation: Seeing her in such a transformed state, Tṛṇabindu then asked her why she was bearing a form so unbefitting her true self.

shloka_text: सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योवाच तपोधनम् । न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम् ।। 7.2.20 ।।
transliteration: sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṃ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam | na jāne kāraṇaṃ tāta yena me rūpamīdṛśam || 7.2.20 ||
translation: सा she, तु indeed, कृत्वा having made, अञ्जलिं a respectful salutation, दीना distressed, कन्या the maiden, उवाच spoke, तपोधनम् to the ascetic, न not, जाने I know, कारणं the reason, तात O father, येन by which, मे my, रूपम् form, ईदृशम् is like this.
explanation: The distressed maiden, having respectfully saluted the ascetic, replied that she did not know the reason, O father, why her form had become like this.

shloka_text: किं तु पूर्वं गतास्म्येका महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं दिव्यमन्वेष्टुं स्वसखीजनम् ।। 7.2.21 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ tu pūrvaṃ gatāsmyekā maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ | pulastyasyāśramaṃ divyamanveṣṭuṃ svasakhījanam || 7.2.21 ||
translation: किं तु but, पूर्वं previously, गतास्मि I went, एका alone, महर्षेः of the great sage, भावितात्मनः whose soul is purified, पुलस्त्यस्य of Pulastya, आश्रमं to the hermitage, दिव्यम् divine, अन्वेष्टुं to search for, स्वसखीजनम् my female companions.
explanation: However, she continued, previously she had gone alone to the divine hermitage of the great sage Pulastya, whose soul was purified, to search for her female companions.

shloka_text: न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् । रूपस्य तु विपर्यासं दृष्ट्वा त्रासादिहागता ।। 7.2.22 ।।
transliteration: na ca paśyāmyahaṃ tatra kāñcidabhyāgatāṃ sakhīm | rūpasya tu viparyāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā trāsādihāgatā || 7.2.22 ||
translation: न not, च and, पश्यामि I see, अहं I, तत्र there, काञ्चित् any, अभ्यागतां arrived, सखीम् friend, रूपस्य of the form, तु but, विपर्यासं transformation, दृष्ट्वा having seen, त्रासात् from fear, इह here, आगता I came.
explanation: She added that she did not see any of her friends who had arrived there, but having seen the transformation of her own form, she came here out of fear.

shloka_text: तृणबिन्दुस्तु राजर्षिस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः । ध्यानं विवेश तच्चापि ह्यपश्यदृषिकर्मजम् ।। 7.2.23 ।।
transliteration: tṛṇabindustu rājarṣistapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ | dhyānaṃ viveśa taccāpi hyapaśyadṛṣikarmajam || 7.2.23 ||
translation: तृणबिन्दुः Tṛṇabindu, तु indeed, राजर्षिः the royal sage, तपसा by penance, द्योतितप्रभः whose splendor was illuminated, ध्यानं meditation, विवेश entered, तत् that, च and, अपि also, हि indeed, अपश्यत् he saw, ऋषिकर्मजम् born of a sage's action.
explanation: The royal sage Tṛṇabindu, whose splendor was illuminated by his penance, then entered into meditation and indeed perceived that the transformation was due to a sage's action.

shloka_text: स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । गृहीत्वा तनयां गत्वा पुलस्त्यमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.2.24 ।।
transliteration: sa tu vijñāya taṃ śāpaṃ maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ | gṛhītvā tanayāṃ gatvā pulastyamidamabravīt || 7.2.24 ||
translation: सः He, तु indeed, विज्ञाय having understood, तम् that, शापम् curse, महर्षेः of the great sage, भावितात्मनः of the self-realized one, गृहीत्वा having taken, तनयाम् his daughter, गत्वा having gone, पुलस्त्यम् to Pulastya, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् he said.
explanation: King Trasabindu, having understood the curse from the great self-realized sage, took his daughter and went to Pulastya, to whom he spoke these words.

shloka_text: भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम् । भिक्षां प्रतिगृहाणेमां महर्षे स्वयमुद्यताम् ।। 7.2.25 ।।
transliteration: bhagavaṃstanayāṃ me tvaṃ guṇaiḥ svaireva bhūṣitām | bhikṣāṃ pratigṛhāṇemāṃ maharṣe svayamudyatām || 7.2.25 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, तनयाम् daughter, मे my, त्वम् you, गुणैः with qualities, स्वैः her own, एव indeed, भूषिताम् adorned, भिक्षाम् alms, प्रतिगृहाण please accept, इमाम् this, महर्षे O great sage, स्वयम् by herself, उद्यताम् offered.
explanation: O revered great sage, please accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her own virtues, as an offering that she herself is ready to make.

shloka_text: तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य श्रम्यमाणेन्द्रियस्य ते । शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.2.26 ।।
transliteration: tapaścaraṇayuktasya śramyamāṇendriyasya te | śuśrūṣaṇaparā nityaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.2.26 ||
translation: तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य of one engaged in ascetic practices, श्रम्यमाणेन्द्रियस्य of one whose senses are fatigued, ते your, शुश्रूषणपरा devoted to service, नित्यम् always, भविष्यति she will be, न no, संशयः doubt.
explanation: She will undoubtedly always be devoted to serving you, whose senses are fatigued from engaging in ascetic practices.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षिं धार्मिकं तदा । जिघृक्षुरब्रवीत्कन्यां बाढमित्येव स द्विजः ।। 7.2.27 ।।
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājarṣiṃ dhārmikaṃ tadā | jighṛkṣurabravītkanyāṃ bāḍhamityeva sa dvijaḥ || 7.2.27 ||
translation: तम् to him, ब्रुवाणम् who was speaking, तु indeed, तद्वाक्यम् those words, राजर्षिम् to the royal sage, धार्मिकम् righteous, तदा then, जिघृक्षुः desirous of taking, अब्रवीत् he said, कन्याम् the daughter, बाढम् certainly, इति thus, एव indeed, सः that, द्विजः brahmin.
explanation: Then, that brahmin (Pulastya), wishing to accept the daughter, said "Certainly, yes" to the righteous royal sage who was speaking those words.

shloka_text: दत्त्वा स तु यथान्यायं स्वमाश्रमपदं गतः । सापि तत्रावसत्कन्या तोषयन्ती पतिं गुणैः ।। 7.2.28 ।।
transliteration: dattvā sa tu yathānyāyaṃ svamāśramapadaṃ gataḥ | sāpi tatrāvasatkanyā toṣayantī patiṃ guṇaiḥ || 7.2.28 ||
translation: दत्त्वा having given, सः he, तु indeed, यथान्यायम् according to custom, स्वम् his own, आश्रमपदम् hermitage, गतः went, सा she, अपि also, तत्र there, अवसत् lived, कन्या the daughter, तोषयन्ती pleasing, पतिम् her husband, गुणैः with her virtues.
explanation: Having properly given his daughter, King Trasabindu returned to his own hermitage, and the daughter also lived there, pleasing her husband with her virtues.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तु शीलवृत्ताभ्यां तुतोष मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.29 ।।
transliteration: tasyāstu śīlavṛttābhyāṃ tutoṣa munipuṅgavaḥ | prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.2.29 ||
translation: तस्याः her, तु indeed, शीलवृत्ताभ्यां by character and conduct, तुतोष was pleased, मुनिपुङ्गवः the excellent sage, प्रीतः pleased, स he, तु indeed, महातेजा the greatly effulgent one, वाक्यम् words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: The excellent sage Pulastya was greatly pleased by her character and conduct, and being delighted, the greatly effulgent one spoke these words.

shloka_text: परितुष्टो ऽस्मि सुश्रोणि गुणानां सम्पदा भृशम् । तस्माद्देवि ददाम्यद्य पुत्रमात्मसमं तव ।। 7.2.30 ।।
transliteration: parituṣṭo 'smi suśroṇi guṇānāṃ sampadā bhṛśam | tasmāddevi dadāmyadya putramātmasamaṃ tava || 7.2.30 ||
translation: परितुष्टः completely satisfied, अस्मि I am, सुश्रोणि O beautiful-hipped one, गुणानाम् of qualities, सम्पदा by abundance, भृशम् exceedingly, तस्मात् therefore, देवि O goddess, ददामि I give, अद्य today, पुत्रम् a son, आत्मसमम् equal to myself, तव to you.
explanation: O beautiful-hipped one, I am exceedingly pleased by your abundance of virtues; therefore, O goddess, I grant you today a son equal to myself.

shloka_text: उभयोर्वंशकर्तारं पौलस्त्य इति विश्रुतम् । यस्मात्तु विश्रुतो वेदस्त्वयैषो ऽध्ययतो मम ।। 7.2.31 ।।
transliteration: ubhayorvaṃśakartāraṃ paulastya iti viśrutam | yasmāttu viśruto vedastvayaiṣo 'dhyayato mama || 7.2.31 ||
translation: उभयोः of both, वंशकर्तारम् the progenitor of the lineage, पौलस्त्यः Pulastya, इति thus, विश्रुतम् renowned, यस्मात् because, तु indeed, विश्रुतः heard, वेदः the Veda, त्वया by you, एषः this, अध्ययतः while studying, मम my.
explanation: He will be renowned as the progenitor of both our lineages, and because you heard this Veda while I was reciting it.

shloka_text: तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः । एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ।। 7.2.32 ।।
transliteration: tasmātsa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ | evamuktā tu sā devī prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā || 7.2.32 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, स he, विश्रवा Vishrava, नाम named, भविष्यति will be, न not, संशयः doubt, एवम् thus, उक्ता spoken to, तु indeed, सा she, देवी the goddess, प्रहृष्टेन delighted, अन्तरात्मना with her inner self.
explanation: Therefore, he will undoubtedly be named Vishrava; thus addressed, that goddess, with a delighted heart.

shloka_text: अचिरेणैव कालेनासूत विश्रवसं सुतम् । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यशोधर्मसमन्वितम् ।। 7.2.33 ।।
transliteration: acireṇaiva kālenāsūta viśravasaṃ sutam | triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ yaśodharmasamanvitam || 7.2.33 ||
translation: अचिरेण in a short time, एव indeed, कालेन by time, असूत gave birth, विश्रवसम् Vishravas, सुतम् a son, त्रिषु in three, लोकेषु worlds, विख्यातं renowned, यशोधर्मसमन्वितम् endowed with fame and righteousness.
explanation: In a short time, she gave birth to a son named Vishravas, who became renowned in the three worlds and was endowed with fame and righteousness.

shloka_text: श्रुतिमान्समदर्शी च व्रताचाररतस्तथा । पितेव तपसा युक्तो ह्यभवद्विश्रवा मुनिः ।। 7.2.34 ।।
transliteration: śrutimānsamadarśī ca vratācāraratastathā | piteva tapasā yukto hyabhavadviśravā muniḥ || 7.2.34 ||
translation: श्रुतिमान् possessed of scriptural knowledge, समदर्शी one who sees all equally, च and, व्रताचाररतः devoted to vows and observances, तथा also, पिता इव like his father, तपसा with austerity, युक्तः endowed, हि indeed, अभवत् became, विश्रवाः Vishrava, मुनिः a sage.
explanation: Sage Vishrava became learned in scriptures, impartial, devoted to vows and observances, and indeed, like his father, engaged in severe austerities. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः ।। 2 ।। Thus ends the second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ पुत्रः पुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । अचिरेणैव कालेन पितेव तपसि स्थितः ।। 7.3.1 ।।
transliteration: atha putraḥ pulastyasya viśravā munipuṅgavaḥ | acireṇaiva kālena piteva tapasi sthitaḥ || 7.3.1 ||
translation: अथ then, पुत्रः the son, पुलस्त्यस्य of Pulastya, विश्रवाः Vishrava, मुनिपुङ्गवः the foremost among sages, अचिरेण एव in a short time, कालेन by time, पिता इव like his father, तपसि in penance, स्थितः engaged.
explanation: Then, Vishrava, the son of Pulastya and foremost among sages, soon became engaged in penance just like his father.
comments: Vishravas weds Bharadvaja's daughter and begets Vaishravana (Kubera) -- by severe penance Kubera wins from Brahma the lordship of wealth, the rank of world-guardian, and the Pushpaka chariot -- at his father's counsel he settles in Lanka on Mount Trikuta, built by Vishvakarma and once abandoned by the rakshasas who fled to Patala in fear of Vishnu -- Kubera dwells there in prosperity.

shloka_text: सत्यवाञ्छीलवाञ्छान्तः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचिः । सर्वभोगेष्वसंसक्तो नित्यं धर्मपरायणः ।। 7.3.2 ।।
transliteration: satyavāñchīlavāñchāntaḥ svādhyāyanirataḥ śuciḥ | sarvabhogeṣvasaṃsakto nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ || 7.3.2 ||
translation: सत्यवान् truthful, शीलवान् virtuous, शान्तः peaceful, स्वाध्यायनिरतः devoted to self-study, शुचिः pure, सर्वभोगेषु in all enjoyments, असंसक्तः unattached, नित्यम् always, धर्मपरायणः devoted to righteousness.
explanation: He was truthful, virtuous, peaceful, devoted to Vedic study, pure, unattached to all worldly enjoyments, and constantly dedicated to righteousness.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा तस्य तु तद्वृत्तं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः । ददौ विश्रवसे भार्यां स्वसुतां देववर्णिनीम् ।। 7.3.3 ।।
transliteration: jñātvā tasya tu tadvṛttaṃ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ | dadau viśravase bhāryāṃ svasutāṃ devavarṇinīm || 7.3.3 ||
translation: ज्ञात्वा having known, तस्य his, तु indeed, तत् वृत्तम् that conduct, भरद्वाजः Bharadvaja, महामुनिः the great sage, ददौ gave, विश्रवसे to Vishrava, भार्याम् a wife, स्वसुताम् his own daughter, देववर्णिनीम् Devavarnini.
explanation: Understanding Vishrava's excellent character, the great sage Bharadvaja gave his own daughter, Devavarnini, as a wife to Vishrava.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु धर्मेण भरद्वाजसुतां तदा । प्रजान्वेक्षिकया बुद्ध्या श्रेयो ह्यस्य विचिन्तयन् ।। 7.3.4 ।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tu dharmeṇa bharadvājasutāṃ tadā | prajānvekṣikayā buddhyā śreyo hyasya vicintayan || 7.3.4 ||
translation: प्रतिगृह्य having accepted, तु indeed, धर्मेण righteously, भरद्वाजसुताम् Bharadvaja's daughter, तदा then, प्रजान्वेक्षिकया with a mind intent on progeny, बुद्ध्या with understanding, श्रेयः the welfare, हि indeed, अस्य his, विचिन्तयन् contemplating.
explanation: Then, Vishrava, having righteously accepted Bharadvaja's daughter, contemplated his welfare with an intellect focused on the desire for progeny.

shloka_text: मुदा परमया युक्तो विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । स तस्यां वीर्यसम्पन्नमपत्यं परमाद्भुतम् ।। 7.3.5 ।।
transliteration: mudā paramayā yukto viśravā munipuṅgavaḥ | sa tasyāṃ vīryasampannamapatyaṃ paramādbhutam || 7.3.5 ||
translation: मुदा with joy, परमया supreme, युक्तो endowed, विश्रवा Vishrava, मुनिपुङ्गवः foremost among sages, स he, तस्यां in her, वीर्यसम्पन्नम् endowed with valor, अपत्यं an offspring, परमाद्भुतम् exceedingly wonderful
explanation: The foremost sage Vishrava, filled with supreme joy, begot in her an exceedingly wonderful offspring endowed with great valor.

shloka_text: जनयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्युतम् । तस्मिञ्जाते तु संहृष्टः सम्बभूव पितामहः ।। 7.3.6 ।।
transliteration: janayāmāsa dharmajñaḥ sarvairbrahmaguṇairyutam | tasmiñjāte tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sambabhūva pitāmahaḥ || 7.3.6 ||
translation: जनयामास begot, धर्मज्ञः the knower of Dharma, सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्युतम् endowed with all divine qualities, तस्मिञ्जाते when he was born, तु indeed, संहृष्टः greatly delighted, सम्बभूव became, पितामहः the grandfather (Brahma)
explanation: This knower of Dharma begot a child endowed with all divine qualities, and when he was born, the grandfather (Brahma) became greatly delighted.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा श्रेयस्करीं बुद्धिं धनाध्यक्षो भविष्यति । नाम तस्याकरोत्प्रीतः सार्धं देवर्षिभिस्तदा ।। 7.3.7 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā śreyaskarīṃ buddhiṃ dhanādhyakṣo bhaviṣyati | nāma tasyākarotprītaḥ sārdhaṃ devarṣibhistadā || 7.3.7 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, श्रेयस्करीं auspicious, बुद्धिं intention, धनाध्यक्षो lord of wealth, भविष्यति will be, नाम a name, तस्याकरोत् he made for him, प्रीतः pleased, सार्धं together with, देवर्षिभिस्तदा the divine sages then
explanation: Having perceived his auspicious intention to become the lord of wealth, the pleased grandfather (Brahma), together with the divine sages, then gave him a name.

shloka_text: यस्माद्विश्रवसो ऽपत्यं सादृश्याद्विश्रवा इव । तस्माद्वैश्रवणो नाम भविष्यत्वेष विश्रुतः ।। 7.3.8 ।।
transliteration: yasmādviśravaso 'patyaṃ sādṛśyādviśravā iva | tasmādvaiśravaṇo nāma bhaviṣyatveṣa viśrutaḥ || 7.3.8 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, विश्रवसो of Vishrava, अपत्यं the offspring, सादृश्यात् due to resemblance, विश्रवा Vishrava, इव like, तस्मात् therefore, वैश्रवणो Vaishravana, नाम by name, भविष्यत्वेष this one will be, विश्रुतः renowned
explanation: Because this offspring of Vishrava resembles Vishrava himself, he will therefore be renowned by the name Vaishravana.

shloka_text: स तु वैश्रवणस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा । अवर्धताहुतिहुतो महातेजा यथानलः ।। 7.3.9 ।।
transliteration: sa tu vaiśravaṇastatra tapovanagatastadā | avardhatāhutihuto mahātejā yathānalaḥ || 7.3.9 ||
translation: स he, तु indeed, वैश्रवणः Vaishravana, तत्र there, तपोवनगतः having gone to the hermitage, तदा then, अवर्धत grew, आहुतिहुतो nourished by oblations, महातेजा greatly effulgent, यथा like, अनलः fire
explanation: Then, Vaishravana, having gone to the hermitage, grew there, greatly effulgent, like a fire nourished by oblations.

shloka_text: तस्याश्रमपदस्थस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः । चरिष्ये परमं धर्मं धर्मो हि परमा गतिः ।। 7.3.10 ।।
transliteration: tasyāśramapadasthasya buddhirjajñe mahātmanaḥ | cariṣye paramaṃ dharmaṃ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ || 7.3.10 ||
translation: तस्याश्रमपदस्थस्य residing in his hermitage, बुद्धिः thought, जज्ञे arose, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, चरिष्ये I shall practice, परमम् supreme, धर्मम् righteousness, धर्मः righteousness, हि indeed, परमा supreme, गतिः goal.
explanation: A thought arose in the mind of the great sage residing in his hermitage that he would practice supreme righteousness, for righteousness is indeed the ultimate goal.

shloka_text: स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने । यन्त्रितो नियमैरुग्रैश्चकार सुमहत्तपः ।। 7.3.11 ।।
transliteration: sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptvā mahāvane | yantrito niyamairugraiścakāra sumahattapaḥ || 7.3.11 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, वर्षसहस्राणि for thousands of years, तपः penance, तप्त्वा having performed, महावने in the great forest, यन्त्रितः restrained, नियमैः by vows, उग्रैः severe, चकार performed, सुमहत्तपः very great penance.
explanation: Indeed, he performed very great penance for thousands of years in the great forest, having restrained himself with severe vows.

shloka_text: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रान्ते तं तं विधिमकल्पयत् । जलाशी मारुताहारो निराहारस्तथैव च ।। 7.3.12 ।।
transliteration: pūrṇe varṣasahasrānte taṃ taṃ vidhimakalpayat | jalāśī mārutāhāro nirāhārastathaiva ca || 7.3.12 ||
translation: पूर्णे at the completion, वर्षसहस्रान्ते of a thousand years, तम् तम् various, विधिम् methods, अकल्पयत् he adopted, जलाशी subsisting on water, मारुताहारः subsisting on air, निराहारः without food, तथैव च and similarly.
explanation: At the completion of each thousand years, he adopted various methods of austerity, such as subsisting only on water, then only on air, and then completely without food.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि जग्मुस्तान्येकवर्षवत् । अथ प्रीतो महातेजाः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह ।। 7.3.13 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi jagmustānyekavarṣavat | atha prīto mahātejāḥ sendraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha || 7.3.13 ||
translation: एवम् thus, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, जग्मुः passed, तानि those, एकवर्षवत् like a single year, अथ then, प्रीतः pleased, महातेजाः the greatly effulgent one, सेन्द्रैः with Indra, सुरगणैः with the hosts of gods, सह together.
explanation: Thus, those thousands of years passed as if they were a single year, and then the greatly effulgent Brahma, pleased, came with Indra and the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: गत्वा तस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मेदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । परितुष्टो ऽस्मि ते वत्स कर्मणानेन सुव्रत । वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते वरार्हस्त्वं महामते ।। 7.3.14 ।।
transliteration: gatvā tasyāśramapadaṃ brahmedaṃ vākyamabravīt | parituṣṭo 'smi te vatsa karmaṇānena suvrata | varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te varārhastvaṃ mahāmate || 7.3.14 ||
translation: गत्वा having gone, तस्य his, आश्रमपदम् hermitage, ब्रह्मा Brahma, इदम् this, वाक्यम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke, परितुष्टः greatly pleased, अस्मि I am, ते with you, वत्स O child, कर्मणा by deed, अनेन this, सुव्रत O one of good vows, वरम् boon, वृणीष्व choose, भद्रम् welfare, ते to you, वरार्हः deserving of a boon, त्वम् you, महामते O great-minded one.
explanation: Having gone to his hermitage, Brahma spoke these words: "O child of good vows, I am greatly pleased with this deed of yours; choose a boon, may there be welfare for you, O great-minded one, for you are deserving of a boon."

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः पितामहमुपस्थितम् । भगवँल्लोकपालत्वमिच्छेयं वित्तरक्षणम् ।। 7.3.15 ।।
transliteration: athābravīdvaiśravaṇaḥ pitāmahamupasthitam | bhagavaँllokapālatvamiccheyaṃ vittarakṣaṇam || 7.3.15 ||
translation: अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, वैश्रवणः Vaishravana, पितामहम् to the grandfather (Brahma), उपस्थितम् who was present, भगवन् O Lord, लोकपालत्वम् the state of being a world-protector, इच्छेयम् I desire, वित्तरक्षणम् the protection of wealth,
explanation: Then Vaishravana, standing before his grandfather Brahma, said, "O Lord, I desire to be a guardian of the world and a protector of wealth."

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणं परितुष्टेन चेतसा । ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धं बाढमित्येव हृष्टवत् ।। 7.3.16 ।।
transliteration: athābravīdvaiśravaṇaṃ parituṣṭena cetasā | brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bāḍhamityeva hṛṣṭavat || 7.3.16 ||
translation: अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, वैश्रवणम् to Vaishravana, परितुष्टेन with a very pleased, चेतसा mind, ब्रह्मा Brahma, सुरगणैः with the hosts of gods, सार्धम् together with, बाढम् "So be it", इति thus, एव indeed, हृष्टवत् joyfully,
explanation: Then Brahma, with a very pleased mind, joyfully spoke to Vaishravana in the presence of the hosts of gods, saying, "So be it."

shloka_text: अहं वै लोकपालानां चतुर्थं स्रष्टुमुद्यतः ।। 7.3.17 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ vai lokapālānāṃ caturthaṃ sraṣṭumudyataḥ || 7.3.17 ||
translation: अहम् I, वै indeed, लोकपालानाम् among the world-protectors, चतुर्थम् the fourth, स्रष्टुम् to create, उद्यतः was ready,
explanation: Brahma declared, "Indeed, I was about to create the fourth among the world-protectors."

shloka_text: यमेन्द्रवरुणानां च पदं यत्तव चेप्सितम् । तद्गच्छ त्वं हि धर्मज्ञ निधीशत्वमवाप्नुहि । शक्राम्बुपयमानां च चतुर्थस्त्वं भविष्यसि ।। 7.3.18 ।।
transliteration: yamendravaruṇānāṃ ca padaṃ yattava cepsitam | tadgaccha tvaṃ hi dharmajña nidhīśatvamavāpnuhi | śakrāmbupayamānāṃ ca caturthastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi || 7.3.18 ||
translation: यम Yama, इन्द्र Indra, वरुणानाम् and Varuna, च and, पदम् the position, यत् which, तव by you, च and, ईप्सितम् desired, तत् that, गच्छ attain, त्वम् you, हि indeed, धर्मज्ञ O knower of dharma, निधीशत्वम् the state of being the lord of treasures, अवाप्नुहि obtain, शक्र Indra, अम्बुप Varuna, यमानाम् and Yama, च and, चतुर्थः the fourth, त्वम् you, भविष्यसि will be,
explanation: Brahma continued, "O righteous one, attain that desired position alongside Yama, Indra, and Varuna; indeed, obtain the lordship of treasures, and you shall be the fourth among Indra, Varuna, and Yama."

shloka_text: एतच्च पुष्पकं नाम विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम् । प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यानार्थं त्रिदशैः समतां व्रज ।। 7.3.19 ।।
transliteration: etacca puṣpakaṃ nāma vimānaṃ sūryasannibham | pratigṛhṇīṣva yānārthaṃ tridaśaiḥ samatāṃ vraja || 7.3.19 ||
translation: एतत् this, च and, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, नाम named, विमानम् aerial chariot, सूर्यसन्निभम् resembling the sun, प्रतिगृह्णीष्व accept, यानार्थम् for the purpose of travel, त्रिदशैः with the gods, समताम् equality, व्रज attain,
explanation: "And accept this aerial chariot named Pushpaka, which resembles the sun, for your travels, and thereby attain equality with the gods."

shloka_text: स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामः सर्व एव यथागतम् । कृतकृत्या वयं तात दत्त्वा तव वरद्वयम् ।। 7.3.20 ।।
transliteration: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmaḥ sarva eva yathāgatam | kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ tāta dattvā tava varadvayam || 7.3.20 ||
translation: स्वस्ति well-being, ते to you, अस्तु let there be, गमिष्यामः we shall go, सर्व all, एव indeed, यथागतम् as we came, कृतकृत्याः having accomplished our purpose, वयम् we, तात dear son, दत्त्वा having given, तव your, वरद्वयम् two boons.
explanation: Brahma declared that they had accomplished their purpose by granting two boons and would now depart as they had arrived, wishing well-being upon the recipient.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा स गतो ब्रह्मा स्वस्थानं त्रिदशैः सह ।। 7.3.21 ।।
transliteration: ityuktvā sa gato brahmā svasthānaṃ tridaśaiḥ saha || 7.3.21 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, सः he, गतः went, ब्रह्मा Brahma, स्वस्थानम् to his own abode, त्रिदशैः with the gods, सह together with.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Brahma returned to his own abode accompanied by the gods.

shloka_text: गतेषु ब्रह्मपूर्वेषु देवेष्वथ नभस्थलम् । वने स पितरं प्राह प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतात्मवान् । निवासनं न मे देवो विदधे स प्रजापतिः ।। 7.3.22 ।।
transliteration: gateṣu brahmapūrveṣu deveṣvatha nabhasthalam | vane sa pitaraṃ prāha prāñjaliḥ prayatātmavān | nivāsanaṃ na me devo vidadhe sa prajāpatiḥ || 7.3.22 ||
translation: गतेषु when they had gone, ब्रह्मपूर्वेषु led by Brahma, देवेषु the gods, अथ then, नभस्थलम् to the sky, वने in the forest, सः he, पितरम् to his father, प्राह said, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, प्रयतात्मवान् with a controlled mind, निवासनम् a dwelling place, न not, मे for me, देवः the god, विदधे provided, सः that, प्रजापतिः lord of creatures.
explanation: After Brahma and the other gods departed to the heavens, Ravana, with folded hands and a controlled mind, addressed his father in the forest, stating that Brahma had not provided him with a dwelling place.

shloka_text: भगवँल्लब्धवानस्मि वरमिष्टं पितामहात् । तं पश्य भगवन्कञ्चिन्निवासं साधु मे प्रभो ।। 7.3.23 ।।
transliteration: bhagavaँllabdhavānasmi varamiṣṭaṃ pitāmahāt | taṃ paśya bhagavankañcinnivāsaṃ sādhu me prabho || 7.3.23 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, लब्धवान् I have obtained, अस्मि I am, वरम् a boon, इष्टम् desired, पितामहात् from the grandfather, तम् that, पश्य find, भगवन् O revered one, कञ्चित् some, निवासम् dwelling place, साधु suitable, मे for me, प्रभो O lord.
explanation: Ravana informed his father that he had received his desired boon from Brahma and requested his father to find a suitable dwelling place for him.

shloka_text: न च पीडा भवेद्यत्र प्राणिनो यस्य कस्यचित् । एवमुक्तस्तु पुत्रेण विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.3.24 ।।
transliteration: na ca pīḍā bhavedyatra prāṇino yasya kasyacit | evamuktastu putreṇa viśravā munipuṅgavaḥ || 7.3.24 ||
translation: न not, च and, पीडा harm, भवेत् should be, यत्र where, प्राणिनः of a living being, यस्य कस्यचित् of any whatsoever, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, पुत्रेण by his son, विश्रवाः Vishrava, मुनिपुङ्गवः the foremost among sages.
explanation: Ravana further specified that the dwelling place should be one where no living being would suffer any harm, and upon hearing this request from his son, Vishrava, the foremost among sages, considered it.

shloka_text: वचनं प्राह धर्मज्ञः श्रूयतामिति सत्तमः । दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः ।। 7.3.25 ।।
transliteration: vacanaṃ prāha dharmajñaḥ śrūyatāmiti sattamaḥ | dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre trikūṭo nāma parvataḥ || 7.3.25 ||
translation: वचनं word, प्राह said, धर्मज्ञः the knower of dharma, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, इति thus, सत्तमः the excellent one. दक्षिणस्य of the southern, उदधेः of the ocean, तीरे on the shore, त्रिकूटो Trikuta, नाम named, पर्वतः mountain.
explanation: The righteous and excellent one spoke, saying, "Listen! On the shore of the southern ocean, there is a mountain named Trikuta."

shloka_text: तस्याग्रे तु विशाला सा महेन्द्रस्य पुरी यथा । लङ्का नाम पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ।। 7.3.26 ।।
transliteration: tasyāgre tu viśālā sā mahendrasya purī yathā | laṅkā nāma purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā || 7.3.26 ||
translation: तस्य of that (mountain), अग्रे on the top, तु indeed, विशाला vast, सा that, महेन्द्रस्य of Mahendra, पुरी city, यथा like. लङ्का Lanka, नाम named, पुरी city, रम्या beautiful, निर्मिता built, विश्वकर्मणा by Vishwakarma.
explanation: On the top of that mountain, there is a vast and beautiful city named Lanka, constructed by Vishwakarma, resembling the city of Mahendra (Indra).

shloka_text: राक्षसानां निवासार्थं यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती । तत्र त्वं वस भद्रं ते लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः ।। 7.3.27 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ nivāsārthaṃ yathendrasyāmarāvatī | tatra tvaṃ vasa bhadraṃ te laṅkāyāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7.3.27 ||
translation: राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas, निवासार्थं for residence, यथा just as, इन्द्रस्य of Indra, अमरावती Amaravati. तत्र there, त्वं you, वस dwell, भद्रं welfare, ते to you, लङ्कायां in Lanka, न not, अत्र here, संशयः doubt.
explanation: That city is meant for the residence of Rakshasas, just as Amaravati is for Indra; you should dwell there in Lanka, and there is no doubt that it will bring you good fortune.

shloka_text: हेमप्राकारपरिघा यन्त्रशस्त्रसमावृता । रमणीया पुरी सा हि रुक्मवैडूर्यतोरणा ।। 7.3.28 ।।
transliteration: hemaprākāraparighā yantraśastrasamāvṛtā | ramaṇīyā purī sā hi rukmavaiḍūryatoraṇā || 7.3.28 ||
translation: हेमप्राकारपरिघा having golden ramparts and moats, यन्त्रशस्त्रसमावृता equipped with machines and weapons. रमणीया charming, पुरी city, सा that, हि indeed, रुक्म gold, वैडूर्य lapis lazuli, तोरणा having archways.
explanation: That delightful city is indeed equipped with golden ramparts and moats, fortified with machines and weapons, and adorned with archways made of gold and lapis lazuli.

shloka_text: राक्षसैः सा परित्यक्ता पुरा विष्णुभयार्दितैः । शून्या रक्षोगणैः सर्वै रसातलतलं गतैः ।। 7.3.29 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasaiḥ sā parityaktā purā viṣṇubhayārditaiḥ | śūnyā rakṣogaṇaiḥ sarvai rasātalatalaṃ gataiḥ || 7.3.29 ||
translation: राक्षसैः by the Rakshasas, सा that (city), परित्यक्ता abandoned, पुरा formerly, विष्णुभयार्दितैः afflicted by fear of Vishnu. शून्या empty, रक्षोगणैः by the hordes of Rakshasas, सर्वैः all, रसातलतलं to the nethermost region, गतैः having gone.
explanation: That city was formerly abandoned by all the hordes of Rakshasas, who, afflicted by fear of Vishnu, had gone to the nethermost regions, leaving it deserted.

shloka_text: शून्या सम्प्रति लङ्का सा प्रभुस्तस्या न विद्यते । स त्वं तत्र निवासाय गच्छ पुत्र यथासुखम् ।। 7.3.30 ।।
transliteration: śūnyā samprati laṅkā sā prabhustasyā na vidyate | sa tvaṃ tatra nivāsāya gaccha putra yathāsukham || 7.3.30 ||
translation: शून्या empty, सम्प्रति now, लङ्का Lanka, सा that, प्रभुः lord, तस्याः of it, न not, विद्यते exists, सः therefore, त्वम् you, तत्र there, निवासाय for dwelling, गच्छ go, पुत्र son, यथासुखम् comfortably.
explanation: That Lanka is now empty and without a master, so you, my son, should go and reside there comfortably.

shloka_text: निर्दोषस्तत्र ते वासो न बाधास्तत्र कस्यचित् । एतच्छुत्वा स धर्मात्मा धर्मिष्ठं वचनं पितुः ।। 7.3.31 ।।
transliteration: nirdoṣastatra te vāso na bādhāstatra kasyacit | etacchutvā sa dharmātmā dharmiṣṭhaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ || 7.3.31 ||
translation: निर्दोषः faultless, तत्र there, ते your, वासः dwelling, न not, बाधाः obstacles, तत्र there, कस्यचित् of anyone, एतत् this, श्रुत्वा having heard, सः he, धर्मात्मा righteous soul, धर्मिष्ठम् most righteous, वचनम् word, पितुः of the father.
explanation: Your dwelling there will be without hindrance, and there will be no obstacles from anyone; having heard this most righteous command from his father, that righteous soul (Kubera)...

shloka_text: निवासयामास तदा लङ्कां पर्वतमूर्धनि । नैर्ऋतानां सहस्रैस्तु हृष्टैः प्रमुदुतैः सह ।। 7.3.32 ।।
transliteration: nivāsayāmāsa tadā laṅkāṃ parvatamūrdhani | nairṛtānāṃ sahasraistu hṛṣṭaiḥ pramudutaiḥ saha || 7.3.32 ||
translation: निवासयामास caused to dwell, तदा then, लङ्काम् Lanka, पर्वतमूर्धनि on the mountain top, नैर्ऋतानाम् of the Rakshasas, सहस्रैः with thousands, तु indeed, हृष्टैः delighted, प्रमुदुतैः greatly joyful, सह with.
explanation: ...then settled Lanka, situated on the mountain top, with thousands of delighted and greatly joyful Rakshasas.

shloka_text: अचिरेणैव कालेन सम्पूर्णा तस्य शासनात् ।। 7.3.33 ।।
transliteration: acireṇaiva kālena sampūrṇā tasya śāsanāt || 7.3.33 ||
translation: अचिरेण in a short, एव indeed, कालेन time, सम्पूर्णा filled, तस्य his, शासनात् by command.
explanation: In a very short time, Lanka was completely filled by his command.

shloka_text: स तु तत्रावसत्प्रीतो धर्मात्मा नैर्ऋतर्षभः । समुद्रपरिघायां तु लङ्कायां विश्रवात्मजः ।। 7.3.34 ।।
transliteration: sa tu tatrāvasatprīto dharmātmā nairṛtarṣabhaḥ | samudraparighāyāṃ tu laṅkāyāṃ viśravātmajaḥ || 7.3.34 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, तत्र there, अवसत् dwelt, प्रीतः pleased, धर्मात्मा righteous soul, नैर्ऋतर्षभः chief of Rakshasas, समुद्रपरिघायाम् surrounded by the ocean, तु indeed, लङ्कायाम् in Lanka, विश्रवात्मजः son of Vishrava.
explanation: That righteous soul, the chief of Rakshasas and son of Vishrava (Kubera), happily dwelt there in Lanka, which was surrounded by the ocean.

shloka_text: काले काले तु धर्मात्मा पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः । अभ्यागच्छद्विनीतात्मा पितरं मातरं च हि ।। 7.3.35 ।।
transliteration: kāle kāle tu dharmātmā puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaraḥ | abhyāgacchadvinītātmā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca hi || 7.3.35 ||
translation: काले काले from time to time, तु indeed, धर्मात्मा righteous-souled, पुष्पकेण by Pushpaka, धनेश्वरः lord of wealth, अभ्यागच्छत् used to come, विनीतात्मा humble-souled, पितरं father, मातरं mother, च and, हि indeed.
explanation: The righteous and humble Kubera, the lord of wealth, used to visit his father and mother from time to time in his Pushpaka chariot.

shloka_text: स देवगन्धर्वगणैरभिष्टुतस्तथाप्सरोनृत्यविभूषितालयः । गभस्तिभिः सूर्य इवावभासयन्पितुः समीपं प्रययौ स वित्तपः ।। 7.3.36 ।।
transliteration: sa devagandharvagaṇairabhiṣṭutastathāpsaronṛtyavibhūṣitālayaḥ | gabhastibhiḥ sūrya ivāvabhāsayanpituḥ samīpaṃ prayayau sa vittapaḥ || 7.3.36 ||
translation: सः he, देवगन्धर्वगणैः by hosts of gods and gandharvas, अभिष्टुतः praised, तथा and, अप्सरोनृत्यविभूषितालयः whose abode was adorned by the dances of Apsaras, गभस्तिभिः by rays, सूर्यः sun, इव like, अवभासयन् illuminating, पितुः father's, समीपं proximity, प्रययौ went, सः he, वित्तपः lord of wealth.
explanation: Praised by hosts of gods and Gandharvas, and with his abode adorned by the dances of Apsaras, that lord of wealth, Kubera, approached his father, shining like the sun with its rays. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः ।। 3 ।। Thus ends the third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वागस्त्येरितं वाक्यं रामो विस्मयमागतः । कथमासीत्तु लङ्कायां सम्भवो रक्षसां पुरा ।। 7.4.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvāgastyeritaṃ vākyaṃ rāmo vismayamāgataḥ | kathamāsīttu laṅkāyāṃ sambhavo rakṣasāṃ purā || 7.4.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, अगस्त्येरितं spoken by Agastya, वाक्यं statement, रामः Rama, विस्मयमागतः became astonished, कथं how, आसीत् was, तु indeed, लङ्कायां in Lanka, सम्भवः origin, रक्षसां of Rakshasas, पुरा formerly.
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, Rama was filled with astonishment, wondering how the Rakshasas could have originated in Lanka in ancient times.
comments: At Rama's wonder over the earlier rakshasas, Agastya tells how Brahma, having created the waters, made beings to guard them -- those who cried 'we will guard' became rakshasas and those 'we will eat' became yakshas -- of the line of Heti and Praheti: Heti weds Bhaya, sister of Death, and begets Vidyutkesha, whose abandoned son is saved and made immortal by Shiva and Parvati as Sukesha, granted a sky-faring city.

shloka_text: ततः शिरः कम्पयित्वा त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम् । तमगस्त्यं मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानो ऽभ्यभाषत ।। 7.4.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śiraḥ kampayitvā tretāgnisamavigraham | tamagastyaṃ muhurdṛṣṭvā smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata || 7.4.2 ||
translation: ततः then, शिरः head, कम्पयित्वा having shaken, त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम् whose body was like the three sacred fires, तम् him, अगस्त्यं Agastya, मुहुः repeatedly, दृष्ट्वा having seen, स्मयमानः smiling, अभ्यभाषत spoke to.
explanation: Then, shaking his head and repeatedly looking at Agastya, whose body resembled the three sacred fires, Rama smiled and spoke to him.

shloka_text: भगवन्पूर्वमप्येषा लङ्कासीत्पिशिताशिनाम् । श्रुत्वेदं भगवद्वाक्यं जातो मे विस्मयः परः ।। 7.4.3 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanpūrvamapyeṣā laṅkāsītpiśitāśinām | śrutvedaṃ bhagavadvākyaṃ jāto me vismayaḥ paraḥ || 7.4.3 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, पूर्वम् formerly, अपि even, एषा this, लङ्का Lanka, आसीत् was, पिशिताशिनाम् of flesh-eaters, श्रुत्वा having heard, इदं this, भगवद्वाक्यं your revered statement, जातः arisen, मे my, विस्मयः astonishment, परः great.
explanation: O revered one, having heard your statement that this Lanka formerly belonged to the flesh-eaters, a great astonishment has arisen within me.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्यवंशादुद्भूता राक्षसा इति नः श्रुतम् । इदानीमन्यतश्चापि सम्भवः कीर्तितस्त्वया ।। 7.4.4 ।।
transliteration: pulastyavaṃśādudbhūtā rākṣasā iti naḥ śrutam | idānīmanyataścāpi sambhavaḥ kīrtitastvayā || 7.4.4 ||
translation: पुलस्त्यवंशात् from Pulastya's lineage, उद्भूताः originated, राक्षसाः Rākṣasas, इति thus, नः by us, श्रुतम् heard, इदानीम् now, अन्यतः from another source, च and, अपि also, सम्भवः origin, कीर्तितः narrated, त्वया by you.
explanation: We have heard that the Rākṣasas originated from Pulastya's lineage, but now you have also spoken of their origin from another source.

shloka_text: रावणात्कुम्भकर्णाच्च प्रहस्ताद्विकटादपि । रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः ।। 7.4.5 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇātkumbhakarṇācca prahastādvikaṭādapi | rāvaṇasya ca putrebhyaḥ kiṃ nu te balavattarāḥ || 7.4.5 ||
translation: रावणात् than Rāvaṇa, कुम्भकर्णात् than Kumbhakarṇa, च and, प्रहस्तात् than Prahasta, विकटात् than Vikaṭa, अपि even, रावणस्य of Rāvaṇa, च and, पुत्रेभ्यः than the sons, किम् what, नु indeed, ते they, बलवत्तराः more powerful.
explanation: Are these new Rākṣasas indeed more powerful than Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Prahasta, Vikaṭa, and even Rāvaṇa's own sons?

shloka_text: क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किन्नामा च बलोत्कटः । अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः कथम् ।। 7.4.6 ।।
transliteration: ka eṣāṃ pūrvako brahmankinnāmā ca balotkaṭaḥ | aparādhaṃ ca kaṃ prāpya viṣṇunā drāvitāḥ katham || 7.4.6 ||
translation: कः who, एषाम् among them, पूर्वकः the first/ancestor, ब्रह्मन् O Brāhmaṇa, किन्नामा what name, च and, बलोत्कटः exceedingly powerful, अपराधम् offense, च and, कम् what, प्राप्य having committed, विष्णुना by Viṣṇu, द्राविताः driven away/destroyed, कथम् how.
explanation: O Brāhmaṇa, who was their first ancestor, what was his name, and how were these exceedingly powerful beings driven away by Viṣṇu after committing what offense?

shloka_text: एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ । कुतूहलमिदं मह्यं नुद भानुर्यथा तमः ।। 7.4.7 ।।
transliteration: etadvistarataḥ sarvaṃ kathayasva mamānagha | kutūhalamidaṃ mahyaṃ nuda bhānuryathā tamaḥ || 7.4.7 ||
translation: एतत् this, विस्तरतः in detail, सर्वम् all, कथयस्व please narrate, मम to me, अनघ O sinless one, कुतूहलम् curiosity, इदम् this, मह्यम् my, नुद dispel, भानुः the sun, यथा just as, तमः darkness.
explanation: O sinless one, please narrate all of this to me in detail and dispel my great curiosity, just as the sun dispels darkness.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संस्कारालङ्कृतं शुभम् । ईषद्विस्मयमानस्तमगस्त्यः प्राह राघवम् ।। 7.4.8 ।।
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃskārālaṅkṛtaṃ śubham | īṣadvismayamānastamagastyaḥ prāha rāghavam || 7.4.8 ||
translation: राघवस्य of Rāghava, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, संस्कारालङ्कृतम् adorned with refinement, शुभम् auspicious/beautiful, ईषत् slightly, विस्मयमानः being surprised, तम् him, अगस्त्यः Agastya, प्राह said, राघवम् to Rāghava.
explanation: Having heard Rāghava's auspicious words, adorned with refinement, Agastya, slightly surprised, spoke to Rāghava.

shloka_text: प्रजापतिः पुरा सृष्ट्वा ह्यपः सलिलसम्भवः । तासां गोपायने सत्त्वानसृजत्पद्मसम्भवः ।। 7.4.9 ।।
transliteration: prajāpatiḥ purā sṛṣṭvā hyapaḥ salilasambhavaḥ | tāsāṃ gopāyane sattvānasṛjatpadmasambhavaḥ || 7.4.9 ||
translation: प्रजापतिः Prajapati, पुरा formerly, सृष्ट्वा having created, हि indeed, अपः waters, सलिलसम्भवः born from water, तासाम् of those (waters), गोपायने for the protection, सत्त्वान् beings, असृजत् created, पद्मसम्भवः born from a lotus.
explanation: In ancient times, Prajapati Brahma, who was born from water and a lotus, first created the waters and then created various beings for their protection.

shloka_text: ते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वकर्तारं विनीतवदुपस्थिताः । किं कुर्म इति भाषन्तः क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः ।। 7.4.10 ।।
transliteration: te sattvāḥ sattvakartāraṃ vinītavadupasthitāḥ | kiṃ kurma iti bhāṣantaḥ kṣutpipāsābhayārditāḥ || 7.4.10 ||
translation: ते those, सत्त्वाः beings, सत्त्वकर्तारम् to the creator of beings, विनीतवत् humbly, उपस्थिताः stood before, किम् what, कुर्मः shall we do, इति thus, भाषन्तः speaking, क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear.
explanation: Those beings, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear, humbly approached their creator and asked, "What shall we do?"

shloka_text: प्रजापतिस्तु तान्याह सत्वानि प्रहसन्निव । आभाष्य वाचा यत्नेन रक्षध्वमिति मानदः ।। 7.4.11 ।।
transliteration: prajāpatistu tānyāha satvāni prahasanniva | ābhāṣya vācā yatnena rakṣadhvamiti mānadaḥ || 7.4.11 ||
translation: प्रजापतिः Prajapati, तु indeed, तान् to them, आह said, सत्त्वानि to the beings, प्रहसन् as if laughing, इव as it were, आभाष्य having addressed, वाचा with words, यत्नेन with effort, रक्षध्वम् protect, इति thus, मानदः the giver of honor.
explanation: Prajapati, the giver of honor, addressed those beings as if with a smile and instructed them with effort, "Protect!"

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च तत्रान्ये जक्षाम इति चापरे । भुक्षिताभुक्षितैरुक्तस्ततस्तानाह भूतकृत् ।। 7.4.12 ।।
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca tatrānye jakṣāma iti cāpare | bhukṣitābhukṣitairuktastatastānāha bhūtakṛt || 7.4.12 ||
translation: रक्षाम we will protect, इति thus, च and, तत्र among them, अन्ये others, जक्षाम we will eat, इति thus, च and, अपरे others, भुक्षिताभुक्षितैः by those who desired to eat and those who did not desire to eat, उक्तः having been spoken to, ततः then, तान् to them, आह said, भूतकृत् the creator of beings.
explanation: Among those beings, some said, "We will protect," while others said, "We will eat"; then, having heard these responses from the hungry and the non-hungry, the creator of beings spoke to them.

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः । जक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं यक्षा एव भवन्तु वः ।। 7.4.13 ।।
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca yairuktaṃ rākṣasāste bhavantu vaḥ | jakṣāma iti yairuktaṃ yakṣā eva bhavantu vaḥ || 7.4.13 ||
translation: रक्षाम we will protect, इति thus, च and, यैः by whom, उक्तम् was said, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, ते those, भवन्तु let them be, वः you. जक्षाम we will eat, इति thus, यैः by whom, उक्तम् was said, यक्षाः Yakshas, एव indeed, भवन्तु let them be, वः you.
explanation: To those who said, "We will protect," he declared, "You shall be Rakshasas," and to those who said, "We will eat," he declared, "You shall indeed be Yakshas."
