shloka_text: तत्र हेतिः प्रहेतिश्च भ्रातरौ राक्षसाधिपौ । मधुकैटभसङ्काशौ बभूवतुररिन्दमौ ।। 7.4.14 ।।
transliteration: tatra hetiḥ prahetiśca bhrātarau rākṣasādhipau | madhukaiṭabhasaṅkāśau babhūvaturarindamau || 7.4.14 ||
translation: तत्र there, हेतिः Heti, प्रहेतिः Praheti, च and, भ्रातरौ two brothers, राक्षसाधिपौ lords of Rākṣasas, मधुकैटभसङ्काशौ resembling Madhu and Kaiṭabha, बभूवतुः existed, अरिन्दमौ subduers of enemies.
explanation: There existed two demon lords, Heti and Praheti, who were brothers, vanquishers of foes, and resembled Madhu and Kaiṭabha.

shloka_text: प्रहेतिर्धार्मिकस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा । हेतिर्दारक्रियार्थे तु परं यत्नमथाकरोत् ।। 7.4.15 ।।
transliteration: prahetirdhārmikastatra tapovanagatastadā | hetirdārakriyārthe tu paraṃ yatnamathākarot || 7.4.15 ||
translation: प्रहेतिः Praheti, धार्मिकः righteous, तत्र there, तपोवनगतः gone to a hermitage, तदा then, हेतिः Heti, दारक्रियार्थे for the purpose of marriage, तु but, परम् great, यत्नम् effort, अथ then, अकरोत् made.
explanation: At that time, Praheti, being righteous, went to a hermitage, while Heti made a great effort to find a wife.

shloka_text: स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम भयावहाम् । उदावहदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव महामतिः ।। 7.4.16 ।।
transliteration: sa kālabhaginīṃ kanyāṃ bhayāṃ nāma bhayāvahām | udāvahadameyātmā svayameva mahāmatiḥ || 7.4.16 ||
translation: सः he, कालभगिनीम् sister of Kala, कन्याम् maiden, भयाम् Bhaya, नाम named, भयावहाम् terrifying, उदावहत married, अमेयात्मा of immeasurable spirit, स्वयम् himself, एव indeed, महामतिः great-minded.
explanation: That great-minded Heti, of immeasurable spirit, himself married a terrifying maiden named Bhaya, who was the sister of Kala (Death).

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः । पुत्रं पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केश इति श्रुतम् ।। 7.4.17 ।।
transliteration: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa hetī rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ | putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭho vidyutkeśa iti śrutam || 7.4.17 ||
translation: सः he, तस्याम् in her, जनयामास begot, हेती Heti, राक्षसपुङ्गवः foremost among Rākṣasas, पुत्रम् a son, पुत्रवताम् among those who have sons, श्रेष्ठः best, विद्युत्केशः Vidyutkeśa, इति thus, श्रुतम् known.
explanation: Heti, the foremost among Rākṣasas and best among those with sons, begot a son named Vidyutkeśa in her (Bhaya).

shloka_text: विद्युत्केशो हेतिपुत्रः स दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः । व्यवर्धत महातेजास्तोयमध्य इवाम्बुदः ।। 7.4.18 ।।
transliteration: vidyutkeśo hetiputraḥ sa dīptārkasamaprabhaḥ | vyavardhata mahātejāstoyamadhya ivāmbudaḥ || 7.4.18 ||
translation: विद्युत्केशः Vidyutkeśa, हेतिपुत्रः Heti's son, सः he, दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः having a brilliance equal to the blazing sun, व्यवर्धत grew, महातेजाः of great splendor, तोयमध्ये in the midst of water, इव like, अम्बुदः a cloud.
explanation: Vidyutkeśa, Heti's son, of great splendor and brilliance like the blazing sun, grew like a cloud in the midst of water.

shloka_text: स यदा यौवनं भद्रमनुप्राप्तो निशाचरः । ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता ।। 7.4.19 ।।
transliteration: sa yadā yauvanaṃ bhadramanuprāpto niśācaraḥ | tato dārakriyāṃ tasya kartuṃ vyavasitaḥ pitā || 7.4.19 ||
translation: सः he, यदा when, यौवनम् youth, भद्रम् auspicious, अनुप्राप्तः attained, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, ततः then, दारक्रियाम् marriage ceremony, तस्य his, कर्तुम् to perform, व्यवसितः resolved, पिता father.
explanation: When the night-wanderer (Vidhyutkesha) attained auspicious youth, his father then resolved to perform his marriage ceremony.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां सो ऽथ सन्ध्यातुल्यां प्रभावतः । वरयामास पुत्रार्थं हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः ।। 7.4.20 ।।
transliteration: sandhyāyāstanayāṃ so 'tha sandhyātulyāṃ prabhāvataḥ | varayāmāsa putrārthaṃ hetī rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ || 7.4.20 ||
translation: सन्ध्यायाः of Sandhya, तनयाम् daughter, सः he, अथ then, सन्ध्यातुल्याम् equal to Sandhya, प्रभावतः in splendor, वरयामास sought as a bride, पुत्रार्थम् for his son, हेती Heti, राक्षसपुङ्गवः the chief of Rakshasas.
explanation: Then Heti, the chief of Rakshasas, sought Sandhya's daughter, who was equal to Sandhya in splendor, as a bride for his son.

shloka_text: अवश्यमेव दातव्या परस्मै सेति सन्ध्यया । चिन्तयित्वा सुता दत्ता विद्युत्केशाय राघव ।। 7.4.21 ।।
transliteration: avaśyameva dātavyā parasmai seti sandhyayā | cintayitvā sutā dattā vidyutkeśāya rāghava || 7.4.21 ||
translation: अवश्यम् certainly, एव indeed, दातव्या to be given, परस्मै to another, सा she, इति thus, सन्ध्यया by Sandhya, चिन्तयित्वा having thought, सुता the daughter, दत्ता was given, विद्युत्केशाय to Vidhyutkesha, राघव O Rama.
explanation: O Rama, Sandhya, having thought that her daughter must certainly be given to another, thus gave her daughter to Vidhyutkesha.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां लब्ध्वा विद्युत्केशो निशाचरः । रमते स्म तया सार्धं पौलोम्या मघवानिव ।। 7.4.22 ।।
transliteration: sandhyāyāstanayāṃ labdhvā vidyutkeśo niśācaraḥ | ramate sma tayā sārdhaṃ paulomyā maghavāniva || 7.4.22 ||
translation: सन्ध्यायाः of Sandhya, तनयाम् daughter, लब्ध्वा having obtained, विद्युत्केशः Vidhyutkesha, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, रमते स्म enjoyed, तया with her, सार्धम् together, पौलोम्या with Paulomi, मघवानिव like Maghavan.
explanation: Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-wanderer Vidhyutkesha enjoyed with her, just as Maghavan (Indra) enjoys with Paulomi.

shloka_text: केनचित्त्वथ कालेन राम सालकटङ्कटा । विद्युत्केशाद्गर्भमाप घनराजिरिवार्णवात् ।। 7.4.23 ।।
transliteration: kenacittvatha kālena rāma sālakaṭaṅkaṭā | vidyutkeśādgarbhamāpa ghanarājirivārṇavāt || 7.4.23 ||
translation: केनचित् by some, तु indeed, अथ then, कालेन by time, राम O Rama, सालकटङ्कटा Salakatankata, विद्युत्केशात् from Vidhyutkesha, गर्भम् conception, आप obtained, घनराजिः a line of clouds, इव like, अर्णवात् from the ocean.
explanation: O Rama, after some time, Salakatankata conceived from Vidhyutkesha, just as a line of clouds obtains moisture from the ocean.

shloka_text: ततः सा राक्षसी गर्भं घनगर्भसमप्रभम् । प्रसूता मन्दरं गत्वा गङ्गा गर्भमिवाग्निजम् ।। 7.4.24 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā rākṣasī garbhaṃ ghanagarbhasamaprabham | prasūtā mandaraṃ gatvā gaṅgā garbhamivāgnijam || 7.4.24 ||
translation: ततः then, सा that, राक्षसी female demon, गर्भं offspring, घनगर्भसमप्रभम् having the luster like a thundercloud, प्रसूता gave birth, मन्दरं to Mandara mountain, गत्वा having gone, गङ्गा Ganga, गर्भमिव like an embryo, अग्निजम् born of fire.
explanation: Then, that female demon, having gone to the Mandara mountain, gave birth to an offspring shining like a thundercloud, just as Ganga gave birth to the fire-born embryo (Kartikeya).

shloka_text: समुत्सृज्य तु सा गर्भं विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी । रेमे तु सार्धं पतिना विस्मृत्य सुतमात्मजम् ।। 7.4.25 ।।
transliteration: samutsṛjya tu sā garbhaṃ vidyutkeśaratārthinī | reme tu sārdhaṃ patinā vismṛtya sutamātmajam || 7.4.25 ||
translation: समुत्सृज्य having abandoned, तु indeed, सा she, गर्भं the offspring, विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी desiring union with Vidyutkesha, रेमे enjoyed, तु indeed, सार्धं with, पतिना her husband, विस्मृत्य having forgotten, सुतम् the son, आत्मजम् her own.
explanation: Having abandoned her offspring, she, desiring union with Vidyutkesha, then enjoyed herself with her husband, completely forgetting her own son.

shloka_text: उत्सृष्टस्तु तदा गर्भो घनशब्दसमस्वनः । तयोत्सृष्टः स तु शिशुः शरदर्कसमद्युतिः । निधायास्ये स्वयं मुष्टिं रुरोद शनकैस्तदा ।। 7.4.26 ।।
transliteration: utsṛṣṭastu tadā garbho ghanaśabdasamasvanaḥ | tayotsṛṣṭaḥ sa tu śiśuḥ śaradarkasamadyutiḥ | nidhāyāsye svayaṃ muṣṭiṃ ruroda śanakaistadā || 7.4.26 ||
translation: उत्सृष्टस्तु but abandoned, तदा then, गर्भो the offspring, घनशब्दसमस्वनः having a sound like the roar of a cloud, तयोत्सृष्टः abandoned by her, स that, तु indeed, शिशुः child, शरदर्कसमद्युतिः having the luster like the autumn sun, निधायास्ये having placed in his mouth, स्वयं himself, मुष्टिं a fist, रुरोद cried, शनकैस्तदा slowly then.
explanation: The abandoned offspring, who had a roar like thunder and a luster like the autumn sun, then cried slowly, having placed his own fist in his mouth.

shloka_text: ततो वृषभमास्थाय पार्वत्या सहितः शिवः । वायुमार्गेण गच्छन्वै शुश्राव रुदितस्वनम् ।। 7.4.27 ।।
transliteration: tato vṛṣabhamāsthāya pārvatyā sahitaḥ śivaḥ | vāyumārgeṇa gacchanvai śuśrāva ruditasvanam || 7.4.27 ||
translation: ततो then, वृषभम् a bull, आस्थाय having mounted, पार्वत्या with Parvati, सहितः accompanied, शिवः Shiva, वायुमार्गेण through the sky-path, गच्छन्वै indeed going, शुश्राव heard, रुदितस्वनम् the sound of crying.
explanation: Then Shiva, accompanied by Parvati and mounted on a bull, was traveling through the sky and heard the sound of crying.

shloka_text: अपश्यदुमया सार्धं रुदन्तं राक्षसात्मजम् । कारुण्यभावात्पार्वत्या भवस्त्रिपुरसूदनः ।। 7.4.28 ।।
transliteration: apaśyadumayā sārdhaṃ rudantaṃ rākṣasātmajam | kāruṇyabhāvātpārvatyā bhavastripurasūdanaḥ || 7.4.28 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, उमया with Uma, सार्धं together, रुदन्तं crying, राक्षसात्मजम् the demon's son, कारुण्यभावात् due to the feeling of compassion, पार्वत्या of Parvati, भवः Shiva, त्रिपुरसूदनः the destroyer of Tripura.
explanation: Shiva, the destroyer of Tripura, then saw the demon's son crying, accompanied by Uma, moved by Parvati's feeling of compassion.

shloka_text: तं राक्षसात्मजं चक्रे मातुरेव वयःसमम् । अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवो ऽक्षरो ऽव्ययः ।। 7.4.29 ।।
transliteration: taṃ rākṣasātmajaṃ cakre mātureva vayaḥsamam | amaraṃ caiva taṃ kṛtvā mahādevo 'kṣaro 'vyayaḥ || 7.4.29 ||
translation: तं him, राक्षसात्मजं the son of the demon, चक्रे made, मातुरेव of his mother only, वयःसमम् equal in age, अमरं immortal, चैव and indeed, तं him, कृत्वा having made, महादेवो Lord Mahadeva, अक्षरो imperishable, अव्ययः immutable.
explanation: The imperishable and immutable Lord Mahadeva made that son of the demon, Sukesha, immortal and equal in age to his mother.

shloka_text: पुरमाकाशगं प्रादात्पार्वत्याः प्रियकाम्यया । उमयापि वरो दत्तो राक्षसानां नृपात्मज ।। 7.4.30 ।।
transliteration: puramākāśagaṃ prādātpārvatyāḥ priyakāmyayā | umayāpi varo datto rākṣasānāṃ nṛpātmaja || 7.4.30 ||
translation: पुरम् a city, आकाशगं moving in the sky, प्रादात् gave, पार्वत्याः of Parvati, प्रियकाम्यया with the desire to please, उमयापि by Uma also, वरो a boon, दत्तो given, राक्षसानां to the demons, नृपात्मज O son of the king.
explanation: To please Parvati, Shiva gave him a city that could move in the sky, and O son of the king, Uma also granted a boon to the demons.

shloka_text: सद्योपलब्धिर्गर्भस्य प्रसूतिः सद्य एव च । सद्य एव वयःप्राप्तिर्मातुरेव वयस्समम् ।। 7.4.31 ।।
transliteration: sadyopalabdhirgarbhasya prasūtiḥ sadya eva ca | sadya eva vayaḥprāptirmātureva vayassamam || 7.4.31 ||
translation: सद्योपलब्धिः immediate conception, गर्भस्य of the embryo, प्रसूतिः birth, सद्य immediately, एव indeed, च and, सद्य immediately, एव indeed, वयःप्राप्तिः attainment of age, मातुरेव of the mother only, वयस्समम् equal in age.
explanation: The boon granted by Uma was that conception would be immediate, birth would be immediate, and the child would immediately attain an age equal to that of its mother.

shloka_text: ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः । चचार सर्वत्र महान्महामतिः खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरन्दरो यथा ।। 7.4.32 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sukeśo varadānagarvitaḥ śriyaṃ prabhoḥ prāpya harasya pārśvataḥ | cacāra sarvatra mahānmahāmatiḥ khagaṃ puraṃ prāpya purandaro yathā || 7.4.32 ||
translation: ततः then, सुकेशो Sukesha, वरदानगर्वितः proud of the boon, श्रियं glory, प्रभोः of the lord, प्राप्य having obtained, हरस्य of Shiva, पार्श्वतः from the presence, चचार roamed, सर्वत्र everywhere, महान् great, महामतिः of great intellect, खगं moving in the sky, पुरं city, प्राप्य having obtained, पुरन्दरो Indra, यथा just as.
explanation: Then, Sukesha, proud of the boon and having obtained glory from the presence of Lord Shiva, roamed everywhere, great and of great intellect, just as Indra does after obtaining his celestial city. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः ।। 4 ।। Thus ends the fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम् । ग्रामणीर्नाम गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुसमप्रभः ।। 7.5.1 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaṃ dhārmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā varalabdhaṃ ca rākṣasam | grāmaṇīrnāma gandharvo viśvāvasusamaprabhaḥ || 7.5.1 ||
translation: सुकेशं Sukesha, धार्मिकं righteous, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वरलब्धं having obtained a boon, च and, राक्षसम् the demon, ग्रामणीर्नाम named Gramani, गन्धर्वो a Gandharva, विश्वावसुसमप्रभः having splendor like Vishvavasu.
explanation: Having seen Sukesha, the righteous demon who had obtained a boon, a Gandharva named Gramani, whose splendor was like that of Vishvavasu, (approached him).
comments: The Gandharva Gramani gives his daughter Devavati to Sukesha, who begets three mighty sons -- Malyavan, Sumali and Mali -- by severe penance they win from Brahma invincibility, long life and mutual devotion, and have Vishvakarma build them the city of Lanka on Trikuta -- wedding three Gandharva maidens they beget numerous rakshasa offspring, among them Kaikasi -- grown arrogant, the three brothers torment the gods, sages, nagas and yakshas.

shloka_text: तस्य देववती नाम द्वितीया श्रीरिवात्मजा । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता रूपयौवनशालिनी । तां सुकेशाय धर्मेण ददौ रक्षःश्रियं यथा ।। 7.5.2 ।।
transliteration: tasya devavatī nāma dvitīyā śrīrivātmajā | triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā rūpayauvanaśālinī | tāṃ sukeśāya dharmeṇa dadau rakṣaḥśriyaṃ yathā || 7.5.2 ||
translation: tasya his, devavatī Devavati, nāma named, dvitīyā second, śrīriva like Lakshmi, ātmajā daughter, triṣu in three, lokeṣu worlds, vikhyātā renowned, rūpayauvanaśālinī endowed with beauty and youth, tāṃ her, sukeśāya to Sukesha, dharmeṇa righteously, dadau gave, rakṣaḥśriyaṃ the prosperity of the Rakshasas, yathā just as.
explanation: He had a second daughter named Devavati, renowned in the three worlds for her beauty and youth, whom he righteously gave to Sukesha, just as one would bestow the prosperity of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम् । आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः ।। 7.5.3 ।।
transliteration: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ sā taṃ prāpya patiṃ priyam | āsīddevavatī tuṣṭā dhanaṃ prāpyeva nirdhanaḥ || 7.5.3 ||
translation: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ whose prosperity was made by boons, sā she, taṃ him, prāpya having obtained, patiṃ husband, priyam dear, āsīt became, devavatī Devavati, tuṣṭā pleased, dhanaṃ wealth, prāpya having obtained, iva as if, nirdhanaḥ a poor man.
explanation: Having obtained him, her dear husband whose prosperity was due to boons, Devavati became as pleased as a poor man who has acquired wealth.

shloka_text: स तया सह संयुक्तो रराज रजनीचरः । अञ्जनादभिनिष्क्रान्तः करेण्वेव महागजः ।। 7.5.4 ।।
transliteration: sa tayā saha saṃyukto rarāja rajanīcaraḥ | añjanādabhiniṣkrāntaḥ kareṇveva mahāgajaḥ || 7.5.4 ||
translation: sa he, tayā with her, saha together, saṃyuktaḥ united, rarāja shone, rajanīcaraḥ the night-wanderer, añjanāt from Anjana mountain, abhiniṣkrāntaḥ having emerged, kareṇvā with a female elephant, iva as if, mahāgajaḥ a great elephant.
explanation: United with her, that Rakshasa shone like a great elephant emerging from the Anjana mountain with a female elephant.

shloka_text: देववत्यां सुकेशस्तु जनयामास राघव ।। 7.5.5 ।।
transliteration: devavatyāṃ sukeśastu janayāmāsa rāghava || 7.5.5 ||
translation: devavatyāṃ in Devavati, sukeśaḥ Sukesha, tu indeed, janayāmāsa begot, rāghava O Raghava.
explanation: Indeed, Sukesha begot children in Devavati, O Raghava.

shloka_text: त्रीन् पुत्रान् जनयामास त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहान् । माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम् । त्रींस्त्रिनेत्रसमान्पुत्रान्राक्षसान्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.5.6 ।।
transliteration: trīn putrān janayāmāsa tretāgnisamavigrahān | mālyavantaṃ sumāliṃ ca māliṃ ca balināṃ varam | trīṃstrinetrasamānputrānrākṣasānrākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.5.6 ||
translation: trīn three, putrān sons, janayāmāsa begot, tretāgnisamavigrahān whose bodies were like the three sacred fires, mālyavantaṃ Malyavan, sumāliṃ Sumali, ca and, māliṃ Mali, ca and, balināṃ among the strong, varam the best, trīn three, trinetrasamān equal to the three-eyed one (Shiva), putrān sons, rākṣasān Rakshasas, rākṣasādhipaḥ the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: The lord of Rakshasas begot three sons, Malyavan, Sumali, and Mali (the best among the strong), who were Rakshasas with bodies like the three sacred fires and equal to Shiva.

shloka_text: त्रयो लोका इवाव्यग्राः स्थितास्त्रय इवाग्नयः । त्रयो मन्त्रा इवात्युग्रास्त्रयो घोरा इवामयाः ।। 7.5.7 ।।
transliteration: trayo lokā ivāvyagrāḥ sthitāstraya ivāgnayaḥ | trayo mantrā ivātyugrāstrayo ghorā ivāmayāḥ || 7.5.7 ||
translation: त्रयः three, लोकाः worlds, इव like, अव्यग्राः undisturbed, स्थिताः stood, त्रयः three, इव like, अग्नयः fires, त्रयः three, मन्त्राः incantations, इव like, अत्युग्राः extremely fierce, त्रयः three, घोराः dreadful, इव like, आमयाः diseases
explanation: They remained like the three undisturbed worlds, like the three sacred fires, like three extremely fierce incantations, and like three dreadful diseases.

shloka_text: त्रयः सुकेशस्य सुतास्त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः । विवृद्धिमगमंस्तत्र व्याधयोपेक्षिता इव ।। 7.5.8 ।।
transliteration: trayaḥ sukeśasya sutāstretāgnisamatejasaḥ | vivṛddhimagamaṃstatra vyādhayopekṣitā iva || 7.5.8 ||
translation: त्रयः three, सुकेशस्य of Sukesha, सुताः sons, त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः having splendor equal to the three sacred fires, विवृद्धिम् growth, अगमन् attained, तत्र there, व्याधयः diseases, उपेक्षिताः neglected, इव like
explanation: The three sons of Sukesha, possessing a brilliance akin to the three sacred fires, grew there like neglected diseases.

shloka_text: वरप्राप्तिं पितुस्ते तु ज्ञात्वेश्वरतपोबलात् । तपस्तप्तुं गता मेरुं भ्रातरः कृतनिश्चयाः ।। 7.5.9 ।।
transliteration: varaprāptiṃ pituste tu jñātveśvaratapobalāt | tapastaptuṃ gatā meruṃ bhrātaraḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ || 7.5.9 ||
translation: वरप्राप्तिम् the obtaining of a boon, पितुः of their father, ते they, तु indeed, ज्ञात्वा having known, ईश्वरतपोबलात् from the power of Shiva's penance, तपः penance, तप्तुम् to perform, गताः went, मेरुम् to Mount Meru, भ्रातरः brothers, कृतनिश्चयाः having made a firm resolve
explanation: Having learned of their father's boon obtained through the power of Shiva's penance, the brothers, having made a firm resolve, went to Mount Meru to perform penance.

shloka_text: प्रगृह्य नियमान्घोरान्राक्षसा नृपसत्तम । विचेरुस्ते तपो घोरं सर्वभूतभयावहम् ।। 7.5.10 ।।
transliteration: pragṛhya niyamānghorānrākṣasā nṛpasattama | viceruste tapo ghoraṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham || 7.5.10 ||
translation: प्रगृह्य having undertaken, नियमान् vows, घोरान् terrible, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, नृपसत्तम O best of kings, विचेरुः they performed, ते they, तपः penance, घोरम् terrible, सर्वभूतभयावहम् causing fear to all beings
explanation: O best of kings, those Rakshasas undertook severe vows and performed terrible penance that instilled fear in all beings.

shloka_text: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैस्तपोभिरतिदुष्करैः । सन्तापयन्तस्त्रील्लोँकान्सदेवासुरमानुषान् ।। 7.5.11 ।।
transliteration: satyārjavaśamopetaistapobhiratiduṣkaraiḥ | santāpayantastrīlloँkānsadevāsuramānuṣān || 7.5.11 ||
translation: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैः endowed with truth, straightforwardness, and self-control, तपोभिः by penances, अतिदुष्करैः extremely difficult to perform, सन्तापयन्तः causing distress, त्रीन् three, लोकान् worlds, सदेवासुरमानुषान् along with gods, asuras, and humans
explanation: Through their extremely difficult penances, which were endowed with truth, straightforwardness, and self-control, they tormented the three worlds, including gods, asuras, and humans.

shloka_text: ततो विभुश्चतुर्वक्त्रो विमानवरमास्थितः । सुकेशपुत्रानामन्त्र्य वरदो ऽस्मीत्यभाषत ।। 7.5.12 ।।
transliteration: tato vibhuścaturvaktro vimānavaramāsthitaḥ | sukeśaputrānāmantrya varado 'smītyabhāṣata || 7.5.12 ||
translation: ततः then, विभुः the powerful one (Brahma), चतुर्वक्त्रः four-faced, विमानवरम् the excellent aerial chariot, आस्थितः having ascended, सुकेशपुत्रान् the sons of Sukesha, आमन्त्र्य having addressed, वरदः a bestower of boons, अस्मि I am, इति thus, अभाषत spoke.
explanation: Then, the powerful, four-faced Brahma, seated on his excellent aerial chariot, addressed the sons of Sukesha, declaring, "I am here to grant boons."

shloka_text: ब्रह्माणं वरदं ज्ञात्वा सेन्द्रैर्देवगणैर्वृतम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव द्रुमाः ।। 7.5.13 ।।
transliteration: brahmāṇaṃ varadaṃ jñātvā sendrairdevagaṇairvṛtam | ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve vepamānā iva drumāḥ || 7.5.13 ||
translation: ब्रह्माणम् Brahma, वरदम् the bestower of boons, ज्ञात्वा having known, सेन्द्रैः with Indra, देवगणैः by hosts of gods, वृतम् surrounded, ऊचुः they spoke, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, सर्वे all, वेपमानाः trembling, इव like, द्रुमाः trees.
explanation: Realizing that Brahma, the bestower of boons, was present, surrounded by Indra and hosts of gods, all of them spoke with folded hands, trembling like trees.

shloka_text: तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम् । अजेयाः शत्रुहन्तारस्तथैव चिरजीविनः ।। 7.5.14 ।।
transliteration: tapasārādhito deva yadi no diśase varam | ajeyāḥ śatruhantārastathaiva cirajīvinaḥ || 7.5.14 ||
translation: तपसा by penance, आराधितः worshipped, देव O Lord, यदि if, नः to us, दिशसे you grant, वरम् a boon, अजेयाः unconquerable, शत्रुहन्तारः destroyers of enemies, तथैव and also, चिरजीविनः long-lived.
explanation: They requested, "O Lord, if you, who have been propitiated by our penance, grant us a boon, let us be unconquerable, destroyers of enemies, and also long-lived."

shloka_text: प्रभविष्ण्वो भवामेति परस्परमनुव्रताः ।। 7.5.15 ।।
transliteration: prabhaviṣṇvo bhavāmeti parasparamanuvratāḥ || 7.5.15 ||
translation: प्रभविष्ण्वः powerful, भवाम let us be, इति thus, परस्परम् mutually, अनुव्रताः devoted.
explanation: They further requested, "And let us be mighty, always devoted to each other."

shloka_text: एवं भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा सुकेशतनयान्विभुः । स ययौ ब्रह्मलोकाय ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणवत्सलः ।। 7.5.16 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā sukeśatanayānvibhuḥ | sa yayau brahmalokāya brahmā brāhmaṇavatsalaḥ || 7.5.16 ||
translation: एवम् thus, भविष्यति it shall be, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, सुकेशतनयान् to the sons of Sukesha, विभुः the powerful one (Brahma), सः he, ययौ went, ब्रह्मलोकाय to the world of Brahma, ब्रह्मा Brahma, ब्राह्मणवत्सलः affectionate to Brahmins.
explanation: Having told the sons of Sukesha, "So it shall be," the powerful Brahma, who is affectionate to Brahmins, then returned to his own world.

shloka_text: वरं लब्ध्वा तु ते सर्वे राम रात्रिञ्चरास्तदा । सुरासुरान्प्रबाधन्ते वरदानसुनिर्भयाः ।। 7.5.17 ।।
transliteration: varaṃ labdhvā tu te sarve rāma rātriñcarāstadā | surāsurānprabādhante varadānasunirbhayāḥ || 7.5.17 ||
translation: वरं boon, लब्ध्वा having obtained, तु indeed, ते those, सर्वे all, राम O Rama, रात्रिञ्चराः night-wanderers, तदा then, सुरासुरान् gods and asuras, प्रबाधन्ते they harass, वरदानसुनिर्भयाः very fearless because of the boon.
explanation: O Rama, having obtained the boon, all those night-wanderers then became very fearless due to the boon and began to harass both gods and asuras.

shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमानास्त्रिदशाः सर्षिसङ्घाः सचारणाः । त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति निरयस्था यथा नराः ।। 7.5.18 ।।
transliteration: tairvadhyamānāstridaśāḥ sarṣisaṅghāḥ sacāraṇāḥ | trātāraṃ nādhigacchanti nirayasthā yathā narāḥ || 7.5.18 ||
translation: तैः by them, वध्यमानाः being tormented, त्रिदशाः the gods, सर्षिसङ्घाः along with groups of sages, सचारणाः along with Charanas, त्रातारं a protector, न not, अधिगच्छन्ति they find, निरयस्थाः those in hell, यथा just as, नराः people.
explanation: Being tormented by them, the gods, along with groups of sages and Charanas, could not find a protector, just like people suffering in hell.

shloka_text: अथ ते विश्वकर्माणं शिल्पिनां वरमव्ययम् । ऊचुः समेत्य संहृष्टा राक्षसा रघुसत्तम ।। 7.5.19 ।।
transliteration: atha te viśvakarmāṇaṃ śilpināṃ varamavyayam | ūcuḥ sametya saṃhṛṣṭā rākṣasā raghusattama || 7.5.19 ||
translation: अथ then, ते those, विश्वकर्माणं to Vishwakarma, शिल्पिनां of artisans, वरं the best, अव्ययम् imperishable, ऊचुः they said, समेत्य having met, संहृष्टाः delighted, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, रघुसत्तम O best of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: O best of Raghu's lineage, then those delighted Rakshasas, having met Vishwakarma, the best and imperishable among artisans, spoke to him.

shloka_text: ओजस्तेजोबलवतां महतामात्मतेजसा । गृहकर्ता भवानेव देवानां हृदयेप्सितम् ।। 7.5.20 ।।
transliteration: ojastejobalavatāṃ mahatāmātmatejasā | gṛhakartā bhavāneva devānāṃ hṛdayepsitam || 7.5.20 ||
translation: ओजः vigor, तेजः splendor, बलवतां of the powerful, महतां of the great, आत्मतेजसा by your own splendor, गृहकर्ता the house-builder, भवान् you, एव alone, देवानां of the gods, हृदयेप्सितम् desired by the heart.
explanation: You alone, by your own splendor, are the cherished house-builder for the great, vigorous, splendid, and powerful gods.

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि तावत्त्वं गृहं कुरु महामते । हिमवन्तमपाश्रित्य मेरुमन्दरमेव वा । महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं गृहं नः क्रियतां महत् ।। 7.5.21 ।।
transliteration: asmākamapi tāvattvaṃ gṛhaṃ kuru mahāmate | himavantamapāśritya merumandarameva vā | maheśvaragṛhaprakhyaṃ gṛhaṃ naḥ kriyatāṃ mahat || 7.5.21 ||
translation: अस्माकम् for us, अपि also, तावत् therefore, त्वं you, गृहं a house, कुरु make, महामते O great-minded one, हिमवन्तम् the Himalayas, अपाश्रित्य having resorted to, मेरुमन्दरम् Meru or Mandara, एव indeed, वा or, महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं resembling the dwelling of Maheswara, गृहं a house, नः for us, क्रियतां let it be made, महत् great.
explanation: O great-minded one, therefore, please build a grand dwelling for us also, resembling the abode of Maheswara, either by resorting to the Himalayas or Mount Meru or Mandara.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मा ततस्तेषां राक्षसानां महाभुजः । निवासं कथयामास शक्रस्येवामरावतीम् ।। 7.5.22 ।।
transliteration: viśvakarmā tatasteṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahābhujaḥ | nivāsaṃ kathayāmāsa śakrasyevāmarāvatīm || 7.5.22 ||
translation: विश्वकर्मा Vishwakarma, ततः then, तेषां to them, राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas, महाभुजः the mighty-armed, निवासं dwelling place, कथयामास described, शक्रस्य of Indra, इव like, अमरावतीम् Amaravati.
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Vishwakarma described to those Rakshasas a dwelling place, which was like Amaravati, the city of Indra.

shloka_text: दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः । सुवेल इति चाप्यन्यो द्वितीयस्तत्र सत्तमाः ।। 7.5.23 ।।
transliteration: dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre trikūṭo nāma parvataḥ | suvela iti cāpyanyo dvitīyastatra sattamāḥ || 7.5.23 ||
translation: दक्षिणस्य of the southern, उदधेः ocean, तीरे on the shore, त्रिकूटो Trikuta, नाम named, पर्वतः mountain, सुवेल Suvela, इति thus, च and, अपि also, अन्यः another, द्वितीयः second, तत्र there, सत्तमाः O best ones.
explanation: O best ones, on the shore of the southern ocean, there is a mountain named Trikuta, and another, a second one, named Suvela.

shloka_text: शिखरे तस्य शैलस्य मध्यमे ऽम्बुदसन्निभे । शकुनैरपि दुष्प्रापे टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि ।। 7.5.24 ।।
transliteration: śikhare tasya śailasya madhyame 'mbudasannibhe | śakunairapi duṣprāpe ṭaṅkacchinnacaturdiśi || 7.5.24 ||
translation: शिखरे on the peak, तस्य of that, शैलस्य mountain, मध्यमे middle, अम्बुदसन्निभे cloud-like, शकुनैः by birds, अपि even, दुष्प्रापे difficult to reach, टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि carved on all four sides with a chisel.
explanation: On the middle peak of that mountain, which resembles a cloud, is difficult for even birds to reach, and is carved on all four sides as if by a chisel.

shloka_text: त्रिंशद्योजनक्स्तीर्णा शतयोजनमायता । स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता हेमतोरणसंवृता ।। 7.5.25 ।।
transliteration: triṃśadyojanakstīrṇā śatayojanamāyatā | svarṇaprākārasaṃvītā hematoraṇasaṃvṛtā || 7.5.25 ||
translation: त्रिंशत् thirty, योजनक्स् yojanas, तीर्णा wide, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयता long, स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता surrounded by golden walls, हेमतोरणसंवृता adorned with golden archways.
explanation: This place is thirty yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, surrounded by golden walls and adorned with golden archways.

shloka_text: मया लङ्केति नगरी शक्राज्ञप्तेन निर्मिता । तस्यां वसत दुर्धर्षा यूयं राक्षसपुङ्गवाः ।। 7.5.26 ।।
transliteration: mayā laṅketi nagarī śakrājñaptena nirmitā | tasyāṃ vasata durdharṣā yūyaṃ rākṣasapuṅgavāḥ || 7.5.26 ||
translation: मया by me, लङ्का Lanka, इति thus, नगरी city, शक्राज्ञप्तेन by Indra's command, निर्मिता built, तस्यां in that, वसत dwell, दुर्धर्षाः O invincible ones, यूयं you, राक्षसपुङ्गवाः O foremost Rakshasas.
explanation: This city, named Lanka, was built by me at Indra's command; O invincible and foremost Rakshasas, you should dwell there.

shloka_text: अमरावतीं समासाद्य सेन्द्रा इव दिवौकसः । लङ्कादुर्गं समासाद्य राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृताः ।। 7.5.27 ।।
transliteration: amarāvatīṃ samāsādya sendrā iva divaukasaḥ | laṅkādurgaṃ samāsādya rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtāḥ || 7.5.27 ||
translation: अमरावतीं Amaravati, समासाद्य having reached, सेन्द्राः with Indra, इव like, दिवौकसः gods, लङ्कादुर्गं the fortress of Lanka, समासाद्य having reached, राक्षसैः by Rakshasas, बहुभिः many, वृताः surrounded.
explanation: Having reached the fortress of Lanka, you will be surrounded by many Rakshasas, just as the gods, led by Indra, dwell in Amaravati.

shloka_text: भविष्यथ दुराधर्षाः शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनाः ।। 7.5.28 ।।
transliteration: bhaviṣyatha durādharṣāḥ śatrūṇāṃ śatrusūdanāḥ || 7.5.28 ||
translation: भविष्यथ you will become, दुराधर्षाः invincible, शत्रूणां of enemies, शत्रुसूदनाः destroyers of enemies.
explanation: You will become invincible and destroyers of your enemies.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मवचः श्रुत्वा ततस्ते राक्षसोत्तमाः । सहस्रानुचरा भूत्वा गत्वा तामवसन्पुरीम् ।। 7.5.29 ।।
transliteration: viśvakarmavacaḥ śrutvā tataste rākṣasottamāḥ | sahasrānucarā bhūtvā gatvā tāmavasanpurīm || 7.5.29 ||
translation: विश्वकर्मवचः the words of Vishwakarma, श्रुत्वा having heard, ततः then, ते those, राक्षसोत्तमाः best of Rakshasas, सहस्रानुचराः with thousands of followers, भूत्वा having become, गत्वा having gone, ताम् that, अवसन् dwelt, पुरीम् city.
explanation: Having heard the words of Vishwakarma, those foremost Rakshasas then went to that city with thousands of followers and dwelt there.

shloka_text: दृढप्राकारपरिखां हैमैर्गृहशतैर्वृताम् । लङ्कामवाप्य ते हृष्टा न्यवसन्रजनीचराः ।। 7.5.30 ।।
transliteration: dṛḍhaprākāraparikhāṃ haimairgṛhaśatairvṛtām | laṅkāmavāpya te hṛṣṭā nyavasanrajanīcarāḥ || 7.5.30 ||
translation: दृढप्राकारपरिखां with strong walls and moats, हैमैः golden, गृहशतैः by hundreds of houses, वृताम् surrounded, लङ्कां Lanka, अवाप्य having obtained, ते those, हृष्टाः delighted, न्यवसन् dwelt, रजनीचराः night-wanderers (Rakshasas).
explanation: Having obtained Lanka, which was surrounded by strong walls and moats and hundreds of golden houses, those delighted night-wanderers (Rakshasas) took up residence there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथाकामं च राघव । नर्मदा नाम गन्धर्वी बभूव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.5.31 ।।
transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu yathākāmaṃ ca rāghava | narmadā nāma gandharvī babhūva raghunandana || 7.5.31 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, एव indeed, काले time, तु and, यथाकामं as desired, च and, राघव O Raghava, नर्मदा Narmada, नाम named, गन्धर्वी a Gandharva woman, बभूव was born, रघुनन्दन O delight of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: O Raghava, O delight of Raghu's lineage, at this very time, a Gandharva woman named Narmada was born as desired.

shloka_text: तस्याः कान्यात्रयं ह्यासीत् धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति । ज्येष्ठक्रमेण सा तेषां राक्षसानामराक्षसी ।। 7.5.32 ।।
transliteration: tasyāḥ kānyātrayaṃ hyāsīt dhīśrīkirtisamadyuti | jyeṣṭhakrameṇa sā teṣāṃ rākṣasānāmarākṣasī || 7.5.32 ||
translation: तस्याः her, कान्यात्रयम् three daughters, हि indeed, आसीत् were, धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति having splendor equal to intellect, prosperity, and fame, ज्येष्ठक्रमेण in order of seniority, सा she, तेषाम् of them, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, अराक्षसी not a Rākṣasī.
explanation: She, who was not a Rākṣasī, indeed had three daughters whose splendor was equal to intellect, prosperity, and fame, and these daughters were for those Rākṣasas in order of their seniority.

shloka_text: कन्यास्ताः प्रददौ हृष्टा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः । त्रयाणां राक्षसेन्द्राणां तिस्रो गन्धर्वकन्यकाः ।। 7.5.33 ।।
transliteration: kanyāstāḥ pradadau hṛṣṭā pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ | trayāṇāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ tisro gandharvakanyakāḥ || 7.5.33 ||
translation: कन्याः daughters, ताः those, प्रददौ gave, हृष्टा delighted, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः having faces like the full moon, त्रयाणाम् to the three, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् chiefs of Rākṣasas, तिस्रः three, गन्धर्वकन्यकाः Gandharva maidens.
explanation: Delighted, she gave those three Gandharva maidens, whose faces resembled the full moon, to the three chiefs of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: दत्ता मात्रा महाभागा नक्षत्रे भगदैवते । कुतदारास्तु ते राम सुकेशतनयास्तदा ।। 7.5.34 ।।
transliteration: dattā mātrā mahābhāgā nakṣatre bhagadaivate | kutadārāstu te rāma sukeśatanayāstadā || 7.5.34 ||
translation: दत्ता given, मात्रा by the mother, महाभागा O greatly fortunate one, नक्षत्रे in the constellation, भगदैवते presided over by Bhaga, कुतदाराः having taken wives, तु indeed, ते those, राम O Rama, सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, तदा then.
explanation: O greatly fortunate Rama, those sons of Sukesha then indeed took wives, given by their mother in the constellation presided over by Bhaga.

shloka_text: चिक्रीडुः सह भार्याभिरप्सरोभिरिवामराः । ततो माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.35 ।।
transliteration: cikrīḍuḥ saha bhāryābhirapsarobhirivāmarāḥ | tato mālyavato bhāryā sundarī nāma sundarī || 7.5.35 ||
translation: चिक्रीडुः they sported, सह with, भार्याभिः their wives, अप्सरोभिः with Apsaras, इव like, अमराः gods, ततः then, माल्यवतः of Malyavan, भार्या wife, सुन्दरी Sundari, नाम named, सुन्दरी beautiful.
explanation: They sported with their wives like gods with Apsaras; then, Malyavan's wife, named Sundari, who was beautiful...

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत् । वज्रमुष्टिर्विरूपाक्षोदुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः ।। 7.5.36 ।।
transliteration: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa yadapatyaṃ nibodha tat | vajramuṣṭirvirūpākṣodurmukhaścaiva rākṣasaḥ || 7.5.36 ||
translation: सः he, तस्याम् in her, जनयामास begot, यत् what, अपत्यम् offspring, निबोध know, तत् that, वज्रमुष्टिः Vajramushti, विरूपाक्षः Virupaksha, दुर्मुखः Durmukha, च and, एव indeed, राक्षसः Rākṣasa.
explanation: He begot in her the following offspring: Vajramushti, Virupaksha, and Durmukha, who were Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च मत्तोन्मत्तौ तथैव च । अनला चाभवत्कन्या सुन्दर्यां राम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.37 ।।
transliteration: suptaghno yajñakopaśca mattonmattau tathaiva ca | analā cābhavatkanyā sundaryāṃ rāma sundarī || 7.5.37 ||
translation: सुप्तघ्नो Suptaghna, यज्ञकोपश्च and Yajñakopa, मत्तोन्मत्तौ Matta and Unmatta, तथैव ca and similarly, अनला Anala, च and, अभवत् was born, कन्या a daughter, सुन्दर्यां from Sundari, राम O Rama, सुन्दरी a beautiful one
explanation: O Rama, from Sundari were born sons named Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, Matta, and Unmatta, and also a beautiful daughter named Anala.

shloka_text: सुमालिनो ऽपि भार्यासीत्पूर्णचद्रनिभानना । नाम्ना केतुमती राम प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयसी ।। 7.5.38 ।।
transliteration: sumālino 'pi bhāryāsītpūrṇacadranibhānanā | nāmnā ketumatī rāma prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī || 7.5.38 ||
translation: सुमालिनो of Sumali, अपि also, भार्या a wife, आसीत् was, पूर्णचद्रनिभानना with a face like the full moon, नाम्ना by name, केतुमती Ketumati, राम O Rama, प्राणेभ्यो than life, अपि even, गरीयसी dearer
explanation: O Rama, Sumali also had a wife named Ketumati, whose face was like the full moon and who was dearer to him than his own life.

shloka_text: सुमाली जनयामास यदपत्यं निशाचरः । केतुमत्यां महाराज तन्निबोधानुपूर्वशः ।। 7.5.39 ।।
transliteration: sumālī janayāmāsa yadapatyaṃ niśācaraḥ | ketumatyāṃ mahārāja tannibodhānupūrvaśaḥ || 7.5.39 ||
translation: सुमाली Sumali, जनयामास begot, यदपत्यं what offspring, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, केतुमत्यां in Ketumati, महाराज O great king, तत् that, निबोध know, अनुपूर्वशः in due order
explanation: O great king, now learn in due order about the offspring that the demon Sumali begot through Ketumati.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तो ऽकम्पनश्चैव विकटः कालकार्मुखः । धूम्राक्षश्चैव दण्डश्च सुपार्श्वश्च महाबलः ।। 7.5.40 ।।
transliteration: prahasto 'kampanaścaiva vikaṭaḥ kālakārmukhaḥ | dhūmrākṣaścaiva daṇḍaśca supārśvaśca mahābalaḥ || 7.5.40 ||
translation: प्रहस्तो Prahasta, अकम्पनश्चैव and Akampana, विकटः Vikata, कालकार्मुखः Kalakarmukha, धूम्राक्षश्चैव and Dhūmrākṣa, दण्डश्च and Danda, सुपार्श्वश्च and Suparshva, महाबलः the mighty
explanation: These sons were Prahasta, Akampana, Vikata, Kalakarmukha, Dhūmrākṣa, Danda, and the mighty Suparshva.

shloka_text: संह्रादिः प्रघसश्चैव भासकर्णश्च राक्षसः । राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिता ।। कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
transliteration: saṃhrādiḥ praghasaścaiva bhāsakarṇaśca rākṣasaḥ | rākā puṣpotkaṭā caiva kaikasī ca śucismitā || kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ || 7.5.41 ||
translation: संह्रादिः Samhradi, प्रघसश्चैव and Praghasa, भासकर्णश्च and Bhasakarna, राक्षसः the demon, राका Raka, पुष्पोत्कटा Pushpotkata, चैव and, कैकसी Kaikasi, च and, शुचिस्मिता with a pure smile, कुम्भीनसी Kumbhinasi, च and, इत्येते these, सुमालेः of Sumali, प्रसवाः offspring, स्मृताः are known
explanation: The demon's other offspring were Samhradi, Praghasa, Bhasakarna, Raka, Pushpotkata, Kaikasi of the pure smile, and Kumbhinasi, all known as Sumali's progeny.

shloka_text: कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
transliteration: kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ || 7.5.41 ||
translation: कुम्भीनसी Kumbhinasi, च and, इत्येते these, सुमालेः of Sumali, प्रसवाः offspring, स्मृताः are known।
explanation: Kumbhinasi and others are known as the offspring of Sumali.

shloka_text: मालेस्तु वसुधा नाम गन्धर्वी रूपशालिनी । भार्यासीत्पद्मपत्राक्षी स्वक्षी यक्षीवरोपमा ।। 7.5.42 ।।
transliteration: mālestu vasudhā nāma gandharvī rūpaśālinī | bhāryāsītpadmapatrākṣī svakṣī yakṣīvaropamā || 7.5.42 ||
translation: मालेः Of Mali, तु indeed, वसुधा Vasudha, नाम named, गन्धर्वी a Gandharva woman, रूपशालिनी beautiful, भार्या wife, आसीत् was, पद्मपत्राक्षी lotus-leaf-eyed, स्वक्षी beautiful-eyed, यक्षीवरोपमा resembling the best of Yakshinis।
explanation: Mali's wife was a beautiful Gandharva woman named Vasudha, who had eyes like lotus petals and was as splendid as a chief Yakshini.

shloka_text: सुमालेरनुजस्तस्यां जनयामास यत् प्रभो । अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तु मया त्वं शृणु राघव ।। 7.5.43 ।।
transliteration: sumāleranujastasyāṃ janayāmāsa yat prabho | apatyaṃ kathyamānaṃ tu mayā tvaṃ śṛṇu rāghava || 7.5.43 ||
translation: सुमालेः Of Sumali, अनुजः the younger brother, तस्यां in her, जनयामास begot, यत् what, प्रभो O Lord, अपत्यं offspring, कथ्यमानं being told, तु indeed, मया by me, त्वं you, शृणु listen, राघव O Raghava।
explanation: O Lord Raghava, listen to the offspring that Sumali's younger brother begot in her, which I am now relating to you.

shloka_text: अनिलश्चानलश्चैव हरः सम्पातिरेव च । एते विभीषणामात्या मालेयास्तु निशाचरः ।। 7.5.44 ।।
transliteration: anilaścānalaścaiva haraḥ sampātireva ca | ete vibhīṣaṇāmātyā māleyāstu niśācaraḥ || 7.5.44 ||
translation: अनिलः Anila, च and, अनलः Anala, च and, एव indeed, हरः Hara, सम्पातिः Sampati, एव indeed, च and, एते these, विभीषणामात्याः ministers of Vibhishana, मालेयाः sons of Mali, तु indeed, निशाचरः night-wanderers।
explanation: Anila, Anala, Hara, and Sampati are these sons of Mali, who were night-wanderers and later became ministers of Vibhishana.

shloka_text: ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुङ्गवास्त्रयो निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृताः । सुरान्सहेन्द्रानृषिनागयक्षान्बबाधिरे तान्बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः ।। 7.5.45 ।।
transliteration: tatastu te rākṣasapuṅgavāstrayo niśācaraiḥ putraśataiśca saṃvṛtāḥ | surānsahendrānṛṣināgayakṣānbabādhire tānbahuvīryadarpitāḥ || 7.5.45 ||
translation: ततः Then, तु indeed, ते those, राक्षसपुङ्गवाः chief Rakshasas, त्रयः three, निशाचरैः by night-wanderers, पुत्रशतैः by hundreds of sons, च and, संवृताः surrounded, सुरान् the gods, सहेन्द्रान् along with Indra, ऋषिनागयक्षान् the Rishis, Nagas, and Yakshas, बबाधिरे tormented, तान् them, बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः arrogant with great power।
explanation: Then, those three chief Rakshasas, surrounded by hundreds of their Rakshasa sons, became arrogant with their immense power and tormented the gods along with Indra, as well as the Rishis, Nagas, and Yakshas.

shloka_text: जगद्भ्रमन्तो ऽनिलवद्दुरासदा रणेषु मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः । वरप्रदानादतिगर्विता भृशं क्रतुक्रियाणां प्रशमङ्कराः सदा ।। 7.5.46 ।।
transliteration: jagadbhramanto 'nilavaddurāsadā raṇeṣu mṛtyupratimānatejasaḥ | varapradānādatigarvitā bhṛśaṃ kratukriyāṇāṃ praśamaṅkarāḥ sadā || 7.5.46 ||
translation: जगत् world, भ्रमन्तः wandering, अनिलवत् like wind, दुरासदा difficult to approach, रणेषु in battles, मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः having valor equal to death, वरप्रदानात् due to the boon, अतिगर्विताः extremely proud, भृशम् exceedingly, क्रतुक्रियाणाम् of sacrificial rites, प्रशमङ्कराः destroyers, सदा always.
explanation: These beings wander the world like the wind, are difficult to approach, possess valor equal to death in battles, are exceedingly proud due to the boon they received, and always destroy sacrificial rites. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः ।। 5 ।। Thus ends the fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमाना देवाश्च ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः । भयार्ताः शरणं जग्मुर्देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ।। 7.6.1 ।।
transliteration: tairvadhyamānā devāśca ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ | bhayārtāḥ śaraṇaṃ jagmurdevadevaṃ maheśvaram || 7.6.1 ||
translation: तैः by them, वध्यमानाः being tormented, देवाः च gods and, ऋषयः च sages and, तपोधनाः whose wealth is penance, भयार्ताः distressed by fear, शरणम् refuge, जग्मुः went, देवदेवम् to the god of gods, महेश्वरम् to Maheśvara.
explanation: Tormented by them, the gods and the sages whose wealth was penance, distressed by fear, went to Maheśvara, the god of gods, for refuge.
comments: The afflicted gods take refuge with Shiva, who, sparing Sukesha's sons himself, directs them to Vishnu, who promises the rakshasas' destruction -- learning of this, the brothers deliberate, and Sumali and Mali, trusting their boons, resolve to attack the gods -- ignoring dire omens the rakshasa host marches on the world of the gods -- Narayana arms himself, mounts Garuda, and the battle opens as the rakshasas assail him.

shloka_text: जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारमजमव्यक्तरूपिणम् । आधारं सर्वलोकानामाराध्यं परमं गुरुम् ।। 7.6.2 ।।
transliteration: jagatsṛṣṭyantakartāramajamavyaktarūpiṇam | ādhāraṃ sarvalokānāmārādhyaṃ paramaṃ gurum || 7.6.2 ||
translation: जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारम् the creator and destroyer of the world, अजम् unborn, अव्यक्तरूपिणम् having an unmanifest form, आधारम् the support, सर्वलोकानाम् of all worlds, आराध्यम् adorable, परमम् supreme, गुरुम् teacher.
explanation: They went to him who is the creator and destroyer of the world, unborn, of unmanifest form, the support of all worlds, adorable, and the supreme teacher.

shloka_text: ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारिं त्रिलोचनम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा भयगद्गदभाषिणः ।। 7.6.3 ।।
transliteration: te sametya tu kāmāriṃ tripurāriṃ trilocanam | ūcuḥ prāñjalayo devā bhayagadgadabhāṣiṇaḥ || 7.6.3 ||
translation: ते they, समेत्य having approached, तु indeed, कामारिम् the enemy of Kama, त्रिपुरारिम् the enemy of Tripura, त्रिलोचनम् the three-eyed one, ऊचुः spoke, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, देवाः the gods, भयगद्गदभाषिणः speaking with voices choked by fear.
explanation: Having approached Shiva, the enemy of Kama, the destroyer of Tripura, and the three-eyed one, the gods, with folded hands and voices choked by fear, spoke to him.

shloka_text: सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः । प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधनैः ।। 7.6.4 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaputrairbhagavanpitāmahavaroddhataiḥ | prajādhyakṣa prajāḥ sarvā bādhyante ripubādhanaiḥ || 7.6.4 ||
translation: सुकेशपुत्रैः by the sons of Sukesha, भगवन् O Lord, पितामहवरोद्धतैः uplifted by the boon of Brahma, प्रजाध्यक्ष O Lord of creatures, प्रजाः creatures, सर्वाः all, बाध्यन्ते are tormented, रिपुबाधनैः by their tormenting acts.
explanation: The gods addressed Shiva, saying, "O Lord, O Lord of creatures, all beings are being tormented by the sons of Sukesha, who are uplifted by the boon of Brahma and act as tormentors."

shloka_text: शरण्यान्यशरण्यानि ह्याश्रमाणि कृतानि नः । स्वर्गाच्च देवान्प्रच्याव्य स्वर्गे क्रीडन्ति देववत् ।। 7.6.5 ।।
transliteration: śaraṇyānyaśaraṇyāni hyāśramāṇi kṛtāni naḥ | svargācca devānpracyāvya svarge krīḍanti devavat || 7.6.5 ||
translation: शरण्यानि places of refuge, अशरण्यानि non-refuge, हि indeed, आश्रमाणि hermitages, कृतानि made, नः by us, स्वर्गात् from heaven, च and, देवान् gods, प्रच्याव्य having dislodged, स्वर्गे in heaven, क्रीडन्ति they play, देववत् like gods.
explanation: They have made our hermitages unsafe, and having driven the gods from heaven, they now play in heaven as if they were gods themselves.

shloka_text: अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम् । अहं यमश्च वरुणश्चन्द्रो ऽहं रविरप्यहम् ।। 7.6.6 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ viṣṇurahaṃ rudro brahmāhaṃ devarāḍaham | ahaṃ yamaśca varuṇaścandro 'haṃ ravirapyaham || 7.6.6 ||
translation: अहं I am, विष्णुः Vishnu, अहं I am, रुद्रः Rudra, ब्रह्मा Brahma, अहं I am, देवराट् king of gods, अहम् I am, अहं I am, यमः Yama, च and, वरुणः Varuna, चन्द्रः Chandra, अहं I am, रविः Ravi, अपि also, अहम् I am.
explanation: They boast, "I am Vishnu, I am Rudra, I am Brahma, I am Indra, I am Yama, and Varuna, I am Chandra, and I am also Ravi."

shloka_text: इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः । बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । तन्नो देव भयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि ।। 7.6.7 ।।
transliteration: iti mālī sumālī ca mālyavāṃścaiva rākṣasāḥ | bādhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ | tanno deva bhayārtānāmabhayaṃ dātumarhasi || 7.6.7 ||
translation: इति thus, माली Mali, सुमाली Sumali, च and, माल्यवान् Malyavan, च and, एव indeed, राक्षसाः demons, बाधन्ते they torment, समरोद्धर्षाः those who delight in battle, ये who, च and, तेषां their, पुरःसराः leaders, तत् therefore, नः to us, देव O god, भयार्तानाम् to those afflicted by fear, अभयं protection, दातुम् to give, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: Thus, Mali, Sumali, and Malyavan, along with their battle-eager leaders, torment us; therefore, O god, you ought to grant protection to us who are afflicted by fear.

shloka_text: अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि वै देवकण्टकान् ।। 7.6.8 ।।
transliteration: aśivaṃ vapurāsthāya jahi vai devakaṇṭakān || 7.6.8 ||
translation: अशिवं inauspicious, वपुः form, आस्थाय having assumed, जहि kill, वै indeed, देवकण्टकान् thorns of the gods.
explanation: Therefore, assuming a terrible form, indeed destroy these thorns of the gods.

shloka_text: धन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः । सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्षः प्राह देवगणान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.9 ।।
transliteration: dhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ | ityuktastu suraiḥ sarvaiḥ kapardī nīlalohitaḥ | sukeśaṃ prati sāpekṣaḥ prāha devagaṇānprabhuḥ || 7.6.9 ||
translation: धन्ते (problematic verb, likely a typo for 'torment' or 'kill'), समरोद्धर्षाः those who delight in battle, ये who, च and, तेषां their, पुरःसराः leaders, इति thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, सुरैः by the gods, सर्वैः all, कपर्दी one with matted hair (Shiva), नीललोहितः blue-red (Shiva), सुकेशं towards Sukesha, प्रति towards, सापेक्षः concerned about, प्राह said, देवगणान् to the hosts of gods, प्रभुः the lord.
explanation: After all the gods had thus spoken about those battle-eager leaders who torment them, Lord Shiva, with matted hair and blue-red form, concerned about Sukesha, spoke to the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि मयावध्या हि ते सुराः । किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.10 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ tānna haniṣyāmi mayāvadhyā hi te surāḥ | kiṃ tu mantraṃ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati || 7.6.10 ||
translation: अहं I, तान् them, न not, हनिष्यामि will kill, मया by me, अवध्याः not to be killed, हि indeed, ते those, सुराः powerful beings, किं तु but, मन्त्रं a counsel, प्रदास्यामि I will give, यः which, वै indeed, तान् them, निहनिष्यति will kill.
explanation: Lord Shiva declared that he would not kill those powerful beings (Rakshasas) because they were invulnerable to him, but he would provide a strategy that would indeed destroy them.

shloka_text: एतमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.11 ।।
transliteration: etameva samudyogaṃ puraskṛtya maharṣayaḥ | gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ haniṣyati sa tānprabhuḥ || 7.6.11 ||
translation: एतम् this, एव indeed, समुद्योगं plan, पुरस्कृत्य having made primary, महर्षयः O great sages, गच्छध्वं go, शरणं for refuge, विष्णुं to Vishnu, हनिष्यति will kill, सः he, तान् them, प्रभुः the Lord.
explanation: O great sages, taking this very plan as your guide, go seek refuge in Lord Vishnu, for that Lord will surely kill them.

shloka_text: ततस्तु जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम् । विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः ।। 7.6.12 ।।
transliteration: tatastu jayaśabdena pratinandya maheśvaram | viṣṇoḥ samīpamājagmurniśācarabhayārditāḥ || 7.6.12 ||
translation: ततः then, तु indeed, जयशब्देन with cries of victory, प्रतिनन्द्य having acclaimed, महेश्वरम् Lord Shiva, विष्णोः of Vishnu, समीपम् to the vicinity, आजग्मुः they came, निशाचरभयार्दिताः afflicted by fear of night-wanderers.
explanation: Then, indeed, those afflicted by the fear of night-wanderers (Rakshasas) acclaimed Lord Shiva with cries of victory and approached Lord Vishnu.

shloka_text: शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च । ऊचुः सम्भ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ।। 7.6.13 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkhacakradharaṃ devaṃ praṇamya bahumānya ca | ūcuḥ sambhrāntavadvākyaṃ sukeśatanayānprati || 7.6.13 ||
translation: शङ्खचक्रधरं bearing the conch and discus, देवं the god, प्रणम्य having bowed down, बहुमान्य having greatly honored, च and, ऊचुः they spoke, सम्भ्रान्तवत् as if bewildered, वाक्यं words, सुकेशतनयान् regarding the sons of Sukesha, प्रति towards.
explanation: Having bowed down and greatly honored the god bearing the conch and discus, they spoke agitatedly concerning the sons of Sukesha.

shloka_text: सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः । आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहृतानि नः ।। 7.6.14 ।।
transliteration: sukeśatanayairdeva tribhistretāgnisannibhaiḥ | ākramya varadānena sthānānyapahṛtāni naḥ || 7.6.14 ||
translation: सुकेशतनयैः by the sons of Sukesha, देव O Lord, त्रिभिः by the three, त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः resembling the three sacred fires, आक्रम्य having overpowered, वरदानेन by the boon, स्थानानि places, अपहृतानि have been taken away, नः our.
explanation: O Lord, our abodes have been seized and taken away by the three sons of Sukesha, who resemble the three sacred fires, by virtue of a boon.

shloka_text: लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता । तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः ।। 7.6.15 ।।
transliteration: laṅkā nāma purī durgā trikūṭaśikhare sthitā | tatra sthitāḥ prabādhante sarvānnaḥ kṣaṇadācarāḥ || 7.6.15 ||
translation: लङ्का Lanka, नाम named, पुरी city, दुर्गा impregnable, त्रिकूटशिखरे on the peak of Trikuta, स्थिता situated, । तत्र there, स्थिताः those who reside, प्रबाधन्ते torment, सर्वान् all, नः us, क्षणदाचराः night-wanderers (Rakshasas) ।।
explanation: There is an impregnable city named Lanka, situated on the peak of Trikuta mountain, where night-roaming Rakshasas reside and torment all of us.

shloka_text: स त्वमस्मद्धितार्थाय जहि तान्मधुसूदन । शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.6.16 ।।
transliteration: sa tvamasmaddhitārthāya jahi tānmadhusūdana | śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ prāptā gatirbhava sureśvara || 7.6.16 ||
translation: सः that, त्वम् you, अस्मत् our, हितार्थाय for the welfare, जहि destroy, तान् them, मधुसूदन O Madhusudana, । शरणम् refuge, त्वाम् you, वयम् we, प्राप्ताः have attained, गतिः protector, भव be, सुरेश्वर O Lord of gods ।।
explanation: O Madhusudana, for our welfare, you must destroy them; we have sought refuge in you, so be our protector, O Lord of gods.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान्निवेदय यमाय वै । भयेष्वभयदो ऽस्माकं नान्यो ऽस्ति भवता विना ।। 7.6.17 ।।
transliteration: cakrakṛttāsyakamalānnivedaya yamāya vai | bhayeṣvabhayado 'smākaṃ nānyo 'sti bhavatā vinā || 7.6.17 ||
translation: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान् whose lotus-like faces are severed by your discus, निवेदय offer, यमाय to Yama, वै indeed, । भयेषु in fears, अभयदः giver of fearlessness, अस्माकम् to us, न not, अन्यः another, अस्ति is, भवता by you, विना without ।।
explanation: Offer to Yama those whose lotus-like faces are severed by your discus, for there is no other giver of fearlessness to us in times of fear except you.

shloka_text: राक्षसान्समरे दुष्टान्सानुबन्धान्मदोद्धतान् । नुदं त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः ।। 7.6.18 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānsamare duṣṭānsānubandhānmadoddhatān | nudaṃ tvaṃ no bhayaṃ deva nīhāramiva bhāskaraḥ || 7.6.18 ||
translation: राक्षसान् Rakshasas, समरे in battle, दुष्टान् wicked, सानुबन्धान् along with their followers, मदोद्धतान् arrogant due to pride, । नुदम् dispel, त्वम् you, नः our, भयम् fear, देव O God, नीहारम् mist, इव like, भास्करः the sun ।।
explanation: O God, just as the sun dispels mist, you should dispel our fear by destroying these wicked, arrogant Rakshasas and their followers in battle.

shloka_text: इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः । अभयं भयदो ऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह ।। 7.6.19 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ daivatairukto devadevo janārdanaḥ | abhayaṃ bhayado 'rīṇāṃ dattvā devānuvāca ha || 7.6.19 ||
translation: इति thus, एवम् indeed, दैवतैः by the gods, उक्तः spoken to, देवदेवः the God of gods, जनार्दनः Janardana (Vishnu), । अभयम् fearlessness, भयदः giver of fear, अरीणाम् to enemies, दत्त्वा having given, देवान् to the gods, उवाच spoke, ह indeed ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the gods, Janardana, the God of gods, who grants fearlessness to his devotees and fear to his enemies, indeed spoke to the gods after granting them protection.

shloka_text: सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम् । तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान् ।। 7.6.20 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaṃ rākṣasaṃ jāne īśānavaradarpitam | tāṃścāsya tanayāñjāne yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa mālyavān || 7.6.20 ||
translation: सुकेशं Sukesha, राक्षसं the demon, जाने I know, ईशानवरदर्पितम् proud due to the boon from Ishana (Shiva), ताम्श्चास्य and his, तनयान् sons, जाने I know, येषां among whom, ज्येष्ठः the eldest, स he, माल्यवान् is Malyavan.
explanation: I know the demon Sukesha, who is arrogant due to a boon from Shiva, and I also know his sons, among whom Malyavan is the eldest.

shloka_text: तानहं समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान्राक्षसाधमान् । निहनिष्यामि सङ्क्रुद्धः सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.21 ।।
transliteration: tānahaṃ samatikrāntamaryādānrākṣasādhamān | nihaniṣyāmi saṅkruddhaḥ surā bhavata vijvarāḥ || 7.6.21 ||
translation: तान् those, अहम् I, समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान् who have transgressed limits, राक्षसाधमान् vile demons, निहनिष्यामि will kill, सङ्क्रुद्धः being very angry, सुराः O gods, भवत become, विज्वराः free from fear/anxiety.
explanation: I, being exceedingly angry, will kill those vile demons who have transgressed all limits; therefore, O gods, be free from fear.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । यथावासं ययुर्हृष्टाः प्रशंसन्तो जनार्दनम् ।। 7.6.22 ।।
transliteration: ityuktāste surāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā | yathāvāsaṃ yayurhṛṣṭāḥ praśaṃsanto janārdanam || 7.6.22 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्ताः spoken to, ते those, सुराः gods, सर्वे all, विष्णुना by Vishnu, प्रभविष्णुना the all-powerful, यथावासम् to their respective abodes, ययुः went, हृष्टाः delighted, प्रशंसन्तः praising, जनार्दनम् Janardana (Vishnu).
explanation: Thus addressed by the all-powerful Vishnu, all the gods, delighted, returned to their respective abodes, praising Janardana.

shloka_text: विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवांस्तु निशाचरः । श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.23 ।।
transliteration: vibudhānāṃ samudyogaṃ mālyavāṃstu niśācaraḥ | śrutvā tau bhrātarau vīrāvidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.6.23 ||
translation: विबुधानाम् of the gods, समुद्योगम् the concerted effort/preparation, माल्यवान् Malyavan, तु indeed, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (demon), श्रुत्वा having heard, तौ to those two, भ्रातरौ brothers, वीरौ brave ones, इदम् this, वचनम् word/speech, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Malyavan, the demon, having heard of the gods' concerted effort, spoke these words to his two brave brothers.

shloka_text: अमरा ऋषयश्चैव सङ्गम्य किल शकरम् । अस्मद्वधं परीप्सन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ।। 7.6.24 ।।
transliteration: amarā ṛṣayaścaiva saṅgamya kila śakaram | asmadvadhaṃ parīpsanta idaṃ vacanamabruvan || 7.6.24 ||
translation: अमराः the immortals (gods), ऋषयः and the sages, च and, एव indeed, सङ्गम्य having met, किल it is said, शकरम् Shankara (Shiva), अस्मद्वधम् our destruction, परीप्सन्तः desiring, इदम् this, वचनम् word/speech, अब्रुवन् spoke.
explanation: It is said that the gods and sages, having met Shankara, spoke these words, desiring our destruction.

shloka_text: सुकेशतनया देव वरदानबलोद्धताः । बाधन्ते ऽस्मान्समुद्दृप्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे ।। 7.6.25 ।।
transliteration: sukeśatanayā deva varadānabaloddhatāḥ | bādhante 'smānsamuddṛptā ghorarūpāḥ pade pade || 7.6.25 ||
translation: सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, देव O god, वरदानबलोद्धताः arrogant due to the strength of boons, बाधन्ते they harass, अस्मान् us, समुद्दृप्ताः exceedingly arrogant, घोररूपाः of terrible form, पदे पदे at every step.
explanation: O god, the sons of Sukesha, who are exceedingly arrogant due to the power of boons and possess terrible forms, harass us at every step.

shloka_text: राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते । स्वेषु सद्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम् ।। 7.6.26 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasairabhibhūtāḥ sma na śaktāḥ sma prajāpate | sveṣu sadmasu saṃsthātuṃ bhayātteṣāṃ durātmanām || 7.6.26 ||
translation: राक्षसैः by the Rakshasas, अभिभूताः overcome, स्म we are, न not, शक्ताः able, स्म we are, प्रजापते O Prajapati, स्वेषु in our own, सद्मसु abodes, संस्थातुम् to stay, भयात् due to fear, तेषाम् of those, दुरात्मनाम् wicked ones.
explanation: O Prajapati, we are overcome by these Rakshasas and are unable to remain in our own abodes due to fear of those wicked beings.

shloka_text: तदस्माकं हितार्थाय जहि तांश्च त्रिलोचन । राक्षसान्हुङ्कृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर ।। 7.6.27 ।।
transliteration: tadasmākaṃ hitārthāya jahi tāṃśca trilocana | rākṣasānhuṅkṛtenaiva daha pradahatāṃ vara || 7.6.27 ||
translation: तत् therefore, अस्माकम् our, हितार्थाय for the sake of welfare, जहि destroy, तांश्च and those, त्रिलोचन O three-eyed one, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, हुङ्कृतेनैव merely with a roar, दह burn, प्रदहताम् of those who burn, वर O best.
explanation: Therefore, O three-eyed one, for our welfare, destroy those Rakshasas and burn them merely with a roar, O best among those who can burn.

shloka_text: इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः । शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.28 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ tridaśairukto niśamyāndhakasūdanaḥ | śiraḥ karaṃ ca dhunvāna idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.6.28 ||
translation: इत्येवम् thus, त्रिदशैः by the gods, उक्तः spoken to, निशम्य having heard, अन्धकसूदनः the destroyer of Andhaka, शिरः head, करम् hand, च and, धुन्वानः shaking, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having thus been addressed by the gods and having heard their plea, the destroyer of Andhaka (Shiva), shaking his head and hand, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे । मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.29 ।।
transliteration: avadhyā mama te devāḥ sukeśatanayā raṇe | mantraṃ tu vaḥ pradāsyāmi yastānvai nihaniṣyati || 7.6.29 ||
translation: अवध्याः not to be killed, मम by me, ते those, देवाः O gods, सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, रणे in battle, मन्त्रम् counsel, तु but, वः to you, प्रदास्यामि I shall give, यः who, तान् them, वै indeed, निहनिष्यति will kill.
explanation: O gods, those sons of Sukesha are not to be killed by me in battle; however, I shall give you a counsel (or a plan) that will indeed lead to their destruction.

shloka_text: यो ऽसौ चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः । हरिर्नारायणः श्रीमान् शरणं तं प्रपद्यथ ।। 7.6.30 ।।
transliteration: yo 'sau cakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ | harirnārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān śaraṇaṃ taṃ prapadyatha || 7.6.30 ||
translation: यः who, असौ that, चक्रगदापाणिः one who holds discus and mace in hand, पीतवासा wearing yellow garments, जनार्दनः Janardana, हरिः Hari, नारायणः Narayana, श्रीमान् glorious, शरणं refuge, तं him, प्रपद्यथ take refuge in
explanation: You should take refuge in that glorious Narayana, also known as Janardana and Hari, who holds the discus and mace in his hands and wears yellow garments.

shloka_text: हरादवाप्य ते मन्त्रं कामारिमभिवाद्य च । नारायणालयं प्राप्य तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन् ।। 7.6.31 ।।
transliteration: harādavāpya te mantraṃ kāmārimabhivādya ca | nārāyaṇālayaṃ prāpya tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayan || 7.6.31 ||
translation: हरात् from Hara (Shiva), अवाप्य having obtained, ते they, मन्त्रं the mantra, कामारिम to the enemy of Kama (Shiva), अभिवाद्य having saluted, च and, नारायणालयं to the abode of Narayana, प्राप्य having reached, तस्मै to him, सर्वं everything, न्यवेदयन् submitted
explanation: Having obtained the mantra from Hara and saluted Shiva, they reached the abode of Narayana and submitted everything to him.

shloka_text: ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः । सुरारींस्तान्हनिष्यामि सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.32 ।।
transliteration: tato nārāyaṇenoktā devā indrapurogamāḥ | surārīṃstānhaniṣyāmi surā bhavata vijvarāḥ || 7.6.32 ||
translation: ततः then, नारायणेन by Narayana, उक्ताः addressed, देवाः the gods, इन्द्रपुरोगमाः led by Indra, सुरारीन् the enemies of the gods, तान् them, हनिष्यामि I will kill, सुराः O gods, भवत become, विज्वराः free from anxiety
explanation: Then Narayana addressed the gods, led by Indra, saying, "I will kill those enemies of the gods; O gods, become free from anxiety."

shloka_text: देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ । प्रतिज्ञातो वधो ऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम् ।। 7.6.33 ।।
transliteration: devānāṃ bhayabhītānāṃ hariṇā rākṣasarṣabhau | pratijñāto vadho 'smākaṃ cintyatāṃ yadiha kṣamam || 7.6.33 ||
translation: देवानां of the gods, भयभीतानां who were terrified, हरिणा by Hari, राक्षसर्षभौ O best of Rakshasas, प्रतिज्ञातो promised, वधः destruction, अस्माकं of us, चिन्त्यतां let it be considered, यत् what, इह here, क्षमम् appropriate
explanation: O best of Rakshasas, Hari has promised the destruction of us (Rakshasas) to the terrified gods; therefore, let us consider what is appropriate to do in this situation.

shloka_text: हिरण्यकशिपोर्मृत्युरन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम् । नमुचिः कालनेमिश्च संह्रादो वीरसत्तमः ।। 7.6.34 ।।
transliteration: hiraṇyakaśipormṛtyuranyeṣāṃ ca suradviṣām | namuciḥ kālanemiśca saṃhrādo vīrasattamaḥ || 7.6.34 ||
translation: हिरण्यकशिपोः of Hiranyakashipu, मृत्युः the death, अन्येषां of others, च and, सुरद्विषाम् of the enemies of gods, नमुचिः Namuchi, कालनेमिः Kalanemi, च and, संह्रादः Samhrada, वीरसत्तमः the best of heroes
explanation: The death of Hiranyakashipu and other enemies of the gods, such as Namuchi, Kalanemi, and Samhrada, the best of heroes, was also caused by him.

shloka_text: राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालो ऽथ धार्मिकः । यमलार्जुनौ च हार्दिक्यः शुम्भश्चैव निशुम्भकः ।। 7.6.35 ।।
transliteration: rādheyo bahumāyī ca lokapālo 'tha dhārmikaḥ | yamalārjunau ca hārdikyaḥ śumbhaścaiva niśumbhakaḥ || 7.6.35 ||
translation: राधेयो Radheya, बहुमायी one with many illusions, च and, लोकपालो Lokapala, अथ and, धार्मिकः Dharmika, यमलार्जुनौ Yamala and Arjuna, च and, हार्दिक्यः Hardikya, शुम्भश्चैव Shumbha and, निशुम्भकः Nishumbhaka.
explanation: This verse lists several powerful and deceitful Asuras, including Radheya, Bahumayi, Lokapala, Dharmika, Yamala and Arjuna, Hardikya, Shumbha, and Nishumbhaka.

shloka_text: असुरा दानवाश्चैव सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः । सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते ऽपराजिताः ।। 7.6.36 ।।
transliteration: asurā dānavāścaiva sattvavanto mahābalāḥ | sarve samaramāsādya na śrūyante 'parājitāḥ || 7.6.36 ||
translation: असुरा Asuras, दानवाश्चैव and Danavas, सत्त्ववन्तो endowed with strength, महाबलाः very powerful, सर्वे all, समरमासाद्य having entered battle, न not, श्रूयन्ते are heard, अपराजिताः unconquered.
explanation: All these Asuras and Danavas, though endowed with great strength and power, are never heard to have remained undefeated once they entered battle.

shloka_text: सर्वैः क्रतुशतैरिष्टं सर्वे मायाविदस्तथा । सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वे शत्रुभयङ्कराः ।। 7.6.37 ।।
transliteration: sarvaiḥ kratuśatairiṣṭaṃ sarve māyāvidastathā | sarve sarvāstrakuśalāḥ sarve śatrubhayaṅkarāḥ || 7.6.37 ||
translation: सर्वैः by all, क्रतुशतैरिष्टं hundreds of sacrifices were performed, सर्वे all, मायाविदस्तथा and skilled in illusion, सर्वे all, सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः skilled in all weapons, सर्वे all, शत्रुभयङ्कराः terrifying to enemies.
explanation: All of them had performed hundreds of sacrifices, were skilled in various illusions, proficient in all weapons, and struck terror into their enemies.

shloka_text: नारायणेन निहताः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु सर्वेषां क्षमं कर्तुमिहार्हथ ।। 7.6.38 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇena nihatāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ | etajjñātvā tu sarveṣāṃ kṣamaṃ kartumihārhatha || 7.6.38 ||
translation: नारायणेन by Narayana, निहताः slain, शतशो by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands, एतज्ज्ञात्वा having known this, तु indeed, सर्वेषां for all, क्षमं forgiveness, कर्तुमिहार्हथ you should do here.
explanation: Knowing that these very beings were slain by Narayana in hundreds and thousands, you should now grant forgiveness to all of them here.

shloka_text: ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः । ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं भगांशाविव वासवम् ।। 7.6.39 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sumālī mālī ca śrutvā mālyavato vacaḥ | ūcaturbhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhagāṃśāviva vāsavam || 7.6.39 ||
translation: ततः then, सुमाली Sumali, माली Mali, च and, श्रुत्वा having heard, माल्यवतो of Malyavan, वचः words, ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं spoke to their brother, ज्येष्ठं elder, भगांशाविव like Bhaga and Amsha, वासवम् to Vasava (Indra).
explanation: Then, Sumali and Mali, having heard the words of Malyavan, spoke to their elder brother, just as Bhaga and Amsha would speak to Indra.

shloka_text: स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं चाप्यैश्वर्यं परिपालितम् । आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं सुधर्मः प्रापितः पथि ।। 7.6.40 ।।
transliteration: svadhītaṃ dattamiṣṭaṃ cāpyaiśvaryaṃ paripālitam | āyurnirāmayaṃ prāptaṃ sudharmaḥ prāpitaḥ pathi || 7.6.40 ||
translation: स्वधीतम् well-studied, दत्तम् given, इष्टम् sacrificed, च and, अपि also, ऐश्वर्यम् sovereignty, परिपालितम् protected, आयुः life, निरामयम् healthy, प्राप्तम् obtained, सुधर्मः good dharma, प्रापितः established, पथि on the path.
explanation: We have diligently studied, given charity, performed sacrifices, maintained our sovereignty, attained a healthy life, and established righteousness on our path.

shloka_text: देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रैः समवगाह्य च । जिता द्विषो ह्यप्रतिमास्तन्नो मृत्युकृतं भयम् ।। 7.6.41 ।।
transliteration: devasāgaramakṣobhyaṃ śastraiḥ samavagāhya ca | jitā dviṣo hyapratimāstanno mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam || 7.6.41 ||
translation: देवसागरम् the ocean of gods, अक्षोभ्यम् unagitable, शस्त्रैः with weapons, समवगाह्य having plunged into, च and, जिताः conquered, द्विषः enemies, हि indeed, अप्रतिमाः unequalled, तत् therefore, नः to us, मृत्युकृतम् caused by death, भयम् fear.
explanation: Having plunged into the unagitable ocean of gods with our weapons, and having conquered unequalled enemies, we therefore have no fear caused by death.

shloka_text: नारायणश्च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा । अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा ।। 7.6.42 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇaśca rudraśca śakraścāpi yamastathā | asmākaṃ pramukhe sthātuṃ sarve bibhyati sarvadā || 7.6.42 ||
translation: नारायणः Narayana, च and, रुद्रः Rudra, च and, शक्रः Shakra, च and, अपि also, यमः Yama, तथा similarly, अस्माकम् our, प्रमुखे in front, स्थातुम् to stand, सर्वे all, बिभ्यति fear, सर्वदा always.
explanation: Narayana, Rudra, Shakra, and Yama, all of them always fear to stand in our presence.

shloka_text: विष्णोर्देवस्य नास्त्येव कारणं राक्षसेश्वर । देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः ।। 7.6.43 ।।
transliteration: viṣṇordevasya nāstyeva kāraṇaṃ rākṣaseśvara | devānāmeva doṣeṇa viṣṇoḥ pracalitaṃ manaḥ || 7.6.43 ||
translation: विष्णोः of Vishnu, देवस्य of the god, न not, अस्ति is, एव indeed, कारणम् reason, राक्षसेश्वर O lord of Rakshasas, देवानाम् of the gods, एव only, दोषेण by the fault, विष्णोः of Vishnu, प्रचलितम् agitated, मनः mind.
explanation: O lord of Rakshasas, there is indeed no inherent reason for the god Vishnu to act against us; it is only due to the fault of the other gods that Vishnu's mind has been agitated.

shloka_text: तस्मादद्य समुद्युक्ताः सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः । देवानेव जिघांसाम एभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः ।। 7.6.44 ।।
transliteration: tasmādadya samudyuktāḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtāḥ | devāneva jighāṃsāma ebhyo doṣaḥ samutthitaḥ || 7.6.44 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, अद्य today, समुद्युक्ताः fully prepared, सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः surrounded by all armies, देवान् the gods, एव only, जिघांसाम we will kill, एभ्यः from them, दोषः the fault, समुत्थितः has arisen.
explanation: Therefore, today, fully prepared and surrounded by all our armies, we shall kill the gods, for the fault has originated from them.

shloka_text: एवं सम्मन्त्र्य बलिनः सर्वे सैन्यसमावृताः । उद्योगं घोषयित्वा तु सर्वे नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः ।। युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धा जम्भवृत्रबला इव ।। 7.6.45 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sammantrya balinaḥ sarve sainyasamāvṛtāḥ | udyogaṃ ghoṣayitvā tu sarve nairṛtapuṅgavāḥ || yuddhāya niryayuḥ kruddhā jambhavṛtrabalā iva || 7.6.45 ||
translation: एवं thus, सम्मन्त्र्य having deliberated, बलिनः the powerful ones, सर्वे all, सैन्यसमावृताः surrounded by armies, उद्योगं the preparation (for war), घोषयित्वा having announced, तु and, सर्वे all, नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः the foremost among the Rākṣasas, युद्धाय for battle, निर्ययुः set out, क्रुद्धा enraged, जम्भवृत्रबला like Jambha, Vṛtra, and Bala (demons), इव as if.
explanation: Having thus deliberated, all the powerful and foremost Rākṣasas, surrounded by their armies, announced their preparations and set out for battle, enraged like the demons Jambha, Vṛtra, and Bala.

shloka_text: इति ते राम सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः । युद्धाय निर्ययुः सर्वे महाकाया महाबलाः ।। 7.6.46 ।।
transliteration: iti te rāma sammantrya sarvodyogena rākṣasāḥ | yuddhāya niryayuḥ sarve mahākāyā mahābalāḥ || 7.6.46 ||
translation: इति thus, ते they, राम O Rama, सम्मन्त्र्य having deliberated, सर्वोद्योगेन with full preparation, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, युद्धाय for battle, निर्ययुः set out, सर्वे all, महाकाया of huge bodies, महाबलाः of great strength.
explanation: O Rama, having thus deliberated with full preparation, all those Rākṣasas of huge bodies and great strength set out for battle.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैर्वारणैश्चैव हयैश्च गिरिसन्निभैः । खरैर्गोभी रथोष्ट्रैश्च शिंशुमारैर्भुजङ्गमैः ।। 7.6.47 ।।
transliteration: syandanairvāraṇaiścaiva hayaiśca girisannibhaiḥ | kharairgobhī rathoṣṭraiśca śiṃśumārairbhujaṅgamaiḥ || 7.6.47 ||
translation: स्यन्दनैः with chariots, वारणैः with elephants, च and, एव indeed, हयैः with horses, च and, गिरिसन्निभैः resembling mountains, खरैः with donkeys, गोभी with cows, रथोष्ट्रैः with chariots drawn by camels, च and, शिंशुमारैः with porpoises (or crocodiles), भुजङ्गमैः with serpents.
explanation: They set out with chariots, elephants, mountain-like horses, donkeys, cows, camel-drawn chariots, porpoises, and serpents.

shloka_text: मकरैः कच्छपैर्मीनैर्विहङ्गैर्गरुडोपमैः । सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्वराहैश्च सृमरैश्चमरैरपि ।। 7.6.48 ।।
transliteration: makaraiḥ kacchapairmīnairvihaṅgairgaruḍopamaiḥ | siṃhairvyāghrairvarāhaiśca sṛmaraiścamarairapi || 7.6.48 ||
translation: मकरैः with crocodiles, कच्छपैः with tortoises, मीनैर with fish, विहङ्गैः with birds, गरुडोपमैः resembling Garuḍa, सिंहैः with lions, व्याघ्रैः with tigers, वराहैः with boars, च and, सृमरैः with antelopes (or a type of deer), चमरैः with yaks, अपि also.
explanation: They also advanced with crocodiles, tortoises, fish, birds resembling Garuḍa, lions, tigers, boars, antelopes, and yaks.

shloka_text: त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । प्रयाता देवलोकाय योद्धुं दैवतशत्रवः ।। 7.6.49 ।।
transliteration: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatāḥ sarve rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ | prayātā devalokāya yoddhuṃ daivataśatravaḥ || 7.6.49 ||
translation: त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, लङ्कां Lanka, गताः went, सर्वे all, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, बलगर्विताः proud of their strength, प्रयाता set out, देवलोकाय for the world of gods, योद्धुं to fight, दैवतशत्रवः the enemies of the gods.
explanation: All the Rākṣasas, proud of their strength and enemies of the gods, abandoned Lanka and set out for the world of the gods to fight.

shloka_text: लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ । भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः ।। 7.6.50 ।।
transliteration: laṅkāviparyayaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāni laṅkālayānyatha | bhūtāni bhayadarśīni vimanaskāni sarvaśaḥ || 7.6.50 ||
translation: लङ्काविपर्ययम् Lanka's destruction, दृष्ट्वा having seen, यानि which, लङ्कालयानि dwelling in Lanka, अथ and, भूतानि beings, भयदर्शीनि fearful, विमनस्कानि dejected, सर्वशः completely,
explanation: Seeing the impending destruction of Lanka, all the beings dwelling there became utterly fearful and disheartened.

shloka_text: रथोत्तमैरुह्यमानाः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.51 ।।
transliteration: rathottamairuhyamānāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ || 7.6.51 ||
translation: रथोत्तमैः by excellent chariots, उह्यमानाः being carried, शतशः by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands,
explanation: Hundreds and thousands of them were being carried by excellent chariots.

shloka_text: प्रयाता राक्षसास्तूर्णं देवलोकं प्रयत्नतः । रक्षसामेव मार्गेण दैवतान्यपचक्रमुः ।। 7.6.52 ।।
transliteration: prayātā rākṣasāstūrṇaṃ devalokaṃ prayatnataḥ | rakṣasāmeva mārgeṇa daivatānyapacakramuḥ || 7.6.52 ||
translation: प्रयाताः departed, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, तूर्णं quickly, देवलोकं to the world of gods, प्रयत्नतः with effort, रक्षसाम् of the Rakshasas, एव indeed, मार्गेण by the path, दैवतानि deities, अपचक्रमुः departed,
explanation: The Rakshasas quickly departed to the world of gods with great effort, and even the deities departed by the very path used by the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: भौमाश्चैवान्तरिक्षाश्च कालाज्ञप्ता भयावहाः । उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावाय समुत्थिताः ।। 7.6.53 ।।
transliteration: bhaumāścaivāntarikṣāśca kālājñaptā bhayāvahāḥ | utpātā rākṣasendrāṇāmabhāvāya samutthitāḥ || 7.6.53 ||
translation: भौमाः earthly, च and, एव indeed, आन्तरिक्षाः atmospheric, च and, कालाज्ञप्ताः commanded by time, भयावहाः terrifying, उत्पाताः portents, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् for the chief Rakshasas, अभावाय for destruction, समुत्थिताः arose,
explanation: Terrifying earthly and atmospheric portents, commanded by fate, arose for the destruction of the chief Rakshasas.

shloka_text: अस्थीनि मेघा ववृषुरुष्णं शोणितमेव च । वेलां समुद्राश्चोत्क्रान्ताश्चेलुश्चाप्यथ भूधराः ।। 7.6.54 ।।
transliteration: asthīni meghā vavṛṣuruṣṇaṃ śoṇitameva ca | velāṃ samudrāścotkrāntāśceluścāpyatha bhūdharāḥ || 7.6.54 ||
translation: अस्थीनि bones, मेघाः clouds, ववृषुः rained, उष्णं hot, शोणितम् blood, एव indeed, च and, वेलां the shore, समुद्राः oceans, च and, उत्क्रान्ताः transgressed, चेलुः trembled, च and, अपि also, अथ then, भूधराः mountains,
explanation: Clouds rained bones and hot blood, oceans overflowed their shores, and mountains also trembled.

shloka_text: अट्टहासान्विमुञ्चन्तो घननादसमस्वनाः । वाश्यन्त्यश्च शिवास्तत्र दारुणं घोरदर्शनाः ।। 7.6.55 ।।
transliteration: aṭṭahāsānvimuñcanto ghananādasamasvanāḥ | vāśyantyaśca śivāstatra dāruṇaṃ ghoradarśanāḥ || 7.6.55 ||
translation: अट्टहासान् loud laughs, विमुञ्चन्तः emitting, घननादसमस्वनाः having sounds like thunder, वाश्यन्त्यश्च and howling, शिवाः jackals, तत्र there, दारुणं terrible, घोरदर्शनाः frightful to behold.
explanation: There, jackals, frightful to behold and making terrible, thunder-like sounds and loud roars, were howling.

shloka_text: सम्पतन्त्यथ भूतानि दृश्यन्ते च यथाक्रमम् । गृध्रचक्रं महच्चात्र ज्वलनोद्गारिभिर्मुखैः ।। 7.6.56 ।।
transliteration: sampatantyatha bhūtāni dṛśyante ca yathākramam | gṛdhracakraṃ mahaccātra jvalanodgāribhirmukhaiḥ || 7.6.56 ||
translation: सम्पतन्त्यथ then appearing, भूतानि spirits, दृश्यन्ते are seen, च and, यथाक्रमम् successively, गृध्रचक्रं a flock of vultures, महत् large, च and, अत्र here, ज्वलनोद्गारिभिः emitting flames, मुखैः with mouths.
explanation: Then, ominous spirits were seen appearing successively, and a large flock of vultures with flame-emitting mouths was also present.

shloka_text: राक्षसानामुपरि खे भ्रमते ऽलातचक्रवत् । कपोता रक्तपादाश्च शारिका विद्रुता ययुः ।। काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडाला वै द्विपादयः ।। 7.6.57 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāmupari khe bhramate 'lātacakravat | kapotā raktapādāśca śārikā vidrutā yayuḥ || kākā vāśyanti tatraiva biḍālā vai dvipādayaḥ || 7.6.57 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of the Rakshasas, उपरि above, खे in the sky, भ्रमते revolves, अलातचक्रवत् like a firebrand wheel, कपोताः pigeons, रक्तपादाः red-footed, च and, शारिकाः mynah birds, विद्रुताः fled, ययुः went, काकाः crows, वाश्यन्ति caw, तत्रैव right there, बिडालाः cats, वै indeed, द्विपादयः two-footed.
explanation: Above the Rakshasas, the vultures hovered in the sky like a fiery wheel, while red-footed pigeons and mynah birds fled, and two-footed cats and crows cawed right there.

shloka_text: उत्पातांस्ताननादृत्य राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । यान्त्येव न निवर्त्तन्ते मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः ।। 7.6.58 ।।
transliteration: utpātāṃstānanādṛtya rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ | yāntyeva na nivarttante mṛtyupāśāvapāśitāḥ || 7.6.58 ||
translation: उत्पातान् omens, तान् those, अनादृत्य disregarding, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, बलगर्विताः proud of their strength, यान्ति go, एव indeed, न not, निवर्त्तन्ते turn back, मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः bound by the noose of death.
explanation: Disregarding those omens, the Rakshasas, proud of their strength and bound by the noose of death, continued to advance and did not turn back.

shloka_text: माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलाः । आसन्पुरःसरास्तेषां क्रतूनामिव पावकाः ।। 7.6.59 ।।
transliteration: mālyavāṃśca sumālī ca mālī ca sumahābalāḥ | āsanpuraḥsarāsteṣāṃ kratūnāmiva pāvakāḥ || 7.6.59 ||
translation: माल्यवान् Malyavan, च and, सुमाली Sumali, च and, माली Mali, च and, सुमहाबलाः exceedingly mighty, आसन् were, पुरःसराः leaders, तेषाम् of them, क्रतूनाम् of sacrifices, इव like, पावकाः fires.
explanation: Malyavan, Sumali, and Mali, all exceedingly mighty, were the leaders of those Rakshasas, just as fires are foremost in sacrifices.

shloka_text: माल्यवन्तं च ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् । निशाचरा ह्याश्रयन्ति धातारमिव देवताः ।। 7.6.60 ।।
transliteration: mālyavantaṃ ca te sarve mālyavantamivācalam | niśācarā hyāśrayanti dhātāramiva devatāḥ || 7.6.60 ||
translation: माल्यवन्तं Malyavan, च and, ते those, सर्वे all, माल्यवन्तम् Malyavan (the mountain), इव like, अचलम् a mountain, निशाचराः night-wanderers (demons), हि indeed, आश्रयन्ति take refuge, धातारम् to Brahma, इव like, देवताः gods.
explanation: All those night-wandering demons indeed took refuge in Malyavan, just as gods resort to Brahma, and as one would take refuge in an unmoving mountain.

shloka_text: तद्बलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम् । जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ मालिवशे स्थितम् ।। 7.6.61 ।।
transliteration: tadbalaṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ mahābhraghananāditam | jayepsayā devalokaṃ yayau mālivaśe sthitam || 7.6.61 ||
translation: तत् that, बलम् army, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् of the lords of Rākṣasas, महाभ्रघननादितम् resounding like the crashing of great clouds, जयेप्सया with the desire for victory, देवलोकम् to the world of gods, ययौ went, मालिवशे under the control of Mali, स्थितम् situated.
explanation: That army of the demon lords, resounding like the crashing of great clouds, went to the world of gods, which was under Mali's sway, with a desire for victory.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः । देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य चक्रे युद्धे तदा मनः ।। 7.6.62 ।।
