transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ samudyogaṃ taṃ tu nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ | devadūtādupaśrutya cakre yuddhe tadā manaḥ || 7.6.62 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, समुद्योगम् preparation, तम् that, तु indeed, नारायणः Nārāyaṇa, प्रभुः the Lord, देवदूतात् from a messenger of the gods, उपश्रुत्य having heard, चक्रे made, युद्धे in battle, तदा then, मनः mind.
explanation: But the Lord Nārāyaṇa, having heard of that preparation by the Rākṣasas from a messenger of the gods, then set his mind on battle.

shloka_text: स सज्जायुधतूणीरो वैनतेयोपरि स्थितः । आसज्ज्य कवचं दिव्यं सहस्रार्कसमद्युति ।। 7.6.63 ।।
transliteration: sa sajjāyudhatūṇīro vainateyopari sthitaḥ | āsajjya kavacaṃ divyaṃ sahasrārkasamadyuti || 7.6.63 ||
translation: सः He, सज्जायुधतूणीरः with weapons and quivers ready, वैनतेयोपरि upon Vainateya (Garuda), स्थितः situated, आसज्ज्य having put on, कवचम् armor, दिव्यम् divine, सहस्रार्कसमद्युति having the brilliance of a thousand suns.
explanation: He, with weapons and quivers ready, stood upon Vainateya (Garuda), having donned his divine armor that shone with the brilliance of a thousand suns.

shloka_text: आबध्य शरसम्पूर्णे इषुधी विमले तदा । श्रोणिसूत्रं च खड्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः ।। शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् ।। 7.6.64 ।।
transliteration: ābadhya śarasampūrṇe iṣudhī vimale tadā | śroṇisūtraṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca vimalaṃ kamalekṣaṇaḥ || śaṅkhacakragadāśārṅgakhaḍgākhyapravarāyudhān || 7.6.64 ||
translation: आबध्य having fastened, शरसम्पूर्णे full of arrows, इषुधी two quivers, विमले pure, तदा then, श्रोणिसूत्रम् waist-band, च and, खड्गम् sword, च and, विमलम् pure, कमलेक्षणः lotus-eyed (Nārāyaṇa), शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् the excellent weapons named conch, discus, mace, bow (Śārṅga), and sword.
explanation: Then, the lotus-eyed Nārāyaṇa fastened his two pure quivers full of arrows, his pure waist-band, and his sword, along with his excellent weapons: the conch, discus, mace, Śārṅga bow, and sword.

shloka_text: सुपर्णं गिरिसङ्काशं वैनतेयमथास्थितः । राक्षसानामभावाय ययौ तूर्णतरं प्रभुः ।। 7.6.65 ।।
transliteration: suparṇaṃ girisaṅkāśaṃ vainateyamathāsthitaḥ | rākṣasānāmabhāvāya yayau tūrṇataraṃ prabhuḥ || 7.6.65 ||
translation: सुपर्णं Suparna (Garuda), गिरिसङ्काशं mountain-like, वैनतेयम् the son of Vinata (Garuda), अथास्थितः then having mounted, राक्षसानाम of the Rakshasas, अभावाय for the destruction, ययौ went, तूर्णतरं very swiftly, प्रभुः the Lord.
explanation: The Lord, having mounted the mountain-like Garuda, the son of Vinata, swiftly departed for the destruction of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपृष्ठे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः । काञ्चनस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.6.66 ।।
transliteration: suparṇapṛṣṭhe sa babhau śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro hariḥ | kāñcanasya gireḥ śṛṅge sataḍittoyado yathā || 7.6.66 ||
translation: सुपर्णपृष्ठे on Garuda's back, सः He, बभौ shone, श्यामः dark-complexioned, पीताम्बरः wearing yellow garments, हरिः Hari (Vishnu), काञ्चनस्य of a golden, गिरेः mountain, शृङ्गे on the peak, सतडित्तोयदो a cloud with lightning, यथा just as.
explanation: Dark-complexioned Hari, adorned in yellow garments, shone on Garuda's back like a lightning-streaked cloud upon the peak of a golden mountain.

shloka_text: स सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च गन्धर्वयक्षैरुपगीयमानः । समाससादासुरसैन्यशत्रूंश्चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः ।। 7.6.67 ।।
transliteration: sa siddhadevarṣimahoragaiśca gandharvayakṣairupagīyamānaḥ | samāsasādāsurasainyaśatrūṃścakrāsiśārṅgāyudhaśaṅkhapāṇiḥ || 7.6.67 ||
translation: सः He, सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च by Siddhas, Devas, Rishis, and great serpents, गन्धर्वयक्षैः by Gandharvas and Yakshas, उपगीयमानः being praised, समाससाद approached, असुरसैन्यशत्रून् the enemies of the Asura army, चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः holding discus, sword, Sharnga bow, and conch in his hands.
explanation: Praised by Siddhas, Devas, Rishis, great serpents, Gandharvas, and Yakshas, he, holding the discus, sword, Sharnga bow, and conch, approached the enemies of the Asura army.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् । चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं चलोपलं नील इवाचलेन्द्रः ।। 7.6.68 ।।
transliteration: suparṇapakṣānilanunnapakṣaṃ bhramatpatākaṃ pravikīrṇaśastram | cacāla tadrākṣasarājasainyaṃ calopalaṃ nīla ivācalendraḥ || 7.6.68 ||
translation: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं whose wings (of banners) were scattered by the wind from Garuda's wings, भ्रमत्पताकं with fluttering banners, प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् with scattered weapons, चचाल trembled/moved, तत् that, राक्षसराजसैन्यं Rakshasa king's army, चलोपलं with moving rocks, नीलः the blue (mountain), इव like, अचलेन्द्रः the king of mountains.
explanation: That army of the Rakshasa king, with its banners scattered by the wind from Garuda's wings, fluttering flags, and scattered weapons, trembled like a blue mountain king with dislodged rocks.

shloka_text: ततः शरैः शोणितमांसरूषितैर्युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः । निशाचराः सम्परिवार्य माधवं वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.69 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śaraiḥ śoṇitamāṃsarūṣitairyugāntavaiśvānaratulyavigrahaiḥ | niśācarāḥ samparivārya mādhavaṃ varāyudhairnirbibhiduḥ sahasraśaḥ || 7.6.69 ||
translation: ततः then, शरैः with arrows, शोणितमांसरूषितैः smeared with blood and flesh, युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः whose forms were like the fire of cosmic dissolution, निशाचराः the night-wanderers (Rakshasas), सम्परिवार्य having surrounded, माधवं Madhava (Vishnu), वरायुधैः with excellent weapons, निर्बिभिदुः pierced, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: Then, the night-wandering Rakshasas, surrounding Madhava, pierced him by thousands with their excellent weapons, which were smeared with blood and flesh and resembled the destructive fire at the end of an eon. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः ।। 6 ।। Thus ends the sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: नारायणगिरिं ते तु गर्जन्तो राक्षसाम्बुदाः । ववर्षुः शरवर्षेण वर्षेणेवाद्रिमम्बुदाः ।। 7.7.1 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇagiriṃ te tu garjanto rākṣasāmbudāḥ | vavarṣuḥ śaravarṣeṇa varṣeṇevādrimambudāḥ || 7.7.1 ||
translation: नारायणगिरिं towards the mountain Narayana, ते those, तु indeed, गर्जन्तः roaring, राक्षसाम्बुदाः the demon-clouds, ववर्षुः showered, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षेण with rain, इव like, अद्रिम् upon a mountain, अम्बुदाः clouds,
explanation: Those roaring demon-clouds, like actual clouds showering rain upon a mountain, indeed showered a rain of arrows upon the mountain-like Narayana (Vishnu/Rama).
comments: The great battle between Vishnu and the rakshasa host -- withstanding their showers of arrows, Vishnu blows his conch Panchajanya, slays them by thousands and routs their army toward Lanka -- Sumali is whirled from the field by his maddened horses -- Mali fights on, striking Garuda with his mace, until the enraged Vishnu severs Mali's head with his discus -- the gods rejoice, and Sumali and Malyavan flee back to Lanka.

shloka_text: श्यामावदातस्तैर्विष्णुर्नीलैर्नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः । वृतो ऽञ्जनगिरीवासीत् वर्षमाणैः पयोधरैः ।। 7.7.2 ।।
transliteration: śyāmāvadātastairviṣṇurnīlairnaktañcarottamaiḥ | vṛto 'ñjanagirīvāsīt varṣamāṇaiḥ payodharaiḥ || 7.7.2 ||
translation: श्यामावदातः dark-complexioned and radiant, तैः by them, विष्णुः Vishnu, नीलैः by the blue ones, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः by the best of night-wanderers, वृतः surrounded, अञ्जनगिरीवासीत् became like a mountain of collyrium, वर्षमाणैः showering, पयोधरैः by clouds,
explanation: The dark-complexioned and radiant Vishnu, surrounded by those blue, best of night-wanderers, became like a collyrium mountain being showered upon by clouds.

shloka_text: शलभा इव केदारं मशका इव पर्वतम् । यथामृतघटं दंशा मकरा इव चार्णवम् ।। 7.7.3 ।।
transliteration: śalabhā iva kedāraṃ maśakā iva parvatam | yathāmṛtaghaṭaṃ daṃśā makarā iva cārṇavam || 7.7.3 ||
translation: शलभाः locusts, इव like, केदारम् a field, मशकाः mosquitoes, इव like, पर्वतम् a mountain, यथा just as, अमृतघटम् a pot of nectar, दंशाः flies, मकराः crocodiles, इव like, च and, अर्णवम् the ocean,
explanation: Just as locusts swarm a field, mosquitoes a mountain, flies a pot of nectar, and crocodiles the ocean, so too did the arrows approach Hari.

shloka_text: तथा रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ता वज्रानिलमनोजवाः । हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोका इव विपर्यये ।। 7.7.4 ।।
transliteration: tathā rakṣodhanurmuktā vajrānilamanojavāḥ | hariṃ viśanti sma śarā lokā iva viparyaye || 7.7.4 ||
translation: तथा similarly, रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ताः released from the bows of demons, वज्रानिलमनोजवाः having the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, हरिम् into Hari, विशन्ति स्म entered, शराः arrows, लोकाः worlds, इव like, विपर्यये at the time of dissolution,
explanation: Similarly, arrows released from the bows of demons, possessing the speed of lightning, wind, and mind, entered Hari, just as all beings merge into the supreme at the time of cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैः स्यन्दनगता गजैश्च गजपृष्ठगाः । अश्वारोहास्तथाश्वैश्च पादाताश्चाम्बरे स्थिताः ।। 7.7.5 ।।
transliteration: syandanaiḥ syandanagatā gajaiśca gajapṛṣṭhagāḥ | aśvārohāstathāśvaiśca pādātāścāmbare sthitāḥ || 7.7.5 ||
translation: स्यन्दनैः with chariots, स्यन्दनगताः those who went in chariots, गजैः with elephants, च and, गजपृष्ठगाः those who went on elephant-backs, अश्वारोहाः horse-riders, तथा similarly, अश्वैः with horses, च and, पादाताः foot-soldiers, च and, अम्बरे in the sky, स्थिताः standing,
explanation: Those who rode in chariots, those on elephant-backs, horse-riders with their horses, and foot-soldiers, all were positioned in the sky.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रा गिरिनिभाः शरैः शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः । निरुछ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायामा इव द्विजम् ।। 7.7.6 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasendrā girinibhāḥ śaraiḥ śaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ | niruchvāsaṃ hariṃ cakruḥ prāṇāyāmā iva dvijam || 7.7.6 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द्राः demon lords, गिरिनिभाः mountain-like, शरैः with arrows, शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः with spears, lances, and javelins, निरुछ्वासं breathless, हरिं Hari, चक्रुः made, प्राणायामाः breath control exercises, इव like, द्विजम् a brahmin.
explanation: The mountain-like demon lords, using arrows, spears, lances, and javelins, rendered Hari breathless, just as breath control exercises make a brahmin breathless.

shloka_text: निशाचरैस्ताड्यमानो मीनैरिव महोदधिः । शार्ङ्गमायम्य दुर्धर्षो राक्षसेभ्यो ऽसृजच्छरान् ।। 7.7.7 ।।
transliteration: niśācaraistāḍyamāno mīnairiva mahodadhiḥ | śārṅgamāyamya durdharṣo rākṣasebhyo 'sṛjaccharān || 7.7.7 ||
translation: निशाचरैः by night-wanderers, ताड्यमानो being struck, मीनैरिव like by fish, महोदधिः the great ocean, शार्ङ्गम् the Sharnga bow, आयम्य having drawn, दुर्धर्षो the unconquerable one, राक्षसेभ्यो at the demons, असृजत् released, शरान् arrows.
explanation: Being tormented by the night-wanderers like the great ocean by fish, the unconquerable one drew his Sharnga bow and discharged arrows at the demons.

shloka_text: शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्वज्रवक्त्रैर्मनोजवैः । चिच्छेद विष्णुर्निशितैः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.8 ।।
transliteration: śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭairvajravaktrairmanojavaiḥ | ciccheda viṣṇurniśitaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ || 7.7.8 ||
translation: शरैः with arrows, पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैः fully drawn and released, वज्रवक्त्रैः having thunderbolt-like points, मनोजवैः swift as thought, चिच्छेद cut, विष्णुः Vishnu, निशितैः sharp, शतशो by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: With sharp arrows, fully drawn and released, having thunderbolt-like points and swift as thought, Vishnu cut them down by hundreds and then by thousands.

shloka_text: विद्राव्य शरवर्षेण वर्षा वायुरिवोत्थितम् । पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्खं प्रदध्मौ पुरुषोत्तमः ।। 7.7.9 ।।
transliteration: vidrāvya śaravarṣeṇa varṣā vāyurivotthitam | pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhaṃ pradadhmau puruṣottamaḥ || 7.7.9 ||
translation: विद्राव्य having dispersed, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, वर्षा rain, वायुः wind, इव like, उत्थितम् risen, पाञ्चजन्यं the Panchajanya, महाशङ्खं the great conch, प्रदध्मौ blew, पुरुषोत्तमः the best among men.
explanation: Having dispersed the rain of arrows with his own arrows, just as wind disperses rain, the best among men blew his great conch, Panchajanya.

shloka_text: सो ऽम्बुजो हरिणा ध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट् । ररास भीमनिर्हादस्त्रैलोक्यं व्यथयन्निव ।। 7.7.10 ।।
transliteration: so 'mbujo hariṇā dhmātaḥ sarvaprāṇena śaṅkharāṭ | rarāsa bhīmanirhādastrailokyaṃ vyathayanniva || 7.7.10 ||
translation: सः that, अम्बुजः water-born (conch), हरिणा by Hari, ध्मातः blown, सर्वप्राणेन with all his might, शङ्खराट् the king of conches, ररास roared, भीमनिर्हादः with a terrible roar, त्रैलोक्यं the three worlds, व्यथयन् distressing, इव as if.
explanation: That water-born king of conches, blown by Hari with all his might, roared with a terrible sound, as if terrifying the three worlds.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवः सो ऽथ त्रासयामास राक्षसान् । मृगराज इवारण्ये समदानिव कुञ्जरान् ।। 7.7.11 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkharājaravaḥ so 'tha trāsayāmāsa rākṣasān | mṛgarāja ivāraṇye samadāniva kuñjarān || 7.7.11 ||
translation: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, सः that, अथ then, त्रासयामास terrified, राक्षसान् the Rākṣasas, मृगराजः a lion, इव like, अरण्ये in the forest, समदान् maddened, इव like, कुञ्जरान् elephants.
explanation: Then, the sound of the king of conches terrified the Rākṣasas, just as a lion in the forest frightens maddened elephants.

shloka_text: न शेकुरश्वाः संस्थातुं विमदाः कुञ्जराभवन् । स्यन्दनेभ्यश्च्युता वीराः शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः ।। 7.7.12 ।।
transliteration: na śekuraśvāḥ saṃsthātuṃ vimadāḥ kuñjarābhavan | syandanebhyaścyutā vīrāḥ śaṅkharāvitadurbalāḥ || 7.7.12 ||
translation: न not, शेकुः were able, अश्वाः horses, संस्थातुम् to stand still, विमदाः bereft of ichor/strength, कुञ्जराः elephants, अभवन् became, स्यन्दनेभ्यः from their chariots, च्युताः fallen, वीराः warriors, शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः weakened by the conch's sound.
explanation: The horses were unable to stand still, the elephants lost their ichor and strength, and warriors, weakened by the conch's sound, fell from their chariots.

shloka_text: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ता वज्रतुल्याननाः शराः । विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम् ।। 7.7.13 ।।
transliteration: śārṅgacāpavinirmuktā vajratulyānanāḥ śarāḥ | vidārya tāni rakṣāṃsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim || 7.7.13 ||
translation: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, वज्रतुल्याननाः having points like a thunderbolt, शराः arrows, विदार्य tearing apart, तानि those, रक्षांसि Rākṣasas, सुपुङ्खाः with good feathers, विविशुः entered, क्षितिम् the earth.
explanation: Arrows released from the Śārṅga bow, with points like thunderbolts, tore through those Rākṣasas and, with their well-feathered shafts, penetrated the earth.

shloka_text: भिद्यमानाः शरैः सङ्ख्ये नारायणकरच्युतैः । निपेतू राक्षसा भूमौ शैला वज्रहता इव ।। 7.7.14 ।।
transliteration: bhidyamānāḥ śaraiḥ saṅkhye nārāyaṇakaracyutaiḥ | nipetū rākṣasā bhūmau śailā vajrahatā iva || 7.7.14 ||
translation: भिद्यमानाः being pierced, शरैः by arrows, सङ्ख्ये in battle, नारायणकरच्युतैः released from Nārāyaṇa's hand, निपेतू fell, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, भूमौ on the ground, शैलाः mountains, वज्रहताः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like.
explanation: Being pierced by arrows released from Nārāyaṇa's hand in battle, the Rākṣasas fell to the ground like mountains struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: व्रणानि परगात्रेभ्यो विष्णुचक्रकृतानि वै । असृक्क्षरन्ति धाराभिः स्वर्णधारा इवाचलाः ।। 7.7.15 ।।
transliteration: vraṇāni paragātrebhyo viṣṇucakrakṛtāni vai | asṛkkṣaranti dhārābhiḥ svarṇadhārā ivācalāḥ || 7.7.15 ||
translation: व्रणानि wounds, परगात्रेभ्यः from the bodies of the enemies, विष्णुचक्रकृतानि made by Viṣṇu's discus, वै indeed, असृक् blood, क्षरन्ति flowed, धाराभिः in streams, स्वर्णधाराः streams of gold, इव like, अचलाः mountains.
explanation: From the enemies' bodies, wounds made by Viṣṇu's discus indeed streamed blood in torrents, resembling mountains from which streams of gold flow.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवश्चापि शार्ङ्गचापरस्वस्तथा । राक्षसानां रवांश्चापि ग्रसते वैष्णवो रवः ।। 7.7.16 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkharājaravaścāpi śārṅgacāparasvastathā | rākṣasānāṃ ravāṃścāpi grasate vaiṣṇavo ravaḥ || 7.7.16 ||
translation: शङ्खराजरवः the sound of the king of conches, च and, अपि also, शार्ङ्गचापरस्वः the twang of the Śārṅga bow, तथा similarly, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, रवान् sounds, च and, अपि also, ग्रसते devours, वैष्णवः the sound pertaining to Viṣṇu, रवः sound.
explanation: The sound of Viṣṇu's conch and the twang of his Śārṅga bow completely overpower and swallow the roars of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: तेषां शिरोधरान्धूताञ्छरध्वजधनूंषि च । रथान्पताकास्तूणीरांश्चिच्छेद स हरिः शरैः ।। 7.7.17 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ śirodharāndhūtāñcharadhvajadhanūṃṣi ca | rathānpatākāstūṇīrāṃściccheda sa hariḥ śaraiḥ || 7.7.17 ||
translation: तेषाम् their, शिरोधरान् necks, धूतान् severed, शरध्वजधनूंषि arrows, banners, and bows, च and, रथान् chariots, पताकाः flags, तूणीरान् quivers, चिच्छेद cut, सः he, हरिः Hari, शरैः with arrows.
explanation: Hari, with his arrows, severed their necks, and cut down their arrows, banners, bows, chariots, flags, and quivers.

shloka_text: सूर्यादिव करा घोरा ऊर्मयः सागरादिव । पर्वतादिव नागेन्द्रा धारौघा इव चाम्बुदात् ।। 7.7.18 ।।
transliteration: sūryādiva karā ghorā ūrmayaḥ sāgarādiva | parvatādiva nāgendrā dhāraughā iva cāmbudāt || 7.7.18 ||
translation: सूर्यात् from the sun, इव as if, कराः rays, घोराः terrible, ऊर्मयः waves, सागरात् from the ocean, इव as if, पर्वतात् from mountains, इव as if, नागेन्द्राः great elephants, धारौघाः torrents of rain, इव as if, च and, अम्बुदात् from a cloud.
explanation: Just as terrible rays emanate from the sun, waves from the ocean, great elephants from mountains, and torrents of rain from a cloud, so too did arrows emerge.

shloka_text: तथा शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः शरा नारायणेरिताः । निर्धावन्तीषवस्तूर्णं शतशोथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.19 ।।
transliteration: tathā śārṅgavinirmuktāḥ śarā nārāyaṇeritāḥ | nirdhāvantīṣavastūrṇaṃ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ || 7.7.19 ||
translation: तथा similarly, शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः released from the Śārṅga bow, शराः arrows, नारायणेरिताः propelled by Nārāyaṇa, निर्धावन्ति rushed forth, इषवः arrows, तूर्णं swiftly, शतशः by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: Similarly, arrows released from the Śārṅga bow and propelled by Nārāyaṇa rushed forth swiftly by hundreds and thousands.

shloka_text: शरभेण यथा सिंहाः सिंहेन द्विरदा यथा । द्विरदेन यथा व्याघ्रा व्याघ्रेण द्वीपिनो यथा ।। 7.7.20 ।।
transliteration: śarabheṇa yathā siṃhāḥ siṃhena dviradā yathā | dviradena yathā vyāghrā vyāghreṇa dvīpino yathā || 7.7.20 ||
translation: शरभेण by a Śarabha, यथा as, सिंहाः lions, सिंहेन by a lion, द्विरदाः elephants, यथा as, द्विरदेन by an elephant, यथा as, व्याघ्राः tigers, व्याघ्रेण by a tiger, द्वीपिनः leopards, यथा as.
explanation: Just as lions are overcome by a Śarabha, elephants by a lion, tigers by an elephant, and leopards by a tiger, so too were the Rākṣasas overwhelmed.

shloka_text: द्वीपिनेव यथा श्वानः शुना मार्जारका यथा । मार्जारेण यथा सर्पाः सर्पेण च यथा ऽ ऽखवः ।। 7.7.21 ।।
transliteration: dvīpineva yathā śvānaḥ śunā mārjārakā yathā | mārjāreṇa yathā sarpāḥ sarpeṇa ca yathā ' 'khavaḥ || 7.7.21 ||
translation: द्वीपिनेन by a leopard, इव as if, यथा just as, श्वानः dogs, शुना by a dog, मार्जारकाः cats, यथा just as, मार्जारेण by a cat, यथा just as, सर्पाः snakes, सर्पेण by a snake, च and, यथा just as, आखवः mice.
explanation: Just as dogs are afraid of a leopard, cats of a dog, snakes of a cat, and mice of a snake, so too were the rakshasas.

shloka_text: तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । द्रवन्ति द्राविताश्चन्ये शायिताश्च महीतले ।। 7.7.22 ।।
transliteration: tathā te rākṣasāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā | dravanti drāvitāścanye śāyitāśca mahītale || 7.7.22 ||
translation: तथा similarly, ते those, राक्षसाः rakshasas, सर्वे all, विष्णुना by Vishnu, प्रभविष्णुना by the all-powerful, द्रवन्ति flee, द्राविताः put to flight, च and, अन्ये others, शायिताः laid down, च and, महीतले on the ground.
explanation: Similarly, all those rakshasas fled from the all-powerful Vishnu, while others were put to flight or laid dead on the ground.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां सहस्राणि निहत्य मधुसूदनः । वारिजं पूरयामास तोयदं सुरराडिव ।। 7.7.23 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ sahasrāṇi nihatya madhusūdanaḥ | vārijaṃ pūrayāmāsa toyadaṃ surarāḍiva || 7.7.23 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of rakshasas, सहस्राणि thousands, निहत्य having killed, मधुसूदनः Madhusudana, वारिजम् the conch, पूरयामास he blew, तोयदम् a cloud, सुरराट् the king of gods, इव as if.
explanation: Having slain thousands of rakshasas, Madhusudana blew his conch, just as the king of gods (Indra) causes a cloud to thunder.

shloka_text: नारायणशरत्रस्तं शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् । ययौ लङ्कामभिमुखं प्रभग्नं राक्षसं बलम् ।। 7.7.24 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇaśaratrastaṃ śaṅkhanādasuvihvalam | yayau laṅkāmabhimukhaṃ prabhagnaṃ rākṣasaṃ balam || 7.7.24 ||
translation: नारायणशरत्रस्तम् terrified by Narayana's arrows, शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् greatly bewildered by the sound of the conch, ययौ went, लङ्काम् to Lanka, अभिमुखम् facing towards, प्रभग्नम् routed, राक्षसम् rakshasa, बलम् army.
explanation: The routed rakshasa army, terrified by Narayana's arrows and greatly bewildered by the sound of his conch, fled towards Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रभग्ने राक्षसबले नारायणशराहते । सुमाली शरवर्षेण निववार रणे हरिम् ।। 7.7.25 ।।
transliteration: prabhagne rākṣasabale nārāyaṇaśarāhate | sumālī śaravarṣeṇa nivavāra raṇe harim || 7.7.25 ||
translation: प्रभग्ने when routed, राक्षसबले the rakshasa army, नारायणशराहते struck by Narayana's arrows, सुमाली Sumali, शरवर्षेण with a rain of arrows, निववार he obstructed, रणे in battle, हरिम् Hari.
explanation: When the rakshasa army was routed and struck by Narayana's arrows, Sumali, in battle, obstructed Hari with a shower of arrows.

shloka_text: स तु तं छादयामास नीहार इव भास्करम् । राक्षसाः सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः पुनर्धैर्यं समादधुः ।। 7.7.26 ।।
transliteration: sa tu taṃ chādayāmāsa nīhāra iva bhāskaram | rākṣasāḥ sattvasampannāḥ punardhairyaṃ samādadhuḥ || 7.7.26 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, तम् him, छादयामास covered, नीहारः mist, इव like, भास्करम् the sun. राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः endowed with strength, पुनः again, धैर्यम् courage, समादधुः regained.
explanation: He covered him like mist covers the sun, and the Rakshasas, filled with courage, regained their composure.

shloka_text: अथ सो ऽभ्यपतद्रोषाद्राक्षसो बलदर्पितः । महानादं प्रकुर्वाणो राक्षसाञ्जीवयन्निव ।। 7.7.27 ।।
transliteration: atha so 'bhyapatadroṣādrākṣaso baladarpitaḥ | mahānādaṃ prakurvāṇo rākṣasāñjīvayanniva || 7.7.27 ||
translation: अथ then, सः he, अभ्यपतत् rushed towards, रोषात् from anger, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, बलदर्पितः proud of his strength. महानादम् a great roar, प्रकुर्वाणः making, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, जीवयन् enlivening, इव as if.
explanation: Then, that Rakshasa, proud of his strength, rushed forward in anger, making a great roar as if to revive the other Rakshasas.

shloka_text: उत्क्षिप्य लम्बाभरणं धुन्वन्करमिव द्विपः । ररास राक्षसो हर्षात्सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.7.28 ।।
transliteration: utkṣipya lambābharaṇaṃ dhunvankaramiva dvipaḥ | rarāsa rākṣaso harṣātsataḍittoyado yathā || 7.7.28 ||
translation: उत्क्षिप्य lifting up, लम्बाभरणम् his long ornaments, धुन्वन् shaking, करम् his trunk, इव like, द्विपः an elephant. ररास roared, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, हर्षात् from joy, सतडित् with lightning, तोयदः a cloud, यथा just as.
explanation: Lifting his long ornaments and shaking them like an elephant shakes its trunk, the Rakshasa roared with joy, just like a thunderous cloud.

shloka_text: सुमालेर्नर्दतस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । चिच्छेद यन्तुरश्वाश्च भ्रान्तास्तस्य तु रक्षसः ।। 7.7.29 ।।
transliteration: sumālernardatastasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam | ciccheda yanturaśvāśca bhrāntāstasya tu rakṣasaḥ || 7.7.29 ||
translation: सुमालेः of Sumali, नर्दतः roaring, तस्य his, शिरः head, ज्वलितकुण्डलम् with shining earrings. चिच्छेद cut off, यन्तुः of the charioteer, अश्वाः horses, च and, भ्रान्ताः bewildered, तस्य his, तु indeed, रक्षसः of the Rakshasa.
explanation: (He) cut off the head of the roaring Sumali, which was adorned with shining earrings, and the horses of that Rakshasa's charioteer became bewildered.

shloka_text: तैरश्वैर्भ्राम्यते भ्रान्तैः सुमाली राक्षसेश्वरः । इन्द्रियाश्वैः परिभ्रान्तैर्धृतिहीनो यथा नरः ।। 7.7.30 ।।
transliteration: tairaśvairbhrāmyate bhrāntaiḥ sumālī rākṣaseśvaraḥ | indriyāśvaiḥ paribhrāntairdhṛtihīno yathā naraḥ || 7.7.30 ||
translation: तैः by those, अश्वैः horses, भ्रान्तैः bewildered, भ्राम्यते was whirled around, सुमाली Sumali, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas. इन्द्रियाश्वैः by the horses of senses, परिभ्रान्तैः bewildered, धृतिहीनः devoid of steadfastness, यथा just as, नरः a man.
explanation: Sumali, the lord of Rakshasas, was whirled around by those bewildered horses, just as a man devoid of steadfastness is bewildered by the horses of his senses.

shloka_text: ततो विष्णुं महाबाहुं प्रपतन्तं रणाजिरे । हृते सुमालेरश्वैश्च रथे विष्णुरथं प्रति ।। 7.7.31 ।।
transliteration: tato viṣṇuṃ mahābāhuṃ prapatantaṃ raṇājire | hṛte sumāleraśvaiśca rathe viṣṇurathaṃ prati || 7.7.31 ||
translation: ततः then, विष्णुम् Vishnu, महाबाहुम् the mighty-armed, प्रपतन्तम् falling down, रणाजिरे in the battlefield, हृते when taken away, सुमालेः by Sumali, अश्वैः by horses, च and, रथे the chariot, विष्णुरथम् Vishnu's chariot, प्रति towards
explanation: Then, as Vishnu's chariot was carried away by Sumali's horses, the mighty-armed Vishnu was seen falling down in the battlefield.

shloka_text: माली चाभ्यद्रवद्युक्तः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः । मालेर्धनुश्च्युता बाणाः कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः । विविशुर्हरिमासाद्य क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव ।। 7.7.32 ।।
transliteration: mālī cābhyadravadyuktaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ | mālerdhanuścyutā bāṇāḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitāḥ | viviśurharimāsādya krauñcaṃ patrarathā iva || 7.7.32 ||
translation: माली Mali, च and, अभ्यद्रवत् rushed towards, युक्तः ready, प्रगृह्य holding, सशरम् with arrows, धनुः bow, मालेः from Mali's, धनुः bow, च्युताः released, बाणाः arrows, कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः adorned with gold, विविशुः entered, हरिम् Vishnu, आसाद्य reaching, क्रौञ्चम् the Krauncha mountain, पत्ररथाः birds, इव like
explanation: Mali, ready and holding his bow with arrows, rushed towards Vishnu, and the gold-adorned arrows released from his bow pierced Vishnu, just as birds enter the Krauncha mountain.

shloka_text: अर्द्यमानः शरैः सो ऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः । चुक्षुभे न रणे विष्णुर्जितेन्द्रिय इवाधिभिः ।। 7.7.33 ।।
transliteration: ardyamānaḥ śaraiḥ so 'tha mālimuktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ | cukṣubhe na raṇe viṣṇurjitendriya ivādhibhiḥ || 7.7.33 ||
translation: अर्द्यमानः being tormented, शरैः by arrows, सः he (Vishnu), अथ then, मालिमुक्तैः released by Mali, सहस्रशः by thousands, चुक्षुभे न did not become agitated, रणे in battle, विष्णुः Vishnu, जितेन्द्रियः one who has controlled his senses, इव like, अधिभिः by mental anxieties
explanation: Though tormented by thousands of arrows released by Mali, Vishnu remained unagitated in battle, like a person who has controlled his senses is unaffected by mental anxieties.

shloka_text: अथ मौर्वीस्वनं कृत्वा भगवान्भूतभावनः । मालिनं प्रति बाणौघान्ससर्जारिनिषूदनः ।। 7.7.34 ।।
transliteration: atha maurvīsvanaṃ kṛtvā bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ | mālinaṃ prati bāṇaughānsasarjāriniṣūdanaḥ || 7.7.34 ||
translation: अथ then, मौर्वीस्वनम् the twang of the bowstring, कृत्वा making, भगवान् the divine one, भूतभावनः the creator of beings, मालिनम् Mali, प्रति towards, बाणौघान् showers of arrows, ससर्ज released, अरिनिषूदनः the destroyer of enemies
explanation: Then, the divine creator of beings and destroyer of enemies, making the twang of his bowstring, released showers of arrows towards Mali.

shloka_text: ते मालिदेहमासाद्य वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः शराः । पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव सुधारसम् ।। 7.7.35 ।।
transliteration: te mālidehamāsādya vajravidyutprabhāḥ śarāḥ | pibanti rudhiraṃ tasya nāgā iva sudhārasam || 7.7.35 ||
translation: ते those, मालिदेहम् Mali's body, आसाद्य reaching, वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः having the brilliance of thunderbolt and lightning, शराः arrows, पिबन्ति drank, रुधिरम् blood, तस्य his, नागाः serpents, इव like, सुधारसम् nectar
explanation: Those arrows, shining like thunderbolts and lightning, reached Mali's body and drank his blood as if serpents were drinking nectar.

shloka_text: मालिनं विमुखं कृत्वा शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः । मालिमौलिं ध्वजं चापं वाजिनश्चाप्यपातयत् ।। 7.7.36 ।।
transliteration: mālinaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ | mālimauliṃ dhvajaṃ cāpaṃ vājinaścāpyapātayat || 7.7.36 ||
translation: मालिनं Mali, विमुखं facing away, कृत्वा having made, शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः the one holding conch, discus, and mace, मालिमौलिं Mali's crown, ध्वजं banner, चापं bow, वाजिनः horses, च and, अपि also, अपातयत् struck down.
explanation: The wielder of the conch, discus, and mace turned Mali away and then struck down Mali's crown, banner, bow, and horses.

shloka_text: विरथस्तु गदां गृह्य माली नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः । आपुप्लुवे गदापाणिर्गिर्यग्रादिव केसरी ।। 7.7.37 ।।
transliteration: virathastu gadāṃ gṛhya mālī naktañcarottamaḥ | āpupluve gadāpāṇirgiryagrādiva kesarī || 7.7.37 ||
translation: विरथः chariot-less, तु but, गदां mace, गृह्य having taken, माली Mali, नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः the best among night-wanderers, आपुप्लुवे sprang, गदापाणिः mace-in-hand, गिरि mountain, अग्रात् from the peak, इव like, केसरी a lion.
explanation: But Mali, the foremost among night-roaming demons, having lost his chariot, took up his mace and, mace in hand, sprang forward like a lion from a mountain peak.

shloka_text: गदया गरुडेशानमीशानमिव चान्तकः । ललाटदेशे ऽभ्यहनद्वज्रेणेन्द्रो यथा ऽचलम् ।। 7.7.38 ।।
transliteration: gadayā garuḍeśānamīśānamiva cāntakaḥ | lalāṭadeśe 'bhyahanadvajreṇendro yathā 'calam || 7.7.38 ||
translation: गदया with the mace, गरुडेशानं the lord of Garuda, ईशानं Shiva, इव like, च and, अन्तकः Yama, ललाटदेशे on the forehead region, अभ्यहनत् struck, वज्रेण with the thunderbolt, इन्द्रः Indra, यथा as, अचलम् a mountain.
explanation: With his mace, Mali struck the lord of Garuda on the forehead, just as Yama strikes Shiva, or as Indra strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: गदयाभिहतस्तेन मालिना गरुडो भृशम् । रणात्पराङ्मुखं देवं कृतवान्वेदनातुरः ।। 7.7.39 ।।
transliteration: gadayābhihatastena mālinā garuḍo bhṛśam | raṇātparāṅmukhaṃ devaṃ kṛtavānvedanāturaḥ || 7.7.39 ||
translation: गदया by the mace, अभिहतः struck, तेन by him, मालिना by Mali, गरुडः Garuda, भृशम् severely, रणात् from the battle, पराङ्मुखं facing away, देवं the god, कृतवान् made, वेदनातुरः distressed by pain.
explanation: Severely struck by Mali's mace, Garuda, distressed by the pain, caused the god (Vishnu) to turn away from the battle.

shloka_text: पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै । उदतिष्ठन्महाञ्छब्दो रक्षसामभिनर्दताम् ।। 7.7.40 ।।
transliteration: parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai | udatiṣṭhanmahāñchabdo rakṣasāmabhinardatām || 7.7.40 ||
translation: पराङ्मुखे facing away, कृते having been made, देवे the god, मालिना by Mali, गरुडेन by Garuda, वै indeed, उदतिष्ठत् arose, महान् great, शब्दः sound, रक्षसां of the demons, अभिनर्दताम् roaring.
explanation: When the god was indeed made to turn away by Mali (through Garuda), a great roaring sound arose from the exultant demons.

shloka_text: रक्षसां रवतां रावं श्रुत्वा हरिहयानुजः ।। 7.7.41 ।।
transliteration: rakṣasāṃ ravatāṃ rāvaṃ śrutvā harihayānujaḥ || 7.7.41 ||
translation: रक्षसां of the Rākṣasas, रवतां roaring, रावं sound, श्रुत्वा having heard, हरिहयानुजः the younger brother of Harihaya (Indra, i.e., Vishnu).
explanation: Having heard the roaring sound of the Rākṣasas, Vishnu, the younger brother of Indra, reacted.

shloka_text: तिर्यगास्थाय सङ्क्रुद्धः पक्षीशे भगवान्हरिः । पराङ्मुखो ऽप्युत्ससर्ज मालेश्चक्रं जिघांसया ।। 7.7.42 ।।
transliteration: tiryagāsthāya saṅkruddhaḥ pakṣīśe bhagavānhariḥ | parāṅmukho 'pyutsasarja māleścakraṃ jighāṃsayā || 7.7.42 ||
translation: तिर्यगास्थाय having stood obliquely, सङ्क्रुद्धः greatly enraged, पक्षीशे on the lord of birds (Garuda), भगवान् the divine, हरिः Hari (Vishnu), पराङ्मुखो ऽपि even though facing away, उत्ससर्ज released, मालेः at Māli, चक्रं the discus, जिघांसया with the desire to kill.
explanation: The divine Hari, greatly enraged, stood sideways on Garuda and, even while facing away, released his discus at Māli with the intention of killing him.

shloka_text: तत्सूर्यमण्डलाभासं स्वभासा भासयन्नभः । कालचक्रनिभं चक्रं मालेः शीर्षमपातयत् ।। 7.7.43 ।।
transliteration: tatsūryamaṇḍalābhāsaṃ svabhāsā bhāsayannabhaḥ | kālacakranibhaṃ cakraṃ māleḥ śīrṣamapātayat || 7.7.43 ||
translation: तत् that, सूर्यमण्डलाभासं resembling the orb of the sun, स्वभासा with its own radiance, भासयन् illuminating, नभः the sky, कालचक्रनिभं resembling the wheel of time, चक्रं discus, मालेः of Māli, शीर्षम् head, अपातयत् cut off.
explanation: That discus, resembling the sun's orb and illuminating the sky with its own brilliance, and appearing like the wheel of time, severed Māli's head.

shloka_text: तच्छिरो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रोत्कृत्तं बिभीषणम् । पपात रुधिरोद्गारि पुरा राहुशिरो यथा ।। 7.7.44 ।।
transliteration: tacchiro rākṣasendrasya cakrotkṛttaṃ bibhīṣaṇam | papāta rudhirodgāri purā rāhuśiro yathā || 7.7.44 ||
translation: तत् that, शिरो head, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of Rākṣasas, चक्रोत्कृत्तं severed by the discus, बिभीषणम् terrifying, पपात fell, रुधिरोद्गारि gushing blood, पुरा formerly, राहुशिरो Rāhu's head, यथा just as.
explanation: That terrifying head of the king of Rākṣasas, severed by the discus and gushing blood, fell just as Rāhu's head had fallen in ancient times.

shloka_text: ततः सुरैः संसहृष्टैः सर्वप्राणसमीरितः । सिंहनादरवोन्मुक्तः साधु देवेतिवादिभिः ।। 7.7.45 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ suraiḥ saṃsahṛṣṭaiḥ sarvaprāṇasamīritaḥ | siṃhanādaravonmuktaḥ sādhu devetivādibhiḥ || 7.7.45 ||
translation: ततः then, सुरैः by the gods, संसहृष्टैः greatly delighted, सर्वप्राणसमीरितः uttered with all their might, सिंहनादरवः a lion's roar (a mighty shout), उन्मुक्तः released, साधु देव "Well done, O God!", इतिवादिभिः those who said thus.
explanation: Then, the greatly delighted gods, exclaiming "Well done, O God!", uttered a mighty roar with all their might.

shloka_text: मालिनं निहतं दृष्ट्वा सुमाली माल्यवानपि । सबलौ शोकसन्तप्तौ लङ्कामेव प्रधावितौ ।। 7.7.46 ।।
transliteration: mālinaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā sumālī mālyavānapi | sabalau śokasantaptau laṅkāmeva pradhāvitau || 7.7.46 ||
translation: मालिनं Malina, निहतं slain, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सुमाली Sumali, माल्यवानपि and Malyavan also, सबलौ with their forces, शोकसन्तप्तौ tormented by grief, लङ्कामेव to Lanka itself, प्रधावितौ they fled
explanation: Seeing Malina slain, Sumali and Malyavan, along with their armies, were overcome with grief and fled back to Lanka.

shloka_text: गरुडस्तु समाश्वस्तः सन्निवृत्य यथा पुरा । राक्षसान्द्रावयामास पक्षवातेन कोपितः ।। 7.7.47 ।।
transliteration: garuḍastu samāśvastaḥ sannivṛtya yathā purā | rākṣasāndrāvayāmāsa pakṣavātena kopitaḥ || 7.7.47 ||
translation: गरुडस्तु but Garuda, समाश्वस्तः having recovered, सन्निवृत्य having returned, यथा as, पुरा before, राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, द्रावयामास he made to flee, पक्षवातेन by the wind from his wings, कोपितः enraged
explanation: Garuda, having recovered and returned as before, angrily chased away the Rakshasas with the powerful wind generated by his wings.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमला गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः । लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवा मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः ।। 7.7.48 ।।
transliteration: cakrakṛttāsyakamalā gadāsañcūrṇitorasaḥ | lāṅgalaglapitagrīvā musalairbhinnamastakāḥ || 7.7.48 ||
translation: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलाः whose lotus-like faces were severed by the discus, गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः whose chests were crushed by maces, लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवाः whose necks were destroyed by ploughs, मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः whose heads were shattered by pestles
explanation: The Rakshasas had their lotus-like faces severed by the discus, their chests crushed by maces, their necks destroyed by ploughs, and their heads shattered by pestles.

shloka_text: केचिच्चैवासिना छिन्नास्तथान्ये शरपीडिताः । निपेतुरम्बरात्तूर्णं राक्षसाः सागराम्भसि ।। 7.7.49 ।।
transliteration: keciccaivāsinā chinnāstathānye śarapīḍitāḥ | nipeturambarāttūrṇaṃ rākṣasāḥ sāgarāmbhasi || 7.7.49 ||
translation: केचित् some, चैव and indeed, असिना by swords, छिन्नाः cut, तथान्ये similarly others, शरपीडिताः tormented by arrows, निपेतुरम्बरात् fell from the sky, तूर्णं quickly, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, सागराम्भसि into the ocean's waters
explanation: Some Rakshasas were cut down by swords, others were wounded by arrows, and all of them swiftly fell from the sky into the ocean's waters.

shloka_text: नारायणो बाणवराशनीभिर्विदारयामास धनुर्विमुक्तैः । नक्तञ्चरान्मुक्तविधूतकेशान्यथा ऽशनीभिः सतडिन्महाभ्राः ।। 7.7.50 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇo bāṇavarāśanībhirvidārayāmāsa dhanurvimuktaiḥ | naktañcarānmuktavidhūtakeśānyathā 'śanībhiḥ sataḍinmahābhrāḥ || 7.7.50 ||
translation: नारायणो Narayana, बाणवराशनीभिः with excellent arrows like thunderbolts, विदारयामास tore apart, धनुर्विमुक्तैः released from his bow, नक्तञ्चरान् the night-wanderers (Rakshasas), मुक्तविधूतकेशान् whose hair was loose and disheveled, यथा just as, अशनीभिः by thunderbolts, सतडिन्महाभ्राः great clouds with lightning
explanation: Narayana, with excellent arrows released from his bow like thunderbolts, tore apart the night-wandering Rakshasas whose hair was loose and disheveled, just as thunderbolts tear apart great clouds accompanied by lightning.

shloka_text: भिन्नातपत्रं पतमानमस्त्रं शरैरपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् । विनिस्सृतान्त्रं भयलोलनेत्रं बलं तदुन्मत्ततरं बभूव ।। 7.7.51 ।।
transliteration: bhinnātapatraṃ patamānamastraṃ śarairapadhvastavinītaveṣam | vinissṛtāntraṃ bhayalolanetraṃ balaṃ tadunmattataraṃ babhūva || 7.7.51 ||
translation: भिन्नातपत्रं with broken umbrellas, पतमानमस्त्रं with falling weapons, शरैः by arrows, अपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् with proper attire destroyed, विनिस्सृतान्त्रं with intestines gushing out, भयलोलनेत्रं with eyes rolling in fear, बलं the army, तत् that, उन्मत्ततरं more maddened, बभूव became
explanation: The army became utterly frenzied, with their royal canopies shattered, weapons dropping, proper attire torn by arrows, intestines spilling out, and eyes wide with terror.

shloka_text: सिंहार्दितानामिव कुञ्जराणां निशाचराणां सह कुञ्जराणाम् । रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम् ।। 7.7.52 ।।
transliteration: siṃhārditānāmiva kuñjarāṇāṃ niśācarāṇāṃ saha kuñjarāṇām | ravāśca vegāśca samaṃ babhūvuḥ purāṇasiṃhena vimarditānām || 7.7.52 ||
translation: सिंहार्दितानाम् of those tormented by a lion, इव like, कुञ्जराणां of elephants, निशाचराणां of night-rovers (Rakshasas), सह with, कुञ्जराणाम् of elephants, रवाः roars/cries, च and, वेगाः speeds/rushes, च and, समं together/simultaneously, बभूवुः became/occurred, पुराणसिंहेन by the ancient lion, विमर्दितानाम् of those crushed
explanation: The roars and frantic movements of the Rakshasas and their elephants, tormented by the ancient lion, were like those of elephants distressed by a lion.

shloka_text: ते वार्यमाणा हरिबाणजालैः सबाणजालानि समुत्सृजन्तः । धावन्ति नक्तञ्चरकालमेघा वायुप्रभिन्ना इव कालमेघाः ।। 7.7.53 ।।
transliteration: te vāryamāṇā haribāṇajālaiḥ sabāṇajālāni samutsṛjantaḥ | dhāvanti naktañcarakālameghā vāyuprabhinnā iva kālameghāḥ || 7.7.53 ||
translation: ते they, वार्यमाणाः being obstructed/repelled, हरिबाणजालैः by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, सबाणजालानि their own showers of arrows, समुत्सृजन्तः abandoning/throwing away, धावन्ति run, नक्तञ्चरकालमेघाः the Rakshasas, like dark clouds, वायुप्रभिन्नाः scattered by the wind, इव like, कालमेघाः dark clouds
explanation: Those Rakshasas, like dark clouds, were repelled by the showers of arrows from the Vanaras, and abandoning their own arrows, they fled like storm clouds scattered by the wind.

shloka_text: चक्रपहारैर्विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाश्च गदाप्रहारैः । अभिप्रहारैर्द्विविधा विभिन्नाः पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः ।। 7.7.54 ।।
transliteration: cakrapahārairvinikṛttaśīrṣāḥ sañcūrṇitāṅgāśca gadāprahāraiḥ | abhiprahārairdvividhā vibhinnāḥ patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ || 7.7.54 ||
translation: चक्रपहारैः by blows of discus, विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः with severed heads, सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाः with crushed limbs, च and, गदाप्रहारैः by blows of mace, अभिप्रहारैः by various attacks, द्विविधाः in two ways/halves, विभिन्नाः split/torn apart, पतन्ति fall, शैलाः mountains, इव like, राक्षसेन्द्राः Rakshasa lords/chiefs
explanation: The chief Rakshasas, with their heads severed by discus blows, limbs crushed by mace blows, and bodies split in two by various attacks, fell like mountains.

shloka_text: विलम्बमानैर्मणिहारकुण्डलैर्निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः । निपात्यमानैर्ददृशे निरन्तरं निपात्यमानैरिव नीलपर्वतैः ।। 7.7.55 ।।
transliteration: vilambamānairmaṇihārakuṇḍalairniśācarairnīlabalāhakopamaiḥ | nipātyamānairdadṛśe nirantaraṃ nipātyamānairiva nīlaparvataiḥ || 7.7.55 ||
translation: विलम्बमानैः hanging down, मणिहारकुण्डलैः with jewel necklaces and earrings, निशाचरैः by the night-rovers (Rakshasas), नीलबलाहकोपमैः resembling blue clouds, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, ददृशे was seen, निरन्तरं continuously/without gap, निपात्यमानैः being struck down/falling, इव like, नीलपर्वतैः by blue mountains
explanation: The falling Rakshasas, who resembled dark blue clouds and wore dangling jewel necklaces and earrings, were continuously seen falling like blue mountains being struck down. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः ।। 7 ।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: हन्यमाने बले तस्मिन्पद्मनाभेन पृष्ठतः । माल्वान्सन्निवृत्तो ऽथ वेलामेत्य इवार्णवः ।। 7.8.1 ।।
transliteration: hanyamāne bale tasminpadmanābhena pṛṣṭhataḥ | mālvānsannivṛtto 'tha velāmetya ivārṇavaḥ || 7.8.1 ||
translation: हन्यमाने being killed, बले (his) army, तस्मिन् that, पद्मनाभेन by Padmanabha, पृष्ठतः from behind, माल्वान् Malvan, सन्निवृत्तो turned back, अथ then, वेलाम् the shore, एत्य having reached, इव like, अर्णवः the ocean.
explanation: When his army was being struck from behind by Padmanabha, Malvan then turned back, like the ocean reaching its shore.
comments: Malyavan turns back to reproach Vishnu for slaying those who flee, and the two duel with spear and mace until Garuda's wing-wind drives him off -- their leaders slain, the rakshasas abandon Lanka and flee with their wives to Patala -- Agastya declares these Pulastya-line rakshasas mightier than Ravana and hails Rama as the eternal Narayana who incarnates to uphold dharma -- meanwhile Kubera comes to dwell in Lanka.

shloka_text: संरक्तनयनः कोपाच्चलन्मौलिर्निशाचरः । पद्मनाभमिदं प्राह वचनं पुरुषोत्तमम् ।। 7.8.2 ।।
transliteration: saṃraktanayanaḥ kopāccalanmaulirniśācaraḥ | padmanābhamidaṃ prāha vacanaṃ puruṣottamam || 7.8.2 ||
translation: संरक्तनयनः with bloodshot eyes, कोपात् from anger, चलन्मौलिः with a trembling crown, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (demon), पद्मनाभम् to Padmanabha, इदम् this, प्राह spoke, वचनम् word, पुरुषोत्तमम् to the best of men.
explanation: With bloodshot eyes from anger and a trembling crown, the demon spoke these words to Padmanabha, the best of men.

shloka_text: नारायण न जानीषे क्षात्रधर्मं पुरातनम् । अयुद्धमनसो भीतानस्मान्हंसि यथेतरः ।। 7.8.3 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇa na jānīṣe kṣātradharmaṃ purātanam | ayuddhamanaso bhītānasmānhaṃsi yathetaraḥ || 7.8.3 ||
translation: नारायण O Narayana, न not, जानीषे you know, क्षात्रधर्मम् the warrior's duty, पुरातनम् ancient, अयुद्धमनसः those not intent on fighting, भीतान् frightened, अस्मान् us, हंसि you kill, यथा like, इतरः a common person.
explanation: O Narayana, you do not know the ancient duty of a warrior, as you kill us, who are frightened and not intent on fighting, like a common person.

shloka_text: पराङ्मुखवधं पापं यः करोत्यसुरेतरः । स हन्ता न गतः स्वर्गं लभते पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।। 7.8.4 ।।
transliteration: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ pāpaṃ yaḥ karotyasuretaraḥ | sa hantā na gataḥ svargaṃ labhate puṇyakarmaṇām || 7.8.4 ||
translation: पराङ्मुखवधम् killing those who have turned their back, पापम् a sin, यः who, करोति does, असुरेतरः one who is not a demon, सः that, हन्ता killer, न not, गतः gone, स्वर्गम् heaven, लभते obtains, पुण्यकर्मणाम् of those with meritorious deeds.
explanation: Whoever, not being a demon, commits the sin of killing those who have turned their back, that killer does not attain the heaven of those who perform meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: युद्धश्रद्धा ऽथवा ते ऽस्ति शङ्खचक्रगदाधर । 4अहं स्थितो ऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत्तव ।। 7.8.5 ।।
transliteration: yuddhaśraddhā 'thavā te 'sti śaṅkhacakragadādhara | 4ahaṃ sthito 'smi paśyāmi balaṃ darśaya yattava || 7.8.5 ||
translation: युद्धश्रद्धा desire for battle, अथवा or, ते to you, अस्ति is, शङ्खचक्रगदाधर O holder of conch, discus, and mace, अहम् I, स्थितः standing, अस्मि am, पश्यामि I see, बलम् strength, दर्शय show, यत् which, तव your.
explanation: Or if you have a desire for battle, O holder of conch, discus, and mace, I am standing here; show me the strength that is yours.

shloka_text: माल्यवन्तं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् । उवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं तं देवराजानुजो बली ।। 7.8.6 ।।
transliteration: mālyavantaṃ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mālyavantamivācalam | uvāca rākṣasendraṃ taṃ devarājānujo balī || 7.8.6 ||
translation: माल्यवन्तं Malyavan, स्थितं standing, दृष्ट्वा having seen, माल्यवन्तम् Malyavan (mountain), इव like, अचलम् an immovable mountain, उवाच spoke, राक्षसेन्द्रं to the king of Rakshasas, तं him, देवराजानुजः the younger brother of the king of gods, बली the powerful one.
explanation: The powerful younger brother of Indra, seeing Malyavan standing like an immovable mountain, spoke to that king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मया ऽभयम् । राक्षसोत्सादनं दत्तं तदेतदनुपाल्यते ।। 7.8.7 ।।
transliteration: yuṣmatto bhayabhītānāṃ devānāṃ vai mayā 'bhayam | rākṣasotsādanaṃ dattaṃ tadetadanupālyate || 7.8.7 ||
translation: युष्मत्तः from you, भयभीतानां of those terrified, देवानां of the gods, वै indeed, मया by me, अभयम् fearlessness/protection, राक्षसोत्सादनं the destruction of Rakshasas, दत्तं was given, तत् that, एतत् this, अनुपाल्यते is being maintained.
explanation: I indeed granted protection and the destruction of Rakshasas to the gods who were terrified of you, and that promise is now being fulfilled.

shloka_text: प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया । सो ऽहं वो निहनिष्यामि रसातलगतानपि ।। 7.8.8 ।।
transliteration: prāṇairapi priyaṃ kāryaṃ devānāṃ hi sadā mayā | so 'haṃ vo nihaniṣyāmi rasātalagatānapi || 7.8.8 ||
translation: प्राणैः than life, अपि even, प्रियं dear, कार्यं deed/duty, देवानां of the gods, हि indeed, सदा always, मया by me, सः that, अहं I, वः you, निहनिष्यामि will kill, रसातलगतान् even if gone to Rasatala, अपि even.
explanation: Indeed, the welfare of the gods is dearer to me than my own life, and therefore I will kill you all, even if you hide in the lowest netherworld.

shloka_text: देवदेवं ब्रुवाणं तं रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम् । शक्त्या बिभेद सङ्क्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रो भुजान्तरे ।। 7.8.9 ।।
transliteration: devadevaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ raktāmburuhalocanam | śaktyā bibheda saṅkruddho rākṣasendro bhujāntare || 7.8.9 ||
translation: देवदेवं the god of gods, ब्रुवाणं speaking, तं him, रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम् whose eyes were like red lotuses, शक्त्या with a spear, बिभेद pierced, सङ्क्रुद्धः greatly enraged, राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of Rakshasas, भुजान्तरे in the chest.
explanation: The greatly enraged king of Rakshasas pierced the chest of the god of gods, whose eyes were like red lotuses, with a spear as he was speaking.

shloka_text: माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना । हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतह्रदा ।। 7.8.10 ।।
transliteration: mālyavadbhujanirmuktā śaktirghaṇṭākṛtasvanā | harerurasi babhrāja meghastheva śatahradā || 7.8.10 ||
translation: माल्यवत्भुजनिर्मुक्ता released from Malyavan's arm, शक्तिः the spear, घण्टाकृतस्वना making a bell-like sound, हरेः of Hari, उरसि on the chest, बभ्राज shone, मेघस्था situated in a cloud, इव like, शतह्रदा lightning.
explanation: The spear, released from Malyavan's arm with a bell-like sound, shone on Hari's chest like a flash of lightning in a cloud.

shloka_text: ततस्तामेव चोत्कृष्य शक्तिं शक्तिधरप्रियः । माल्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य चिक्षेपाम्बुरुहेक्षणः ।। 7.8.11 ।।
transliteration: tatastāmeva cotkṛṣya śaktiṃ śaktidharapriyaḥ | mālyavantaṃ samuddiśya cikṣepāmburuhekṣaṇaḥ || 7.8.11 ||
translation: ततः then, ताम् एव च that very (weapon) also, उत्कृष्य having drawn out, शक्तिम् the spear, शक्तिधरप्रियः the beloved of the wielder of Shakti (Vishnu), माल्यवन्तम् Malyavan, समुद्दिश्य having aimed at, चिक्षेप threw, अम्बुरुहेक्षणः the lotus-eyed one.
explanation: Then, the lotus-eyed Vishnu, dear to the wielder of Shakti, drew out that very spear and hurled it, aiming at Malyavan.

shloka_text: स्कन्दोत्सृष्टेव सा शक्तिर्गोविन्दकरनिस्सृता । काङ्क्षन्ती राक्षसं प्रायान्माहेन्द्रीवाञ्जनाचलम् ।। 7.8.12 ।।
transliteration: skandotsṛṣṭeva sā śaktirgovindakaranissṛtā | kāṅkṣantī rākṣasaṃ prāyānmāhendrīvāñjanācalam || 7.8.12 ||
translation: स्कन्दोत्सृष्टा इव as if thrown by Skanda, सा शक्तिः that spear, गोविन्दकरनिस्सृता released from Govinda's hand, काङ्क्षन्ती desiring (to strike), राक्षसम् the demon, प्रायात् went, माहेन्द्री इव like Mahendri (Indra's thunderbolt), अञ्जनाचलम् (towards) Anjana mountain.
explanation: That spear, released from Govinda's hand, flew towards the demon as if thrown by Skanda, desiring to strike, just as Indra's thunderbolt strikes the Anjana mountain.

shloka_text: सा तस्योरसि विस्तीर्णे हारभारा ऽवभासिते । अपतद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गिरिकूट इवाशनिः ।। 7.8.13 ।।
transliteration: sā tasyorasi vistīrṇe hārabhārā 'vabhāsite | apatadrākṣasendrasya girikūṭa ivāśaniḥ || 7.8.13 ||
translation: सा that (spear), तस्य his, उरसि on the chest, विस्तीर्णे broad, हारभारावभासिते shining with many necklaces, अपतत् fell, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of demons, गिरिकूट इव like a mountain peak, अशनिः a thunderbolt.
explanation: That spear fell upon the broad chest of the king of demons, which was shining with many necklaces, just as a thunderbolt strikes a mountain peak.

shloka_text: तया भिन्नतनुत्राणः प्राविशद्विपुलं तमः । माल्यवान्पुनराश्वस्तस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः ।। 7.8.14 ।।
transliteration: tayā bhinnatanutrāṇaḥ prāviśadvipulaṃ tamaḥ | mālyavānpunarāśvastastasthau giririvācalaḥ || 7.8.14 ||
translation: तया by that (spear), भिन्नतनुत्राणः with his armor shattered, प्राविशत् entered, विपुलम् deep, तमः darkness (unconsciousness), माल्यवान् Malyavan, पुनराश्वस्तः having regained consciousness again, तस्थौ stood, गिरिः इव like a mountain, अचलः unmoving.
explanation: With his armor shattered by that spear, Malyavan fell into deep unconsciousness, but then regained consciousness and stood unmoving like a mountain.

shloka_text: ततः कार्ष्णायसं शूलं कण्टकैर्बहुभिर्वतम् । प्रगृह्याभ्यहनद्देवं स्तनयोरन्तरे दृढम् ।। 7.8.15 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kārṣṇāyasaṃ śūlaṃ kaṇṭakairbahubhirvatam | pragṛhyābhyahanaddevaṃ stanayorantare dṛḍham || 7.8.15 ||
translation: ततः then, कार्ष्णायसम् made of black iron, शूलम् a spear, कण्टकैः with spikes, बहुभिः many, वतम् covered, प्रगृह्य having seized, अभ्यहनत् struck, देवम् the god, स्तनयोः of the breasts, अन्तरे in the middle, दृढम् firmly.
explanation: Then, seizing a black iron spear covered with many spikes, Malyavan firmly struck the god between his breasts.

shloka_text: तथैव रणरक्तस्तु मुष्टिना वासवानुजम् । ताडयित्वा धनुर्मात्रमपक्रान्तो निशाचरः ।। 7.8.16 ।।
transliteration: tathaiva raṇaraktastu muṣṭinā vāsavānujam | tāḍayitvā dhanurmātramapakrānto niśācaraḥ || 7.8.16 ||
translation: तथैव just so, रणरक्तस्तु indeed eager for battle, मुष्टिना with a fist, वासवानुजम् the younger brother of Vasava (Vishnu), ताडयित्वा having struck, धनुर्मात्रम् a bow's length, अपक्रान्तः retreated, निशाचरः the demon.
explanation: The demon, eager for battle, struck Vishnu (Upendra) with his fist and then retreated a bow's length.

shloka_text: ततो ऽम्बरे महाञ्छब्दः साधुसाध्विति चोदितः । आहत्य राक्षसो विष्णुं गरुडं चाप्यताडयत् ।। 7.8.17 ।।
transliteration: tato 'mbare mahāñchabdaḥ sādhusādhviti coditaḥ | āhatya rākṣaso viṣṇuṃ garuḍaṃ cāpyatāḍayat || 7.8.17 ||
translation: ततः then, अम्बरे in the sky, महान् a great, शब्दः sound, साधुसाध्विति 'well done, well done' thus, चोदितः arose, आहत्य having struck, राक्षसः the demon, विष्णुम् Vishnu, गरुडम् Garuda, च and, अपि also, अताडयत् struck.
explanation: Then a great cry of "well done, well done" arose in the sky as the demon, having struck Vishnu, also struck Garuda.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्ततः क्रुद्धः पक्षवातेन राक्षसम् । व्यपोहद्बलवान्वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयं यथा ।। 7.8.18 ।।
transliteration: vainateyastataḥ kruddhaḥ pakṣavātena rākṣasam | vyapohadbalavānvāyuḥ śuṣkaparṇacayaṃ yathā || 7.8.18 ||
translation: वैनतेयः Garuda, ततः then, क्रुद्धः enraged, पक्षवातेन with the wind from his wings, राक्षसम् the demon, व्यपोहत् blew away, बलवान् powerful, वायुः wind, शुष्कपर्णचयम् a heap of dry leaves, यथा just as.
explanation: Enraged, Garuda then blew away the demon with the powerful wind from his wings, just as a strong wind scatters a heap of dry leaves.

shloka_text: द्विजेन्द्रपक्षवातेन द्रावितं दृश्य पूर्वजम् । सुमाली स्वबलैः सार्धं लङ्कामभिमुखो ययौ ।। 7.8.19 ।।
transliteration: dvijendrapakṣavātena drāvitaṃ dṛśya pūrvajam | sumālī svabalaiḥ sārdhaṃ laṅkāmabhimukho yayau || 7.8.19 ||
translation: द्विजेन्द्र king of birds (Garuda), पक्षवातेन by the wind from the wings, द्रावितम् driven away, दृश्य having seen, पूर्वजम् his elder brother, सुमाली Sumali, स्वबलैः with his own forces, सार्धम् together with, लङ्काम् towards Lanka, अभिमुखः facing, ययौ went.
explanation: Seeing his elder brother (Malyavan) driven away by the wind from Garuda's wings, Sumali, along with his own forces, headed towards Lanka.

shloka_text: पक्षवातबलोद्धूतो माल्यवानपि राक्षसः । स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः ।। 7.8.20 ।।
transliteration: pakṣavātabaloddhūto mālyavānapi rākṣasaḥ | svabalena samāgamya yayau laṅkāṃ hriyā vṛtaḥ || 7.8.20 ||
translation: पक्षवात wind from the wings, बल force, उद्धूतः tossed up, माल्यवान् Malyavan, अपि also, राक्षसः the demon, स्वबलेन with his own forces, समागम्य having rejoined, ययौ went, लङ्काम् towards Lanka, ह्रिया with shame, वृतः overcome.
explanation: Malyavan, the demon who was tossed up by the force of the wing-wind, also rejoined his forces and went towards Lanka, overcome with shame.

shloka_text: एवं ते राक्षसा तेन हरिणा कमलेक्षण । बहुशः संयुगे भग्ना हतप्रवरनायकाः ।। 7.8.21 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ te rākṣasā tena hariṇā kamalekṣaṇa | bahuśaḥ saṃyuge bhagnā hatapravaranāyakāḥ || 7.8.21 ||
translation: एवं thus, ते those, राक्षसाः Rākṣasas, तेन by that, हरिणा Hari (Vishnu), कमलेक्षण O lotus-eyed one, बहुशः many times, संयुगे in battle, भग्नाः defeated, हतप्रवरनायकाः having their chief leaders killed
explanation: O lotus-eyed one, those Rākṣasas were repeatedly defeated in battle by that Hari (Vishnu), having their chief leaders slain.

shloka_text: अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धुं भयार्दिताः । त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः ।। 7.8.22 ।।
transliteration: aśaknuvantaste viṣṇuṃ pratiyoddhuṃ bhayārditāḥ | tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatā vastuṃ pātālaṃ sahapatnayaḥ || 7.8.22 ||
translation: अशक्नुवन्तः being unable, ते they, विष्णुं Vishnu, प्रतियोद्धुं to fight against, भयार्दिताः afflicted by fear, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, लङ्कां Lanka, गताः went, वस्तुं to dwell, पातालं to Pātāla, सहपत्नयः along with their wives
explanation: Being unable to fight against Vishnu and afflicted by fear, they abandoned Lanka and went to dwell in Pātāla along with their wives.

shloka_text: सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुसत्तम । स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे ।। 7.8.23 ।।
transliteration: sumālinaṃ samāsādya rākṣasaṃ raghusattama | sthitāḥ prakhyātavīryāste vaṃśe sālakaṭaṅkaṭe || 7.8.23 ||
translation: सुमालिनं Sumālin, समासाद्य having approached, राक्षसं Rākṣasa, रघुसत्तम O best of Raghu's lineage, स्थिताः remained, प्रख्यातवीर्याः renowned for valor, ते they, वंशे in the lineage, सालकटङ्कटे of Sālakaṭaṅkaṭa
explanation: O best of Raghu's lineage, those Rākṣasas, renowned for their valor, joined the Rākṣasa Sumālin and settled in the lineage of Sālakaṭaṅkaṭa.

shloka_text: ये त्वया निहतास्ते तु पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः । सुमाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः ।।
transliteration: ye tvayā nihatāste tu paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ | sumālī mālyavānmālī ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ ||
translation: ये those who, त्वया by you, निहताः killed, ते those, तु indeed, पौलस्त्याः descendants of Pulastya, नाम named, राक्षसाः Rākṣasas, सुमाली Sumālī, माल्यवान् Mālyavān, माली Mālī, ये those who, च and, तेषां their, पुरःसराः leaders
explanation: The Rākṣasas of the Pulastya lineage whom you killed, O Rama, include Sumālī, Mālyavān, Mālī, and their other leaders.

shloka_text: सर्वे तेभ्यो महाभागा रावणाद्बलवत्तराः ।। 7.8.24 ।।
transliteration: sarve tebhyo mahābhāgā rāvaṇādbalavattarāḥ || 7.8.24 ||
translation: सर्वे all, तेभ्यः than them, महाभागाः O highly fortunate one, रावणात् than Rāvaṇa, बलवत्तराः more powerful
explanation: O highly fortunate one, all of them were more powerful than Rāvaṇa.

shloka_text: न चान्यो राक्षसान्हन्ता सुरारीन्देवकण्टकान् । ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ।। 7.8.25 ।।
transliteration: na cānyo rākṣasānhantā surārīndevakaṇṭakān | ṛte nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam || 7.8.25 ||
translation: न not, च and, अन्यः another, राक्षसान् the Rākṣasas, हन्ता killer, सुरारीन् the enemies of the gods, देवकण्टकान् the tormentors of the gods, ऋते except, नारायणं Nārāyaṇa, देवं the god, शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् who holds the conch, discus, and mace
explanation: No one else can kill the Rākṣasas, who are enemies and tormentors of the gods, except for the god Nārāyaṇa, who holds the conch, discus, and mace.

shloka_text: भवान्नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः । राक्षसान्हन्तुमुत्पन्नो ह्यजेयः प्रभुरव्ययः ।। 7.8.26 ।।
transliteration: bhavānnārāyaṇo devaścaturbāhuḥ sanātanaḥ | rākṣasānhantumutpanno hyajeyaḥ prabhuravyayaḥ || 7.8.26 ||
translation: भवान् You, नारायणः Nārāyaṇa, देवः the god, चतुर्बाहुः four-armed, सनातनः eternal, राक्षसान् the Rākṣasas, हन्तुम् to kill, उत्पन्नः born (manifested), हि indeed, अजेयः unconquerable, प्रभुः lord, अव्ययः imperishable
explanation: You are indeed the eternal, four-armed god Nārāyaṇa, manifested to kill the Rākṣasas, and you are the unconquerable, imperishable lord.

shloka_text: नष्टधर्मव्यवस्थाता काले काले प्रजाकरः । उत्पद्यते दस्युवधे शरणागतवत्सलः ।। 7.8.27 ।।
transliteration: naṣṭadharmavyavasthātā kāle kāle prajākaraḥ | utpadyate dasyuvadhe śaraṇāgatavatsalaḥ || 7.8.27 ||
translation: नष्टधर्मव्यवस्थाता one who re-establishes the lost order of Dharma, काले काले from time to time, प्रजाकरः creator of beings (or protector of subjects), उत्पद्यते is born (manifests), दस्युवधे for the destruction of villains, शरणागतवत्सलः affectionate towards those who seek refuge
explanation: He, who is affectionate towards those who seek refuge, manifests from time to time to re-establish the lost order of Dharma, protect beings, and destroy villains.

shloka_text: एषा मया तव नराधिप राक्षसानामुत्पत्तिरद्य कथिता सकला यथावत् । भूयो निबोध रघुसत्तम रावणस्य जन्मप्रभावमतुलं ससुतस्य सर्वम् ।। 7.8.28 ।।
transliteration: eṣā mayā tava narādhipa rākṣasānāmutpattiradya kathitā sakalā yathāvat | bhūyo nibodha raghusattama rāvaṇasya janmaprabhāvamatulaṃ sasutasya sarvam || 7.8.28 ||
translation: एषा this, मया by me, तव to you, नराधिप O king of men, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, उत्पत्तिः origin, अद्य today, कथिता narrated, सकला complete, यथावत् properly, भूयः further, निबोध understand (listen), रघुसत्तम O best of Raghu's lineage, रावणस्य of Rāvaṇa, जन्मप्रभावम् the power of birth (origin and might), अतुलं incomparable, ससुतस्य along with his sons, सर्वम् all
explanation: O King of men, I have today narrated to you the complete and proper origin of the Rākṣasas; now, O best of Raghu's lineage, listen further to the entire incomparable power and birth of Rāvaṇa along with his sons.

shloka_text: चिरात्सुमाली व्यचरद्रसातलं स राक्षसो विष्णुभयार्दितस्तदा । पुत्रैश्च पौत्रैश्च समन्वितो बली ततस्तु लङ्कामवसद्धनेश्वरः ।। 7.8.29 ।।
transliteration: cirātsumālī vyacaradrasātalaṃ sa rākṣaso viṣṇubhayārditastadā | putraiśca pautraiśca samanvito balī tatastu laṅkāmavasaddhaneśvaraḥ || 7.8.29 ||
translation: चिरात् for a long time, सुमाली Sumālī, व्यचरत् wandered, रसातलं in Rasātala (the netherworld), सः that, राक्षसः Rākṣasa, विष्णुभयार्दितः tormented by fear of Viṣṇu, तदा then, पुत्रैः with sons, च and, पौत्रैः with grandsons, च and, समन्वितः accompanied, बली powerful, ततः then, तु indeed, लङ्काम् to Laṅkā, अवसत् resided (or occupied), धनेश्वरः the lord of wealth (Kubera)
explanation: For a long time, that powerful Rākṣasa Sumālī, tormented by fear of Viṣṇu, wandered in Rasātala accompanied by his sons and grandsons, while the lord of wealth (Kubera) then resided in Laṅkā. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टमः सर्गः ।। 8 ।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य सुमाली नाम राक्षसः । रसातलान्मर्त्यलोकं सर्वं वै विचचार ह ।। 7.9.1 ।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ | rasātalānmartyalokaṃ sarvaṃ vai vicacāra ha || 7.9.1 ||
translation: कस्यचित् of some, तु indeed, अथ then, कालस्य time, सुमाली Sumali, नाम named, राक्षसः demon, रसातलात् from Rasatala (the netherworld), मर्त्यलोकं to the mortal world, सर्वं all, वै indeed, विचचार wandered, ह (an emphatic particle).
explanation: Then, after some time, a demon named Sumali wandered throughout the entire mortal world, having come from Rasatala.
comments: From Patala, Sumali sees Kubera riding the Pushpaka and resolves to raise his line, bidding his daughter Kaikasi wed the sage Vishravas -- approaching him at a dread hour she is granted sons who, owing to the inauspicious time, will be cruel rakshasas, though her last shall be righteous -- she bears the ten-necked Dashagriva (Ravana), Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the virtuous Vibhishana -- spurred by his mother's envy of Kubera, Ravana vows to equal him and departs to perform penance.

shloka_text: नीलजीमूतसङ्काशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः । कन्यां दुहितरं गृह्य विना पद्ममिव श्रियम् ।। 7.9.2 ।।
transliteration: nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśastaptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ | kanyāṃ duhitaraṃ gṛhya vinā padmamiva śriyam || 7.9.2 ||
translation: नीलजीमूतसङ्काशः resembling a dark cloud, तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः wearing earrings of molten gold, कन्यां daughter, दुहितरं (his) daughter, गृह्य taking, विना without, पद्मम् a lotus, इव like, श्रियम् Lakshmi.
explanation: He, resembling a dark cloud and adorned with earrings of molten gold, took his daughter, who was as beautiful as Lakshmi without her lotus.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा विचरन्वै महीतलम् । तदापश्यत्स गच्छन्तं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरम् ।। 7.9.3 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasendraḥ sa tu tadā vicaranvai mahītalam | tadāpaśyatsa gacchantaṃ puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaram || 7.9.3 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of demons, सः he, तु indeed, तदा then, विचरन् wandering, वै indeed, महीतलम् on the earth's surface, तदा then, अपश्यत् saw, सः he, गच्छन्तं going, पुष्पकेण by the Pushpaka (aerial chariot), धनेश्वरम् the lord of wealth (Kubera).
explanation: While the king of demons was wandering on the surface of the earth, he then saw Kubera, the lord of wealth, traveling in the Pushpaka chariot.

shloka_text: गच्छन्तं पितरं द्रष्टुं पुलस्त्यतनयं विभुम् । तं दृष्ट्वा ऽमरसङ्काशं स्वच्छन्दं तपनोपमम् ।। 7.9.4 ।।
transliteration: gacchantaṃ pitaraṃ draṣṭuṃ pulastyatanayaṃ vibhum | taṃ dṛṣṭvā 'marasaṅkāśaṃ svacchandaṃ tapanopamam || 7.9.4 ||
translation: गच्छन्तं going, पितरं father, द्रष्टुं to see, पुलस्त्यतनयं son of Pulastya (Kubera), विभुम् the powerful one, तं him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, अमरसङ्काशं resembling an immortal, स्वच्छन्दं moving freely, तपनोपमम् resembling the sun.
explanation: Having seen him, the powerful son of Pulastya (Kubera), who was going to see his father, resembling an immortal, moving freely, and radiant like the sun.

shloka_text: रसातलं प्रविष्टः सन्मर्त्यलोकात्सविस्मयः । इत्येवं चिन्तयामास राक्षसानां महामतिः ।। 7.9.5 ।।
transliteration: rasātalaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sanmartyalokātsavismayaḥ | ityevaṃ cintayāmāsa rākṣasānāṃ mahāmatiḥ || 7.9.5 ||
translation: रसातलं to Rasatala, प्रविष्टः having entered, सन् being, मर्त्यलोकात् from the mortal world, सविस्मयः with wonder, इति thus, एवं in this manner, चिन्तयामास thought, राक्षसानां of the demons, महामतिः the great-minded one (Sumali).
explanation: Having returned to Rasatala from the mortal world, the great-minded Sumali, filled with wonder, began to ponder in this manner.

shloka_text: किं कृतं श्रेय इत्येवं वर्धेमहि कथं वयम् । अथाब्रवीत्सुतां रक्षः कैकसीं नाम नामतः ।। 7.9.6 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ kṛtaṃ śreya ityevaṃ vardhemahi kathaṃ vayam | athābravītsutāṃ rakṣaḥ kaikasīṃ nāma nāmataḥ || 7.9.6 ||
translation: किं what, कृतं done, श्रेयः good, इति thus, एवं in this manner, वर्धेमहि may we prosper, कथं how, वयम् we, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, सुतां to his daughter, रक्षः the Rakshasa, कैकसीं Kaikasi, नाम named, नामतः by name.
explanation: The Rakshasa then spoke to his daughter, Kaikasi by name, pondering how they might prosper and what good they should do.

shloka_text: पुत्रि प्रदानकालो ऽयं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते । प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः प्रतिगृह्यसे ।। 7.9.7 ।।
transliteration: putri pradānakālo 'yaṃ yauvanaṃ vyativartate | pratyākhyānācca bhītaistvaṃ na varaiḥ pratigṛhyase || 7.9.7 ||
translation: पुत्रि O daughter, प्रदानकालः time for giving in marriage, अयम् this, यौवनं youth, व्यतिवर्तते is passing away, प्रत्याख्यानात् from rejection, च and, भीतैः by those who are afraid, त्वं you, न not, वरैः by suitors, प्रतिगृह्यसे are accepted.
explanation: O daughter, this is the time for your marriage, and your youth is passing; you are not being accepted by suitors, who are afraid of rejection.

shloka_text: त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः । त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके । कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम् ।। 7.9.8 ।।
transliteration: tvatkṛte ca vayaṃ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ | tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sākṣādiva putrike | kanyāpitṛtvaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ mānakāṅkṣiṇām || 7.9.8 ||
translation: त्वत्कृते for your sake, च and, वयं we, सर्वे all, यन्त्रिताः troubled, धर्मबुद्धयः righteous-minded, त्वं you, हि indeed, सर्वगुणोपेता endowed with all virtues, श्रीः goddess of fortune, साक्षात् directly, इव as if, पुत्रिके O daughter, कन्यापितृत्वं fatherhood of a daughter, दुःखं sorrow, हि indeed, सर्वेषां for all, मानकाङ्क्षिणाम् those desiring honor.
explanation: For your sake, all of us, though righteous-minded, are troubled, for you, O daughter, are indeed endowed with all virtues, like the goddess Shri herself; indeed, the fatherhood of a daughter is a sorrow for all who desire honor.

shloka_text: न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति कन्यके ।। 7.9.9 ।।
transliteration: na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṃ varayediti kanyake || 7.9.9 ||
translation: न not, ज्ञायते is known, च and, कः who, कन्यां the daughter, वरयेत् would choose, इति thus, कन्यके O daughter.
explanation: And it is not known, O daughter, who would choose to marry such a maiden.

shloka_text: त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके । मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते । कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति ।। 7.9.10 ।।
transliteration: tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sākṣādiva putrike | mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra caiva pradīyate | kulatrayaṃ sadā kanyā saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati || 7.9.10 ||
translation: त्वं you, हि indeed, सर्वगुणोपेता endowed with all virtues, श्रीः goddess of fortune, साक्षात् directly, इव as if, पुत्रिके O daughter, मातुः of the mother, कुलं family, पितृकुलं father's family, यत्र where, च and, एव indeed, प्रदीयते is given, कुलत्रयं three families, सदा always, कन्या a daughter, संशये in doubt, स्थाप्य having placed, तिष्ठति remains.
explanation: O daughter, you are indeed endowed with all virtues, like the goddess Shri herself; a daughter always keeps three families—her mother's, her father's, and the one to which she is given—in a state of uncertainty.

shloka_text: सा त्वं मुनिवरं श्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम् । भज विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम् ।। 7.9.11 ।।
transliteration: sā tvaṃ munivaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prajāpatikulodbhavam | bhaja viśravasaṃ putri paulastyaṃ varaya svayam || 7.9.11 ||
translation: सा she, त्वं you, मुनिवरं the best of sages, श्रेष्ठं excellent, प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम् born in the lineage of Prajapati, भज resort to, विश्रवसं Vishravas, पुत्रि O daughter, पौलस्त्यं son of Pulastya, वरय choose, स्वयम् yourself.
explanation: O daughter, you yourself should choose and resort to Vishravas, the excellent and best of sages, born in the lineage of Prajapati and son of Pulastya.

shloka_text: ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः । तेजसा भास्करसमो यादृशो ऽयं धनेश्वरः ।। 7.9.12 ।।
transliteration: īdṛśāste bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṃśayaḥ | tejasā bhāskarasamo yādṛśo 'yaṃ dhaneśvaraḥ || 7.9.12 ||
translation: ईदृशाः such, ते your, भविष्यन्ति will be, पुत्राः sons, पुत्रि O daughter, न not, संशयः doubt, तेजसा by splendor, भास्करसमः equal to the sun, यादृशः like whom, अयं this, धनेश्वरः lord of wealth.
explanation: O daughter, without a doubt, your sons will be like this lord of wealth (Kubera), equal to the sun in splendor.

shloka_text: सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्यका पितृगौरवात् । तत्रोपागम्य सा तस्थौ विश्रवा यत्र तप्यते ।। 7.9.13 ।।
transliteration: sā tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kanyakā pitṛgauravāt | tatropāgamya sā tasthau viśravā yatra tapyate || 7.9.13 ||
translation: सा she, तु indeed, तद्वचनं that word, श्रुत्वा having heard, कन्यका the maiden, पितृगौरवात् out of respect for her father, तत्र there, उपागम्य having approached, सा she, तस्थौ stood, विश्रवाः Vishravas, यत्र where, तप्यते was performing penance.
explanation: Having heard that instruction, the maiden, out of respect for her father, approached the place where Vishravas was performing penance and stood there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः । अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः ।। 7.9.14 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare rāma pulastyatanayo dvijaḥ | agnihotramupātiṣṭhaccaturtha iva pāvakaḥ || 7.9.14 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, अन्तरे interval, राम O Rama, पुलस्त्यतनयः son of Pulastya, द्विजः the brahmin, अग्निहोत्रं the fire sacrifice, उपातिष्ठत् performed, चतुर्थः fourth, इव like, पावकः fire.
explanation: O Rama, in the meantime, the brahmin Vishravas, son of Pulastya, performed the Agnihotra ritual, appearing like a fourth sacred fire himself.

shloka_text: अविचिन्त्य तु तां वेलां दारुणां पितृगौरवात् । उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता । विलिखन्ती मुहुर्भूमिमङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण भामिनी ।। 7.9.15 ।।
transliteration: avicintya tu tāṃ velāṃ dāruṇāṃ pitṛgauravāt | upasṛtyāgratastasya caraṇādhomukhī sthitā | vilikhantī muhurbhūmimaṅguṣṭhāgreṇa bhāminī || 7.9.15 ||
translation: अविचिन्त्य not considering, तु indeed, तां that, वेलां time, दारुणां dreadful, पितृगौरवात् out of respect for her father, उपसृत्य having approached, अग्रतः in front of, तस्य his, चरणाधोमुखी with face bowed towards his feet, स्थिता stood, विलिखन्ती scratching, मुहुः repeatedly, भूमिं the ground, अङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण with the tip of her big toe, भामिनी the beautiful woman.
explanation: Disregarding that dreadful time, out of respect for her father, the beautiful maiden approached and stood before him, her face bowed towards his feet, repeatedly scratching the ground with the tip of her big toe.

shloka_text: स तु तां वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । अब्रवीत्परमोदारो दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा ।। 7.9.16 ।।
transliteration: sa tu tāṃ vīkṣya suśroṇīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām | abravītparamodāro dīpyamānāṃ svatejasā || 7.9.16 ||
translation: सः He, तु indeed, ताम् her, वीक्ष्य having seen, सुश्रोणीम् one with beautiful hips, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् one whose face resembles the full moon, अब्रवीत् spoke, परमोदारो the most noble (sage), दीप्यमानाम् shining, स्वतेजसा with her own radiance
explanation: The exceedingly noble sage, having seen her, who had beautiful hips, a face like the full moon, and was shining with her own radiance, spoke to her.

shloka_text: भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता । किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने ।। 7.9.17 ।।
transliteration: bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvamihāgatā | kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetostattvato brūhi śobhane || 7.9.17 ||
translation: भद्रे O auspicious one, कस्यासि whose are you, दुहिता daughter, कुतो from where, वा or, त्वम् you, इह here, आगता have come, किम् what, कार्यम् purpose, कस्य for what, वा or, हेतोः reason, तत्त्वतः truly, ब्रूहि tell, शोभने O beautiful one
explanation: O gentle lady, whose daughter are you, and from where have you come here; O beautiful one, tell me truly what your purpose is or for what reason you are here.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या कृताञ्जलिरथाब्रवीत् । आत्मप्रभावेण मुने ज्ञातुमर्हसि मे मतम् ।। 7.9.18 ।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā kanyā kṛtāñjalirathābravīt | ātmaprabhāveṇa mune jñātumarhasi me matam || 7.9.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ता spoken to, तु indeed, सा she, कन्या the maiden, कृताञ्जलिः having made a respectful gesture with folded hands, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, आत्मप्रभावेण by your own spiritual power, मुने O sage, ज्ञातुम् to know, अर्हसि you ought, मे my, मतम् intention
explanation: Thus addressed, the maiden, having folded her hands, then spoke, saying, "O sage, you are capable of knowing my intention by your own spiritual power."

shloka_text: किं तु मां विद्धि ब्रह्मर्षे शासनात्पितुरागताम् । कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.9.19 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ tu māṃ viddhi brahmarṣe śāsanātpiturāgatām | kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṃ śeṣaṃ tvaṃ jñātumarhasi || 7.9.19 ||
translation: किम् but, तु indeed, माम् me, विद्धि know, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi, शासनात् by the command, पितुः of my father, आगताम् having come, कैकसी Kaikasi, नाम named, नाम्ना by name, अहम् I, शेषम् the rest, त्वम् you, ज्ञातुम् to know, अर्हसि you ought
explanation: "But know me, O Brahmarshi, as one who has come by the command of my father; I am named Kaikasi by name, and you are capable of knowing the rest."

shloka_text: स तु गत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह । विज्ञातं ते मया भद्रे कारणं यन्मनोगतम् ।। 7.9.20 ।।
transliteration: sa tu gatvā munirdhyānaṃ vākyametaduvāca ha | vijñātaṃ te mayā bhadre kāraṇaṃ yanmanogatam || 7.9.20 ||
translation: सः He, तु indeed, गत्वा having gone, मुनिः the sage, ध्यानम् into meditation, वाक्यम् words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed, विज्ञातम् known, ते your, मया by me, भद्रे O auspicious one, कारणम् the reason, यत् which, मनोगतम् residing in the mind
explanation: The sage, having then entered into meditation, spoke these words: "O gentle lady, the reason that was in your mind has been known by me."

shloka_text: सुताभिलाषो मत्तस्ते मत्तमातङ्गगामिनि । दारुणायां तु वेलायां यस्मात्त्वं मामुपस्थिता ।। 7.9.21 ।।
transliteration: sutābhilāṣo mattaste mattamātaṅgagāmini | dāruṇāyāṃ tu velāyāṃ yasmāttvaṃ māmupasthitā || 7.9.21 ||
translation: सुताभिलाषो desire for a son, मत्तः from me, ते your, मत्तमातङ्गगामिनि O you who walk like an intoxicated elephant, दारुणायां terrible, तु indeed, वेलायां at the time, यस्मात् because, त्वं you, माम् me, उपस्थिता approached.
explanation: O you who walk like an intoxicated elephant, since you have approached me at this dreadful time with a desire for a son from me.

shloka_text: शृणु तस्मात्सुतान्भद्रे यादृशाञ्जनयिष्यसि । दारुणान्दारुणाकारान्दारुणाभिजनप्रियान् ।। 7.9.22 ।।
transliteration: śṛṇu tasmātsutānbhadre yādṛśāñjanayiṣyasi | dāruṇāndāruṇākārāndāruṇābhijanapriyān || 7.9.22 ||
translation: शृणु listen, तस्मात् therefore, सुतान् sons, भद्रे O auspicious one, यादृशान् of what kind, जनयिष्यसि you will give birth to, दारुणान् terrible, दारुणाकारान् of dreadful appearance, दारुणाभिजनप्रियान् fond of cruel deeds.
explanation: Therefore, O auspicious one, listen to the kind of sons you will give birth to: they will be terrible, of dreadful appearance, and fond of cruel deeds.

shloka_text: प्रसविष्यसि सुश्रोणि राक्षसान्क्रूरकर्मणः । सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद्वचः ।। 7.9.23 ।।
transliteration: prasaviṣyasi suśroṇi rākṣasānkrūrakarmaṇaḥ | sā tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā praṇipatyābravīdvacaḥ || 7.9.23 ||
translation: प्रसविष्यसि you will give birth to, सुश्रोणि O lady with beautiful hips, राक्षसान् demons, क्रूरकर्मणः of cruel deeds, सा she, तु but, तद्वचनं his words, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रणिपत्य having bowed down, अब्रवीत् spoke, वचः words.
explanation: O lady with beautiful hips, you will give birth to Rakshasas who perform cruel deeds; but she, having heard his words, bowed down and spoke.

shloka_text: भगवन्नीदृशान्पुत्रांस्त्वत्तो ऽहं ब्रह्मवादिनः । नेच्छामि सुदुराचारान्प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.9.24 ।।
transliteration: bhagavannīdṛśānputrāṃstvatto 'haṃ brahmavādinaḥ | necchāmi sudurācārānprasādaṃ kartumarhasi || 7.9.24 ||
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, ईदृशान् such, पुत्रान् sons, त्वत्तः from you, अहं I, ब्रह्मवादिनः O speaker of Brahman, नेच्छामि do not desire, सुदुराचारान् extremely ill-behaved, प्रसादं favor, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: O venerable one, O speaker of Brahman, I do not desire such extremely ill-behaved sons from you; please show me your grace.

shloka_text: कन्यया त्वेवमुक्तस्तु विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । उवाच कैकसीं भूयः पूर्णेन्दुरिव रोहिणीम् ।। 7.9.25 ।।
transliteration: kanyayā tvevamuktastu viśravā munipuṅgavaḥ | uvāca kaikasīṃ bhūyaḥ pūrṇenduriva rohiṇīm || 7.9.25 ||
translation: कन्यया by the maiden, तु indeed, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, तु indeed, विश्रवा Vishrava, मुनिपुङ्गवः foremost among sages, उवाच spoke, कैकसीं to Kaikasi, भूयः again, पूर्णेन्दुः the full moon, इव like, रोहिणीम् to Rohini.
explanation: But Vishrava, the foremost among sages, thus spoken to by the maiden, spoke again to Kaikasi, just as the full moon speaks to Rohini.

shloka_text: पश्चिमो यस्तव सुतो भविष्यति शुभानने । मम वंशानुरूपः स धर्मात्मा च भविष्यति ।। 7.9.26 ।।
transliteration: paścimo yastava suto bhaviṣyati śubhānane | mama vaṃśānurūpaḥ sa dharmātmā ca bhaviṣyati || 7.9.26 ||
translation: पश्चिमो the last one, यः who, तव your, सुतः son, भविष्यति will be, शुभानने O fair-faced one, मम my, वंशानुरूपः suitable to the lineage, सः he, धर्मात्मा righteous-souled, च and, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: O fair-faced one, your last son will be worthy of my lineage and will be righteous.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित् । जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम् ।। 7.9.27 ।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā kanyā rāma kālena kenacit | janayāmāsa bībhatsaṃ rakṣorūpaṃ sudāruṇam || 7.9.27 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ता spoken to, तु indeed, सा that, कन्या maiden, राम O Rama, कालेन by time, केनचित् by some, जनयामास gave birth to, बीभत्सं repulsive, रक्षोरूपं having the form of a Rakshasa, सुदारुणम् very terrible.
explanation: O Rama, that maiden, thus addressed, after some time gave birth to a repulsive and very terrible Rakshasa-shaped child.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवं महादंष्ट्रं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् । ताम्रोष्ठं विंशतिभुजं महास्यं दीप्तमूर्धजम् ।। 7.9.28 ।।
transliteration: daśagrīvaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ nīlāñjanacayopamam | tāmroṣṭhaṃ viṃśatibhujaṃ mahāsyaṃ dīptamūrdhajam || 7.9.28 ||
translation: दशग्रीवं having ten necks, महादंष्ट्रं having great fangs, नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् resembling a heap of blue collyrium, ताम्रोष्ठं having copper-red lips, विंशतिभुजं having twenty arms, महास्यं having a huge mouth, दीप्तमूर्धजम् having blazing hair.
explanation: The child had ten necks, great fangs, resembled a heap of blue collyrium, possessed copper-red lips, twenty arms, a huge mouth, and blazing hair.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्जाते तु तत्काले सज्वालकवलाः शिवाः । क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रमुः ।। 7.9.29 ।।
transliteration: tasmiñjāte tu tatkāle sajvālakavalāḥ śivāḥ | kravyādāścāpasavyāni maṇḍalāni pracakramuḥ || 7.9.29 ||
translation: तस्मिन् when he, जाते was born, तु indeed, तत्काले at that very time, सज्वालकवलाः having mouthfuls of flames, शिवाः jackals, क्रव्यादाः flesh-eaters, च and, अपसव्यानि inauspicious, मण्डलानि circles, प्रचक्रमुः moved around.
