shloka_text: ततो मायां प्रविष्टो ऽसौ राक्षसीं राक्षसेश्वरः । रूपाणां शतसाहस्रं विनाशाय चकार च ।। 7.15.32 ।।
transliteration: tato māyāṃ praviṣṭo 'sau rākṣasīṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ | rūpāṇāṃ śatasāhasraṃ vināśāya cakāra ca || 7.15.32 ||
translation: ततः then, मायाम् illusion, प्रविष्टः entered, असौ that, राक्षसीम् demonic, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas, रूपाणाम् of forms, शतसाहस्रम् a hundred thousand, विनाशाय for destruction, चकार made, च and
explanation: Then, that lord of Rakshasas entered into a demonic illusion and created a hundred thousand forms for destruction.

shloka_text: व्याघ्रो वराहो जीमूतः पर्वतः सागरो द्रुमः । यक्षो दैत्यस्वरूपी च सो ऽदृश्यत दशाननः ।। 7.15.33 ।।
transliteration: vyāghro varāho jīmūtaḥ parvataḥ sāgaro drumaḥ | yakṣo daityasvarūpī ca so 'dṛśyata daśānanaḥ || 7.15.33 ||
translation: व्याघ्रः a tiger, वराहः a boar, जीमूतः a cloud, पर्वतः a mountain, सागरः an ocean, द्रुमः a tree, यक्षः a Yaksha, दैत्यस्वरूपी having the form of a Daitya, च and, सः he, अदृश्यत was seen, दशाननः Dashanana
explanation: Dashanana was then seen in the forms of a tiger, a boar, a cloud, a mountain, an ocean, a tree, a Yaksha, and a Daitya.

shloka_text: बहूनि च करोति स्म दृश्यन्ते न त्वसौ ततः । प्रतिगृह्य ततो राम महदस्त्रं दशाननः ।। 7.15.34 ।।
transliteration: bahūni ca karoti sma dṛśyante na tvasau tataḥ | pratigṛhya tato rāma mahadastraṃ daśānanaḥ || 7.15.34 ||
translation: बहूनि many, च and, करोति स्म was doing, दृश्यन्ते are seen, न not, तु indeed, असौ he (Ravana), ततः from that, प्रतिगृह्य having received, ततो then, राम O Rama, महत् great, अस्त्रम् weapon, दशाननः Ravana.
explanation: Ravana, having received a great weapon, was performing many actions, but he himself was not visible.

shloka_text: जघान मूर्ध्नि धनदं व्याविद्ध्य महतीं गदाम् । एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः ।। 7.15.35 ।।
transliteration: jaghāna mūrdhni dhanadaṃ vyāviddhya mahatīṃ gadām | evaṃ sa tenābhihato vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ || 7.15.35 ||
translation: जघान struck, मूर्ध्नि on the head, धनदम् Kubera, व्याविद्ध्य having whirled, महतीम् great, गदाम् mace, एवम् thus, सः he (Kubera), तेन by him (Ravana), अभिहतः struck, विह्वलः bewildered, शोणितोक्षितः drenched in blood.
explanation: Having whirled a great mace, Ravana struck Kubera on the head, and thus Kubera, bewildered and drenched in blood, was struck by him.

shloka_text: कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः ।। 7.15.36 ।।
transliteration: kṛttamūla ivāśoko nipapāta dhanādhipaḥ || 7.15.36 ||
translation: कृत्तमूलः with roots cut, इव like, अशोकः an Ashoka tree, निपपात fell down, धनाधिपः the lord of wealth (Kubera).
explanation: The lord of wealth, Kubera, fell down like an Ashoka tree whose roots had been cut.

shloka_text: ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स तदा वृतः । धनदोच्छ्वासितस्तैस्तु वनमानीय नन्दनम् ।। 7.15.37 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ padmādibhistatra nidhibhiḥ sa tadā vṛtaḥ | dhanadocchvāsitastaistu vanamānīya nandanam || 7.15.37 ||
translation: ततः then, पद्मादिभिः by Padma and others, तत्र there, निधिभिः by the treasures, सः he (Kubera), तदा then, वृतः surrounded, धनदः Kubera, उच्छ्वासितः revived, तैस्तु by them, वनम् to the forest, आनीय having brought, नन्दनम् Nandana.
explanation: Then, surrounded by the treasures like Padma and others, Kubera was revived by them and brought to the Nandana forest.

shloka_text: निर्जित्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्तं धनदं हृष्टमानसः । पुष्पकं तस्य जग्राह विमानं जयलक्षणम् ।। 7.15.38 ।।
transliteration: nirjitya rākṣasendrastaṃ dhanadaṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ | puṣpakaṃ tasya jagrāha vimānaṃ jayalakṣaṇam || 7.15.38 ||
translation: निर्जित्य having conquered, राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of Rakshasas (Ravana), तम् him, धनदम् Kubera, हृष्टमानसः with a joyful mind, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, तस्य his, जग्राह took, विमानम् aerial chariot, जयलक्षणम् marked by victory.
explanation: Having conquered Kubera, the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, with a joyful mind, took his Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was a symbol of victory.

shloka_text: काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं वैडूर्यमणितोरणम् । मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं सर्वकामफलद्रुमम् ।। 7.15.39 ।।
transliteration: kāñcanastambhasaṃvītaṃ vaiḍūryamaṇitoraṇam | muktājālapraticchannaṃ sarvakāmaphaladrumam || 7.15.39 ||
translation: काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं surrounded by golden pillars, वैडूर्यमणितोरणम् with archways of cat's eye gems, मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं covered with nets of pearls, सर्वकामफलद्रुमम् a wish-fulfilling tree.
explanation: The Pushpaka Vimana was adorned with golden pillars, archways made of cat's eye gems, and covered with nets of pearls, resembling a wish-fulfilling tree that grants all desires.

shloka_text: मनोजवं कामगमं कामरूपं विहङ्गमम् । मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् ।। 7.15.40 ।।
transliteration: manojavaṃ kāmagamaṃ kāmarūpaṃ vihaṅgamam | maṇikāñcanasopānaṃ taptakāñcanavedikam || 7.15.40 ||
translation: मनोजवं swift as thought, कामगमं moving at will, कामरूपं changing form at will, विहङ्गमम् a flying vehicle, मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं with stairs of gems and gold, तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् with platforms of refined gold.
explanation: This flying vehicle was swift as thought, could move and change its form at will, and featured stairs made of gems and gold, along with platforms of refined gold.

shloka_text: देवोपवाह्यमक्षय्यं सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम् । बह्वाश्चर्यं भक्तिचित्रं ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितम् ।। 7.15.41 ।।
transliteration: devopavāhyamakṣayyaṃ sadādṛṣṭimanaḥsukham | bahvāścaryaṃ bhakticitraṃ brahmaṇā parinirmitam || 7.15.41 ||
translation: देवोपवाह्यम a vehicle for gods, अक्षय्यं imperishable, सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम् always pleasing to sight and mind, बह्वाश्चर्यं full of many wonders, भक्तिचित्रं wonderfully adorned, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, परिनिर्मितम् perfectly created.
explanation: This imperishable vehicle, created perfectly by Brahma, was fit for gods, always pleasing to the eyes and mind, and wonderfully adorned with many marvels.

shloka_text: निर्मितं सर्वकामैस्तु मनोहरमनुत्तमम् । न तु शीतं न चोष्णं च सर्वर्तुसुखदं शुभम् ।। 7.15.42 ।।
transliteration: nirmitaṃ sarvakāmaistu manoharamanuttamam | na tu śītaṃ na coṣṇaṃ ca sarvartusukhadaṃ śubham || 7.15.42 ||
translation: निर्मितं created, सर्वकामैस्तु indeed with all desired comforts, मनोहरम captivating the mind, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed, न तु शीतं neither cold, न चोष्णं nor hot, च and, सर्वर्तुसुखदं giving comfort in all seasons, शुभम् auspicious.
explanation: It was an unsurpassed, mind-captivating creation, endowed with all desired comforts, neither cold nor hot, providing pleasantness in all seasons, and truly auspicious.

shloka_text: स तं राजा समारुह्य कामगं वीर्यनिर्जितम् । जितं त्रिभुवनं मेने दर्पोत्सेकात्सुदुर्मतिः ।। 7.15.43 ।।
transliteration: sa taṃ rājā samāruhya kāmagaṃ vīryanirjitam | jitaṃ tribhuvanaṃ mene darpotsekātsudurmatiḥ || 7.15.43 ||
translation: स He, तं that, राजा king (Ravana), समारुह्य having ascended, कामगं moving at will, वीर्यनिर्जितम् conquered by his prowess, जितं conquered, त्रिभुवनं the three worlds, मेने he thought, दर्पोत्सेकात् due to excessive pride, सुदुर्मतिः the very foolish one.
explanation: Having ascended that wish-fulfilling vehicle, which he had conquered by his prowess, the very foolish King Ravana, swollen with excessive pride, believed he had conquered the three worlds.

shloka_text: जित्वा वैश्रवणं देवं कैलासात्समवातरत् ।। 7.15.44 ।।
transliteration: jitvā vaiśravaṇaṃ devaṃ kailāsātsamavātarat || 7.15.44 ||
translation: जित्वा having conquered, वैश्रवणं Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), देवं the god, कैलासात् from Kailasa, समवातरत् descended.
explanation: Having conquered the god Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), he descended from Mount Kailasa.

shloka_text: स्वतेजसा विपुलमवाप्य तं जयं प्रतापवान्विमलकिरीटहारवान् । रराज वै परमविमानमास्थितो निशाचरः सदसि गतो यथानलः ।। 7.15.45 ।।
transliteration: svatejasā vipulamavāpya taṃ jayaṃ pratāpavānvimalakirīṭahāravān | rarāja vai paramavimānamāsthito niśācaraḥ sadasi gato yathānalaḥ || 7.15.45 ||
translation: स्वतेजसा by his own prowess, विपुलम् great, अवाप्य having obtained, तं that, जयं victory, प्रतापवान् the mighty one, विमलकिरीटहारवान् adorned with a spotless crown and necklace, रराज shone, वै indeed, परमविमानम् the excellent aerial chariot, आस्थितः having mounted, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (Rakshasa), सदसि in an assembly, गतः present, यथा like, अनलः fire.
explanation: Having achieved that great victory by his own prowess, the mighty Rakshasa, adorned with a spotless crown and necklace, shone brightly while seated in the excellent aerial chariot, like fire present in an assembly. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः ।। 15 ।। Thus ends the fifteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स जित्वा धनदं राम भ्रातरं राक्षसाधिपः । महासेनप्रसूतिं तद्ययौ शरवणं महत् ।। 7.16.1 ।।
transliteration: sa jitvā dhanadaṃ rāma bhrātaraṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ | mahāsenaprasūtiṃ tadyayau śaravaṇaṃ mahat || 7.16.1 ||
translation: स he, जित्वा having conquered, धनदं the bestower of wealth (Kubera), राम O Rama, भ्रातरं his brother, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas, महासेनप्रसूतिं the birthplace of Mahasena (Kartikeya), तत् that, ययौ went, शरवणं the thicket of reeds, महत् great.
explanation: O Rama, having conquered his brother Kubera, the lord of Rakshasas then went to that great thicket of reeds, the birthplace of Kartikeya.
comments: On Mount Kailasa, where Shiva sports, Ravana's chariot is halted -- Nandi bars his way, and when Ravana mocks his monkey-face, Nandi curses that monkeys will arise to destroy his race -- arrogantly Ravana tries to uproot the mountain, but Shiva pins it with his toe, crushing his arms -- after a thousand years of crying out and praise, Shiva, who names him 'Ravana,' releases him and grants the sword Chandrahasa -- Ravana resumes harassing the kings of the earth.

shloka_text: अथापश्यदृशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं महत् । गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम् ।। 7.16.2 ।।
transliteration: athāpaśyadṛśagrīvo raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat | gabhastijālasaṃvītaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram || 7.16.2 ||
translation: अथ then, अपश्यत् saw, दशग्रीवः Daśagrīva (Ravana), रौक्मं golden, शरवणं the thicket of reeds, महत् great, गभस्तिजालसंवीतं enveloped in a network of rays, द्वितीयम् a second, इव like, भास्करम् sun.
explanation: Then Daśagrīva (Ravana) saw that great golden thicket of reeds, which was enveloped in a network of rays, appearing like a second sun.

shloka_text: स पर्वतं समारुह्य कञ्चिद्रम्यवनान्तरम् । अपश्यत् पुष्पकं तत्र रामविष्टम्भितं तदा ।। 7.16.3 ।।
transliteration: sa parvataṃ samāruhya kañcidramyavanāntaram | apaśyat puṣpakaṃ tatra rāmaviṣṭambhitaṃ tadā || 7.16.3 ||
translation: स he, पर्वतं a mountain, समारुह्य having ascended, कञ्चित् some, रम्यवनान्तरम् having beautiful forest interiors, अपश्यत् saw, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka (aerial chariot), तत्र there, रामविष्टम्भितं stopped by Rama, तदा then.
explanation: Then, having ascended a certain mountain with beautiful forest interiors, he saw the Pushpaka aerial chariot stopped there by Rama.

shloka_text: विष्टब्धं पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा ह्यगमं कामागं कृतम् । अचिन्तयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः सचिवैस्तैः समावृतः ।। 7.16.4 ।।
transliteration: viṣṭabdhaṃ puṣpakaṃ dṛṣṭvā hyagamaṃ kāmāgaṃ kṛtam | acintayadrākṣasendraḥ sacivaistaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ || 7.16.4 ||
translation: विष्टब्धं stopped, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka, दृष्ट्वा having seen, हि indeed, अगमं motionless, कामागं moving at will, कृतम् become, अचिन्तयत् thought, राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of Rakshasas, सचिवैः by ministers, तैः those, समावृतः surrounded.
explanation: Seeing the Pushpaka chariot, which was supposed to move at will, now stopped and motionless, the lord of Rakshasas, surrounded by his ministers, began to ponder.

shloka_text: किन्निमित्तं चेच्छया मे नेदं गच्छति पुष्पकम् । पर्वतस्योपरिष्ठस्य कर्मेदं कस्यचिद्भवेत् ।। 7.16.5 ।।
transliteration: kinnimittaṃ cecchayā me nedaṃ gacchati puṣpakam | parvatasyopariṣṭhasya karmedaṃ kasyacidbhavet || 7.16.5 ||
translation: किन्निमित्तं for what reason, च and, इच्छया by will, मे my, न not, इदं this, गच्छति moves, पुष्पकम् the Pushpaka, पर्वतस्य of the mountain, उपरिष्ठस्य situated above, कर्म deed, इदं this, कस्यचित् of someone, भवेत् might be.
explanation: He wondered why this Pushpaka, which should move according to his will, was not moving, and speculated that this obstruction might be the work of someone on top of the mountain.

shloka_text: ततो ऽब्रवीत्तदा राम मारीचो बुद्धिकोविदः । नेदं निष्कारणं राजन्पुष्पकं यन्न गच्छति ।। 7.16.6 ।।
transliteration: tato 'bravīttadā rāma mārīco buddhikovidaḥ | nedaṃ niṣkāraṇaṃ rājanpuṣpakaṃ yanna gacchati || 7.16.6 ||
translation: ततः then, अब्रवीत् spoke, तदा at that time, राम O Rama, मारीचः Maricha, बुद्धिकोविदः wise, न not, इदं this, निष्कारणं without reason, राजन् O King, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka, यत् which, न not, गच्छति moves.
explanation: Then, at that moment, the wise Maricha spoke, saying, "O King, this Pushpaka chariot does not stop moving without a cause."

shloka_text: अथवा पुष्पकमिदं धनदान्नान्यवाहनम् । अतो निष्पन्दमभवद्धनाध्यक्षविनाकृतम् ।। 7.16.7 ।।
transliteration: athavā puṣpakamidaṃ dhanadānnānyavāhanam | ato niṣpandamabhavaddhanādhyakṣavinākṛtam || 7.16.7 ||
translation: अथवा or, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka, इदं this, धनदात् from Kubera, न not, अन्यवाहनम् another's vehicle, अतः therefore, निष्पन्दम् motionless, अभवत् became, धनाध्यक्षविनाकृतम् deprived of the lord of wealth.
explanation: Alternatively, he suggested that this Pushpaka, being Kubera's vehicle and not meant for anyone else, has become motionless because it is now separated from its true owner, the lord of wealth.

shloka_text: इति वाक्यान्तरे तस्य करालः कृष्णपिङ्गलः । वामनो विकटो मुण्डी नन्दी प्रह्वभुजो बली ।। 7.16.8 ।।
transliteration: iti vākyāntare tasya karālaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ | vāmano vikaṭo muṇḍī nandī prahvabhujo balī || 7.16.8 ||
translation: इति thus, वाक्यान्तरे in the middle of the speech, तस्य his, करालः formidable, कृष्णपिङ्गलः black and tawny, वामनः dwarf, विकटः monstrous, मुण्डी bald-headed, नन्दी Nandi, प्रह्वभुजः with bowed arms, बली powerful.
explanation: Just as Maricha was speaking, a formidable, black and tawny, dwarfish, monstrous, bald-headed, powerful being named Nandi, with bowed arms, appeared.

shloka_text: ततः पार्श्वमुपागम्य भवस्यानुचरो ऽब्रवीत् । नन्दीश्वरो वचश्चेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः ।। 7.16.9 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pārśvamupāgamya bhavasyānucaro 'bravīt | nandīśvaro vacaścedaṃ rākṣasendramaśaṅkitaḥ || 7.16.9 ||
translation: ततः then, पार्श्वम् side, उपागम्य having approached, भवस्य of Bhava (Shiva), अनुचरः attendant, अब्रवीत् spoke, नन्दीश्वरः Nandi, the lord, वचः words, च and, इदम् these, राक्षसेन्द्रम् to the lord of Rakshasas, अशङ्कितः fearless,
explanation: Then, Nandi, the fearless attendant of Shiva, approached the lord of Rakshasas and spoke these words.

shloka_text: निवर्तस्व दशग्रीव शैले क्रीडति शङ्करः । सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् ।। 7.16.10 ।।
transliteration: nivartasva daśagrīva śaile krīḍati śaṅkaraḥ | suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṃ devagandharvarakṣasām || 7.16.10 ||
translation: निवर्तस्व turn back, दशग्रीव O Dashagriva, शैले on the mountain, क्रीडति plays, शङ्करः Shankara, सुपर्णनागयक्षाणाम् of Suparnas, Nagas, and Yakshas, देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् of Devas, Gandharvas, and Rakshasas,
explanation: "Turn back, O Dashagriva, for Shankara is sporting on this mountain, which is inaccessible to Suparnas, Nagas, Yakshas, Devas, Gandharvas, and Rakshasas."

shloka_text: सर्वेषामेव भूतानामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः । इति नन्दिवचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधात्कम्पितकुण्डलः ।। 7.16.11 ।।
transliteration: sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāmagamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ | iti nandivacaḥ śrutvā krodhātkampitakuṇḍalaḥ || 7.16.11 ||
translation: सर्वेषाम् of all, एव indeed, भूतानाम् beings, अगम्यः inaccessible, पर्वतः mountain, कृतः made, इति thus, नन्दिवचः Nandi's words, श्रुत्वा having heard, क्रोधात् from anger, कम्पितकुण्डलः with trembling earrings,
explanation: "This mountain has been made inaccessible to all beings," Nandi declared, and having heard these words, Ravana's earrings trembled with anger.

shloka_text: रोषात्तु ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य सः । को ऽयं शङ्कर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागतः ।। 7.16.12 ।।
transliteration: roṣāttu tāmranayanaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya saḥ | ko 'yaṃ śaṅkara ityuktvā śailamūlamupāgataḥ || 7.16.12 ||
translation: रोषात् from rage, तु indeed, ताम्रनयनः with coppery eyes, पुष्पकात् from the Pushpaka (chariot), अवरुह्य having descended, सः he, कः who, अयम् this, शङ्करः Shankara, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, शैलमूलम् to the base of the mountain, उपागतः approached,
explanation: With eyes reddened by rage, he descended from the Pushpaka chariot, exclaiming, "Who is this Shankara?" and approached the base of the mountain.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यन्नन्दिनं तत्र देवस्यादूरतः स्थितम् । दीप्तं शूलमवष्टभ्य द्वितीयमिव शङ्करम् ।। 7.16.13 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyannandinaṃ tatra devasyādūrataḥ sthitam | dīptaṃ śūlamavaṣṭabhya dvitīyamiva śaṅkaram || 7.16.13 ||
translation: सः he, अपश्यत् saw, नन्दिनम् Nandi, तत्र there, देवस्य of the god (Shiva), अदूरतः not far, स्थितम् standing, दीप्तम् shining, शूलम् trident, अवष्टभ्य holding firmly, द्वितीयम् second, इव like, शङ्करम् Shankara,
explanation: There, not far from Shiva, he saw Nandi standing, firmly holding a shining trident, appearing like a second Shankara himself.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा वानरमुखमवज्ञाय स राक्षसः । प्रहासं मुमुचे तत्र सतोय इव तोयदः ।। 7.16.14 ।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vānaramukhamavajñāya sa rākṣasaḥ | prahāsaṃ mumuce tatra satoya iva toyadaḥ || 7.16.14 ||
translation: तं him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वानरमुखम् monkey-faced, अवज्ञाय having disdained, सः that, राक्षसः demon, प्रहासं a loud laugh, मुमुचे released, तत्र there, सतोयः with water, इव like, तोयदः a cloud.
explanation: That demon, having seen his monkey-face and disdained him, burst into a loud laugh there, like a cloud thundering with water.

shloka_text: तं क्रुद्धो भगवान्नन्दी शङ्करस्यापरा तनुः । अब्रवीत्तत्र तद्रक्षो दशाननमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.16.15 ।।
transliteration: taṃ kruddho bhagavānnandī śaṅkarasyāparā tanuḥ | abravīttatra tadrakṣo daśānanamupasthitam || 7.16.15 ||
translation: तं to him, क्रुद्धः enraged, भगवान् the divine, नन्दी Nandi, शङ्करस्य of Shiva, अपरा another, तनुः form, अब्रवीत् spoke, तत्र there, तद्रक्षः to that demon, दशाननम् to the ten-headed one, उपस्थितम् who was present.
explanation: Enraged, the divine Nandi, who was another form of Shiva, spoke there to that demon Ravana who was present.

shloka_text: यस्माद्वानररूपं मामवज्ञाय दशानन । अशनीपातसङ्काशमपहासं प्रमुक्तवान् ।। 7.16.16 ।।
transliteration: yasmādvānararūpaṃ māmavajñāya daśānana | aśanīpātasaṅkāśamapahāsaṃ pramuktavān || 7.16.16 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, वानररूपं monkey-formed, माम् me, अवज्ञाय having disdained, दशानन O ten-headed one, अशनीपातसङ्काशम् resembling a thunderbolt's fall, अपहासं a loud laugh, प्रमुक्तवान् you have uttered.
explanation: Because, O ten-headed one, you have disdained me, who am in the form of a monkey, and uttered a loud laugh resembling the fall of a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तस्मान्मद्रूपसम्पन्ना मद्वीर्यसमतेजसः । उत्पत्स्यन्ति वधार्थं हि कुलस्य तव वानराः ।। 7.16.17 ।।
transliteration: tasmānmadrūpasampannā madvīryasamatejasaḥ | utpatsyanti vadhārthaṃ hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ || 7.16.17 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, मद्रूपसम्पन्नाः endowed with my form, मद्वीर्यसमतेजसः having might and splendor equal to mine, उत्पत्स्यन्ति will be born, वधार्थं for the purpose of destruction, हि indeed, कुलस्य of the lineage, तव your, वानराः monkeys.
explanation: Therefore, monkeys endowed with my form and possessing might and splendor equal to mine will indeed be born for the destruction of your lineage.

shloka_text: नखदंष्ट्रायुधाः क्रूरा मनःसम्पातरंहसः । युद्धोन्मत्ता बलोद्रिक्ताः शैला इव विसर्पिणः ।। 7.16.18 ।।
transliteration: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāḥ krūrā manaḥsampātaraṃhasaḥ | yuddhonmattā balodriktāḥ śailā iva visarpiṇaḥ || 7.16.18 ||
translation: नखदंष्ट्रायुधाः having nails and fangs as weapons, क्रूराः fierce, मनःसम्पातरंहसः having speed like the flight of thought, युद्धोन्मत्ताः intoxicated with battle, बलोद्रिक्ताः overflowing with strength, शैलाः mountains, इव like, विसर्पिणः moving.
explanation: They will be fierce, with nails and fangs as their weapons, swift as thought, intoxicated with battle, overflowing with strength, and moving like mountains.

shloka_text: ते तव प्रबलं दर्पमुत्सेधं च पृथग्विधम् । व्यपनेष्यन्ति सम्भूय सहामात्यसुतस्य च ।। 7.16.19 ।।
transliteration: te tava prabalaṃ darpamutsedhaṃ ca pṛthagvidham | vyapaneṣyanti sambhūya sahāmātyasutasya ca || 7.16.19 ||
translation: ते they, तव your, प्रबलं mighty, दर्पम् arrogance, उत्सेधं haughtiness, च and, पृथग्विधम् of various kinds, व्यपनेष्यन्ति will remove, सम्भूय having come together, सहामात्यसुतस्य along with your ministers and sons, च and.
explanation: They will unitedly destroy your mighty and diverse arrogance and haughtiness, along with your ministers and sons.

shloka_text: किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं हन्तुं त्वां हे निशाचर । न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः ।। 7.16.20 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ hantuṃ tvāṃ he niśācara | na hantavyo hatastvaṃ hi pūrvameva svakarmabhiḥ || 7.16.20 ||
translation: किं what, तु but, इदानीं now, मया by me, शक्यं possible, हन्तुं to kill, त्वां you, हे O, निशाचर night-wanderer, न not, हन्तव्यो to be killed, हतः killed, त्वं you, हि indeed, पूर्वमेव already, स्वकर्मभिः by your own deeds.
explanation: O night-wanderer, what is possible for me to do to kill you now, for you are not to be killed, as you have already been destroyed by your own actions.

shloka_text: इत्युदीरितवाक्ये तु देवे तस्मिन्महात्मनि । देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता ।। 7.16.21 ।।
transliteration: ityudīritavākye tu deve tasminmahātmani | devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā || 7.16.21 ||
translation: इति thus, उदीरितवाक्ये when the words were spoken, तु indeed, देवे by the god, तस्मिन् by that, महात्मनि great-souled one, देवदुन्दुभयः divine drums, नेदुः sounded, पुष्पवृष्टिः shower of flowers, च and, खात् from the sky, च्युता fell.
explanation: When those words were spoken by that great-souled god, divine drums sounded, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky.

shloka_text: अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं महाबलः । पर्वतं तु समासाद्य वाक्यमाह दशाननः ।। 7.16.22 ।।
transliteration: acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṃ mahābalaḥ | parvataṃ tu samāsādya vākyamāha daśānanaḥ || 7.16.22 ||
translation: अचिन्तयित्वा not considering, सः he, तदा then, नन्दिवाक्यं Nandi's words, महाबलः the mighty one, पर्वतं the mountain, तु but, समासाद्य having approached, वाक्यम् words, आह spoke, दशाननः Dashanana.
explanation: Disregarding Nandi's words, the mighty Dashanana then approached the mountain and spoke.

shloka_text: पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः । तमिमं शैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते ।। 7.16.23 ।।
transliteration: puṣpakasya gatiśchinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ | tamimaṃ śailamunmūlaṃ karomi tava gopate || 7.16.23 ||
translation: पुष्पकस्य of the Pushpaka, गतिः movement, छिन्ना obstructed, यत्कृते because of which, मम my, गच्छतः going, तम् that, इमं this, शैलम् mountain, उन्मूलं uprooted, करोमि I will make, तव your, गोपते O lord of cattle.
explanation: O lord of cattle, I will uproot this mountain, because of which the movement of my Pushpaka chariot has been obstructed while I was going.

shloka_text: केन प्रभावेण भवो नित्यं क्रीडति राजवत् । विज्ञातव्यं न जानीते भयस्थानमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.16.24 ।।
transliteration: kena prabhāveṇa bhavo nityaṃ krīḍati rājavat | vijñātavyaṃ na jānīte bhayasthānamupasthitam || 7.16.24 ||
translation: केन by what, प्रभावेण power, भवो Shiva, नित्यं constantly, क्रीडति plays, राजवत् like a king, विज्ञातव्यं what should be known, न not, जानीते knows, भयस्थानम् place of fear, उपस्थितम् present.
explanation: By what power does Shiva constantly play like a king, not recognizing the imminent danger that should be known?

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा ततो राम भुजान्विक्षिप्य पर्वते । तोलयामास तं शीघ्रं स शैलं समकम्पत ।। 7.16.25 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tato rāma bhujānvikṣipya parvate | tolayāmāsa taṃ śīghraṃ sa śailaṃ samakampata || 7.16.25 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having said, ततो then, राम O Rama, भुजान् arms, विक्षिप्य having spread out, पर्वते on the mountain, तोलयामास he began to lift, तं that, शीघ्रं quickly, स that, शैलं mountain, समकम्पत trembled.
explanation: Having thus spoken, O Rama, (Ravana) spread his arms on the mountain and quickly began to lift it, causing that mountain to tremble.

shloka_text: चालनात्पर्वतस्यैव गणा देवस्य कम्पिताः । चचाल पार्वती चापि तदा ऽ ऽश्लिष्टा महेश्वरम् ।। 7.16.26 ।।
transliteration: cālanātparvatasyaiva gaṇā devasya kampitāḥ | cacāla pārvatī cāpi tadā ' 'śliṣṭā maheśvaram || 7.16.26 ||
translation: चालनात् from the shaking, पर्वतस्य of the mountain, एव indeed, गणाः the attendants, देवस्य of the god (Shiva), कम्पिताः trembled, चचाल trembled, पार्वती Parvati, च and, अपि also, तदा then, आश्लिष्टा having embraced, महेश्वरम् Maheshvara.
explanation: Due to the shaking of the mountain, Shiva's attendants trembled, and Parvati, who was embracing Maheshvara, also trembled then.

shloka_text: ततो राम महादवो देवानां प्रवरो हरः । पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया ।। 7.16.27 ।।
transliteration: tato rāma mahādavo devānāṃ pravaro haraḥ | pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ śailaṃ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā || 7.16.27 ||
translation: ततो then, राम O Rama, महादेवो the great god, देवानां of the gods, प्रवरो the foremost, हरः Hara (Shiva), पादाङ्गुष्ठेन with the big toe, तं that, शैलं mountain, पीडयामास pressed down, लीलया playfully.
explanation: Then, O Rama, the great god Hara, the foremost among the gods, playfully pressed down that mountain with his big toe.

shloka_text: पीडितास्तु ततस्तस्य शैलस्याधोगता भुजाः । विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.16.28 ।।
transliteration: pīḍitāstu tatastasya śailasyādhogatā bhujāḥ | vismitāścābhavaṃstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ || 7.16.28 ||
translation: पीडिताः crushed, तु indeed, ततस् then, तस्य his, शैलस्य of the mountain, अधोगताः went down, भुजाः arms, विस्मिताः astonished, च and, अभवन् became, तत्र there, सचिवाः the ministers, तस्य his, रक्षसः of the demon.
explanation: Indeed, his arms were then crushed beneath the mountain, and the demon's ministers there became astonished.

shloka_text: रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात्तदा । मुक्तो विरावः सहसा त्रैलोक्यं येन कम्पितम् ।। 7.16.29 ।।
transliteration: rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṃ pīḍanāttadā | mukto virāvaḥ sahasā trailokyaṃ yena kampitam || 7.16.29 ||
translation: रक्षसा by the demon, तेन by him, रोषात् from anger, च and, भुजानाम् of the arms, पीडनात् from the pressing, तदा then, मुक्तः released, विरावः a cry, सहसा suddenly, त्रैलोक्यम् the three worlds, येन by which, कम्पितम् was shaken.
explanation: Then, from the anger and the crushing of his arms, that demon suddenly let out a roar by which the three worlds were shaken.

shloka_text: मेनिरे वज्रनिष्पेषं तस्यामात्या युगक्षये । तदा वर्त्मस्थचलिता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः ।। 7.16.30 ।।
transliteration: menire vajraniṣpeṣaṃ tasyāmātyā yugakṣaye | tadā vartmasthacalitā devā indrapurogamāḥ || 7.16.30 ||
translation: मेनिरे they considered, वज्रनिष्पेषम् a thunderbolt's strike, तस्य his, अमात्याः ministers, युगक्षये at the end of an age; तदा then, वर्त्मस्थचलिताः disturbed from their paths, देवाः the gods, इन्द्रपुरोगमाः with Indra as their leader.
explanation: His ministers considered the sound to be a thunderbolt's strike signaling the end of an age, while the gods, led by Indra, were disturbed from their celestial paths.

shloka_text: समुद्राश्चापि सङ्क्षुब्धाश्चलिताश्चापि पर्वताः । यक्षा विद्याधराः सिद्धाः किमेतदिति चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.16.31 ।।
transliteration: samudrāścāpi saṅkṣubdhāścalitāścāpi parvatāḥ | yakṣā vidyādharāḥ siddhāḥ kimetaditi cābruvan || 7.16.31 ||
translation: समुद्राः the oceans, च and, अपि also, सङ्क्षुब्धाः greatly agitated, चलिताः moved, च and, अपि also, पर्वताः the mountains; यक्षाः Yakshas, विद्याधराः Vidyadharas, सिद्धाः Siddhas, किम् what, एतत् is this, इति thus, च and, अब्रुवन् they said.
explanation: The oceans became greatly agitated, the mountains were shaken, and Yakshas, Vidyadharas, and Siddhas all exclaimed, "What is this?"

shloka_text: अथ ते मन्त्रिणस्तस्य विक्रोशन्तमथाब्रुवन् । तोषयस्व महादेवं नीलकण्ठमुमापतिम् ।। 7.16.32 ।।
transliteration: atha te mantriṇastasya vikrośantamathābruvan | toṣayasva mahādevaṃ nīlakaṇṭhamumāpatim || 7.16.32 ||
translation: अथ then, ते those, मन्त्रिणः ministers, तस्य his, विक्रोशन्तम् to the one who was crying out, अथ then, अब्रुवन् they said, तोषयस्व please propitiate, महादेवम् Mahadeva, नीलकण्ठम् the blue-throated one, उमापतिम् the husband of Uma.
explanation: Then his ministers said to him, who was crying out, "Please propitiate Mahadeva, the blue-throated one, the husband of Uma."

shloka_text: तमृते शरणं नान्यं पश्यामो ऽत्र दशानन । स्तुतिभिः प्रणतो भूत्वा तमेव शरणं व्रज ।। 7.16.33 ।।
transliteration: tamṛte śaraṇaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmo 'tra daśānana | stutibhiḥ praṇato bhūtvā tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja || 7.16.33 ||
translation: तम् him, ऋते without, शरणम् refuge, न not, अन्यम् another, पश्यामः we see, अत्र here, दशानन O ten-headed one; स्तुतिभिः with praises, प्रणतः bowed down, भूत्वा having become, तम् him, एव only, शरणम् refuge, व्रज seek.
explanation: "O ten-headed one, we see no other refuge here except him; therefore, having bowed down with praises, seek refuge in him alone."

shloka_text: कृपालुः शङ्करस्तुष्टः प्रसादं ते विधास्यति । एवमुक्तस्तदामात्यैस्तुष्टाव वृषभध्वजम् ।। 7.16.34 ।।
transliteration: kṛpāluḥ śaṅkarastuṣṭaḥ prasādaṃ te vidhāsyati | evamuktastadāmātyaistuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam || 7.16.34 ||
translation: कृपालुः compassionate, शङ्करः Shankara, तुष्टः pleased, प्रसादम् grace, ते to you, विधास्यति will bestow, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तदा then, अमात्यैः by the ministers, तुष्टाव praised, वृषभध्वजम् the one with the bull banner.
explanation: The compassionate Lord Shankara, being pleased, will bestow his grace upon you; thus advised by his ministers, Ravana then praised Lord Shiva.

shloka_text: सामभिर्विविधैः स्तोत्रैः प्रणम्य स दशाननः । संवत्सरसहस्रं तु रुदतो रक्षसो गतम् ।। 7.16.35 ।।
transliteration: sāmabhirvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ praṇamya sa daśānanaḥ | saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu rudato rakṣaso gatam || 7.16.35 ||
translation: सामभिः with hymns, विविधैः various, स्तोत्रैः with praises, प्रणम्य having bowed down, सः he, दशाननः the ten-headed one, संवत्सरसहस्रम् a thousand years, तु indeed, रुदतः of the crying one, रक्षसः of the demon, गतम् passed.
explanation: Having bowed down with various hymns and praises, the ten-headed Ravana spent a thousand years crying and performing penance.

shloka_text: ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाग्रे विष्ठितः प्रभुः । मुक्त्वा चास्य भुजान्राम प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम् ।। 7.16.36 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāgre viṣṭhitaḥ prabhuḥ | muktvā cāsya bhujānrāma prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam || 7.16.36 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रीतः pleased, महादेवः the great god, शैलाग्रे on the peak of the mountain, विष्ठितः situated, प्रभुः the lord, मुक्त्वा having released, च and, अस्य his, भुजान् arms, राम O Rama, प्राह spoke, वाक्यम् words, दशाननम् to the ten-headed one.
explanation: Then, O Rama, the pleased Lord Mahadeva, situated on the mountain peak, released Ravana's arms and spoke to the ten-headed one.

shloka_text: प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव वीर्यस्य शौण्डार्याच्च दशानन । शैलाक्रान्तेन यो मुक्तस्त्वया रावः सुदारुणः ।। 7.16.37 ।।
transliteration: prīto 'smi tava vīryasya śauṇḍāryācca daśānana | śailākrāntena yo muktastvayā rāvaḥ sudāruṇaḥ || 7.16.37 ||
translation: प्रीतः pleased, अस्मि I am, तव your, वीर्यस्य of valor, शौण्डार्यात् of prowess, च and, दशानन O ten-headed one, शैलाक्रान्तेन by the mountain being pressed, यः which, मुक्तः released, त्वया by you, रावः cry, सुदारुणः very terrible.
explanation: O ten-headed one, I am pleased with your valor and prowess, demonstrated by the very terrible cry you released while being crushed by the mountain.

shloka_text: यस्माल्लोकत्रयं चैतद्रावितं भयमागतम् । तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना राजन्भविष्यसि ।। 7.16.38 ।।
transliteration: yasmāllokatrayaṃ caitadrāvitaṃ bhayamāgatam | tasmāttvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā rājanbhaviṣyasi || 7.16.38 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, लोकत्रयम् the three worlds, च and, एतत् this, रावितम् made to cry out, भयम् fear, आगतम् came, तस्मात् therefore, त्वम् you, रावणः Ravana, नाम named, नाम्ना by name, राजन् O king, भविष्यसि will be.
explanation: Because the three worlds were made to cry out and fear came upon them due to your roar, therefore, O king, you shall henceforth be known by the name Ravana.

shloka_text: देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले । एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम् ।। 7.16.39 ।।
transliteration: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale | evaṃ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam || 7.16.39 ||
translation: देवता gods, मानुषा humans, यक्षा yakshas, ये who, च and, अन्ये others, जगतीतले on the earth's surface, एवम् thus, त्वाम् you, अभिधास्यन्ति will call, रावणम् Ravana, लोकरावणम् one who makes the worlds cry.
explanation: Gods, humans, yakshas, and all others on earth will thus call you Ravana, the one who makes the worlds cry.

shloka_text: गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धं पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि । मया चैवाभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम् ।। 7.16.40 ।।
transliteration: gaccha paulastya visrabdhaṃ pathā yena tvamicchasi | mayā caivābhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām || 7.16.40 ||
translation: गच्छ go, पौलस्त्य O son of Pulastya, विस्रब्धम् confidently, पथा by the path, येन by which, त्वम् you, इच्छसि desire, मया by me, च and, एव indeed, अभ्यनुज्ञातः permitted, राक्षसाधिप O king of rakshasas, गम्यताम् you may go.
explanation: O son of Pulastya, O king of rakshasas, go confidently by the path you desire, for you are indeed permitted by me to depart.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशः शम्भुना स्वयमब्रवीत् । प्रीतो यदि महादेव वरं मे देहि याचतः ।। 7.16.41 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu laṅkeśaḥ śambhunā svayamabravīt | prīto yadi mahādeva varaṃ me dehi yācataḥ || 7.16.41 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, लङ्केशः the lord of Lanka, शम्भुना by Shambhu, स्वयम् himself, अब्रवीत् spoke, प्रीतः pleased, यदि if, महादेव O Mahadeva, वरम् a boon, मे to me, देहि give, याचतः who is asking.
explanation: Thus spoken to by Shambhu, the lord of Lanka himself replied, "If you are pleased, O Mahadeva, then grant me a boon as I ask."

shloka_text: अवध्यत्वं मया प्राप्तं देवगन्धर्वदानवैः । राक्षसैर्गुह्यकैर्नागैर्ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः ।। 7.16.42 ।।
transliteration: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ devagandharvadānavaiḥ | rākṣasairguhyakairnāgairye cānye balavattarāḥ || 7.16.42 ||
translation: अवध्यत्वम् invincibility, मया by me, प्राप्तम् obtained, देवगन्धर्वदानवैः from gods, gandharvas, and danavas, राक्षसैः from rakshasas, गुह्यकैः from guhyakas, नागैः from nagas, ये who, च and, अन्ये others, बलवत्तराः more powerful.
explanation: I have already obtained the boon of invincibility against gods, gandharvas, danavas, rakshasas, guhyakas, nagas, and any other more powerful beings.

shloka_text: मानुषान्न गणे देव स्वल्पास्ते मम सम्मताः । दीर्घमायुश्च मे प्राप्तं ब्रह्मणस्त्रिपुरान्तक ।। 7.16.43 ।।
transliteration: mānuṣānna gaṇe deva svalpāste mama sammatāḥ | dīrghamāyuśca me prāptaṃ brahmaṇastripurāntaka || 7.16.43 ||
translation: मानुषान् humans, न not, गणे I count, देव O god, स्वल्पाः insignificant, ते they, मम to me, सम्मताः considered, दीर्घम् long, आयुः life, च and, मे by me, प्राप्तम् obtained, ब्रह्मणः from Brahma, त्रिपुरान्तक O destroyer of Tripura.
explanation: O god, I do not count humans, as they are considered insignificant by me; and O destroyer of Tripura, I have already obtained a long life from Brahma.

shloka_text: वाञ्छितं चायुषः शेषं शस्त्रं त्वं च प्रयच्छ मे । एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन रावणेन स शङ्करः ।। 7.16.44 ।।
transliteration: vāñchitaṃ cāyuṣaḥ śeṣaṃ śastraṃ tvaṃ ca prayaccha me | evamuktastatastena rāvaṇena sa śaṅkaraḥ || 7.16.44 ||
translation: वाञ्छितं desired, च and, आयुषः of life, शेषं remaining part, शस्त्रं weapon, त्वं you, च and, प्रयच्छ give, मे to me, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, ततः then, तेन by him, रावणेन by Ravana, सः that, शङ्करः Shankara.
explanation: Ravana thus requested Lord Shankara to grant him his desired remaining lifespan and a weapon.

shloka_text: ददौ खड्गं महादीप्तं चन्द्रहासमिति श्रुतम् । आयुषश्चावशेषं च स्थित्वा भूतपतिस्तदा ।। 7.16.45 ।।
transliteration: dadau khaḍgaṃ mahādīptaṃ candrahāsamiti śrutam | āyuṣaścāvaśeṣaṃ ca sthitvā bhūtapatistadā || 7.16.45 ||
translation: ददौ gave, खड्गं sword, महादीप्तं greatly radiant, चन्द्रहासम् Chandrahāsa, इति thus, श्रुतम् known, आयुषः of life, च and, अवशेषं remainder, च and, स्थित्वा having granted, भूतपतिः Lord of beings, तदा then.
explanation: Then, Lord Shiva, the lord of beings, granted him the greatly radiant sword known as Chandrahāsa, and also the remainder of his life.

shloka_text: दत्त्वोवाच ततः शम्भुर्नावज्ञेयमिदं त्वया । अवज्ञातं यदि हि ते मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ।। 7.16.46 ।।
transliteration: dattvovāca tataḥ śambhurnāvajñeyamidaṃ tvayā | avajñātaṃ yadi hi te māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ || 7.16.46 ||
translation: दत्त्वा having given, उवाच said, ततः then, शम्भुः Shambhu, न not, अवज्ञेयम् to be disregarded, इदं this, त्वया by you, अवज्ञातं disregarded, यदि if, हि indeed, ते by you, माम् to me, एव indeed, एष्यति will come, असंशयः without doubt.
explanation: Having given it, Shambhu then said, "This (sword) is not to be disrespected by you; if it is indeed disregarded by you, it will undoubtedly return to me."

shloka_text: एवं महेश्वरेणैव कृतनामा स रावणः । अभिवाद्य महादेवमारुरोहाथ पुष्पकम् ।। 7.16.47 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ maheśvareṇaiva kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ | abhivādya mahādevamārurohātha puṣpakam || 7.16.47 ||
translation: एवम् thus, महेश्वरेण by Maheśvara, एव indeed, कृतनामा one whose name was made, सः that, रावणः Ravana, अभिवाद्य having saluted, महादेवम् Mahadeva, आरुरोह ascended, अथ then, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka.
explanation: Thus, Ravana, whose name was indeed established by Maheśvara, then saluted Mahadeva and ascended the Pushpaka chariot.

shloka_text: ततो महीतले राम पर्यक्रामत रावणः । क्षत्ऺित्रयान्सुमहावीर्यान्बाधमान इतस्ततः ।। 7.16.48 ।।
transliteration: tato mahītale rāma paryakrāmata rāvaṇaḥ | kṣatऺ्itrayānsumahāvīryānbādhamāna itastataḥ || 7.16.48 ||
translation: ततः then, महीतले on the earth's surface, राम O Rama, पर्यक्रामत roamed about, रावणः Ravana, क्षत्ऺित्रयान् Kshatriyas, सुमहावीर्यान् very mighty, बाधमानः harassing, इतस्ततः here and there.
explanation: Then, O Rama, Ravana roamed about on the earth's surface, harassing very mighty Kshatriyas here and there.

shloka_text: केचित्तेजस्विनः शूराः क्षत्ऺित्रया युद्धदुर्मदाः । तच्छासनमकुर्वन्तो विनेशुः सपरिच्छदाः ।। 7.16.49 ।।
transliteration: kecittejasvinaḥ śūrāḥ kṣatऺ्itrayā yuddhadurmadāḥ | tacchāsanamakurvanto vineśuḥ saparicchadāḥ || 7.16.49 ||
translation: केचित् some, तेजस्विनः powerful, शूराः brave, क्षत्ऺित्रया Kshatriyas, युद्धदुर्मदाः unyielding in battle, तच्छासनम् his command, अकुर्वन्तः not obeying, विनेशुः perished, सपरिच्छदाः along with their retinue.
explanation: Some powerful and brave Kshatriyas, unyielding in battle, who disobeyed his command, perished along with their retinue.

shloka_text: अपरे दुर्जयं रक्षो जानन्तः प्राज्ञसम्मताः । जिताः स्म इत्यभाषन्त राक्षसं बलदर्पितम् ।। 7.16.50 ।।
transliteration: apare durjayaṃ rakṣo jānantaḥ prājñasammatāḥ | jitāḥ sma ityabhāṣanta rākṣasaṃ baladarpitam || 7.16.50 ||
translation: अपरे others, दुर्जयम् unconquerable, रक्षो Rakshasa, जानन्तः knowing, प्राज्ञसम्मताः approved by the wise, जिताः स्म we are conquered, इति thus, अभाषन्त they spoke, राक्षसम् to the Rakshasa, बलदर्पितम् proud of his strength.
explanation: Others, knowing the Rakshasa to be unconquerable and being considered wise, declared to the strength-proud Rakshasa, "We are conquered.". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः ।। 16 ।। Thus ends the sixteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ राजन्महाबाहुर्विचरन्स महीतले । हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः ।। 7.17.1 ।।
transliteration: atha rājanmahābāhurvicaransa mahītale | himavadvanamāsādya paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ || 7.17.1 ||
translation: अथ then, राजन् O King, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, विचरण्स wandering, महीतले on the earth, हिमवद्वनम् the forest of the Himalayas, आसाद्य reaching, परिचक्राम roamed, रावणः Ravana.
explanation: Then, O King, the mighty-armed Ravana, wandering on the earth, reached the Himalayan forest and roamed there.
comments: Ravana finds the ascetic maiden Vedavati, daughter of the brahmin Kushadhvaja, who is vowed to win Vishnu as her husband -- when Ravana woos her and insults her by seizing her hair, she shears it off, enters the fire, and curses that she will be reborn for his destruction -- Agastya reveals that she was reborn as Sita, sprung from the furrow, to bring about Ravana's death.

shloka_text: तत्रापश्यत्स वै कन्यां कृष्णाजिनजटाधराम् । आर्षेण विधिना युक्तां दीप्यन्तीं देवतामिव ।। 7.17.2 ।।
transliteration: tatrāpaśyatsa vai kanyāṃ kṛṣṇājinajaṭādharām | ārṣeṇa vidhinā yuktāṃ dīpyantīṃ devatāmiva || 7.17.2 ||
translation: तत्र there, अपश्यत् he saw, स he, वै indeed, कन्याम् a maiden, कृष्णाजिनजटाधराम् wearing a black deer-skin and matted hair, आर्षेण ascetic's, विधिना practice, युक्ताम् engaged in, दीप्यन्तीम् shining, देवतामिव like a goddess.
explanation: There he indeed saw a maiden, wearing a black deer-skin and matted hair, engaged in ascetic practices, shining like a goddess.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम् । काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव ।। 7.17.3 ।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā rūpasampannāṃ kanyāṃ tāṃ sumahāvratām | kāmamohaparītātmā papraccha prahasanniva || 7.17.3 ||
translation: स he, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रूपसम्पन्नाम् endowed with beauty, कन्याम् maiden, ताम् that, सुमहाव्रताम् observing great vows, काममोहपरीतात्मा whose mind was overcome by the delusion of desire, पप्रच्छ he asked, प्रहसन्निव as if laughing.
explanation: Having seen that beautiful maiden observing great vows, he, whose mind was overcome by the delusion of desire, asked her as if with a smile.

shloka_text: किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते । नहि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्यैव प्रतिक्रिया ।। 7.17.4 ।।
transliteration: kimidaṃ vartase bhadre viruddhaṃ yauvanasya te | nahi yuktā tavaitasya rūpasyaiva pratikriyā || 7.17.4 ||
translation: किम् what, इदम् this, वर्तसे you are doing, भद्रे O auspicious one, विरुद्धम् contrary, यौवनस्य to youth, ते your, नहि indeed not, युक्ता suitable, तव for your, एतस्य this, रूपस्य beauty, एव indeed, प्रतिक्रिया action/conduct
explanation: O gentle lady, what is this conduct of yours, which is contrary to your youth, for such actions are indeed not suitable for your beauty.

shloka_text: रूपं ते ऽनुपमं भीरु कामोन्मादकरं नृणाम् । न युक्तं तपसि स्थातुं निर्गतो ह्येष निर्णयः ।। 7.17.5 ।।
transliteration: rūpaṃ te 'nupamaṃ bhīru kāmonmādakaraṃ nṛṇām | na yuktaṃ tapasi sthātuṃ nirgato hyeṣa nirṇayaḥ || 7.17.5 ||
translation: रूपम् beauty, ते your, अनुपमम् incomparable, भीरु O timid one, कामोन्मादकरम् causing infatuation of desire, नृणाम् for men, न not, युक्तम् suitable, तपसि in penance, स्थातुम् to stay, निर्गतः has come out/is established, हि indeed, एषः this, निर्णयः conclusion
explanation: O timid one, your incomparable beauty, which incites desire and madness in men, is not suitable for ascetic practices, for this is indeed a well-established conclusion.

shloka_text: कस्यासि किमिदं भद्रे कश्च भर्ता वरानने । येन सम्भुज्यसे भीरु स नरः पुण्यभाग्भुवि ।। 7.17.6 ।।
transliteration: kasyāsi kimidaṃ bhadre kaśca bhartā varānane | yena sambhujyase bhīru sa naraḥ puṇyabhāgbhuvi || 7.17.6 ||
translation: कस्याः whose, असि you are, किम् what, इदम् this (activity), भद्रे O gentle lady, कः who, च and, भर्ता husband, वरानने O beautiful-faced one, येन by whom, सम्भुज्यसे you are enjoyed/possessed, भीरु O timid one, सः that, नरः man, पुण्यभाक् fortunate, भुवि on earth
explanation: O gentle lady, whose are you, and what is this activity; O beautiful-faced one, who is your husband, for the man by whom you are enjoyed, O timid one, is indeed fortunate on this earth.

shloka_text: पृच्छतः शंस मे सर्वं कस्य हेतोः परिश्रमः । एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या रावणेन यशस्विनी ।। 7.17.7 ।।
transliteration: pṛcchataḥ śaṃsa me sarvaṃ kasya hetoḥ pariśramaḥ | evamuktā tu sā kanyā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī || 7.17.7 ||
translation: पृच्छतः to me who asks, शंस tell, मे me, सर्वम् everything, कस्य for what, हेतोः reason, परिश्रमः effort/exertion (here, penance), एवम् thus, उक्ता spoken to, तु then, सा that, कन्या maiden, रावणेन by Ravana, यशस्विनी glorious
explanation: Tell me everything, who am asking, for what reason is this exertion; thus spoken to by Ravana, that glorious maiden then replied.

shloka_text: कुशध्वजो मम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिरमितप्रभः । बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान्बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः ।। 7.17.8 ।।
transliteration: kuśadhvajo mama pitā brahmarṣiramitaprabhaḥ | bṛhaspatisutaḥ śrīmānbuddhyā tulyo bṛhaspateḥ || 7.17.8 ||
translation: कुशध्वजः Kushadhvaja, मम my, पिता father, ब्रह्मर्षिः a Brahmarshi, अमितप्रभः of immeasurable splendor, बृहस्पतिसुतः son of Brihaspati, श्रीमान् glorious, बुद्ध्या in intellect, तुल्यः equal, बृहस्पतेः to Brihaspati
explanation: My father is Kushadhvaja, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, the glorious son of Brihaspati, and equal to Brihaspati in intellect.

shloka_text: तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः । सम्भूय वाङ्मयी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता ।। 7.17.9 ।।
transliteration: tasyāhaṃ kurvato nityaṃ vedābhyāsaṃ mahātmanaḥ | sambhūya vāṅmayī kanyā nāmnā vedavatī smṛtā || 7.17.9 ||
translation: तस्य his, अहं I, कुर्वतः while performing, नित्यं constantly, वेदाभ्यासं study of Vedas, महात्मनः of the great soul, सम्भूय having been born, वाङ्मयी consisting of speech, कन्या a daughter, नाम्ना by name, वेदवती Vedavati, स्मृता was known.
explanation: While my great-souled father was constantly engaged in the study of the Vedas, I was born as a daughter, manifested from his speech, and was known by the name Vedavati.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः । ते ऽपि गत्वा हि पितरं वरणं रोचयन्ति मे ।। 7.17.10 ।।
transliteration: tato devāḥ sagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ | te 'pi gatvā hi pitaraṃ varaṇaṃ rocayanti me || 7.17.10 ||
translation: ततः then, देवाः gods, सगन्धर्वाः along with Gandharvas, यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pannagas, ते they, अपि also, गत्वा having gone, हि indeed, पितरं to my father, वरणं a marriage proposal, रोचयन्ति desired, मे for me.
explanation: Then, gods along with Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pannagas, all went to my father and sought my hand in marriage.

shloka_text: न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान्राक्षसर्षभ । कारणं तद्वदिष्यामि निशाचर निशामय ।। 7.17.11 ।।
transliteration: na ca māṃ sa pitā tebhyo dattavānrākṣasarṣabha | kāraṇaṃ tadvadiṣyāmi niśācara niśāmaya || 7.17.11 ||
translation: न not, च and, मां me, सः that, पिता father, तेभ्यः to them, दत्तवान् gave, राक्षसर्षभ O best of Rakshasas, कारणं the reason, तत् that, वदिष्यामि I will tell, निशाचर O night-wanderer, निशामय listen.
explanation: But that father of mine did not give me to them, O best of Rakshasas; I will now tell you the reason for that, O night-wanderer, so listen.

shloka_text: पितुस्तु मम जामाता विष्णुः किल सुरेश्वरः । अभिप्रेतस्त्रिलोकेशस्तस्मान्नान्यस्य मे पिता ।। 7.17.12 ।।
transliteration: pitustu mama jāmātā viṣṇuḥ kila sureśvaraḥ | abhipretastrilokeśastasmānnānyasya me pitā || 7.17.12 ||
translation: पितुः of my father, तु indeed, मम my, जामाता son-in-law, विष्णुः Vishnu, किल it is said, सुरेश्वरः the lord of gods, अभिप्रेतः desired, त्रिलोकेशः the lord of the three worlds, तस्मात् therefore, न not, अन्यस्य to another, मे my, पिता father (gave me).
explanation: My father indeed desired Vishnu, the lord of gods and the lord of the three worlds, to be his son-in-law, and therefore he would not give me to anyone else.

shloka_text: दातुमिच्छति तस्मै तु तच्छ्रुत्वा बलदर्पितः । दम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितो ऽभवत् ।। 7.17.13 ।।
transliteration: dātumicchati tasmai tu tacchrutvā baladarpitaḥ | dambhurnāma tato rājā daityānāṃ kupito 'bhavat || 7.17.13 ||
translation: दातुम् to give, इच्छति desired, तस्मै to him, तु but, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, बलदर्पितः proud of his strength, दम्भुः Dambhu, नाम named, ततः then, राजा king, दैत्यानां of the Daityas, कुपितः enraged, अभवत् became.
explanation: But upon hearing that my father desired to give me to Vishnu, the king of Daityas named Dambhu, who was proud of his strength, became enraged.

transliteration: tena rātrau śayāno me pitā pāpena hiṃsitaḥ || 7.17.14 ||
translation: तेन by him, रात्रौ at night, शयानः sleeping, मे my, पिता father, पापेन by the wicked one, हिंसितः was killed.
explanation: My father, while sleeping at night, was killed by that wicked one.

shloka_text: ततो मे जननी दीना तच्छरीरं पितुर्मम । परिष्वज्य महाभागा प्रविष्टा हव्यवाहनम् ।। 7.17.15 ।।
transliteration: tato me jananī dīnā taccharīraṃ piturmama | pariṣvajya mahābhāgā praviṣṭā havyavāhanam || 7.17.15 ||
translation: ततः then, मे my, जननी mother, दीना distressed, तत् that, शरीरम् body, पितुः of father, मम my, परिष्वज्य embracing, महाभागा the noble lady, प्रविष्टा entered, हव्यवाहनम् the fire.
explanation: Then, my distressed mother, that noble lady, embraced my father's body and entered the fire.

shloka_text: ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति । करोमीति तमेवाहं हृदयेन समुद्वहे ।। 7.17.16 ।।
transliteration: tato manorathaṃ satyaṃ piturnārāyaṇaṃ prati | karomīti tamevāhaṃ hṛdayena samudvahe || 7.17.16 ||
translation: ततः then, मनोरथम् the desire, सत्यम् true, पितुः of my father, नारायणम् Narayana, प्रति towards, करोमि I will fulfill, इति thus, तम् that (desire), एव indeed, अहम् I, हृदयेन with my heart, समुद्वहे bear.
explanation: Then, I bear in my heart the true desire of my father towards Narayana, vowing to fulfill it.

shloka_text: इति प्रतिज्ञामारुह्य चरामि विपुलं तपः । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया राक्षसपुङ्गव ।। 7.17.17 ।।
transliteration: iti pratijñāmāruhya carāmi vipulaṃ tapaḥ | etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ mayā rākṣasapuṅgava || 7.17.17 ||
translation: इति thus, प्रतिज्ञाम् a vow, आरुह्य having undertaken, चरामि I perform, विपुलम् great, तपः austerity, एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातम् has been told, मया by me, राक्षसपुङ्गव O best of Rakshasas.
explanation: Thus, having undertaken this vow, I perform great austerity, and all this has been told to you by me, O best of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: नारायणो मम पतिर्न त्वन्यः पुरुषोत्तमात् । आश्रये नियमं घोरं नारायणपरीप्सया । विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन्गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन ।। 7.17.18 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇo mama patirna tvanyaḥ puruṣottamāt | āśraye niyamaṃ ghoraṃ nārāyaṇaparīpsayā | vijñātastvaṃ hi me rājangaccha paulastyanandana || 7.17.18 ||
translation: नारायणः Narayana, मम my, पतिः husband, न not, तु indeed, अन्यः another, पुरुषोत्तमात् than Purushottama, आश्रये I undertake, नियमम् a vow, घोरम् severe, नारायणपरीप्सया with the desire to obtain Narayana, विज्ञातः known, त्वम् you, हि indeed, मे to me, राजन् O king, गच्छ go, पौलस्त्यनन्दन O delight of Pulastya.
explanation: Narayana is my husband, and no one else is superior to Purushottama; I undertake a severe vow with the desire to obtain Narayana, and now that you are known to me, O king, O delight of Pulastya, you may go.

shloka_text: जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते ।। 7.17.19 ।।
transliteration: jānāmi tapasā sarvaṃ trailokye yaddhi vartate || 7.17.19 ||
translation: जानामि I know, तपसा by asceticism, सर्वम् all, त्रैलोक्ये in the three worlds, यत् whatever, हि indeed, वर्तते exists.
explanation: I know all that indeed exists in the three worlds through my ascetic power.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीद्रावणो भूयस्तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम् । अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात्कन्दर्पशरपीडितः ।। 7.17.20 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravīdrāvaṇo bhūyastāṃ kanyāṃ sumahāvratām | avaruhya vimānāgrātkandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ || 7.17.20 ||
translation: सः He, अब्रवीत् spoke, रावणः Ravana, भूयः again, ताम् to that, कन्याम् maiden, सुमहाव्रताम् of great vows, अवरुह्य having descended, विमानाग्रात् from the top of the aerial car, कन्दर्पशरपीडितः afflicted by the arrows of Kama (god of love).
explanation: Afflicted by the arrows of Kama, Ravana descended from the top of his aerial car and spoke again to that maiden of great vows.

shloka_text: अवलिप्ता ऽसि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी । वृद्धानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते पुण्यसञ्चयः ।। 7.17.21 ।।
transliteration: avaliptā 'si suśroṇi yasyāste matirīdṛśī | vṛddhānāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣi bhrājate puṇyasañcayaḥ || 7.17.21 ||
translation: अवलिप्ता arrogant, असि you are, सुश्रोणि O beautiful-hipped one, यस्याः whose, ते your, मतिः mind, ईदृशी such, वृद्धानाम् of the old, मृगशावाक्षि O deer-eyed one, भ्राजते shines, पुण्यसञ्चयः accumulation of merit.
explanation: O beautiful-hipped one, you are arrogant to have such a mind; O deer-eyed one, the accumulation of merit shines only for the aged.

shloka_text: त्वं सर्वंगुणसम्पन्ना नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम् । त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवनं ते निवर्तते ।। 7.17.22 ।।
transliteration: tvaṃ sarvaṃguṇasampannā nārhase vaktumīdṛśam | trailokyasundarī bhīru yauvanaṃ te nivartate || 7.17.22 ||
translation: त्वम् You, सर्वंगुणसम्पन्ना endowed with all virtues, न not, अर्हसे ought, वक्तुम् to speak, ईदृशम् such (a thing), त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी O most beautiful in the three worlds, भीरु O timid one, यौवनम् youth, ते your, निवर्तते is passing away.
explanation: O most beautiful in the three worlds and O timid one, you who are endowed with all virtues ought not to speak such a thing, for your youth is passing away.

shloka_text: अहं लङ्कापतिर्भद्रे दशग्रीव इति श्रुतः । तस्य मे भव भार्या त्वं भुङ्क्ष्व भोगान्यथासुखम् ।। 7.17.23 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ laṅkāpatirbhadre daśagrīva iti śrutaḥ | tasya me bhava bhāryā tvaṃ bhuṅkṣva bhogānyathāsukham || 7.17.23 ||
translation: अहम् I, लङ्कापतिः lord of Lanka, भद्रे O auspicious one, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, इति thus, श्रुतः known, तस्य his, मे my, भव become, भार्या wife, त्वम् you, भुङ्क्ष्व enjoy, भोगान् pleasures, यथासुखम् as you please.
explanation: O auspicious one, I am known as Dashagriva, the lord of Lanka; become my wife and enjoy pleasures as you please.

shloka_text: कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे । वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च ।।
transliteration: kaśca tāvadasau yaṃ tvaṃ viṣṇurityabhibhāṣase | vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca ||
translation: कश्च who indeed, तावत् then, असौ that one, यम् whom, त्वम् you, विष्णुः Vishnu, इति thus, अभिभाषसे you speak of, वीर्येण by valor, तपसा by penance, च and, एव indeed, भोगेन by enjoyment, च and, बलेन by strength, च and
explanation: Ravana asks Vedavati who this Vishnu is, whom she speaks of, and what he possesses in terms of valor, penance, enjoyment, and strength.

shloka_text: न मया स समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसे ऽङ्गने ।। 7.17.24 ।।
transliteration: na mayā sa samo bhadre yaṃ tvaṃ kāmayase 'ṅgane || 7.17.24 ||
translation: न not, मया with me, सः he, समः equal, भद्रे O auspicious one, यम् whom, त्वम् you, कामयसे desire, अङ्गने O lady
explanation: Ravana declares to Vedavati that the one she desires is not equal to him.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु वेदवत्यथ सा ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.17.25 ।।
transliteration: ityuktavati tasmiṃstu vedavatyatha sā 'bravīt || 7.17.25 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्तवति having spoken, तस्मिन् when he, तु indeed, वेदवती Vedavati, अथ then, सा she, अब्रवीत् spoke
explanation: After Ravana had spoken thus, Vedavati then replied to him.

shloka_text: वै भोगेन च बलेन च ।। मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम् । त्रैलोक्याधिपति विष्णुं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् । त्वदृते राक्षसेन्द्रान्यः को ऽवमन्येत बुद्धिमान् ।। 7.17.26 ।।
transliteration: vai bhogena ca balena ca || mā maivamiti sā kanyā tamuvāca niśācaram | trailokyādhipati viṣṇuṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtam | tvadṛte rākṣasendrānyaḥ ko 'vamanyeta buddhimān || 7.17.26 ||
translation: वै indeed, भोगेन by enjoyment, च and, बलेन by strength, च and, मा not, मा not, एवम् thus, इति thus, सा she, कन्या the maiden, तम् to him, उवाच spoke, निशाचरम् to the night-wanderer, त्रैलोक्याधिपतिम् the lord of the three worlds, विष्णुम् Vishnu, सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् worshipped by all worlds, त्वत् than you, ऋते except, राक्षसेन्द्र O king of Rakshasas, अन्यः another, कः who, अवमन्येत would disrespect, बुद्धिमान् intelligent one
explanation: Vedavati, the maiden, told the night-wanderer Ravana, "No, not so!" and asked, "O king of Rakshasas, who else among intelligent beings, besides you, would disrespect Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds, who is worshipped by all?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तया तत्र वेदवत्या निशाचरः । मूर्धजेषु तदा कन्यां कराग्रेण परामृशत् ।। 7.17.27 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastayā tatra vedavatyā niśācaraḥ | mūrdhajeṣu tadā kanyāṃ karāgreṇa parāmṛśat || 7.17.27 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, तया by her, तत्र there, वेदवत्या by Vedavati, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, मूर्धजेषु on the hair of the head, तदा then, कन्याम् the maiden, कराग्रेण with the tip of his hand, परामृशत् touched
explanation: When Vedavati had spoken thus to him there, the night-wanderer Ravana then touched the maiden's hair with the tip of his hand.

shloka_text: ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन सा ऽच्छिनत् । असिर्भूत्वा करस्तस्याः केशांश्छिन्नांस्तदा ऽकरोत् ।। 7.17.28 ।।
transliteration: tato vedavatī kruddhā keśānhastena sā 'cchinat | asirbhūtvā karastasyāḥ keśāṃśchinnāṃstadā 'karot || 7.17.28 ||
translation: ततः then, वेदवती Vedavati, क्रुद्धा enraged, केशान् her hair, हस्तेन with her hand, सा she, अच्छिनत् cut off । असिर्भूत्वा having become a sword, करः the hand, तस्याः her, केशान् hair, छिन्नान् cut off, तदा then, अकरोत् made (it) ।
explanation: Then, enraged Vedavati cut off her hair with her hand, which, having transformed into a sword, severed her locks.

shloka_text: सा ज्वलन्तीव रोषेण दहन्तीव निशाचरम् । उवाचाग्निं समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा ।। 7.17.29 ।।
transliteration: sā jvalantīva roṣeṇa dahantīva niśācaram | uvācāgniṃ samādhāya maraṇāya kṛtatvarā || 7.17.29 ||
translation: सा She, ज्वलन्तीव as if burning, रोषेण with rage, दहन्तीव as if burning, निशाचरम् the night-wanderer (Ravana), उवाच spoke, अग्निम् fire, समाधाय having kindled/meditated upon, मरणाय for death, कृतत्वरा having made haste/resolved ।
explanation: Burning with rage as if to consume the night-wanderer, she, resolved to die, kindled a fire and spoke.

shloka_text: धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य न मे जीवितमिष्यते । रक्षस्तस्मात्प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम् ।। 7.17.30 ।।
transliteration: dharṣitāyāstvayānārya na me jīvitamiṣyate | rakṣastasmātpravekṣyāmi paśyataste hutāśanam || 7.17.30 ||
translation: धर्षितायाः of me, who has been molested, त्वया by you, अनार्य O ignoble one, न not, मे my, जीवितम् life, इष्यते is desired । रक्षः O Rakshasa, तस्मात् therefore, प्रवेक्ष्यामि I shall enter, पश्यतः while seeing, ते you, हुताशनम् the fire ।
explanation: O ignoble one, since I have been molested by you, I no longer desire to live, O Rakshasa; therefore, I shall enter the fire before your very eyes.

shloka_text: यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहं त्वया पापात्मना वने । तस्मात्तव वधार्थं हि समुत्पत्स्ये ह्यहं पुनः ।। 7.17.31 ।।
transliteration: yasmāttu dharṣitā cāhaṃ tvayā pāpātmanā vane | tasmāttava vadhārthaṃ hi samutpatsye hyahaṃ punaḥ || 7.17.31 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, तु indeed, धर्षिता molested, च and, अहम् I, त्वया by you, पापात्मना evil-souled, वने in the forest, तस्मात् therefore, तव your, वधार्थम् for the sake of destruction, हि indeed, समुत्पत्स्ये I shall be born, हि indeed, अहम् I, पुनः again ।
explanation: Because I have been molested by your evil self in this forest, I shall indeed be born again for the sole purpose of your destruction.

shloka_text: न हि शक्यं स्त्रिया हन्तुं पुरुषः पापनिश्चः । शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत् ।। 7.17.32 ।।
transliteration: na hi śakyaṃ striyā hantuṃ puruṣaḥ pāpaniścaḥ | śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaśca vyayo bhavet || 7.17.32 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, शक्यम् possible, स्त्रिया by a woman, हन्तुम् to kill, पुरुषः a man, पापनिश्चयः one whose resolve is evil । शापे if a curse, त्वयि upon you, मया by me, उत्सृष्टे is uttered, तपसः of penance, च and, व्ययः loss, भवेत् would be ।
explanation: Indeed, it is not possible for a woman to kill a man of evil resolve, and if I were to utter a curse upon you, my accumulated penance would be lost.

shloka_text: यदि त्वस्ति मया किञ्चित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा । तस्मात्त्वयोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता ।। 7.17.33 ।।
transliteration: yadi tvasti mayā kiñcitkṛtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ tathā | tasmāttvayonijā sādhvī bhaveyaṃ dharmiṇaḥ sutā || 7.17.33 ||
translation: यदि if, तु indeed, अस्ति is, मया by me, किञ्चित् anything, कृतं done, दत्तं given, हुतं offered, तथा and so, तस्मात् therefore, त्वयोनिजा not born from a womb, साध्वी virtuous, भवेयं may I be, धर्मिणः of a righteous man, सुता daughter,
explanation: If I have indeed performed any good deeds, given charity, or offered sacrifices, then may I be born as the virtuous, womb-born daughter of a righteous man.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलितं जातवेदसम् । पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः ।। 7.17.34 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā praviṣṭā sā jvalitaṃ jātavedasam | papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ || 7.17.34 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having said, प्रविष्टा entered, सा she, ज्वलितं blazing, जातवेदसम् fire, पपात fell, च and, दिवो from the sky, दिव्या divine, पुष्पवृष्टिः shower of flowers, समन्ततः all around,
explanation: Having spoken thus, she entered the blazing fire, and simultaneously, a divine shower of flowers fell from the sky all around.

shloka_text: पुनरेव समुद्भूता पद्मे पद्मसमप्रभा । तस्मादपि पुनः प्राप्ता पूर्ववत्तेन रक्षसा ।। 7.17.35 ।।
transliteration: punareva samudbhūtā padme padmasamaprabhā | tasmādapi punaḥ prāptā pūrvavattena rakṣasā || 7.17.35 ||
translation: पुनरेव again indeed, समुद्भूता emerged, पद्मे in a lotus, पद्मसमप्रभा having the radiance of a lotus, तस्मादपि from that also, पुनः again, प्राप्ता obtained, पूर्ववत् as before, तेन by that, रक्षसा demon,
explanation: She emerged again from a lotus, radiant like a lotus, and from that lotus, she was again taken by that demon as before.

shloka_text: कन्यां कमलगर्भाभां प्रगृह्य स्वगृहं ययौ । प्रगृह्य रावणस्त्वेतां दर्शयामास मन्त्रिणे ।। 7.17.36 ।।
transliteration: kanyāṃ kamalagarbhābhāṃ pragṛhya svagṛhaṃ yayau | pragṛhya rāvaṇastvetāṃ darśayāmāsa mantriṇe || 7.17.36 ||
translation: कन्यां the maiden, कमलगर्भाभां having the radiance of a lotus's inner part, प्रगृह्य having taken, स्वगृहं to his own house, ययौ went, प्रगृह्य having taken, रावणस्तु but Ravana, एतां her, दर्शयामास showed, मन्त्रिणे to his minister,
explanation: Having seized the maiden, who shone like the heart of a lotus, the demon went to his own house, and Ravana then showed her to his minister.

shloka_text: लक्षणज्ञो निरीक्ष्यैव रावणं चैवमब्रवीत् । गृहस्थैषां हि सुश्रोणी त्वद्वधायैव दृश्यते ।। 7.17.37 ।।
transliteration: lakṣaṇajño nirīkṣyaiva rāvaṇaṃ caivamabravīt | gṛhasthaiṣāṃ hi suśroṇī tvadvadhāyaiva dṛśyate || 7.17.37 ||
translation: लक्षणज्ञो the knower of auspicious marks, निरीक्ष्यैव having seen her indeed, रावणं to Ravana, चैवम् and thus, अब्रवीत् spoke, गृहस्था staying in your house, एषा this one, हि indeed, सुश्रोणी beautiful-hipped, त्वद्वधायैव for your destruction indeed, दृश्यते is seen,
explanation: The physiognomist, having observed her, spoke to Ravana, saying, "This beautiful-hipped maiden, staying in your house, is indeed destined for your destruction."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ऽर्णवे राम तां प्रचिक्षेप रावणः । सा चैव क्षितिमासाद्य यज्ञायतनमध्यगा ।। 7.17.38 ।।
transliteration: etacchrutvā 'rṇave rāma tāṃ pracikṣepa rāvaṇaḥ | sā caiva kṣitimāsādya yajñāyatanamadhyagā || 7.17.38 ||
translation: एतत् this, श्रुत्वा having heard, अर्णवे into the water/ocean, राम O Rama, तां her, प्रचिक्षेप threw, रावणः Ravana, सा she, च and, एव indeed, क्षितिम् the earth, आसाद्य having reached, यज्ञायतनमध्यगा went into the middle of a sacrificial ground.
explanation: O Rama, having heard this, Ravana threw her into the water, and she, having reached the earth, indeed went into the middle of a sacrificial ground.

shloka_text: राज्ञो हलमुखोत्कृष्टा पुनरप्युत्थिता सती । सैषा जनकराजस्य प्रसूता तनया प्रभो । तव भार्या महाबाहो विष्णुस्त्वं हि सनातनः ।। 7.17.39 ।।
transliteration: rājño halamukhotkṛṣṭā punarapyutthitā satī | saiṣā janakarājasya prasūtā tanayā prabho | tava bhāryā mahābāho viṣṇustvaṃ hi sanātanaḥ || 7.17.39 ||
translation: राज्ञः of the king, हलमुखोत्कृष्टा drawn out by the ploughshare, पुनरपि again, उत्थिता arisen, सती being, सा she, एषा this, जनकराजस्य of King Janaka, प्रसूता born, तनया daughter, प्रभो O Lord, तव your, भार्या wife, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, विष्णुः Vishnu, त्वं you, हि indeed, सनातनः the eternal one.
explanation: O Lord, O mighty-armed one, she, having again arisen, drawn out by the ploughshare of King Janaka, is this daughter born to King Janaka, your wife, for you are indeed the eternal Vishnu.

shloka_text: पूर्वं क्रोधाहितः शत्रुर्यया ऽसौ निहतस्तथा । उपाश्रयित्वा शैलभस्तव वीर्यममानुषम् ।। 7.17.40 ।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃ krodhāhitaḥ śatruryayā 'sau nihatastathā | upāśrayitvā śailabhastava vīryamamānuṣam || 7.17.40 ||
translation: पूर्वम् previously, क्रोधाहितः filled with anger, शत्रुः the enemy, यया by whom, असौ that, निहतः killed, तथा thus, उपाश्रयित्वा having resorted to, शैलभः mountain-like (Ravana), तव your, वीर्यम् prowess, अमानुषम् superhuman.
explanation: Previously, that mountain-like enemy, filled with anger, was thus killed by her, having resorted to your superhuman prowess.

shloka_text: एवमेषा महाभागा मर्त्येषूत्पत्स्यते पुनः । क्षेत्रे हलमुखोत्कृष्टे वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा ।। 7.17.41 ।।
transliteration: evameṣā mahābhāgā martyeṣūtpatsyate punaḥ | kṣetre halamukhotkṛṣṭe vedyāmagniśikhopamā || 7.17.41 ||
translation: एवम् thus, एषा this, महाभागा highly fortunate one, मर्त्येषु among mortals, उत्पत्स्यते will be born, पुनः again, क्षेत्रे in the field, हलमुखोत्कृष्टे drawn out by the ploughshare, वेद्याम् on the altar/sacrificial ground, अग्निशिखोपमा like a flame of fire.
explanation: Thus, this highly fortunate one will again be born among mortals, in a field drawn out by the ploughshare, appearing like a flame of fire on the sacrificial ground.

shloka_text: एषा वेदवती नाम पूर्वमासीत्कृते युगे । त्रेतायुगमनुप्राप्य वधार्थं तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.17.42 ।।
transliteration: eṣā vedavatī nāma pūrvamāsītkṛte yuge | tretāyugamanuprāpya vadhārthaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ || 7.17.42 ||
translation: एषा this, वेदवती Vedavati, नाम named, पूर्वम् previously, आसीत् was, कृते युगे in the Krita Yuga, त्रेतायुगम् the Treta Yuga, अनुप्राप्य having reached/upon the arrival of, वधार्थम् for the purpose of killing, तस्य that, रक्षसः demon.
explanation: This one, named Vedavati, was previously in the Krita Yuga, and upon the arrival of the Treta Yuga, she appeared for the purpose of killing that demon.

shloka_text: उत्पन्ना मैथिलकुले जनकस्य महात्मनः । सीतोत्पन्ना तु सीतेति मानुषैः पुनरुच्यते ।। 7.17.43 ।।
transliteration: utpannā maithilakule janakasya mahātmanaḥ | sītotpannā tu sīteti mānuṣaiḥ punarucyate || 7.17.43 ||
translation: उत्पन्ना born, मैथिलकुले in the family of the Maithila (king of Mithila), जनकस्य of Janaka, महात्मनः the great-souled, सीतोत्पन्ना born from the furrow, तु indeed, सीतेति as Sita, मानुषैः by humans, पुनरुच्यते is again called.
explanation: She was born in the family of the great-souled Janaka, the king of Mithila, and because she emerged from the furrow, she is known by humans as Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः ।। 17 ।। Thus ends the seventeenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः । पुष्पकं तु समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् ।। 7.18.1 ।।
transliteration: praviṣṭāyāṃ hutāśaṃ tu vedavatyāṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ | puṣpakaṃ tu samāruhya paricakrāma medinīm || 7.18.1 ||
translation: प्रविष्टायां having entered, हुताशं fire, तु indeed, वेदवत्यां Vedavati, सः he, रावणः Ravana, पुष्पकं Pushpaka (chariot), तु indeed, समारुह्य having ascended, परिचक्राम wandered around, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: After Vedavati entered the fire, Ravana ascended his Pushpaka chariot and wandered across the earth.
comments: Ravana comes upon King Marutta's sacrifice, where the terrified gods hide in animal forms -- Indra as a peacock, Yama as a crow, Kubera as a lizard and Varuna as a swan -- restrained by the sage Samvarta from breaking his consecration, Marutta does not fight, and Ravana, proclaimed victor, devours the assembled sages and departs -- the gods resume their forms and bless the creatures whose shapes they had taken.

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः । उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु रावणः ।। 7.18.2 ।।
transliteration: tato maruttaṃ nṛpatiṃ yajantaṃ saha daivataiḥ | uśīrabījamāsādya dadarśa sa tu rāvaṇaḥ || 7.18.2 ||
translation: ततः then, मरुत्तं Marutta, नृपतिं king, यजन्तं sacrificing, सह with, दैवतैः deities, उशीरबीजम् Ushirabija (a place), आसाद्य having reached, ददर्श saw, सः he, तु indeed, रावणः Ravana.
explanation: Then, having arrived at Ushirabija, Ravana saw King Marutta performing a sacrifice with the deities.

shloka_text: संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षाद्भ्राता बृहस्पतेः । याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्देवगणैर्वृतः ।। 7.18.3 ।।
transliteration: saṃvarto nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣādbhrātā bṛhaspateḥ | yājayāmāsa dharmajñaḥ sarvairdevagaṇairvṛtaḥ || 7.18.3 ||
translation: संवर्तः Samvarta, नाम named, ब्रह्मर्षिः a Brahmarshi (sage), साक्षात् directly, भ्राता brother, बृहस्पतेः of Brihaspati, याजयामास officiated (the sacrifice), धर्मज्ञः knower of dharma, सर्वैः all, देवगणैः hosts of gods, वृतः surrounded by.
explanation: The righteous Brahmarshi named Samvarta, who was the direct brother of Brihaspati, officiated the sacrifice, surrounded by all the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद्रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम् । तिर्यग्योनिं समाविष्टास्तस्य दर्शनभीरवः ।। 7.18.4 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā devāstu tadrakṣo varadānena durjayam | tiryagyoniṃ samāviṣṭāstasya darśanabhīravaḥ || 7.18.4 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, देवाः the gods, तु indeed, तत् that, रक्षः demon, वरदानेन by the boon, दुर्जयम् unconquerable, तिर्यग्योनिं animal forms, समाविष्टाः entered, तस्य his, दर्शनभीरवः fearful of the sight.
explanation: The gods, fearful of the sight of that demon who was unconquerable due to a boon, assumed animal forms.

shloka_text: इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः । कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसश्च वरुणो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.5 ।।
transliteration: indro mayūraḥ saṃvṛtto dharmarājastu vāyasaḥ | kṛkalāso dhanādhyakṣo haṃsaśca varuṇo 'bhavat || 7.18.5 ||
translation: इन्द्रो Indra, मयूरः a peacock, संवृत्तो became, धर्मराजस्तु Dharma-raja (Yama) and, वायसः a crow, कृकलासो a chameleon, धनाध्यक्षो the lord of wealth (Kubera), हंसश्च a swan and, वरुणो Varuna, ऽभवत् became
explanation: Indra transformed into a peacock, Yama into a crow, Kubera into a chameleon, and Varuna into a swan.

shloka_text: अन्येष्वपि गतेष्वेवं देवेष्वरिनिषूदन । रावणः प्राविशद्यज्ञं सारमेय इवाशुचिः ।। 7.18.6 ।।
transliteration: anyeṣvapi gateṣvevaṃ deveṣvariniṣūdana | rāvaṇaḥ prāviśadyajñaṃ sārameya ivāśuciḥ || 7.18.6 ||
translation: अन्येष्वपि even among others, गतेष्वेवं having gone thus, देवेषु among the gods, अरिनिषूदन O destroyer of enemies, रावणः Ravana, प्राविशत् entered, यज्ञं the sacrifice, सारमेय a dog, इव like, अशुचिः impure
explanation: O destroyer of enemies, while other gods had also transformed and departed, Ravana entered the sacrifice like an impure dog.

shloka_text: तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा वद ।। 7.18.7 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ca rājānamāsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ | prāha yuddhaṃ prayaccheti nirjito 'smīti vā vada || 7.18.7 ||
translation: तं him, च and, राजानम् the king, आसाद्य having approached, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas, प्राह said, युद्धं battle, प्रयच्छेति give (me), निर्जितो conquered, ऽस्मीति I am, वा or, वद say
explanation: And having approached that king, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, said, "Either give me battle, or declare that I am conquered."

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम् । अपहासं ततो मुक्त्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.8 ।।
transliteration: tato marutto nṛpatiḥ ko bhavānityuvāca tam | apahāsaṃ tato muktvā rāvaṇo vākyamabravīt || 7.18.8 ||
translation: ततो then, मरुत्तो Marutta, नृपतिः the king, को who, भवान् are you, इति thus, उवाच said, तम् to him, अपहासं a scornful laugh, ततो then, मुक्त्वा having let out, रावणो Ravana, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke
explanation: Then King Marutta asked him, "Who are you?", whereupon Ravana, letting out a scornful laugh, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव पार्थिव । धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम् ।। 7.18.9 ।।
transliteration: akutūhalabhāvena prīto 'smi tava pārthiva | dhanadasyānujaṃ yo māṃ nāvagacchasi rāvaṇam || 7.18.9 ||
translation: अकुतूहलभावेन by your lack of curiosity, प्रीतो pleased, ऽस्मि I am, तव your, पार्थिव O king, धनदस्य of Kubera, अनुजं the younger brother, यो who, मां me, न not, अवगच्छसि you recognize, रावणम् Ravana
explanation: Ravana said, "O king, I am pleased by your lack of curiosity, as you do not recognize me, Ravana, the younger brother of Kubera."

shloka_text: त्रिषु लोकेषु को ऽन्यो ऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम् । भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम् । ततो मरुत्तः स नृपस्तं रावणमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.10 ।।
transliteration: triṣu lokeṣu ko 'nyo 'sti yo na jānāti me balam | bhrātaraṃ yena nirjitya vimānamidamāhṛtam | tato maruttaḥ sa nṛpastaṃ rāvaṇamathābravīt || 7.18.10 ||
translation: त्रिषु in three, लोकेषु worlds, कः who, अन्यः other, अस्ति is, यः who, न not, जानाति knows, मे my, बलम् strength, भ्रातरम् brother, येन by whom, निर्जित्य having conquered, विमानम् aerial chariot, इदम् this, आहृतम् was brought, ततः then, मरुत्तः Marutta, सः that, नृपः king, तम् to him, रावणम् to Ravana, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Ravana boasts, "Who in the three worlds does not know my strength, by which I conquered my brother and brought this aerial chariot?"; then King Marutta spoke to Ravana.

shloka_text: धन्यः खलु भवान्येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः । न त्वया सदृशः श्लाध्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ।। 7.18.11 ।।
transliteration: dhanyaḥ khalu bhavānyena jyeṣṭho bhrātā raṇe jitaḥ | na tvayā sadṛśaḥ ślādhyastriṣu lokeṣu vidyate || 7.18.11 ||
translation: धन्यः blessed, खलु indeed, भवान् you, येन by whom, ज्येष्ठः elder, भ्राता brother, रणे in battle, जितः was conquered, न not, त्वया by you, सदृशः similar, श्लाध्यः praiseworthy, त्रिषु in three, लोकेषु worlds, विद्यते exists.
explanation: Marutta sarcastically remarks, "Indeed, you are blessed, by whom the elder brother was conquered in battle; there is no one praiseworthy like you in the three worlds."

shloka_text: नाधर्मसहितं श्लाध्यं तल्लोकं प्रतिसंहितम् । कर्म दौरात्म्यकं कृत्वा श्लाघ्यसे भ्रातृनिर्जयात् ।। 7.18.12 ।।
transliteration: nādharmasahitaṃ ślādhyaṃ tallokaṃ pratisaṃhitam | karma daurātmyakaṃ kṛtvā ślāghyase bhrātṛnirjayāt || 7.18.12 ||
translation: न not, अधर्मसहितम् associated with unrighteousness, श्लाध्यम् praiseworthy, तत् that, लोकम् people, प्रतिसंहितम् connected to, कर्म act, दौरात्म्यकम् wicked, कृत्वा having done, श्लाघ्यसे you boast, भ्रातृनिर्जयात् from conquering a brother.
explanation: Marutta continues, "An act associated with unrighteousness is not praiseworthy among people; having performed such a wicked deed, you boast about conquering your brother."

shloka_text: क त्वं प्राक्केवलं धर्मं चरित्वा लब्धवान्वरम् । श्रूतपूर्वं हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम् ।। 7.18.13 ।।
transliteration: ka tvaṃ prākkevalaṃ dharmaṃ caritvā labdhavānvaram | śrūtapūrvaṃ hi na mayā bhāṣase yādṛśaṃ svayam || 7.18.13 ||
translation: क how, त्वम् you, प्राक् formerly, केवलम् only, धर्मम् righteousness, चरित्वा having practiced, लब्धवान् obtained, वरम् boon, श्रूतपूर्वं heard before, हि indeed, न not, मया by me, भाषसे you speak, यादृशम् such as, स्वयम् yourself.
explanation: Marutta questions, "How did you, who formerly practiced only righteousness, obtain a boon? Indeed, I have never heard you speak such words as you now utter."

shloka_text: तिष्ठेदानीं न मे जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि दुर्मते । अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम् ।। 7.18.14 ।।
transliteration: tiṣṭhedānīṃ na me jīvanpratiyāsyasi durmate | adya tvāṃ niśitairbāṇaiḥ preṣayāmi yamakṣayam || 7.18.14 ||
translation: तिष्ठ stop, इदानीम् now, न not, मे from me, जीवन् living, प्रतियास्यसि you will return, दुर्मते O evil-minded one, अद्य today, त्वाम् you, निशितैः sharp, बाणैः with arrows, प्रेषयामि I send, यमक्षयम् to Yama's abode.
explanation: Marutta declares, "Stop now, O evil-minded one, you will not return alive from me; today I will send you to Yama's abode with sharp arrows."

shloka_text: ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च नराधिपः । रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत् ।। 7.18.15 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śarāsanaṃ gṛhya sāyakāṃśca narādhipaḥ | raṇāya niryayau kruddhaḥ saṃvarto mārgamāvṛṇot || 7.18.15 ||
translation: ततः then, शरासनं bow, गृह्य having taken, सायकांश्च and arrows, नराधिपः the king, रणाय for battle, निर्ययौ went forth, क्रुद्धः enraged, संवर्तो Samvarta, मार्गम् the path, आवृणोत् blocked.
explanation: Then, the enraged King Marutta, having taken his bow and arrows, went forth for battle, but the sage Samvarta blocked his path.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीत्स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः । श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं सम्प्रहारो न ते क्षमः ।। 7.18.16 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravītsnehasaṃyuktaṃ maruttaṃ taṃ mahānṛṣiḥ | śrotavyaṃ yadi madvākyaṃ samprahāro na te kṣamaḥ || 7.18.16 ||
translation: सः he, अब्रवीत् spoke, स्नेहसंयुक्तं affectionately, मरुत्तं to Marutta, तं that, महानृषिः great sage, श्रोतव्यं should be heard, यदि if, मद्वाक्यं my words, सम्प्रहारो battle, न not, ते for you, क्षमः suitable.
explanation: That great sage Samvarta affectionately spoke to Marutta, saying that if his words were to be heard, then battle was not suitable for him.

shloka_text: माहेश्वरमिदं सत्रमसमाप्तं कुलं दहेत् ।। 7.18.17 ।।
transliteration: māheśvaramidaṃ satramasamāptaṃ kulaṃ dahet || 7.18.17 ||
translation: इदं this, माहेश्वरम् सत्रम् sacrifice dedicated to Maheshvara, असमाप्तम् if left unfinished, कुलं the lineage, दहेत् would consume.
explanation: This sacrifice dedicated to Maheshvara, if left unfinished, would consume the whole lineage.

shloka_text: दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः । संशयश्च जये नित्यं राक्षसश्च सुदुर्जयः ।। 7.18.18 ।।
transliteration: dīkṣitasya kuto yuddhaṃ krodhitvaṃ dīkṣite kutaḥ | saṃśayaśca jaye nityaṃ rākṣasaśca sudurjayaḥ || 7.18.18 ||
translation: दीक्षितस्य for one who is consecrated, कुतो whence, युद्धं battle, क्रोधित्वं anger, दीक्षिते in one who is consecrated, कुतः whence, संशयश्च and doubt, जये in victory, नित्यं always, राक्षसश्च and the demon, सुदुर्जयः very difficult to conquer.
explanation: For one consecrated for a sacrifice, whence comes battle, and whence comes anger; moreover, there is always doubt in victory, and the demon is very difficult to conquer.

shloka_text: स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः । विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.19 ।।
transliteration: sa nivṛtto gurorvākyānmaruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ | visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ svastho makhamukho 'bhavat || 7.18.19 ||
translation: सः he, निवृत्तो turned back, गुरोर्वाक्यात् from the guru's words, मरुत्तः Marutta, पृथिवीपतिः the king, विसृज्य having abandoned, सशरं with arrows, चापं the bow, स्वस्थो composed, मखमुखो intent on the sacrifice, अभवत् became.
explanation: Following his guru's words, King Marutta turned back, abandoned his bow and arrows, and became composed and intent on his sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः । रावणो जयतीत्युच्चैर्हर्षान्नादं विमुक्तवान् ।। 7.18.20 ।।
transliteration: tatastaṃ nirjitaṃ matvā ghoṣayāmāsa vai śukaḥ | rāvaṇo jayatītyuccairharṣānnādaṃ vimuktavān || 7.18.20 ||
translation: ततः then, तं him, निर्जितं defeated, मत्वा having considered, घोषयामास announced, वै indeed, शुकः Shuka, रावणो Ravana, जयति is victorious, इति thus, उच्चैः loudly, हर्षात् from joy, नादं a proclamation, विमुक्तवान् uttered.
