explanation: Then, Shuka, considering Marutta defeated, loudly proclaimed with joy, "Ravana is victorious!"

shloka_text: तान्भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान्महर्षीन्यज्ञमागतान् । वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः सम्प्रययौ महीम् ।। 7.18.21 ।।
transliteration: tānbhakṣayitvā tatrasthānmaharṣīnyajñamāgatān | vitṛpto rudhiraisteṣāṃ punaḥ samprayayau mahīm || 7.18.21 ||
translation: तान् them, भक्षयित्वा having devoured, तत्रस्थान् who were there, महर्षीन् great sages, यज्ञम् to the sacrifice, आगतान् who had come, वितृप्तः fully satisfied, रुधिरैः with the blood, तेषाम् of them, पुनः again, सम्प्रययौ he went, महीम् to the earth.
explanation: Having devoured those great sages who had come to the sacrifice and were there, and being fully satisfied with their blood, he again went to the earth.

shloka_text: रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः । ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.18.22 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāścaiva divaukasaḥ | tataḥ svāṃ yonimāsādya tāni sattvāni cābruvan || 7.18.22 ||
translation: रावणे when Ravana, तु indeed, गते had gone, देवाः the gods, सेन्द्राः with Indra, च and, एव indeed, दिवौकसः the dwellers of heaven, ततः then, स्वाम् their own, योनिम् form, आसाद्य having attained, तानि to those, सत्त्वानि beings, च and, अब्रुवन् they spoke.
explanation: When Ravana had indeed gone, the gods, along with Indra and other dwellers of heaven, then regained their own forms and spoke to those beings.

shloka_text: हर्षात्तदाब्रवीदिन्द्रो मयूरं नीलबर्हिणम् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजङ्गाद्धि न ते भयम् ।। 7.18.23 ।।
transliteration: harṣāttadābravīdindro mayūraṃ nīlabarhiṇam | prīto 'smi tava dharmajña bhujaṅgāddhi na te bhayam || 7.18.23 ||
translation: हर्षात् from joy, तदा then, अब्रवीत् spoke, इन्द्रः Indra, मयूरम् to the peacock, नीलबर्हिणम् with blue feathers, प्रीतः pleased, अस्मि I am, तव with you, धर्मज्ञ O knower of dharma, भुजङ्गात् from serpents, हि indeed, न not, ते to you, भयम् fear.
explanation: Then, from joy, Indra spoke to the blue-feathered peacock, saying, "O knower of dharma, I am pleased with you, and indeed, you shall have no fear from serpents."

shloka_text: इदं नेत्रसहस्रं तु यत्त्वद्बर्हे भविष्यति । वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणाम् । एवमिन्द्रो वरं प्रादान्मयूरस्य सुरेश्वरः ।। 7.18.24 ।।
transliteration: idaṃ netrasahasraṃ tu yattvadbarhe bhaviṣyati | varṣamāṇe mayi mudaṃ prāpsyase prītilakṣaṇām | evamindro varaṃ prādānmayūrasya sureśvaraḥ || 7.18.24 ||
translation: इदम् this, नेत्रसहस्रम् thousand eyes, तु indeed, यत् which, त्वद्बर्हे on your tail-feathers, भविष्यति will be, वर्षमाणे while raining, मयि by me, मुदम् joy, प्राप्स्यसे you will obtain, प्रीतिलक्षणाम् marked by pleasure, एवम् thus, इन्द्रः Indra, वरम् a boon, प्रादात् gave, मयूरस्य to the peacock, सुरेश्वरः the lord of gods.
explanation: Indra, the lord of gods, thus granted a boon to the peacock, saying that the thousand eyes would appear on its tail-feathers, and it would experience joy, a sign of pleasure, when he (Indra) rained.

shloka_text: नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप । सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वे ऽपि बर्हिणः ।। 7.18.25 ।।
transliteration: nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṃ narādhipa | surādhipādvaraṃ prāpya gatāḥ sarve 'pi barhiṇaḥ || 7.18.25 ||
translation: नीलाः blue, किल it is said, पुरा formerly, बर्हाः feathers, मयूराणाम् of peacocks, नराधिप O king of men, सुराधिपात् from the lord of gods, वरम् a boon, प्राप्य having obtained, गताः they became, सर्वे all, अपि even, बर्हिणः peacocks.
explanation: O king of men, it is said that formerly the feathers of peacocks were blue, and having obtained a boon from the lord of gods, all peacocks became (as they are now, with the characteristic 'eyes' on their feathers).

shloka_text: धर्मराजो ऽब्रवीद्राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं स्थितम् । पक्षिंस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य वचनं शृणु ।। 7.18.26 ।।
transliteration: dharmarājo 'bravīdrāma prāgvaṃśe vāyasaṃ sthitam | pakṣiṃstavāsmi suprītaḥ prītasya vacanaṃ śṛṇu || 7.18.26 ||
translation: धर्मराजो Dharmaraja, अब्रवीत् said, राम O Rama, प्राग्वंशे in the eastern part of the house, वायसं to the crow, स्थितम् situated, पक्षिंस्तवास्मि O bird, I am, सुप्रीतः very pleased, प्रीतस्य of the pleased one, वचनं words, शृणु listen.
explanation: Dharmaraja (Yama) addressed the crow, who was formerly Rama, situated in the eastern part of the house, saying, "O bird, I am very pleased with you; listen to the words of one who is pleased."

shloka_text: यथान्ये विविधै रोगै; पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया । ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः ।। 7.18.27 ।।
transliteration: yathānye vividhai rogai; pīḍyante prāṇino mayā | te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṃśayaḥ || 7.18.27 ||
translation: यथा just as, अन्ये others, विविधै by various, रोगैः diseases, पीड्यन्ते are tormented, प्राणिनो living beings, मया by me, ते those (diseases), न not, ते you (will affect), प्रभविष्यन्ति will be powerful over, मयि when I am, प्रीते pleased, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: Just as other living beings are tormented by various diseases through me, those diseases will not affect you when I am pleased, of this there is no doubt.

shloka_text: मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान्मम विहङ्गम । यावत्त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद्भविष्यसि ।। 7.18.28 ।।
transliteration: mṛtyutaste bhayaṃ nāsti varānmama vihaṅgama | yāvattvāṃ na vadhiṣyanti narāstāvadbhaviṣyasi || 7.18.28 ||
translation: मृत्युतः from death, ते to you, भयं fear, न नास्ति is not, वरान्मम from my boon, विहङ्गम O bird, यावत्त्वां as long as you, न not, वधिष्यन्ति will kill, नराः humans, तावत् so long, भविष्यसि you will be.
explanation: O bird, you have no fear of death due to my boon; you will continue to exist as long as humans do not kill you.

shloka_text: एते मद्विषयस्था वै मानवाः क्षुद्भयार्दिताः । त्वयि भुक्ते तु तृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः ।। 7.18.29 ।।
transliteration: ete madviṣayasthā vai mānavāḥ kṣudbhayārditāḥ | tvayi bhukte tu tṛptāste bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ || 7.18.29 ||
translation: एते these, मद्विषयस्था situated in my realm, वै indeed, मानवाः humans, क्षुद्भयार्दिताः afflicted by the fear of hunger, त्वयि when you, भुक्ते are eaten, तु indeed, तृप्तास्ते satisfied they, भविष्यन्ति will be, सबान्धवाः with their relatives.
explanation: Indeed, these humans in my realm, afflicted by the fear of hunger, will become satisfied along with their relatives when you are eaten.

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविहारिणम् । श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं वचः पत्ररथेश्वर ।। 7.18.30 ।।
transliteration: varuṇastvabravīddhaṃsaṃ gaṅgātoyavihāriṇam | śrūyatāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ vacaḥ patraratheśvara || 7.18.30 ||
translation: वरुणः Varuna, तु then, अब्रवीत् said, हंसं to the swan, गङ्गातोयविहारिणम् sporting in the waters of Ganga, श्रूयतां let it be heard, प्रीतिसंयुक्तं filled with affection, वचः words, पत्ररथेश्वर O lord of birds.
explanation: Then Varuna spoke to the swan, who was sporting in the waters of the Ganga, saying, "O lord of birds, listen to these words filled with affection."

shloka_text: वर्णो मनोहरः सौम्यश्चन्द्रमण्डलसन्निभः । भविष्यति तवोदग्रः शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः ।। 7.18.31 ।।
transliteration: varṇo manoharaḥ saumyaścandramaṇḍalasannibhaḥ | bhaviṣyati tavodagraḥ śuddhaphenasamaprabhaḥ || 7.18.31 ||
translation: वर्णो color, मनोहरः charming, सौम्यः gentle, चन्द्रमण्डलसन्निभः resembling the disc of the moon, भविष्यति will be, तव your, उदग्रः excellent, शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः having the luster of pure foam.
explanation: Your complexion will be charming, gentle, resembling the moon's disc, excellent, and will possess the luster of pure foam.

shloka_text: मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि । प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम् ।। 7.18.32 ।।
transliteration: maccharīraṃ samāsādya kānto nityaṃ bhaviṣyasi | prāpsyase cātulāṃ prītimetanme prītilakṣaṇam || 7.18.32 ||
translation: मच्छरीरं my body, समासाद्य having obtained, कान्तः beautiful, नित्यं always, भविष्यसि you will be, प्राप्स्यसे you will obtain, च and, अतुलां incomparable, प्रीतिं joy, एतत् this, मे my, प्रीतिलक्षणम् sign of affection.
explanation: By obtaining my body, you will always be beautiful and will attain incomparable joy, for this is a sign of my favor.

shloka_text: हंसानां हि पुरा राम नीलवर्णः सपाण्डुरः । पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः ।। 7.18.33 ।।
transliteration: haṃsānāṃ hi purā rāma nīlavarṇaḥ sapāṇḍuraḥ | pakṣā nīlāgrasaṃvītāḥ kroḍāḥ śaṣpāgranirmalāḥ || 7.18.33 ||
translation: हंसानां of swans, हि indeed, पुरा formerly, राम O Rama, नीलवर्णः blue-colored, सपाण्डुरः with a whitish tinge, पक्षाः wings, नीलाग्रसंवीताः covered with blue tips, क्रोडाः breasts, शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः pure like the tips of fresh grass.
explanation: Indeed, O Rama, in the past, swans were blue-colored with a whitish tinge, their wings were covered with blue tips, and their breasts were pure like the tips of fresh grass.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः कृकलासं गिरौ स्थितम् । हैरण्यं सम्प्रयच्छामि वर्णं प्रीतस्तवाप्यहम् ।। 7.18.34 ।।
transliteration: athābravīdvaiśravaṇaḥ kṛkalāsaṃ girau sthitam | hairaṇyaṃ samprayacchāmi varṇaṃ prītastavāpyaham || 7.18.34 ||
translation: अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, वैश्रवणः Vaishravana, कृकलासं to the chameleon, गिरौ on the mountain, स्थितम् situated, हैरण्यं golden, सम्प्रयच्छामि I bestow, वर्णं color, प्रीतः pleased, तव to you, अपि also, अहम् I.
explanation: Then Vaishravana, pleased, spoke to the chameleon situated on the mountain, saying, "I bestow upon you a golden color."

shloka_text: सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम् । एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति ।। 7.18.35 ।।
transliteration: sadravyaṃ ca śiro nityaṃ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam | eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati || 7.18.35 ||
translation: सद्रव्यं with wealth, च and, शिरो head, नित्यं always, भविष्यति will be, तव your, अक्षयम् inexhaustible, एष this, काञ्चनकः golden, वर्णः color, मत्प्रीत्या by my favor, ते for you, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Your head will always be rich and inexhaustible, and this golden color will be yours by my favor.

shloka_text: एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन्यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः । निवृत्ताः सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः ।। 7.18.36 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ dattvā varāṃstebhyastasminyajñotsave surāḥ | nivṛttāḥ saha rājñā te punaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ || 7.18.36 ||
translation: एवं thus, दत्त्वा having given, वरान् boons, तेभ्यः to them, तस्मिन् in that, यज्ञोत्सवे sacrificial festival, सुराः the gods, निवृत्ताः having departed, सह with, राज्ञा the king, ते they, पुनः again, स्वभवनं to their own abodes, गताः went.
explanation: After granting boons to them during that sacrificial festival, the gods, along with the king, returned to their respective abodes. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टादशः सर्गः ।। 18 ।। Thus ends the eighteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः । नगराणि नरेन्द्राणां युद्धकाङ्क्षी दशाननः ।। 7.19.1 ।।
transliteration: atha jitvā maruttaṃ sa prayayau rākṣasādhipaḥ | nagarāṇi narendrāṇāṃ yuddhakāṅkṣī daśānanaḥ || 7.19.1 ||
translation: अथ thereafter, जित्वा having conquered, मरुत्तं Marutta, सः he, प्रययौ went forth, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rākṣasas, नगराणि to the cities, नरेन्द्राणां of kings, युद्धकाङ्क्षी desirous of battle, दशाननः Daśānana.
explanation: After conquering Marutta, Daśānana, the lord of Rākṣasas, being desirous of battle, then proceeded to the cities of other kings.
comments: Ravana ranges the earth demanding that kings submit, and many yield -- but at Ayodhya King Anaranya gives battle; his army is consumed and he himself struck down -- dying, Anaranya curses Ravana that one born of his own Ikshvaku line, Rama son of Dasharatha, shall take his life, and then ascends to heaven.

shloka_text: समासाद्य तु राजेन्द्रान्महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान् । अब्रवीद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु युद्धं मे दीयतामिति ।। 7.19.2 ।।
transliteration: samāsādya tu rājendrānmahendravaruṇopamān | abravīdrākṣasendrastu yuddhaṃ me dīyatāmiti || 7.19.2 ||
translation: समासाद्य having approached, तु indeed, राजेन्द्रान् the great kings, महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान् comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa, अब्रवीत् said, राक्षससेन्द्रस्तु but the lord of Rākṣasas, युद्धं battle, मे to me, दीयताम् let it be given, इति thus.
explanation: Having approached those great kings who were comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas then demanded, "Let battle be given to me."

shloka_text: निर्जिताः स्मेति वा ब्रूत एष मे हि सुनिश्चयः । अन्यथा कुर्वतामेवं मोक्षो नैवोपपद्यते ।। 7.19.3 ।।
transliteration: nirjitāḥ smeti vā brūta eṣa me hi suniścayaḥ | anyathā kurvatāmevaṃ mokṣo naivopapadyate || 7.19.3 ||
translation: निर्जिताः we are conquered, स्म are, इति thus, वा or, ब्रूत say, एषः this, मे my, हि indeed, सुनिश्चयः firm resolve, अन्यथा otherwise, कुर्वताम् for those acting, एवं thus, मोक्षः liberation, न not, एव indeed, उपपद्यते is possible.
explanation: He declared, "Either say 'we are conquered,' for this is my firm resolve; otherwise, for those who act differently, there is no escape."

shloka_text: ततस्त्वभीरवः प्राज्ञाः पार्थिवा धर्मनिश्चयाः । मन्त्रयित्वा ततो ऽन्योन्यं राजानः सुमहाबलाः । निर्जिताः स्मेत्यभाषन्त ज्ञात्वा वरबलं रिपोः ।। 7.19.4 ।।
transliteration: tatastvabhīravaḥ prājñāḥ pārthivā dharmaniścayāḥ | mantrayitvā tato 'nyonyaṃ rājānaḥ sumahābalāḥ | nirjitāḥ smetyabhāṣanta jñātvā varabalaṃ ripoḥ || 7.19.4 ||
translation: ततः then, तु indeed, अभीरवः fearless, प्राज्ञाः wise, पार्थिवाः kings, धर्मनिश्चयाः firm in righteousness, मन्त्रयित्वा having consulted, ततः then, अन्योन्यं among themselves, राजानः the kings, सुमहाबलाः exceedingly powerful, निर्जिताः we are conquered, स्म are, इति thus, अभाषन्त they said, ज्ञात्वा having known, वरबलं the strength of the boon, रिपोः of the enemy.
explanation: Then, those fearless, wise, and righteous kings, though exceedingly powerful, consulted among themselves and, recognizing the enemy's strength derived from boons, declared, "We are conquered."

shloka_text: दुष्यन्तः सुरथो गाधिर्गयो राजा पुरूरवाः । एते सर्वे ऽब्रुवंस्तात निर्जिताः स्मेति पार्थिवाः ।। 7.19.5 ।।
transliteration: duṣyantaḥ suratho gādhirgayo rājā purūravāḥ | ete sarve 'bruvaṃstāta nirjitāḥ smeti pārthivāḥ || 7.19.5 ||
translation: दुष्यन्तः Dushyanta, सुरथो Suratha, गाधिर् Gadhi, गयो Gaya, राजा king, पुरूरवाः Pururava, एते these, सर्वे all, अब्रुवंस् said, तात O dear one, निर्जिताः conquered, स्म are, इति thus, पार्थिवाः kings.
explanation: Kings like Dushyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, Gaya, and Pururava all declared themselves conquered, saying, "O dear one, we are vanquished."

shloka_text: अथायोध्यां समासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.19.6 ।।
transliteration: athāyodhyāṃ samāsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.19.6 ||
translation: अथ then, अयोध्यां Ayodhya, समासाद्य having reached, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: Then, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, having reached Ayodhya...

shloka_text: सुगुप्तामनरण्येन शक्रेणेवामरावतीम् । स तं पुरुषशार्दूलं पुरन्दरसमं बले ।। 7.19.7 ।।
transliteration: suguptāmanaraṇyena śakreṇevāmarāvatīm | sa taṃ puruṣaśārdūlaṃ purandarasamaṃ bale || 7.19.7 ||
translation: सुगुप्ताम् well-protected, अनरण्येन by Anaranya, शक्रेण by Indra, इव as if, अमरावतीम् Amaravati, स he, तं that, पुरुषशार्दूलं tiger among men, पुरन्दरसमं equal to Indra, बले in strength.
explanation: ...(Ravana reached Ayodhya) which was well-protected by Anaranya, just as Amaravati is protected by Indra; he (Ravana) then approached that tiger among men, Anaranya, who was equal to Indra in strength.

shloka_text: प्राह राजानमासाद्य युद्धं देहीति रावणः । निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा ब्रूहि त्वमेवं मम शासनम् ।। 7.19.8 ।।
transliteration: prāha rājānamāsādya yuddhaṃ dehīti rāvaṇaḥ | nirjito 'smīti vā brūhi tvamevaṃ mama śāsanam || 7.19.8 ||
translation: प्राह said, राजानम् to the king, आसाद्य having approached, युद्धं battle, देहि give, इति thus, रावणः Ravana, निर्जितो conquered, अस्मि I am, इति thus, वा or, ब्रूहि say, त्वम् you, एवम् thus, मम my, शासनम् command.
explanation: Having approached the king, Ravana said, "Give me battle, or else declare 'I am conquered' – this is my command to you."

shloka_text: अयोध्याधिपतिस्तस्य श्रुत्वा पापात्मनो वचः । अनरण्यस्तु सङ्क्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.19.9 ।।
transliteration: ayodhyādhipatistasya śrutvā pāpātmano vacaḥ | anaraṇyastu saṅkruddho rākṣasendramathābravīt || 7.19.9 ||
translation: अयोध्याधिपतिस् the lord of Ayodhya, तस्य his, श्रुत्वा having heard, पापात्मनः of the evil-minded one, वचः words, अनरण्यस् Anaranya, तु but, सङ्क्रुद्धो greatly enraged, राक्षसेन्द्रम् to the lord of Rakshasas, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard the words of that evil-minded Ravana, Anaranya, the lord of Ayodhya, became greatly enraged and then spoke to the lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: दीयते द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ते राक्षसाधिपते मया । सन्तिष्ठ क्षिप्रमायत्तो भव चैवं भवाम्यहम् ।। 7.19.10 ।।
transliteration: dīyate dvandvayuddhaṃ te rākṣasādhipate mayā | santiṣṭha kṣipramāyatto bhava caivaṃ bhavāmyaham || 7.19.10 ||
translation: दीयते is offered, द्वन्द्वयुद्धं a duel, ते to you, राक्षसाधिपते O lord of Rākṣasas, मया by me, सन्तिष्ठ prepare yourself, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आयत्तः ready, भव be, च and, एवम् thus, भवामि I will be, अहम् I.
explanation: O lord of Rākṣasas, I offer you a duel; prepare yourself quickly, and I too shall be ready in the same manner.

shloka_text: अथ पूर्वं श्रुतार्थेन निर्जितं सुमहद्बलम् । निष्क्रामत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्य बलं रक्षोवधोद्यतम् ।। 7.19.11 ।।
transliteration: atha pūrvaṃ śrutārthena nirjitaṃ sumahadbalam | niṣkrāmattannarendrasya balaṃ rakṣovadhodyatam || 7.19.11 ||
translation: अथ then, पूर्वम् previously, श्रुतार्थेन by the heard prophecy, निर्जितं destined to be defeated, सुमहद्बलम् a very great army, निष्क्रामत् marched out, तत् that, नरेन्द्रस्य of the king, बलं army, रक्षोवधोद्यतम् intent on killing Rākṣasas.
explanation: Then, that very great army of the king, which was previously destined to be defeated by the heard prophecy and was intent on killing Rākṣasas, marched out.

shloka_text: नागानां दशसाहस्रं वाजिनां नियुतं तथा । रथानां बहुसाहस्रं पत्तीनां च नरोत्तम ।। 7.19.12 ।।
transliteration: nāgānāṃ daśasāhasraṃ vājināṃ niyutaṃ tathā | rathānāṃ bahusāhasraṃ pattīnāṃ ca narottama || 7.19.12 ||
translation: नागानां of elephants, दशसाहस्रं ten thousand, वाजिनां of horses, नियुतं a hundred thousand, तथा and, रथानां of chariots, बहुसाहस्रं many thousands, पत्तीनां of foot soldiers, च and, नरोत्तम O best among men.
explanation: O best among men, that army consisted of ten thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses, many thousands of chariots, and foot soldiers.

shloka_text: महीं सञ्छाद्य निष्क्रान्तं सपदातिरथं रणे । ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहद्युद्धं युद्धविशारद ।। 7.19.13 ।।
transliteration: mahīṃ sañchādya niṣkrāntaṃ sapadātirathaṃ raṇe | tataḥ pravṛttaṃ sumahadyuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada || 7.19.13 ||
translation: महीं the earth, सञ्छाद्य having covered, निष्क्रान्तं marched out, सपदातिरथं with foot soldiers and chariots, रणे for battle, ततः then, प्रवृत्तं commenced, सुमहत् a very great, युद्धं battle, युद्धविशारद O expert in warfare.
explanation: O expert in warfare, that army, covering the earth with its foot soldiers and chariots, marched out for battle, and then a very great battle commenced.

shloka_text: अनरण्यस्य नृपते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चाद्भुतम् । तद्रावणबलं प्राप्य बलं तस्य महीपतेः ।। 7.19.14 ।।
transliteration: anaraṇyasya nṛpate rākṣasendrasya cādbhutam | tadrāvaṇabalaṃ prāpya balaṃ tasya mahīpateḥ || 7.19.14 ||
translation: तत् that, अद्भुतम् amazing (battle), अनरण्यस्य of Anaraṇya, नृपतेः of the king, च and, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the lord of Rākṣasas, बलं the army, तस्य of that, महीपतेः king, रावणबलं Ravana's army, प्राप्य having encountered.
explanation: That amazing battle between King Anaraṇya and the lord of Rākṣasas commenced when the king's army encountered Ravana's army.

shloka_text: प्राणश्यत तदा सर्वं हव्यं हुतमिवानले । युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं कृत्वा विक्रममुत्तमम् ।। 7.19.15 ।।
transliteration: prāṇaśyata tadā sarvaṃ havyaṃ hutamivānale | yuddhvā ca suciraṃ kālaṃ kṛtvā vikramamuttamam || 7.19.15 ||
translation: प्राणश्यत perished, तदा then, सर्वम् all, हव्यम् oblation, हुतम् offered, इव like, अनले in fire, युद्ध्वा having fought, च and, सुचिरम् for a very long, कालम् time, कृत्वा having performed, विक्रमम् valor, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: Then, all (the army) perished like an oblation offered into fire, even after fighting for a very long time and displaying excellent valor.

shloka_text: प्रज्वलन्तं तमासाद्य क्षिप्रमेवावशेषितम् । प्राविशत्सङ्कुलं तत्र शलभा इव पावकम् । नश्यति स्म बलं तत्र हव्यं हुतमिवानले ।। 7.19.16 ।।
transliteration: prajvalantaṃ tamāsādya kṣipramevāvaśeṣitam | prāviśatsaṅkulaṃ tatra śalabhā iva pāvakam | naśyati sma balaṃ tatra havyaṃ hutamivānale || 7.19.16 ||
translation: प्रज्वलन्तम् blazing, तम् him, आसाद्य having approached, क्षिप्रम् quickly, एव indeed, अवशेषितम् was left (destroyed), प्राविशत् entered, सङ्कुलम् the multitude, तत्र there, शलभाः moths, इव like, पावकम् fire, नश्यति perished, स्म (past tense), बलम् the army, तत्र there, हव्यम् oblation, हुतम् offered, इव like, अनले in fire.
explanation: Having approached that blazing (Anaranya), the multitude of soldiers quickly perished, entering him like moths into a fire; the army there was destroyed like an oblation offered into fire.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्तु नश्यमानं महाबलम् । महार्णवं समासाद्य वनापगशतं यथा ।। 7.19.17 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyattannarendrastu naśyamānaṃ mahābalam | mahārṇavaṃ samāsādya vanāpagaśataṃ yathā || 7.19.17 ||
translation: सः he, अपश्यत् saw, तत् that, नरेन्द्रः king, तु indeed, नश्यमानम् perishing, महाबलम् great army, महार्णवम् great ocean, समासाद्य having reached, वनापगशतम् hundreds of forest rivers, यथा just as.
explanation: That king (Anaranya) indeed saw his great army perishing, just as hundreds of forest rivers disappear upon reaching the great ocean.

shloka_text: ततः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं धनुर्विस्फारयन्स्वयम् । आससाद नरेन्द्रस्तं रावणं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.19.18 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śakradhanuḥprakhyaṃ dhanurvisphārayansvayam | āsasāda narendrastaṃ rāvaṇaṃ krodhamūrcchitaḥ || 7.19.18 ||
translation: ततः then, शक्रधनुःप्रख्यम् resembling Indra's bow, धनुः his bow, विस्फारयन् stretching, स्वयम् himself, आससाद approached, नरेन्द्रः the king, तम् him, रावणम् Ravana, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with rage.
explanation: Then, the king (Anaranya), himself stretching his bow which resembled Indra's rainbow, approached Ravana, overcome with rage.

shloka_text: अनरण्येन ते ऽमात्या मारीचशुकसारणाः । प्रहस्तसहिता भग्ना व्यद्रवन्त मृगा इव ।। 7.19.19 ।।
transliteration: anaraṇyena te 'mātyā mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ | prahastasahitā bhagnā vyadravanta mṛgā iva || 7.19.19 ||
translation: अनरण्येन by Anaranya, ते those, अमात्याः ministers, मारीचशुकसारणाः Maricha, Shuka, Sarana, प्रहस्तसहिताः along with Prahasta, भग्नाः defeated, व्यद्रवन्त fled, मृगाः deer, इव like.
explanation: Those ministers of Ravana, namely Maricha, Shuka, Sarana, along with Prahasta, were defeated by Anaranya and fled like deer.

shloka_text: ततो बाणशतान्यष्टौ पातयामास मूर्धनि । तस्य राक्षसराजस्य इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः ।। 7.19.20 ।।
transliteration: tato bāṇaśatānyaṣṭau pātayāmāsa mūrdhani | tasya rākṣasarājasya ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ || 7.19.20 ||
translation: ततः then, बाणशतानि hundreds of arrows, अष्टौ eight, पातयामास shot, मूर्धनि on the head, तस्य of that, राक्षसराजस्य of the king of Rakshasas, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvaku family.
explanation: Then, the delight of the Ikshvaku family (King Anaranya) shot eight hundred arrows onto the head of that king of Rakshasas (Ravana).

shloka_text: तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित् । वारिधारा इवाभ्रेभ्यः पतन्त्यो गिरिमूर्धनि ।। 7.19.21 ।।
transliteration: tasya bāṇāḥ patantaste cakrire na kṣataṃ kvacit | vāridhārā ivābhrebhyaḥ patantyo girimūrdhani || 7.19.21 ||
translation: तस्य his, बाणाः arrows, पतन्तः falling, ते those, चक्रिरे caused, न not, क्षतम् injury, क्वचित् anywhere, वारिधाराः streams of water, इव like, अभ्रेभ्यः from clouds, पतन्त्यः falling, गिरिमूर्धनि on the mountain peak.
explanation: Those falling arrows of his caused no injury anywhere, just like streams of water falling from clouds onto a mountain peak.

shloka_text: ततो राक्षसराजेन क्रुद्धेन नृपतिस्तदा । तलेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि स रथान्निपपात ह ।। 7.19.22 ।।
transliteration: tato rākṣasarājena kruddhena nṛpatistadā | talenābhihato mūrdhni sa rathānnipapāta ha || 7.19.22 ||
translation: ततः then, राक्षसराजेन by the king of Rakshasas, क्रुद्धेन enraged, नृपतिः the king, तदा then, तलेनाभिहतः struck with the palm of the hand, मूर्ध्नि on the head, सः he, रथात् from the chariot, निपपात fell down, ह indeed.
explanation: Then, the enraged king of Rakshasas struck the king on the head with his palm, and he indeed fell down from his chariot.

shloka_text: स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलाङ्गः प्रवेपितः । वज्रदग्ध इवारण्ये सालो निपतितो यथा ।। 7.19.23 ।।
transliteration: sa rājā patito bhūmau vihvalāṅgaḥ pravepitaḥ | vajradagdha ivāraṇye sālo nipatito yathā || 7.19.23 ||
translation: सः that, राजा king, पतितः fallen, भूमौ on the ground, विह्वलाङ्गः with trembling limbs, प्रवेपितः greatly trembling, वज्रदग्धः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like, अरण्ये in the forest, सालः a Sala tree, निपतितः fallen, यथा just as.
explanation: That king, fallen on the ground with trembling and bewildered limbs, was greatly trembling, just like a Sala tree struck down by a thunderbolt in the forest.

shloka_text: तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद्द्रक्ष इक्ष्वाकुं पृथिवीपतिम् । किमिदानीं फलं प्राप्तं त्वया मां प्रति युद्ध्यता ।। 7.19.24 ।।
transliteration: taṃ prahasyābravīddrakṣa ikṣvākuṃ pṛthivīpatim | kimidānīṃ phalaṃ prāptaṃ tvayā māṃ prati yuddhyatā || 7.19.24 ||
translation: तम् to him, प्रहस्य laughing loudly, अब्रवीत् said, रक्षः the Rakshasa, इक्ष्वाकुम् to the Ikshvaku, पृथिवीपतिम् the king, किम् what, इदानीम् now, फलम् result, प्राप्तम् obtained, त्वया by you, माम् me, प्रति against, युद्ध्यता fighting.
explanation: Laughing loudly, the Rakshasa (Ravana) then said to that Ikshvaku king, "What result have you now obtained by fighting against me?"

shloka_text: त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यान्नराधिप । शङ्के प्रसक्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम ।। 7.19.25 ।।
transliteration: trailokye nāsti yo dvandvaṃ mama dadyānnarādhipa | śaṅke prasakto bhogeṣu na śṛṇoṣi balaṃ mama || 7.19.25 ||
translation: त्रैलोक्ये in the three worlds, न not, अस्ति there is, यः who, द्वन्द्वम् a challenge, मम to me, दद्यात् would give, नराधिप O king of men, शङ्के I suspect, प्रसक्तः attached, भोगेषु to pleasures, न not, शृणोषि you hear, बलम् strength, मम my.
explanation: O king of men, there is no one in the three worlds who can challenge me; I suspect you are too engrossed in pleasures to know my strength.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो राजा मन्दासुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् । किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः ।। 7.19.26 ।।
transliteration: tasyaivaṃ bruvato rājā mandāsurvākyamabravīt | kiṃ śakyamiha kartuṃ vai kālo hi duratikramaḥ || 7.19.26 ||
translation: तस्य to him, एवम् thus, ब्रुवतः speaking, राजा the king, मन्दासुः with failing life, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, किम् what, शक्यम् is possible, इह here, कर्तुम् to do, वै indeed, कालः time, हि for, दुरतिक्रमः difficult to overcome.
explanation: To him who spoke thus, the king, with his life ebbing away, replied, "What can be done now, for time is indeed insurmountable?"

shloka_text: नह्यहं निर्जितो रक्षस्त्वया चात्मप्रशंसिना । कालेनैव विपन्नो ऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान् ।। 7.19.27 ।।
transliteration: nahyahaṃ nirjito rakṣastvayā cātmapraśaṃsinā | kālenaiva vipanno 'haṃ hetubhūtastu me bhavān || 7.19.27 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, अहम् I, निर्जितः conquered, रक्षः O demon, त्वया by you, च and, आत्मप्रशंसिना self-praising, कालेन by time, एव alone, विपन्नः destroyed, अहम् I, हेतुभूतः being the cause, तु but, मे my, भवान् you.
explanation: O self-praising demon, I am not conquered by you; I am destroyed by time itself, and you are merely the instrument of my demise.

shloka_text: किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं प्राणपरिक्षये । नह्यहं विमुखी रक्षो युध्यमानस्त्वया हतः ।। 7.19.28 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ prāṇaparikṣaye | nahyahaṃ vimukhī rakṣo yudhyamānastvayā hataḥ || 7.19.28 ||
translation: किम् what, तु but, इदानीम् now, मया by me, शक्यम् is possible, कर्तुम् to do, प्राणपरिक्षये at the exhaustion of life, न not, हि indeed, अहम् I, विमुखी turning away, रक्षः O demon, युध्यमानः fighting, त्वया by you, हतः killed.
explanation: What can I possibly do now, with my life force depleted? O demon, I was not killed by you while turning away, but while fighting.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकुपरिभावित्वाद्वचो वक्ष्यामि राक्षस । यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः ।। यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक्तदा सत्यं वचो ऽस्तु मे ।। 7.19.29 ।।
transliteration: ikṣvākuparibhāvitvādvaco vakṣyāmi rākṣasa | yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ yadi me sukṛtaṃ tapaḥ || yadi guptāḥ prajāḥ samyaktadā satyaṃ vaco 'stu me || 7.19.29 ||
translation: इक्ष्वाकुपरिभावित्वात् due to being born in the Ikshvaku lineage, वचः words, वक्ष्यामि I will speak, राक्षस O demon, यदि if, दत्तम् given (charity), यदि if, हुतम् offered (sacrifices), यदि if, मे my, सुकृतम् well-performed, तपः penance, यदि if, गुप्ताः protected, प्रजाः subjects, सम्यक् properly, तदा then, सत्यम् true, वचः words, अस्तु let it be, मे my.
explanation: O demon, by virtue of my birth in the Ikshvaku lineage, I will speak these words: if I have given charity, offered sacrifices, performed penance well, and protected my subjects properly, then let my words be true.

shloka_text: उत्पत्स्यते कुले ह्यस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । रामो दाशरथिर्नाम यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति ।। 7.19.30 ।।
transliteration: utpatsyate kule hyasminnikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām | rāmo dāśarathirnāma yaste prāṇānhariṣyati || 7.19.30 ||
translation: उत्पत्स्यते will be born, कुले in the family, हि indeed, अस्मिन् in this, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् of the Ikshvakus, महात्मनाम् of the great-souled ones, रामः Rama, दाशरथिः son of Dasharatha, नाम named, यः who, ते your, प्राणान् lives, हरिष्यति will take away.
explanation: Indeed, in this family of the great-souled Ikshvakus, a son named Rama, the son of Dasharatha, will be born, who will take away your life.

shloka_text: ततो जलधरोदग्रस्ताडितो देवदुन्दुभिः । तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता ।। 7.19.31 ।।
transliteration: tato jaladharodagrastāḍito devadundubhiḥ | tasminnudāhṛte śāpe puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā || 7.19.31 ||
translation: ततः then, जलधरोदग्र mighty as a cloud, ताडितः struck, देवदुन्दुभिः the divine drum, तस्मिन् when that, उदाहृते was uttered, शापे curse, पुष्पवृष्टिः shower of flowers, च and, खात् from the sky, च्युता fell.
explanation: Then, as that curse was uttered, a divine drum, struck with a sound mighty as a cloud, resounded, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम् । स्वर्गते च नृपे तस्मिन्राक्षसः सो ऽपसर्पत ।। 7.19.32 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā rājendra gataḥ sthānaṃ triviṣṭapam | svargate ca nṛpe tasminrākṣasaḥ so 'pasarpata || 7.19.32 ||
translation: ततः then, सः that, राजा king, राजेन्द्र O king of kings, गतः went, स्थानम् to the abode, त्रिविष्टपम् of heaven, स्वर्गते having gone to heaven, च and, नृपे the king, तस्मिन् that, राक्षसः the demon, सः he, अपसर्पत departed.
explanation: Then, O king of kings, that king went to the abode of heaven, and when that king had ascended to heaven, the demon departed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः ।। 19 ।। Thus ends the nineteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो वित्रासयन्मर्त्यान्पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः । आससाद घने तस्मिन्नारदं मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।। 7.20.1 ।।
transliteration: tato vitrāsayanmartyānpṛthivyāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ | āsasāda ghane tasminnāradaṃ munipuṅgavam || 7.20.1 ||
translation: ततः then, वित्रासयन् terrifying, मर्त्यान् mortals, पृथिव्याम् on earth, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of demons, आससाद met, घने in that dense (region), तस्मिन् that, नारदम् Narada, मुनिपुङ्गवम् the foremost among sages.
explanation: Then, the lord of demons, terrifying mortals on earth, met Narada, the foremost among sages, in that dense region.
comments: Ravana meets the sage Narada, who, to turn him from tormenting the already death-bound mortal world, counsels that to conquer Yama is to conquer all -- delighted, Ravana vows to subdue Death and the world-guardians and sets off southward to Yama's abode -- marvelling that any could conquer Yama, Narada follows to witness the clash.

shloka_text: तस्याभिवादनं कृत्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । अब्रवीत्कुशलं पृष्ट्वा हेतुमागमनस्य च ।। 7.20.2 ।।
transliteration: tasyābhivādanaṃ kṛtvā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ | abravītkuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvā hetumāgamanasya ca || 7.20.2 ||
translation: तस्य his, अभिवादनम् salutation, कृत्वा having done, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, अब्रवीत् spoke, कुशलम् well-being, पृष्ट्वा having asked, हेतुम् the reason, आगमनस्य for coming, च and.
explanation: Having offered his salutations, Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, spoke after inquiring about his well-being and the reason for his arrival.

shloka_text: नारदस्तु महातेजा देवर्षिरमितप्रभः । अब्रवीन्मेघपृष्ठस्थो रावणं पुष्पके स्थितम् ।। 7.20.3 ।।
transliteration: nāradastu mahātejā devarṣiramitaprabhaḥ | abravīnmeghapṛṣṭhastho rāvaṇaṃ puṣpake sthitam || 7.20.3 ||
translation: नारदः Narada, तु indeed, महातेजा of great splendor, देवर्षिः the divine sage, अमितप्रभः of immeasurable effulgence, अब्रवीत् spoke, मेघपृष्ठस्थः situated on a cloud-top, रावणं to Ravana, पुष्पके in the Pushpaka (chariot), स्थितम् who was situated.
explanation: The divine sage Narada, of immense splendor and effulgence, spoke to Ravana, who was seated in the Pushpaka chariot, while Narada himself was positioned on a cloud-top.

shloka_text: राक्षसाधिपते सौम्य तिष्ठ विश्रवसः सुत । प्रीतो ऽस्म्यभिजनोपेतविक्रमैरूर्जितैस्तव ।। 7.20.4 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasādhipate saumya tiṣṭha viśravasaḥ suta | prīto 'smyabhijanopetavikramairūrjitaistava || 7.20.4 ||
translation: राक्षसाधिपते O lord of Rakshasas, सौम्य O gentle one, तिष्ठ stop, विश्रवसः of Vishravas, सुत O son, प्रीतो pleased, अस्मि I am, अभिजनोपेतविक्रमैः by valor endowed with noble birth, ऊर्जितैः mighty, तव your.
explanation: "O gentle lord of Rakshasas, son of Vishravas, stop," Narada said, "I am pleased by your mighty valor, which is befitting your noble lineage."

shloka_text: विष्णुना दैत्यघातैश्च गन्धर्वोरगधर्षणैः । त्वया समं विमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः ।। 7.20.5 ।।
transliteration: viṣṇunā daityaghātaiśca gandharvoragadharṣaṇaiḥ | tvayā samaṃ vimardaiśca bhṛśaṃ hi paritoṣitaḥ || 7.20.5 ||
translation: विष्णुना by Vishnu, दैत्यघातैः by the slaying of Daityas, च and, गन्धर्वोरगधर्षणैः by the subjugation of Gandharvas and Uragas, त्वया by you, समं equal, विमर्दैः by battles, च and, भृशं greatly, हि indeed, परितोषितः I am pleased.
explanation: I am indeed greatly pleased by your battles, which are comparable to Vishnu's slaying of demons and your subjugation of Gandharvas and Uragas.

shloka_text: किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तावत्ते श्रोतव्यं श्रोष्यसे यदि । श्रुत्वा चानन्तरं कार्यं त्वया राक्षससत्तम । तन्मे निगदतस्तात समाधिं श्रवणे कुरु ।। 7.20.6 ।।
transliteration: kiṃcidvakṣyāmi tāvatte śrotavyaṃ śroṣyase yadi | śrutvā cānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tvayā rākṣasasattama | tanme nigadatastāta samādhiṃ śravaṇe kuru || 7.20.6 ||
translation: किंचित् something, वक्ष्यामि I will say, तावत् first, ते to you, श्रोतव्यं to be heard, श्रोष्यसे you will hear, यदि if, श्रुत्वा having heard, च and, अनन्तरं afterwards, कार्यं to be done, त्वया by you, राक्षससत्तम O best of Rakshasas, तत् that, मे by me, निगदतः while speaking, तात O dear one, समाधिं attention, श्रवणे in listening, कुरु make.
explanation: I will first tell you something that should be heard, if you are willing to listen, and after hearing it, you, O best of Rakshasas, must act upon it; therefore, O dear one, pay close attention to my words.

shloka_text: किमयं वध्यते तात त्वया ऽवध्येन दैवतैः । हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः ।। 7.20.7 ।। ्तम ।
transliteration: kimayaṃ vadhyate tāta tvayā 'vadhyena daivataiḥ | hata eva hyayaṃ loko yadā mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ || 7.20.7 || ्tama |
translation: किम् why, अयं this (world/people), वध्यते is being killed, तात O dear one, त्वया by you, अवध्येन who is not to be killed, दैवतैः by gods, हतः killed, एव indeed, हि surely, अयं this, लोकः world/people, यदा when, मृत्युवशं under the sway of death, गतः gone.
explanation: O dear one, why do you kill this world, which is already destined to die and cannot be killed by the gods, when it is already under the sway of death?

shloka_text: देवदानवदैत्यानां यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् । अवध्येन त्वया लोकः क्लेष्टुं युक्तो न मानुषः ।। 7.20.8 ।।
transliteration: devadānavadaityānāṃ yakṣagandharvarakṣasām | avadhyena tvayā lokaḥ kleṣṭuṃ yukto na mānuṣaḥ || 7.20.8 ||
translation: देवदानवदैत्यानां of gods, danavas, and daityas, यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् of yakshas, gandharvas, and rakshasas, अवध्येन by one who is not to be killed, त्वया by you, लोकः the world, क्लेष्टुं to torment, युक्तो fit, न not, मानुषः human.
explanation: It is not proper for you, who are invincible to gods, danavas, daityas, yakshas, gandharvas, and rakshasas, to torment the human world.

shloka_text: नित्यं श्रेयसि सम्मूढं महद्भिर्व्यसनैर्वृतम् । हन्यात्कस्तादृशं लोकं जराव्याधिशतैर्युतम् ।। 7.20.9 ।।
transliteration: nityaṃ śreyasi sammūḍhaṃ mahadbhirvyasanairvṛtam | hanyātkastādṛśaṃ lokaṃ jarāvyādhiśatairyutam || 7.20.9 ||
translation: नित्यं constantly, श्रेयसि in welfare, सम्मूढं bewildered, महद्भिः by great, व्यसनैः calamities, वृतम् surrounded, हन्यात् would kill, कः who, तादृशं such, लोकं people, जराव्याधिशतैः by hundreds of old age and diseases, युतम् afflicted.
explanation: Who would kill such people who are constantly bewildered about their welfare, surrounded by great misfortunes, and afflicted by hundreds of old age and diseases?

shloka_text: तैस्तैरनिष्टोपगमैरजस्रं यत्र कुत्र कः । मतिमान्मानुषे लोके युद्धेन प्रणयी भवेत् ।। 7.20.10 ।।
transliteration: taistairaniṣṭopagamairajasraṃ yatra kutra kaḥ | matimānmānuṣe loke yuddhena praṇayī bhavet || 7.20.10 ||
translation: तैस्तैः by those various, अनिष्टोपगमैः by undesirable occurrences, अजस्रं constantly, यत्र where, कुत्र anywhere, कः who, मतिमान् intelligent, मानुषे in the human, लोके world, युद्धेन by war, प्रणयी desirous, भवेत् would be.
explanation: Who among the intelligent would be fond of war in the human world, which is constantly afflicted by various undesirable occurrences everywhere?

shloka_text: क्षीयमाणं दैवहतं श्रुत्पिपासाजरादिभिः । विषादशोकसम्मूढं लोकं त्वं क्षपयस्व मा ।। 7.20.11 ।।
transliteration: kṣīyamāṇaṃ daivahataṃ śrutpipāsājarādibhiḥ | viṣādaśokasammūḍhaṃ lokaṃ tvaṃ kṣapayasva mā || 7.20.11 ||
translation: क्षीयमाणं wasting away, दैवहतं struck by fate, श्रुत्पिपासाजरादिभिः by hunger, thirst, old age, and others, विषादशोकसम्मूढं bewildered by dejection and sorrow, लोकं people, त्वं you, क्षपयस्व destroy, मा not.
explanation: Do not you destroy the human world, which is already wasting away, struck by fate, afflicted by hunger, thirst, old age, and other miseries, and bewildered by dejection and sorrow.

shloka_text: पश्य तावन्महाबाहो राक्षसेश्वर मानुषम् । मूढमेवं विचित्रार्थं यस्य न ज्ञायते गतिः ।। 7.20.12 ।।
transliteration: paśya tāvanmahābāho rākṣaseśvara mānuṣam | mūḍhamevaṃ vicitrārthaṃ yasya na jñāyate gatiḥ || 7.20.12 ||
translation: पश्य behold, तावत just, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, राक्षसेश्वर O lord of Rakshasas, मानुषम् human being, मूढम् foolish, एवम् thus, विचित्रार्थं having strange purposes, यस्य whose, न not, ज्ञायते is known, गतिः destiny.
explanation: O mighty-armed lord of Rakshasas, just behold the human being, who is so foolish and whose strange nature or destiny is not truly known.

shloka_text: क्वचिद्वादित्रनृत्यादि सेव्यते मुदितैर्जनैः । रुद्यते चापरैरार्तैर्धाराश्रुनयनाननैः ।। 7.20.13 ।।
transliteration: kvacidvāditranṛtyādi sevyate muditairjanaiḥ | rudyate cāparairārtairdhārāśrunayanānanaiḥ || 7.20.13 ||
translation: क्वचित् at times, वादित्रनृत्यादि musical instruments and dance etc., सेव्यते are enjoyed, मुदितैः by joyful, जनैः people, रुद्यते is wept, च and, अपरैः by others, आर्तैः by distressed, धाराश्रुनयनाननैः with faces and eyes streaming with tears.
explanation: At times, joyful people engage in music and dance, while at other times, distressed individuals weep with faces and eyes streaming with tears.

shloka_text: मातापितृसुतस्नेहैर्भार्याबन्धुमनोरमैः । मोहितो ऽयं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते ।। 7.20.14 ।।
transliteration: mātāpitṛsutasnehairbhāryābandhumanoramaiḥ | mohito 'yaṃ jano dhvastaḥ kleśaṃ svaṃ nāvabudhyate || 7.20.14 ||
translation: मातापितृसुतस्नेहैः by the affections for mother, father, and son, भार्याबन्धुमनोरमैः by charming wife and relatives, मोहितः deluded, अयम् this, जनः person, ध्वस्तः afflicted, क्लेशम् suffering, स्वम् own, न not, अवबुध्यते understands.
explanation: Deluded by affection for parents, children, charming wives, and relatives, this afflicted person does not comprehend his own suffering.

shloka_text: अलमेनं परिक्लिश्य लोकं मोहनिराकृतम् । जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः ।। 7.20.15 ।।
transliteration: alamenaṃ parikliśya lokaṃ mohanirākṛtam | jita eva tvayā saumya martyaloko na saṃśayaḥ || 7.20.15 ||
translation: अलम् enough, एनम् this, परिक्लिश्य having tormented, लोकम् world, मोहनिराकृतम् overcome by delusion, जितः conquered, एव indeed, त्वया by you, सौम्य O gentle one, मर्त्यलोकः the mortal world, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: Enough of tormenting this world, which is already overcome by delusion; O gentle one, the mortal world has indeed been conquered by you, there is no doubt about it.

shloka_text: अवश्यमेभिः सर्वैश्च गन्तव्यं यमसादनम् । तन्निगृह्णीष्व पौलस्त्य यमं परपुरञ्जय ।। 7.20.16 ।।
transliteration: avaśyamebhiḥ sarvaiśca gantavyaṃ yamasādanam | tannigṛhṇīṣva paulastya yamaṃ parapurañjaya || 7.20.16 ||
translation: अवश्यम् inevitably, एभिः by these, सर्वैः all, च and, गन्तव्यम् must go, यमसादनम् to the abode of Yama, तत् therefore, निगृह्णीष्व subdue, पौलस्त्य O son of Pulastya, यमम् Yama, परपुरञ्जय O conqueror of enemy cities.
explanation: All these beings must inevitably go to the abode of Yama, therefore, O son of Pulastya, O conqueror of enemy cities, subdue Yama himself.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्जिते जितं सर्वं भवत्येव न संशयः । एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशो दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । अब्रवीन्नारदं तत्र सम्प्रहस्याभिवाद्य च ।। 7.20.17 ।।
transliteration: tasmiñjite jitaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ | evamuktastu laṅkeśo dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā | abravīnnāradaṃ tatra samprahasyābhivādya ca || 7.20.17 ||
translation: तस्मिन् when he, जिते is conquered, जितम् conquered, सर्वम् all, भवति becomes, एव indeed, न not, संशयः doubt, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, लङ्केशः the lord of Lanka, दीप्यमानम् shining, स्वतेजसा with his own splendor, अब्रवीत् spoke, नारदम् to Narada, तत्र there, सम्प्रहस्य having laughed heartily, अभिवाद्य having saluted, च and.
explanation: When Yama is conquered, everything is indeed conquered, there is no doubt; thus addressed, the lord of Lanka, shining with his own splendor, then spoke to Narada, having laughed heartily and saluted him.

shloka_text: महर्षे देवगन्धर्वविहार समरप्रिय । अहं समुद्यतो गन्तुं विजयार्थं रसातलम् ।। 7.20.18 ।।
transliteration: maharṣe devagandharvavihāra samarapriya | ahaṃ samudyato gantuṃ vijayārthaṃ rasātalam || 7.20.18 ||
translation: महर्षे O great sage, देवगन्धर्वविहार O one who sports with gods and gandharvas, समरप्रिय O lover of battle, अहम् I, समुद्यतः am ready, गन्तुम् to go, विजयार्थम् for the sake of victory, रसातलम् to Rasatala.
explanation: Ravana addresses the sage, declaring his readiness to descend to Rasatala for conquest.

shloka_text: ततो लोकत्रयं जित्वा स्थाप्य नागान्सुरान्वशे । समुद्रममृतार्थं च मथिष्यामि रसालयम् ।। 7.20.19 ।।
transliteration: tato lokatrayaṃ jitvā sthāpya nāgānsurānvaśe | samudramamṛtārthaṃ ca mathiṣyāmi rasālayam || 7.20.19 ||
translation: ततः Then, लोकत्रयम् the three worlds, जित्वा having conquered, स्थाप्य having placed, नागान् the Nagas, सुरान् the gods, वशे under control, समुद्रम् the ocean, अमृतार्थम् for the sake of nectar, च and, मथिष्यामि I will churn, रसालयम् the abode of waters.
explanation: Ravana further states that after conquering the three worlds and subjugating the Nagas and gods, he will churn the ocean for nectar.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीदृशग्रीवं नारदो भगवानृषिः । क्व खल्विदानीं मार्गेण त्वया ह्यन्येन गम्यते ।। 7.20.20 ।।
transliteration: athābravīdṛśagrīvaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ | kva khalvidānīṃ mārgeṇa tvayā hyanyena gamyate || 7.20.20 ||
translation: अथ Then, अब्रवीत् spoke, दशग्रीवम् to Dashagriva, नारदः Narada, भगवान् the divine, ऋषिः sage, क्व where, खलु indeed, इदानीम् now, मार्गेण by which path, त्वया by you, हि surely, अन्येन by another, गम्यते is it gone (are you going).
explanation: Then, the divine sage Narada asked Ravana, "By which path are you indeed going now?"

shloka_text: अयं खलु सुदुर्गम्यः प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति । मार्गो गच्छति दुर्धर्षो यमस्यामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.20.21 ।।
transliteration: ayaṃ khalu sudurgamyaḥ pretarājapuraṃ prati | mārgo gacchati durdharṣo yamasyāmitrakarśana || 7.20.21 ||
translation: अयम् This, खलु indeed, सुदुर्गम्यः very difficult to traverse, प्रेतराजपुरम् to the city of the king of the dead, प्रति towards, मार्गः path, गच्छति goes, दुर्धर्षः unassailable, यमस्य of Yama, अमित्रकर्शन O tormentor of enemies.
explanation: Narada warns Ravana that this path, O tormentor of enemies, is indeed very difficult to traverse and leads to the formidable city of Yama, the king of the dead.

shloka_text: स तु शारदमेघाभं हासं मुक्त्वा दशाननः । उवाच कृतमित्येव वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.20.22 ।।
transliteration: sa tu śāradameghābhaṃ hāsaṃ muktvā daśānanaḥ | uvāca kṛtamityeva vacanaṃ cedamabravīt || 7.20.22 ||
translation: सः He, तु but, शारदमेघाभम् resembling an autumn cloud, हासम् a laugh, मुक्त्वा having let out, दशाननः Dashanana, उवाच said, कृतम् done, इति एव thus only, वचनम् words, च and, इदम् these, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Dashanana, however, let out a laugh resembling an autumn cloud and then spoke these words, saying, "It is done."

shloka_text: तस्मादेवमहं ब्रह्मन् वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः । गच्छामि दक्षिणामाशां यत्र सूर्यात्मजो नृपः ।। 7.20.23 ।।
transliteration: tasmādevamahaṃ brahman vaivasvatavadhodyataḥ | gacchāmi dakṣiṇāmāśāṃ yatra sūryātmajo nṛpaḥ || 7.20.23 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, एवम् thus, अहम् I, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः intent on killing Vaivasvata (Yama), गच्छामि I go, दक्षिणाम् southern, आशाम् direction, यत्र where, सूर्यात्मजः the son of Surya, नृपः the king.
explanation: Therefore, O Brahmana, being thus intent on slaying Vaivasvata (Yama), I proceed to the southern direction where the son of Surya, the king (Yama), resides.

shloka_text: मया हि भगवन्क्रोधात्प्रतिज्ञातं रणार्थिना । अवजेष्यामि चतुरो लोकपालानिति प्रभो ।। 7.20.24 ।।
transliteration: mayā hi bhagavankrodhātpratijñātaṃ raṇārthinā | avajeṣyāmi caturo lokapālāniti prabho || 7.20.24 ||
translation: मया by me, हि indeed, भगवन् O revered one, क्रोधात् out of anger, प्रतिज्ञातम् it has been vowed, रणार्थिना by one desirous of battle, अवजेष्यामि I shall conquer, चतुरः the four, लोकपालान् guardians of the world, इति thus, प्रभो O lord.
explanation: Indeed, O revered one, I, desirous of battle, have vowed in my anger, "I shall conquer the four guardians of the world, O lord."

shloka_text: तदिह प्रस्थितो ऽहं वै प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति । प्राणिसङ्क्लेशकर्तारं योजयिष्यामि मृत्युना ।। 7.20.25 ।।
transliteration: tadiha prasthito 'haṃ vai pretarājapuraṃ prati | prāṇisaṅkleśakartāraṃ yojayiṣyāmi mṛtyunā || 7.20.25 ||
translation: तत् therefore, इह now, प्रस्थितः having set out, अहम् I, वै indeed, प्रेतराजपुरम् to the city of the king of the dead, प्रति towards, प्राणिसङ्क्लेशकर्तारम् the one who causes distress to living beings, योजयिष्यामि I shall unite, मृत्युना with death.
explanation: Therefore, I have now indeed set out towards the city of the king of the dead, and I shall unite with death the one who causes distress to living beings.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मुनिं तमभिवाद्य च । प्रययौ दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टः सह मन्त्रिभिः ।। 7.20.26 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā daśagrīvo muniṃ tamabhivādya ca | prayayau dakṣiṇāmāśāṃ praviṣṭaḥ saha mantribhiḥ || 7.20.26 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva (Ravana), मुनिम् the sage, तम् him, अभिवाद्य having saluted, च and, प्रययौ he departed, दक्षिणाम् southern, आशाम् direction, प्रविष्टः having entered, सह with, मन्त्रिभिः his ministers.
explanation: Having thus spoken and saluted that sage, Dashagriva (Ravana) departed towards the southern direction, accompanied by his ministers.

shloka_text: नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः । चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः ।। 7.20.27 ।।
transliteration: nāradastu mahātejā muhūrtaṃ dhyānamāsthitaḥ | cintayāmāsa viprendro vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ || 7.20.27 ||
translation: नारदः Narada, तु but, महातेजाः the greatly effulgent one, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, ध्यानम् meditation, आस्थितः having assumed, चिन्तयामास he pondered, विप्रेन्द्रः the chief among Brahmanas, विधूमः smokeless, इव like, पावकः fire.
explanation: But the greatly effulgent Narada, the chief among Brahmanas, having assumed meditation for a moment, pondered like a smokeless fire.

shloka_text: येन लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः क्लिश्यन्ते सचराचराः । क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मेण स कालो जेष्यते कथम् ।। 7.20.28 ।।
transliteration: yena lokāstrayaḥ sendrāḥ kliśyante sacarācarāḥ | kṣīṇe cāyuṣi dharmeṇa sa kālo jeṣyate katham || 7.20.28 ||
translation: येन by whom, लोकाः worlds, त्रयः three, सेन्द्राः including Indra, क्लिश्यन्ते are tormented, सचराचराः with all moving and non-moving beings, क्षीणे when exhausted, च and, आयुषि in lifespan, धर्मेण by the law of nature/dharma, सः that, कालः Time/Death, जेष्यते will be conquered, कथम् how
explanation: How can that Time, by whom the three worlds including Indra and all animate and inanimate beings are tormented, and by whose law life itself is exhausted, ever be conquered?

shloka_text: स्वदत्तकृतसाक्षी यो द्वितीय इव पावकः । लब्धसञ्ज्ञा विजेष्यन्ते लोका यस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.20.29 ।।
transliteration: svadattakṛtasākṣī yo dvitīya iva pāvakaḥ | labdhasañjñā vijeṣyante lokā yasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.20.29 ||
translation: स्वदत्तकृतसाक्षी who is a witness to one's own deeds, यः who, द्वितीयः second, इव like, पावकः fire, लब्धसञ्ज्ञाः having gained consciousness, विजेष्यन्ते will be conquered, लोकाः worlds, यस्य whose, महात्मनः of the great soul (Yama)
explanation: How can one conquer that great being (Yama), who is a witness to all deeds, like a second fire, and by whom all conscious beings in the worlds are eventually overcome?

shloka_text: यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः । तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽसौ स्वयमेव गमिष्यति ।। 7.20.30 ।।
transliteration: yasya nityaṃ trayo lokā vidravanti bhayārditāḥ | taṃ kathaṃ rākṣasendro 'sau svayameva gamiṣyati || 7.20.30 ||
translation: यस्य from whom, नित्यं always, त्रयः three, लोकाः worlds, विद्रवन्ति flee, भयार्दिताः tormented by fear, तं him, कथं how, राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of Rakshasas, असौ this, स्वयमेव by himself, गमिष्यति will go (to conquer)
explanation: How can this king of Rakshasas (Ravana) personally go to conquer him, from whom the three worlds always flee, tormented by fear?

shloka_text: यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा । त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं विजयिष्यते ।। 7.20.31 ।।
transliteration: yo vidhātā ca dhātā ca sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ tathā | trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ yena taṃ kathaṃ vijayiṣyate || 7.20.31 ||
translation: यः who, विधाता the ordainer, च and, धाता the sustainer, च and, सुकृतं good deeds, दुष्कृतं bad deeds, तथा also, त्रैलोक्यं the three worlds, विजितं conquered, येन by whom, तं him, कथं how, विजयिष्यते will he conquer
explanation: How will he conquer him who is the ordainer and sustainer of both good and bad deeds, and by whom the three worlds are already subdued?

shloka_text: अपरं किन्तु कृत्वायं विधानं संविधास्यति । कौतूहलसमुत्पन्नो यास्यामि यमसादनम् ।। 7.20.32 ।।
transliteration: aparaṃ kintu kṛtvāyaṃ vidhānaṃ saṃvidhāsyati | kautūhalasamutpanno yāsyāmi yamasādanam || 7.20.32 ||
translation: अपरं what else, किन्तु but, कृत्वा having done, अयं this (Ravana), विधानं arrangement, संविधास्यति will make, कौतूहलसमुत्पन्नः filled with curiosity, यास्यामि I will go, यमसादनम् to the abode of Yama
explanation: What other plan will this Ravana make after this, but filled with curiosity, I myself will go to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: विमर्दं द्रष्टुमनयोर्यमराक्षसयोः स्वयम् ।। 7.20.33 ।।
transliteration: vimardaṃ draṣṭumanayoryamarākṣasayoḥ svayam || 7.20.33 ||
translation: विमर्दं conflict, द्रष्टुम् to see, अनयोः of these two, यमराक्षसयोः of Yama and the Rakshasa, स्वयम् himself,
explanation: He himself wished to witness the conflict between Yama and the Rakshasa. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः ।। 20 ।। Thus ends the twentieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवं सञ्चिन्त्य विप्रेन्दो जगाम लघुविक्रमः । आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति ।। 7.21.1 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sañcintya viprendo jagāma laghuvikramaḥ | ākhyātuṃ tadyathāvṛttaṃ yamasya sadanaṃ prati || 7.21.1 ||
translation: एवम् thus, सञ्चिन्त्य having thought, विप्रेन्दो the best of Brahmins (Narada), जगाम went, लघुविक्रमः with swift steps, आख्यातुम् to tell, तत् that, यथावृत्तम् as it happened, यमस्य of Yama, सदनम् abode, प्रति towards,
explanation: Having thus pondered, Narada, moving swiftly, went towards Yama's abode to narrate the events as they had transpired.
comments: Narada hastens ahead to forewarn Yama -- entering Yama's realm, Ravana beholds the torments of the damned and the bliss of the righteous and sets free those being punished -- Yama's hosts fall upon him, and in the great battle Ravana's son, wielding the Pashupata weapon, consumes Yama's army with fire.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम् । विधानमुपतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम् ।। 7.21.2 ।।
transliteration: apaśyatsa yamaṃ tatra devamagnipuraskṛtam | vidhānamupatiṣṭhantaṃ prāṇino yasya yādṛśam || 7.21.2 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, स he, यमम् Yama, तत्र there, देवम् the god, अग्निपुरस्कृतम् with fire placed in front, विधानम् the ordinance, उपतिष्ठन्तम् administering, प्राणिनो of beings, यस्य whose, यादृशम् as it is,
explanation: There, Narada saw the god Yama, honored by fire, administering the fate of all beings as it was ordained for each.

shloka_text: स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम् । अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः ।। 7.21.3 ।।
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṃ maharṣiṃ tatra nāradam | abravītsukhamāsīnamarghyamāvedya dharmataḥ || 7.21.3 ||
translation: स he, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, यमः Yama, प्राप्तम् arrived, महर्षिम् the great sage, तत्र there, नारदम् Narada, अब्रवीत् he spoke, सुखमासीनम् comfortably seated, अर्घ्यम् water offering, आवेद्य having offered, धर्मतः according to dharma,
explanation: Upon seeing the great sage Narada arrive there, Yama, having properly offered him a water offering and seated him comfortably, then spoke.

shloka_text: कच्चित्क्षेमं तु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति । किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित ।। 7.21.4 ।।
transliteration: kaccitkṣemaṃ tu devarṣe kacciddharmo na naśyati | kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ te devagandharvasevita || 7.21.4 ||
translation: कच्चित् is it that, क्षेमम् well-being, तु indeed, देवर्षे O divine sage, कच्चित् is it that, धर्मो dharma, न not, नश्यति perishes, किम् what, आगमनकृत्यम् purpose of arrival, ते your, देवगन्धर्वसेवित O one served by gods and gandharvas,
explanation: Yama asked, "O divine sage, is all well with you, and is dharma not perishing? What is the purpose of your visit, O one revered by gods and gandharvas?"

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः । श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम् ।। 7.21.5 ।।
transliteration: abravīttu tadā vākyaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ | śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi vidhānaṃ ca vidhīyatām || 7.21.5 ||
translation: अब्रवीत् spoke, तु indeed, तदा then, वाक्यं words, नारदः Narada, भगवान् revered, ऋषिः sage, श्रूयताम् listen, अभिधास्यामि I will tell, विधानं the plan, च and, विधीयताम् let it be done.
explanation: Then, the revered sage Narada spoke these words: "Listen, I will tell you the plan, and let it be carried out."

shloka_text: एष नाम्नो दशग्रीवः पितृराज निशाचरः । उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रमैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम् ।। 7.21.6 ।।
transliteration: eṣa nāmno daśagrīvaḥ pitṛrāja niśācaraḥ | upayāti vaśaṃ netuṃ vikramaistvāṃ sudurjayam || 7.21.6 ||
translation: एषः this one, नाम्नः by name, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, पितृराज O King of Pitrus, निशाचरः the demon, उपयाति approaches, वशं under control, नेतुं to bring, विक्रमैः by his valor, त्वां you, सुदुर्जयम् who are very difficult to conquer.
explanation: O King of Pitrus, this demon named Dashagriva is approaching to bring you, who are very difficult to conquer, under his control through his valor.

shloka_text: एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो । दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति ।। 7.21.7 ।।
transliteration: etena kāraṇenāhaṃ tvarito hyāgataḥ prabho | daṇḍapraharaṇasyādya tava kiṃ nu bhaviṣyati || 7.21.7 ||
translation: एतेन by this, कारणेन reason, अहं I, त्वरितः quickly, हि indeed, आगतः have come, प्रभो O Lord, दण्डप्रहरणस्य of the wielder of the staff, अद्य today, तव your, किं what, नु indeed, भविष्यति will happen.
explanation: O Lord, it is for this reason that I have quickly come; what will happen today to you, the wielder of the staff of punishment?

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दुरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम् । ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.21.8 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare durādaṃśumantamivoditam | dadṛśurdīptamāyāntaṃ vimānaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ || 7.21.8 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, अन्तरे interval, दुरात् from afar, अंशुमन्तम् the sun, इव like, उदितम् risen, ददृशुः they saw, दीप्तम् shining, आयान्तं coming, विमानं the aerial chariot, तस्य his, रक्षसः of the demon.
explanation: In the meantime, from afar, they saw the demon's radiant aerial chariot approaching, shining like the rising sun.

shloka_text: तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः । कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.21.9 ।।
transliteration: taṃ deśaṃ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ | kṛtvā vitimiraṃ sarvaṃ samīpaṃ so 'bhyavartata || 7.21.9 ||
translation: तं that, देशं region, प्रभया by the radiance, तस्य of that, पुष्पकस्य Pushpaka, महाबलः the mighty one, कृत्वा having made, वितिमिरं free from darkness, सर्वं all, समीपं near, सः he, अभ्यवर्तत approached.
explanation: The mighty one, Ravana, having illuminated the entire region with the radiance of his Pushpaka chariot, then approached that place.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः । प्राणिनः सुकृतं कर्म भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम् ।। 7.21.10 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyatsa mahābāhurdaśagrīvastatastataḥ | prāṇinaḥ sukṛtaṃ karma bhuñjānāṃścaiva duṣkṛtam || 7.21.10 ||
translation: सः he, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, अपश्यत् saw, ततस्ततः here and there, प्राणिनः living beings, सुकृतं कर्म good deeds, भुञ्जानान् experiencing, च and, एव indeed, दुष्कृतम् evil deeds.
explanation: The mighty-armed Dashagriva saw living beings everywhere experiencing the fruits of both their good and evil deeds.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह । यमस्य पुरुषैरुग्रैर्घोररूपैर्भयानकैः ।। 7.21.11 ।।
transliteration: apaśyatsainikāṃścāsya yamasyānucaraiḥ saha | yamasya puruṣairugrairghorarūpairbhayānakaiḥ || 7.21.11 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, सैनिकान् soldiers, च and, अस्य his, यमस्य of Yama, अनुचरैः attendants, सह with, यमस्य of Yama, पुरुषैः by men, उग्रैः fierce, घोररूपैः of dreadful form, भयानकैः terrifying.
explanation: He also saw Yama's soldiers along with his fierce, dreadful, and terrifying attendants.

shloka_text: ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च क्लिश्यमानांश्च देहिनः । क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् ।। 7.21.12 ।।
transliteration: dadarśa vadhyamānāṃśca kliśyamānāṃśca dehinaḥ | krośataśca mahānādaṃ tīvraniṣṭanatatparān || 7.21.12 ||
translation: ददर्श he saw, वध्यमानान् being killed, च and, क्लिश्यमानान् being tormented, च and, देहिनः embodied beings, क्रोशतः crying out, च and, महानादं a great cry, तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् intent on intense wailing.
explanation: He saw embodied beings being killed and tormented, crying out with a great cry and intent on intense wailing.

shloka_text: कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः ।। 7.21.13 ।।
transliteration: kṛmibhirbhakṣyamāṇāṃśca sārameyaiśca dāruṇaiḥ || 7.21.13 ||
translation: कृमिभिः by worms, भक्ष्यमाणान् being devoured, च and, सारमेयैः by dogs, च and, दारुणैः fierce.
explanation: He saw them being devoured by worms and by fierce dogs.

shloka_text: क्षोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः । सन्तार्यमाणान्वैतरणीं बहुशः शोणितोदकाम् ।। 7.21.14 ।।
transliteration: kṣotrāyāsakarā vāco vadataśca bhayāvahāḥ | santāryamāṇānvaitaraṇīṃ bahuśaḥ śoṇitodakām || 7.21.14 ||
translation: क्षोत्रायासकराः causing distress to the ears, वाचः words, वदतः speaking, च and, भयावहाः terrifying, सन्तार्यमाणान् being made to cross, वैतरणीं the Vaitarani, बहुशः repeatedly, शोणितोदकाम् having blood as water.
explanation: He heard them uttering terrifying cries that caused distress to the ears, and saw them repeatedly being made to cross the Vaitarani river, whose waters were blood.

shloka_text: वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान्मुहूर्मुहुः । असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान् ।। 7.21.15 ।।
transliteration: vālukāsu ca taptāsu tapyamānānmuhūrmuhuḥ | asipatravane caiva bhidyamānānadhārmikān || 7.21.15 ||
translation: वालुकासु in sands, च and, तप्तासु hot, तप्यमानान् being tormented, मुहूर्मुहुः again and again, असिपत्रवने in the forest of sword-leaves, च and, एव indeed, भिद्यमानान् being cut/pierced, अधार्मिकान् the unrighteous ones
explanation: Ravana saw the unrighteous being tormented repeatedly in hot sands and cut in the forest of sword-leaves.

shloka_text: रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि । पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान्क्षुधितानपि ।। 7.21.16 ।।
transliteration: raurave kṣāranadyāṃ ca kṣuradhārāsu caiva hi | pānīyaṃ yācamānāṃśca tṛṣitānkṣudhitānapi || 7.21.16 ||
translation: रौरवे in Raurava (hell), क्षारनद्यां in the river of caustic liquid, च and, क्षुरधारासु on razor-sharp edges, च and, एव indeed, हि surely, पानीयं water, याचमानांश्च and begging, तृषितान् thirsty, क्षुधितानपि and hungry
explanation: He also saw them in Raurava hell, in the caustic river, and on razor-sharp edges, begging for water while thirsty and hungry.

shloka_text: शवभूतान्कृशान्दीनान्विवर्णान्मुक्तमूर्धजान् । मलपङ्कधरान्दीनान्रूक्षांश्च परिधावतः ।। 7.21.17 ।।
transliteration: śavabhūtānkṛśāndīnānvivarṇānmuktamūrdhajān | malapaṅkadharāndīnānrūkṣāṃśca paridhāvataḥ || 7.21.17 ||
translation: शवभूतान् like corpses, कृशान् emaciated, दीनान् miserable, विवर्णान् discolored, मुक्तमूर्धजान् with disheveled hair, मलपङ्कधरान् covered in dirt and mud, दीनान् miserable, रूक्षान् rough (in appearance), च and, परिधावतः running around
explanation: These miserable beings appeared like corpses, emaciated, discolored, with disheveled hair, covered in dirt and mud, and were running around frantically.

shloka_text: ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः । प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद्रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः ।। 7.21.18 ।।
transliteration: dadarśa rāvaṇo mārge śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ | kāṃścicca gṛhamukhyeṣu gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ | pramodamānānadrākṣīdrāvaṇaḥ sukṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ || 7.21.18 ||
translation: ददर्श saw, रावणो Ravana, मार्गे on the path, शतशो by hundreds, अथ then, सहस्रशः by thousands, कांश्चित् some, च and, गृहमुख्येषु in excellent houses, गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः with sounds of singing and musical instruments, प्रमोदमानान् rejoicing, अद्राक्षीत् saw, रावणः Ravana, सुकृतैः by their good deeds, स्वकैः own
explanation: Ravana saw hundreds and thousands of such beings on his path, but he also saw others rejoicing in splendid houses with sounds of music and singing, enjoying the fruits of their own good deeds.

shloka_text: गौरसं गोप्रदातारो ह्यन्नं चैवान्नदायिनः । गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः ।। 7.21.19 ।।
transliteration: gaurasaṃ gopradātāro hyannaṃ caivānnadāyinaḥ | gṛhāṃśca gṛhadātāraḥ svakarmaphalamaśnataḥ || 7.21.19 ||
translation: गौरसं milk products (or cows), गोप्रदातारो givers of cows, हि indeed, अन्नं food, च and, एव indeed, अन्नदायिनः givers of food, गृहान् houses, च and, गृहदातारः givers of houses, स्वकर्मफलम् the fruit of their own actions, अश्नतः enjoying
explanation: Those who gave cows enjoyed milk products, givers of food enjoyed food, and givers of houses enjoyed houses, thus partaking in the fruits of their own good deeds.

shloka_text: सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलङ्कृतान् ।। 7.21.20 ।।
transliteration: suvarṇamaṇimuktābhiḥ pramadābhiralaṅkṛtān || 7.21.20 ||
translation: सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः with gold, gems, and pearls, प्रमदाभिः by beautiful women, अलङ्कृतान् adorned.
explanation: This describes beings who were adorned by beautiful women with gold, gems, and pearls.

shloka_text: धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान्स्वतेजसा । ददर्श सुमहाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.21 ।।
transliteration: dhārmikānaparāṃstatra dīpyamānānsvatejasā | dadarśa sumahābāhū rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.21.21 ||
translation: धार्मिकान् righteous ones, अपरान् others, तत्र there, दीप्यमानान् shining, स्वतेजसा by their own splendor, ददर्श saw, सुमहाबाहू the very mighty-armed, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: The very mighty-armed Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, saw other righteous beings there, shining with their own splendor.

shloka_text: ततस्तान्भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः । रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाद्बली ।। 7.21.22 ।।
transliteration: tatastānbhidyamānāṃśca karmabhirduṣkṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ | rāvaṇo mocayāmāsa vikrameṇa balādbalī || 7.21.22 ||
translation: ततः then, तान् them, भिद्यमानांश्च and being tormented, कर्मभिः by deeds, दुष्कृतैः evil, स्वकैः their own, रावणो Ravana, मोचयामास released, विक्रमेण by valor, बलात् by force, बली the powerful one.
explanation: Then, the powerful Ravana, by his valor and force, released those who were being tormented by their own evil deeds.

shloka_text: प्राणिनो मोचितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा । सुखमापुर्मुहूर्तं ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम् ।। 7.21.23 ।।
transliteration: prāṇino mocitāstena daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā | sukhamāpurmuhūrtaṃ te hyatarkitamacintitam || 7.21.23 ||
translation: प्राणिनो the beings, मोचिताः released, तेन by him, दशग्रीवेण by Dashagriva, रक्षसा by the Rakshasa, सुखम् happiness, आपूः attained, मुहूर्तं for a moment, ते they, हि indeed, अतर्कितम् unexpected, अचिन्तितम् unthought of.
explanation: The beings released by that Rakshasa Dashagriva indeed attained unexpected and unthought-of happiness for a moment.

shloka_text: प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा । प्रेतगोपाः सुसङ्क्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन् ।। 7.21.24 ।।
transliteration: preteṣu mucyamāneṣu rākṣasena mahīyasā | pretagopāḥ susaṅkruddhā rākṣasendramabhidravan || 7.21.24 ||
translation: प्रेतेषु when the dead, मुच्यमानेषु were being released, राक्षसेन by the Rakshasa, महीयसा the mighty, प्रेतगोपाः the guardians of the dead, सुसङ्क्रुद्धाः very enraged, राक्षसेन्द्रम् towards the lord of Rakshasas, अभिद्रवन् rushed.
explanation: When the dead were being released by the mighty Rakshasa, the guardians of the dead became very enraged and rushed towards the lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः । धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां सम्प्रधावताम् ।। 7.21.25 ।।
transliteration: tato halahalāśabdaḥ sarvadigbhyaḥ samutthitaḥ | dharmarājasya yodhānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ sampradhāvatām || 7.21.25 ||
translation: ततः then, हलहलाशब्दः a tumultuous sound, सर्वदिग्भ्यः from all directions, समुत्थितः arose, धर्मराजस्य of Yama, योधानाम् of the warriors, शूराणाम् of the brave ones, सम्प्रधावताम् who were rushing forward.
explanation: Then, a great tumultuous roar arose from all directions, made by the brave warriors of Yama who were charging forward.

shloka_text: ते प्रासैः परिघैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः । पुष्पकं समवर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.26 ।।
transliteration: te prāsaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlairmusalaiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ | puṣpakaṃ samavarṣanta śūrāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ || 7.21.26 ||
translation: ते they, प्रासैः with spears, परिघैः with iron clubs, शूलैः with lances, मुसलैः with maces, शक्तितोमरैः with javelins and lances, पुष्पकम् upon the Pushpaka, समवर्षन्त showered, शूराः the brave ones, शतसहस्रशः by hundreds of thousands.
explanation: Hundreds of thousands of those brave warriors showered the Pushpaka chariot with spears, iron clubs, lances, maces, javelins, and other missiles.

shloka_text: तस्यासनानि प्रासादान्वेदिकास्तोरणानि च । पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव ।। 7.21.27 ।।
transliteration: tasyāsanāni prāsādānvedikāstoraṇāni ca | puṣpakasya babhañjuste śīghraṃ madhukarā iva || 7.21.27 ||
translation: ते they, पुष्पकस्य of the Pushpaka, आसनानि its seats, प्रासादान् its palaces, वेदिकाः its platforms, तोरणानि its archways, च and, बभञ्जुः broke, शीघ्रम् quickly, मधुकराः bees, इव like.
explanation: They quickly shattered the seats, palaces, platforms, and archways of the Pushpaka chariot, just like bees.

shloka_text: देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे । भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा ।। 7.21.28 ।।
transliteration: devaniṣṭhānabhūtaṃ tadvimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ mṛdhe | bhajyamānaṃ tathaivāsīdakṣayaṃ brahmatejasā || 7.21.28 ||
translation: तत् that, देवनिष्ठानभूतम् which was a dwelling place of gods, विमानम् aerial chariot, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, मृधे in battle, भज्यमानम् being broken, तथैव even so, ब्रह्मतेजसा by the power of Brahma, अक्षयम् indestructible, आसीत् remained.
explanation: Even though that divine Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was a dwelling place for gods, was being shattered in battle, it remained indestructible due to the power of Brahma.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्या सुमहत्यासीत्तस्य सेना महात्मनः । शूराणामग्रयातऽणां सहस्राणि शतानि च ।। 7.21.29 ।।
transliteration: asaṅkhyā sumahatyāsīttasya senā mahātmanaḥ | śūrāṇāmagrayāta'ṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca || 7.21.29 ||
translation: तस्य his, महात्मनः of the great-souled one (Yama), सेना army, असङ्ख्या countless, सुमहती very great, आसीत् was, शूराणाम् of brave ones, अग्रयातानाम् who were leading, शतानि hundreds, च and, सहस्राणि thousands.
explanation: The army of that great-souled Yama was immeasurably vast, comprising hundreds and thousands of brave warriors leading the charge.

shloka_text: ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा । ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम् । अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः ।। 7.21.30 ।।
transliteration: tato vṛkṣaiśca śailaiśca prāsādānāṃ śataistathā | tataste sacivāstasya yathākāmaṃ yathābalam | ayudhyanta mahāvīrāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ || 7.21.30 ||
translation: ततः then, वृक्षैः च with trees and, शैलैः च with mountains and, प्रासादानाम् शतैः तथा with hundreds of palaces also, ततः then, ते those, सचिवाः तस्य his ministers, यथाकामम् as desired, यथाबलम् according to their strength, अयुध्यन्त fought, महावीराः great heroes, सः च and he, राजा king, दशाननः Dashanana.
explanation: Then, those great heroic ministers of Ravana, along with King Dashanana himself, fought using trees, mountains, and hundreds of palaces, as they wished and according to their strength.

shloka_text: ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः । अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत् ।। 7.21.31 ।।
transliteration: te tu śoṇitadigdhāṅgāḥ sarvaśastrasamāhatāḥ | amātyā rākṣasendrasya cakrurāyodhanaṃ mahat || 7.21.31 ||
translation: ते तु but they, शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः whose limbs were smeared with blood, सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः struck by all weapons, अमात्याः ministers, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of Rakshasas, चक्रुः waged, आयोधनम् battle, महत् great.
explanation: Though their limbs were smeared with blood and they were struck by all sorts of weapons, those ministers of the Rakshasa king waged a great battle.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणैर्भृशम् । यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः ।। 7.21.32 ।।
transliteration: anyonyaṃ te mahābhāgā jaghnuḥ praharaṇairbhṛśam | yamasya ca mahābāho rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇaḥ || 7.21.32 ||
translation: अन्योन्यम् each other, ते those, महाभागाः great ones, जघ्नुः struck, प्रहरणैः with weapons, भृशम् fiercely, यमस्य च and of Yama, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, रावणस्य च and of Ravana, मन्त्रिणः ministers.
explanation: O mighty-armed one, those great ministers of Yama and Ravana fiercely struck each other with their weapons.

shloka_text: अमात्यांस्तांस्तु सन्त्यज्य यमयोधा महाबलाः । तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्षैर्दशाननम् ।। 7.21.33 ।।
transliteration: amātyāṃstāṃstu santyajya yamayodhā mahābalāḥ | tameva cābhyadhāvanta śūlavarṣairdaśānanam || 7.21.33 ||
translation: अमात्यान् तान् तु but those ministers, सन्त्यज्य abandoning, यमयोधाः Yama's warriors, महाबलाः mighty, तम् एव च and him alone, अभ्यधावन्त rushed towards, शूलवर्षैः with showers of spears, दशाननम् Dashanana.
explanation: The mighty warriors of Yama, abandoning those ministers, rushed directly towards Dashanana (Ravana) with showers of spears.

shloka_text: ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः । फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.34 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtaḥ | phullāśoka ivābhāti puṣpake rākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.21.34 ||
translation: ततः then, शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः whose limbs were smeared with blood, प्रहारैः by blows, जर्जरीकृतः wounded, फुल्ल अशोकः a blooming Ashoka tree, इव like, आभाति appeared, पुष्पके on the Pushpaka, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: Then, the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, with his limbs smeared with blood and wounded by the blows, appeared on his Pushpaka chariot like a blooming Ashoka tree.

shloka_text: स तु शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् । मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली ।। 7.21.35 ।।
transliteration: sa tu śūlagadāpāsāñchaktitomarasāyakān | musalāni śilāvṛkṣānmumocāstrabalādbalī || 7.21.35 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् spears, maces, nooses, shaktis, javelins, and arrows, मुसलानि pestles, शिलावृक्षान् stones and trees, मुमोच hurled, अस्त्रबलात् by the power of his weapons, बली the powerful one.
explanation: The powerful one indeed hurled spears, maces, nooses, shaktis, javelins, arrows, pestles, stones, and trees, empowered by his missile knowledge.

shloka_text: तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम् । यमसैन्येषु तद्वर्षं पपात धरणीतले ।। 7.21.36 ।।
transliteration: tarūṇāṃ ca śilānāṃ ca śastrāṇāṃ cātidāruṇam | yamasainyeṣu tadvarṣaṃ papāta dharaṇītale || 7.21.36 ||
translation: तरूणां of trees, च and, शिलानां of stones, च and, शस्त्राणां of weapons, च and, अतिदारुणम् very terrible, तत् that, वर्षं shower, यमसैन्येषु upon Yama's armies, पपात fell, धरणीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: That extremely terrible shower of trees, stones, and weapons fell upon Yama's armies on the surface of the earth.

shloka_text: तांस्तु सर्वान्विनिर्भिद्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च । जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.37 ।।
transliteration: tāṃstu sarvānvinirbhidya tadastramapahatya ca | jaghnuste rākṣasaṃ ghoramekaṃ śatasahasraśaḥ || 7.21.37 ||
translation: तान् them, तु but, सर्वान् all, विनिर्भिद्य having pierced through, तत् that, अस्त्रम् weapon, अपहत्य having repelled, च and, जघ्नुः they struck, ते they, राक्षसं the demon, घोरम् terrible, एकं one, शतसहस्रशः by hundreds of thousands.
explanation: But having pierced through all those weapons and repelled that missile, Yama's soldiers, in hundreds of thousands, struck that single terrible demon.

shloka_text: परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मोघोत्करा इव । भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमपोथयन् ।। 7.21.38 ।।
transliteration: parivārya ca taṃ sarve śailaṃ moghotkarā iva | bhindipālaiśca śūlaiśca nirucchvāsamapothayan || 7.21.38 ||
translation: परिवार्य having surrounded, च and, तं him, सर्वे all, शैलं a mountain, मोघोत्करा dense clouds, इव like, भिन्दिपालैः with bhindipalas, च and, शूलैः with spears, च and, निरुच्छ्वासम् breathless, अपोथयन् they crushed.
explanation: And all of them, having surrounded him like dense clouds surrounding a mountain, crushed him with bhindipalas and spears until he was breathless.

shloka_text: विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिक्तः शोणितविस्रवैः । ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत ।। 7.21.39 ।।
transliteration: vimuktakavacaḥ kruddhaḥ siktaḥ śoṇitavisravaiḥ | tataḥ sa puṣpakaṃ tyaktvā pṛthivyāmavatiṣṭhata || 7.21.39 ||
translation: विमुक्तकवचः with his armor loosened, क्रुद्धः enraged, सिक्तः drenched, शोणितविस्रवैः with streams of blood, ततः then, सः he, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, पृथिव्याम् on the earth, अवतिष्ठत stood.
explanation: With his armor loosened, enraged, and drenched in streams of blood, he then abandoned the Pushpaka chariot and stood on the earth.

shloka_text: ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्तत । लब्धसञ्ज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः ।। 7.21.40 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa kārmukī vāṇī samare cābhivartata | labdhasañjño muhūrtena kruddhastasthau yathāntakaḥ || 7.21.40 ||
translation: ततः then, स he, कार्मुकी one with a bow, वाणी (the warrior) Indrajit, समरे in battle, च and, अभिवर्तत advanced, लब्धसञ्ज्ञः having regained consciousness, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, क्रुद्धः enraged, तस्थौ stood, यथान्तकः like Yama.
explanation: Then, the bow-wielding Indrajit, having regained consciousness in a moment, stood enraged in battle like the god of death.

shloka_text: ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं सन्धाय कार्मुके । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं विचकर्ष स ।। 7.21.41 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pāśupataṃ divyamastraṃ sandhāya kārmuke | tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tānuktvā taccāpaṃ vicakarṣa sa || 7.21.41 ||
translation: ततः then, पाशुपतम् the Pāśupata, दिव्यम् divine, अस्त्रम् weapon, सन्धाय having fixed, कार्मुके on the bow, तिष्ठ तिष्ठ Stop! Stop!, इति thus, तान् them, उक्त्वा having said, तत् that, चापम् bow, विचकर्ष drew, स he.
explanation: Then, he fixed the divine Pāśupata weapon on his bow, and having told them "Stop! Stop!", he drew that bow.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे । मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शङ्करो यथा ।। 7.21.42 ।।
transliteration: ākarṇātsa vikṛṣyātha cāpamindrārirāhave | mumoca taṃ śaraṃ kruddhastripure śaṅkaro yathā || 7.21.42 ||
translation: आकर्णात् up to his ear, स he, विकृष्य having drawn, अथ then, चापम् the bow, इन्द्रारिः the enemy of Indra (Indrajit), आहवे in battle, मुमोच released, तम् that, शरम् arrow, क्रुद्धः enraged, त्रिपुरे at Tripura, शङ्करः Shiva, यथा just as.
explanation: Then, Indrajit, the enemy of Indra, enraged in battle, drew his bow up to his ear and released that arrow, just as Shiva did at Tripura.

shloka_text: तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत्विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् । वनं दहिष्यतो घर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः ।। 7.21.43 ।।
transliteration: tasya rūpaṃ śarasyāsītvidhūmajvālamaṇḍalam | vanaṃ dahiṣyato gharme dāvāgneriva mūrcchataḥ || 7.21.43 ||
translation: तस्य its, रूपम् form, शरस्य of the arrow, आसीत् was, विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् a smokeless circle of flames, वनम् a forest, दहिष्यतः about to burn, घर्मे in summer, दावाग्नेः of a forest fire, इव like, मूर्च्छतः raging.
explanation: The form of that arrow was a smokeless circle of flames, like a raging forest fire intensifying in summer, about to consume a forest.

shloka_text: ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे । मुक्तो गुल्मान्द्रुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति ।। 7.21.44 ।।
transliteration: jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe | mukto gulmāndrumāṃścāpi bhasma kṛtvā pradhāvati || 7.21.44 ||
translation: ज्वालामाली having a garland of flames, स that, तु indeed, शरः arrow, क्रव्यादानुगतः followed by flesh-eaters, रणे in battle, मुक्तः released, गुल्मान् bushes, द्रुमान् trees, च and, अपि even, भस्म ashes, कृत्वा having made, प्रधावति rushes forward.
explanation: That arrow, wreathed in flames and followed by flesh-eating demons, once released in battle, rushed forward, turning bushes and even trees into ashes.

shloka_text: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु । रणे तस्मिन्निपतिता दावदग्धा नगा इव ।। 7.21.45 ।।
