shloka_text: श्रुत्वैतद्राघवो वाक्यमगस्त्यस्योग्रतेजसः । प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतश्चापि महर्षिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.36.54 ।।
transliteration: śrutvaitadrāghavo vākyamagastyasyogratejasaḥ | prāñjaliḥ praṇataścāpi maharṣimidamabravīt || 7.36.54 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, एतत् this, राघवः Rama, वाक्यम् speech, अगस्त्यस्य of Agastya, उग्रतेजसः of mighty ascetic power, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, प्रणतः bowed down, च and, अपि also, महर्षिम् to the great sage, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard this speech of Agastya, who possessed mighty ascetic power, Rama, with folded hands and bowing down, spoke this to the great sage.

shloka_text: अद्य मे देवता हृष्टाः पितरः प्रपितामहाः । युष्माकं दर्शनादेव नित्यं तुष्टाः सबान्धवाः ।। 7.36.55 ।।
transliteration: adya me devatā hṛṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ prapitāmahāḥ | yuṣmākaṃ darśanādeva nityaṃ tuṣṭāḥ sabāndhavāḥ || 7.36.55 ||
translation: अद्य today, मे my, देवताः deities, हृष्टाः pleased, पितरः ancestors, प्रपितामहाः great-grandfathers, युष्माकम् your, दर्शनात् by the sight, एव only, नित्यम् always, तुष्टाः satisfied, सबान्धवाः with relatives.
explanation: Rama declared that today his deities, ancestors, and great-grandfathers, along with their relatives, were always pleased merely by the sight of Agastya.

shloka_text: विज्ञाप्यं तु ममैतद्धि यद्वदाम्यागतस्पृहः । तद्भवद्भिर्मम कृते कर्तव्यमनुकम्पया ।। 7.36.56 ।।
transliteration: vijñāpyaṃ tu mamaitaddhi yadvadāmyāgataspṛhaḥ | tadbhavadbhirmama kṛte kartavyamanukampayā || 7.36.56 ||
translation: विज्ञाप्यम् a request, तु indeed, मम my, एतत् this, हि indeed, यत् which, वदामि I speak, आगतस्पृहः eagerly, तत् that, भवद्भिः by you, मम for my, कृते sake, कर्तव्यम् should be done, अनुकम्पया with compassion.
explanation: Rama then stated that the request he was eagerly making should indeed be fulfilled by Agastya out of compassion for him.

shloka_text: पौरजानपदान्स्थाप्य स्वकार्येष्वहमागतः । क्रतूनेव करिष्यामि प्रभावाद्भवतां सताम् ।। 7.36.57 ।।
transliteration: paurajānapadānsthāpya svakāryeṣvahamāgataḥ | kratūneva kariṣyāmi prabhāvādbhavatāṃ satām || 7.36.57 ||
translation: पौरजानपदान् citizens and country-dwellers, स्थाप्य having established, स्वकार्येषु in their own duties, अहम् I, आगतः have come, क्रतून् sacrifices, एव indeed, करिष्यामि I shall perform, प्रभावात् by the power, भवताम् of you, सताम् good ones.
explanation: Having settled the citizens and country-dwellers in their respective duties, I have come here and shall indeed perform sacrifices by the power and influence of you, the virtuous ones.

shloka_text: सदस्या मम यज्ञेषु भवन्तो नित्यमेव तत् । भविष्यथ महावीर्या ममानुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः ।। 7.36.58 ।।
transliteration: sadasyā mama yajñeṣu bhavanto nityameva tat | bhaviṣyatha mahāvīryā mamānugrahakāṅkṣiṇaḥ || 7.36.58 ||
translation: सदस्याः members of the assembly, मम my, यज्ञेषु in sacrifices, भवन्तः you, नित्यम् always, एव indeed, तत् that, भविष्यथ you shall be, महावीर्याः of great prowess, मम my, अनुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः desiring favor.
explanation: You, who are of great prowess and desire my favor, shall always indeed be the members of the assembly in my sacrifices.

shloka_text: अहं युष्मान्समाश्रित्य तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् । अनुग्रहीतः पितृभिर्भविष्यामि सुनिर्वृतः ।। 7.36.59 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ yuṣmānsamāśritya taponirdhūtakalmaṣān | anugrahītaḥ pitṛbhirbhaviṣyāmi sunirvṛtaḥ || 7.36.59 ||
translation: अहम् I, युष्मान् you, समाश्रित्य having resorted to, तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् whose sins are cleansed by penance, अनुग्रहीतः blessed, पितृभिः by the ancestors, भविष्यामि I shall be, सुनिर्वृतः greatly contented.
explanation: Having resorted to you, whose sins have been purified by penance, I shall be blessed by my ancestors and thus become greatly contented.

shloka_text: तदागन्तव्यमनिशं भवद्भिरिह सङ्गतैः । अगस्त्याद्यास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषयः संशितव्रताः ।। 7.36.60 ।।
transliteration: tadāgantavyamaniśaṃ bhavadbhiriha saṅgataiḥ | agastyādyāstu tacchrutvā ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ || 7.36.60 ||
translation: तत् therefore, आगन्तव्यम् should be come, अनिशम् constantly, भवद्भिः by you, इह here, सङ्गतैः assembled, अगस्त्याद्याः Agastya and others, तु and, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, ऋषयः sages, संशितव्रताः of firm vows.
explanation: Therefore, you should constantly come here assembled together; and Agastya and other sages of firm vows, having heard that (request)...

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रयातुमुपचक्रमुः ।। 7.36.61 ।।
transliteration: evamastviti taṃ coktvā prayātumupacakramuḥ || 7.36.61 ||
translation: एवम् thus, अस्तु let it be, इति thus, तम् to him, च and, उक्त्वा having said, प्रयातुम् to depart, उपचक्रमुः began.
explanation: ...and having said "So be it" to him, they began to depart.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा गताः सर्वे ऋषयस्ते यथागतम् । राघवश्च तमेवार्थं चिन्तयामास विस्मितः ।। 7.36.62 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā gatāḥ sarve ṛṣayaste yathāgatam | rāghavaśca tamevārthaṃ cintayāmāsa vismitaḥ || 7.36.62 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, गताः went, सर्वे all, ऋषयः sages, ते those, यथागतम् as they had come, राघवः Rama, च and, तम् that, एव indeed, अर्थम् matter, चिन्तयामास pondered, विस्मितः astonished.
explanation: Having spoken thus, all those sages departed the way they had come, and Rama, astonished, pondered over that very matter.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्तं भास्करे याते विसृज्य नृपवानरान् । सन्ध्यामुपास्य विधिवत्तदा नरवरोत्तमः । प्रवृत्तायां रजन्यां तु सो ऽन्तःपुरचरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.36.63 ।।
transliteration: tato 'staṃ bhāskare yāte visṛjya nṛpavānarān | sandhyāmupāsya vidhivattadā naravarottamaḥ | pravṛttāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu so 'ntaḥpuracaro 'bhavat || 7.36.63 ||
translation: ततः then, अस्तम् setting, भास्करे when the sun, याते had gone, विसृज्य having dismissed, नृपवानरान् kings and monkeys, सन्ध्याम् evening prayer, उपास्य having performed, विधिवत् according to ritual, तदा then, नरवरोत्तमः the best among men, प्रवृत्तायाम् having commenced, रजन्याम् when night, तु indeed, सः he, अन्तःपुरचरः entered the inner apartments, अभवत् became.
explanation: Then, when the sun had set, having dismissed the kings and monkeys, the best among men, Rama, performed his evening prayers according to ritual, and when night had truly begun, he entered his inner apartments. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 36 ।। Thus ends the thirty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्स्थे धर्मेण विदितात्मनि । व्यतीता या निशा पूर्वा पौराणां हर्षवर्धिनी ।। 7.37.1 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣikte tu kākutsthe dharmeṇa viditātmani | vyatītā yā niśā pūrvā paurāṇāṃ harṣavardhinī || 7.37.1 ||
translation: अभिषिक्ते having been consecrated, तु indeed, काकुत्स्थे when Rama, धर्मेण righteously, विदितात्मनि whose soul was known, व्यतीता passed, या which, निशा night, पूर्वा first, पौराणाम् of the citizens, हर्षवर्धिनी increasing joy.
explanation: When Rama, whose soul was known for righteousness, had been consecrated, the first night, which increased the joy of the citizens, passed.
comments: On the first morning after his consecration Rama is awakened by the praises of bards, performs his ablutions and worship, and holds court -- attended by Vasishtha and the ministers, his brothers, the assembled kings, the monkey-chiefs led by Sugriva, and Vibhishana with his rakshasas, he shines amid them like Indra among the gods.

shloka_text: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां प्रातर्नृपतिबोधकाः । वन्दिनः समुपातिष्ठन्सौम्या नृपतिवेश्मनि ।। 7.37.2 ।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ prātarnṛpatibodhakāḥ | vandinaḥ samupātiṣṭhansaumyā nṛpativeśmani || 7.37.2 ||
translation: तस्याम् in that, रजन्याम् night, व्युष्टायाम् having dawned, प्रातः in the morning, नृपतिबोधकाः awakeners of the king, वन्दिनः bards, समुपातिष्ठन् stood near, सौम्याः gentle, नृपतिवेश्मनि in the king's palace.
explanation: As that night dawned, in the morning, gentle bards, who were the awakeners of the king, stood near the king's palace.

shloka_text: ते रक्तकण्ठिनः सर्वे किन्नरा इव शिक्षिताः । तुष्टुवुर्नपतिं वीरं यथावत् सम्प्रहर्षिणः ।। 7.37.3 ।।
transliteration: te raktakaṇṭhinaḥ sarve kinnarā iva śikṣitāḥ | tuṣṭuvurnapatiṃ vīraṃ yathāvat sampraharṣiṇaḥ || 7.37.3 ||
translation: ते they, रक्तकण्ठिनः with melodious voices, सर्वे all, किन्नराः Kinnaras, इव like, शिक्षिताः trained, तुष्टुवुः praised, नृपतिम् the king, वीरम् the hero, यथावत् appropriately, सम्प्रहर्षिणः greatly rejoicing.
explanation: All of them, with melodious voices, trained like Kinnaras, greatly rejoicing, duly praised the heroic king.

shloka_text: वीर सौम्य प्रबुध्यस्व कौसल्याप्रीतिवर्धन । जगद्धि सर्वं स्वपिति त्वयि सुप्ते नराधिप ।। 7.37.4 ।।
transliteration: vīra saumya prabudhyasva kausalyāprītivardhana | jagaddhi sarvaṃ svapiti tvayi supte narādhipa || 7.37.4 ||
translation: वीर O hero, सौम्य O gentle one, प्रबुध्यस्व wake up, कौसल्याप्रीतिवर्धन O enhancer of Kausalya's joy, जगत् the world, हि indeed, सर्वम् all, स्वपिति sleeps, त्वयि when you, सुप्ते are asleep, नराधिप O king of men.
explanation: O heroic and gentle king, who increases Kausalya's joy, please awaken, for indeed, when you sleep, the entire world sleeps.

shloka_text: विक्रमस्ते यथा विष्णो रूपं चैवाश्विनोरिव । बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यः प्रजापतिसमो ह्यसि ।। 7.37.5 ।।
transliteration: vikramaste yathā viṣṇo rūpaṃ caivāśvinoriva | buddhyā bṛhaspatestulyaḥ prajāpatisamo hyasi || 7.37.5 ||
translation: विक्रमः valor, ते your, यथा like, विष्णोः of Vishnu, रूपम् form/beauty, च and, एव indeed, अश्विनोः of the Ashvins, इव like, बुद्ध्या in intellect, बृहस्पतेः of Brihaspati, तुल्यः equal, प्रजापतिसमः equal to Prajapati, हि indeed, असि you are.
explanation: Your valor is like that of Vishnu, your beauty is like that of the Ashvins, you are equal to Brihaspati in intellect, and indeed, you are like Prajapati himself.

shloka_text: क्षमा ते पृथिवीतुल्या तेजसा भास्करोपमः । वेगस्ते वायुना तुल्यो गाम्भीर्यमुदधेरिव ।। 7.37.6 ।।
transliteration: kṣamā te pṛthivītulyā tejasā bhāskaropamaḥ | vegaste vāyunā tulyo gāmbhīryamudadheriva || 7.37.6 ||
translation: क्षमा forgiveness/patience, ते your, पृथिवीतुल्या equal to the earth, तेजसा in splendor, भास्करोपमः comparable to the sun, वेगः speed, ते your, वायुना to the wind, तुल्यः equal, गाम्भीर्यम् depth, उदधेः of the ocean, इव like.
explanation: Your patience is like that of the earth, your splendor is comparable to the sun, your speed is equal to the wind, and your depth is like that of the ocean.

shloka_text: अप्रकम्प्यो यता स्थाणुश्चन्द्रे सौम्यत्वमीदृशम् । नेदृशाः पार्थिवाः पूर्वं भवितारो नराधिप ।। 7.37.7 ।।
transliteration: aprakampyo yatā sthāṇuścandre saumyatvamīdṛśam | nedṛśāḥ pārthivāḥ pūrvaṃ bhavitāro narādhipa || 7.37.7 ||
translation: अप्रकम्प्यः unshakable, यथा like, स्थाणुः a pillar, चन्द्रे in the moon, सौम्यत्वम् gentleness, ईदृशम् such, न not, ईदृशाः such, पार्थिवाः kings, पूर्वम् before, भवितारः will be, नराधिप O king of men.
explanation: You are unshakable like a pillar, and possess such gentleness as found in the moon; O king of men, there have been no such kings before, nor will there be in the future.

shloka_text: यथा त्वमतिदुर्धर्षो धर्मनित्यः प्रजाहितः । न त्वां जहाति कीर्तिश्च लक्ष्मीश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.37.8 ।।
transliteration: yathā tvamatidurdharṣo dharmanityaḥ prajāhitaḥ | na tvāṃ jahāti kīrtiśca lakṣmīśca puruṣarṣabha || 7.37.8 ||
translation: यथा as, त्वम् you, अतिदुर्धर्षः extremely formidable, धर्मनित्यः always righteous, प्रजाहितः devoted to the welfare of the subjects, न not, त्वाम् you, जहाति abandons, कीर्तिः fame, च and, लक्ष्मीः prosperity, च and, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: As you are extremely formidable, always righteous, and devoted to the welfare of your subjects, O best among men, neither fame nor prosperity ever abandons you.

shloka_text: श्रीश्च धर्मश्च काकुत्स्थ त्वयि नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितौ । एताश्चान्याश्च मधुरा वन्दिभिः परिकीर्तिताः ।। 7.37.9 ।।
transliteration: śrīśca dharmaśca kākutstha tvayi nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitau | etāścānyāśca madhurā vandibhiḥ parikīrtitāḥ || 7.37.9 ||
translation: श्रीश्च prosperity and, धर्मश्च righteousness and, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha (Rama), त्वयि in you, नित्यं always, प्रतिष्ठितौ are established. एताश्च these and, अन्याश्च other, मधुरा sweet (praises), वन्दिभिः by bards, परिकीर्तिताः were proclaimed.
explanation: O Rama, prosperity and righteousness are eternally established in you, and these and other sweet praises were sung by the bards.

shloka_text: सूताश्च संस्तवैर्दिव्यैर्बोधयन्ति स्म राघवम् । स्तुतिभिः स्तूयमानाभिः प्रत्यबुध्यत राघवः ।। 7.37.10 ।।
transliteration: sūtāśca saṃstavairdivyairbodhayanti sma rāghavam | stutibhiḥ stūyamānābhiḥ pratyabudhyata rāghavaḥ || 7.37.10 ||
translation: सूताश्च and charioteers/bards, संस्तवैः with praises, दिव्यैः divine, बोधयन्ति awakened, स्म (past tense indicator), राघवम् Rama. स्तुतिभिः with praises, स्तूयमानाभिः being sung, प्रत्यबुध्यत awoke, राघवः Rama.
explanation: The bards, with their divine praises, awakened Rama, and Rama awoke to the sound of these eulogies being sung.

shloka_text: स तद्विहाय शयनं पाण्डराच्छादनास्तृतम् । उत्तस्थौ नागशयनाद्धरिर्नारायणो यथा ।। 7.37.11 ।।
transliteration: sa tadvihāya śayanaṃ pāṇḍarācchādanāstṛtam | uttasthau nāgaśayanāddharirnārāyaṇo yathā || 7.37.11 ||
translation: स He, तत् that, विहाय having left, शयनं bed, पाण्डराच्छादनास्तृतम् covered with white sheets, उत्तस्थौ rose up, नागशयनात् from the serpent-bed, हरिः Vishnu, नारायणो Narayana, यथा as.
explanation: He rose from that bed, which was covered with white sheets, just as Lord Narayana (Vishnu) rises from his serpent-bed.

shloka_text: तमुत्थितं महात्मानं प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो नराः । सलिलं भाजनैः शुभ्रैरुपतस्थुः सहस्रशः ।। 7.37.12 ।।
transliteration: tamutthitaṃ mahātmānaṃ prahvāḥ prāñjalayo narāḥ | salilaṃ bhājanaiḥ śubhrairupatasthuḥ sahasraśaḥ || 7.37.12 ||
translation: तम् Him, उत्थितं risen, महात्मानं the great-souled one, प्रह्वाः humble, प्राञ्जलयो with folded hands, नराः men, सलिलं water, भाजनैः with vessels, शुभ्रैः pure/clean, उपतस्थुः approached/offered, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: Thousands of humble men, with folded hands, approached the risen great-souled Rama, offering him water in pure vessels.

shloka_text: कृतोदकशुचिर्भूत्वा काले हुतहुताशनः । देवागारं जगामाशु पुण्यमिक्ष्वाकुसेवितम् ।। 7.37.13 ।।
transliteration: kṛtodakaśucirbhūtvā kāle hutahutāśanaḥ | devāgāraṃ jagāmāśu puṇyamikṣvākusevitam || 7.37.13 ||
translation: कृतोदकशुचिः having performed ablutions and become pure, भूत्वा having become, काले at the proper time, हुतहुताशनः having offered oblations to the fire, देवागारं to the temple, जगाम went, आशु quickly, पुण्यम् sacred, इक्ष्वाकुसेवितम् frequented by the Ikshvakus.
explanation: Having purified himself with ablutions and offered oblations to the sacred fire at the appropriate time, he quickly went to the holy temple, which was traditionally frequented by the Ikshvaku kings.

shloka_text: तत्र देवान्पितऽन्विप्रानर्चयित्वा यथाविधि । बाह्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम जनैर्वृतः ।। 7.37.14 ।।
transliteration: tatra devānpita'nviprānarcayitvā yathāvidhi | bāhyakakṣāntaraṃ rāmo nirjagāma janairvṛtaḥ || 7.37.14 ||
translation: तत्र there, देवान् gods, पितॄन् ancestors, विप्रान् Brahmins, अर्चयित्वा having worshipped, यथाविधि according to custom, बाह्यकक्षान्तरम् to the outer chamber, रामः Rama, निर्जगाम emerged, जनैः by people, वृतः surrounded.
explanation: After duly worshipping the gods, ancestors, and Brahmins, Rama emerged into the outer chamber, surrounded by many people.

shloka_text: उपतस्थुर्महात्मानो मन्त्रिणः सपुरोहिताः । वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्वे दीप्यमाना इवाग्नयः ।। 7.37.15 ।।
transliteration: upatasthurmahātmāno mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ | vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarve dīpyamānā ivāgnayaḥ || 7.37.15 ||
translation: उपतस्थुः approached, महात्मानः great-souled ones, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सपुरोहिताः with their priests, वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः headed by Vasishtha, सर्वे all, दीप्यमानाः shining, इव like, अग्नयः fires.
explanation: All the great-souled ministers, along with their priests and headed by Vasishtha, approached Rama, shining brightly like fires.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियाश्च महात्मानो नानाजनपदेश्वराः । रामस्योपाविशन्पार्श्वे शक्रस्येव यथा ऽमराः ।। 7.37.16 ।।
transliteration: kṣatriyāśca mahātmāno nānājanapadeśvarāḥ | rāmasyopāviśanpārśve śakrasyeva yathā 'marāḥ || 7.37.16 ||
translation: क्षत्रियाः Kshatriyas, च and, महात्मानः great-souled ones, नानाजनपदेश्वराः rulers of various countries, रामस्य of Rama, उपाविशन् sat near, पार्श्वे at the side, शक्रस्य of Indra, इव like, यथा just as, अमराः immortals.
explanation: Great-souled Kshatriyas and rulers from various regions sat by Rama's side, just as the immortals sit by Indra.

shloka_text: भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चात्र शत्रुघ्नश्च महायशाः । उपासाञ्चक्रिरे हृष्टा वेदास्त्रय इवाध्वरम् ।। 7.37.17 ।।
transliteration: bharato lakṣmaṇaścātra śatrughnaśca mahāyaśāḥ | upāsāñcakrire hṛṣṭā vedāstraya ivādhvaram || 7.37.17 ||
translation: भरतः Bharata, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, च and, अत्र there, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, च and, महायशाः highly renowned, उपासाञ्चक्रिरे attended, हृष्टाः delighted, वेदाः Vedas, त्रयः three, इव like, अध्वरम् a sacrifice.
explanation: There, the highly renowned Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna attended upon Rama with delight, just as the three Vedas attend upon a sacrifice.

shloka_text: याताः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा किङ्करा मुदिताननाः । मुदिता नाम पार्श्वस्था बहवः समुपाविशन् ।। 7.37.18 ।।
transliteration: yātāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā kiṅkarā muditānanāḥ | muditā nāma pārśvasthā bahavaḥ samupāviśan || 7.37.18 ||
translation: याताः came, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, किङ्कराः servants, मुदिताननाः with joyful faces, मुदिताः joyful ones, नाम indeed, पार्श्वस्थाः standing by the side, बहवः many, समुपाविशन् sat down together.
explanation: Many servants with joyful faces came with folded hands and, indeed joyful, sat down by his side.

shloka_text: वानराश्च महावीर्या विंशतिः कामरूपिणः । सुग्रीवप्रमुखा राममुपासन्ते महौजसः ।। 7.37.19 ।।
transliteration: vānarāśca mahāvīryā viṃśatiḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ | sugrīvapramukhā rāmamupāsante mahaujasaḥ || 7.37.19 ||
translation: वानराः monkeys, च and, महावीर्याः greatly valorous, विंशतिः twenty, कामरूपिणः assuming any form at will, सुग्रीवप्रमुखाः led by Sugriva, महौजसः greatly powerful, रामम् Rama, उपासन्ते serve.
explanation: Twenty greatly valorous and powerful monkeys, led by Sugriva, who can assume any form at will, serve Rama.

shloka_text: विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिः परिवारितः । उपासते महात्मानं धनेशमिव गुह्यकाः ।। 7.37.20 ।।
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇaśca rakṣobhiścaturbhiḥ parivāritaḥ | upāsate mahātmānaṃ dhaneśamiva guhyakāḥ || 7.37.20 ||
translation: विभीषणः Vibhishana, च and, चतुर्भिः by four, रक्षोभिः rakshasas, परिवारितः surrounded, महात्मानम् the great-souled one (Rama), उपासते serve, धनेशम् the lord of wealth (Kubera), गुह्यकाः Guhyakas, इव like.
explanation: And Vibhishana, surrounded by four rakshasas, serves the great-souled Rama, just as Guhyakas serve Kubera, the lord of wealth.

shloka_text: तथा निगमवृद्धाश्च कुलीना ये च मानवाः । शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः ।। 7.37.21 ।।
transliteration: tathā nigamavṛddhāśca kulīnā ye ca mānavāḥ | śirasā ' 'vandya rājānamupāsante vicakṣaṇāḥ || 7.37.21 ||
translation: तथा similarly, निगमवृद्धाः elders of the guilds/cities, च and, ये who, कुलीनाः of noble birth, च and, मानवाः men, विचक्षणाः wise, शिरसा with their heads, आवन्द्य having bowed down, राजानम् the king (Rama), उपासन्ते serve.
explanation: Similarly, the wise elders of the guilds and noble-born men serve the king, Rama, having bowed down with their heads.

shloka_text: तथा परिवृतो राजा श्रीमद्भिर्ऋषिभिर्वृतः । राजभिश्च महावीर्यैर्वानरैश्च सराक्षसैः ।। 7.37.22 ।।
transliteration: tathā parivṛto rājā śrīmadbhirṛṣibhirvṛtaḥ | rājabhiśca mahāvīryairvānaraiśca sarākṣasaiḥ || 7.37.22 ||
translation: तथा thus, राजा the king (Rama), श्रीमद्भिः by glorious, ऋषिभिः sages, वृतः surrounded, च and, महावीर्यैः greatly valorous, राजभिः kings, च and, वानरैः monkeys, च and, सराक्षसैः with rakshasas, परिवृतः surrounded.
explanation: Thus, the king Rama is surrounded by glorious sages, greatly valorous kings, monkeys, and rakshasas.

shloka_text: यथा देवेश्वरो नित्यमृषिभिः समुपास्यते । अधिकस्तेन रूपेण सहस्राक्षाद्विरोचते ।। 7.37.23 ।।
transliteration: yathā deveśvaro nityamṛṣibhiḥ samupāsyate | adhikastena rūpeṇa sahasrākṣādvirocate || 7.37.23 ||
translation: यथा just as, देवेश्वरः the lord of gods (Indra), नित्यम् always, ऋषिभिः by sages, समुपास्यते is served, तेन by that, रूपेण in form/splendor, अधिकः superior, सहस्राक्षात् than the thousand-eyed one (Indra), विरोचते shines.
explanation: Just as the lord of gods, Indra, is always served by sages, Rama shines with a splendor superior to that of the thousand-eyed Indra.

shloka_text: तेषां समुपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः । कथ्यन्ते धर्मसंयुक्ताः पुराणज्ञैर्महात्मभिः ।। 7.37.24 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ tāstāḥ sumadhurāḥ kathāḥ | kathyante dharmasaṃyuktāḥ purāṇajñairmahātmabhiḥ || 7.37.24 ||
translation: तेषां of them, समुपविष्टानां who were seated, तास्ताः those various, सुमधुराः very sweet, कथाः stories, कथ्यन्ते are narrated, धर्मसंयुक्ताः endowed with righteousness, पुराणज्ञैः by those who know the Puranas, महात्मभिः by great souls,
explanation: To those who were seated, various very sweet stories imbued with righteousness were narrated by great souls who were learned in the Puranas. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 37 ।। Thus ends the thirty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमास्ते महाबाहुरहन्यहनि राघवः । प्रशासत्सर्वकार्याणि पौरजानपदेषु च ।। 7.38.1 ।।
transliteration: evamāste mahābāhurahanyahani rāghavaḥ | praśāsatsarvakāryāṇi paurajānapadeṣu ca || 7.38.1 ||
translation: एवम् thus, आस्ते remained, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, अहन्यहनि day after day, राघवः Rama, प्रशासत् ruling, सर्वकार्याणि all affairs, पौरजानपदेषु among the citizens and country people, च and,
explanation: Thus, the mighty-armed Rama lived day after day, administering all affairs concerning both the city dwellers and the rural populace.
comments: Rama dismisses his allies to their homes -- King Janaka returns to Mithila escorted by Bharata, his uncle Yudhajit to Kekaya with Lakshmana, Pratardana of Kashi to Varanasi, and the three hundred other kings to their lands -- thanking them and crediting their valour for Ravana's fall, he sends them off amid mutual affection.

shloka_text: ततः कतिपयाहःसु वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम् । राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.38.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ katipayāhaḥsu vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam | rāghavaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.38.2 ||
translation: ततः then, कतिपयाहःसु after a few days, वैदेहं to the king of Videha, मिथिलाधिपम् the lord of Mithila, राघवः Rama, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, वाक्यम् words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed,
explanation: Then, after a few days, Rama, with folded hands, spoke these words to Janaka, the king of Videha and lord of Mithila.

shloka_text: भवान्हि गतिरव्यग्रा भवता पालिता वयम् । भवतस्तेजसोग्रेण रावणो निहतो मया ।। 7.38.3 ।।
transliteration: bhavānhi gatiravyagrā bhavatā pālitā vayam | bhavatastejasogreṇa rāvaṇo nihato mayā || 7.38.3 ||
translation: भवान् you, हि indeed, गतिः refuge, अव्यग्रा steadfast, भवता by you, पालिताः protected, वयम् we, भवतः your, तेजसः by the might, उग्रेण fierce, रावणः Ravana, निहतः killed, मया by me,
explanation: You are indeed our steadfast refuge, and we have been protected by you; it was by your fierce might that Ravana was killed by me.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां च सर्वेषां मैथिलानां च सर्वशः । अतुलाः प्रीतयो राजन्सम्बन्धकपुरोगमाः ।। 7.38.4 ।।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ maithilānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ | atulāḥ prītayo rājansambandhakapurogamāḥ || 7.38.4 ||
translation: इक्ष्वाकूणां of the Ikshvakus, च and, सर्वेषां of all, मैथिलानां of the Maithilas, च and, सर्वशः in every respect, अतुलाः incomparable, प्रीतयः affections, राजन् O King, सम्बन्धकपुरोगमाः headed by the relationship (of marriage),
explanation: O King, the affections between all the Ikshvakus and all the Maithilas, especially those stemming from our marital relationship, are truly incomparable.

shloka_text: तद्भवान्स्वपुरं यातु रत्नान्यादाय पार्थिव । भरतश्च सहायार्थं पृष्ठतस्ते ऽनुयास्यति ।। 7.38.5 ।।
transliteration: tadbhavānsvapuraṃ yātu ratnānyādāya pārthiva | bharataśca sahāyārthaṃ pṛṣṭhataste 'nuyāsyati || 7.38.5 ||
translation: तद् therefore, भवान् you, स्वपुरं to your own city, यातु may go, रत्नानि jewels, आदाय taking, पार्थिव O King, भरतश्च and Bharata, सहायार्थं for assistance, पृष्ठतः behind, ते you, अनुयास्यति will follow,
explanation: Therefore, O King, you may return to your city taking the jewels, and Bharata will follow behind you for assistance.

shloka_text: स तथेति नृपः कृत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि भवतो राजन्दर्शनेन नयेन च ।। 7.38.6 ।।
transliteration: sa tatheti nṛpaḥ kṛtvā rāghavaṃ vākyamabravīt | prīto 'smi bhavato rājandarśanena nayena ca || 7.38.6 ||
translation: सः he, तथा so be it, इति thus, नृपः the king, कृत्वा having said, राघवं to Rama, वाक्यं words, अब्रवीत् spoke, प्रीतः pleased, अस्मि I am, भवतः your, राजन् O King, दर्शनेन by the sight, नयेन by the wisdom, च and,
explanation: Having agreed, King Janaka then spoke to Rama, saying, "O King, I am pleased by your sight and your wisdom."

shloka_text: यान्येतानि तु रत्नानि मदर्थं सञ्चितानि वै । दुहित्रे तानि वै राजन्सर्वाण्येव ददामि च ।। 7.38.7 ।।
transliteration: yānyetāni tu ratnāni madarthaṃ sañcitāni vai | duhitre tāni vai rājansarvāṇyeva dadāmi ca || 7.38.7 ||
translation: यानि which, एतानि these, तु indeed, रत्नानि jewels, मदर्थं for my sake, सञ्चितानि collected, वै indeed, दुहित्रे to my daughter, तानि those, वै indeed, राजन् O King, सर्वाणि all, एव certainly, ददामि I give, च and,
explanation: O King, I give all these jewels, which were collected for my sake, to my daughter.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं जनको हृष्टमानसः । प्रययौ मिथिलां श्रीमांस्तमनुज्ञाय राघवम् ।। 7.38.8 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu kākutsthaṃ janako hṛṣṭamānasaḥ | prayayau mithilāṃ śrīmāṃstamanujñāya rāghavam || 7.38.8 ||
translation: एवं thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तु indeed, काकुत्स्थं to Rama, जनकः Janaka, हृष्टमानसः with a joyful mind, प्रययौ departed, मिथिलां to Mithila, श्रीमान् glorious, तं him, अनुज्ञाय having taken leave of, राघवम् Rama,
explanation: Having thus spoken to Rama, the glorious Janaka, with a joyful mind, took leave of Rama and departed for Mithila.

shloka_text: ततः प्रयाते जनके केकयं मातुलं प्रभुः । राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.38.9 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prayāte janake kekayaṃ mātulaṃ prabhuḥ | rāghavaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.38.9 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, प्रयाते having departed, जनके Janaka, केकयं to Kekaya, मातुलं maternal uncle, प्रभुः the lord, राघवः Rama, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, वाक्यं words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed,
explanation: After Janaka had departed, Lord Rama, with folded hands, then spoke these words to his maternal uncle, Kekaya.

shloka_text: इदं राज्यमहं चैव भरतश्च सलक्ष्मणः । आयत्तास्त्वं हि नो राजन्गतिश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.38.10 ।।
transliteration: idaṃ rājyamahaṃ caiva bharataśca salakṣmaṇaḥ | āyattāstvaṃ hi no rājangatiśca puruṣarṣabha || 7.38.10 ||
translation: इदं this, राज्यम् kingdom, अहं I, चैव and indeed, भरतश्च Bharata and, सलक्ष्मणः with Lakshmana, आयत्ताः dependent, त्वं you, हि indeed, नः our, राजन् O King, गतिश्च and refuge, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O King, O best among men, this kingdom, I, Bharata, and Lakshmana are all dependent on you, for you are indeed our refuge.

shloka_text: राजा हि वृद्धः सन्तापं त्वदर्थमुपयास्यति । तस्माद्गमनमद्यैव रोचते तव पार्थिव ।। 7.38.11 ।।
transliteration: rājā hi vṛddhaḥ santāpaṃ tvadarthamupayāsyati | tasmādgamanamadyaiva rocate tava pārthiva || 7.38.11 ||
translation: राजा the king, हि indeed, वृद्धः old, सन्तापं sorrow, त्वदर्थम् for your sake, उपयास्यति will experience, तस्मात् therefore, गमनम् departure, अद्यैव today itself, रोचते is suitable, तव for you, पार्थिव O prince.
explanation: The old king will indeed suffer sorrow for your sake, therefore, O prince, your departure today itself is suitable.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनानुयात्रेण पृष्ठतो ऽनुगमिष्यते । धनमादाय विपुलं रत्नानि विविधानि च ।। 7.38.12 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenānuyātreṇa pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyate | dhanamādāya vipulaṃ ratnāni vividhāni ca || 7.38.12 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, अनुयात्रेण as a follower, पृष्ठतः from behind, अनुगमिष्यते will follow, धनम् wealth, आदाय taking, विपुलं abundant, रत्नानि jewels, विविधानि various, च and.
explanation: Lakshmana will follow behind as a companion, taking abundant wealth and various jewels.

shloka_text: युधाजित्तु तथेत्याह गमनं प्रति राघवम् । रत्नानि च धनं चैव त्वय्येवाक्षय्यमस्त्विति ।। 7.38.13 ।।
transliteration: yudhājittu tathetyāha gamanaṃ prati rāghavam | ratnāni ca dhanaṃ caiva tvayyevākṣayyamastviti || 7.38.13 ||
translation: युधाजित् Yudhājit, तु and, तथा so be it, इति thus, आह said, गमनं departure, प्रति regarding, राघवम् to Rama, रत्नानि jewels, च and, धनं wealth, चैव and indeed, त्वय्येव in you alone, अक्षय्यम् inexhaustible, अस्तु let it be, इति thus.
explanation: Yudhājit then said to Rama regarding his departure, "So be it; let the jewels and wealth indeed be inexhaustible in you alone."

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणं स राजानं कृत्वा केकयवर्धनः । रामेण हि कृतः पूर्वमभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम् ।। 7.38.14 ।।
transliteration: pradakṣiṇaṃ sa rājānaṃ kṛtvā kekayavardhanaḥ | rāmeṇa hi kṛtaḥ pūrvamabhivādya pradakṣiṇam || 7.38.14 ||
translation: प्रदक्षिणं circumambulation, सः he, राजानं the king, कृत्वा having done, केकयवर्धनः the enhancer of Kekaya (Yudhājit), रामेण by Rama, हि indeed, कृतः done, पूर्वम् previously, अभिवाद्य having saluted, प्रदक्षिणम् circumambulation.
explanation: Having circumambulated the king, Yudhājit, the enhancer of Kekaya, departed, just as Rama had previously saluted and circumambulated.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन सहायेन प्रयातः केकयेश्वरः । हते ऽसुरे यथा वृत्रे विष्णुना सह वासवः ।। 7.38.15 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena sahāyena prayātaḥ kekayeśvaraḥ | hate 'sure yathā vṛtre viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ || 7.38.15 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, सहायेन with help, प्रयातः departed, केकयेश्वरः the lord of Kekaya, हते when killed, असुरे the demon, यथा just as, वृत्रे Vritra, विष्णुना by Vishnu, सह with, वासवः Indra.
explanation: The lord of Kekaya departed with Lakshmana's help, just as Indra, with Vishnu, went after the demon Vritra was killed.

shloka_text: तं विसृज्य ततो रामो वयस्यमकुतोभयम् । प्रतर्दनं काशिपतिं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.38.16 ।।
transliteration: taṃ visṛjya tato rāmo vayasyamakutobhayam | pratardanaṃ kāśipatiṃ pariṣvajyedamabravīt || 7.38.16 ||
translation: तम् him, विसृज्य having dismissed, ततः then, रामः Rama, वयस्यम् friend, अकुतोभयम् fearless, प्रतर्दनम् Pratardana, काशिपतिम् the lord of Kashi, परिष्वज्य having embraced, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then, having dismissed that fearless friend, Rama embraced Pratardana, the lord of Kashi, and spoke this.

shloka_text: दर्शिता भवता प्रीतिर्दर्शितं सौहृदं परम् । उद्योगश्च कृतो राजन्भरतेन त्वया सह ।। 7.38.17 ।।
transliteration: darśitā bhavatā prītirdarśitaṃ sauhṛdaṃ param | udyogaśca kṛto rājanbharatena tvayā saha || 7.38.17 ||
translation: दर्शिता shown, भवता by you, प्रीतिः affection, दर्शितम् shown, सौहृदम् friendship, परम् supreme, उद्योगः effort, च and, कृतः made, राजन् O King, भरतेन by Bharata, त्वया by you, सह with.
explanation: O King, you have shown great affection and supreme friendship, and you, along with Bharata, have made a great effort.

shloka_text: तद्भवानद्य काशेय पुरीं वाराणसीं व्रज । रमणीयां त्वया गुप्तां सुप्रकाशां सुतोरणाम् ।। 7.38.18 ।।
transliteration: tadbhavānadya kāśeya purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ vraja | ramaṇīyāṃ tvayā guptāṃ suprakāśāṃ sutoraṇām || 7.38.18 ||
translation: तत् therefore, भवान् you, अद्य today, काशेय O King of Kashi, पुरीम् city, वाराणसीम् Varanasi, व्रज go, रमणीयाम् beautiful, त्वया by you, गुप्ताम् protected, सुप्रकाशाम् well-illuminated, सुतोरणाम् with beautiful arches.
explanation: Therefore, O King of Kashi, you should go today to your beautiful city of Varanasi, which is protected by you, well-illuminated, and adorned with beautiful arches.

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वा चोत्थाय काकुत्स्थः परमासनात् । पर्यष्वजत धर्मात्मा निरन्तरमुरोगतम् ।। 7.38.19 ।।
transliteration: etāvaduktvā cotthāya kākutsthaḥ paramāsanāt | paryaṣvajata dharmātmā nirantaramurogatam || 7.38.19 ||
translation: एतावत् thus much, उक्त्वा having said, च and, उत्थाय having risen, काकुत्स्थः Rama, परमासनात् from his excellent seat, पर्यष्वजत embraced, धर्मात्मा the righteous one, निरन्तरम् closely, उरोगतम् to his chest.
explanation: Having said this much, the righteous Rama rose from his excellent seat and embraced him closely to his chest.

shloka_text: विसर्जयामास तदा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । राघवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातः काशीशो ऽप्यकुतोभयः । वाराणसीं ययौ तूर्णं राघवेण विसर्जितः ।। 7.38.20 ।।
transliteration: visarjayāmāsa tadā kausalyānandavardhanaḥ | rāghaveṇābhyanujñātaḥ kāśīśo 'pyakutobhayaḥ | vārāṇasīṃ yayau tūrṇaṃ rāghaveṇa visarjitaḥ || 7.38.20 ||
translation: विसर्जयामास sent away, तदा then, कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः the one who increases Kaushalya's joy (Rama), राघवेण by Rama, अभ्यनुज्ञातः permitted, काशीशः the lord of Kashi, अपि also, अकुतोभयः fearless, वाराणसीं to Varanasi, ययौ went, तूर्णं quickly, राघवेण by Rama, विसर्जितः dismissed.
explanation: Then, Rama, who brings joy to Kaushalya, dismissed the fearless lord of Kashi, who, having been permitted and sent off by Rama, quickly returned to Varanasi.

shloka_text: विसृज्य तं काशिपतिं त्रिशतं पृथिवीपतीन् । प्रहसन्राघवो वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम् ।। 7.38.21 ।।
transliteration: visṛjya taṃ kāśipatiṃ triśataṃ pṛthivīpatīn | prahasanrāghavo vākyamuvāca madhurākṣaram || 7.38.21 ||
translation: विसृज्य having dismissed, तं that, काशिपतिं lord of Kashi, त्रिशतं three hundred, पृथिवीपतीन् kings, प्रहसन् smiling, राघवः Rama, वाक्यं words, उवाच spoke, मधुराक्षरम् sweet-worded.
explanation: Having dismissed that lord of Kashi and three hundred other kings, Rama, with a smile, spoke words that were sweet.

shloka_text: भवतां प्रीतिरव्यग्रा तेजसा परिरक्षिता । धर्मश्च नियतो नित्यं सत्यं च भवतां सदा ।। 7.38.22 ।।
transliteration: bhavatāṃ prītiravyagrā tejasā parirakṣitā | dharmaśca niyato nityaṃ satyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sadā || 7.38.22 ||
translation: भवतां your, प्रीतिः affection, अव्यग्रा undisturbed, तेजसा by valor, परिरक्षिता protected, धर्मः righteousness, च and, नियतः firm, नित्यं always, सत्यं truth, च and, भवतां your, सदा always.
explanation: Your unwavering affection is protected by your valor, and your righteousness and truth are always constant.

shloka_text: युष्माकं चानुभावेन तेजसा च महात्मनाम् । हतो दुरात्मा दुर्बुद्धी रावणो राक्षसाधमः ।। 7.38.23 ।।
transliteration: yuṣmākaṃ cānubhāvena tejasā ca mahātmanām | hato durātmā durbuddhī rāvaṇo rākṣasādhamaḥ || 7.38.23 ||
translation: युष्माकं your, च and, अनुभावेन by influence, तेजसा by valor, च and, महात्मनां of great souls, हतः killed, दुरात्मा evil-minded, दुर्बुद्धी ill-intentioned, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसाधमः the vilest of rakshasas.
explanation: It is by your influence and the valor of you great souls that the evil-minded, ill-intentioned Ravana, the vilest of rakshasas, was killed.

shloka_text: हेतुमात्रमहं तत्र भवतां तेजसा हतः । रावणः सगणो युद्धे सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवः ।। 7.38.24 ।।
transliteration: hetumātramahaṃ tatra bhavatāṃ tejasā hataḥ | rāvaṇaḥ sagaṇo yuddhe saputrāmātyabāndhavaḥ || 7.38.24 ||
translation: हेतुमात्रं merely an instrument, अहं I, तत्र there, भवतां your, तेजसा by valor, हतः killed, रावणः Ravana, सगणः with his retinue, युद्धे in battle, सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवः with his sons, ministers, and relatives.
explanation: In that matter, I was merely an instrument; it was by your valor that Ravana, along with his retinue, sons, ministers, and relatives, was killed in battle.

shloka_text: भवन्तश्च समानीता भरतेन महात्मना । श्रुत्वा जनकराजस्य काननात्तनयां हृताम् ।। 7.38.25 ।।
transliteration: bhavantaśca samānītā bharatena mahātmanā | śrutvā janakarājasya kānanāttanayāṃ hṛtām || 7.38.25 ||
translation: भवन्तः you (plural, respectful), च and, समानीताः brought together, भरतेन by Bharata, महात्मना by the great-souled one, श्रुत्वा having heard, जनकराजस्य of King Janaka, काननात् from the forest, तनयां daughter, हृताम् abducted.
explanation: You all were brought here by the great-souled Bharata, having heard that King Janaka's daughter was abducted from the forest.

shloka_text: उद्युक्तानां च सर्वेषां पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम् । कालो व्यतीतः सुमहान्गमनं रोचयाम्यतः ।। 7.38.26 ।।
transliteration: udyuktānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ pārthivānāṃ mahātmanām | kālo vyatītaḥ sumahāngamanaṃ rocayāmyataḥ || 7.38.26 ||
translation: उद्युक्तानां of those who were ready, च and, सर्वेषां of all, पार्थिवानां of kings, महात्मनाम् of great-souled ones, कालः time, व्यतीतः passed, सुमहान् very long, गमनं departure, रोचयामि I approve, अतः therefore.
explanation: A very long time has passed since all you great-souled kings were ready, therefore I approve of your departure.

shloka_text: प्रत्यूचुस्तं च राजानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । दिष्ट्यां त्वं विजयी राम स्वराज्ये ऽपि प्रतिष्ठितः ।। 7.38.27 ।।
transliteration: pratyūcustaṃ ca rājāno harṣeṇa mahatā vṛtāḥ | diṣṭyāṃ tvaṃ vijayī rāma svarājye 'pi pratiṣṭhitaḥ || 7.38.27 ||
translation: प्रत्यूचुः replied, तं to him, च and, राजानः kings, हर्षेण with joy, महता great, वृताः filled, दिष्ट्यां fortunately, त्वं you, विजयी victorious, राम O Rama, स्वराज्ये in your own kingdom, अपि also, प्रतिष्ठितः established.
explanation: The kings, filled with great joy, replied to him, saying, "Fortunately, O Rama, you are victorious and re-established in your own kingdom."

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या प्रत्याहृता सीता दिष्ट्या शत्रुः पराजितः । एष नः परमः काम एषा नः पीतिरुत्तमा ।। 7.38.28 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā pratyāhṛtā sītā diṣṭyā śatruḥ parājitaḥ | eṣa naḥ paramaḥ kāma eṣā naḥ pītiruttamā || 7.38.28 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, प्रत्याहृता brought back, सीता Sita, दिष्ट्या fortunately, शत्रुः enemy, पराजितः defeated, एषः this, नः our, परमः highest, कामः desire, एषा this, नः our, पीतिः joy, उत्तमा supreme.
explanation: Fortunately, Sita has been brought back, and fortunately, the enemy has been defeated; this is our highest desire and our supreme joy.

shloka_text: यत्त्वां विजयिनं राम पश्यामो हतशात्रवम् ।। 7.38.29 ।।
transliteration: yattvāṃ vijayinaṃ rāma paśyāmo hataśātravam || 7.38.29 ||
translation: यत् that, त्वां you, विजयिनं victorious, राम O Rama, पश्यामः we see, हतशात्रवम् with enemies slain.
explanation: Our greatest joy is that we see you, O Rama, victorious and with your enemies slain.

shloka_text: एतत्त्वय्युपपन्नं च यदस्मांस्त्वं प्रशंससे । प्रशंसार्ह न जानीमः प्रशंसां वक्तुमीदृशीम् ।। 7.38.30 ।।
transliteration: etattvayyupapannaṃ ca yadasmāṃstvaṃ praśaṃsase | praśaṃsārha na jānīmaḥ praśaṃsāṃ vaktumīdṛśīm || 7.38.30 ||
translation: एतत् This, त्वयि in you, उपपन्नं is fitting, च and, यत् that, अस्मान् us, त्वं you, प्रशंससे praise, प्रशंसार्ह O worthy of praise, न not, जानीमः we know, प्रशंसां praise, वक्तुम् to speak, ईदृशीम् such.
explanation: It is fitting for you to praise us, but O worthy of praise, we do not know how to utter such praise in return.

shloka_text: आपृच्छामो गमिष्यामो हृदिस्थो नः सदा भवान् । वर्तामहे महाबाहो प्रीत्यात्र महता वृताः । भवेच्च ते महाराज प्रीतिरस्मासु नित्यदा ।। 7.38.31 ।।
transliteration: āpṛcchāmo gamiṣyāmo hṛdistho naḥ sadā bhavān | vartāmahe mahābāho prītyātra mahatā vṛtāḥ | bhavecca te mahārāja prītirasmāsu nityadā || 7.38.31 ||
translation: आपृच्छामः We take leave, गमिष्यामः we shall go, हृदिस्थः residing in the heart, नः our, सदा always, भवान् you, वर्तामहे we have been, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, प्रीत्या with affection, अत्र here, महता great, वृताः filled, भवेत् may there be, च and, ते your, महाराज O great king, प्रीतिः affection, अस्मासु in us, नित्यदा always.
explanation: We take our leave and shall depart, for you will always reside in our hearts; O mighty-armed one, we have been filled with great affection here, and O great king, may your affection for us always remain.

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव राजानो हर्षेण परमान्विताः । उचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे राघवं गमनोत्सुकाः ।। 7.38.32 ।।
transliteration: bāḍhamityeva rājāno harṣeṇa paramānvitāḥ | ucuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve rāghavaṃ gamanotsukāḥ || 7.38.32 ||
translation: बाढम् Very well, इति thus, एव indeed, राजानः kings, हर्षेण with joy, परम supreme, अन्विताः endowed with, उचुः said, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, सर्वे all, राघवं to Rama, गमनोत्सुकाः eager to depart.
explanation: All the kings, filled with supreme joy and eager to depart, said "Very well" to Rama with folded hands.

shloka_text: पूजिताश्चैव रामेण जग्मुर्देशान्स्वकान्स्वकान् ।। 7.38.33 ।।
transliteration: pūjitāścaiva rāmeṇa jagmurdeśānsvakānsvakān || 7.38.33 ||
translation: पूजिताः Honored, च and, एव indeed, रामेण by Rama, जग्मुः they went, देशान् to their countries, स्वकान् their own, स्वकान् their own.
explanation: Honored by Rama, they all departed to their respective countries. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 38 ।। Thus ends the thirty-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ते प्रयाता महात्मानः पार्थिवास्ते प्रहृष्टवत् । गजवाजिसहस्रौघैः कम्पयन्तो वसुन्धराम् ।। 7.39.1 ।।
transliteration: te prayātā mahātmānaḥ pārthivāste prahṛṣṭavat | gajavājisahasraughaiḥ kampayanto vasundharām || 7.39.1 ||
translation: ते Those, प्रयाताः departed, महात्मानः great-souled ones, पार्थिवाः kings, ते those, प्रहृष्टवत् joyfully, गजवाजिसहस्रौघैः with thousands of elephants and horses, कम्पयन्तः shaking, वसुन्धराम् the earth.
explanation: Those great-souled kings departed joyfully, shaking the earth with their throngs of thousands of elephants and horses.
comments: The departed kings, regretting they had no chance to fight, send back rich gifts, which Bharata and his brothers bring to Rama -- Rama distributes the treasures among Sugriva, Vibhishana and the vanaras and bears, honouring Hanuman and Angada especially -- the allies feast and dwell happily for two months, perceiving the time as a moment in their devotion to Rama.

shloka_text: अक्षौहिण्यो हि तत्रासन्राघवार्थे समुद्यताः । भरतस्याज्ञया ऽनेकाः प्रहृष्टा बलवाहनाः ।। 7.39.2 ।।
transliteration: akṣauhiṇyo hi tatrāsanrāghavārthe samudyatāḥ | bharatasyājñayā 'nekāḥ prahṛṣṭā balavāhanāḥ || 7.39.2 ||
translation: अक्षौहिण्यो many Akshauhinis, हि indeed, तत्र there, आसन् were, राघवार्थे for the sake of Rama, समुद्यताः prepared, भरतस्य of Bharata, आज्ञया by the command, अनेकाः many, प्रहृष्टाः delighted, बलवाहनाः with strong forces and vehicles.
explanation: Many Akshauhinis, with their delighted forces and vehicles, were indeed present there, prepared for Rama's cause by Bharata's command.

shloka_text: ऊचुस्ते च महीपाला बलदर्पसमन्विताः । न रामरावणं युद्धे पश्यामः पुरतः स्थितम् ।। 7.39.3 ।।
transliteration: ūcuste ca mahīpālā baladarpasamanvitāḥ | na rāmarāvaṇaṃ yuddhe paśyāmaḥ purataḥ sthitam || 7.39.3 ||
translation: ऊचुः they said, ते those, च and, महीपालाः kings, बलदर्पसमन्विताः endowed with the pride of strength, न not, रामरावणम् Rama and Ravana, युद्धे in battle, पश्यामः we see, पुरतः in front, स्थितम् standing.
explanation: And those kings, filled with the pride of their strength, said that they did not see Rama and Ravana standing before them in battle.

shloka_text: भरतेन वयं पश्चात्समानीता निरर्थकम् । हता हि राक्षसाः क्षिप्रं पार्थिवैः स्युर्न संशयः ।। 7.39.4 ।।
transliteration: bharatena vayaṃ paścātsamānītā nirarthakam | hatā hi rākṣasāḥ kṣipraṃ pārthivaiḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ || 7.39.4 ||
translation: भरतेन by Bharata, वयम् we, पश्चात् afterwards, समानीताः brought, निरर्थकम् uselessly, हताः killed, हि indeed, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, क्षिप्रम् quickly, पार्थिवैः by kings, स्युः would be, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: They felt that they had been brought uselessly by Bharata, as the Rakshasas would have certainly been quickly killed by the kings themselves.

shloka_text: रामस्य बाहुवीर्येण रक्षिता लक्ष्मणस्य च । सुखं पारेसमुद्रस्य युध्येम विगतज्वराः ।। 7.39.5 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bāhuvīryeṇa rakṣitā lakṣmaṇasya ca | sukhaṃ pāresamudrasya yudhyema vigatajvarāḥ || 7.39.5 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, बाहुवीर्येण by the strength of the arms, रक्षिताः protected, लक्ष्मणस्य of Lakshmana, च and, सुखम् happily, पारेसमुद्रस्य on the other side of the ocean, युध्येम we would fight, विगतज्वराः free from anxiety.
explanation: Protected by the strength of Rama's and Lakshmana's arms, they would have happily fought on the other side of the ocean, free from any anxiety.

shloka_text: एताश्चान्याश्च राजानः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः । कथयन्तः स्वराज्यानि जग्मुर्हर्षसमन्विताः ।। 7.39.6 ।।
transliteration: etāścānyāśca rājānaḥ kathāstatra sahasraśaḥ | kathayantaḥ svarājyāni jagmurharṣasamanvitāḥ || 7.39.6 ||
translation: एताः these, च and, अन्याः other, च and, राजानः kings, कथाः stories, तत्र there, सहस्रशः by thousands, कथयन्तः narrating, स्वराज्यानि their own kingdoms, जग्मुः went, हर्षसमन्विताः filled with joy.
explanation: These and many other stories, thousands of them, were narrated by the kings there as they returned to their own kingdoms, filled with joy.

shloka_text: स्वानि राज्यानि मुख्यानि ऋद्धानि मुदितानि च । समृद्धधनधान्यानि पूर्णानि वसुमन्ति च ।। 7.39.7 ।।
transliteration: svāni rājyāni mukhyāni ṛddhāni muditāni ca | samṛddhadhanadhānyāni pūrṇāni vasumanti ca || 7.39.7 ||
translation: स्वानि their own, राज्यानि kingdoms, मुख्यानि excellent, ऋद्धानि prosperous, मुदितानि joyful, च and, समृद्धधनधान्यानि rich in wealth and grain, पूर्णानि full, वसुमन्ति possessing wealth, च and.
explanation: Their own excellent and prosperous kingdoms were joyful, full of abundant wealth and grain, and rich in resources.

shloka_text: यथापुराणि ते गत्वा रत्नानि विविधान्यथ । रामस्य प्रियकामार्थमुपहारान् नृपा ददुः ।। 7.39.8 ।।
transliteration: yathāpurāṇi te gatvā ratnāni vividhānyatha | rāmasya priyakāmārthamupahārān nṛpā daduḥ || 7.39.8 ||
translation: यथापुराणि to their respective cities, ते they, गत्वा having gone, रत्नानि jewels, विविधानि various, अथ then, रामस्य of Rama, प्रियकामार्थम् for the sake of pleasing, उपहारान् gifts, नृपाः kings, ददुः gave.
explanation: The kings, having returned to their respective cities, then brought various jewels and gifts to please Rama.

shloka_text: अश्वान्यानानि रत्नानि हस्तिनश्च मदोत्कटान् । चन्दनानि च मुख्यानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.39.9 ।।
transliteration: aśvānyānāni ratnāni hastinaśca madotkaṭān | candanāni ca mukhyāni divyānyābharaṇāni ca || 7.39.9 ||
translation: अश्वान् horses, यानानि vehicles, रत्नानि jewels, हस्तिनः elephants, च and, मदोत्कटान् intoxicated, चन्दनानि sandalwoods, च and, मुख्यानि excellent, दिव्यानि divine, आभरणानि ornaments, च and.
explanation: They presented horses, vehicles, jewels, rutting elephants, excellent sandalwoods, and divine ornaments.

shloka_text: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालांस्तु दास्यो रूपसमन्विताः । अजाविकांश्च विविधान् रथांस्तु विविधान्ददुः ।। 7.39.10 ।।
transliteration: maṇimuktāpravālāṃstu dāsyo rūpasamanvitāḥ | ajāvikāṃśca vividhān rathāṃstu vividhāndaduḥ || 7.39.10 ||
translation: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालान् gems, pearls, and corals, तु and, दास्यः female servants, रूपसमन्विताः endowed with beauty, अजाविकांश्च goats and sheep, विविधान् various, रथान् chariots, तु and, विविधान् various, ददुः gave.
explanation: They also offered gems, pearls, corals, beautiful female servants, various goats and sheep, and diverse chariots.

shloka_text: भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलाः । आदाय तानि रत्नानि स्वां पुरीं पुनरागताः ।। 7.39.11 ।।
transliteration: bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahābalāḥ | ādāya tāni ratnāni svāṃ purīṃ punarāgatāḥ || 7.39.11 ||
translation: भरतः Bharata, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, च and, एव indeed, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, च and, महाबलाः mighty, आदाय having taken, तानि those, रत्नानि jewels, स्वां their own, पुरीम् city, पुनः again, आगताः returned.
explanation: Bharata, Lakshmana, and the mighty Shatrughna, having received those treasures, then returned to their own city.

shloka_text: आगम्य च पुरीं रम्यामयोध्यां पुरुषर्षभाः । तानि रत्नानि चित्राणि रामाय समुपाहरन् ।। 7.39.12 ।।
transliteration: āgamya ca purīṃ ramyāmayodhyāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ | tāni ratnāni citrāṇi rāmāya samupāharan || 7.39.12 ||
translation: आगम्य having arrived, च and, पुरीं city, रम्याम् beautiful, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, पुरुषर्षभाः best among men, तानि those, रत्नानि jewels, चित्राणि various, रामाय to Rama, समुपाहरन् offered.
explanation: Having arrived back in the beautiful city of Ayodhya, those best among men presented the various wonderful jewels to Rama.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिसमन्वितः । सुग्रीवाय ददौ राज्ञे महात्मा कृतकर्मणे ।। 7.39.13 ।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tatsarvaṃ rāmaḥ prītisamanvitaḥ | sugrīvāya dadau rājñe mahātmā kṛtakarmaṇe || 7.39.13 ||
translation: प्रतिगृह्य having received, च and, तत्सर्वं all that, रामः Rama, प्रीतिसमन्वितः filled with joy, सुग्रीवाय to Sugriva, ददौ gave, राज्ञे to the king, महात्मा the great-souled one, कृतकर्मणे who had accomplished great deeds.
explanation: The great-souled Rama, filled with joy, received all those gifts and then gave them to King Sugriva, who had accomplished great deeds.

shloka_text: बिभीषणाय च ददौ तथान्येभ्यो ऽपि राघवः । राक्षसेभ्यः कपिभ्यश्च यैर्वृतो जयमाप्तवान् ।। 7.39.14 ।।
transliteration: bibhīṣaṇāya ca dadau tathānyebhyo 'pi rāghavaḥ | rākṣasebhyaḥ kapibhyaśca yairvṛto jayamāptavān || 7.39.14 ||
translation: बिभीषणाय to Vibhishana, च and, ददौ gave, तथा similarly, अन्येभ्यो to others, अपि also, राघवः Rama, राक्षसेभ्यः to the Rakshasas, कपिभ्यश्च and to the Vanaras, यैः by whom, वृतः surrounded, जयम् victory, आप्तवान् obtained.
explanation: Rama similarly gave gifts to Vibhishana and also to the other Rakshasas and Vanaras by whom he was surrounded and with whose help he had achieved victory.

shloka_text: ते सर्वे रामदत्तानि रत्नानि कपिराक्षसाः । शिरोभिर्धारयामासुर्बाहुभिश्च महाबलाः ।। 7.39.15 ।।
transliteration: te sarve rāmadattāni ratnāni kapirākṣasāḥ | śirobhirdhārayāmāsurbāhubhiśca mahābalāḥ || 7.39.15 ||
translation: ते those, सर्वे all, रामदत्तानि given by Rama, रत्नानि jewels, कपिराक्षसाः Vanaras and Rakshasas, शिरोभिः on their heads, धारयामासुः wore, बाहुभिश्च and on their arms, महाबलाः mighty.
explanation: All those mighty Vanaras and Rakshasas wore the jewels given by Rama on their heads and arms.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च नृपतिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः । अङ्गदं च महाबाहुमङ्कमारोप्य वीर्यवान् ।। 7.39.16 ।।
transliteration: hanūmantaṃ ca nṛpatirikṣvākūṇāṃ mahārathaḥ | aṅgadaṃ ca mahābāhumaṅkamāropya vīryavān || 7.39.16 ||
translation: हनूमन्तं Hanuman, च and, नृपतिः the king, इक्ष्वाकूणां of the Ikshvakus, महारथः the great warrior, अङ्गदं Angada, च and, महाबाहुम् mighty-armed, अङ्कम् on his lap, आरोप्य having placed, वीर्यवान् the valiant one.
explanation: The valiant King of the Ikshvakus, the great warrior Rama, placed Hanuman and the mighty-armed Angada on his lap.

shloka_text: रामः कमलपत्राक्षः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् । अङ्गदस्ते सुपुत्रो ऽयं मन्त्री चाप्यनिलात्मजः ।। 7.39.17 ।।
transliteration: rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt | aṅgadaste suputro 'yaṃ mantrī cāpyanilātmajaḥ || 7.39.17 ||
translation: रामः Rama, कमलपत्राक्षः lotus-petal-eyed, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke, अङ्गदः Angada, ते your, सुपुत्रः good son, अयम् this, मन्त्री minister, च and, अपि also, अनिलात्मजः son of Anila (Hanuman),
explanation: Rama, whose eyes resembled lotus petals, spoke to Sugriva, saying that Angada was his good son and Hanuman was also his minister.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवमन्त्रिते युक्तौ मम चापि हिते रतौ । अर्हतो विविधां पूजां त्वत्कृते वै हरीश्वर ।। 7.39.18 ।।
transliteration: sugrīvamantrite yuktau mama cāpi hite ratau | arhato vividhāṃ pūjāṃ tvatkṛte vai harīśvara || 7.39.18 ||
translation: सुग्रीवमन्त्रिते in Sugriva's counsel, युक्तौ engaged, मम my, च and, अपि also, हिते in welfare, रतौ devoted, अर्हतः they deserve, विविधां various, पूजां honors, त्वत्कृते for your sake, वै indeed, हरीश्वर O lord of monkeys,
explanation: O lord of monkeys, Angada and Hanuman, being engaged in your counsel and devoted to my welfare, indeed deserve various honors for your sake.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा व्यवमुच्याङ्गाद्भूषणानि महायशाः । स बबन्ध महार्हाणि तदाङ्गदहनूमतोः ।। 7.39.19 ।।
transliteration: ityuktvā vyavamucyāṅgādbhūṣaṇāni mahāyaśāḥ | sa babandha mahārhāṇi tadāṅgadahanūmatoḥ || 7.39.19 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, व्यवमुच्य having removed, अङ्गात् from his body, भूषणानि ornaments, महायशाः the greatly renowned, सः he, बबन्ध tied, महार्हाणि very valuable, तदा then, अङ्गदहनूमतोः on Angada and Hanuman,
explanation: Having spoken thus, the greatly renowned Rama then removed valuable ornaments from his own body and fastened them upon Angada and Hanuman.

shloka_text: आभाष्य च महावीर्यान्राघवो यूथपर्षभान् । नीलं नलं केसरिणं कुमुदं गन्धमादनम् ।। 7.39.20 ।।
transliteration: ābhāṣya ca mahāvīryānrāghavo yūthaparṣabhān | nīlaṃ nalaṃ kesariṇaṃ kumudaṃ gandhamādanam || 7.39.20 ||
translation: आभाष्य having addressed, च and, महावीर्यान् the very powerful, राघवः Rama, यूथपर्षभान् the best of the troop leaders, नीलम् Nila, नलम् Nala, केसरिणम् Kesarin, कुमुदम् Kumuda, गन्धमादनम् Gandhamadana,
explanation: And Rama then addressed the very powerful best of the troop leaders: Nila, Nala, Kesarin, Kumuda, and Gandhamadana.

shloka_text: सुषेणं पनसं वीरं मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च । जाम्बवन्तं गवाक्षं च विनतं धूम्रमेव च ।। 7.39.21 ।।
transliteration: suṣeṇaṃ panasaṃ vīraṃ maindaṃ dvividameva ca | jāmbavantaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca vinataṃ dhūmrameva ca || 7.39.21 ||
translation: सुषेणम् Sushena, पनसम् Panasa, वीरम् the brave, मैन्दम् Mainda, द्विविदम् Dvivida, एव indeed, च and, जाम्बवन्तम् Jambavan, गवाक्षम् Gavaksha, च and, विनतम् Vinata, धूम्रम् Dhumra, एव indeed, च and,
explanation: He also addressed Sushena, Panasa, the brave Mainda, Dvivida, Jambavan, Gavaksha, Vinata, and Dhumra.

shloka_text: वलीमुखं प्रजङ्घं च सन्नादं च महाबलम् । दरीमुखं दधिमुखमिन्द्रजानुं च यूथपम् ।। 7.39.22 ।।
transliteration: valīmukhaṃ prajaṅghaṃ ca sannādaṃ ca mahābalam | darīmukhaṃ dadhimukhamindrajānuṃ ca yūthapam || 7.39.22 ||
translation: वलीमुखं Valimukha, प्रजङ्घं Prajangha, च and, सन्नादं Sannada, च and, महाबलम् the mighty, दरीमुखं Darimukha, दधिमुखम् Dadhimukha, इन्द्रजानुं Indrajānu, च and, यूथपम् the troop leader.
explanation: This verse lists the names of several prominent monkey chiefs: Valimukha, Prajangha, the mighty Sannada, Darimukha, Dadhimukha, and Indrajānu, who were all leaders of troops.

shloka_text: मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा नेत्राभ्यामापिबन्निव । सुहृदो मे भवन्तश्च शरीरं भ्रातरस्तथा ।। 7.39.23 ।।
transliteration: madhuraṃ ślakṣṇayā vācā netrābhyāmāpibanniva | suhṛdo me bhavantaśca śarīraṃ bhrātarastathā || 7.39.23 ||
translation: मधुरं sweetly, श्लक्ष्णया with gentle, वाचा words, नेत्राभ्याम् with his eyes, आपिबन्निव as if drinking (them in), सुहृदः friends, मे my, भवन्तश्च you are, शरीरं (part of my) body, भ्रातरः brothers, तथा likewise.
explanation: Speaking sweetly and gently, as if drinking them in with his eyes, Rama declared that they were his friends, his very body, and his brothers.

shloka_text: युष्माभिरुद्धृतश्चाहं व्यसनात्काननौकसः । धन्यो राजा च सुग्रीवो भवद्भिः सुहृदां वरैः ।। 7.39.24 ।।
transliteration: yuṣmābhiruddhṛtaścāhaṃ vyasanātkānanaukasaḥ | dhanyo rājā ca sugrīvo bhavadbhiḥ suhṛdāṃ varaiḥ || 7.39.24 ||
translation: युष्माभिः by you, उद्धृतश्च and rescued, अहम् I, व्यसनात् from distress, काननौकसः O dwellers of the forest, धन्यः blessed, राजा king, च and, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, भवद्भिः by you, सुहृदाम् among friends, वरैः the best.
explanation: Rama declared that he, a dweller of the forest, was rescued from distress by them, and King Sugriva was blessed to have them, the best among friends.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा ददौ तेभ्यो भूषणानि यथार्हतः । वज्राणि च महार्हाणि सस्वजे च नरर्षभः ।। 7.39.25 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā dadau tebhyo bhūṣaṇāni yathārhataḥ | vajrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi sasvaje ca nararṣabhaḥ || 7.39.25 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, ददौ he gave, तेभ्यः to them, भूषणानि ornaments, यथार्हतः as was fitting, वज्राणि diamonds, च and, महार्हाणि very valuable, सस्वजे he embraced, च and, नरर्षभः the best among men.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Rama, the best among men, gave them ornaments and very valuable diamonds as was fitting, and also embraced them.

shloka_text: ते पिबन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः । मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि मूलानि च फलानि च ।। 7.39.26 ।।
transliteration: te pibantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ | māṃsāni ca sumṛṣṭāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca || 7.39.26 ||
translation: ते they, पिबन्तः drinking, सुगन्धीनि fragrant, मधूनि honey, मधुपिङ्गलाः tawny like honey (the monkeys), मांसानि meats, च and, सुमृष्टानि well-prepared, मूलानि roots, च and, फलानि fruits, च and.
explanation: The monkeys, tawny like honey, drank fragrant honey and ate well-prepared meats, roots, and fruits.

shloka_text: एवं तेषां निवसतां मासः साग्रो ययौ तदा । मुहूर्तमिव ते सर्वे रामभक्त्या च मेनिरे ।। 7.39.27 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ teṣāṃ nivasatāṃ māsaḥ sāgro yayau tadā | muhūrtamiva te sarve rāmabhaktyā ca menire || 7.39.27 ||
translation: एवं thus, तेषां of them, निवसतां while dwelling, मासः a month, साग्रो with a part (more than), ययौ passed, तदा then, मुहूर्तमिव like a moment, ते they, सर्वे all, रामभक्त्या due to devotion to Rama, च and, मेनिरे considered.
explanation: While they were thus dwelling, more than a month passed, yet all of them perceived it as merely a moment due to their profound devotion to Rama.

shloka_text: रामो ऽपि रेमे तैः सार्धं वानरैः कामरूपिभिः । राक्षसैश्च महावीर्यैर्ऋक्षैश्चैव महाबलैः ।। 7.39.28 ।।
transliteration: rāmo 'pi reme taiḥ sārdhaṃ vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ | rākṣasaiśca mahāvīryairṛkṣaiścaiva mahābalaiḥ || 7.39.28 ||
translation: रामः Rama, अपि also, रेमे enjoyed, तैः with them, सार्धं together with, वानरैः with monkeys, कामरूपिभिः who could change form at will, राक्षसैः with Rakshasas, च and, महावीर्यैः of great valor, ऋक्षैः with bears, च and, एव indeed, महाबलैः of great strength.
explanation: Rama also delighted in the company of those form-changing monkeys, the greatly valorous Rakshasas, and the exceedingly strong bears.

shloka_text: एवं तेषां ययौ मासो द्वितीयः शिशिरः सुखम् । वानराणां प्रहृष्टानां राक्षसानां च सर्वशः ।। 7.39.29 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ teṣāṃ yayau māso dvitīyaḥ śiśiraḥ sukham | vānarāṇāṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ || 7.39.29 ||
translation: एवं thus, तेषां of them, ययौ passed, मासः a month, द्वितीयः the second, शिशिरः cool/pleasant, सुखम् happily, वानराणां of the monkeys, प्रहृष्टानां who were greatly delighted, राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas, च and, सर्वशः entirely.
explanation: Thus, for all those greatly delighted monkeys and Rakshasas, the second pleasant month passed happily.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकुनगरे रम्ये परां प्रीतिमुपासताम् । रामस्य प्रीतिकरणैः कालस्तेषां सुखं ययौ ।। 7.39.30 ।।
transliteration: ikṣvākunagare ramye parāṃ prītimupāsatām | rāmasya prītikaraṇaiḥ kālasteṣāṃ sukhaṃ yayau || 7.39.30 ||
translation: इक्ष्वाकुनगरे in the city of Ikshvaku, रम्ये beautiful, परां supreme, प्रीतिम् joy, उपासताम् while experiencing, रामस्य of Rama, प्रीतिकरणैः by the acts causing joy, कालः time, तेषां of them, सुखं happily, ययौ passed.
explanation: While they were experiencing supreme joy in the beautiful city of Ikshvaku, time passed happily for them due to Rama's delightful actions. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 39 ।। Thus ends the thirty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथा स्म तेषां वसतामृक्षवानररक्षसाम् । राघवस्तु महातेजाः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.40.1 ।।
transliteration: tathā sma teṣāṃ vasatāmṛkṣavānararakṣasām | rāghavastu mahātejāḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt || 7.40.1 ||
translation: तथा thus, स्म (past tense particle), तेषां of them, वसतां while dwelling, ऋक्षवानररक्षसाम् of the bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas, राघवः Rama, तु indeed, महातेजाः of great splendor, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: While those bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas were thus dwelling, the greatly effulgent Rama then spoke these words to Sugriva.
comments: Rama bids his allies return to their realms -- Sugriva to Kishkindha and Vibhishana to rule Lanka righteously -- Hanuman asks that he may live as long as Rama's story is told on earth, and Rama grants the boon and gives him his own necklace -- amid tears the vanaras, bears and rakshasas take their leave and depart for their homes.

shloka_text: गम्यतां सौम्य किष्किन्धां दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः । पालयस्व सहामात्यो राज्यं निहतकण्टकम् ।। 7.40.2 ।।
transliteration: gamyatāṃ saumya kiṣkindhāṃ durādharṣāṃ surāsuraiḥ | pālayasva sahāmātyo rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam || 7.40.2 ||
translation: गम्यतां go, सौम्य O gentle one, किष्किन्धां to Kishkindha, दुराधर्षां unassailable, सुरासुरैः by gods and demons, पालयस्व rule, सहामात्यो with your ministers, राज्यं the kingdom, निहतकण्टकम् free from enemies.
explanation: O gentle one, go to Kishkindha, which is unassailable even by gods and demons, and rule your kingdom with your ministers, having removed all its enemies.

shloka_text: अङ्गदं च महाबाहो प्रीत्या परमया युतः । पश्य त्वं हनुमन्तं च नलं च सुमहाबलम् ।। 7.40.3 ।।
transliteration: aṅgadaṃ ca mahābāho prītyā paramayā yutaḥ | paśya tvaṃ hanumantaṃ ca nalaṃ ca sumahābalam || 7.40.3 ||
translation: अङ्गदं Angada, च and, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, प्रीत्या with affection, परमया supreme, युतः endowed with, पश्य see, त्वं you, हनुमन्तं Hanuman, च and, नलं Nala, च and, सुमहाबलम् of great strength.
explanation: O mighty-armed one, you should look upon Angada, Hanuman, and Nala of great strength with supreme affection.

shloka_text: सुषेणं श्वशुरं वीरं तारं च बलिनां वरम् । कुमुदं चैव दुर्धर्षं नीलं चैव महाबलम् ।। 7.40.4 ।।
transliteration: suṣeṇaṃ śvaśuraṃ vīraṃ tāraṃ ca balināṃ varam | kumudaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ nīlaṃ caiva mahābalam || 7.40.4 ||
translation: सुषेणं Sushena, श्वशुरं your father-in-law, वीरं the brave, तारं Tara, च and, बलिनां among the strong, वरम् the best, कुमुदं Kumuda, चैव and also, दुर्धर्षं unassailable, नीलं Nila, चैव and also, महाबलम् of great strength.
explanation: Also see the brave Sushena, your father-in-law, Tara, the best among the strong, and the unassailable Kumuda, and Nila of great strength.

shloka_text: वीरं शतवलिं चैव मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च । गजं गवाक्षं गवयं शरभं च महाबलम् । पश्य प्रीतिसमायुक्तो गन्धमादनमेव च ।। 7.40.5 ।।
transliteration: vīraṃ śatavaliṃ caiva maindaṃ dvividameva ca | gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ śarabhaṃ ca mahābalam | paśya prītisamāyukto gandhamādanameva ca || 7.40.5 ||
translation: वीरं the brave, शतवलिं Shatavali, चैव and also, मैन्दं Mainda, द्विविदमेव and Dvivida, च and, गजं Gaja, गवाक्षं Gavaksha, गवयं Gavaya, शरभं Sharabha, च and, महाबलम् of great strength, पश्य see, प्रीतिसमायुक्तो filled with affection, गन्धमादनमेव and Gandhamadana, च and.
explanation: Look with affection upon the brave Shatavali, Mainda, Dvivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha of great strength, and Gandhamadana.

shloka_text: ऋषभं च सुविक्रान्तं जाम्बवन्तं महाबलम् । ये चेमे सुमहात्मानो मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।। 7.40.6 ।।
transliteration: ṛṣabhaṃ ca suvikrāntaṃ jāmbavantaṃ mahābalam | ye ceme sumahātmāno madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ || 7.40.6 ||
translation: ऋषभं Rishabha, च and, सुविक्रान्तं very valorous, जाम्बवन्तं Jambavan, महाबलम् of great strength, ये those who, च and, इमे these, सुमहात्मानो great-souled ones, मदर्थे for my sake, त्यक्तजीविताः who risked their lives.
explanation: Also see Rishabha, the very valorous, and Jambavan of great strength, and all these other great-souled beings who risked their lives for my sake.

shloka_text: पश्य त्वं प्रीतिसंयुक्तो मा चैषां विप्रियं कृथाः ।। 7.40.7 ।।
transliteration: paśya tvaṃ prītisaṃyukto mā caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kṛthāḥ || 7.40.7 ||
translation: पश्य see, त्वं you, प्रीतिसंयुक्तो endowed with affection, मा not, च and, एषां to them, विप्रियं harm, कृथाः do.
explanation: You should look upon them with affection and never cause them any harm.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवमाश्लिष्य च पुनः पुनः । विभीषणमुवाचाथ रामो मधुरया गिरा ।। 7.40.8 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu sugrīvamāśliṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ | vibhīṣaṇamuvācātha rāmo madhurayā girā || 7.40.8 ||
translation: एवमुक्त्वा having said thus, तु then, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, आश्लिष्य having embraced, च and, पुनः पुनः again and again, विभीषणम् to Vibhishana, उवाच spoke, अथ then, रामो Rama, मधुरया with sweet, गिरा words.
explanation: Having spoken thus and repeatedly embraced Sugriva, Rama then addressed Vibhishana with sweet words.

shloka_text: लङ्कां प्रशाधि धर्मेण धर्मज्ञस्त्वं मतो मम । पुरस्य राक्षसानां च स्वभ्रातुस्सम्मतो ह्यसि ।। 7.40.9 ।।
transliteration: laṅkāṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa dharmajñastvaṃ mato mama | purasya rākṣasānāṃ ca svabhrātussammato hyasi || 7.40.9 ||
translation: लङ्कां Lanka, प्रशाधि rule, धर्मेण with righteousness, धर्मज्ञः one who knows dharma, त्वं you, मतो considered, मम by me, पुरस्य of the city, राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas, च and, स्वभ्रातुः by your own brother, सम्मतो approved, हि indeed, असि you are.
explanation: Rule Lanka righteously, for I consider you knowledgeable in dharma, and you are indeed approved by your own brother, by the city, and by the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: मा च बुद्धिमधर्मे त्वं कुर्या राजन्कथञ्चन । बुद्धिमन्तो हि राजानो ध्रुवमश्नन्ति मेदिनीम् ।। 7.40.10 ।।
transliteration: mā ca buddhimadharme tvaṃ kuryā rājankathañcana | buddhimanto hi rājāno dhruvamaśnanti medinīm || 7.40.10 ||
translation: मा not, च and, बुद्धिम् mind, अधर्मे in unrighteousness, त्वं you, कुर्याः should place, राजन् O King, कथञ्चन ever, बुद्धिमन्तो intelligent, हि indeed, राजानो kings, ध्रुवम् certainly, अश्नन्ति enjoy, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: O King, never let your mind incline towards unrighteousness, for intelligent kings certainly rule the earth.

shloka_text: अहं च नित्यशो राजन्सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया । स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः ।। 7.40.11 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ ca nityaśo rājansugrīvasahitastvayā | smartavyaḥ parayā prītyā gaccha tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ || 7.40.11 ||
translation: अहं I, च and, नित्यशो always, राजन् O King, सुग्रीवसहितः along with Sugriva, त्वया by you, स्मर्तव्यः should be remembered, परया with great, प्रीत्या affection, गच्छ go, त्वं you, विगतज्वरः free from sorrow.
explanation: O King, you should always remember me and Sugriva with great affection; now go, free from all sorrow.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः । साधुसाध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः ।। 7.40.12 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā ṛkṣavānararākṣasāḥ | sādhusādhviti kākutsthaṃ praśaśaṃsuḥ punaḥ punaḥ || 7.40.12 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितं speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, साधुसाध्विति "Excellent! Excellent!" thus, काकुत्स्थं Kakutstha (Rama), प्रशशंसुः praised, पुनः पुनः again and again.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, the bears, monkeys, and rakshasas repeatedly praised him, exclaiming "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: तव बुद्धिर्महाबाहो वीर्यमद्भुतमेव च । माधुर्यं परमं राम स्वयम्भोरिव नित्यदा ।। 7.40.13 ।।
transliteration: tava buddhirmahābāho vīryamadbhutameva ca | mādhuryaṃ paramaṃ rāma svayambhoriva nityadā || 7.40.13 ||
translation: तव Your, बुद्धिः intellect, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, वीर्यम् valor, अद्भुतम् wonderful, एव indeed, च and, माधुर्यं sweetness, परमं supreme, राम O Rama, स्वयम्भोः of the Self-born (Brahma), इव like, नित्यदा always.
explanation: O mighty-armed Rama, your intellect and valor are truly wonderful, and your supreme sweetness is eternal, like that of the Self-born Brahma.

shloka_text: तेषामेवं ब्रुवाणानां वानराणां च राक्षसाम् । हनूमान्प्रवणः भूत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.40.14 ।।
transliteration: teṣāmevaṃ bruvāṇānāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rākṣasām | hanūmānpravaṇaḥ bhūtvā rāghavaṃ vākyamabravīt || 7.40.14 ||
translation: तेषाम् of them, एवम् thus, ब्रुवाणानां speaking, वानराणां of the monkeys, च and, राक्षसाम् of the rakshasas, हनूमान् Hanuman, प्रवणः bowing down, भूत्वा having become, राघवं to Raghava (Rama), वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: While the monkeys and rakshasas were speaking thus, Hanuman, bowing down humbly, addressed Rama.

shloka_text: स्नेहो मे परमो राजंस्त्वयि तिष्ठतु नित्यदा । भक्तिश्च नियता वीर भावो नान्यत्र गच्छतु ।। 7.40.15 ।।
transliteration: sneho me paramo rājaṃstvayi tiṣṭhatu nityadā | bhaktiśca niyatā vīra bhāvo nānyatra gacchatu || 7.40.15 ||
translation: स्नेहः affection, मे my, परमः supreme, राजन् O King, त्वयि in you, तिष्ठतु may it remain, नित्यदा always, भक्तिः devotion, च and, नियता constant, वीर O hero, भावः feeling, न not, अन्यत्र elsewhere, गच्छतु may it go.
explanation: O King, may my supreme affection for you remain always, and O hero, may my devotion be unwavering, with my feelings never straying elsewhere.

shloka_text: वायद्रामकथा वीर चरिष्यति महीतले । तावच्छरीरे वत्स्यन्ति प्राणा मम न संशयः ।। 7.40.16 ।।
transliteration: vāyadrāmakathā vīra cariṣyati mahītale | tāvaccharīre vatsyanti prāṇā mama na saṃśayaḥ || 7.40.16 ||
translation: यावत् as long as, रामकथा the story of Rama, वीर O hero, चरिष्यति will prevail, महीतले on the earth's surface, तावत् so long, शरीरे in the body, वत्स्यन्ति will reside, प्राणाः life breaths, मम my, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: O hero, as long as the story of Rama is told on the earth, my life breaths will undoubtedly remain in my body.

shloka_text: यच्चैतच्चरितं दिव्यं कथा ते रघुनन्दन । तन्मयाप्सरसो नाम श्रावयेयुर्नरर्षभ ।। 7.40.17 ।।
transliteration: yaccaitaccaritaṃ divyaṃ kathā te raghunandana | tanmayāpsaraso nāma śrāvayeyurnararṣabha || 7.40.17 ||
translation: यत् which, च and, एतत् this, चरितं divine story/deed, दिव्यं divine, कथा story, ते your, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus, तत् that, मया by me, अप्सरसः Apsaras, नाम indeed, श्रावयेयुः should make me hear, नरर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O Rama, delight of the Raghus and best among men, may the Apsaras indeed make me hear this divine story and your divine deeds.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वाहं ततो वीर तव चर्यामृतं प्रभो । उत्कण्ठां तां हरिष्यामि मेघलेखामिवानिलः ।। 7.40.18 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvāhaṃ tato vīra tava caryāmṛtaṃ prabho | utkaṇṭhāṃ tāṃ hariṣyāmi meghalekhāmivānilaḥ || 7.40.18 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, अहं I, ततः then, वीर O hero, तव your, चर्यामृतं nectar-like deeds/story, प्रभो O lord, उत्कण्ठां longing/sorrow, तां that, हरिष्यामि I shall remove, मेघलेखाम् a line of clouds, इव like, अनिलः wind.
explanation: O hero, O lord, having heard that nectar-like story of your deeds, I shall then remove that longing/sorrow, just as the wind disperses a line of clouds.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणं रामस्तु हनूमन्तं वरासनात् । उत्थाय सस्वजे स्नेहाद्वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.40.19 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ rāmastu hanūmantaṃ varāsanāt | utthāya sasvaje snehādvākyametaduvāca ha || 7.40.19 ||
translation: एवं thus, ब्रुवाणं speaking, रामः Rama, तु indeed, हनूमन्तं Hanuman, वरासनात् from his excellent seat, उत्थाय having risen, सस्वजे embraced, स्नेहात् out of affection, वाक्यम् word, एतत् this, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Rama, having risen from his excellent seat, embraced Hanuman who was speaking thus, and out of affection, indeed spoke these words.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्कपिश्रेष्ठ भविता नात्र संशयः । चरिष्यति कथा यावदेषा लोके च मामिका । तावत्ते भविता कीर्तिः शरीरे ऽप्यसवस्तथा ।। 7.40.20 ।।
transliteration: evametatkapiśreṣṭha bhavitā nātra saṃśayaḥ | cariṣyati kathā yāvadeṣā loke ca māmikā | tāvatte bhavitā kīrtiḥ śarīre 'pyasavastathā || 7.40.20 ||
translation: एवम् thus, एतत् this, कपिश्रेष्ठ O best of monkeys, भविता it will be, न no, अत्र here, संशयः doubt, चरिष्यति will spread/exist, कथा story, यावत् as long as, एषा this, लोके in the world, च and, मामिका my, तावत् so long, ते your, भविता will be, कीर्तिः fame, शरीरे in the body, अपि even, असवाः life-breaths, तथा similarly.
explanation: O best of monkeys, it will indeed be so, there is no doubt about it; as long as this story of mine spreads in the world, so long will your fame and life-breaths remain in your body.

shloka_text: लोका हि यावत्स्थास्यन्ति तावत्स्थास्यति मे कथा ।। 7.40.21 ।।
transliteration: lokā hi yāvatsthāsyanti tāvatsthāsyati me kathā || 7.40.21 ||
translation: लोकाः worlds/people, हि indeed, यावत् as long as, स्थास्यन्ति will exist/remain, तावत् so long, स्थास्यति will exist/remain, मे my, कथा story.
explanation: Indeed, as long as the worlds exist, so long will my story endure.

shloka_text: लोके च मामिका । एकैकस्योपकारस्य प्राणान्दास्यामि ते कपे । नरः प्रत्युपकाराणामापस्त्वायाति पात्रताम् ।। 7.40.22 ।।
transliteration: loke ca māmikā | ekaikasyopakārasya prāṇāndāsyāmi te kape | naraḥ pratyupakārāṇāmāpastvāyāti pātratām || 7.40.22 ||
translation: लोके in the world, च and, मामिका mine (gratitude), एकैकस्य of each and every, उपकारस्य favor, प्राणान् lives, दास्यामि I will give, ते to you, कपे O monkey, नरः a man, प्रत्युपकाराणाम् of return favors, आपस्त्वायाति आपत्सु in distress, आयाति comes, पात्रताम् worthiness.
explanation: Rama declares that his gratitude is such that he would give his life for each of Hanuman's favors, emphasizing that a person becomes worthy of receiving return favors even when in distress.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्य हारं चन्द्राभं मुच्य कण्ठात्स राघवः । वैडूर्यतरलं कण्ठे बबन्ध च हनूमतः ।। 7.40.23 ।।
transliteration: tato 'sya hāraṃ candrābhaṃ mucya kaṇṭhātsa rāghavaḥ | vaiḍūryataralaṃ kaṇṭhe babandha ca hanūmataḥ || 7.40.23 ||
translation: ततः then, अस्य his (Rama's), हारम् necklace, चन्द्राभम् moon-like, मुच्य having taken off, कण्ठात् from the neck, सः he, राघवः Rama, वैडूर्यतरलम् with a cat's eye gem pendant, कण्ठे on the neck, बबन्ध tied, च and, हनूमतः of Hanuman.
explanation: Then, Rama took off his own moon-like necklace from his neck and fastened it, adorned with a cat's eye gem, onto Hanuman's neck.

shloka_text: तेनोरसि निबद्धेन हारेण महता कपिः । रराज हेमशैलेन्द्रश्चन्द्रेणाक्रान्तमस्तकः ।। 7.40.24 ।।
transliteration: tenorasi nibaddhena hāreṇa mahatā kapiḥ | rarāja hemaśailendraścandreṇākrāntamastakaḥ || 7.40.24 ||
translation: तेन by that, उरसि on the chest, निबद्धेन fastened, हारेण by the necklace, महता great, कपिः the monkey (Hanuman), रराज shone, हेमशैलेन्द्रः like a great golden mountain, चन्द्रेण by the moon, आक्रान्तमस्तकः whose peak is covered.
explanation: With that great necklace fastened on his chest, Hanuman shone like a magnificent golden mountain whose peak is adorned by the moon.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतदुत्थायोत्थाय वानराः । प्रणम्य शिरसा पादौ निर्जग्मुस्ते महाबलाः ।। 7.40.25 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu rāghavasyaitadutthāyotthāya vānarāḥ | praṇamya śirasā pādau nirjagmuste mahābalāḥ || 7.40.25 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, राघवस्य of Rama, एतत् this, उत्थायोत्थाय repeatedly rising up, वानराः the monkeys, प्रणम्य having bowed, शिरसा with their heads, पादौ at the feet, निर्जग्मुः they departed, ते those, महाबलाः mighty ones.
explanation: Having heard these words from Rama, those mighty monkeys repeatedly rose, bowed their heads at his feet, and then departed.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवः स च रामेण निरन्तरमुरोगतः । विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा सर्वे ते बाष्पविक्लवाः ।। 7.40.26 ।।
transliteration: sugrīvaḥ sa ca rāmeṇa nirantaramurogataḥ | vibhīṣaṇaśca dharmātmā sarve te bāṣpaviklavāḥ || 7.40.26 ||
translation: सुग्रीवः Sugriva, सः he, च and, रामेण by Rama, निरन्तरम् closely, उरोगतः embraced, विभीषणः Vibhishana, च and, धर्मात्मा righteous-souled, सर्वे all, ते they, बाष्पविक्लवाः overcome with tears.
explanation: Sugriva, who was constantly embraced by Rama, and the righteous Vibhishana, along with all the others, were overcome with tears.

shloka_text: सर्वे च ते बाष्पकलाः साश्रुनेत्रा विचेतसः । सम्मूढा इव दुःखेन त्यजन्तो राघवं तदा ।। 7.40.27 ।।
transliteration: sarve ca te bāṣpakalāḥ sāśrunetrā vicetasaḥ | sammūḍhā iva duḥkhena tyajanto rāghavaṃ tadā || 7.40.27 ||
translation: सर्वे all, च and, ते they, बाष्पकलाः full of tears, साश्रुनेत्राः with tearful eyes, विचेतसः bewildered, सम्मूढाः stupefied, इव as if, दुःखेन by sorrow, त्यजन्तः leaving, राघवं Rama, तदा then
explanation: At that time, all of them, full of tears and with tearful eyes, were bewildered and stupefied by sorrow as they were leaving Rama.

shloka_text: कृतप्रसादास्तेनैवं राघवेण महात्मना । जग्मुः स्वं स्वं गृहं सर्वे देही देहमिव त्यजन् ।। 7.40.28 ।।
transliteration: kṛtaprasādāstenaivaṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā | jagmuḥ svaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ sarve dehī dehamiva tyajan || 7.40.28 ||
translation: कृतप्रसादाः having received grace, तेन by him, एवं thus, राघवेण by Rama, महात्मना by the great-souled, जग्मुः they went, स्वं स्वं their own respective, गृहं home, सर्वे all, देही an embodied soul, देहं the body, इव as if, त्यजन् abandoning
explanation: Having thus received grace from the great-souled Rama, all of them returned to their respective homes, feeling as if an embodied soul abandoning its body.

shloka_text: ततस्तु ते राक्षसऋक्षवानराः प्रणम्य रामं रघुवंशवर्धनम् । वियोगजाश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचनाः प्रतिप्रयातास्तु यथा निवासिनः ।। 7.40.29 ।।
transliteration: tatastu te rākṣasaṛkṣavānarāḥ praṇamya rāmaṃ raghuvaṃśavardhanam | viyogajāśrupratipūrṇalocanāḥ pratiprayātāstu yathā nivāsinaḥ || 7.40.29 ||
translation: ततः then, तु indeed, ते those, राक्षसऋक्षवानराः Rakshasas, bears, and monkeys, प्रणम्य having bowed down, रामं to Rama, रघुवंशवर्धनम् the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty, वियोगजाश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचनाः with eyes full of tears born of separation, प्रतिप्रयाताः returned, तु indeed, यथा to their respective, निवासिनः abodes
explanation: Then, those Rakshasas, bears, and monkeys, having bowed down to Rama, the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty, returned to their respective abodes with eyes full of tears born of separation. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 40 ।। Thus ends the fortieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विसृज्य च महाबाहुर्ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान् । भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः प्रमुमोद सुखं सुखी ।। 7.41.1 ।।
transliteration: visṛjya ca mahābāhurṛkṣavānararākṣasān | bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ pramumoda sukhaṃ sukhī || 7.41.1 ||
translation: विसृज्य having dismissed, च and, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed one, ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान् the bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas, भ्रातृभिः with his brothers, सहितः accompanied, रामः Rama, प्रमुमोद rejoiced greatly, सुखं happily, सुखी happy
explanation: And the mighty-armed Rama, having dismissed the bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas, was very happy and rejoiced greatly along with his brothers.
comments: The Pushpaka chariot, released by Kubera, returns and offers itself to Rama, who worships and dismisses it, bidding it come whenever summoned -- Bharata then tells how, under Rama's righteous reign, no disease or untimely death afflicts the people, the rains and seasons are auspicious, and the citizens pray that such a king be immortal.

shloka_text: अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः । शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षात् प्रभाषिताम् ।। 7.41.2 ।।
transliteration: athāparāhṇasamaye bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rāghavaḥ | śuśrāva madhurāṃ vāṇīmantarikṣāt prabhāṣitām || 7.41.2 ||
translation: अथ then, अपराह्णसमये in the afternoon, भ्रातृभिः with his brothers, सह together with, राघवः Rama, शुश्राव he heard, मधुरां a sweet, वाणीं voice, अन्तरिक्षात् from the sky, प्रभाषिताम् spoken
explanation: Then, in the afternoon, Rama, along with his brothers, heard a sweet voice spoken from the sky.

shloka_text: सौम्य राम निरीक्षस्व सौम्येन वदनेन माम् । कुबेरभवनात्प्राप्तं विद्धि मां पुष्पकं प्रभो ।। 7.41.3 ।।
transliteration: saumya rāma nirīkṣasva saumyena vadanena mām | kuberabhavanātprāptaṃ viddhi māṃ puṣpakaṃ prabho || 7.41.3 ||
