translation: सौम्य O gentle one, राम O Rama, निरीक्षस्व look at, सौम्येन with a gentle, वदनेन face, माम् me, कुबेरभवनात् from Kubera's abode, प्राप्तम् arrived, विद्धि know, माम् me, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, प्रभो O Lord.
explanation: O gentle Rama, look at me with a gentle face; know me, O Lord, to be the Pushpaka chariot that has arrived from Kubera's abode.

shloka_text: तव शासनमाज्ञाय गतो ऽस्मि भवनं प्रति । उपस्थातुं नरश्रेष्ठ स च मां प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.41.4 ।।
transliteration: tava śāsanamājñāya gato 'smi bhavanaṃ prati | upasthātuṃ naraśreṣṭha sa ca māṃ pratyabhāṣata || 7.41.4 ||
translation: तव your, शासनम् command, आज्ञाय having understood, गतः अस्मि I have gone, भवनम् abode, प्रति towards, उपस्थातुम् to serve, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, सः he, च and, माम् to me, प्रत्यभाषत replied.
explanation: O best among men, having understood your command, I went to his abode to serve, and he (Kubera) spoke to me in return.

shloka_text: निर्जितस्त्वं नरेन्द्रेण राघवेण महात्मना । निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम् ।। 7.41.5 ।।
transliteration: nirjitastvaṃ narendreṇa rāghaveṇa mahātmanā | nihatya yudhi durdharṣaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram || 7.41.5 ||
translation: निर्जितः conquered, त्वम् you, नरेन्द्रेण by the king, राघवेण by Rama, महात्मना by the great-souled one, निहत्य having killed, युधि in battle, दुर्धर्षम् formidable, रावणम् Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरम् the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: He said, "You have been conquered by the great-souled king Rama, the descendant of Raghu, who slew the formidable Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, in battle."

shloka_text: ममापि परमा प्रीतर्हते तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि । रावणे सगणे चैव सपुत्रे सहबान्धवे ।। 7.41.6 ।।
transliteration: mamāpi paramā prītarhate tasmindurātmani | rāvaṇe sagaṇe caiva saputre sahabāndhave || 7.41.6 ||
translation: मम my, अपि also, परमा supreme, प्रीतिः joy, हते when killed, तस्मिन् that, दुरात्मनि evil-minded one, रावणे Ravana, सगणे with his retinue, च and, एव indeed, सपुत्रे with his sons, सहबान्धवे with his relatives.
explanation: He further said, "My supreme joy also arises from the killing of that evil-minded Ravana, along with his retinue, sons, and relatives."

shloka_text: स त्वं रामेण लङ्कायां निर्जितः परमात्मना । वह सौम्य तमेव त्वमहमाज्ञापयामि ते ।। 7.41.7 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ rāmeṇa laṅkāyāṃ nirjitaḥ paramātmanā | vaha saumya tameva tvamahamājñāpayāmi te || 7.41.7 ||
translation: सः that, त्वम् you, रामेण by Rama, लङ्कायाम् in Lanka, निर्जितः conquered, परमात्मना by the supreme soul, वह carry, सौम्य O gentle one, तम् him, एव indeed, त्वम् you, अहम् I, आज्ञपयामि command, ते you.
explanation: He concluded, "Therefore, O gentle Pushpaka, since you were conquered by the supreme Rama in Lanka, you must carry him; I command you to do so."

shloka_text: परमो ह्येष मे कामो यत्त्वं राघवनन्दनम् । वहेर्लोकस्य संयानं गच्छस्व विगतज्वरः ।। 7.41.8 ।।
transliteration: paramo hyeṣa me kāmo yattvaṃ rāghavanandanam | vaherlokasya saṃyānaṃ gacchasva vigatajvaraḥ || 7.41.8 ||
translation: परमो supreme, हि indeed, एष this, मे my, कामो desire, यत् that, त्वं you, राघवनन्दनम् Rama, वहेः should carry, लोकस्य of the people, संयानं the journey, गच्छस्व go, विगतज्वरः free from distress.
explanation: This is indeed my greatest desire, that you should carry Rama and the people on their journey; therefore, go forth without any anxiety.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं शासनमाज्ञाय धनदस्य महात्मनः । त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तो निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीक्ष माम् ।। 7.41.9 ।।
transliteration: so 'haṃ śāsanamājñāya dhanadasya mahātmanaḥ | tvatsakāśamanuprāpto nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīkṣa mām || 7.41.9 ||
translation: सो that, अहं I, शासनम् command, आज्ञाय having understood, धनदस्य of Kubera, महात्मनः the great-souled, त्वत्सकाशम् to your presence, अनुप्राप्तो arrived, निर्विशङ्कः without doubt, प्रतीक्ष wait for, माम् me.
explanation: Having understood the command of the great-souled Kubera, I have arrived in your presence; therefore, wait for me without any apprehension.

shloka_text: अदृष्यः सर्वभूतानां सर्वेषां धनदाज्ञया । चराम्यहं प्रभावेण तवाज्ञां परिपालयन् ।। 7.41.10 ।।
transliteration: adṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dhanadājñayā | carāmyahaṃ prabhāveṇa tavājñāṃ paripālayan || 7.41.10 ||
translation: अदृष्यः invisible, सर्वभूतानां to all beings, सर्वेषां to all, धनदाज्ञया by Kubera's command, चरामि I move, अहं I, प्रभावेण by my power, तवाज्ञां your command, परिपालयन् obeying.
explanation: By Kubera's command, I am invisible to all beings and I move by my own power, obeying your command.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तदा रामः पुष्पकेण महाबलः । उवाच पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा विमानं पुनरागतम् ।। 7.41.11 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastadā rāmaḥ puṣpakeṇa mahābalaḥ | uvāca puṣpakaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimānaṃ punarāgatam || 7.41.11 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः addressed, तदा then, रामः Rama, पुष्पकेण by Pushpaka, महाबलः the mighty, उवाच spoke, पुष्पकं Pushpaka, दृष्ट्वा having seen, विमानं the aerial car, पुनरागतम् returned again.
explanation: Thus addressed by Pushpaka, the mighty Rama then spoke, having seen the Pushpaka aerial car returned again.

shloka_text: यद्येवं स्वागतं ते ऽस्तु विमानवर पुष्पक । आनुकूल्याद्धनेशस्य वृत्तदोषो न नो भवेत् ।। 7.41.12 ।।
transliteration: yadyevaṃ svāgataṃ te 'stu vimānavara puṣpaka | ānukūlyāddhaneśasya vṛttadoṣo na no bhavet || 7.41.12 ||
translation: यदि if, एवम् so, स्वागतं welcome, ते to you, अस्तु let it be, विमानवर O best of aerial cars, पुष्पक Pushpaka, आनुकूल्यात् due to the favor, धनेशस्य of Kubera, वृत्तदोषो fault in conduct, न not, नः our, भवेत् may it be.
explanation: If it is so, then welcome to you, O best of aerial cars, Pushpaka; due to the favor of Kubera, no impropriety shall befall us.

shloka_text: लाजैश्चैव तथा पुष्पैर्धूपैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः । पूजयित्वा महाबाहू राघवः पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.13 ।।
transliteration: lājaiścaiva tathā puṣpairdhūpaiścaiva sugandhibhiḥ | pūjayitvā mahābāhū rāghavaḥ puṣpakaṃ tadā || 7.41.13 ||
translation: लाजैः with parched grains, च and, एव indeed, तथा similarly, पुष्पैः with flowers, धूपैः with incense, च and, एव indeed, सुगन्धिभिः fragrant, पूजयित्वा having worshipped, महाबाहू the mighty-armed one, राघवः Rama, पुष्पकम् the Pushpaka, तदा then.
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Rama worshipped the Pushpaka chariot with parched grains, flowers, and fragrant incense.

shloka_text: गम्यतामिति चोवाच आगच्छ त्वं स्मरे यदा । सिद्धानां च गतौ सौम्य मा विषादेन योजय । प्रतिघातश्च ते मा भूद्यथेष्टं गच्छतो दिशः ।। 7.41.14 ।।
transliteration: gamyatāmiti covāca āgaccha tvaṃ smare yadā | siddhānāṃ ca gatau saumya mā viṣādena yojaya | pratighātaśca te mā bhūdyatheṣṭaṃ gacchato diśaḥ || 7.41.14 ||
translation: गम्यताम् let it go, इति thus, च and, उवाच he said, आगच्छ come, त्वम् you, स्मरे remember, यदा when, सिद्धानाम् of the Siddhas, च and, गतौ in flight, सौम्य O gentle one, मा do not, विषादेन with sorrow, योजय afflict, प्रतिघातः obstruction, च and, ते to you, मा do not, भूत् let it be, यथेष्टम् as desired, गच्छतः going, दिशः directions.
explanation: Rama then told the Pushpaka, "Depart now, and remember to return whenever I recall you; O gentle one, do not be afflicted with sorrow, and may there be no obstruction to your desired flight in any direction, like that of the Siddhas."

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति रामेण पूजयित्वा विसर्जितम् । अभिप्रेतां दिशं तस्मात्प्रायात्तत्पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.15 ।।
transliteration: evamastviti rāmeṇa pūjayitvā visarjitam | abhipretāṃ diśaṃ tasmātprāyāttatpuṣpakaṃ tadā || 7.41.15 ||
translation: एवम् thus, अस्तु let it be, इति thus, रामेण by Rama, पूजयित्वा having worshipped, विसर्जितम् dismissed, अभिप्रेताम् desired, दिशम् direction, तस्मात् from there, प्रायात् departed, तत् that, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, तदा then.
explanation: Having been worshipped and dismissed by Rama with the words "So be it," the Pushpaka then departed from there towards its desired direction.

shloka_text: एवमन्तर्हिते तस्मिन्पुष्पके सुकृतात्मनि । भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.41.16 ।।
transliteration: evamantarhite tasminpuṣpake sukṛtātmani | bharataḥ prāñjalirvākyamuvāca raghunandanam || 7.41.16 ||
translation: एवम् thus, अन्तर्हिते having disappeared, तस्मिन् that, पुष्पके Pushpaka, सुकृतात्मनि of good deeds, भरतः Bharata, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यम् words, उवाच spoke, रघुनन्दनम् to Rama.
explanation: After that Pushpaka, which was of good deeds, had thus disappeared, Bharata, with folded hands, spoke these words to Rama.

shloka_text: विविधात्मनि दृश्यन्ते त्वयि वीर प्रशासति । अमानुषाणां सत्त्वानां व्याहृतानि मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.41.17 ।।
transliteration: vividhātmani dṛśyante tvayi vīra praśāsati | amānuṣāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vyāhṛtāni muhurmuhuḥ || 7.41.17 ||
translation: विविधात्मनि in various forms, दृश्यन्ते are seen, त्वयि in you, वीर O hero, प्रशासति ruling, अमानुषाणाम् of non-human, सत्त्वानाम् beings, व्याहृतानि utterances, मुहुर्मुहुः repeatedly.
explanation: O hero, while you rule, the utterances of non-human beings are repeatedly seen in various forms.

shloka_text: अनामयश्च सत्वानां साग्रो मासो गतो ह्ययम् । जीर्णानामपि सत्त्वानां मृत्युर्नायाति राघव ।। 7.41.18 ।।
transliteration: anāmayaśca satvānāṃ sāgro māso gato hyayam | jīrṇānāmapi sattvānāṃ mṛtyurnāyāti rāghava || 7.41.18 ||
translation: अनामयः without disease, च and, सत्वानां of beings, साग्रः full, मासः month, गतः passed, हि indeed, अयम् this, जीर्णानाम् of the old, अपि even, सत्त्वानां of beings, मृत्युः death, न not, आयाति comes, राघव O Raghava.
explanation: O Raghava, this full month has passed without any disease among beings, and even for the aged, death does not come.

shloka_text: अरोगप्रसवा नार्यो वपुष्मन्तो हि मानवाः । हर्षश्चाभ्यधिको राजञ्जनस्य पुरवासिनः ।। 7.41.19 ।।
transliteration: arogaprasavā nāryo vapuṣmanto hi mānavāḥ | harṣaścābhyadhiko rājañjanasya puravāsinaḥ || 7.41.19 ||
translation: अरोगप्रसवाः giving birth without illness, नार्यः women, वपुष्मन्तः healthy, हि indeed, मानवाः humans, हर्षः joy, च and, अभ्यधिकः excessive, राजन् O King, जनस्य of the people, पुरवासिनः of the city dwellers.
explanation: Women give birth without illness, humans are healthy, and O King, the joy of the city dwellers is exceedingly great.

shloka_text: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः पातयन्नमृतं पयः । वाताश्चापि प्रवान्त्येते स्पर्शयुक्ताः सुखाः शिवाः ।। 7.41.20 ।।
transliteration: kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ pātayannamṛtaṃ payaḥ | vātāścāpi pravāntyete sparśayuktāḥ sukhāḥ śivāḥ || 7.41.20 ||
translation: काले at the proper time, वर्षति rains, पर्जन्यः the cloud, पातयन् causing to fall, अमृतं nectar-like, पयः water, वाताः winds, च and, अपि also, प्रवान्ति blow, एते these, स्पर्शयुक्ताः endowed with pleasant touch, सुखाः pleasant, शिवाः auspicious.
explanation: The clouds rain nectar-like water at the proper time, and these winds blow, pleasant to the touch, agreeable, and auspicious.

shloka_text: ईदृशो ऽनश्वरो राजा भवेदिति नरेश्वरः । कथयन्ति पुरे राजन्पौरजानपदास्तथा ।। 7.41.21 ।।
transliteration: īdṛśo 'naśvaro rājā bhavediti nareśvaraḥ | kathayanti pure rājanpaurajānapadāstathā || 7.41.21 ||
translation: ईदृशः such, अनश्वरः immortal, राजा king, भवेत् may be, इति thus, नरेश्वरः O King, कथयन्ति say, पुरे in the city, राजन् O King, पौरजानपदाः city and country dwellers, तथा also.
explanation: O King, the city and country dwellers say in the city, "May such a king be immortal!"

shloka_text: एता वाचः सुमधुरा भरतेन समीरिताः । श्रुत्वा रामो मुदा युक्तो बभूव नृपसत्तमः ।। 7.41.22 ।।
transliteration: etā vācaḥ sumadhurā bharatena samīritāḥ | śrutvā rāmo mudā yukto babhūva nṛpasattamaḥ || 7.41.22 ||
translation: एता these, वाचः words, सुमधुरा very sweet, भरतेन by Bharata, समीरिताः spoken, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामः Rama, मुदा with joy, युक्तः filled, बभूव became, नृपसत्तमः the best of kings.
explanation: Having heard these very sweet words spoken by Bharata, Rama, the best of kings, became filled with joy. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 41 ।। Thus ends the forty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स विसृज्य ततो रामः पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम् । प्रविवेश महाबाहुरशोकवनिकां तदा ।। 7.42.1 ।।
transliteration: sa visṛjya tato rāmaḥ puṣpakaṃ hemabhūṣitam | praviveśa mahābāhuraśokavanikāṃ tadā || 7.42.1 ||
translation: सः He, विसृज्य having dismissed, ततः then, रामः Rama, पुष्पकम् the Pushpaka (chariot), हेमभूषितम् adorned with gold, प्रविवेश entered, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed one, अशोकवनिकाम् the Ashoka grove, तदा at that time.
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Rama, having dismissed the gold-adorned Pushpaka chariot, entered the Ashoka grove.
comments: Rama disports with Sita in the beautiful Ashoka grove, attended by song, dance and wine, and the winter passes happily -- learning that Sita is now with child, Rama asks her wish, and she longs to visit the hermitages of the ascetics on the bank of the Ganga -- Rama promises she shall go on the morrow.

shloka_text: चन्दनागुरुचूतैश्च तुङ्गकालेयकैरपि । देवदारुवनैश्चापि समन्तादुपशोभिताम् ।। 7.42.2 ।।
transliteration: candanāgurucūtaiśca tuṅgakāleyakairapi | devadāruvanaiścāpi samantādupaśobhitām || 7.42.2 ||
translation: चन्दन sandalwood trees, अगरु aloe wood trees, चूतैः mango trees, च and, तुङ्गकालेयकैः tall Kāleyaka trees, अपि also, देवदारुवनैः forests of Deodar trees, च and, अपि also, समन्तात् all around, उपशोभिताम् adorned.
explanation: The grove was beautified all around by sandalwood, aloe wood, and mango trees, as well as tall Kāleyaka trees and forests of Deodar.

shloka_text: चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागमधूकपनसासनैः । शोभितां पारिजातैश्च विधूमज्वलनप्रभैः ।। 7.42.3 ।।
transliteration: campakāśokapunnāgamadhūkapanasāsanaiḥ | śobhitāṃ pārijātaiśca vidhūmajvalanaprabhaiḥ || 7.42.3 ||
translation: चम्पक Champaka trees, अशोक Ashoka trees, पुन्नाग Punnaga trees, मधूक Madhuka trees, पनस Jackfruit trees, आसनैः Asana trees, शोभिताम् adorned, पारिजातैः by Parijata trees, च and, विधूमज्वलनप्रभैः shining like smokeless fire.
explanation: It was adorned with Champaka, Ashoka, Punnaga, Madhuka, Jackfruit, and Asana trees, and by Parijata trees that shone like smokeless flames.

shloka_text: लोध्रनीपार्जुनैर्नागैः सप्तपर्णातिमुक्तकैः । मन्दारकदलीगुल्मलताजालसमावृताम् ।। 7.42.4 ।।
transliteration: lodhranīpārjunairnāgaiḥ saptaparṇātimuktakaiḥ | mandārakadalīgulmalatājālasamāvṛtām || 7.42.4 ||
translation: लोध्र Lodhra trees, नीप Nipa trees, अर्जुनैः Arjuna trees, नागैः Naga trees, सप्तपर्ण Saptaparna trees, अतिमुक्तकैः Atimuktaka creepers, मन्दार Mandara trees, कदली banana plants, गुल्म bushes, लताजाल networks of creepers, समावृताम् covered.
explanation: The grove was covered with Lodhra, Nipa, Arjuna, Naga, and Saptaparna trees, Atimuktaka creepers, Mandara trees, banana plants, and dense networks of bushes and vines.

shloka_text: प्रियङ्गुभिः कदम्बैश्च तथा च वकुलैरपि । जम्बूभिर्दाडिमैश्चैव कोविदारैश्च शोभिताम् ।। 7.42.5 ।।
transliteration: priyaṅgubhiḥ kadambaiśca tathā ca vakulairapi | jambūbhirdāḍimaiścaiva kovidāraiśca śobhitām || 7.42.5 ||
translation: प्रियङ्गुभिः by Priyangu trees, कदम्बैः by Kadamba trees, च and, तथा similarly, च and, वकुलैः by Bakula trees, अपि also, जम्बूभिः by Jambu trees, दाडिमैः by Pomegranate trees, च and, एव indeed, कोविदारैः by Kovidara trees, च and, शोभिताम् adorned.
explanation: It was further adorned by Priyangu, Kadamba, Bakula, Jambu, Pomegranate, and Kovidara trees.

shloka_text: सर्वदा कुसुमै रम्यैः फलवद्भिर्मनोरमैः । दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतैस्तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवैः ।। 7.42.6 ।।
transliteration: sarvadā kusumai ramyaiḥ phalavadbhirmanoramaiḥ | divyagandharasopetaistaruṇāṅkurapallavaiḥ || 7.42.6 ||
translation: सर्वदा always, कुसुमैः with flowers, रम्यैः beautiful, फलवद्भिः bearing fruit, मनोरमैः charming, दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतैः endowed with divine fragrance and taste, तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवैः with young sprouts and tender leaves
explanation: The description refers to trees that are always adorned with beautiful flowers, charming fruit, and young sprouts and tender leaves, all possessing divine fragrance and taste.

shloka_text: तथैव तरुभिर्दिव्यैः शिल्पिभिः परिकल्पितैः । चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यैर्मत्तभ्रमरसङ्कुलैः ।। 7.42.7 ।।
transliteration: tathaiva tarubhirdivyaiḥ śilpibhiḥ parikalpitaiḥ | cārupallavapuṣpāḍhyairmattabhramarasaṅkulaiḥ || 7.42.7 ||
translation: तथैव similarly, तरुभिः by trees, दिव्यैः divine, शिल्पिभिः by artisans, परिकल्पितैः arranged, चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यैः rich with beautiful sprouts and flowers, मत्तभ्रमरसङ्कुलैः crowded with intoxicated bees
explanation: The trees, appearing as if divinely crafted by artisans, were similarly splendid, abundant with beautiful sprouts and flowers, and teeming with intoxicated bees.

shloka_text: कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च नानावर्णैश्च पक्षिभिः । शोभितां शतशश्चित्रां चूतवृक्षावतंसकैः ।। 7.42.8 ।।
transliteration: kokilairbhṛṅgarājaiśca nānāvarṇaiśca pakṣibhiḥ | śobhitāṃ śataśaścitrāṃ cūtavṛkṣāvataṃsakaiḥ || 7.42.8 ||
translation: कोकिलैः by cuckoos, भृङ्गराजैः by king-bees, च and, नानावर्णैः of various colors, च and, पक्षिभिः by birds, शोभिताम् adorned, शतशः by hundreds, चित्राम् variegated, चूतवृक्षावतंसकैः with mango trees as prominent features
explanation: The place was adorned and made variegated by hundreds of cuckoos, king-bees, and birds of various colors, with mango trees serving as its prominent features.

shloka_text: शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः । नीलाञ्जननिभाश्चान्ये भान्ति तत्रत्यपादपाः ।। 7.42.9 ।।
transliteration: śātakumbhanibhāḥ kecitkecidagniśikhopamāḥ | nīlāñjananibhāścānye bhānti tatratyapādapāḥ || 7.42.9 ||
translation: शातकुम्भनिभाः resembling refined gold, केचित् some, केचित् some, अग्निशिखोपमाः resembling flames of fire, नीलाञ्जननिभाः resembling blue collyrium, च and, अन्ये others, भान्ति shine, तत्रत्यपादपाः the trees there
explanation: The trees in that place shone with various hues, some resembling refined gold, others like flames of fire, and still others like blue collyrium.

shloka_text: सुरभीणि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि विविधानि च । दीर्घिका विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा ।। 7.42.10 ।।
transliteration: surabhīṇi ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni vividhāni ca | dīrghikā vividhākārāḥ pūrṇāḥ paramavāriṇā || 7.42.10 ||
translation: सुरभीणि fragrant, च and, पुष्पाणि flowers, माल्यानि garlands, विविधानि various, च and, दीर्घिकाः long ponds, विविधाकाराः of various shapes, पूर्णाः full, परमवारिणा with excellent water
explanation: There were fragrant flowers and various garlands, along with long ponds of diverse shapes filled with excellent water.

shloka_text: माणिक्यकृतसोपानाः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः । फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः ।। 7.42.11 ।।
transliteration: māṇikyakṛtasopānāḥ sphāṭikāntarakuṭṭimāḥ | phullapadmotpalavanāścakravākopaśobhitāḥ || 7.42.11 ||
translation: माणिक्यकृतसोपानाः with steps made of rubies, स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः with inner floors paved with crystal, फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाः with groves of blooming lotuses and water lilies, चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः adorned by chakravaka birds.
explanation: The place featured steps crafted from rubies, inner floors paved with crystal, abundant groves of blooming lotuses and water lilies, and was graced by the presence of chakravaka birds.

shloka_text: दात्यूहशुकसङ्घुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः । तरुभिः पुष्पवद्भिश्च तीरजैरुपशोभिताः ।। 7.42.12 ।।
transliteration: dātyūhaśukasaṅghuṣṭā haṃsasārasanāditāḥ | tarubhiḥ puṣpavadbhiśca tīrajairupaśobhitāḥ || 7.42.12 ||
translation: दात्यूहशुकसङ्घुष्टा resonant with the calls of gallinules and parrots, हंससारसनादिताः made to resound by swans and cranes, तरुभिः by trees, पुष्पवद्भिश्च and full of flowers, तीरजैः growing on the banks, उपशोभिताः adorned.
explanation: It was filled with the sounds of gallinules, parrots, swans, and cranes, and beautifully adorned by flowering trees growing along its banks.

shloka_text: प्राकारैर्विविधाकारैः शोभिताश्च शिलातलैः । तत्रैव च वनोद्देशे वैडूर्यमणिसन्निभैः ।। 7.42.13 ।।
transliteration: prākārairvividhākāraiḥ śobhitāśca śilātalaiḥ | tatraiva ca vanoddeśe vaiḍūryamaṇisannibhaiḥ || 7.42.13 ||
translation: प्राकारैः by enclosures, विविधाकारैः of various forms, शोभिताश्च and adorned, शिलातलैः by rock surfaces, तत्रैव there indeed, च and, वनोद्देशे in that part of the forest, वैडूर्यमणिसन्निभैः resembling lapis lazuli gems.
explanation: The area was embellished with diverse enclosures and rock surfaces, and within that forest region, there were spots that shimmered like lapis lazuli gems.

shloka_text: शाद्वलैः परमोपेतां पुष्पितद्रुमकाननाम् । तत्र सङ्घर्षजातानां वृक्षाणां पुष्पशालिनाम् ।। 7.42.14 ।।
transliteration: śādvalaiḥ paramopetāṃ puṣpitadrumakānanām | tatra saṅgharṣajātānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpaśālinām || 7.42.14 ||
translation: शाद्वलैः by green meadows, परमोपेतां supremely endowed, पुष्पितद्रुमकाननाम् with groves of flowering trees, तत्र there, सङ्घर्षजातानां grown from close proximity, वृक्षाणां of trees, पुष्पशालिनाम् adorned with flowers.
explanation: It was supremely rich with green meadows and flowering tree groves, where trees growing in close proximity were resplendent with blossoms.

shloka_text: प्रस्तराः पुष्पशबला नभस्तारागणैरिव । नन्दनं हि यथेन्द्रस्य ब्राह्मं चैत्ररथं यथा ।। 7.42.15 ।।
transliteration: prastarāḥ puṣpaśabalā nabhastārāgaṇairiva | nandanaṃ hi yathendrasya brāhmaṃ caitrarathaṃ yathā | tathābhūtaṃ hi rāmasya kānanaṃ sanniveśanam || 7.42.15 ||
translation: प्रस्तराः the rock surfaces, पुष्पशबला variegated with flowers, नभः the sky, तारागणैः by clusters of stars, इव as if, नन्दनं Nandana, हि indeed, यथा just as, इन्द्रस्य of Indra, ब्राह्मं of Brahma, चैत्ररथं Chaitraratha, यथा just as, तथाभूतं such, हि indeed, रामस्य of Rama, काननं the garden, सन्निवेशनाम् the dwelling/setting.
explanation: The rock surfaces were variegated with flowers, resembling the sky adorned with clusters of stars, and indeed, Rama's garden and dwelling were as magnificent as Indra's Nandana or Kubera's Chaitraratha.

shloka_text: तथाभूतं हि रामस्य काननं सन्निवेशनम् । बह्वासनगृहोपेतां लतागृहसमावृताम् ।। 7.42.16 ।।
transliteration: bahvāsanagṛhopetāṃ latāgṛhasamāvṛtām | aśokavanikāṃ sphītāṃ praviśya raghunandanaḥ || 7.42.16 ||
translation: तथाभूतं such, हि indeed, रामस्य of Rama, काननं garden, सन्निवेशनम् dwelling, बह्वासनगृहोपेतां endowed with many seats and houses, लतागृहसमावृताम् surrounded by creeper-houses.
explanation: Indeed, such was Rama's dwelling garden, adorned with numerous seats and pavilions, and enveloped by charming creeper-houses.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिकां स्फीतां प्रविश्य रघुनन्दनः । आसने च शुभाकारे पुष्पप्रकरभूषिते ।। 7.42.17 ।।
transliteration: āsane ca śubhākāre puṣpaprakarabhūṣite | kuśāstaraṇasaṃstīrṇe rāmaḥ sanniṣasāda ha || 7.42.17 ||
translation: अशोकवनिकां into the Ashoka grove, स्फीतां extensive, प्रविश्य having entered, रघुनन्दनः Rama, the delight of the Raghus, आसने on a seat, च and, शुभाकारे of beautiful form, पुष्पप्रकरभूषिते adorned with heaps of flowers.
explanation: Having entered the extensive Ashoka grove, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, found a beautifully shaped seat adorned with heaps of flowers.

shloka_text: कुशास्तरणसंस्तीर्णे रामः सन्निषसाद ह । सीतामादायं हस्तेन मधुमैरेयकं शुचि ।। 7.42.18 ।।
transliteration: sītāmādāyaṃ hastena madhumaireyakaṃ śuci | pāyayāmāsa kākutsthaḥ śacīmiva purandaraḥ || 7.42.18 ||
translation: कुशास्तरणसंस्तीर्णे spread with a mat of Kusa grass, रामः Rama, सन्निषसाद sat down, ह indeed, सीतामादायं taking Sita, हस्तेन by the hand, मधुमैरेयकं the wine called Madhu-Maireyaka, शुचि pure.
explanation: Rama indeed sat down on the seat, which was spread with a mat of Kusa grass, and with Sita by his hand, he had the pure Madhu-Maireyaka wine ready.

shloka_text: पाययामास काकुत्स्थः शचीमिव पुरन्दरः । मांसानि च समृष्टानि फलानि विविधानि च ।। 7.42.19 ।।
transliteration: māṃsāni ca samṛṣṭāni phalāni vividhāni ca | rāmasyābhyavahārārthaṃ kiṅkarāstūrṇamāharan || 7.42.19 ||
translation: पाययामास made to drink, काकुत्स्थः Rama, शचीमिव like Shachi, पुरन्दरः Indra, मांसानि meats, च and, समृष्टानि well-prepared, फलानि fruits, विविधानि various, च and.
explanation: Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, made her drink, just as Indra makes Shachi drink, and there were well-prepared meats and various fruits.

shloka_text: रामस्याभ्यवहारार्थं किङ्करास्तूर्णमाहरन्उ । उपानृत्यंश्च राजानं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः ।। 7.42.20 ।।
transliteration: upānṛtyaṃśca rājānaṃ nṛtyagītaviśāradāḥ | bālāśca rūpavatyaśca striyaḥ pānavaśānugāḥ || 7.42.20 ||
translation: रामस्याभ्यवहारार्थं for Rama's meal, किङ्कराः servants, तूर्णम् quickly, आहरन् brought, उपानृत्यंश्च and danced before, राजानं the king, नृत्यगीतविशारदाः skilled in dance and song.
explanation: Servants quickly brought food for Rama's meal, and those skilled in dance and song performed before the king.

shloka_text: बालाश्च रूपवत्यश्च स्त्रियः पानवशानुगाः । मनोभिरामा रामास्ता रामो रमयतां वरः ।। 7.42.21 ।।
transliteration: manobhirāmā rāmāstā rāmo ramayatāṃ varaḥ | ramayāmāsa dharmātmā nityaṃ paramabhūṣitaḥ || 7.42.21 ||
translation: बालाः young, च and, रूपवत्यः beautiful, च and, स्त्रियः women, पानवशानुगाः subservient to drink, मनोभिरामाः charming, रामाः women, ताः those, रामः Rama, रमयतां among those who delight, वरः the best.
explanation: Rama, the best among those who delight, was in the company of young, beautiful, and charming women who were under the influence of drink.

shloka_text: उपानृत्यन्त काकुत्स्थं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः । मनोभिरामा रामास्ता रामो रमयतां वरः ।। 7.42.22 ।।
transliteration: sa tayā sītayā sārdhamāsīno virarāja ha | arundhatyā sahāsīno vasiṣṭha iva tejasā || 7.42.22 ||
translation: उपानृत्यन्त danced before, काकुत्स्थम् Kakutstha (Rama), नृत्यगीतविशारदाः skilled in dance and song, मनोभिरामाः charming, रामाः women, ताः those, रामः Rama, रमयतां among those who delight, वरः the best.
explanation: Skilled in dance and song, charming women danced before Rama, the best among those who delight.

shloka_text: रमयामास धर्मात्मा नित्यं परमभूषितः । स तया सीतया सार्धमासीनो विरराज ह ।। 7.42.23 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ rāmo mudā yuktaḥ sītāṃ surasutopamām | ramayāmāsa vaidehīmahanyahani devavat || 7.42.23 ||
translation: रमयामास he delighted, धर्मात्मा the righteous soul (Rama), नित्यम् always, परमभूषितः highly adorned, सः he, तया with her, सीतया Sita, सार्धम् together with, आसीनः seated, विरराज shone, ह indeed.
explanation: The righteous Rama, always highly adorned, delighted (them), and he shone splendidly while seated with Sita.

shloka_text: अरुन्धत्या सहासीनो वसिष्ठ इव तेजसा । एवं रामो मुदा युक्तः सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम् ।। 7.42.24 ।।
transliteration: tathā tayorviharatoḥ sītārāghavayościram | atyakrāmacchubhaḥ kālaḥ śaiśiro bhogadaḥ sadā || 7.42.24 ||
translation: अरुन्धत्या with Arundhati, सह with, आसीनः seated, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, इव like, तेजसा with splendor, एवम् thus, रामः Rama, मुदा with joy, युक्तः endowed, सीताम् Sita, सुरसुतोपमाम् resembling a celestial nymph.
explanation: Rama, filled with joy, thus shone with splendor like Vasishtha seated with Arundhati, with Sita resembling a celestial nymph.

shloka_text: रमयामास वैदेहीमहन्यहनि देववत्त । था तयोर्विहरतोः सीताराघवयोश्चिरम् ।। 7.42.25 ।।
transliteration: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi gatāni sumahātmanoḥ | prāptayorvividhānbhogānatītaḥ śiśirāgamaḥ || 7.42.25 ||
translation: रमयामास he delighted, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi (Sita), अहन्यहनि day after day, देववत् like a god, तथा thus, तयोः of those two, विहरतोः while sporting, सीताराघवयोः of Sita and Raghava, चिरम् for a long time.
explanation: Rama, like a god, delighted Sita day after day, and thus Sita and Raghava sported together for a long time.

shloka_text: अत्यक्रामच्छुभः कालः शैशिरो भोगदः सदा । प्राप्तयोर्विविधान्भोगानतीतः शिशिरागमः ।। 7.42.26 ।।
transliteration: pūrvāhṇe dharmakāryāṇi kṛtvā dharmeṇa dharmavit | śeṣaṃ divasabhāgārdhamantaḥpuragato 'bhavat || 7.42.26 ||
translation: अत्यक्रामत् passed away, शुभः auspicious, कालः time, शैशिरः winter, भोगदः giving enjoyment, सदा always, प्राप्तयोः for the two who had obtained, विविधान् various, भोगान् enjoyments, अतीतः passed, शिशिरागमः winter season.
explanation: The auspicious and always pleasure-giving winter season, during which Rama and Sita had enjoyed various pleasures, passed away.

shloka_text: पूर्वाह्णे धर्मकार्याणि कृत्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित् । शेषं दिवसभागार्धमन्तःपुरगतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.42.27 ।।
transliteration: sītāpi devakāryāṇi kṛtvā paurvāhṇikāni vai | śvaśrūṇāmakarotpūjāṃ sarvāsāmaviśeṣataḥ || 7.42.27 ||
translation: पूर्वाह्णे in the forenoon, धर्मकार्याणि religious duties, कृत्वा having done, धर्मेण righteously, धर्मवित् the knower of dharma, शेषं the remaining, दिवसभागार्धम् half of the day's portion, अन्तःपुरगतः gone to the inner apartments, अभवत् became.
explanation: Having performed his religious duties righteously in the forenoon, the knower of dharma, Rama, spent the remaining half of the day in his inner apartments.

shloka_text: सीतापि देवकार्याणि कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकानि वै । श्वश्रूणामकरोत्पूजां सर्वासामविशेषतः ।। 7.42.28 ।।
transliteration: abhyagacchattato rāmaṃ vicitrābharaṇāmbarā | triviṣṭape sahasrākṣamupaviṣṭaṃ yathā śacī || 7.42.28 ||
translation: सीतापि Sita also, देवकार्याणि divine duties, कृत्वा having done, पौर्वाह्णिकानि morning, वै indeed, श्वश्रूणाम् of the mothers-in-law, अकरोत् performed, पूजां reverence, सर्वासाम् of all, अविशेषतः without distinction.
explanation: Sita also, having performed her morning divine duties, reverently honored all her mothers-in-law without any distinction.

shloka_text: अभ्यगच्छत्ततो रामं विचित्राभरणाम्बरा । त्रिविष्टपे सहस्राक्षमुपविष्टं यथा शची ।। 7.42.29 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ patnīṃ kalyāṇena samanvitām | praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt || 7.42.29 ||
translation: अभ्यगच्छत् approached, ततः then, रामं Rama, विचित्राभरणाम्बरा adorned with various ornaments and garments, त्रिविष्टपे in heaven, सहस्राक्षम् the thousand-eyed one, उपविष्टं seated, यथा just as, शची Shachi.
explanation: Then, adorned with various ornaments and garments, Sita approached Rama, just as Shachi approaches the thousand-eyed Indra seated in heaven.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः पत्नीं कल्याणेन समन्विताम् । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.42.30 ।।
transliteration: abravīcca varārohāṃ sītāṃ surasutopamām | apatyalābho vaidehi tvayi me samupasthitaḥ || 7.42.30 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, तु indeed, राघवः Rama, पत्नीं wife, कल्याणेन with auspiciousness, समन्विताम् endowed, प्रहर्षम् great joy, अतुलं incomparable, लेभे obtained, साधु excellent, साधु excellent, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Having seen his wife, Sita, endowed with auspiciousness, Rama felt incomparable joy and exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent!"

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम् । अपत्यलाभो वैदेहि त्वयि मे समुपस्थितः ।। 7.42.31 ।।
transliteration: kimicchasi varārohe kāmaḥ kiṃ kriyatāṃ tava || 7.42.31 ||
translation: अब्रवीत् said, च and, वरारोहां to the one with beautiful thighs, सीतां Sita, सुरसुतोपमाम् who was like a daughter of a god, अपत्यलाभः the gain of offspring, वैदेहि O Vaidehi, त्वयि in you, मे to me, समुपस्थितः has come.
explanation: Rama said to Sita, who had beautiful thighs and resembled a divine daughter, "O Vaidehi, the blessing of progeny has come to me through you."

shloka_text: किमिच्छसि वरारोहे कामः किं क्रियतां तव । स्मितं कृत्वा तु वैदेही रामं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.42.32 ।।
transliteration: smitaṃ kṛtvā tu vaidehī rāmaṃ vākyamathābravīt | tapovanāni puṇyāni draṣṭumicchāmi rāghava || 7.42.32 ||
translation: किम् what, इच्छसि do you desire, वरारोहे O one with beautiful thighs, कामः desire, किम् what, क्रियताम् may be done, तव for you, स्मितं smile, कृत्वा having made, तु indeed, वैदेही Vaidehi, रामं to Rama, वाक्यम् words, अथ then, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Rama asked Sita, "O one with beautiful thighs, what do you desire? What wish of yours may I fulfill?" Then, smiling, Vaidehi spoke these words to Rama.

shloka_text: तपोवनानि पुण्यानि द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघव । गङ्गातीरोपविष्टानामृषीणामुग्रतेजसाम् ।। 7.42.33 ।।
transliteration: gaṅgātīropaviṣṭānāmṛṣīṇāmugratejasām | phalamūlāśināṃ deva pādamūleṣu vartitum || 7.42.33 ||
translation: तपोवनानि hermitages, पुण्यानि sacred, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छामि I desire, राघव O Raghava, गङ्गातीरोपविष्टानाम् of those seated on the banks of the Ganga, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, उग्रतेजसाम् of fierce ascetic power.
explanation: Sita said, "O Raghava, I desire to see the sacred hermitages and the sages of fierce ascetic power seated on the banks of the Ganga."

shloka_text: फलमूलाशिनां देव पादमूलेषु वर्तितुम् । एष मे परमः कामो यन्मूलफलभोजिनाम् ।। 7.42.34 ।।
transliteration: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yanmūlaphalabhojinām | apyekarātraṃ kākutstha nivaseyaṃ tapovane || 7.42.34 ||
translation: फलमूलाशिनाम् of those who subsist on fruits and roots, देव O Lord, पादमूलेषु at the feet, वर्तितुम् to dwell, एषः this, मे my, परमः greatest, कामः desire, यत् that, मूलफलभोजिनाम् of those who subsist on roots and fruits.
explanation: Sita continued, "O Lord, to dwell at the feet of those who subsist on fruits and roots—this is my greatest desire, that I may be among those who eat roots and fruits."

shloka_text: अप्येकरात्रं काकुत्स्थ निवसेयं तपोवने । तथेति च प्रतिज्ञातं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । विस्रब्धा भव वैदेहि श्वो गमिष्यस्यसंशयम् ।। 7.42.35 ।।
transliteration: tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā | visrabdhā bhava vaidehi śvo gamiṣyasyasaṃśayam || 7.42.35 ||
translation: अपि even, एकरात्रम् for one night, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, निवसेयम् I may dwell, तपोवने in a hermitage, तथा so be it, इति thus, च and, प्रतिज्ञातम् was promised, रामेण by Rama, अक्लिष्टकर्मणा whose deeds are unwearied, विस्रब्धा confident, भव be, वैदेहि O Vaidehi, श्वः tomorrow, गमिष्यसि you will go, असंशयम् without doubt.
explanation: Sita expressed her desire to dwell in a hermitage for even one night, to which Rama, whose deeds were effortless, promised, "So be it, O Vaidehi, be confident, you will undoubtedly go tomorrow."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम् । मध्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम सुहृद्वृतः ।। 7.42.36 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu kākutstho maithilīṃ janakātmajām | madhyakakṣāntaraṃ rāmo nirjagāma suhṛdvṛtaḥ || 7.42.36 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तु indeed, काकुत्स्थः Rama, मैथिलीम् to Maithili, जनकात्मजाम् Janaka's daughter, मध्यकक्षान्तरम् to the middle apartment, रामः Rama, निर्जगाम went out, सुहृद्वृतः surrounded by friends.
explanation: After speaking thus to Sita, Janaka's daughter, Rama, surrounded by his friends, went out to the middle apartment. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 42 ।। Thus ends the forty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तत्रोपविष्टं राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः । कथानां बहुरूपाणां हास्यकाराः समन्ततः ।। 7.43.1 ।।
transliteration: tatropaviṣṭaṃ rājānamupāsante vicakṣaṇāḥ | kathānāṃ bahurūpāṇāṃ hāsyakārāḥ samantataḥ || 7.43.1 ||
translation: तत्र there, उपविष्टम् seated, राजानम् the king, उपासन्ते attend upon, विचक्षणाः wise men, कथानाम् of stories, बहुरूपाणाम् of many kinds, हास्यकाराः jesters, समन्ततः all around.
explanation: There, wise men, jesters, and storytellers of various kinds surrounded and attended upon the seated king.
comments: Rama asks his companions, led by Bhadra, what the people say of him -- pressed to speak frankly, Bhadra reports the citizens' scandal: they fault Rama for taking back Sita, who had dwelt in Ravana's Lanka, and fear they must now tolerate the like in their own wives -- stricken, Rama confirms the report and dismisses his friends.

shloka_text: विजयो मधुमत्तश्च काश्यपो मङ्गलः कुटः । सुराजः कालियो भद्रो दन्तवक्रः सुमागधः ।। 7.43.2 ।।
transliteration: vijayo madhumattaśca kāśyapo maṅgalaḥ kuṭaḥ | surājaḥ kāliyo bhadro dantavakraḥ sumāgadhaḥ || 7.43.2 ||
translation: विजयः Vijaya, मधुमत्तः Madhumatta, च and, काश्यपः Kashyapa, मङ्गलः Mangala, कुटः Kuta, सुराजः Suraja, कालियः Kaliya, भद्रः Bhadra, दन्तवक्रः Dantavakra, सुमागधः Sumagadha.
explanation: These were the names of some of the attendees: Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kashyapa, Mangala, Kuta, Suraja, Kaliya, Bhadra, Dantavakra, and Sumagadha.

shloka_text: एते कथा बहुविधाः परिहाससमन्विताः । कथयन्ति स्म संहृष्टा राघवस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.43.3 ।।
transliteration: ete kathā bahuvidhāḥ parihāsasamanvitāḥ | kathayanti sma saṃhṛṣṭā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.43.3 ||
translation: एते these, कथाः stories, बहुविधाः of many kinds, परिहाससमन्विताः full of jokes, कथयन्ति tell, स्म (past tense indicator), संहृष्टाः delighted, राघवस्य of Rama, महात्मनः the great-souled.
explanation: These delighted individuals used to tell the great-souled Rama many kinds of stories filled with humor.

shloka_text: ततः कथायां कस्याञ्चिद्राघवः समभाषत । काः कथा नगरे भद्र वर्तन्ते विषयेषु च ।। 7.43.4 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kathāyāṃ kasyāñcidrāghavaḥ samabhāṣata | kāḥ kathā nagare bhadra vartante viṣayeṣu ca || 7.43.4 ||
translation: ततः then, कथायाम् in a story, कस्याञ्चित् in a certain, राघवः Rama, समभाषत spoke, काः what, कथाः stories, नगरे in the city, भद्र O good one, वर्तन्ते are current, विषयेषु in the provinces, च and.
explanation: Then, during a certain conversation, Rama spoke, asking, "O good one, what stories are current in the city and in the provinces?"

shloka_text: मामाश्रितानि कान्याहुः पौरजानपदा जनाः । किं च सीतां समाश्रित्य भरतं किं च लक्ष्मणम् ।। 7.43.5 ।।
transliteration: māmāśritāni kānyāhuḥ paurajānapadā janāḥ | kiṃ ca sītāṃ samāśritya bharataṃ kiṃ ca lakṣmaṇam || 7.43.5 ||
translation: माम् me, आश्रितानि concerning, कानि what, आहुः say, पौरजानपदाः citizens and country people, जनाः people, किं च and what, सीताम् Sita, समाश्रित्य concerning, भरतम् Bharata, किं च and what, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana
explanation: What do the city dwellers and country folk say about me, and what do they say about Sita, Bharata, and Lakshmana?

shloka_text: किं नु शत्रुघ्नमुद्दिश्य कैकयीं किं नु मातरम् । वक्तव्यतां च राजानो वरे राज्ये व्रजन्ति च ।। 7.43.6 ।।
transliteration: kiṃ nu śatrughnamuddiśya kaikayīṃ kiṃ nu mātaram | vaktavyatāṃ ca rājāno vare rājye vrajanti ca || 7.43.6 ||
translation: किं नु and what, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, उद्दिश्य concerning, कैकयीम् Kaikeyi, किं नु and what, मातरम् mother, वक्तव्यताम् subject of criticism, च and, राजानः kings, वरे in the excellent, राज्ये kingdom, व्रजन्ति become, च and
explanation: What do they say about Shatrughna, and what about mother Kaikeyi, and what kind of criticism do kings face in an excellent kingdom?

shloka_text: एवमुक्ते तु रामेण भद्रः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् । स्थिताः कथा शुभाः राजन्वर्तन्ते पुरवासिनाम् ।। 7.43.7 ।।
transliteration: evamukte tu rāmeṇa bhadraḥ prāñjalirabravīt | sthitāḥ kathā śubhāḥ rājanvartante puravāsinām || 7.43.7 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ते having been spoken, तु indeed, रामेण by Rama, भद्रः Bhadra, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, अब्रवीत् said, स्थिताः existing, कथाः stories, शुभाः auspicious, राजन् O King, वर्तन्ते are current, पुरवासिनाम् among the city dwellers
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Bhadra, with folded hands, replied, "O King, auspicious talks are indeed current among the city dwellers."

shloka_text: अमुं तु विजयं सौम्य दशग्रीववधार्जितम् । भूयिष्ठं स्वपुरे पौरैः कथ्यन्ते पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.43.8 ।।
transliteration: amuṃ tu vijayaṃ saumya daśagrīvavadhārjitam | bhūyiṣṭhaṃ svapure pauraiḥ kathyante puruṣarṣabha || 7.43.8 ||
translation: अमुम् this, तु indeed, विजयम् victory, सौम्य O gentle one, दशग्रीववधार्जितम् obtained by the slaying of Dashagriva, भूयिष्ठम् mostly, स्वपुरे in your city, पौरैः by the citizens, कथ्यन्ते are narrated, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men
explanation: O gentle one, O best among men, this victory, indeed, obtained by the slaying of Dashagriva, is mostly narrated by the citizens in your city.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु भद्रेण राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । कथयस्व यथातत्त्वं सर्वं निरवशेषतः ।। 7.43.9 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu bhadreṇa rāghavo vākyamabravīt | kathayasva yathātattvaṃ sarvaṃ niravaśeṣataḥ || 7.43.9 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः having been spoken to, तु indeed, भद्रेण by Bhadra, राघवः Rama, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, कथयस्व tell, यथातत्त्वम् truthfully, सर्वम् all, निरवशेषतः completely
explanation: When Bhadra had thus spoken, Rama indeed replied, "Tell everything truthfully and completely, without omitting anything."

shloka_text: शुभाशुभानि वाक्यानि यान्याहुः पुरवासिनः । श्रुत्वेदानीं शुभं कुर्यां नकुर्यामशुभानि च ।। 7.43.10 ।।
transliteration: śubhāśubhāni vākyāni yānyāhuḥ puravāsinaḥ | śrutvedānīṃ śubhaṃ kuryāṃ nakuryāmaśubhāni ca || 7.43.10 ||
translation: शुभाशुभानि good and bad, वाक्यानि words, यानि which, आहुः say, पुरवासिनः city dwellers, श्रुत्वा having heard, इदानीं now, शुभं good, कुर्यां I should do, न not, कुर्याम् I should do, अशुभानि bad, च and
explanation: Having heard the good and bad words spoken by the city dwellers, I should now do what is good and avoid what is bad.

shloka_text: कथयस्व च विस्रब्धो निर्भयं विगतज्वरः । कथयन्ति यथा पौराः पापा जनपदेषु च ।। 7.43.11 ।।
transliteration: kathayasva ca visrabdho nirbhayaṃ vigatajvaraḥ | kathayanti yathā paurāḥ pāpā janapadeṣu ca || 7.43.11 ||
translation: कथयस्व tell, च and, विस्रब्धः confidently, निर्भयं fearlessly, विगतज्वरः free from anxiety, कथयन्ति speak, यथा as, पौराः citizens, पापाः wicked things (or wicked people), जनपदेषु in the districts, च and
explanation: Speak confidently, fearlessly, and without anxiety, just as the citizens and people in the districts speak, even about wicked things.

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भद्रः सुरुचिरं वचः । प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुं प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः ।। 7.43.12 ।।
transliteration: rāghaveṇaivamuktastu bhadraḥ suruciraṃ vacaḥ | pratyuvāca mahābāhuṃ prāñjaliḥ susamāhitaḥ || 7.43.12 ||
translation: राघवेण by Rama, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, भद्रः Bhadra, सुरुचिरं very pleasing, वचः words, प्रत्युवाच replied, महाबाहुं to the mighty-armed (Rama), प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, सुसमाहितः very attentive
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Bhadra, with folded hands and great attention, replied with very pleasing words to the mighty-armed king.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्यथा पौराः कथयन्ति शुभाशुभम् । चत्वरापणरथ्यासु वनेषूपवनेषु च ।। 7.43.13 ।।
transliteration: śṛṇu rājanyathā paurāḥ kathayanti śubhāśubham | catvarāpaṇarathyāsu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca || 7.43.13 ||
translation: शृणु listen, राजन् O King, यथा as, पौराः citizens, कथयन्ति speak, शुभाशुभम् good and bad, चत्वर squares, आपण markets, रथ्यासु in the streets, वनेषु in the forests, उपवनेषु in the gardens, च and
explanation: O King, listen to how the citizens speak of good and bad things in the squares, markets, streets, forests, and gardens.

shloka_text: दुष्करं कृतवान्रामः समुद्रे सेतुबन्धनम् । अश्रुतं पूर्वकैः कैश्चिद्देवैरपि सदानवैः ।। 7.43.14 ।।
transliteration: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavānrāmaḥ samudre setubandhanam | aśrutaṃ pūrvakaiḥ kaiściddevairapi sadānavaiḥ || 7.43.14 ||
translation: दुष्करं difficult, कृतवान् has done, रामः Rama, समुद्रे in the ocean, सेतुबन्धनम् the building of a bridge, अश्रुतं unheard of, पूर्वकैः by ancestors, कैश्चित् by anyone, देवैः by gods, अपि even, सदानवैः along with Danavas
explanation: Rama has accomplished the impossible task of building a bridge in the ocean, a feat unheard of by any ancestors, gods, or even demons.

shloka_text: रावणश्च दुराधर्षो हतः सबलवाहनः । वानराश्च वशं नीता ऋक्षाश्च सह राक्षसैः ।। 7.43.15 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaśca durādharṣo hataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ | vānarāśca vaśaṃ nītā ṛkṣāśca saha rākṣasaiḥ || 7.43.15 ||
translation: रावणश्च Rāvaṇa and, दुराधर्षो formidable, हतः killed, सबलवाहनः with his army and vehicles, वानराश्च and monkeys, वशं under control, नीता brought, ऋक्षाश्च and bears, सह with, राक्षसैः the Rākṣasas.
explanation: The formidable Rāvaṇa was killed along with his army and vehicles, and the monkeys and bears were brought under control along with the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: हत्वा च रावणं सङ्ख्ये सीतामाहृत्य राघवः । अमर्षं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा स्ववेश्म पुनरानयत् ।। 7.43.16 ।।
transliteration: hatvā ca rāvaṇaṃ saṅkhye sītāmāhṛtya rāghavaḥ | amarṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā svaveśma punarānayat || 7.43.16 ||
translation: हत्वा having killed, च and, रावणं Rāvaṇa, सङ्ख्ये in battle, सीताम् Sītā, आहृत्य having brought back, राघवः Rāma, अमर्षं indignation, पृष्ठतः behind, कृत्वा having placed, स्ववेश्म to his own house, पुनः again, आनयत् brought.
explanation: Having killed Rāvaṇa in battle and brought Sītā back, Rāma set aside his indignation and brought her back to his own house.

shloka_text: कीदृशं हृदये तस्य सीतासम्भोगजं सुखम् । अङ्कमारोप्य तु पुरा रावणेन बलाद्धृताम् ।। 7.43.17 ।।
transliteration: kīdṛśaṃ hṛdaye tasya sītāsambhogajaṃ sukham | aṅkamāropya tu purā rāvaṇena balāddhṛtām || 7.43.17 ||
translation: कीदृशं of what kind, हृदये in the heart, तस्य his, सीतासम्भोगजं born from union with Sītā, सुखम् happiness, अङ्कम् on his lap, आरोप्य having placed, तु indeed, पुरा formerly, रावणेन by Rāvaṇa, बलात् by force, धृताम् seized.
explanation: What kind of happiness, born from union with Sītā, could be in his heart, when she was previously forcibly seized and placed on his lap by Rāvaṇa?

shloka_text: लङ्कामपि पुरा नीतामशोकवनिकां गताम् । रक्षसां वशमापन्नां कथं रामो न कुत्सते ।। 7.43.18 ।।
transliteration: laṅkāmapi purā nītāmaśokavanikāṃ gatām | rakṣasāṃ vaśamāpannāṃ kathaṃ rāmo na kutsate || 7.43.18 ||
translation: लङ्काम् to Laṅkā, अपि even, पुरा formerly, नीताम् taken, अशोकवनिकाम् to the Aśoka grove, गताम् gone, रक्षसां of Rākṣasas, वशम् under the control, आपन्नां having fallen, कथं how, रामः Rāma, न not, कुत्सते despises.
explanation: How can Rāma not despise her, who was formerly taken to Laṅkā, went to the Aśoka grove, and fell under the control of Rākṣasas?

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि दारेषु सहनीयं भविष्यति । यथा हि कुरुते राजा प्रजा तमनुवर्तते ।। 7.43.19 ।।
transliteration: asmākamapi dāreṣu sahanīyaṃ bhaviṣyati | yathā hi kurute rājā prajā tamanuvartate || 7.43.19 ||
translation: अस्माकम् of us, अपि even, दारेषु regarding wives, सहनीयं to be endured, भविष्यति it will be, यथा as, हि indeed, कुरुते does, राजा the king, प्रजा the subjects, तम् him, अनुवर्तते follow.
explanation: If the king acts this way, then even for us, regarding our wives, such things will become tolerable, because indeed, as the king acts, so do the subjects follow him.

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधा वाचो वदन्ति पुरवासिनः । नगरेषु च सर्वेषु राजञ्जनपदेषु च ।। 7.43.20 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bahuvidhā vāco vadanti puravāsinaḥ | nagareṣu ca sarveṣu rājañjanapadeṣu ca || 7.43.20 ||
translation: एवम् thus, बहुविधाः various kinds of, वाचः words, वदन्ति they speak, पुरवासिनः city dwellers, नगरेषु in cities, च and, सर्वेषु in all, राजन् O King, जनपदेषु in districts, च and.
explanation: O King, thus, the city dwellers speak various kinds of words in all cities and districts.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं भाषितं श्रुत्वा राघवः परमार्तवत् । उवाच सुहृदः सर्वान्कथमेतद्ब्रवीथ माम् ।। 7.43.21 ।।
transliteration: tasyaivaṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāghavaḥ paramārtavat | uvāca suhṛdaḥ sarvānkathametadbravītha mām || 7.43.21 ||
translation: तस्य his, एवम् thus, भाषितम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवः Rama, परमार्तवत् like one greatly distressed, उवाच he said, सुहृदः friends, सर्वान् all, कथम् how, एतत् this, ब्रवीथ you speak, माम् to me.
explanation: Having heard his words, Rama, greatly distressed, asked all his friends, "How can you say this to me?"

shloka_text: सर्वे तु शिरसा भूमावभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च । प्रत्यूचू राघवं दीनमेवमेतन्न संशयः ।। 7.43.22 ।।
transliteration: sarve tu śirasā bhūmāvabhivādya praṇamya ca | pratyūcū rāghavaṃ dīnamevametanna saṃśayaḥ || 7.43.22 ||
translation: सर्वे all, तु indeed, शिरसा with their heads, भूमौ on the ground, अभिवाद्य having saluted, प्रणम्य having bowed down, च and, प्रत्यूचुः they replied, राघवम् to Rama, दीनम् distressed, एवम् thus, एतत् this, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: All of them, having saluted and bowed down with their heads to the ground, replied to the distressed Rama, "This is indeed so, there is no doubt."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु वाक्यं काकुत्स्थः सर्वेषां समुदीरितम् । विसर्जयामास तदा वयस्याञ्छत्रुसूदनः ।। 7.43.23 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu vākyaṃ kākutsthaḥ sarveṣāṃ samudīritam | visarjayāmāsa tadā vayasyāñchatrusūdanaḥ || 7.43.23 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, वाक्यम् the words, काकुत्स्थः Rama, सर्वेषाम् of all, समुदीरितम् uttered, विसर्जयामास he dismissed, तदा then, वयस्यान् his friends, शत्रुसूदनः the destroyer of enemies.
explanation: Having heard the words uttered by all, Rama, the destroyer of enemies, then dismissed his friends. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 43 ।। Thus ends the forty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विसृज्य तु सुहृद्वर्गं बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य राघवः । समीपे द्वाःस्थमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.1 ।।
transliteration: visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṃ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ | samīpe dvāḥsthamāsīnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.44.1 ||
translation: विसृज्य having dismissed, तु indeed, सुहृद्वर्गम् the group of friends, बुद्ध्या with his intellect, निश्चित्य having resolved, राघवः Rama, समीपे nearby, द्वाःस्थम् the doorkeeper, आसीनम् seated, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् he spoke.
explanation: Having dismissed his group of friends and having resolved with his intellect, Rama then spoke these words to the doorkeeper who was seated nearby.
comments: Rama summons his brothers Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna -- coming, they are dismayed to find his face grief-stricken and tear-stained -- embracing them, Rama declares they are his very life and asks them to join him in weighing the grave matter that troubles him.

shloka_text: शीघ्रमानय सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम् । भरतं च महाभागं शत्रुघ्नमपराजितम् ।। 7.44.2 ।।
transliteration: śīghramānaya saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam | bharataṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ śatrughnamaparājitam || 7.44.2 ||
translation: शीघ्रम् quickly, आनय bring, सौमित्रिं Saumitri, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, शुभलक्षणम् endowed with auspicious marks, भरतं Bharata, च and, महाभागं the highly fortunate one, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, अपराजितम् the unconquered
explanation: Bring quickly Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra and one with auspicious marks, and also Bharata, the highly fortunate one, and Shatrughna, the unconquered.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । लक्ष्मणस्य गृहं गत्वा प्रविवेशानिवारितः ।। 7.44.3 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ | lakṣmaṇasya gṛhaṃ gatvā praviveśānivāritaḥ || 7.44.3 ||
translation: रामस्य Rama's, वचनं word, श्रुत्वा having heard, द्वाःस्थो the doorkeeper, मूर्ध्नि on his head, कृताञ्जलिः having made an anjali, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, गृहं house, गत्वा having gone, प्रविवेश entered, अनिवारितः unhindered
explanation: Having heard Rama's command, the doorkeeper, with folded hands placed on his head, went to Lakshmana's house and entered unhindered.

shloka_text: उवाच सुमहात्मानं वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः । द्रष्टुमिच्छति राजा त्वां गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम् ।। 7.44.4 ।।
transliteration: uvāca sumahātmānaṃ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ | draṣṭumicchati rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram || 7.44.4 ||
translation: उवाच he said, सुमहात्मानं to the great-souled one, वर्धयित्वा having greeted, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छति wishes, राजा the king, त्वां you, गम्यतां you should go, तत्र there, मा not, चिरम् delay
explanation: With folded hands, he greeted the great-souled Lakshmana and said, 'The king wishes to see you; go there without delay.'

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव सौमित्रिः श्रुत्वा राघवशासनम् । प्राद्रवद्रथमारुह्य राघवस्य निवेशनम् ।। 7.44.5 ।।
transliteration: bāḍhamityeva saumitriḥ śrutvā rāghavaśāsanam | prādravadrathamāruhya rāghavasya niveśanam || 7.44.5 ||
translation: बाढम् 'Alright', इति thus, एव indeed, सौमित्रिः Saumitri, श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवशासनम् Rama's command, प्राद्रवत् he hastened, रथम् chariot, आरुह्य having ascended, राघवस्य Rama's, निवेशनम् abode
explanation: Having heard Rama's command, Saumitri (Lakshmana) immediately said 'Alright' and hastened to Rama's abode, having mounted his chariot.

shloka_text: प्रयान्तं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा द्वाःस्थो भरतमन्तिकात् । उवाच भरतं तत्र वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.6 ।।
transliteration: prayāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvāḥstho bharatamantikāt | uvāca bharataṃ tatra vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ || 7.44.6 ||
translation: प्रयान्तं departing, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, दृष्ट्वा having seen, द्वाःस्थो the doorkeeper, भरतम् Bharata, अन्तिकात् from nearby, उवाच he said, भरतं to Bharata, तत्र there, वर्धयित्वा having greeted, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands
explanation: Having seen Lakshmana departing, the doorkeeper, from nearby, then greeted Bharata with folded hands and spoke to him.

shloka_text: विनयावनतो भूत्वा राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति । भरतस्तु वचःश्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थाद्रामसमीरितम् ।। 7.44.7 ।।
transliteration: vinayāvanato bhūtvā rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati | bharatastu vacaḥśrutvā dvāḥsthādrāmasamīritam || 7.44.7 ||
translation: विनयावनतः humbly bowed, भूत्वा having become, राजा the king, त्वां you, द्रष्टुमिच्छति wishes to see. भरतस्तु But Bharata, वचःश्रुत्वा having heard the words, द्वाःस्थात् from the doorkeeper, रामसमीरितम् spoken by Rama.
explanation: The doorkeeper informed Bharata that the king, having become humble, wished to see him, and Bharata heard these words spoken by Rama through the doorkeeper.

shloka_text: उत्पपातासनात्तूर्णं पद्भ्यामेव ययौ बली । दृष्ट्वा प्रयान्तं भरतं त्वरमाणः कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.8 ।।
transliteration: utpapātāsanāttūrṇaṃ padbhyāmeva yayau balī | dṛṣṭvā prayāntaṃ bharataṃ tvaramāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ || 7.44.8 ||
translation: उत्पपात sprang up, आसनात् from his seat, तूर्णं quickly, पद्भ्यामेव by his feet alone, ययौ went, बली the mighty one (Bharata). दृष्ट्वा Having seen, प्रयान्तं going, भरतं Bharata, त्वरमाणः hurrying, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands (the doorkeeper).
explanation: The mighty Bharata quickly sprang from his seat and went on foot, while the doorkeeper, seeing Bharata depart, hurried along with folded hands.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नभवनं गत्वा ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह । एह्यागच्छ रघुश्रेष्ठ राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति ।। 7.44.9 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnabhavanaṃ gatvā tato vākyamuvāca ha | ehyāgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati || 7.44.9 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नभवनं to Shatrughna's abode, गत्वा having gone, ततो then, वाक्यमुवाच spoke words, ह indeed. एह्यागच्छ Come, come, रघुश्रेष्ठ O best of Raghus, राजा the king, त्वां you, द्रष्टुमिच्छति wishes to see.
explanation: The doorkeeper then went to Shatrughna's abode and spoke, saying, "Come, O best of Raghus, the king wishes to see you."

shloka_text: गतो हि लक्ष्मणः पूर्वं भरतश्च महायशाः । श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य शत्रुघ्नः परमासनात् ।। 7.44.10 ।।
transliteration: gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ | śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughnaḥ paramāsanāt || 7.44.10 ||
translation: गतो has gone, हि indeed, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, पूर्वं previously, भरतश्च and Bharata, महायशाः the greatly renowned. श्रुत्वा Having heard, तु but, वचनं the words, तस्य of him (the doorkeeper), शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, परमासनात् from his excellent seat.
explanation: The doorkeeper also informed Shatrughna that Lakshmana had already gone, and the greatly renowned Bharata too, and upon hearing these words, Shatrughna rose from his excellent seat.

shloka_text: शिरसा धरणीं प्राप्य प्रययौ यत्र राघवः । द्वाःस्थस्त्वागम्य रामाय सर्वानेव कृताञ्जलिः । निवेदयामास तदा भ्रातऽन्स्वान्समुपस्थितान् ।। 7.44.11 ।।
transliteration: śirasā dharaṇīṃ prāpya prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ | dvāḥsthastvāgamya rāmāya sarvāneva kṛtāñjaliḥ | nivedayāmāsa tadā bhrāta'nsvānsamupasthitān || 7.44.11 ||
translation: शिरसा with his head, धरणीं the ground, प्राप्य having touched, प्रययौ went, यत्र where, राघवः Rama. द्वाःस्थस्तु But the doorkeeper, आगम्य having come, रामाय to Rama, सर्वान् एव all of them indeed, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, निवेदयामास reported, तदा then, भ्रातॄन् his brothers, स्वान् his own, समुपस्थितान् having arrived.
explanation: Shatrughna, having bowed his head to the ground, went to where Rama was, and then the doorkeeper, with folded hands, reported to Rama that all his brothers had arrived.

shloka_text: कुमारानागताञ्छ्रुत्वा चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना द्वाःस्थं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.12 ।।
transliteration: kumārānāgatāñchrutvā cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ | avāṅmukho dīnamanā dvāḥsthaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.44.12 ||
translation: कुमारानागतान् the princes arrived, श्रुत्वा having heard, चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः whose senses were agitated by worry, अवाङ्मुखः with a downcast face, दीनमनाः distressed in mind, द्वाःस्थम् to the doorkeeper, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard that the princes had arrived, Rama, with his senses agitated by worry, a downcast face, and a distressed mind, spoke to the doorkeeper.

shloka_text: प्रवेशय कुमारांस्त्वं मत्समीपं त्वरान्वितः । एतेषु जीवितं मह्यमेते प्राणाः प्रिया मम ।। 7.44.13 ।।
transliteration: praveśaya kumārāṃstvaṃ matsamīpaṃ tvarānvitaḥ | eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyamete prāṇāḥ priyā mama || 7.44.13 ||
translation: प्रवेशय make them enter, कुमारान् the princes, त्वम् you, मत्समीपम् to my presence, त्वरान्वितः quickly, एतेषु in these, जीवितम् life, मह्यम् is mine, एते these, प्राणाः vital airs, प्रियाः dear, मम to me.
explanation: "You, quickly usher the princes into my presence, for my life is in them, and these are my dear vital breaths."

shloka_text: आज्ञप्तास्तु नरेन्द्रेण कुमाराः शक्रतेजसः । प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा विविशुस्ते समाहिताः ।। 7.44.14 ।।
transliteration: ājñaptāstu narendreṇa kumārāḥ śakratejasaḥ | prahvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā viviśuste samāhitāḥ || 7.44.14 ||
translation: आज्ञप्ताः commanded, तु indeed, नरेन्द्रेण by the king, कुमाराः the princes, शक्रतेजसः having the splendor of Indra, प्रह्वाः bowed down, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, विविशुः entered, ते they, समाहिताः composed.
explanation: Commanded by the king, the princes, who possessed the splendor of Indra, entered composedly, having bowed down with folded hands.

shloka_text: ते तु दृष्ट्वा मुखं तस्य सग्रहं शशिनं यथा । सन्ध्यागतमिवादित्यं प्रभया परिवर्जितम् ।। 7.44.15 ।।
transliteration: te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ tasya sagrahaṃ śaśinaṃ yathā | sandhyāgatamivādityaṃ prabhayā parivarjitam || 7.44.15 ||
translation: ते they, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, मुखम् the face, तस्य his, सग्रहम् eclipsed, शशिनम् the moon, यथा like, सन्ध्यागतम् set in the evening, इव like, आदित्यम् the sun, प्रभया by splendor, परिवर्जितम् devoid of.
explanation: They, having seen his face, which was like the moon eclipsed or the sun at dusk devoid of its splendor, were struck by his sorrowful appearance.

shloka_text: बाष्पपूर्णे च नयने दृष्ट्वा रामस्य धीमतः । हतशोभं यथा पद्मं मुखं वीक्ष्य च तस्य ते ।। 7.44.16 ।।
transliteration: bāṣpapūrṇe ca nayane dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ | hataśobhaṃ yathā padmaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya ca tasya te || 7.44.16 ||
translation: बाष्पपूर्णे full of tears, च and, नयने eyes, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रामस्य of Rama, धीमतः the wise, हतशोभम् lost its beauty, यथा like, पद्मम् a lotus, मुखम् the face, वीक्ष्य having seen, च and, तस्य his, ते they.
explanation: And having seen the wise Rama's eyes full of tears, and his face, which was like a lotus that had lost its beauty, they were deeply affected.

shloka_text: ततो ऽभिवाद्य त्वरिताः पादौ रामस्य मूर्धभिः । तस्थुः समाहिताः सर्वे रामस्त्वश्रूण्यवर्तयत् ।। 7.44.17 ।।
transliteration: tato 'bhivādya tvaritāḥ pādau rāmasya mūrdhabhiḥ | tasthuḥ samāhitāḥ sarve rāmastvaśrūṇyavartayat || 7.44.17 ||
translation: ततः then, अभिवाद्य having saluted, त्वरिताः swiftly, पादौ the feet, रामस्य of Rama, मूर्धभिः with their heads, तस्थुः they stood, समाहिताः attentive, सर्वे all, रामः Rama, तु indeed, अश्रूणि tears, अवर्तयत् shed.
explanation: After swiftly saluting Rama's feet with their heads, all of them stood attentively, while Rama, in turn, shed tears.

shloka_text: तान्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यामुत्थाप्य च महाबलः । आसनेष्वासतेत्युक्त्वा ततो वाक्यं जगाद ह ।। 7.44.18 ।।
transliteration: tānpariṣvajya bāhubhyāmutthāpya ca mahābalaḥ | āsaneṣvāsatetyuktvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha || 7.44.18 ||
translation: तान् them, परिष्वज्य having embraced, बाहुभ्याम् with his two arms, उत्थाप्य having raised up, च and, महाबलः the mighty one, आसनेषु on the seats, आसत sit, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, ततः then, वाक्यम् a speech, जगाद spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: The mighty Rama, embracing them with his arms and raising them up, asked them to sit on their seats, and then he spoke these words.

shloka_text: भवन्तो मम सर्वस्वं भवन्तो जीवितं मम । भवद्भिश्च कृतं राज्यं पालयामि नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.19 ।।
transliteration: bhavanto mama sarvasvaṃ bhavanto jīvitaṃ mama | bhavadbhiśca kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ pālayāmi nareśvarāḥ || 7.44.19 ||
translation: भवन्तः you, मम my, सर्वस्वम् all, भवन्तः you, जीवितम् life, मम my, भवद्भिः by you, च and, कृतम् established, राज्यम् kingdom, पालयामि I rule, नरेश्वराः O kings.
explanation: Rama declared to the kings that they were his everything and his very life, and that he ruled the kingdom which they had helped establish.

shloka_text: भवन्तः कृतशास्त्रार्था बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठिताः । सम्भूय च मदर्थो ऽयमन्वेष्टव्यो नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.20 ।।
transliteration: bhavantaḥ kṛtaśāstrārthā buddhyā ca pariniṣṭhitāḥ | sambhūya ca madartho 'yamanveṣṭavyo nareśvarāḥ || 7.44.20 ||
translation: भवन्तः you, कृतशास्त्रार्थाः learned in scriptures, बुद्ध्या by intellect, च and, परिनिष्ठिताः perfected, सम्भूय having assembled, च and, मदर्थः my purpose, अयम् this, अन्वेष्टव्यः should be investigated, नरेश्वराः O kings.
explanation: Rama further stated that since they were learned in scriptures and perfected in intellect, they should all together investigate this matter of his.

shloka_text: तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे अवधानपरायणाः । उद्विग्नमनसः सर्वे किं नु राजाभिधास्यति ।। 7.44.21 ।।
transliteration: tathā vadati kākutsthe avadhānaparāyaṇāḥ | udvignamanasaḥ sarve kiṃ nu rājābhidhāsyati || 7.44.21 ||
translation: तथा thus, वदति while speaking, काकुत्स्थे by Kakutstha, अवधानपरायणाः very attentive, उद्विग्नमनसः with agitated minds, सर्वे all, किम् what, नु indeed, राजा the king, अभिधास्यति will say.
explanation: As Rama spoke thus, all the kings, though very attentive, became anxious in their minds, wondering what the king would say next. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 44 ।। Thus ends the forty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीनचेतसाम् । उवाच वाक्यं काकुत्स्थो मुखेन परिशुष्यता ।। 7.45.1 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dīnacetasām | uvāca vākyaṃ kākutstho mukhena pariśuṣyatā || 7.45.1 ||
translation: तेषां of them, समुपविष्टानां who were seated, सर्वेषां of all, दीनचेतसाम् whose minds were distressed, काकुत्स्थो Kakutstha (Rama), परिशुष्यता drying up, मुखेन with his face, वाक्यं a word, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Rama, with a face parched by sorrow, spoke to all those who were seated before him with distressed minds.
comments: Rama discloses to his brothers the people's scandal against Sita and the unbearable infamy it brings, though he knows her pure, her innocence proven by fire and attested by the gods -- dreading dishonour above all, he commands Lakshmana to take Sita on the morrow and abandon her near Valmiki's hermitage on the Ganga, forbidding all argument, and withdraws sighing in grief.

shloka_text: सर्वे शृणुत भद्रं वो मा कुरुध्वं मनो ऽन्यथा । पौराणां मम सीतायां यादृशी वर्तते कथा ।। 7.45.2 ।।
transliteration: sarve śṛṇuta bhadraṃ vo mā kurudhvaṃ mano 'nyathā | paurāṇāṃ mama sītāyāṃ yādṛśī vartate kathā || 7.45.2 ||
translation: सर्वे all (of you), शृणुत listen, वः to you, भद्रं welfare (may there be), मनो mind, अन्यथा otherwise, मा do not, कुरुध्वं make, पौराणां of the citizens, मम my, सीतायां regarding Sita, यादृशी what kind of, कथा talk, वर्तते exists.
explanation: He asked them all to listen, wishing them well, and not to misunderstand, as he was about to reveal the kind of talk that existed among the citizens concerning his Sita.

shloka_text: पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च । वर्तते मयि बीभत्सा सा मे मर्माणि कृन्तति ।। 7.45.3 ।।
transliteration: paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṃstathā janapadasya ca | vartate mayi bībhatsā sā me marmāṇi kṛntati || 7.45.3 ||
translation: सुमहांस् very great, पौरापवादः scandal of the citizens, तथा and, जनपदस्य of the people of the country, च and, बीभत्सा disgusting (talk), मयि regarding me, वर्तते exists, सा that, मे my, मर्माणि vital parts, कृन्तति cuts.
explanation: A very great and abhorrent scandal from both the citizens and the people of the country exists concerning me, and that talk cuts into my very vitals.

shloka_text: अहं किल कुले जात इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । सीता ऽपि सत्कुले जाता जनकानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.45.4 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ kila kule jāta ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām | sītā 'pi satkule jātā janakānāṃ mahātmanām || 7.45.4 ||
translation: अहं I, किल indeed, महात्मनाम् of the great-souled, इक्ष्वाकूणां of the Ikshvakus, कुले in the family, जात born, सीता Sita, अपि also, महात्मनाम् of the great-souled, जनकानां of the Janakas, सत्कुले in a noble family, जाता born.
explanation: He stated that he was born in the family of the great-souled Ikshvakus, and Sita too was born in the noble family of the great-souled Janakas.

shloka_text: जानासि त्वं यथा सौम्य दण्डके विजने वने । रावणेन हृता सीता स च विध्वंसितो मया ।। 7.45.5 ।।
transliteration: jānāsi tvaṃ yathā saumya daṇḍake vijane vane | rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā sa ca vidhvaṃsito mayā || 7.45.5 ||
translation: सौम्य O gentle one, त्वं you, जानासि know, यथा how, दण्डके in Dandaka, विजने solitary, वने in the forest, सीता Sita, रावणेन by Ravana, हृता was abducted, च and, स he (Ravana), मया by me, विध्वंसितो was destroyed.
explanation: He reminded them, "O gentle one, you know how Sita was abducted by Ravana in the solitary Dandaka forest, and how I subsequently destroyed him."

shloka_text: तत्र मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना जनकस्य सुतां प्रति । अत्रोषितामिमां सीतामानयेयं कथं पुरीम् ।। 7.45.6 ।।
transliteration: tatra me buddhirutpannā janakasya sutāṃ prati | atroṣitāmimāṃ sītāmānayeyaṃ kathaṃ purīm || 7.45.6 ||
translation: तत्र there, मे my, बुद्धिः thought, उत्पन्ना arose, जनकस्य of Janaka, सुताम् daughter, प्रति regarding, अत्र here, उषिताम् having resided, इमाम् this, सीताम् Sita, आनयेयम् I should bring, कथम् how, पुरीम् to the city.
explanation: At that time, a thought arose in my mind concerning Janaka's daughter, Sita, wondering how I could bring this Sita, who had resided here, back to the city.

shloka_text: प्रत्ययार्थं ततः सीता विवेश ज्वलनं तदा । प्रत्यक्षं तव सौमित्रे देवानां हव्यवाहनः । अपापां मैथिलीमाह वायुश्चाकाशगोचरः ।। 7.45.7 ।।
transliteration: pratyayārthaṃ tataḥ sītā viveśa jvalanaṃ tadā | pratyakṣaṃ tava saumitre devānāṃ havyavāhanaḥ | apāpāṃ maithilīmāha vāyuścākāśagocaraḥ || 7.45.7 ||
translation: प्रत्ययार्थम् for the sake of proof, ततः then, सीता Sita, विवेश entered, ज्वलनम् fire, तदा then, प्रत्यक्षम् in the presence of, तव your, सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, देवानाम् of the gods, हव्यवाहनः the fire-god, अपापाम् sinless, मैथिलीम् Maithili, आह declared, वायुः the wind-god, च and, आकाशगोचरः moving in the sky.
explanation: Then, for the sake of proof, Sita entered the fire, and in your presence, O Lakshmana, the fire-god and the wind-god, who moves in the sky, declared Maithili to be sinless.

shloka_text: चन्द्रादित्यौ च शंसेते सुराणां सन्निधौ पुरा । ऋषीणां चैव सर्वेषामपापां जनकात्मजाम् ।। 7.45.8 ।।
transliteration: candrādityau ca śaṃsete surāṇāṃ sannidhau purā | ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāmapāpāṃ janakātmajām || 7.45.8 ||
translation: चन्द्रादित्यौ the moon and the sun, च and, शंसेते declared, सुराणाम् of the gods, सन्निधौ in the presence, पुरा formerly, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, च and, एव indeed, सर्वेषाम् of all, अपापाम् sinless, जनकात्मजाम् Janaka's daughter.
explanation: Furthermore, the moon and the sun, in the presence of all the gods and sages, formerly declared Janaka's daughter to be sinless.

shloka_text: एवं शुद्धसमाचारा देवगन्धर्वसन्निधौ । लङ्काद्वीपे महेन्द्रेण मम हस्ते निवेशिता ।। 7.45.9 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ śuddhasamācārā devagandharvasannidhau | laṅkādvīpe mahendreṇa mama haste niveśitā || 7.45.9 ||
translation: एवम् thus, शुद्धसमाचारा of pure conduct, देवगन्धर्वसन्निधौ in the presence of gods and Gandharvas, लङ्काद्वीपे on the island of Lanka, महेन्द्रेण by the great Indra, मम my, हस्ते in the hand, निवेशिता placed.
explanation: Thus, she of pure conduct was entrusted into my hands by the great Indra himself on the island of Lanka, in the presence of gods and Gandharvas.

shloka_text: अन्तरात्मा च मे वेत्ति सीतां शुद्धां यशस्विनीम् । ततो गृहीत्वा वैदेहीमयोध्यामहमागतः ।। 7.45.10 ।।
transliteration: antarātmā ca me vetti sītāṃ śuddhāṃ yaśasvinīm | tato gṛhītvā vaidehīmayodhyāmahamāgataḥ || 7.45.10 ||
translation: अन्तरात्मा my inner self, च and, मे my, वेत्ति knows, सीताम् Sita, शुद्धाम् pure, यशस्विनीम् glorious, ततः then, गृहीत्वा having taken, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, अहम् I, आगतः came.
explanation: And my inner self knows Sita to be pure and glorious, so thereafter, I brought Vaidehi to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: अयं तु मे महान्वादः शोकश्च हृदि वर्तते । पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च ।। 7.45.11 ।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu me mahānvādaḥ śokaśca hṛdi vartate | paurāpavādaḥ sumahāṃstathā janapadasya ca || 7.45.11 ||
translation: अयं this, तु indeed, मे my, महान् great, वादः accusation, शोकः sorrow, च and, हृदि in the heart, वर्तते exists, पौरापवादः the slander of the citizens, सुमहान् very great, तथा and, जनपदस्य of the country, च also.
explanation: This great accusation and sorrow, which is the very great slander of the citizens and the people of the country, exists in my heart.

shloka_text: अकीर्तिर्यस्य गीयेत लोके भूतस्य कस्यचित् । पतत्येवाधमाँल्लोकान्यावच्छब्दः प्रकीर्त्यते ।। 7.45.12 ।।
transliteration: akīrtiryasya gīyeta loke bhūtasya kasyacit | patatyevādhamāँllokānyāvacchabdaḥ prakīrtyate || 7.45.12 ||
translation: अकीर्तिः infamy, यस्य whose, गीयेत is sung, लोके in the world, भूतस्य of a being, कस्यचित् any, पतति falls, एव indeed, अधमान् to lower, लोकान् worlds, यावत् as long as, शब्दः the word, प्रकीर्त्यते is proclaimed.
explanation: Any being whose infamy is spoken of in the world falls to lower realms as long as that word of disgrace is proclaimed.

shloka_text: अकीर्तिर्निन्द्यते देवैः कीर्तिर्लोकेषु पूज्यते । कीर्त्यर्थं तु समारम्भः सर्वेषां सुमहात्मनाम् ।। 7.45.13 ।।
transliteration: akīrtirnindyate devaiḥ kīrtirlokeṣu pūjyate | kīrtyarthaṃ tu samārambhaḥ sarveṣāṃ sumahātmanām || 7.45.13 ||
translation: अकीर्तिः infamy, निन्द्यते is condemned, देवैः by the gods, कीर्तिः fame, लोकेषु in the worlds, पूज्यते is honored, कीर्त्यर्थम् for the sake of fame, तु indeed, समारम्भः the undertaking, सर्वेषाम् of all, सुमहात्मनाम् great-souled ones.
explanation: Infamy is condemned by the gods, while fame is honored in all worlds, and indeed, all great-souled individuals undertake their endeavors for the sake of renown.

shloka_text: अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां युष्मान्वा पुरुषर्षभाः । अपवादभयाद्भीतः किं पुनर्जनकात्मजाम् ।। 7.45.14 ।।
transliteration: apyahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyāṃ yuṣmānvā puruṣarṣabhāḥ | apavādabhayādbhītaḥ kiṃ punarjanakātmajām || 7.45.14 ||
translation: अपि even, अहम् I, जीवितम् life, जह्याम् would abandon, युष्मान् you, वा or, पुरुषर्षभाः O best among men, अपवादभयात् from the fear of slander, भीतः afraid, किम् what, पुनर् then, जनकात्मजाम् Janaka's daughter.
explanation: O best among men, I, being afraid of the fear of slander, would even abandon my life or you all, so what then of Janaka's daughter?

shloka_text: तस्माद्भवन्तः पश्यन्तु पतितं शोकसागरे । नहि पश्याम्यहं भूतं किञ्चिद्दुःखमतो ऽधिकम् ।। 7.45.15 ।।
transliteration: tasmādbhavantaḥ paśyantu patitaṃ śokasāgare | nahi paśyāmyahaṃ bhūtaṃ kiñcidduḥkhamato 'dhikam || 7.45.15 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, भवन्तः you, पश्यन्तु may see, पतितम् fallen, शोकसागरे in the ocean of sorrow, न not, हि indeed, पश्याम्यहम् I see, भूतं existing, किञ्चित् any, दुःखम् sorrow, अतः than this, अधिकम् greater.
explanation: Therefore, you should see me fallen into an ocean of sorrow, for I indeed do not see any existing sorrow greater than this.

shloka_text: श्वस्त्वं प्रभाते सौमित्रे सुमन्त्राधिष्ठितं रथम् । आरुह्य सीतामारोप्य विषयान्ते समुत्सृज ।। 7.45.16 ।।
transliteration: śvastvaṃ prabhāte saumitre sumantrādhiṣṭhitaṃ ratham | āruhya sītāmāropya viṣayānte samutsṛja || 7.45.16 ||
translation: श्वः tomorrow, त्वं you, प्रभाते in the morning, सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, सुमन्त्राधिष्ठितं driven by Sumantra, रथम् chariot, आरुह्य having ascended, सीताम् Sita, आरोप्य having made to ascend, विषयान्ते at the border of the kingdom, समुत्सृज abandon.
explanation: O Lakshmana, tomorrow morning, you must ascend the chariot driven by Sumantra, place Sita in it, and abandon her at the border of the kingdom.

shloka_text: गङ्गायास्तु परे पारे वाल्मीकेस्तु महात्मनः । आश्रमो दिव्यसङ्काशस्तमसातीरमाश्रितः ।। 7.45.17 ।।
transliteration: gaṅgāyāstu pare pāre vālmīkestu mahātmanaḥ | āśramo divyasaṅkāśastamasātīramāśritaḥ || 7.45.17 ||
translation: गङ्गायाः of Ganga, तु indeed, परे on the other, पारे bank, वाल्मीकेः of Valmiki, तु indeed, महात्मनः of the great soul, आश्रमः hermitage, दिव्यसङ्काशः divine-looking, तमसातीरम् the bank of Tamasa, आश्रितः situated.
explanation: On the other bank of the Ganga, there is the divine-looking hermitage of the great sage Valmiki, situated on the banks of the Tamasa river.

shloka_text: तत्रैनां विजने देशे विसृज्य रघुनन्दन । शीघ्रमागच्छ भद्रं ते कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.45.18 ।।
transliteration: tatraināṃ vijane deśe visṛjya raghunandana | śīghramāgaccha bhadraṃ te kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama || 7.45.18 ||
translation: तत्र there, एनां her, विजने solitary, देशे in the place, विसृज्य having abandoned, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghu dynasty, शीघ्रम् quickly, आगच्छ come back, भद्रं welfare, ते to you, कुरुष्व do, वचनं command, मम my.
explanation: O Lakshmana, having abandoned her there in that solitary place, return quickly; may good fortune be yours, and carry out my command.

shloka_text: न चास्मिन् प्रतिवक्तव्यः सीतां प्रति कथञ्चन । तस्मात्त्वं गच्छ सौमित्रे नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।। 7.45.19 ।।
transliteration: na cāsmin prativaktavyaḥ sītāṃ prati kathañcana | tasmāttvaṃ gaccha saumitre nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 7.45.19 ||
translation: न not, च and, अस्मिन् in this matter, प्रतिवक्तव्यः to be argued against, सीतां Sita, प्रति regarding, कथञ्चन in any way, तस्मात् therefore, त्वं you, गच्छ go, सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, न not, अत्र here, कार्या to be done, विचारणा deliberation.
explanation: And regarding Sita, you must not argue against this command in any way; therefore, O Lakshmana, go, for no deliberation is to be done in this matter.

shloka_text: अप्रीतिर्हि परा मह्यं त्वयेतत्प्रतिवारिते । शापिता हि मया यूयं भुजाभ्यां जीवितेन च ।। 7.45.20 ।।
transliteration: aprītirhi parā mahyaṃ tvayetatprativārite | śāpitā hi mayā yūyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ jīvitena ca || 7.45.20 ||
translation: अप्रीतिः displeasure, हि indeed, परा great, मह्यं to me, त्वया by you, एतत् this, प्रतिवारिते if opposed, शापिता sworn, हि indeed, मया by me, यूयं you all, भुजाभ्यां by my arms, जीवितेन by my life, च and.
explanation: Indeed, great displeasure will befall me if you oppose this, for I have made you all swear by my arms and by my very life.

shloka_text: ये मां वाक्यान्तरे ब्रूयुरनुनेतुं कथञ्चन । अहिता नाम ते नित्यं मदभीष्टविघातनात् ।। 7.45.21 ।।
transliteration: ye māṃ vākyāntare brūyuranunetuṃ kathañcana | ahitā nāma te nityaṃ madabhīṣṭavighātanāt || 7.45.21 ||
translation: ये those who, मां me, वाक्यान्तरे with other words, ब्रूयुः would speak, अनुनेतुम् to persuade, कथञ्चन in any way, अहिताः enemies, नाम indeed, ते they, नित्यम् always, मदभीष्टविघातनात् because of obstructing my desire.
explanation: Those who would speak to me with other words, attempting to persuade me in any way, are indeed always my enemies because they obstruct my desire.

shloka_text: मानयन्तु भवन्तो मां यदि मच्छासने स्थिताः । इतो ऽद्य नीयतां सीता कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.45.22 ।।
transliteration: mānayantu bhavanto māṃ yadi macchāsane sthitāḥ | ito 'dya nīyatāṃ sītā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama || 7.45.22 ||
translation: मानयन्तु let them respect, भवन्तः you, मां me, यदि if, मच्छासने in my command, स्थिताः established, इतः from here, अद्य today, नीयताम् let her be taken, सीता Sita, कुरुष्व do, वचनम् the command, मम my.
explanation: If you abide by my command, then respect me; let Sita be taken from here today, and obey my word.

shloka_text: पूर्वमुक्तो ऽहमनया गङ्गातीरे ऽहमाश्रमान् । पश्येयमिति तस्याश्च कामः संवर्त्यतामयम् ।। 7.45.23 ।।
transliteration: pūrvamukto 'hamanayā gaṅgātīre 'hamāśramān | paśyeyamiti tasyāśca kāmaḥ saṃvartyatāmayam || 7.45.23 ||
translation: पूर्वम् previously, उक्तः said, अहम् I, अनया by her, गङ्गातीरे on the bank of the Ganga, अहम् I, आश्रमान् hermitages, पश्येयम् may see, इति thus, तस्याः her, च and, कामः desire, संवर्त्यताम् let it be fulfilled, अयम् this.
explanation: She had previously told me that she wished to see the hermitages on the bank of the Ganga, so let this desire of hers be fulfilled.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो बाष्पेण पिहिताननः । प्रविवेश स धर्मात्मा भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः ।। 7.45.24 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu kākutstho bāṣpeṇa pihitānanaḥ | praviveśa sa dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ || 7.45.24 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तु indeed, काकुत्स्थः Rama, बाष्पेण with tears, पिहिताननः having his face covered, प्रविवेश entered, सः he, धर्मात्मा the righteous one, भ्रातृभिः by his brothers, परिवारितः surrounded.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Rama, the righteous one, with his face covered in tears, entered, surrounded by his brothers.

shloka_text: शोकसंलग्नहृदयो निशश्वास यथा द्विपः ।। 7.45.25 ।।
transliteration: śokasaṃlagnahṛdayo niśaśvāsa yathā dvipaḥ || 7.45.25 ||
translation: शोकसंलग्नहृदयः with a heart engulfed by sorrow, निशश्वास he sighed, यथा like, द्विपः an elephant.
explanation: With his heart engulfed by sorrow, he sighed like an elephant. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 45 ।। Thus ends the forty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो रजन्यां व्युष्टायां लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । सुमन्त्रमब्रवीद्वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता ।। 7.46.1 ।।
transliteration: tato rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ | sumantramabravīdvākyaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā || 7.46.1 ||
translation: ततो then, रजन्यां night, व्युष्टायां having dawned, लक्ष्मणो Lakshmana, दीनचेतनः with a sorrowful mind, सुमन्त्रम् to Sumantra, अब्रवीत् spoke, वाक्यं words, मुखेन with a face, परिशुष्यता drying up.
explanation: Then, when the night had dawned, Lakshmana, with a sorrowful mind and a parched face, spoke to Sumantra.
comments: At dawn the heartsick Lakshmana readies the chariot and tells Sita she is to be taken to the hermitages she had wished to see -- joyfully she gathers gifts for the sages' wives and sets out, troubled on the way by evil omens -- reaching the Ganga, Lakshmana weeps, and the puzzled Sita comforts him and asks to be ferried across.

shloka_text: सारथे तुरगाञ्छीघ्रं योजयस्व रथोत्तमे । स्वास्तीर्णं राजभवनात्सीतायाश्चासनं कुरु ।। 7.46.2 ।।
transliteration: sārathe turagāñchīghraṃ yojayasva rathottame | svāstīrṇaṃ rājabhavanātsītāyāścāsanaṃ kuru || 7.46.2 ||
translation: सारथे O charioteer, तुरगान् horses, शीघ्रं quickly, योजयस्व harness, रथोत्तमे to the excellent chariot, स्वास्तीर्णं well-cushioned, राजभवनात् from the royal palace, सीतायाश्च and for Sita, आसनं seat, कुरु prepare.
explanation: O charioteer, quickly harness the horses to the excellent chariot and prepare a well-cushioned seat for Sita from the royal palace.

shloka_text: सीता हि राजवचनादाश्रमं पुण्यकर्मणाम् । मया नेया महर्षीणां श्रीघ्रमानीयतां रथः ।। 7.46.3 ।।
transliteration: sītā hi rājavacanādāśramaṃ puṇyakarmaṇām | mayā neyā maharṣīṇāṃ śrīghramānīyatāṃ rathaḥ || 7.46.3 ||
translation: सीता Sita, हि indeed, राजवचनात् by the king's command, आश्रमं to the hermitage, पुण्यकर्मणाम् of the virtuous ones, मया by me, नेया to be taken, महर्षीणां of the great sages, शीघ्रम् quickly, आनीयतां let it be brought, रथः the chariot.
explanation: Indeed, Sita is to be taken by me to the hermitage of the virtuous great sages by the king's command, so let the chariot be brought quickly.
