translation: पाद्येन with water for feet, फलमूलैः with fruits and roots, च and, उवास stayed, मुनिभिः सह with the sages.
explanation: He (Rama) stayed with the sages, having been honored with water for his feet and offerings of fruits and roots.

shloka_text: तेषां तत्रोपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः । बभूवुः परमर्षीणां मध्यादित्यगते ऽहनि ।। 7.51.6 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tatropaviṣṭānāṃ tāstāḥ sumadhurāḥ kathāḥ | babhūvuḥ paramarṣīṇāṃ madhyādityagate 'hani || 7.51.6 ||
translation: तेषां among them, तत्रोपविष्टानां who were seated there, तास्ताः various, सुमधुराः very sweet, कथाः conversations, बभूवुः took place, परमर्षीणां among the great sages, मध्यादित्यगते when the sun was in the middle, अहनि in the day.
explanation: As they sat there, various very pleasant conversations took place among the great sages during the midday.

shloka_text: ततः कथायां कस्याञ्चित्प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः । उवाच तं महात्मानमत्रेः पुत्रं तपोधनम् ।। 7.51.7 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kathāyāṃ kasyāñcitprāñjaliḥ pragraho nṛpaḥ | uvāca taṃ mahātmānamatreḥ putraṃ tapodhanam || 7.51.7 ||
translation: ततः then, कथायां कस्याञ्चित् in some conversation, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, प्रग्रहः humble, नृपः the king, उवाच spoke, तं to him, महात्मानम् the great-souled one, अत्रेः पुत्रं the son of Atri, तपोधनम् rich in asceticism.
explanation: Then, during one of the conversations, the king (Rama), with folded hands and humility, spoke to that great-souled sage, the son of Atri, who was rich in asceticism.

shloka_text: भगवन्किं प्रमाणेन मम वंशो भविष्यति । किमायुश्च हि मे रामः पुत्राश्चान्ये किमायुषः ।। 7.51.8 ।।
transliteration: bhagavankiṃ pramāṇena mama vaṃśo bhaviṣyati | kimāyuśca hi me rāmaḥ putrāścānye kimāyuṣaḥ || 7.51.8 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, किं what, प्रमाणेन by measure, मम my, वंशो lineage, भविष्यति will be, किम् what, आयुः lifespan, च and, हि indeed, मे my, रामः Rama, पुत्राः sons, च and, अन्ये others, किम् what, आयुषः of lifespan.
explanation: Dasharatha asks the sage about the extent of his lineage, the lifespan of his son Rama, and the lifespans of his other sons.

shloka_text: रामस्य च सुता ये स्युस्तेषामायुः कियद्भवेत् । काम्यया भगवन्बूहि वंशस्यास्य गतिं मम ।। 7.51.9 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya ca sutā ye syusteṣāmāyuḥ kiyadbhavet | kāmyayā bhagavanbūhi vaṃśasyāsya gatiṃ mama || 7.51.9 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, च and, सुताः sons, ये who, स्युः may be, तेषाम् their, आयुः lifespan, कियत् how much, भवेत् may be, काम्यया with desire, भगवन् O revered one, ब्रूहि tell, वंशस्य of the lineage, अस्य this, गतिम् course, मम my.
explanation: Dasharatha further inquires about the lifespans of Rama's future sons and eagerly requests the sage to reveal the future course of his dynasty.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं राज्ञो दशरथस्य च । दुर्वासाः सुमहातेजा व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.51.10 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rājño daśarathasya ca | durvāsāḥ sumahātejā vyāhartumupacakrame || 7.51.10 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, व्याहृतम् spoken, वाक्यम् word, राज्ञः of the king, दशरथस्य Dasharatha, च and, दुर्वासाः Durvasa, सुमहातेजाः of great splendor, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by King Dasharatha, the exceedingly powerful sage Durvasa began to reply.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्पुरावृत्तं तदा देवासुरे युधि । दैत्याः सुरैर्भर्त्स्यमाना भृगुपत्नीं समाश्रिताः ।। 7.51.11 ।।
transliteration: śṛṇu rājanpurāvṛttaṃ tadā devāsure yudhi | daityāḥ surairbhartsyamānā bhṛgupatnīṃ samāśritāḥ || 7.51.11 ||
translation: शृणु listen, राजन् O king, पुरावृत्तम् ancient event, तदा then, देवासुरे between gods and asuras, युधि in battle, दैत्याः demons, सुरैः by gods, भर्त्स्यमानाः being oppressed, भृगुपत्नीम् to Bhrigu's wife, समाश्रिताः took refuge.
explanation: Durvasa instructs the king to listen to an ancient event from the time of the war between gods and asuras, when the demons, being oppressed by the gods, sought refuge with Bhrigu's wife.

shloka_text: तया परिगृहीतांस्तान्दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धः सुरेश्वरः । चक्रेण शितधारेण भृगुपत्न्याः शिरो ऽहरत् ।। 7.51.13 ।।
transliteration: tayā parigṛhītāṃstāndṛṣṭvā kruddhaḥ sureśvaraḥ | cakreṇa śitadhāreṇa bhṛgupatnyāḥ śiro 'harat || 7.51.13 ||
translation: तया by her, परिगृहीतान् protected, तान् them, दृष्ट्वा having seen, क्रुद्धः enraged, सुरेश्वरः the lord of gods, चक्रेण with the discus, शितधारेण sharp-edged, भृगुपत्न्याः of Bhrigu's wife, शिरः head, अहरत् cut off.
explanation: Seeing the demons protected by her, the enraged lord of gods (Vishnu) cut off the head of Bhrigu's wife with his sharp-edged discus.

shloka_text: ततस्तां निहतां दृष्ट्वा पत्नीं भृगुकुलोद्वहः । शशाप सहसा क्रुद्धो विष्णुं रिपुकुलार्दनम् ।। 7.51.14 ।।
transliteration: tatastāṃ nihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā patnīṃ bhṛgukulodvahaḥ | śaśāpa sahasā kruddho viṣṇuṃ ripukulārdanam || 7.51.14 ||
translation: ततः then, तां her, निहतां slain, दृष्ट्वा having seen, पत्नीं wife, भृगुकुलोद्वहः the upholder of the Bhrigu lineage, शशाप cursed, सहसा suddenly, क्रुद्धो enraged, विष्णुं Vishnu, रिपुकुलार्दनम् the destroyer of the family of enemies.
explanation: Then, the enraged upholder of the Bhrigu lineage, having suddenly seen his wife slain, cursed Vishnu, the destroyer of the family of enemies.

shloka_text: यस्मादवध्यां मे पत्नीमवधीः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । तस्मात्त्वं मानुषे लोके जनिष्यसि जनार्दन ।। 7.51.15 ।।
transliteration: yasmādavadhyāṃ me patnīmavadhīḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ | tasmāttvaṃ mānuṣe loke janiṣyasi janārdana || 7.51.15 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, अवध्यां inviolable, मे my, पत्नीम् wife, अवधीः you killed, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome by anger, तस्मात् therefore, त्वं you, मानुषे in the human, लोके world, जनिष्यसि will be born, जनार्दन O Janardana.
explanation: Because you, overcome by anger, killed my inviolable wife, therefore you, O Janardana, will be born in the human world.

shloka_text: तत्र पत्नीवियोगं त्वं प्राप्स्यसे बहुवार्षिकम् ।। 7.51.16 ।।
transliteration: tatra patnīviyogaṃ tvaṃ prāpsyase bahuvārṣikam || 7.51.16 ||
translation: तत्र there, पत्नीवियोगं separation from wife, त्वं you, प्राप्स्यसे will experience, बहुवार्षिकम् for many years.
explanation: There, you will experience separation from your wife for many years.

shloka_text: शापाभिहतचेतास्स स्वात्मना भावितो ऽभवत् ।। 7.51.17 ।।
transliteration: śāpābhihatacetāssa svātmanā bhāvito 'bhavat || 7.51.17 ||
translation: शापाभिहतचेताः whose mind was afflicted by the curse, सः he, स्वात्मना by his own self, भावितो understood/realized, अभवत् became.
explanation: Though his mind was afflicted by the curse, he (Vishnu) realized it was in accordance with his own divine will.

shloka_text: अर्चयामास तं देवं भृगुः शापेन पीडितः । तपसाराधितो देवो ह्यब्रवीद्भक्तवत्सलः । लोकानां संहितार्थं तु तं शापं ग्राह्यमुक्तवान् ।। 7.51.19 ।।
transliteration: arcayāmāsa taṃ devaṃ bhṛguḥ śāpena pīḍitaḥ | tapasārādhito devo hyabravīdbhaktavatsalaḥ | lokānāṃ saṃhitārthaṃ tu taṃ śāpaṃ grāhyamuktavān || 7.51.19 ||
translation: अर्चयामास worshipped, तं that, देवं god, भृगुः Bhrigu, शापेन by the curse, पीडितः distressed, तपसा by penance, आराधितो worshipped, देवो the god, हि indeed, अब्रवीत् said, भक्तवत्सलः affectionate to his devotees, लोकानां for the worlds, संहितार्थं for the welfare, तु indeed, तं that, शापं curse, ग्राह्यं acceptable, उक्तवान् declared.
explanation: Distressed by his own curse, Bhrigu worshipped that god (Vishnu), and the god, affectionate to his devotees and propitiated by penance, indeed declared that the curse was acceptable for the welfare of the worlds.

shloka_text: इति शप्तो महातेजा भृगुणा पूर्वजन्मनि । इहागतो हि पुत्रत्वं तव पार्थिवसत्तम ।। 7.51.20 ।।
transliteration: iti śapto mahātejā bhṛguṇā pūrvajanmani | ihāgato hi putratvaṃ tava pārthivasattama || 7.51.20 ||
translation: इति thus, शप्तो cursed, महातेजा the greatly effulgent one, भृगुणा by Bhrigu, पूर्वजन्मनि in a previous birth, इहागतो has come here, हि indeed, पुत्रत्वं to sonship, तव your, पार्थिवसत्तम O best among kings,
explanation: The greatly effulgent one, who was cursed by Bhrigu in a previous birth, has indeed come here to be your son, O best among kings.

shloka_text: राम इत्यभिविख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु मानद । तत्फलं प्राप्स्यते चापि भृगुशापकृतं महत् ।। 7.51.21 ।।
transliteration: rāma ityabhivikhyātastriṣu lokeṣu mānada | tatphalaṃ prāpsyate cāpi bhṛguśāpakṛtaṃ mahat || 7.51.21 ||
translation: राम Rama, इत्यभिविख्यातस् thus renowned, त्रिषु in the three, लोकेषु worlds, मानद O giver of honor, तत्फलं that fruit/consequence, प्राप्स्यते will obtain, च and, अपि also, भृगुशापकृतं caused by Bhrigu's curse, महत् great,
explanation: He will be renowned as Rama in the three worlds, O giver of honor, and will also obtain the great consequence caused by Bhrigu's curse.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायाः पती रामो दीर्घकालं भविष्यति । सुखिनश्च समृद्धाश्च भविष्यन्त्यस्य ये ऽनुगाः ।। 7.51.22 ।।
transliteration: ayodhyāyāḥ patī rāmo dīrghakālaṃ bhaviṣyati | sukhinaśca samṛddhāśca bhaviṣyantyasya ye 'nugāḥ || 7.51.22 ||
translation: अयोध्यायाः of Ayodhya, पती the lord, रामो Rama, दीर्घकालं for a long time, भविष्यति will be, सुखिनश्च and happy, समृद्धाश्च and prosperous, भविष्यन्ति will be, अस्य his, ये who, अनुगाः followers,
explanation: Rama will be the lord of Ayodhya for a long time, and his followers will be happy and prosperous.

shloka_text: दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च । रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति ।। 7.51.23 ।।
transliteration: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca | rāmo rājyamupāsitvā brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyati || 7.51.23 ||
translation: दश ten, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, दश ten, वर्षशतानि hundreds of years, च and, रामो Rama, राज्यम् the kingdom, उपासित्वा having ruled, ब्रह्मलोकं to the world of Brahma, गमिष्यति will go,
explanation: Rama, having ruled the kingdom for eleven thousand years, will then go to the world of Brahma.

shloka_text: समृद्धैश्चाश्वमेधैश्च इष्ट्वा परमदुर्जयः । राजवंशांश्च बहुशो बहून्संस्थापयिष्यति ।। 7.51.24 ।।
transliteration: samṛddhaiścāśvamedhaiśca iṣṭvā paramadurjayaḥ | rājavaṃśāṃśca bahuśo bahūnsaṃsthāpayiṣyati || 7.51.24 ||
translation: समृद्धैश्च and with prosperous, अश्वमेधैश्च and with Ashwamedha sacrifices, इष्ट्वा having performed sacrifices, परमदुर्जयः extremely unconquerable, राजवंशांश्च and royal lineages, बहुशो many times, बहून् many, संस्थापयिष्यति will establish,
explanation: The extremely unconquerable Rama, having performed many prosperous Ashwamedha sacrifices, will establish many royal lineages in various places.

shloka_text: द्वौ पुत्रौ तु भविष्येते सीतायां राघवस्य तु । अन्यत्र न त्वयोध्यायां सत्यमेतन्नसंशयः ।। 7.51.25 ।।
transliteration: dvau putrau tu bhaviṣyete sītāyāṃ rāghavasya tu | anyatra na tvayodhyāyāṃ satyametannasaṃśayaḥ || 7.51.25 ||
translation: द्वौ two, पुत्रौ sons, तु indeed, भविष्येते will be born, सीतायां in Sita, राघवस्य of Rama, तु indeed, अन्यत्र elsewhere, न not, त्वयोध्यायां in Ayodhya, सत्यम् truth, एतत् this, न no, संशयः doubt
explanation: Two sons will indeed be born to Rama through Sita, but they will be born elsewhere and not in Ayodhya; this is the truth, without a doubt.

shloka_text: सीतायाश्च ततः पुत्रावभिषेक्ष्यति राघवः ।। 7.51.26 ।।
transliteration: sītāyāśca tataḥ putrāvabhiṣekṣyati rāghavaḥ || 7.51.26 ||
translation: सीतायाश्च and of Sita, ततः then, पुत्रौ two sons, अभिषेक्ष्यति will anoint, राघवः Rama
explanation: Then, Rama will anoint Sita's two sons (as kings).

shloka_text: स सर्वमखिलं राज्ञो वंशस्याह गतागतम् । आख्याय सुमहातेजास्तूष्णीमासीन्महामुनिः ।। 7.51.27 ।।
transliteration: sa sarvamakhilaṃ rājño vaṃśasyāha gatāgatam | ākhyāya sumahātejāstūṣṇīmāsīnmahāmuniḥ || 7.51.27 ||
translation: स he, सर्वम् all, अखिलम् complete, राज्ञः of the king, वंशस्य of the lineage, आह told, गतागतम् past and future, आख्याय having narrated, सुमहातेजाः the greatly effulgent one, तूष्णीम् silent, आसीत् became, महामुनिः the great sage
explanation: Having narrated the entire past and future of the king's lineage, the greatly effulgent great sage then became silent.

shloka_text: तूष्णीम्भूते तदा तस्मिन्राजा दशरथो मुनौ । अभिवाद्य महात्मानौ पुनरायात्पुरोत्तमम् ।। 7.51.28 ।।
transliteration: tūṣṇīmbhūte tadā tasminrājā daśaratho munau | abhivādya mahātmānau punarāyātpurottamam || 7.51.28 ||
translation: तूष्णीम्भूते when silent became, तदा then, तस्मिन् that, राजा king, दशरथः Dasharatha, मुनौ sage, अभिवाद्य having saluted, महात्मानौ the two great souls, पुनरायात् returned again, पुरोत्तमम् to the best of cities
explanation: When that sage became silent, King Dasharatha, having saluted the great sage, then returned to the excellent city (Ayodhya).

shloka_text: एतद्वचो मया तत्र मुनिना व्याहृतं पुरा । श्रुतं हृदि च निक्षिप्तं नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति ।। 7.51.29 ।।
transliteration: etadvaco mayā tatra muninā vyāhṛtaṃ purā | śrutaṃ hṛdi ca nikṣiptaṃ nānyathā tadbhaviṣyati || 7.51.29 ||
translation: एतत् this, वचः word, मया by me, तत्र there, मुनिना by the sage, व्याहृतम् spoken, पुरा formerly, श्रुतम् heard, हृदि in the heart, च and, निक्षिप्तम् placed, न not, अन्यथा otherwise, तत् that, भविष्यति will be
explanation: This word, spoken by the sage there formerly, was heard by me and placed in my heart, and it will not be otherwise.

shloka_text: एवं गते न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि राघव । सीतार्थे राघवार्थे वा दृढो भव नरोत्तम ।। 7.51.30 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ gate na santāpaṃ kartumarhasi rāghava | sītārthe rāghavārthe vā dṛḍho bhava narottama || 7.51.30 ||
translation: एवं thus, गते having happened, न not, सन्तापं sorrow, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought, राघव O Raghava, सीतार्थे for Sita's sake, राघवार्थे for Raghava's sake, वा or, दृढो firm, भव be, नरोत्तम O best among men,
explanation: O Raghava, since things have come to this pass, you should not grieve, but rather be resolute, whether for Sita's sake or for your own, O best among men.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु व्याहृतं वाक्यं सूतस्य परमाद्भुतम् । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.51.31 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ sūtasya paramādbhutam | praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt || 7.51.31 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, व्याहृतं spoken, वाक्यं word, सूतस्य of the charioteer, परमाद्भुतम् exceedingly wonderful, प्रहर्षम् joy, अतुलं incomparable, लेभे obtained, साधु excellent, साधु excellent, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् he said,
explanation: Having heard the charioteer's exceedingly wonderful words, he felt incomparable joy and exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent!"

shloka_text: ततः संवदतोरेवं सूतलक्ष्मणयोः पथि । अस्तमर्के गते वासं केशिन्यां तावथोषतुः ।। 7.51.32 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ saṃvadatorevaṃ sūtalakṣmaṇayoḥ pathi | astamarke gate vāsaṃ keśinyāṃ tāvathoṣatuḥ || 7.51.32 ||
translation: ततः then, संवदतोरेवं while thus conversing, सूतलक्ष्मणयोः of the charioteer and Lakshmana, पथि on the path, अस्तम् setting, अर्के the sun, गते having gone, वासम् dwelling, केशिन्यां in Keshini, तावथ then they two, उषतुः stayed,
explanation: Then, as the charioteer and Lakshmana were conversing on the path, the sun set, and they stayed in Keshini for the night. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 51 ।। Thus ends the fifty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तत्र तां रजनीमुष्य केशिन्यां रघुनन्दनः । प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय लक्ष्मणः प्रययौ तदा ।। 7.52.1 ।।
transliteration: tatra tāṃ rajanīmuṣya keśinyāṃ raghunandanaḥ | prabhāte punarutthāya lakṣmaṇaḥ prayayau tadā || 7.52.1 ||
translation: तत्र there, तां that, रजनीम् night, उष्य having stayed, केशिन्यां in Keshini, रघुनन्दनः the delight of the Raghus, प्रभाते in the morning, पुनरुत्थाय having risen again, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, प्रययौ departed, तदा then,
explanation: Having stayed that night in Keshini, Lakshmana, the delight of the Raghus, rose again in the morning and then departed.
comments: Returned to Ayodhya, Lakshmana grasps Rama's feet and reports that he has left Sita at Valmiki's hermitage -- he consoles his grieving brother with the truth that all unions end in separation and that the wise are not bewildered by such sorrow -- comforted by his counsel, Rama thanks him.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते प्रविवेश महारथः । अयोध्यां रत्नसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम् ।। 7.52.2 ।।
transliteration: tato 'rdhadivase prāpte praviveśa mahārathaḥ | ayodhyāṃ ratnasampūrṇāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām || 7.52.2 ||
translation: ततः then, अर्धदिवसे at midday, प्राप्ते having arrived, प्रविवेश he entered, महारथः the great warrior, अयोध्यां Ayodhya, रत्नसम्पूर्णां full of jewels, हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम् filled with happy and well-nourished people,
explanation: Then, at midday, the great warrior Lakshmana entered Ayodhya, which was full of jewels and teeming with happy and well-nourished people.

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु परं दैन्यं जगाम सुमहामतिः । रामपादौ समासाद्य वक्ष्यामि किमहं गतः ।। 7.52.3 ।।
transliteration: saumitristu paraṃ dainyaṃ jagāma sumahāmatiḥ | rāmapādau samāsādya vakṣyāmi kimahaṃ gataḥ || 7.52.3 ||
translation: सौमित्रिस्तु Saumitri (Lakshmana) indeed, परं extreme, दैन्यं distress, जगाम experienced, सुमहामतिः the very intelligent one. रामपादौ Rama's feet, समासाद्य having approached, वक्ष्यामि shall I say, किम् what, अहम् I, गतः having gone?
explanation: The highly intelligent Lakshmana was overcome with extreme distress, wondering what he would say to Rama upon reaching his feet.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं चिन्तयानस्य भवनं शशिसन्निभम् । रामस्य परमोदारं पुरस्तान्समदृश्यत ।। 7.52.4 ।।
transliteration: tasyaivaṃ cintayānasya bhavanaṃ śaśisannibham | rāmasya paramodāraṃ purastānsamadṛśyata || 7.52.4 ||
translation: तस्य his, एवम् thus, चिन्तयानस्य while thinking, भवनं palace, शशिसन्निभम् moon-like, रामस्य Rama's, परमोदारम् most magnificent, पुरस्तात् in front, समदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: As he was thus contemplating, Rama's most magnificent palace, shining like the moon, appeared before him.

shloka_text: राज्ञस्तु भवनद्वारि सो ऽवतीर्य रथोत्तमात् । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमनाः प्रविवेशानिवारितः ।। 7.52.5 ।।
transliteration: rājñastu bhavanadvāri so 'vatīrya rathottamāt | avāṅmukho dīnamanāḥ praviveśānivāritaḥ || 7.52.5 ||
translation: राज्ञः of the king, तु indeed, भवनद्वारि at the palace gate, सः he, अवतीर्य having alighted, रथोत्तमात् from the excellent chariot, अवाङ्मुखः with downcast face, दीनमनाः with a sorrowful mind, प्रविवेश entered, अनिवारितः unhindered.
explanation: At the king's palace gate, he alighted from his excellent chariot and, with a downcast face and sorrowful mind, entered unhindered.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा राघवं दीनमासीनं परमासने । नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां ददर्शाग्रजमग्रतः ।। 7.52.6 ।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṃ dīnamāsīnaṃ paramāsane | netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāṃ dadarśāgrajamagrataḥ || 7.52.6 ||
translation: सः he, दृष्ट्वा having seen, राघवम् Rama, दीनम् distressed, आसीनम् seated, परमासने on the excellent seat, नेत्राभ्याम् with eyes, अश्रुपूर्णाभ्याम् filled with tears, ददर्श saw, अग्रजम् his elder brother, अग्रतः in front.
explanation: He saw Rama, his elder brother, seated on an excellent seat in front of him, looking distressed, and his own eyes filled with tears.

shloka_text: जग्राह चरणौ तस्य लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । उवाच दीनया वाचा प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः ।। 7.52.7 ।।
transliteration: jagrāha caraṇau tasya lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ | uvāca dīnayā vācā prāñjaliḥ susamāhitaḥ || 7.52.7 ||
translation: जग्राह grasped, चरणौ feet, तस्य his, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, दीनचेतनः with a sorrowful mind, उवाच spoke, दीनया with a humble, वाचा voice, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, सुसमाहितः very composed.
explanation: Lakshmana, with a sorrowful mind, grasped Rama's feet and, with folded hands and a very composed yet humble voice, began to speak.

shloka_text: आर्यस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम् । गङ्गातीरे यथोद्दिष्टे वाल्मीकेराश्रमे शुचौ ।। 7.52.8 ।।
transliteration: āryasyājñāṃ puraskṛtya visṛjya janakātmajām | gaṅgātīre yathoddiṣṭe vālmīkerāśrame śucau || 7.52.8 ||
translation: आर्यस्य your, आज्ञाम् command, पुरस्कृत्य having followed, विसृज्य having left, जनकात्मजाम् Janaka's daughter, गङ्गातीरे on the bank of the Ganga, यथोद्दिष्टे as instructed, वाल्मीकेः of Valmiki, आश्रमे in the hermitage, शुचौ pure,
explanation: Having followed your command, I left Janaka's daughter on the pure bank of the Ganga, in Valmiki's hermitage as instructed.

shloka_text: तत्र तां च शुभाचारामाश्रमान्ते यशस्विनीम् । पुनरप्यागतो वीर पादमूलमुपासितुम् ।। 7.52.9 ।।
transliteration: tatra tāṃ ca śubhācārāmāśramānte yaśasvinīm | punarapyāgato vīra pādamūlamupāsitum || 7.52.9 ||
translation: तत्र there, ताम् her, च and, शुभाचाराम् of auspicious conduct, आश्रमान्ते at the edge of the hermitage, यशस्विनीम् glorious, पुनरपि again, आगतः I have come, वीर O hero, पादमूलम् at your feet, उपासितुम् to serve,
explanation: O hero, I have returned to serve at your feet, having left her, who is of auspicious conduct and glorious, there at the edge of the hermitage.

shloka_text: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र कालस्य गतिरीदृशी । त्वद्विधा न हि शोचन्ति बुद्धिमन्तो मनस्विनः ।। 7.52.10 ।।
transliteration: mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra kālasya gatirīdṛśī | tvadvidhā na hi śocanti buddhimanto manasvinaḥ || 7.52.10 ||
translation: मा शुचः do not grieve, पुरुषव्याघ्र O tiger among men, कालस्य of time, गतिः the course, ईदृशी such, त्वद्विधाः those like you, न हि certainly not, शोचन्ति grieve, बुद्धिमन्तः intelligent ones, मनस्विनः wise ones,
explanation: O tiger among men, do not grieve, for such is the course of time, and intelligent, high-minded individuals like you certainly do not lament.

shloka_text: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ।। 7.52.11 ।।
transliteration: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ | saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam || 7.52.11 ||
translation: सर्वे all, क्षयान्ताः ending in decay, निचयाः accumulations, पतनान्ताः ending in fall, समुच्छ्रयाः elevations, संयोगाः unions, विप्रयोगान्ताः ending in separation, मरणान्तम् ending in death, च and, जीवितम् life,
explanation: All accumulations end in decay, all elevations end in a fall, all unions end in separation, and life itself ends in death.

shloka_text: तस्मात्पुत्रेषु दारेषु मित्रेषु च धनेषु च । नातिप्रसङ्गः कर्तव्यो विप्रयोगो हि तैर्ध्रुवम् ।। 7.52.12 ।।
transliteration: tasmātputreṣu dāreṣu mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca | nātiprasaṅgaḥ kartavyo viprayogo hi tairdhruvam || 7.52.12 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, पुत्रेषु in sons, दारेषु in wives, मित्रेषु in friends, च and, धनेषु in wealth, च and, न अतिप्रसङ्गः no excessive attachment, कर्तव्यः should be done, विप्रयोगः separation, हि indeed, तैः from them, ध्रुवम् certain,
explanation: Therefore, one should not have excessive attachment to sons, wives, friends, or wealth, for separation from them is indeed inevitable.

shloka_text: शक्तस्त्वमात्मना ऽ ऽत्मानं विनेतुं मनसैव हि । लोकान्सर्वांश्च काकुत्स्थ किं पुनः शोकमात्मनः ।। 7.52.13 ।।
transliteration: śaktastvamātmanā ' 'tmānaṃ vinetuṃ manasaiva hi | lokānsarvāṃśca kākutstha kiṃ punaḥ śokamātmanaḥ || 7.52.13 ||
translation: शक्तः capable, त्वम् you, आत्मना by yourself, आत्मानम् your own self, विनेतुम् to control, मनसा by mind, एव indeed, हि surely, लोकान् worlds, सर्वान् all, च and, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, किम् पुनः what then, शोकम् sorrow, आत्मनः your own.
explanation: O Kakutstha, you are surely capable of controlling your own self and indeed all worlds by your mind, so how much more easily can you control your own sorrow?

shloka_text: नेदृशेषु विमुह्यन्ति त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभाः । अपवादः स किल ते पुनरेष्यति राघव ।। 7.52.14 ।।
transliteration: nedṛśeṣu vimuhyanti tvadvidhāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ | apavādaḥ sa kila te punareṣyati rāghava || 7.52.14 ||
translation: न not, ईदृशेषु in such matters, विमुह्यन्ति become bewildered, त्वद्विधाः those like you, पुरुषर्षभाः best among men, अपवादः blame, सः that, किल indeed, ते to you, पुनः again, एष्यति will come, राघव O Raghava.
explanation: Best among men like you do not become bewildered in such situations, and indeed, O Raghava, that very blame will come upon you again.

shloka_text: यदर्थं मैथिली त्यक्ता अपवादभयान्नृप । सो ऽपवादः पुरे राजन्भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.52.15 ।।
transliteration: yadarthaṃ maithilī tyaktā apavādabhayānnṛpa | so 'pavādaḥ pure rājanbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.52.15 ||
translation: यदर्थम् for which reason, मैथिली Maithili, त्यक्ता abandoned, अपवादभयात् from fear of blame, नृप O King, सः that, अपवादः blame, पुरे in the city, राजन् O King, भविष्यति will be, न संशयः no doubt.
explanation: O King, that very blame for which Maithili was abandoned out of fear of scandal will undoubtedly arise again among the people in the city.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धैर्येण सुसमाहितः । त्यजैनां दुर्बलां बुद्धिं सन्तापं मा कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.52.16 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla dhairyeṇa susamāhitaḥ | tyajaināṃ durbalāṃ buddhiṃ santāpaṃ mā kuruṣva ha || 7.52.16 ||
translation: सः such, त्वम् you, पुरुषशार्दूल O best of men, धैर्येण with fortitude, सुसमाहितः well-composed, त्यज abandon, एनाम् this, दुर्बलाम् weak, बुद्धिम् thought, सन्तापम् grief, मा कुरुष्व do not make, ह indeed.
explanation: O best of men, you, being well-composed with fortitude, should abandon this weak thought and indeed do not give in to grief.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः स काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । उवाच परया प्रीत्या सौमित्रिं मित्रवत्सलः ।। 7.52.17 ।।
transliteration: evamuktaḥ sa kākutstho lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā | uvāca parayā prītyā saumitriṃ mitravatsalaḥ || 7.52.17 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, सः that, काकुत्स्थः Kakutstha, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, महात्मना by the great-souled one, उवाच spoke, परया with great, प्रीत्या affection, सौमित्रिम् to Saumitri, मित्रवत्सलः affectionate towards friends.
explanation: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakshmana, that Kakutstha, who was affectionate towards his friends, spoke to Saumitri with great affection.

shloka_text: एवमेतन्नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण । परितोषश्च मे वीर मम कार्यानुशासने ।। 7.52.18 ।।
transliteration: evametannaraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa | paritoṣaśca me vīra mama kāryānuśāsane || 7.52.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, एतत् this, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, यथा as, वदसि you speak, लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, परितोषः satisfaction, च and, मे my, वीर O hero, मम my, कार्यानुशासने in the instruction of duty.
explanation: O best among men, Lakshmana, this is indeed as you say, and I am greatly satisfied, O hero, with your counsel regarding my duty.

shloka_text: निवृत्तिश्चागता सौम्य सन्तापश्च निराकृतः । भवद्वाक्यैः सुरुचिरैरनुनीतो ऽस्मि लक्ष्मण ।। 7.52.19 ।।
transliteration: nivṛttiścāgatā saumya santāpaśca nirākṛtaḥ | bhavadvākyaiḥ surucirairanunīto 'smi lakṣmaṇa || 7.52.19 ||
translation: निवृत्तिः cessation, च and, आगता has come, सौम्य O gentle one, सन्तापः sorrow, च and, निराकृतः removed, भवद्वाक्यैः by your words, सुरुचिरैः very pleasing, अनुनीतः अस्मि I have been comforted, लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana.
explanation: O gentle Lakshmana, relief has come, and my sorrow has been dispelled; I have been comforted by your very pleasing words. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 52 ।। Thus ends the fifty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं निशम्य परमाद्भुतम् । सुप्रीतश्चाभवद्रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.53.1 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya tu tadvākyaṃ niśamya paramādbhutam | suprītaścābhavadrāmo vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.53.1 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणस्य of Lakshmana, तु indeed, तत् that, वाक्यम् word, निशम्य having heard, परमाद्भुतम् exceedingly wonderful, सुप्रीतः very pleased, च and, अभवत् became, रामः Rama, वाक्यम् word, एतत् this, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Having heard that exceedingly wonderful speech of Lakshmana, Rama became very pleased and indeed spoke these words.
comments: Troubled that his neglect of public affairs is itself a sin, Rama bids Lakshmana summon the officers and petitioners -- he tells the cautionary tale of King Nrga, who for failing to give audience to two brahmins disputing over a gift-cow was cursed to live as a lizard until a later age -- and he charges Lakshmana to attend to every suitor.

shloka_text: दुर्लभस्त्वीदृशो बन्धुरस्मिन्काले विशेषतः । यादृशस्त्वं महाबुद्धेर्मम सौम्य मनो ऽनुगः ।। 7.53.2 ।।
transliteration: durlabhastvīdṛśo bandhurasminkāle viśeṣataḥ | yādṛśastvaṃ mahābuddhermama saumya mano 'nugaḥ || 7.53.2 ||
translation: दुर्लभः rare, तु indeed, ईदृशः such, बन्धुः a kinsman, अस्मिन् काले in this time, विशेषतः especially, यादृशः such as, त्वम् you, महाबुद्धेः O greatly intelligent one, मम my, सौम्य O gentle one, मनः अनुगः following the mind.
explanation: Indeed, such a kinsman as you, O greatly intelligent and gentle one, who follows my mind, is rare to find, especially in these times.

shloka_text: यच्च मे हृदये किञ्चिद्वर्तते शुभलक्षण । तन्निशामय च श्रुत्वा कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.53.3 ।।
transliteration: yacca me hṛdaye kiñcidvartate śubhalakṣaṇa | tanniśāmaya ca śrutvā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama || 7.53.3 ||
translation: यत् what, च and, मे my, हृदये in the heart, किञ्चित् something, वर्तते exists, शुभलक्षण O one with auspicious marks, तत् that, निशामय listen carefully, च and, श्रुत्वा having heard, कुरुष्व do, वचनम् command, मम my.
explanation: O one with auspicious marks, listen carefully to what is in my heart, and having heard it, carry out my command.

shloka_text: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्यं पौरजनस्य वै । अकुर्वाणस्य सौमित्रे तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति ।। 7.53.4 ।।
transliteration: catvāro divasāḥ saumya kāryaṃ paurajanasya vai | akurvāṇasya saumitre tanme marmāṇi kṛntati || 7.53.4 ||
translation: चत्वारो four, दिवसाः days, सौम्य O gentle one, कार्यं work, पौरजनस्य of the citizens, वै indeed, अकुर्वाणस्य of one who neglects, सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, तत् that, मे my, मर्माणि vital parts, कृन्तति cuts.
explanation: O gentle Lakshmana, the neglect of the citizens' work for four days indeed pierces my vital parts.

shloka_text: आहूयन्तां प्रकृतयः पुरोधा मन्त्रिणस्तथा । कार्यार्थिनश्च पुरुषाः स्त्रियश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.53.5 ।।
transliteration: āhūyantāṃ prakṛtayaḥ purodhā mantriṇastathā | kāryārthinaśca puruṣāḥ striyaśca puruṣarṣabha || 7.53.5 ||
translation: आहूयन्तां let them be called, प्रकृतयः the principal officers, पुरोधा the chief priest, मन्त्रिणः the ministers, तथा and, कार्यार्थिनः those seeking justice, च and, पुरुषाः men, स्त्रियः women, च and, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O best among men, let the principal officers, the chief priest, the ministers, and also the men and women seeking justice be summoned.

shloka_text: पौरकार्याणि यो राजा न करोति दिने दिने । संवृते नरके घोरे पतितो नात्र संशयः ।। 7.53.6 ।।
transliteration: paurakāryāṇi yo rājā na karoti dine dine | saṃvṛte narake ghore patito nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7.53.6 ||
translation: पौरकार्याणि the affairs of the citizens, यः who, राजा king, न not, करोति does, दिने दिने day by day, संवृते in an enclosed, नरके hell, घोरे terrible, पतितः fallen, न not, अत्र here, संशयः doubt.
explanation: There is no doubt that a king who does not attend to the affairs of his citizens daily falls into a terrible, enclosed hell.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि पुरा राजा नृगो नाम महायशाः । बभूव पृथिवीपालो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाक् शुचिः ।। 7.53.7 ।।
transliteration: śrūyate hi purā rājā nṛgo nāma mahāyaśāḥ | babhūva pṛthivīpālo brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ || 7.53.7 ||
translation: श्रूयते it is heard, हि indeed, पुरा formerly, राजा king, नृगः Nṛga, नाम named, महायशाः very famous, बभूव was, पृथिवीपालः a protector of the earth, ब्रह्मण्यः devoted to Brahmins, सत्यवाक् truthful, शुचिः pure.
explanation: Indeed, it is heard that formerly there was a very famous king named Nṛga, a protector of the earth, who was devoted to Brahmins, truthful, and pure.

shloka_text: स कदाचिद्गवां कोटीः सवत्साः स्वर्णभूषिताः । नृदेवो भूमिदेवेभ्यः पुष्करेषु ददौ नृपः ।। 7.53.8 ।।
transliteration: sa kadācidgavāṃ koṭīḥ savatsāḥ svarṇabhūṣitāḥ | nṛdevo bhūmidevebhyaḥ puṣkareṣu dadau nṛpaḥ || 7.53.8 ||
translation: सः he, कदाचित् once, गवां of cows, कोटीः crores, सवत्साः with their calves, स्वर्णभूषिताः adorned with gold, नृदेवः the king, भूमिदेवेभ्यः to the Brahmins, पुष्करेषु at Pushkara, ददौ gave, नृपः the king.
explanation: That king, Nṛga, once at Pushkara, gave crores of cows, along with their calves and adorned with gold, to the Brahmins.

shloka_text: ततः सङ्गाद्गता धेनुः सवत्सा स्पर्शिता ऽनघ । ब्राह्मणस्याहिताग्नेश्च दरिद्रस्योञ्छवर्तिनः ।। 7.53.9 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ saṅgādgatā dhenuḥ savatsā sparśitā 'nagha | brāhmaṇasyāhitāgneśca daridrasyoñchavartinaḥ || 7.53.9 ||
translation: ततः then, सङ्गात् from association, गता went, धेनुः the cow, सवत्सा with its calf, स्पर्शिता touched/taken, अनघ O sinless one, ब्राह्मणस्य of a Brahmana, आहिताग्नेः who maintains sacred fires, च and, दरिद्रस्य of a poor man, उञ्छवर्तिनः who lives by gleaning,
explanation: O sinless one, then that cow with its calf, having come into contact, was taken by a poor Brahmana who maintained sacred fires and lived by gleaning.

shloka_text: स नष्टां गां क्षुधार्तो वै अन्विषंस्तत्र तत्र च । नापश्यत्सर्वराज्येषु संवत्सरगणान्बहून् ।। 7.53.10 ।।
transliteration: sa naṣṭāṃ gāṃ kṣudhārto vai anviṣaṃstatra tatra ca | nāpaśyatsarvarājyeṣu saṃvatsaragaṇānbahūn || 7.53.10 ||
translation: सः he, नष्टां lost, गां cow, क्षुधार्तः afflicted by hunger, वै indeed, अन्विषन् searching, तत्र तत्र here and there, च and, न not, अपश्यत् saw, सर्वराज्येषु in all kingdoms, संवत्सरगणान् groups of years, बहून् many,
explanation: Afflicted by hunger, he searched for his lost cow here and there in all kingdoms for many years but could not find it.

shloka_text: ततः कनखलं गत्वा जीर्णवत्सां निरामयाम् । ददर्श गां स्वकां धेनुं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने ।। 7.53.11 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kanakhalaṃ gatvā jīrṇavatsāṃ nirāmayām | dadarśa gāṃ svakāṃ dhenuṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane || 7.53.11 ||
translation: ततः then, कनखलं to Kanakhala, गत्वा having gone, जीर्णवत्सां whose calf was old, निरामयाम् healthy, ददर्श he saw, गां the cow, स्वकां his own, धेनुं cow, ब्राह्मणस्य of the Brahmana, निवेशने in the dwelling,
explanation: Then, having gone to Kanakhala, he saw his own cow, whose calf had grown old and was healthy, in the dwelling of the Brahmana.

shloka_text: अथ तां नामधेयेन स्वकेनोवाच स द्विजः । आगच्छ शबलेत्येवं सा तु शुश्राव गौः स्वरम् ।। 7.53.12 ।।
transliteration: atha tāṃ nāmadheyena svakenovāca sa dvijaḥ | āgaccha śabaletyevaṃ sā tu śuśrāva gauḥ svaram || 7.53.12 ||
translation: अथ then, तां her, नामधेयेन by name, स्वकेन his own, उवाच said, सः that, द्विजः Brahmana, आगच्छ come, शबलेति O Shabala, एवं thus, सा she, तु indeed, शुश्राव heard, गौः the cow, स्वरम् the voice,
explanation: Then that Brahmana called her by her own name, saying, "Come, Shabala!" and the cow indeed heard his voice.

shloka_text: तस्य तं स्वरमाज्ञाय क्षुधार्तस्य द्विजस्य वै । अन्वगात्पृष्ठतः सा गौर्गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम् ।। 7.53.13 ।।
transliteration: tasya taṃ svaramājñāya kṣudhārtasya dvijasya vai | anvagātpṛṣṭhataḥ sā gaurgacchantaṃ pāvakopamam || 7.53.13 ||
translation: तस्य his, तं that, स्वरं voice, आज्ञाय having recognized, क्षुधार्तस्य of the hungry, द्विजस्य Brahmana, वै indeed, अन्वगात् followed, पृष्ठतः from behind, सा she, गौः the cow, गच्छन्तं him who was going, पावकोपमम् like fire,
explanation: Having recognized the voice of that hungry Brahmana, the cow indeed followed him from behind as he, radiant like fire, walked away.

shloka_text: यो ऽपि पालयते विप्रः सो ऽपि गामन्वगाद्द्रुतम् । गत्वा तमृषिमाचष्ट मम गौरिति सत्वरम् ।। 7.53.14 ।।
transliteration: yo 'pi pālayate vipraḥ so 'pi gāmanvagāddrutam | gatvā tamṛṣimācaṣṭa mama gauriti satvaram || 7.53.14 ||
translation: यः who, अपि also, पालयते protects, विप्रः brahmin, सः he, अपि also, गाम् cow, अन्वगात् followed, द्रुतम् quickly, गत्वा having gone, तम् that, ऋषिम् sage, आचष्ट told, मम my, गौः cow, इति thus, सत्वरम् quickly.
explanation: The brahmin who was tending the cow also quickly followed it, and having gone, swiftly told that sage, "This is my cow."

shloka_text: स्पर्शिता राजसिंहेन मम दत्ता नृगेण ह । तयोर्ब्राह्मणयोर्वादो महानासीद्विपश्चितोः ।। 7.53.15 ।।
transliteration: sparśitā rājasiṃhena mama dattā nṛgeṇa ha | tayorbrāhmaṇayorvādo mahānāsīdvipaścitoḥ || 7.53.15 ||
translation: स्पर्शिता touched, राजसिंहेन by the lion among kings, मम my, दत्ता given, नृगेण by Nṛga, ह indeed, तयोः of those two, ब्राह्मणयोः brahmins, वादः dispute, महान् great, आसीत् was, विपश्चितोः learned.
explanation: One brahmin claimed the cow was touched by the king, while the other insisted it was given to him by Nṛga, leading to a great dispute between the two learned brahmins.

shloka_text: विवदन्तौ ततो ऽन्योन्यं दातारमभिजग्मतुः । तौ राजभवनद्वारि न प्राप्तौ नृगशासनम् ।। 7.53.16 ।।
transliteration: vivadantau tato 'nyonyaṃ dātāramabhijagmatuḥ | tau rājabhavanadvāri na prāptau nṛgaśāsanam || 7.53.16 ||
translation: विवदन्तौ disputing, ततः then, अन्योन्यम् each other, दातारम् the giver, अभिजग्मतुः approached, तौ those two, राजभवनद्वारि at the palace gate, न not, प्राप्तौ obtained, नृगशासनम् Nṛga's command.
explanation: Then, disputing with each other, they approached the giver (King Nṛga), but those two did not meet King Nṛga at the palace gate.

shloka_text: अहोरात्राण्यनेकानि वसन्तौ क्रोधमीयतुः । ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ तावुभौ द्विजसत्तमौ ।। क्रुद्धौ परमसम्प्राप्तौ वाक्यं घोराभिसंहितम् ।। 7.53.17 ।।
transliteration: ahorātrāṇyanekāni vasantau krodhamīyatuḥ | ūcatuśca mahātmānau tāvubhau dvijasattamau || kruddhau paramasamprāptau vākyaṃ ghorābhisaṃhitam || 7.53.17 ||
translation: अहोरात्राणि days and nights, अनेकानि many, वसन्तौ staying, क्रोधम् anger, ईयतुः reached, ऊचतुः spoke, च and, महात्मानौ great-souled ones, तौ those, उभौ both, द्विजसत्तमौ best among brahmins, क्रुद्धौ angry, परमसम्प्राप्तौ having reached the highest, वाक्यम् words, घोराभिसंहितम् terrible and connected.
explanation: After staying for many days and nights, those two great-souled and best among brahmins became exceedingly angry and spoke terrible words filled with a curse.

shloka_text: अर्थिनां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं यस्मात्त्वं नैषि दर्शनम् । अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां कृकलासो भविष्यसि ।। 7.53.18 ।।
transliteration: arthināṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ yasmāttvaṃ naiṣi darśanam | adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kṛkalāso bhaviṣyasi || 7.53.18 ||
translation: अर्थिनाम् of petitioners, कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थम् for the accomplishment of their purpose, यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, न not, एषि go, दर्शनम् sight, अदृश्यः invisible, सर्वभूतानाम् to all beings, कृकलासः a chameleon, भविष्यसि you will become.
explanation: Because you do not grant an audience to petitioners for the accomplishment of their purpose, you shall become a chameleon, invisible to all beings.

shloka_text: बहुवर्षसहस्राणि बहुवर्षशतानि च । श्वभ्रे ऽस्मिन् कृकलासो वै दीर्घकालं वसिष्यसि ।। 7.53.19 ।।
transliteration: bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi bahuvarṣaśatāni ca | śvabhre 'smin kṛkalāso vai dīrghakālaṃ vasiṣyasi || 7.53.19 ||
translation: बहुवर्षसहस्राणि many thousands of years, बहुवर्षशतानि many hundreds of years, च and, श्वभ्रे in this pit, अस्मिन् this, कृकलासो a chameleon, वै indeed, दीर्घकालं for a long time, वसिष्यसि you will reside.
explanation: For many thousands and hundreds of years, you will indeed reside in this pit as a chameleon for a long duration.

shloka_text: उत्पत्स्यते हि लोके ऽस्मिन्यदूनां कीर्तिवर्धनः । वासुदेव इति ख्यातो विष्णुः पुरुषविग्रहः ।। 7.53.20 ।।
transliteration: utpatsyate hi loke 'sminyadūnāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ | vāsudeva iti khyāto viṣṇuḥ puruṣavigrahaḥ || 7.53.20 ||
translation: उत्पत्स्यते will be born, हि indeed, लोके in the world, अस्मिन् this, यदूनां of the Yadus, कीर्तिवर्धनः increaser of fame, वासुदेव Vasudeva, इति thus named, ख्यातो renowned, विष्णुः Vishnu, पुरुषविग्रहः having a human form.
explanation: Indeed, in this world, Vishnu, renowned as Vasudeva, the increaser of the Yadus' glory and having a human form, will be born.

shloka_text: स ते मोक्षयिता राजंस्तस्माच्छापाद्भविष्यसि । कृता च तेन कालेन निष्कृतिस्ते भविष्यति ।। 7.53.21 ।।
transliteration: sa te mokṣayitā rājaṃstasmācchāpādbhaviṣyasi | kṛtā ca tena kālena niṣkṛtiste bhaviṣyati || 7.53.21 ||
translation: स He, ते your, मोक्षयिता liberator, राजंस् O King, तस्मात् from that, शापात् curse, भविष्यसि you will be, कृता done, च and, तेन by him, कालेन by time, निष्कृतिस् expiation, ते your, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: O King, he will be your liberator from that curse, and by him, your expiation will be accomplished in due course.

shloka_text: भारावतरणार्थं हि नरनारायणावुभौ । उत्पत्स्येते महावीर्यौ कलौ युग उपस्थिते ।। 7.53.22 ।।
transliteration: bhārāvataraṇārthaṃ hi naranārāyaṇāvubhau | utpatsyete mahāvīryau kalau yuga upasthite || 7.53.22 ||
translation: भारावतरणार्थं for the purpose of alleviating the burden, हि indeed, नरनारायणौ Nara and Narayana, उभौ both, उत्पत्स्येते will be born, महावीर्यौ greatly powerful, कलौ in the Kali, युगे in the age, उपस्थिते when it has arrived.
explanation: Indeed, both Nara and Narayana, greatly powerful, will be born for the purpose of alleviating the earth's burden when the Kali Yuga has arrived.

shloka_text: एवं तौ शापमुत्सृज्य ब्राह्मणौ विगतज्वरौ । तां गां हि दुर्बलां वृद्धां ददतुर्ब्राह्मणाय वै ।। 7.53.23 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ tau śāpamutsṛjya brāhmaṇau vigatajvarau | tāṃ gāṃ hi durbalāṃ vṛddhāṃ dadaturbrāhmaṇāya vai || 7.53.23 ||
translation: एवं thus, तौ those two, शापम् curse, उत्सृज्य having uttered, ब्राह्मणौ the two Brahmins, विगतज्वरौ free from distress, तां that, गां cow, हि indeed, दुर्बलां weak, वृद्धां old, ददतुर् they gave, ब्राह्मणाय to a Brahmin, वै indeed.
explanation: Thus, having pronounced the curse, those two Brahmins, now free from distress, indeed gave that weak, old cow to a Brahmin.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुङ्क्ते सुदारुणम् ।। 7.53.24 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā taṃ śāpamupabhuṅkte sudāruṇam || 7.53.24 ||
translation: एवं thus, सः that, राजा king, तम् that, शापम् curse, उपभुङ्क्ते experiences, सुदारुणम् very terrible.
explanation: In this manner, that king experiences that very terrible curse.

shloka_text: कार्यार्थिनां विमर्दो हि राज्ञां दोषाय कल्पते । तच्छीघ्रं दर्शनं मह्यमभिवर्तन्तु कार्यिणः ।। 7.53.25 ।।
transliteration: kāryārthināṃ vimardo hi rājñāṃ doṣāya kalpate | tacchīghraṃ darśanaṃ mahyamabhivartantu kāryiṇaḥ || 7.53.25 ||
translation: कार्यार्थिनाम् of those seeking their purpose, विमर्दः crowding, हि indeed, राज्ञाम् for kings, दोषाय for harm, कल्पते leads to, तत् therefore, शीघ्रम् quickly, दर्शनम् audience, मह्यम् to me, अभिवर्तन्तु let them approach, कार्यिणः petitioners.
explanation: Indeed, the crowding of petitioners leads to harm for kings; therefore, let the petitioners quickly approach me for an audience.

shloka_text: सुकृतस्य हि कार्यस्य फलं नापैति पार्थिवः । तस्माद्गच्छ प्रतीक्षस्व सौमित्रे कार्यवाञ्जनः ।। 7.53.26 ।।
transliteration: sukṛtasya hi kāryasya phalaṃ nāpaiti pārthivaḥ | tasmādgaccha pratīkṣasva saumitre kāryavāñjanaḥ || 7.53.26 ||
translation: सुकृतस्य of a well-done, हि indeed, कार्यस्य of work, फलम् the fruit, न not, अपैति is lost, पार्थिवः O king, तस्मात् therefore, गच्छ go, प्रतीक्षस्व wait, सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, कार्यवान् one who has business, जनः person.
explanation: Indeed, the fruit of a well-done work is not lost, O king; therefore, O son of Sumitra, go and wait for any person who has business. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 53 ।। Thus ends the fifty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परमार्थवित् । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.54.1 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ paramārthavit | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ rāghavaṃ dīptatejasam || 7.54.1 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितम् the speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परमार्थवित् knower of the highest truth, उवाच spoke, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यम् words, राघवम् to Rama, दीप्ततेजसम् radiant with splendor.
explanation: Having heard Rama's speech, Lakshmana, who knew the highest truth, spoke words with folded hands to Rama, who was radiant with splendor.
comments: Lakshmana asks how King Nrga met his curse -- Rama recounts that Nrga, learning the brahmins had cursed and departed, consecrated his son Vasu, had pleasant caves prepared for his long ordeal, counselled his son on a Kshatriya's duty and the might of destiny, and then entered the well to live out the curse.

shloka_text: अल्पापराधे काकुत्स्थ द्विजाभ्यां शाप ईदृशः । महान्नृगस्य राजर्षेर्यमदण्ड इवापरः ।। 7.54.2 ।।
transliteration: alpāparādhe kākutstha dvijābhyāṃ śāpa īdṛśaḥ | mahānnṛgasya rājarṣeryamadaṇḍa ivāparaḥ || 7.54.2 ||
translation: अल्पापराधे for a small offense, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, शापः a curse, ईदृशः such, महान् severe, नृगस्य of Nṛga, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, यमदण्डः the punishment of Yama, इव like, अपरः another.
explanation: O Kakutstha, for a minor offense, such a severe curse was given by the two Brahmins, like another punishment from Yama for the royal sage Nṛga.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु पापसंयुक्तमात्मानं पुरषर्षभ । किमुवाच नृगो राजा द्विजौ क्रोधसमन्वितौ ।। 7.54.3 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu pāpasaṃyuktamātmānaṃ puraṣarṣabha | kimuvāca nṛgo rājā dvijau krodhasamanvitau || 7.54.3 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, पापसंयुक्तम् associated with sin, आत्मानम् himself, पुरषर्षभ O best of men, किम् what, उवाच did say, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, द्विजौ to the two Brahmins, क्रोधसमन्वितौ filled with anger.
explanation: O best of men, what did King Nṛga say to the two enraged Brahmins after hearing himself accused of sin?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । शृणु सौम्य यथा पूर्वं स राजा शापविक्षतः ।। 7.54.4 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāghavaḥ punarabravīt | śṛṇu saumya yathā pūrvaṃ sa rājā śāpavikṣataḥ || 7.54.4 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, राघवः Rama, पुनः again, अब्रवीत् said, शृणु listen, सौम्य O gentle one, यथा how, पूर्वम् previously, सः that, राजा king, शापविक्षतः afflicted by the curse.
explanation: When Lakshmana thus spoke, Rama again said, "O gentle one, listen to how that king was previously afflicted by the curse."

shloka_text: अथाध्वनि गतौ विप्रौ विज्ञाय स नृगस्तदा । आहूय मन्त्रिणः सर्वान्नैगमान्सपुरोधसः ।। 7.54.5 ।।
transliteration: athādhvani gatau viprau vijñāya sa nṛgastadā | āhūya mantriṇaḥ sarvānnaigamānsapurodhasaḥ || 7.54.5 ||
translation: अथ then, अध्वनि on the way, गतौ gone, विप्रौ the two Brahmins, विज्ञाय having known, सः that, नृगः Nṛga, तदा then, आहूय having summoned, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सर्वान् all, नैगमान् citizens, सपुरोधसः along with the priests.
explanation: Then, having understood that the two Brahmins had departed, King Nṛga summoned all his ministers, citizens, and priests.

shloka_text: तानुवाच नृगो राजा सर्वाश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा । दुःखेन सुसमाविष्टः श्रूयतां मे समाहितैः ।। 7.54.6 ।।
transliteration: tānuvāca nṛgo rājā sarvāśca prakṛtīstathā | duḥkhena susamāviṣṭaḥ śrūyatāṃ me samāhitaiḥ || 7.54.6 ||
translation: तान् to them, उवाच said, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, सर्वाः all, च and, प्रकृतीः subjects, तथा also, दुःखेन by sorrow, सुसमाविष्टः deeply afflicted, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, मे from me, समाहितैः by those who are attentive.
explanation: Deeply afflicted by sorrow, King Nṛga spoke to all of them, including his subjects, saying, "Let my words be heard by all of you with attention."

shloka_text: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव मम दत्त्वा महद्भयम् । गतौ त्रिभुवनं भद्रौ वायुभूतावनिन्दितौ ।। 7.54.7 ।।
transliteration: nāradaḥ parvataścaiva mama dattvā mahadbhayam | gatau tribhuvanaṃ bhadrau vāyubhūtāvaninditau || 7.54.7 ||
translation: नारदः Narada, पर्वतः Parvata, च and, एव indeed, मम to me, दत्त्वा having given, महत् great, भयम् fear, गतौ have gone, त्रिभुवनम् to the three worlds, भद्रौ the two noble ones, वायुभूतौ having become like wind, अनिन्दितौ the two blameless ones.
explanation: The noble and blameless Narada and Parvata, having instilled great fear in me, have indeed departed to the three worlds, swift as the wind.

shloka_text: कुमारो ऽयं वसुर्नाम स देवो ऽद्याभिषिच्यताम् । श्वभ्रं च यत्सुखस्पर्शं क्रियतां शिल्पिभिर्मम । यत्राहं सङ्क्षयिष्यामि शापं ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् ।। 7.54.8 ।।
transliteration: kumāro 'yaṃ vasurnāma sa devo 'dyābhiṣicyatām | śvabhraṃ ca yatsukhasparśaṃ kriyatāṃ śilpibhirmama | yatrāhaṃ saṅkṣayiṣyāmi śāpaṃ brāhmaṇaniḥsṛtam || 7.54.8 ||
translation: कुमारो अयम् this boy, वसुः नाम by name Vasu, सः he, देवः god, अद्य today, अभिषिच्यताम् let him be consecrated, श्वभ्रम् a pit/cave, च and, यत् which is, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, क्रियताम् let it be made, शिल्पिभिः by artisans, मम for me, यत्र where, अहम् I, सङ्क्षयिष्यामि will exhaust/destroy, शापम् the curse, ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् issued from a Brahmin.
explanation: Let this boy named Vasu be consecrated as a god today, and let artisans construct for me a pleasant cave where I can exhaust the curse issued by a Brahmin.

shloka_text: वर्षघ्नमेकं श्वभ्रं तु हिमघ्नमपरं तथा । ग्रीष्मघ्नं तु सुखस्पर्शमेकं कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः ।। 7.54.9 ।।
transliteration: varṣaghnamekaṃ śvabhraṃ tu himaghnamaparaṃ tathā | grīṣmaghnaṃ tu sukhasparśamekaṃ kurvantu śilpinaḥ || 7.54.9 ||
translation: वर्षघ्नम् rain-proof, एकम् one, श्वभ्रम् pit/cave, तु indeed, हिमघ्नम् cold-proof, अपरम् another, तथा similarly, ग्रीष्मघ्नम् summer-proof, तु and, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, एकम् one, कुर्वन्तु let them make, शिल्पिनः artisans.
explanation: The artisans should construct one cave that is rain-proof, another that is cold-proof, and a third, pleasant to touch, that is summer-proof.

shloka_text: फलवन्तश्च ये वृक्षाः पुष्पवत्यश्च या लताः । विरोप्यन्तां बहुविधाश्छायावन्तश्च गुल्मिनः ।। 7.54.10 ।।
transliteration: phalavantaśca ye vṛkṣāḥ puṣpavatyaśca yā latāḥ | viropyantāṃ bahuvidhāśchāyāvantaśca gulminaḥ || 7.54.10 ||
translation: फलवन्तः fruit-bearing, च and, ये which, वृक्षाः trees, पुष्पवत्यः flower-bearing, च and, या which, लताः creepers, विरोप्यन्ताम् let them be planted, बहुविधाः of many kinds, छायावन्तः shade-giving, च and, गुल्मिनः shrubs.
explanation: Let fruit-bearing trees, flowering creepers, and various kinds of shade-giving shrubs be planted.

shloka_text: क्रियतां रमणीयं च श्वभ्राणां सर्वतोदिशम् । सुखमत्र वसिष्यामि यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः ।। 7.54.11 ।।
transliteration: kriyatāṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ca śvabhrāṇāṃ sarvatodiśam | sukhamatra vasiṣyāmi yāvatkālasya paryayaḥ || 7.54.11 ||
translation: क्रियताम् let it be made, रमणीयम् beautiful, च and, श्वभ्राणाम् of the pits/caves, सर्वतोदिशम् in all directions, सुखम् comfortably, अत्र here, वसिष्यामि I will dwell, यावत् as long as, कालस्य of time, पर्ययः the change/end.
explanation: Let the surroundings of the caves be made beautiful in all directions, for I will dwell there comfortably until the end of my destined time.

shloka_text: पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि क्रियतां तेषु नित्यशः । परिवार्य यथा मे स्युरध्यर्धं योजनं तथा ।। 7.54.12 ।।
transliteration: puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni kriyatāṃ teṣu nityaśaḥ | parivārya yathā me syuradhyardhaṃ yojanaṃ tathā || 7.54.12 ||
translation: पुष्पाणि flowers, च and, सुगन्धीनि fragrant, क्रियताम् let them be placed/made, तेषु in them, नित्यशः always, परिवार्य surrounding, यथा so that, मे for me, स्युः they may be, अध्यर्धम् one and a half, योजनम् Yojana, तथा thus.
explanation: Let fragrant flowers always be placed in them, surrounding the area for me to a distance of one and a half Yojanas.

shloka_text: एवं कृत्वा विधानं स सन्दिदेश वसं तदा । धर्मनित्यः प्रजाः पुत्र क्षत्रधर्मेण पालय ।। 7.54.13 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ sa sandideśa vasaṃ tadā | dharmanityaḥ prajāḥ putra kṣatradharmeṇa pālaya || 7.54.13 ||
translation: एवं thus, कृत्वा having made, विधानं arrangement, स he, सन्दिदेश instructed, वसं O son, तदा then, धर्मनित्यः ever devoted to dharma, प्रजाः subjects, पुत्र O son, क्षत्रधर्मेण by the duty of a Kshatriya, पालय protect.
explanation: Having made this arrangement, the king then instructed his son, "O son, ever devoted to righteousness, protect your subjects according to the duty of a Kshatriya."

shloka_text: प्रत्यक्षं ते यथा शापो द्विजाभ्यां मयि पातितः । नरश्रेष्ठ सरोषाभ्यामपराधे ऽपि तादृशे ।। 7.54.14 ।।
transliteration: pratyakṣaṃ te yathā śāpo dvijābhyāṃ mayi pātitaḥ | naraśreṣṭha saroṣābhyāmaparādhe 'pi tādṛśe || 7.54.14 ||
translation: प्रत्यक्षं directly, ते by you, यथा how, शापो curse, द्विजाभ्यां by the two Brahmins, मयि upon me, पातितः cast, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, सरोषाभ्यां by the two angry ones, अपराधे in the offense, अपि even, तादृशे such.
explanation: O best among men, you yourself witnessed how a curse was inflicted upon me by the two angry Brahmins, even for such an offense.

shloka_text: मा कृथास्तनुसन्तापं मत्कृते ऽपि नरर्षभ । कृतान्तः कुशलः पुत्र येनास्मि व्यसनीकृतः ।। 7.54.15 ।।
transliteration: mā kṛthāstanusantāpaṃ matkṛte 'pi nararṣabha | kṛtāntaḥ kuśalaḥ putra yenāsmi vyasanīkṛtaḥ || 7.54.15 ||
translation: मा do not, कृथाः make, तनुसन्तापं bodily distress, मत्कृते for my sake, अपि even, नरर्षभ O best of men, कृतान्तः destiny, कुशलः powerful, पुत्र O son, येन by which, अस्मि I am, व्यसनीकृतः made miserable.
explanation: O best of men, do not grieve for my sake, O son, for destiny is powerful, and it is by its force that I have been afflicted with this misery.

shloka_text: प्राप्तव्यान्येव प्राप्नोति गन्तव्यान्येव गच्छति । लब्धव्यान्येव लभते दुःखानि च सुखानि च ।। 7.54.16 ।।
transliteration: prāptavyānyeva prāpnoti gantavyānyeva gacchati | labdhavyānyeva labhate duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca || 7.54.16 ||
translation: प्राप्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be obtained, प्राप्नोति one obtains, गन्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be gone to, गच्छति one goes, लब्धव्यान्येव only those that are to be received, लभते one receives, दुःखानि sorrows, च and, सुखानि joys, च and.
explanation: One obtains only what is destined to be obtained, goes only where one is destined to go, and receives only the sorrows and joys that are destined to be received.

shloka_text: पूर्वे जात्यन्तरे वत्स मा विषादं कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.54.17 ।।
transliteration: pūrve jātyantare vatsa mā viṣādaṃ kuruṣva ha || 7.54.17 ||
translation: पूर्वे in a former, जात्यन्तरे birth, वत्स O son, मा do not, विषादं sorrow, कुरुष्व make, ह indeed.
explanation: O son, do not grieve over what happened in a former birth.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा नृपस्तत्र सुतं राजा महायशाः । श्वभ्रं जगाम सुकृतं वासाय पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.54.18 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā nṛpastatra sutaṃ rājā mahāyaśāḥ | śvabhraṃ jagāma sukṛtaṃ vāsāya puruṣarṣabha || 7.54.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, नृपः the king, तत्र there, सुतम् to his son, राजा the king, महायशाः highly renowned, श्वभ्रम् into the well, जगाम went, सुकृतम् well-made, वासाय for dwelling, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O best among men, having thus spoken to his son, the highly renowned king went into the well, which was well-constructed for his dwelling.

shloka_text: एवं प्रविश्यैव नृपस्तदानीं श्वभ्रं महारत्नविभूषितं तत् । सम्पादयामास तदा महात्मा शापं द्विजाभ्यां हि रुषा विमुक्तम् ।। 7.54.19 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ praviśyaiva nṛpastadānīṃ śvabhraṃ mahāratnavibhūṣitaṃ tat | sampādayāmāsa tadā mahātmā śāpaṃ dvijābhyāṃ hi ruṣā vimuktam || 7.54.19 ||
translation: एवम् thus, प्रविश्यैव having just entered, नृपः the king, तदानीम् at that time, श्वभ्रम् into the well, महारत्नविभूषितम् adorned with great jewels, तत् that, सम्पादयामास he fulfilled, तदा then, महात्मा the great-souled one, शापम् the curse, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, हि indeed, रुषा with anger, विमुक्तम् uttered.
explanation: Having thus just entered that well adorned with great jewels, the great-souled king then fulfilled the curse that had indeed been uttered with anger by the two Brahmins. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 54 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरो ऽभिहितो मया । यद्यस्ति श्रवणे श्रद्धा शृणुष्वेहापरां कथाम् ।। 7.55.1 ।।
transliteration: eṣa te nṛgaśāpasya vistaro 'bhihito mayā | yadyasti śravaṇe śraddhā śṛṇuṣvehāparāṃ kathām || 7.55.1 ||
translation: एषः this, ते to you, नृगशापस्य of Nṛga's curse, विस्तरः the detailed account, अभिहितः has been told, मया by me, यदि if, अस्ति there is, श्रवणे in listening, श्रद्धा faith/desire, शृणुष्व listen, इह here, अपराम् another, कथाम् story.
explanation: I have told you this detailed account of Nṛga's curse; if you have a desire to listen, then hear another story here.
comments: At Lakshmana's wish Rama tells of King Nimi of the Ikshvakus, who founds a city near Gautama's hermitage and begins a long sacrifice -- choosing Vasishtha, who being already engaged by Indra bids him wait, Nimi has Gautama officiate instead -- returning to find himself passed over and the sleeping king failing to receive him, the angered Vasishtha curses Nimi to lose his body, Nimi curses him in return, and both become bodiless.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सौमित्रिः पुनरब्रवीत् । तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे नृप ।। 7.55.2 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu rāmeṇa saumitriḥ punarabravīt | tṛptirāścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ nāsti me nṛpa || 7.55.2 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामेण by Rama, सौमित्रिः Saumitri (Lakshmana), पुनः again, अब्रवीत् spoke, तृप्तिः satisfaction, आश्चर्यभूतानाम् of wonderful, कथानाम् stories, न not, अस्ति is, मे to me, नृप O king.
explanation: But thus spoken to by Rama, Saumitri spoke again, saying, "O king, I have no satisfaction from wonderful stories."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । कथां परमधर्मिष्ठां व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.3 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāma ikṣvākunandanaḥ | kathāṃ paramadharmiṣṭhāṃ vyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.3 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामः Rama, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvakus, कथाम् a story, परमधर्मिष्ठाम् most righteous, व्याहर्तुम् to narrate, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: But thus spoken to by Lakshmana, Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, began to narrate a most righteous story.

shloka_text: आसीद्राजा निमिर्नाम इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः ।। 7.55.4 ।।
transliteration: āsīdrājā nimirnāma ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām | putro dvādaśamo vīrye dharme ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ || 7.55.4 ||
translation: आसीत् was, राजा a king, निमिः Nimi, नाम by name, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् among the Ikshvakus, महात्मनाम् of great souls, पुत्रः son, द्वादशमः twelfth, वीर्ये in valor, धर्मे in righteousness, च and, परिनिष्ठितः firmly established
explanation: There was a king named Nimi, the twelfth son among the noble Ikshvakus, who was firmly established in both valor and righteousness.

shloka_text: स राजा वीर्यसम्पन्नः पुरं देवपुरोपमम् । निवेशयामास तदा अभ्याशे गौतमस्य तु ।। 7.55.5 ।।
transliteration: sa rājā vīryasampannaḥ puraṃ devapuropamam | niveśayāmāsa tadā abhyāśe gautamasya tu || 7.55.5 ||
translation: सः that, राजा king, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, पुरम् a city, देवपुरोपमम् resembling a city of gods, निवेशयामास established, तदा then, अभ्याशे near, गौतमस्य of Gautama, तु indeed
explanation: That valiant king then founded a city, resembling a divine city, near the hermitage of Gautama.

shloka_text: पुरस्य सुकृतं नाम वैजयन्तमिति श्रुतम् । निवेशं यत्र राजर्षिर्निमिश्चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.55.6 ।।
transliteration: purasya sukṛtaṃ nāma vaijayantamiti śrutam | niveśaṃ yatra rājarṣirnimiścakre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.55.6 ||
translation: पुरस्य of the city, सुकृतम् well-made, नाम by name, वैजयन्तम् Vaijayanta, इति thus, श्रुतम् known, निवेशम् settlement, यत्र where, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निमिः Nimi, चक्रे made, महायशाः greatly renowned
explanation: The city was known as Sukrita, or Vaijayanta, where the greatly renowned royal sage Nimi established his settlement.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य सुमहापुरम् । यजेयं दीर्घसत्रेण पितुः प्रह्लादयन्मनः ।। 7.55.7 ।।
transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya sumahāpuram | yajeyaṃ dīrghasatreṇa pituḥ prahlādayanmanaḥ || 7.55.7 ||
translation: तस्य to him, बुद्धिः thought, समुत्पन्ना arose, निवेश्य having established, सुमहापुरम् a very great city, यजेयम् I should sacrifice, दीर्घसत्रेण with a long sacrifice, पितुः of the father, प्रह्लादयन् delighting, मनः the mind
explanation: After establishing that magnificent city, the thought arose in him, "I should perform a long sacrifice, delighting my father's mind."

shloka_text: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम् । वसिष्ठं वरयामास पूर्वं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् ।। 7.55.8 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pitaramāmantrya ikṣvākuṃ hi manoḥ sutam | vasiṣṭhaṃ varayāmāsa pūrvaṃ brahmarṣisattamam || 7.55.8 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, पितरम् father, आमन्त्र्य having invited, इक्ष्वाकुम् Ikshvaku, हि indeed, मनोः of Manu, सुतम् the son, वसिष्ठम् Vasishtha, वरयामास chose, पूर्वम् first, ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् the foremost among Brahmarishis
explanation: Thereafter, having consulted his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he first chose Vasishtha, the foremost among Brahmarishis, to officiate the sacrifice.

shloka_text: अनन्तरं स राजर्षिर्निमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोधनम् ।। 7.55.9 ।।
transliteration: anantaraṃ sa rājarṣirnimirikṣvākunandanaḥ | atrimaṅgirasaṃ caiva bhṛguṃ caiva tapodhanam || 7.55.9 ||
translation: अनन्तरम् thereafter, स that, राजर्षिः royal sage, निमिः Nimi, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः descendant of Ikshvaku, अत्रिम् Atri, अङ्गिरसम् Angiras, च एव and also, भृगुम् Bhrigu, च एव and also, तपोधनम् rich in penance,
explanation: Subsequently, the royal sage Nimi, a descendant of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, who were rich in penance.

shloka_text: तमुवाच वसिष्ठस्तु निमिं राजर्षिसत्तमम् । वृतो ऽहं पूर्वमिन्द्रेण अन्तरं प्रतिपालय ।। 7.55.10 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca vasiṣṭhastu nimiṃ rājarṣisattamam | vṛto 'haṃ pūrvamindreṇa antaraṃ pratipālaya || 7.55.10 ||
translation: तम् to him, उवाच said, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, तु however, निमिम् to Nimi, राजर्षिसत्तमम् the best among royal sages, वृतः chosen, अहम् I am, पूर्वम् previously, इन्द्रेण by Indra, अन्तरम् an interval, प्रतिपालय wait for,
explanation: However, Vasishtha said to Nimi, the best of royal sages, "I have already been chosen by Indra, so please wait for some time."

shloka_text: अनन्तरं महाविप्रो गौतमः प्रत्यपूरयत् । वसिष्ठो ऽपि महातेजा इन्द्रयज्ञमथाकरोत् ।। 7.55.11 ।।
transliteration: anantaraṃ mahāvipro gautamaḥ pratyapūrayat | vasiṣṭho 'pi mahātejā indrayajñamathākarot || 7.55.11 ||
translation: अनन्तरम् thereafter, महाविप्रः the great brahmin, गौतमः Gautama, प्रत्यपूरयत् fulfilled (the request), वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, अपि also, महातेजा greatly effulgent, इन्द्रयज्ञम् Indra's sacrifice, अथ then, अकरोत् performed,
explanation: Subsequently, the great brahmin Gautama fulfilled Nimi's request, while the greatly effulgent Vasishtha then performed Indra's sacrifice.

shloka_text: निमिस्तु राजा विप्रांस्तान्समानीय नराधिपः । अयजद्धिमवत्पार्श्वे स्वपुरस्य समीपतः । पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राजा दीक्षामुपागमत् ।। 7.55.12 ।।
transliteration: nimistu rājā viprāṃstānsamānīya narādhipaḥ | ayajaddhimavatpārśve svapurasya samīpataḥ | pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi rājā dīkṣāmupāgamat || 7.55.12 ||
translation: निमिः Nimi, तु however, राजा king, विप्रान् those brahmins, तान् them, समानीय having gathered, नराधिपः the lord of men, अयजत् performed sacrifice, हिमवत्पार्श्वे on the side of the Himalayas, स्वपुरस्य of his own city, समीपतः near, पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि for five thousand years, राजा the king, दीक्षाम् the vow (of sacrifice), उपागमत् undertook,
explanation: King Nimi, the lord of men, however, gathered those brahmins and performed a sacrifice near his own city, on the side of the Himalayas, undertaking the sacrificial vow for five thousand years.

shloka_text: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने तु वसिष्ठो भगवनृषिः । सकाशमागतो राज्ञो हौत्रं कर्तुमनिन्दितः ।। 7.55.13 ।।
transliteration: indrayajñāvasāne tu vasiṣṭho bhagavanṛṣiḥ | sakāśamāgato rājño hautraṃ kartumaninditaḥ || 7.55.13 ||
translation: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, तु however, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, भगवन् divine, ऋषिः sage, सकाशम् near, आगतः came, राज्ञः of the king, हौत्रम् the role of hotri, कर्तुम् to perform, अनिन्दितः blameless,
explanation: However, at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, the blameless divine sage Vasishtha came near the king to perform the role of the hotri priest.

shloka_text: तदन्तरमथापश्यद्गौतमेनाभिपूरितम् । कोपेन महताविष्टो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।। 7.55.14 ।।
transliteration: tadantaramathāpaśyadgautamenābhipūritam | kopena mahatāviṣṭo vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 7.55.14 ||
translation: तदन्तरम् thereafter, अथ then, अपश्यत् (he) saw, गौतमेन by Gautama, अभिपूरितम् filled (the place), कोपेन with anger, महता great, आविष्टः overcome, वसिष्ठः Vasiṣṭha, ब्रह्मणः of Brahma, सुतः the son.
explanation: Then, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, saw the place occupied by Gautama and was overcome with great anger.

shloka_text: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी मुहूर्तं समुपाविशत् । तस्मिन्नहनि राजर्षिर्निद्रया ऽपहृतो भृशम् ।। 7.55.15 ।।
transliteration: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī muhūrtaṃ samupāviśat | tasminnahani rājarṣirnidrayā 'pahṛto bhṛśam || 7.55.15 ||
translation: सः He, राज्ञः of the king, दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी desirous of seeing, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, समुपाविशत् sat down, तस्मिन् on that, अहनि day, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निद्रया by sleep, अपहृतः overcome, भृशम् greatly.
explanation: Desirous of seeing the king, Vasiṣṭha sat down for a moment, but on that day, the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.

shloka_text: ततो मन्युर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः । अदर्शनेन राजर्षेर्व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.16 ।।
transliteration: tato manyurvasiṣṭhasya prādurāsīnmahātmanaḥ | adarśanena rājarṣervyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.16 ||
translation: ततः Then, मन्युः anger, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasiṣṭha, प्रादुरासीत् arose, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, अदर्शनेन by the non-seeing, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Then, anger arose in the great-souled Vasiṣṭha due to the absence of the royal sage, and he began to speak.

shloka_text: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव । चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्तव भविष्यति ।। 7.55.17 ।।
transliteration: yasmāttvamanyaṃ vṛtavānmāmavajñāya pārthiva | cetanena vinābhūto dehastava bhaviṣyati || 7.55.17 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, अन्यम् another, वृतवान् have chosen, माम् me, अवज्ञाय disregarding, पार्थिव O King, चेतनेन with consciousness, विनाभूतः devoid of, देहः body, तव your, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: "O King, because you have chosen another, disregarding me, your body will become devoid of consciousness."

shloka_text: ततः प्रबुद्धो राजर्षिः श्रुत्वा शापमुदाहृतम् । ब्रह्मयोनिमथोवाच संरम्भात् क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.55.18 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prabuddho rājarṣiḥ śrutvā śāpamudāhṛtam | brahmayonimathovāca saṃrambhāt krodhamūrcchitaḥ || 7.55.18 ||
translation: ततः Then, प्रबुद्धः awakened, राजर्षिः the royal sage, श्रुत्वा having heard, शापम् the curse, उदाहृतम् uttered, ब्रह्मयोनिम् to the one born from Brahma, अथ then, उवाच spoke, संरम्भात् from agitation, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with anger.
explanation: Then, the royal sage, awakened and having heard the uttered curse, spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, overcome with fury and anger.

shloka_text: अजानतः शयानस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः । मुक्तवान्मयि शापाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम् ।। 7.55.19 ।।
transliteration: ajānataḥ śayānasya krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ | muktavānmayi śāpāgniṃ yamadaṇḍamivāparam || 7.55.19 ||
translation: अजानतः unaware, शयानस्य of one who was sleeping, क्रोधेन by anger, कलुषीकृतः enraged, मुक्तवान् he released, मयि upon me, शापाग्निं the fire of a curse, यमदण्डम् the rod of Yama, इव like, अपरम् another.
explanation: Enraged by anger, he, unaware of me sleeping, cast upon me the fire of a curse, like a second rod of Yama.

shloka_text: तस्मात्तवापि ब्रह्मर्षे चेतनेन विना कृतः । देहः सुरुचिरप्रख्यो भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.55.20 ।।
transliteration: tasmāttavāpi brahmarṣe cetanena vinā kṛtaḥ | dehaḥ suruciraprakhyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.55.20 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, तवापि even your, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi, चेतनेन by consciousness, विना कृतः deprived of, देहः body, सुरुचिरप्रख्यो exceedingly charming in appearance, भविष्यति will be, न संशयः no doubt.
explanation: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, without a doubt, even your exceedingly charming body will be deprived of consciousness.

shloka_text: इति रोषवशादुभौ तदानीमन्योन्यं शपितौ नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ । सहसैव बभूवतुर्विदेहौ तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ ।। 7.55.21 ।।
transliteration: iti roṣavaśādubhau tadānīmanyonyaṃ śapitau nṛpadvijendrau | sahasaiva babhūvaturvidehau tattulyādhigataprabhāvavantau || 7.55.21 ||
translation: इति thus, रोषवशात् due to the power of anger, उभौ both, तदानीम् then, अन्योन्यं each other, शपितौ cursed, नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ the king and the chief of Brahmins, सहसैव suddenly, बभूवतुः became, विदेहौ bodiless, तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ possessing equally acquired power.
explanation: Thus, under the sway of anger, both the king and the chief of Brahmins, having cursed each other, suddenly became bodiless, each possessing an equally acquired power. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.56.1 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ rāghavaṃ dīptatejasam || 7.56.1 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितं words, श्रुत्वा having heard, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परवीरहा destroyer of enemy heroes, उवाच spoke, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यं words, राघवं to Rama, दीप्ततेजसम् of blazing splendor.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemy heroes, spoke with folded hands to the radiant Rama.
comments: Lakshmana asks how the two regained their bodies -- Rama tells that the bodiless Vasishtha, sent by Brahma to be reborn without a womb, goes to Varuna's abode, where Varuna, smitten by the apsara Urvashi who is pledged to Mitra, sheds his seed into a pot -- slighted, Mitra curses Urvashi to dwell among men as the wife of King Pururavas, ancestress of Ayus and Nahusha.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्य कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ । पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मतुर्देवसम्मतौ ।। 7.56.2 ।।
transliteration: nikṣiptadehau kākutsya kathaṃ tau dvijapārthivau | punardehena saṃyogaṃ jagmaturdevasammatau || 7.56.2 ||
translation: निक्षिप्तदेहौ having cast off their bodies, काकुत्स्य O Kakutstha, कथं how, तौ those two, द्विजपार्थिवौ the Brahmin and the king, पुनः again, देहेन with a body, संयोगं union, जग्मतुः attained, देवसम्मतौ honored by the gods.
explanation: O Kakutstha, how did those two, the Brahmin and the king, who had cast off their bodies and were honored by the gods, attain union with a body again?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु रामश्चेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजा लक्ष्मणं पुरुषर्षभः ।। 7.56.3 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāmaścekṣvākunandanaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejā lakṣmaṇaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ || 7.56.3 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, रामः Rama, च and, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः delight of Ikshvaku, प्रत्युवाच replied, महातेजाः greatly effulgent, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, पुरुषर्षभः best among men.
explanation: Rama, the greatly effulgent best among men and descendant of Ikshvaku, thus replied to Lakshmana who had spoken to him.

shloka_text: तौ परस्परशापेन देहावुत्सृज्य धार्मिकौ । अभूतां नृपविप्रर्षी वायुभूतौ तपोधनौ ।। 7.56.4 ।।
transliteration: tau parasparaśāpena dehāvutsṛjya dhārmikau | abhūtāṃ nṛpaviprarṣī vāyubhūtau tapodhanau || 7.56.4 ||
translation: तौ those two, परस्परशापेन by mutual curse, देहौ bodies, उत्सृज्य having abandoned, धार्मिकौ righteous ones, अभूताम् became, नृपविप्रर्षी the king and the brahmin sage, वायुभूतौ having become air, तपोधनौ whose wealth is penance.
explanation: Those two righteous ones, the king and the brahmin sage, having abandoned their bodies due to a mutual curse, became beings of air, their wealth being penance.

shloka_text: अशरीरः शरीरस्य कृते ऽन्यस्य महामुनिः । वसिष्ठः सुमहातेजा जगाम पितुरन्तिकम् ।। 7.56.5 ।।
transliteration: aśarīraḥ śarīrasya kṛte 'nyasya mahāmuniḥ | vasiṣṭhaḥ sumahātejā jagāma piturantikam || 7.56.5 ||
translation: अशरीरः bodiless, शरीरस्य for a body, कृते for the sake of, अन्यस्य another, महामुनिः the great sage, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, सुमहातेजाः exceedingly greatly effulgent, जगाम went, पितुः of his father, अन्तिकम् to the presence.
explanation: The great sage Vasishtha, exceedingly greatly effulgent, being bodiless, went to his father's presence for the sake of another body.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ देवदेवस्य धर्मवित् । पितामहमथोवाच वायुभूत इदं वचः ।। 7.56.6 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya tataḥ pādau devadevasya dharmavit | pitāmahamathovāca vāyubhūta idaṃ vacaḥ || 7.56.6 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, ततः then, पादौ the feet, देवदेवस्य of the god of gods, धर्मवित् knower of dharma, पितामहम् to the grandfather, अथ then, उवाच spoke, वायुभूतः having become air, इदम् this, वचः word.
explanation: Then, he, the knower of dharma, having become air, saluted the feet of the god of gods, his grandfather (Brahma), and spoke these words.

shloka_text: भगवन्निमिशापेन विदेहत्वमुपागमम् । लोकनाथ महादेव अण्डजो ऽपि त्वमब्जजः ।। 7.56.7 ।।
transliteration: bhagavannimiśāpena videhatvamupāgamam | lokanātha mahādeva aṇḍajo 'pi tvamabjajaḥ || 7.56.7 ||
translation: भगवन् O Lord, निमि Nimi, शापेन by the curse, विदेहत्वम् bodiless state, उपागमम् I have attained, लोकनाथ O Lord of the worlds, महादेव O great god, अण्डजः born from an egg, अपि even, त्वम् you, अब्जजः born from a lotus.
explanation: O Lord, O Lord of the worlds, O great god, I have attained a bodiless state due to Nimi's curse, and you yourself are born from an egg and a lotus.

shloka_text: सर्वेषां देहहीनानां महद्दुःखं भविष्यति । लुप्यन्ते सर्वकार्यणि हीनदेहस्य वै प्रभो । देहस्यान्यस्य सद्भावे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.56.8 ।।
transliteration: sarveṣāṃ dehahīnānāṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati | lupyante sarvakāryaṇi hīnadehasya vai prabho | dehasyānyasya sadbhāve prasādaṃ kartumarhasi || 7.56.8 ||
translation: सर्वेषां of all, देहहीनानां of those without a body, महद्दुःखं great sorrow, भविष्यति will be, लुप्यन्ते are destroyed, सर्वकार्यणि all actions, हीनदेहस्य of one without a body, वै indeed, प्रभो O Lord, देहस्य of a body, अन्यस्य another, सद्भावे in the existence, प्रसादं favor, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: O Lord, great sorrow will befall all those without a body, as all actions are lost for one who lacks a physical form; therefore, you ought to grant the favor of another body.

shloka_text: तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूरमितप्रभः । मित्रावरुणजं तेज प्रविश त्वं महायशः ।। 7.56.9 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca tato brahmā svayambhūramitaprabhaḥ | mitrāvaruṇajaṃ teja praviśa tvaṃ mahāyaśaḥ || 7.56.9 ||
translation: तम् him, उवाच said, ततो then, ब्रह्मा Brahma, स्वयम्भूः the self-born, अमितप्रभः of immeasurable splendor, मित्रावरुणजं born of Mitra and Varuna, तेज the essence, प्रविश enter, त्वं you, महायशः O greatly renowned one.
explanation: Then, Brahma, the self-born one of immeasurable splendor, said to him, "O greatly renowned one, enter the essence born of Mitra and Varuna."

shloka_text: अयोनिजस्त्वं भविता तत्रापि द्विजसत्तम । धर्मेण महता युक्तः पुनरेष्यसि मे वशम् ।। 7.56.10 ।।
transliteration: ayonijastvaṃ bhavitā tatrāpi dvijasattama | dharmeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ punareṣyasi me vaśam || 7.56.10 ||
translation: अयोनिजः not born from a womb, त्वं you, भविता will be, तत्रापि even there, द्विजसत्तम O best among twice-born, धर्मेण with righteousness, महता great, युक्तः endowed, पुनः again, एष्यसि you will come, मे my, वशम् control.
explanation: O best among twice-born, even there you will be born without a womb, and endowed with great righteousness, you will again return to my control.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन चाभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम् । कृत्वा पितामहं तूर्णं प्रययौ वरुणालयम् ।। 7.56.11 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu devena cābhivādya pradakṣiṇam | kṛtvā pitāmahaṃ tūrṇaṃ prayayau varuṇālayam || 7.56.11 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, देवेन by the god, च and, अभिवाद्य having saluted, प्रदक्षिणम् circumambulation, कृत्वा having done, पितामहं the grandfather, तूर्णं quickly, प्रययौ went, वरुणालयम् to the abode of Varuna.
explanation: Thus spoken to by the god, and having saluted and circumambulated the grandfather Brahma, he quickly went to the abode of Varuna.

shloka_text: तमेव कालं मित्रो ऽपि वरुणत्वमकारयत् । क्षीरोदेन सहोपेतः पूज्यमानः सुरोत्तमैः ।। 7.56.12 ।।
transliteration: tameva kālaṃ mitro 'pi varuṇatvamakārayat | kṣīrodena sahopetaḥ pūjyamānaḥ surottamaiḥ || 7.56.12 ||
translation: तम् that, एव very, कालं time, मित्रो Mitra, अपि also, वरुणत्वम् the state of Varuna, अकारयत् caused to be done, क्षीरोदेन with the ocean of milk, सह with, उपेतः accompanied, पूज्यमानः being worshipped, सुरोत्तमैः by the best of gods.
explanation: At that very time, Mitra also performed the role of Varuna, accompanied by the Ocean of Milk and being worshipped by the best of gods.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु उर्वशी परमाप्सराः । यदृच्छया तमुद्देशमाययौ सखिभिर्वृता ।। 7.56.13 ।।
transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu urvaśī paramāpsarāḥ | yadṛcchayā tamuddeśamāyayau sakhibhirvṛtā || 7.56.13 ||
translation: एतस्मिन्नेव काले in that very time, तु indeed, उर्वशी Urvashi, परमाप्सराः the chief Apsara, यदृच्छया by chance, तम् उद्देशम् to that place, आययौ came, सखिभिर्वृता surrounded by friends.
explanation: At that very time, Urvashi, the foremost Apsara, arrived at that place by chance, accompanied by her friends.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां क्रीडन्तीं वरुणालये । आविशत्परमो हर्षो वरुणं चोर्वशीकृते ।। 7.56.14 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpasampannāṃ krīḍantīṃ varuṇālaye | āviśatparamo harṣo varuṇaṃ corvaśīkṛte || 7.56.14 ||
translation: ताम् her, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रूपसम्पन्नाम् endowed with beauty, क्रीडन्तीम् playing, वरुणालये in Varuna's abode, आविशत् entered, परमो हर्षो great joy, वरुणम् Varuna, च and, उर्वशीकृते for Urvashi's sake.
explanation: Having seen her, beautiful and playing in Varuna's abode, great joy entered Varuna because of Urvashi.

shloka_text: स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । वरुणो वरयामास मैथुनायाप्सरोवराम् ।। 7.56.15 ।।
transliteration: sa tāṃ padmapalāśākṣīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām | varuṇo varayāmāsa maithunāyāpsarovarām || 7.56.15 ||
translation: सः he, ताम् her, पद्मपलाशाक्षीम् lotus-petal-eyed, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् with a face like the full moon, वरुणः Varuna, वरयामास desired, मैथुनाय for union, अप्सरोवराम् the best of Apsaras.
explanation: Varuna, seeing her with lotus-petal eyes and a face like the full moon, desired her, the best of Apsaras, for union.

shloka_text: प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता । मित्रेणाहं वृता साक्षात्पूर्वमेव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.56.16 ।।
transliteration: pratyuvāca tataḥ sā tu varuṇaṃ prāñjaliḥ sthitā | mitreṇāhaṃ vṛtā sākṣātpūrvameva sureśvara || 7.56.16 ||
translation: प्रत्युवाच replied, ततः then, सा she, तु indeed, वरुणम् to Varuna, प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता standing with folded hands, मित्रेण by Mitra, अहम् I, वृता chosen, साक्षात् directly, पूर्वम् एव already, सुरेश्वर O Lord of gods.
explanation: Then she, standing with folded hands, replied to Varuna, saying, "O Lord of gods, I have already been directly chosen by Mitra."

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं कन्दर्पशरपीडितः । इदं तेजः समुत्स्रक्ष्ये कुम्भे ऽस्मिन्देवनिर्मिते ।। 7.56.17 ।।
transliteration: varuṇastvabravīdvākyaṃ kandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ | idaṃ tejaḥ samutsrakṣye kumbhe 'smindevanirmite || 7.56.17 ||
translation: वरुणः Varuna, तु however, अब्रवीत् spoke, वाक्यम् words, कन्दर्पशरपीडितः tormented by the arrows of Kama, इदम् this, तेजः semen, समुत्स्रक्ष्ये I shall discharge, कुम्भे in the pot, अस्मिन् this, देवनिर्मिते made by gods.
explanation: Tormented by the arrows of Kama, Varuna then spoke, saying, "I shall discharge this semen into this pot made by the gods."
