shloka_text: एवमुत्सृज्य सुश्रोणि त्वय्यहं वरवर्णिनि । कृतकामो भविष्यामि यदि नेच्छसि सङ्गमम् ।। 7.56.18 ।।
transliteration: evamutsṛjya suśroṇi tvayyahaṃ varavarṇini | kṛtakāmo bhaviṣyāmi yadi necchasi saṅgamam || 7.56.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उत्सृज्य abandoning (desire), सुश्रोणि O beautiful-hipped one, त्वयि in you, अहम् I, वरवर्णिनि O lady of excellent complexion, कृतकामः one whose desire is fulfilled, भविष्यामि I shall become, यदि if, न not, इच्छसि you desire, सङ्गमम् union,
explanation: O beautiful-hipped lady of excellent complexion, if you do not desire union, I shall thus abandon my desire for you and consider my wish fulfilled.

shloka_text: तस्य तल्लोकपालस्य वरुणस्य सुभाषितम् । उर्वशी परमप्रीता श्रुत्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.56.19 ।।
transliteration: tasya tallokapālasya varuṇasya subhāṣitam | urvaśī paramaprītā śrutvā vākyamuvāca ha || 7.56.19 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, लोकपालस्य of the protector of the world, वरुणस्य of Varuna, सुभाषितम् well-spoken word, उर्वशी Urvashi, परमप्रीता extremely pleased, श्रुत्वा having heard, वाक्यम् words, उवाच ह spoke indeed,
explanation: Having heard those well-spoken words of Varuna, the protector of the world, Urvashi was extremely pleased and spoke.

shloka_text: काममेतद्भवत्वेवं हृदयं मे त्वयि स्थितम् । भावश्चाप्यधिकस्तुभ्यं देहो मित्रस्य तु प्रभो ।। 7.56.20 ।।
transliteration: kāmametadbhavatvevaṃ hṛdayaṃ me tvayi sthitam | bhāvaścāpyadhikastubhyaṃ deho mitrasya tu prabho || 7.56.20 ||
translation: कामम् indeed, एतत् this, भवतु let it be, एवम् thus, हृदयम् heart, मे my, त्वयि in you, स्थितम् situated, भावः च अपि and also feeling, अधिकः great, तुभ्यम् for you, देहः body, मित्रस्य of Mitra, तु but, प्रभो O lord,
explanation: O lord, let it be so; my heart is indeed fixed on you, and my affection for you is great, but my body belongs to Mitra.

shloka_text: उर्वश्या एवमुक्तस्तु रेतस्तन्महदद्भुतम् । ज्वलदग्निशिखाप्रख्यं तस्मिन्कुम्भे ह्यपासृजत् ।। 7.56.21 ।।
transliteration: urvaśyā evamuktastu retastanmahadadbhutam | jvaladagniśikhāprakhyaṃ tasminkumbhe hyapāsṛjat || 7.56.21 ||
translation: उर्वश्या by Urvashi, एवम् thus, उक्तः तु having been spoken to, indeed, रेतः semen, तत् that, महत् great, अद्भुतम् wonderful, ज्वलत् burning, अग्निशिखा flame of fire, प्रख्यम् resembling, तस्मिन् in that, कुम्भे pot, हि indeed, अपासृजत् he discharged,
explanation: Thus addressed by Urvashi, he indeed discharged that great and wonderful semen, resembling a burning flame of fire, into that pot.

shloka_text: उर्वशी त्वगमत्तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता । तां तु मित्रः सुसङ्क्रम्य उर्वशीमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.56.22 ।।
transliteration: urvaśī tvagamattatra mitro vai yatra devatā | tāṃ tu mitraḥ susaṅkramya urvaśīmidamabravīt || 7.56.22 ||
translation: उर्वशी Urvashi, तु but, अगमत् went, तत्र there, मित्रः Mitra, वै indeed, यत्र where, देवता the deity, ताम् her, तु but, मित्रः Mitra, सुसङ्क्रम्य having approached well, उर्वशीम् to Urvashi, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke,
explanation: But Urvashi went to the place where the deity Mitra was, and Mitra, having approached her, spoke these words to Urvashi.

shloka_text: मया निमन्त्रिता पूर्वं कस्मात्त्वमवसर्जिता । पतिमन्यं वृतवती तस्मात्त्वं दुष्टचारिणी ।। 7.56.23 ।।
transliteration: mayā nimantritā pūrvaṃ kasmāttvamavasarjitā | patimanyaṃ vṛtavatī tasmāttvaṃ duṣṭacāriṇī || 7.56.23 ||
translation: मया by me, निमन्त्रिता invited, पूर्वम् previously, कस्मात् why, त्वम् you, अवसर्जिता abandoned, पतिम् husband, अन्यम् another, वृतवती chosen, तस्मात् therefore, त्वम् you, दुष्टचारिणी ill-behaved woman.
explanation: Why did you abandon me, whom I had previously invited, and choose another husband; therefore, you are an ill-behaved woman.

shloka_text: अनेन दुष्कृतेन त्वं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता । मनुष्यलोकमास्थाय कञ्चित्कालं निवत्स्यसि ।। 7.56.24 ।।
transliteration: anena duṣkṛtena tvaṃ matkrodhakaluṣīkṛtā | manuṣyalokamāsthāya kañcitkālaṃ nivatsyasi || 7.56.24 ||
translation: अनेन by this, दुष्कृतेन misdeed, त्वम् you, मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता sullied by my wrath, मनुष्यलोकम् the human world, आस्थाय having resorted to, कञ्चित्कालम् for some time, निवत्स्यसि you will reside.
explanation: Due to this misdeed, you, sullied by my wrath, will reside in the human world for some time.

shloka_text: बुधस्य पुत्रो राजर्षिः काशीराजः पुरूरवाः । तमद्य गच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति ।। 7.56.25 ।।
transliteration: budhasya putro rājarṣiḥ kāśīrājaḥ purūravāḥ | tamadya gaccha durbuddhe sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati || 7.56.25 ||
translation: बुधस्य of Budha, पुत्रः son, राजर्षिः royal sage, काशीराजः king of Kashi, पुरूरवाः Pururavas, तम् him, अद्य today, गच्छ go, दुर्बुद्धे O ill-minded one, सः he, ते your, भर्ता husband, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Go today to Pururavas, the royal sage, son of Budha and king of Kashi, O ill-minded one, for he will be your husband.

shloka_text: ततः सा शापदोषेण पुरूरवसमभ्यगात् । प्रतियाते पुरूरवं बुधस्यात्मजमौरसम् ।। 7.56.26 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā śāpadoṣeṇa purūravasamabhyagāt | pratiyāte purūravaṃ budhasyātmajamaurasam || 7.56.26 ||
translation: ततः then, सा she, शापदोषेण by the effect of the curse, पुरूरवसम् to Pururavas, अभ्यगात् went, प्रतियाते to the one who had returned, पुरूरवम् Pururavas, बुधस्य of Budha, आत्मजम् son, औरसम् legitimate.
explanation: Then she, by the effect of the curse, went to Pururavas, the legitimate son of Budha, who had returned.

shloka_text: तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः । नहुषो यस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवेन्द्रसमद्युतिः ।। 7.56.27 ।।
transliteration: tasya jajñe tataḥ śrīmānāyuḥ putro mahābalaḥ | nahuṣo yasya putrastu babhūvendrasamadyutiḥ || 7.56.27 ||
translation: तस्य to him, जज्ञे was born, ततः then, श्रीमान् glorious, आयुः Ayus, पुत्रः son, महाबलः very powerful, नहुषः Nahusha, यस्य whose, पुत्रस्तु son, however, बभूव became, इन्द्रसमद्युतिः having splendor equal to Indra.
explanation: Then to him was born a glorious and very powerful son named Ayus, whose son, Nahusha, became one with splendor equal to Indra.

shloka_text: वज्रमुत्सृज्य वृत्राय भ्रान्ते ऽथ त्रिदिवेश्वरे । शतं वर्षसहस्राणि येनेन्द्रत्वं प्रशासितम् ।। 7.56.28 ।।
transliteration: vajramutsṛjya vṛtrāya bhrānte 'tha tridiveśvare | śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇi yenendratvaṃ praśāsitam || 7.56.28 ||
translation: वज्रम् thunderbolt, उत्सृज्य having cast, वृत्राय at Vritra, भ्रान्ते having erred, अथ then, त्रिदिवेश्वरे when the lord of the three heavens (Indra), शतम् a hundred, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, येन by whom, इन्द्रत्वम् the position of Indra, प्रशासितम् was ruled
explanation: This refers to the one who ruled as Indra for a hundred thousand years when the actual Indra was agitated after casting his thunderbolt at Vritra.

shloka_text: सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमिं तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा । बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च ।। 7.56.29 ।।
transliteration: sā tena śāpena jagāma bhūmiṃ tadorvaśī cārudatī sunetrā | bahūni varṣāṇyavasacca subhrūḥ śāpakṣayādindrasado yayau ca || 7.56.29 ||
translation: सा she, तेन by that, शापेन curse, जगाम went, भूमिम् to the earth, तदा then, उर्वशी Urvashi, चारुदती having beautiful teeth, सुनेत्रा having beautiful eyes, बहूनि many, वर्षाणि years, अवसत् resided, च and, सुभ्रूः having beautiful eyebrows, शापक्षयात् from the end of the curse, इन्द्रसदः to Indra's assembly, ययौ went, च and
explanation: That Urvashi, with beautiful teeth, eyes, and eyebrows, then went to the earth due to that curse, resided there for many years, and returned to Indra's assembly upon the curse's expiration. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 56 ।। Thus ends the fifty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तां श्रुत्वा दिव्यसङ्काशां कथामद्भुतदर्शनाम् । लक्ष्मणः परमप्रीतो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.57.1 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ śrutvā divyasaṅkāśāṃ kathāmadbhutadarśanām | lakṣmaṇaḥ paramaprīto rāghavaṃ vākyamabravīt || 7.57.1 ||
translation: ताम् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, दिव्यसङ्काशां divine-like, कथाम् story, अद्भुतदर्शनाम् amazing to behold, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परमप्रीतः greatly pleased, राघवम् to Rama, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke
explanation: Having heard that divine-like and amazing story, Lakshmana was greatly pleased and spoke these words to Rama.
comments: Rama continues: from the pot are born two sages, Agastya and then Vasishtha, who becomes Ikshvaku's priest -- meanwhile Nimi, by the gods' boon, comes to dwell as the blinking in the eyes of all beings, and from the churning of his preserved body is born a son called Mithi, Janaka and Vaideha, ancestor of the kings of Videha, whence the land is named Maithila.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्थ कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ । पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मुर्देवसम्मतौ ।। 7.57.2 ।।
transliteration: nikṣiptadehau kākutstha kathaṃ tau dvijapārthivau | punardehena saṃyogaṃ jagmurdevasammatau || 7.57.2 ||
translation: निक्षिप्तदेहौ having abandoned their bodies, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, कथम् how, तौ those two, द्विजपार्थिवौ the Brahmin and the king, पुनर्देहेन again with a body, संयोगम् union, जग्मुः attained, देवसम्मतौ approved by the gods
explanation: Lakshmana asked Rama how those two, the Brahmin and the king, who had abandoned their bodies and were respected by the gods, managed to regain a physical form.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः । तां कथां कथयामास वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.57.3 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ | tāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmāsa vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.57.3 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, भाषितम् speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामः Rama, सत्यपराक्रमः of true valor, ताम् that, कथाम् story, कथयामास narrated, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasishtha, महात्मनः of the great-souled one
explanation: Having heard Lakshmana's words, Rama, whose valor is truth, then narrated the story of the great-souled Vasishtha.

shloka_text: यस्तु कुम्भो रघुश्रेष्ठ तेजःपूर्णो महात्मनोः । तस्मिंस्तेजोमयौ विप्रौ सम्भूतावृषिसत्तमौ ।। 7.57.4 ।।
transliteration: yastu kumbho raghuśreṣṭha tejaḥpūrṇo mahātmanoḥ | tasmiṃstejomayau viprau sambhūtāvṛṣisattamau || 7.57.4 ||
translation: यः who, तु indeed, कुम्भः pot, रघुश्रेष्ठ O best of Raghu's lineage, तेजःपूर्णः filled with semen/radiance, महात्मनोः of the two great souls, तस्मिन् in that, तेजोमयौ radiant, विप्रौ two Brahmins, सम्भूतौ were born, ऋषिसत्तमौ two excellent sages.
explanation: O best of Raghu's lineage, in that pot, which was filled with the radiant semen of the two great souls (Mitra and Varuna), two radiant Brahmins, who were excellent sages, were born.

shloka_text: पूर्वं समभवत्तत्र ह्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः । नाहं सुतस्तवेत्युक्त्वा मित्रं तस्मादपाक्रमत् ।। 7.57.5 ।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃ samabhavattatra hyagastyo bhagavānṛṣiḥ | nāhaṃ sutastavetyuktvā mitraṃ tasmādapākramat || 7.57.5 ||
translation: पूर्वम् first, समभवत् was born, तत्र there, हि indeed, अगस्त्यः Agastya, भगवान् divine, ऋषिः sage, न not, अहम् I, सुतः son, तव your, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, मित्रम् Mitra, तस्मात् from him, अपाक्रमत् departed.
explanation: First, the divine sage Agastya was born there, and having said "I am not your son," Mitra then departed from him.

shloka_text: तद्धि तेजस्तु मित्रस्य उर्वस्याः पूर्वमाहितम् । तस्मिन्समभवत्कुम्भे तत्तेजो यत्र वारुणम् ।। 7.57.6 ।।
transliteration: taddhi tejastu mitrasya urvasyāḥ pūrvamāhitam | tasminsamabhavatkumbhe tattejo yatra vāruṇam || 7.57.6 ||
translation: तत् that, हि indeed, तेजः semen/radiance, तु but, मित्रस्य of Mitra, उर्वस्याः in Urvashi, पूर्वम् previously, आहितम् placed, तस्मिन् in that, समभवत् was born, कुम्भे in the pot, तत् that, तेजः semen/radiance, यत्र where, वारुणम् of Varuna.
explanation: That semen of Mitra, which had previously been placed in Urvashi, was born in that pot where the semen of Varuna was also present.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य मित्रावरुणसम्भवः । वसिष्ठस्तेजसा युक्तो जज्ञे इक्ष्वाकुदैवतम् ।। 7.57.7 ।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya mitrāvaruṇasambhavaḥ | vasiṣṭhastejasā yukto jajñe ikṣvākudaivatam || 7.57.7 ||
translation: कस्यचित् after some, तु indeed, अथ then, कालस्य time, मित्रावरुणसम्भवः born of Mitra and Varuna, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, तेजसा with radiance, युक्तः endowed, जज्ञे was born, इक्ष्वाकुदैवतम् the deity/priest of Ikshvaku.
explanation: Then, after some time, Vasishtha, born of Mitra and Varuna and endowed with radiance, was born as the priest of Ikshvaku.

shloka_text: तमिक्ष्वाकुर्महातेजा जातमात्रमनिन्दितम् । वव्रे पुरोधसं सौम्य वंशस्यास्य भवाय नः ।। 7.57.8 ।।
transliteration: tamikṣvākurmahātejā jātamātramaninditam | vavre purodhasaṃ saumya vaṃśasyāsya bhavāya naḥ || 7.57.8 ||
translation: तम् him, इक्ष्वाकुः Ikshvaku, महातेजा exceedingly radiant, जातमात्रम् as soon as born, अनिन्दितम् blameless, वव्रे chose, पुरोधसम् as family priest, सौम्य O gentle one, वंशस्य of the lineage, अस्य this, भवाय for the prosperity, नः our.
explanation: O gentle one, the exceedingly radiant Ikshvaku chose that blameless Vasishtha, as soon as he was born, to be the family priest for the prosperity of our lineage.

shloka_text: एवं त्वपूर्वदेहस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः । कथितो निर्गमः सौम्य निमेः शृणु यथा ऽभवत् ।। 7.57.9 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ tvapūrvadehasya vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ | kathito nirgamaḥ saumya nimeḥ śṛṇu yathā 'bhavat || 7.57.9 ||
translation: एवं thus, तु indeed, अपूर्वदेहस्य of one with an unprecedented body, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasistha, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, कथितो has been told, निर्गमः the departure, सौम्य O gentle one, निमेः of Nimi, शृणु listen, यथा how, अभवत् it happened.
explanation: O gentle one, thus has been narrated the birth of the great-souled Vasistha, who had an unprecedented body; now listen to how it happened with Nimi.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा विदेहं राजानमृषयः सर्व एव ते । तं च ते योजयामासुर्यागदीक्षां मनीषिणः ।। 7.57.10 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā videhaṃ rājānamṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te | taṃ ca te yojayāmāsuryāgadīkṣāṃ manīṣiṇaḥ || 7.57.10 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, विदेहं bodiless, राजानम् the king, ऋषयः the sages, सर्व all, एव indeed, ते they, तं him, च and, ते they, योजयामासुः made him undertake, यागदीक्षाम् the initiation for the sacrifice, मनीषिणः the wise ones.
explanation: All those wise sages, having seen the king Nimi bodiless, then engaged him in the initiation rites for the sacrifice.

shloka_text: तं च देहं नरेन्द्रस्य रक्षन्ति स्म द्विजोत्तमाः । गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च वस्त्रैश्च पौरभृत्यसमन्विताः ।। 7.57.11 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ca dehaṃ narendrasya rakṣanti sma dvijottamāḥ | gandhairmālyaiśca vastraiśca paurabhṛtyasamanvitāḥ || 7.57.11 ||
translation: तं that, च and, देहं body, नरेन्द्रस्य of the king, रक्षन्ति protected, स्म (past tense indicator), द्विजोत्तमाः the best among the twice-born, गन्धैः with fragrances, माल्यैः with garlands, च and, वस्त्रैः with clothes, च and, पौरभृत्यसमन्विताः accompanied by citizens and servants.
explanation: And the best among the twice-born, accompanied by citizens and servants, protected that body of the king with fragrances, garlands, and clothes.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु भृगुस्तत्रेदमब्रवीत् । आनयिष्यामि ते चेतस्तुष्टो ऽस्मि तव पार्थिव ।। 7.57.12 ।।
transliteration: tato yajñe samāpte tu bhṛgustatredamabravīt | ānayiṣyāmi te cetastuṣṭo 'smi tava pārthiva || 7.57.12 ||
translation: ततः then, यज्ञे समाप्ते when the sacrifice was concluded, भृगुः Bhrigu, तत्र there, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke, पार्थिव O king, तव तुष्टः अस्मि I am pleased with you, ते your, चेतः consciousness, आनयिष्यामि I shall restore.
explanation: Then, when the sacrifice was concluded, Bhrigu said: O king, I am pleased with you, and I shall restore your consciousness.

shloka_text: सुप्रीताश्च सुराः सर्वे निमेश्चेतस्तथाब्रुवन् । वरं वरय राजर्षे क्व ते चेतो निरूप्यताम् ।। 7.57.13 ।।
transliteration: suprītāśca surāḥ sarve nimeścetastathābruvan | varaṃ varaya rājarṣe kva te ceto nirūpyatām || 7.57.13 ||
translation: सुप्रीताः very pleased, च and, सुराः the gods, सर्वे all, निमेः to Nimi, चेतः (to his spirit), तथा thus, अब्रुवन् they spoke, वरं a boon, वरय choose, राजर्षे O royal sage, क्व where, ते your, चेतो mind, निरूप्यताम् let it be fixed.
explanation: And all the gods, being very pleased, thus spoke to Nimi's spirit: "O royal sage, choose a boon; where should your mind be fixed?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुरैः सर्वैर्निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रवीत् । नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वसेयं सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.57.14 ।।
transliteration: evamuktaḥ suraiḥ sarvairnimeścetastadābravīt | netreṣu sarvabhūtānāṃ vaseyaṃ surasattamāḥ || 7.57.14 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, सुरैः by the gods, सर्वैः by all, निमेः Nimi's, चेतः spirit, तदा then, अब्रवीत् spoke, नेत्रेषु in the eyes, सर्वभूतानां of all beings, वसेयं may I dwell, सुरसत्तमाः O best among gods.
explanation: Thus spoken to by all the gods, Nimi's spirit then said: "O best among gods, may I dwell in the eyes of all beings."

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव विबुधा निमेश्चेतस्तदा ऽब्रुवन् । नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वायुभूतश्चरिष्यसि ।। 7.57.15 ।।
transliteration: bāḍhamityeva vibudhā nimeścetastadā 'bruvan | netreṣu sarvabhūtānāṃ vāyubhūtaścariṣyasi || 7.57.15 ||
translation: बाढम् certainly, इति thus, एव indeed, विबुधाः the gods, निमेः of Nimi, चेतः to the mind, तदा then, अब्रुवन् spoke, नेत्रेषु in the eyes, सर्वभूतानाम् of all beings, वायुभूतः having become air, चरिष्यसि you will move.
explanation: The gods then spoke to Nimi's spirit, saying, "Indeed, you will move as air within the eyes of all beings."

shloka_text: त्वत्कृते च निमिष्यन्ति चक्षूंषि पृथिवीपते । वायुभूतेन चरता विश्रमार्थं मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.57.16 ।।
transliteration: tvatkṛte ca nimiṣyanti cakṣūṃṣi pṛthivīpate | vāyubhūtena caratā viśramārthaṃ muhurmuhuḥ || 7.57.16 ||
translation: त्वत्कृते for your sake, च and, निमिष्यन्ति will blink, चक्षूंषि the eyes, पृथिवीपते O king, वायुभूतेन by you having become air, चरता moving, विश्रमार्थम् for the sake of rest, मुहुर्मुहुः repeatedly.
explanation: O King, for your sake, the eyes will blink repeatedly for rest, as you move within them as air.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु विबुधाः सर्वे जग्मुर्यथागतम् । ऋषयो ऽपि महात्मानो निमेर्देहं समाहरन् ।। 7.57.17 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu vibudhāḥ sarve jagmuryathāgatam | ṛṣayo 'pi mahātmāno nimerdehaṃ samāharan || 7.57.17 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तु indeed, विबुधाः the gods, सर्वे all, जग्मुः went, यथागतम् as they had come, ऋषयः the sages, अपि also, महात्मानः great-souled ones, निमेः of Nimi, देहम् the body, समाहरन् gathered.
explanation: Having spoken thus, all the gods departed to their respective abodes, and the great-souled sages then collected Nimi's body.

shloka_text: अरणिं तत्र निक्षिप्य मथनं चक्रुरोजसा । मन्त्रहोमैर्महात्मानः पुत्रहेतोर्निमेस्तदा ।। 7.57.18 ।।
transliteration: araṇiṃ tatra nikṣipya mathanaṃ cakrurojasā | mantrahomairmahātmānaḥ putrahetornimestadā || 7.57.18 ||
translation: अरणिम् the fire-stick, तत्र there, निक्षिप्य having placed, मथनम् churning, चक्रुः they performed, ओजसा with might, मन्त्रहोमैः with mantra-oblations, महात्मानः the great-souled ones, पुत्रहेतोः for the sake of a son, निमेः of Nimi, तदा then.
explanation: Then, the great-souled sages, for the sake of a son for Nimi, placed the fire-stick there and performed churning with might and mantra-oblations.

shloka_text: अरण्यां मथ्यामानायां प्रादुर्भूतो महातपाः । मथनान्मिथिरित्याहुर्जननाज्जनको ऽभवत् । यस्माद्विदेहात्सम्भूतो वैदेहस्तु ततः स्मृतः ।। 7.57.19 ।।
transliteration: araṇyāṃ mathyāmānāyāṃ prādurbhūto mahātapāḥ | mathanānmithirityāhurjananājjanako 'bhavat | yasmādvidehātsambhūto vaidehastu tataḥ smṛtaḥ || 7.57.19 ||
translation: अरण्याम् from the fire-stick, मथ्यमानायाम् being churned, प्रादुर्भूतः appeared, महातपाः a great ascetic, मथनात् from churning, मिथिरिति as Mithi, आहुः they called, जननात् from birth, जनकः Janaka, अभवत् became, यस्मात् because, विदेहात् from the bodyless (Nimi), सम्भूतः born, वैदेहः Vaideha, तु indeed, ततः therefore, स्मृतः remembered.
explanation: From the churned fire-stick, a great ascetic appeared, who was called Mithi because of the churning, became Janaka due to his birth, and was known as Vaideha because he was born from the bodyless Nimi.

shloka_text: एवं विदेहराजश्च जनकः पूर्वको ऽभवत् । मिथिर्नाम महातेजास्तेनायं मैथिलो ऽभवत् ।। 7.57.20 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ videharājaśca janakaḥ pūrvako 'bhavat | mithirnāma mahātejāstenāyaṃ maithilo 'bhavat || 7.57.20 ||
translation: एवं thus, विदेहराजः the king of Videha, च and, जनकः Janaka, पूर्वकः the ancestor, अभवत् was, मिथिर्नाम by the name Mithi, महातेजाः greatly effulgent, तेन by him, अयम् this, मैथिलः Maithila, अभवत् became.
explanation: Thus, the ancestor of Janaka, the king of Videha, was the greatly effulgent Mithi, from whom this region became known as Maithila. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 57 ।। Thus ends the fifty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा ।। 7.58.1 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvati rāme tu lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā | pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ jvalantamiva tejasā || 7.58.1 ||
translation: एवं thus, ब्रुवति while speaking, रामे Rama, तु indeed, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परवीरहा the destroyer of enemy heroes, प्रत्युवाच replied, महात्मानम् to the great-souled one, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, इव as if, तेजसा with splendor.
explanation: While Rama was speaking thus, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemy heroes, replied to the great-souled Rama, who was shining as if blazing with splendor.
comments: Lakshmana remarks how the consecrated Nimi would not forgive Vasishtha -- Rama replies that forbearance is not in every man and tells of Yayati, son of Nahusha, with his two wives, the favoured Sharmishtha, mother of Puru, and the slighted Devayani, mother of Yadu -- the grieving Devayani summons her father Shukra, who in wrath pronounces a curse.

shloka_text: महदद्भुतमाश्चर्यं विदेहस्य पुरातनम् । निर्वृत्तं राजशार्दूल वसिष्ठस्य निमेस्सह ।। 7.58.2 ।।
transliteration: mahadadbhutamāścaryaṃ videhasya purātanam | nirvṛttaṃ rājaśārdūla vasiṣṭhasya nimessaha || 7.58.2 ||
translation: महत् great, अद्भुतम् wonderful, आश्चर्यम् astonishing event, विदेहस्य of Videha, पुरातनम् ancient, निर्वृत्तम् occurred, राजशार्दूल O tiger among kings, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasishtha, निमेः of Nimi, सह with.
explanation: O tiger among kings, a great and ancient astonishing event concerning Videha occurred involving Vasishtha and Nimi.

shloka_text: निमिस्तु क्षत्रियः शूरो विशेषेण च दीक्षितः । न क्षमां कृतवान्राजा वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.58.3 ।।
transliteration: nimistu kṣatriyaḥ śūro viśeṣeṇa ca dīkṣitaḥ | na kṣamāṃ kṛtavānrājā vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.58.3 ||
translation: निमिः Nimi, तु but, क्षत्रियः a Kshatriya, शूरः brave, विशेषेण especially, च and, दीक्षितः initiated, न not, क्षमाम् forgiveness, कृतवान् showed, राजा the king, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasishtha, महात्मनः the great-souled one.
explanation: But King Nimi, a brave Kshatriya who was especially initiated into a sacrifice, did not show forgiveness towards the great-souled Vasishtha.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु तेनायं श्रीमान् क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः । उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् ।। 7.58.4 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu tenāyaṃ śrīmān kṣatriyapuṅgavaḥ | uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam || 7.58.4 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, तेन by him, अयम् this, श्रीमान् glorious, क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः best among Kshatriyas, उवाच spoke, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, वाक्यम् words, सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् skilled in all scriptures.
explanation: Thus addressed by him (Lakshmana), the glorious Rama, the best among Kshatriyas, spoke words to Lakshmana, who was skilled in all scriptures.

shloka_text: रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम् । न सर्वत्र क्षमा वीर पुरुषेषु प्रदृश्यते ।। 7.58.5 ।।
transliteration: rāmo ramayatāṃ śreṣṭho bhrātaraṃ dīptatejasam | na sarvatra kṣamā vīra puruṣeṣu pradṛśyate || 7.58.5 ||
translation: रामो Rama, रमयतां among those who delight, श्रेष्ठो the best, भ्रातरं to his brother, दीप्ततेजसम् of blazing splendor, न not, सर्वत्र everywhere, क्षमा forgiveness/patience, वीर O hero, पुरुषेषु among men, प्रदृश्यते is seen.
explanation: Rama, the best among those who delight, addresses his brother of blazing splendor, stating that forgiveness is not always observed among all men, O hero.

shloka_text: सौमित्रे दुःसहो रोषो यथा क्षान्तो ययातिना । सत्त्वानुगं पुरस्कृत्य तन्निबोध समाहितः ।। 7.58.6 ।।
transliteration: saumitre duḥsaho roṣo yathā kṣānto yayātinā | sattvānugaṃ puraskṛtya tannibodha samāhitaḥ || 7.58.6 ||
translation: सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra (Lakshmana), दुःसहो difficult to bear, रोषो anger, यथा as, क्षान्तो endured/forgiven, ययातिना by Yayati, सत्त्वानुगं following virtue/goodness, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front/considering, तत् that, निबोध understand, समाहितः with concentrated mind.
explanation: O Lakshmana, understand with a concentrated mind how the unbearable anger was endured by Yayati, considering the path of virtue.

shloka_text: नहुषस्य सुतो राजा ययातिः पौरवर्धनः । तस्य भार्याद्वयं सौम्य रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि ।। 7.58.7 ।।
transliteration: nahuṣasya suto rājā yayātiḥ pauravardhanaḥ | tasya bhāryādvayaṃ saumya rūpeṇāpratimaṃ bhuvi || 7.58.7 ||
translation: नहुषस्य of Nahusha, सुतो son, राजा king, ययातिः Yayati, पौरवर्धनः who increased the Paurava lineage, तस्य his, भार्याद्वयं two wives, सौम्य O gentle one, रूपेण in beauty, अप्रतिमं unequalled, भुवि on earth.
explanation: O gentle one, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha and augmenter of the Paurava lineage, had two wives whose beauty was unequalled on earth.

shloka_text: एका तु तस्य राजर्षेर्नाहुषस्य पुरस्कृता । शर्मिष्ठा नाम दैतेयी दुहिता वृषपर्वणः ।। 7.58.8 ।।
transliteration: ekā tu tasya rājarṣernāhuṣasya puraskṛtā | śarmiṣṭhā nāma daiteyī duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ || 7.58.8 ||
translation: एका one, तु indeed, तस्य of him, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, नाहुषस्य of Nahusha's son (Yayati), पुरस्कृता honored/chief, शर्मिष्ठा Sharmishtha, नाम named, दैतेयी daughter of a Daitya, दुहिता daughter, वृषपर्वणः of Vrishaparvan.
explanation: One of those wives, honored by the royal sage Yayati, son of Nahusha, was named Sharmishtha, the daughter of the Daitya king Vrishaparvan.

shloka_text: अन्या तूशनसः पत्नी ययातेः पुरुषर्षभ । न तु सा दयिता राज्ञो देवयानी सुमध्यमा ।। 7.58.9 ।।
transliteration: anyā tūśanasaḥ patnī yayāteḥ puruṣarṣabha | na tu sā dayitā rājño devayānī sumadhyamā || 7.58.9 ||
translation: अन्या the other, तु indeed, ऊशनसः of Ushanas (Shukra), पत्नी daughter (literally wife, but here refers to daughter of Ushanas who became Yayati's wife), ययातेः of Yayati, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, न not, तु but, सा she, दयिता beloved, राज्ञो of the king, देवयानी Devayani, सुमध्यमा slender-waisted.
explanation: O best among men, the other wife of Yayati was Devayani, the daughter of Ushanas, but that slender-waisted Devayani was not beloved by the king.

shloka_text: तयोः पुत्रौ तु सम्भूतौ रूपवन्तौ समाहितौ । शर्मिष्ठा ऽजनयत्पूरुं देवयानी यदुं तदा ।। 7.58.10 ।।
transliteration: tayoḥ putrau tu sambhūtau rūpavantau samāhitau | śarmiṣṭhā 'janayatpūruṃ devayānī yaduṃ tadā || 7.58.10 ||
translation: तयोः of them, पुत्रौ two sons, तु indeed, सम्भूतौ were born, रूपवन्तौ handsome, समाहितौ well-composed, शर्मिष्ठा Sharmishtha, अजनयत् gave birth to, पूरुं Puru, देवयानी Devayani, यदुं Yadu, तदा then,
explanation: Then, two handsome and well-composed sons were born to them; Sharmishtha gave birth to Puru, and Devayani gave birth to Yadu.

shloka_text: पूरुस्तु दयितो राज्ञो गुणैर्मातृकृतेन च । ततो दुःखसमाविष्टो यदुर्मातरमब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.11 ।।
transliteration: pūrustu dayito rājño guṇairmātṛkṛtena ca | tato duḥkhasamāviṣṭo yadurmātaramabravīt || 7.58.11 ||
translation: पूरुस्तु Puru, दयितो beloved, राज्ञो of the king, गुणैः by qualities, मातृकृतेन and because of his mother's situation, च and, ततो then, दुःखसमाविष्टो filled with sorrow, यदुः Yadu, मातरम् to his mother, अब्रवीत् spoke,
explanation: Puru was beloved by the king due to his qualities and his mother's situation, so Yadu, filled with sorrow, then spoke to his mother.

shloka_text: भार्गवस्य कुले जाता देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । सहसे हृद्गतं दुःखमवमानं च दुःसहम् ।। 7.58.12 ।।
transliteration: bhārgavasya kule jātā devasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ | sahase hṛdgataṃ duḥkhamavamānaṃ ca duḥsaham || 7.58.12 ||
translation: भार्गवस्य of Bhrigu, कुले in the lineage, जाता born, देवस्य of the divine one, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः whose deeds are unblemished, सहसे you endure, हृद्गतं deep-seated, दुःखम् sorrow, अवमानं insult, च and, दुःसहम् unbearable,
explanation: Yadu questioned his mother, Devayani, born in the lineage of the divine Bhrigu whose deeds are unblemished, asking why she endures such deep-seated sorrow and unbearable insult.

shloka_text: आवां च सहितौ देवि प्रविशाव हुताशनम् । राजा तु रमतां सार्धं दैत्यपुत्र्या बहुक्षपाः ।। 7.58.13 ।।
transliteration: āvāṃ ca sahitau devi praviśāva hutāśanam | rājā tu ramatāṃ sārdhaṃ daityaputryā bahukṣapāḥ || 7.58.13 ||
translation: आवां we two, च and, सहितौ together, देवि O goddess, प्रविशाव let us enter, हुताशनम् fire, राजा the king, तु but, रमतां let him enjoy, सार्धं with, दैत्यपुत्र्या the daughter of the Daitya, बहुक्षपाः for many nights,
explanation: Yadu proposed to his mother, "O goddess, let us both enter the fire together, while the king enjoys himself with the Daitya's daughter for many nights."

shloka_text: यदि वा सहनीयं ते मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि । क्षम त्वं न क्षमिष्ये ऽहं मरिष्यामि न संशयः ।। 7.58.14 ।।
transliteration: yadi vā sahanīyaṃ te māmanujñātumarhasi | kṣama tvaṃ na kṣamiṣye 'haṃ mariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ || 7.58.14 ||
translation: यदि if, वा or, सहनीयं bearable, ते by you, माम् me, अनुज्ञातुम् to permit, अर्हसि you should, क्षम endure, त्वं you, न not, क्षमिष्ये I will endure, अहं I, मरिष्यामि I will die, न not, संशयः doubt,
explanation: Yadu continued, "If this is bearable for you, then you should permit me; you may endure it, but I will not, and I will surely die."

shloka_text: पुत्रस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा परमार्तस्य रोदतः । देवयानी तु सङ्क्रुद्धा सस्मार पितरं तदा ।। 7.58.15 ।।
transliteration: putrasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā paramārtasya rodataḥ | devayānī tu saṅkruddhā sasmāra pitaraṃ tadā || 7.58.15 ||
translation: पुत्रस्य of the son, भाषितं words, श्रुत्वा having heard, परमार्तस्य of the greatly distressed, रोदतः weeping, देवयानी Devayani, तु indeed, सङ्क्रुद्धा greatly enraged, सस्मार remembered, पितरं father, तदा then.
explanation: Having heard the words of her greatly distressed and weeping son, Devayani became exceedingly enraged and then remembered her father.

shloka_text: इङ्गितं तदभिज्ञाय दुहितुर्भार्गवस्तदा । आगतस्त्वरितं तत्र देवयानी तु यत्र सा ।। 7.58.16 ।।
transliteration: iṅgitaṃ tadabhijñāya duhiturbhārgavastadā | āgatastvaritaṃ tatra devayānī tu yatra sā || 7.58.16 ||
translation: इङ्गितं sign, तत् that, अभिज्ञाय having understood, दुहितुः of the daughter, भार्गवः Bhargava, तदा then, आगतः came, त्वरितं quickly, तत्र there, देवयानी Devayani, तु indeed, यत्र where, सा she.
explanation: Then, understanding that sign of his daughter, Bhargava quickly came to where Devayani was.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा चाप्रकृतिस्थां तामप्रहृष्टामचेतनाम् । पिता दुहितरं वाक्यं किमेतदिति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.17 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā cāprakṛtisthāṃ tāmaprahṛṣṭāmacetanām | pitā duhitaraṃ vākyaṃ kimetaditi cābravīt || 7.58.17 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, च and, अप्रकृतिस्थां not in her natural state, तां her, अप्रहृष्टां unhappy, अचेतनाम् distraught, पिता father, दुहितरं to the daughter, वाक्यं words, किम् what, एतत् this, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: And having seen her in a disturbed, unhappy, and distraught state, the father spoke to his daughter, asking, "What is this?"

shloka_text: पृच्छन्तमसकृत्तं वै भार्गवं दीप्ततेजसम् । देवयानी तु सङ्क्रुद्धा पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.18 ।।
transliteration: pṛcchantamasakṛttaṃ vai bhārgavaṃ dīptatejasam | devayānī tu saṅkruddhā pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt || 7.58.18 ||
translation: पृच्छन्तं asking, असकृत् repeatedly, तं him, वै indeed, भार्गवं to Bhargava, दीप्ततेजसम् of blazing splendor, देवयानी Devayani, तु indeed, सङ्क्रुद्धा greatly enraged, पितरं to the father, वाक्यं words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: To that Bhargava of blazing splendor, who was repeatedly asking her, Devayani, greatly enraged, indeed spoke these words to her father.

shloka_text: अहमग्निं विषं तीक्ष्णमपो वा मुनिसत्तम । भक्षयिष्ये प्रवेक्ष्यामि न तु शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम् ।। 7.58.19 ।।
transliteration: ahamagniṃ viṣaṃ tīkṣṇamapo vā munisattama | bhakṣayiṣye pravekṣyāmi na tu śakṣyāmi jīvitum || 7.58.19 ||
translation: अहं I, अग्निं fire, विषं poison, तीक्ष्णं potent, अपो water, वा or, मुनिसत्तम O best of sages, भक्षयिष्ये I will consume, प्रवेक्ष्यामि I will enter, न not, तु but, शक्ष्यामि I will be able, जीवितुम् to live.
explanation: O best of sages, I will consume fire or potent poison, or I will enter water, but I will not be able to live.

shloka_text: न मां त्वमवजानीषे दुःखितामवमानिताम् । वृक्षस्यावज्ञया ब्रह्मंश्छिद्यन्ते वृक्षजीविनः ।। 7.58.20 ।।
transliteration: na māṃ tvamavajānīṣe duḥkhitāmavamānitām | vṛkṣasyāvajñayā brahmaṃśchidyante vṛkṣajīvinaḥ || 7.58.20 ||
translation: न not, माम् me, त्वम् you, अवजानीषे disregard, दुःखिताम् distressed, अवमानिताम् humiliated, वृक्षस्य of a tree, अवज्ञया by disrespect, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, छिद्यन्ते are cut off, वृक्षजीविनः tree-dwellers.
explanation: Indrani complains to Chyavana that Nahusha disregards her, who is distressed and humiliated, just as tree-dwellers are destroyed by disrespecting the tree.

shloka_text: अवज्ञया च राजर्षिः परिभूय च भार्गव । मय्यवज्ञां प्रयुङ्क्ते हि न च मां बहु मन्यते ।। 7.58.21 ।।
transliteration: avajñayā ca rājarṣiḥ paribhūya ca bhārgava | mayyavajñāṃ prayuṅkte hi na ca māṃ bahu manyate || 7.58.21 ||
translation: अवज्ञया with disrespect, च and, राजर्षिः the royal sage (Nahusha), परिभूय having insulted, च and, भार्गव O son of Bhrigu (Chyavana), मयि towards me, अवज्ञाम् disrespect, प्रयुङ्क्ते he shows, हि indeed, न not, च and, माम् me, बहु highly, मन्यते he regards.
explanation: Indrani further complains to Chyavana, stating that the royal sage Nahusha, having insulted her, indeed shows disrespect towards her and does not regard her highly.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कोपेनाभिपरिप्लुतः । व्याहर्तुमुपचक्राम भार्गवो नहुषात्मजम् ।। 7.58.22 ।।
transliteration: tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā kopenābhipariplutaḥ | vyāhartumupacakrāma bhārgavo nahuṣātmajam || 7.58.22 ||
translation: तस्याः her, तत् that, वचनम् speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, कोपेन with anger, अभिपरिप्लुतः overwhelmed, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्राम he began, भार्गवः the son of Bhrigu (Chyavana), नहुषात्मजम् to Nahusha (descendant of Nahusha).
explanation: Having heard her words, Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu, was overwhelmed with anger and began to speak to Nahusha.

shloka_text: यस्मान्मामवजानीषे नाहुष त्वं दुरात्मवान् । जरया परया जीर्णः शैथिल्यमुपयास्यसि ।। 7.58.23 ।।
transliteration: yasmānmāmavajānīṣe nāhuṣa tvaṃ durātmavān | jarayā parayā jīrṇaḥ śaithilyamupayāsyasi || 7.58.23 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, माम् me, अवजानीषे you disregard, नाहुष O Nahusha, त्वम् you, दुरात्मवान् evil-minded, जरया by old age, परया extreme, जीर्णः worn out, शैथिल्यम् weakness, उपयास्यसि you will attain.
explanation: Chyavana cursed Nahusha, declaring that because the evil-minded Nahusha disregarded him, he would become extremely worn out by old age and attain great weakness.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दुहितरं समाश्वास्य च भार्गवः । पुनर्जगाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्भवनं स्वं महायशाः ।। 7.58.24 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā duhitaraṃ samāśvāsya ca bhārgavaḥ | punarjagāma brahmarṣirbhavanaṃ svaṃ mahāyaśāḥ || 7.58.24 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, दुहितरम् to his daughter, समाश्वास्य having comforted, च and, भार्गवः the son of Bhrigu (Chyavana), पुनः again, जगाम he went, ब्रह्मर्षिः the Brahmarshi, भवनम् to his abode, स्वम् his own, महायशाः highly renowned.
explanation: Having thus spoken and comforted his daughter, the highly renowned Brahmarshi Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu, returned to his own abode.

shloka_text: स एवमुक्त्वा द्विजपुङ्गवाग्र्यः सुतां समाश्वास्य च देवयानीम् । पुनर्ययौ सूर्यसमानतेजा दत्त्वा च शापं नहुषात्मजाय ।। 7.58.25 ।।
transliteration: sa evamuktvā dvijapuṅgavāgryaḥ sutāṃ samāśvāsya ca devayānīm | punaryayau sūryasamānatejā dattvā ca śāpaṃ nahuṣātmajāya || 7.58.25 ||
translation: सः he, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, द्विजपुङ्गवाग्र्यः the foremost among Brahmins, सुताम् his daughter, समाश्वास्य having consoled, च and, देवयानीम् Devayani, पुनः again, ययौ went, सूर्यसमानतेजाः having splendor equal to the sun, दत्त्वा having given, च and, शापम् a curse, नहुषात्मजाय to the son of Nahusha.
explanation: Having thus spoken, the foremost Brahmin Shukra, after consoling his daughter Devayani and cursing Yayati, the son of Nahusha, departed again with a splendor like the sun. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 58 ।। Thus ends the fifty-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तूशनसं क्रुद्धं तदा ऽ ऽर्तो नहुषात्मजः । जरां परमिकां प्राप्य यदुं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.59.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tūśanasaṃ kruddhaṃ tadā ' 'rto nahuṣātmajaḥ | jarāṃ paramikāṃ prāpya yaduṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.59.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, ऊशनसम् Ushanas (Shukra), क्रुद्धम् angry, तदा then, आर्तः distressed, नहुषात्मजः the son of Nahusha (Yayati), जराम् old age, परमिकाम् extreme, प्राप्य having obtained, यदुम् to Yadu, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard that Ushanas was angry, the distressed son of Nahusha, Yayati, then, having immediately obtained extreme old age, spoke these words to Yadu.
comments: Cursed with premature old age by Shukra, Yayati asks his sons to bear it; Yadu refuses but Puru accepts -- young again, Yayati enjoys life for ages, then returns the burden to Puru, anoints him king, and curses the refusing Yadu, whose line is cast out -- Rama draws the lesson of forbearance, and as he finishes, dawn breaks.

shloka_text: यदो त्वमसि धर्मज्ञो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम् । जरां परमिकां पुत्र भोगै रंस्ये महायशः ।। 7.59.2 ।।
transliteration: yado tvamasi dharmajño madarthaṃ pratigṛhyatām | jarāṃ paramikāṃ putra bhogai raṃsye mahāyaśaḥ || 7.59.2 ||
translation: यदो O Yadu, त्वम् you, असि are, धर्मज्ञः knower of dharma, मदर्थम् for my sake, प्रतिगृह्यताम् let it be accepted (by you), जराम् old age, परमिकाम् extreme, पुत्र O son, भोगैः with enjoyments, रंस्ये I shall delight, महायशः O greatly renowned one.
explanation: Yayati said, "O Yadu, you are a knower of righteousness; for my sake, please accept this extreme old age, O son, so that I, O greatly renowned one, may delight in enjoyments."

shloka_text: न तावत्कृतकृत्यो ऽस्मि विषयेषु नरर्षभ । अनुभूय तदा कामं ततः प्राप्स्याम्यहं जराम् ।। 7.59.3 ।।
transliteration: na tāvatkṛtakṛtyo 'smi viṣayeṣu nararṣabha | anubhūya tadā kāmaṃ tataḥ prāpsyāmyahaṃ jarām || 7.59.3 ||
translation: न not, तावत् yet, कृतकृत्यः fulfilled (my desires), अस्मि I am, विषयेषु in worldly pleasures, नरर्षभ O best among men, अनुभूय having experienced, तदा then, कामम् desire, ततः thereafter, प्राप्स्यामि I shall obtain, अहम् I, जराम् old age.
explanation: Yayati continued, "O best among men, I am not yet satisfied with worldly pleasures; only after fully experiencing my desires will I then accept old age."

shloka_text: यदुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच नरर्षभम् । पुत्रस्ते दयितः पूरुः प्रतिगृह्णातु वै जराम् ।। 7.59.4 ।।
transliteration: yadustadvacanaṃ śrutvā pratyuvāca nararṣabham | putraste dayitaḥ pūruḥ pratigṛhṇātu vai jarām || 7.59.4 ||
translation: यदुः Yadu, तत् those, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रत्युवाच replied, नरर्षभम् to the best among men, पुत्रः son, ते your, दयितः beloved, पूरुः Puru, प्रतिगृह्णातु let him accept, वै indeed, जराम् old age.
explanation: Having heard those words, Yadu replied to his father, the best among men, saying, "Let your beloved son Puru indeed accept this old age."

shloka_text: बहिष्कृतो ऽहमर्थेषु सन्निकर्षाच्च पार्थिव । प्रतिगृह्णातु वै राजन्क सहाश्नाति भोजनम् ।। 7.59.5 ।।
transliteration: bahiṣkṛto 'hamartheṣu sannikarṣācca pārthiva | pratigṛhṇātu vai rājanka sahāśnāti bhojanam || 7.59.5 ||
translation: बहिष्कृतो excluded, अहम् I, अर्थेषु from worldly pleasures, सन्निकर्षात् due to old age, च and, पार्थिव O king, प्रतिगृह्णातु let him accept, वै indeed, राजन् O king, क who, सहाश्नाति eats together, भोजनम् food.
explanation: O King, I am excluded from worldly pleasures due to old age; who indeed would eat food with me?

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत् । इयं जरा महाबाहो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ।। 7.59.6 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā pūrumathābravīt | iyaṃ jarā mahābāho madarthaṃ pratigṛhyatām || 7.59.6 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, राजा the king, पूरुम् to Puru, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, इयम् this, जरा old age, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, मदर्थम् for my sake, प्रतिगृह्यताम् let it be accepted.
explanation: Having heard his words, the king then spoke to Puru, saying, "O mighty-armed one, let this old age be accepted for my sake."

shloka_text: नाहुषेणैवमुक्तस्तु पूरुः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् । धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि शासने ऽस्मि तव स्थितः ।। 7.59.7 ।।
transliteration: nāhuṣeṇaivamuktastu pūruḥ prāñjalirabravīt | dhanyo 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi śāsane 'smi tava sthitaḥ || 7.59.7 ||
translation: नाहुषेण by Nahusha's son, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, पूरुः Puru, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, अब्रवीत् spoke, धन्यः blessed, अस्मि I am, अनुगृहीतः favored, अस्मि I am, शासने in the command, अस्मि I am, तव your, स्थितः abiding.
explanation: Thus addressed by Yayati, Puru spoke with folded hands, saying, "I am blessed, I am favored, and I abide by your command."

shloka_text: पूरोर्वचनमाज्ञाय नाहुषः परया मुदा । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे जरां सङ्क्रामयच्च ताम् ।। 7.59.8 ।।
transliteration: pūrorvacanamājñāya nāhuṣaḥ parayā mudā | praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe jarāṃ saṅkrāmayacca tām || 7.59.8 ||
translation: पूरोः Puru's, वचनम् word, आज्ञाय having understood, नाहुषः Nahusha's son, परया with great, मुदा joy, प्रहर्षम् delight, अतुलम् unequalled, लेभे obtained, जराम् old age, सङ्क्रामयत् transferred, च and, ताम् that.
explanation: Having understood Puru's words, Yayati obtained unequalled delight with great joy and transferred that old age to him.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा तरुणः प्राप्य यज्ञान्सहस्रशः । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि पालयामास मेदिनीम् ।। 7.59.9 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā taruṇaḥ prāpya yajñānsahasraśaḥ | bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi pālayāmāsa medinīm || 7.59.9 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, सः that, राजा king, तरुणः young, प्राप्य having obtained, यज्ञान् sacrifices, सहस्रशः by thousands, बहुवर्षसहस्राणि for many thousands of years, पालयमास ruled, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: Thereafter, that king, having become young again, performed thousands of sacrifices and ruled the earth for many thousands of years.

shloka_text: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत् । आनयस्व जरां पुत्र न्यासं निर्यातयस्व मे ।। 7.59.10 ।।
transliteration: atha dīrghasya kālasya rājā pūrumathābravīt | ānayasva jarāṃ putra nyāsaṃ niryātayasva me || 7.59.10 ||
translation: अथ then, दीर्घस्य कालस्य after a long time, राजा the king, पूरुम् to Puru, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, आनयस्व bring back, जराम् old age, पुत्र O son, न्यासम् the deposit, निर्यातयस्व return, मे to me.
explanation: After a long time, King Yayati then spoke to Puru, saying, "O son, bring back my old age; return the deposit to me."

shloka_text: न्यासभूता मया पुत्र त्वयि सङ्क्रामिता जरा । तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि तां जरां मा व्यथां कृथाः ।। 7.59.11 ।।
transliteration: nyāsabhūtā mayā putra tvayi saṅkrāmitā jarā | tasmātpratigrahīṣyāmi tāṃ jarāṃ mā vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ || 7.59.11 ||
translation: न्यासभूता as a deposit, मया by me, पुत्र O son, त्वयि in you, सङ्क्रामिता transferred, जरा old age, तस्मात् therefore, प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि I will take back, ताम् that, जराम् old age, मा व्यथाम् कृथाः do not feel distressed.
explanation: O son, that old age was transferred to you by me as a deposit; therefore, I will take it back, so do not feel distressed.

shloka_text: प्रीतश्चास्मि महाबाहो शासनस्य प्रतिग्रहात् । त्वां चाहमभिषेक्ष्यामि प्रीतियुक्तो नराधिपम् ।। 7.59.12 ।।
transliteration: prītaścāsmi mahābāho śāsanasya pratigrahāt | tvāṃ cāhamabhiṣekṣyāmi prītiyukto narādhipam || 7.59.12 ||
translation: प्रीतः pleased, च and, अस्मि I am, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, शासनस्य of the command, प्रतिग्रहात् by the acceptance, त्वाम् you, च and, अहम् I, अभिषेक्ष्यामि will anoint, प्रीतियुक्तः filled with affection, नराधिपम् as king of men.
explanation: O mighty-armed one, I am pleased by your acceptance of my command, and I will affectionately anoint you as the king of men.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा सुतं पूरुं ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः । देवयानीसुतं क्रुद्धो राजा वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.59.13 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā sutaṃ pūruṃ yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ | devayānīsutaṃ kruddho rājā vākyamuvāca ha || 7.59.13 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, सुतम् to son, पूरुम् Puru, ययातिः Yayati, नहुषात्मजः son of Nahusha, देवयानीसुतम् to Devayani's son, क्रुद्धः enraged, राजा the king, वाक्यम् words, उवाच ह spoke indeed.
explanation: Having thus spoken to his son Puru, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha, then spoke enraged words to Devayani's son.

shloka_text: राक्षसस्त्वं मया जातः पुत्ररूपो दुरासदः । प्रतिहंसि ममाज्ञां यत् प्रजार्थे विफलो भव ।। 7.59.14 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasastvaṃ mayā jātaḥ putrarūpo durāsadaḥ | pratihaṃsi mamājñāṃ yat prajārthe viphalo bhava || 7.59.14 ||
translation: राक्षसः a demon, त्वम् you, मया by me, जातः born, पुत्ररूपः in the form of a son, दुरासदः wicked, प्रतिहंसि you reject, मम आज्ञाम् my command, यत् because, प्रजार्थे for the purpose of progeny, विफलः fruitless, भव become.
explanation: You are a wicked demon born by me in the form of a son, because you reject my command, you shall become fruitless in terms of progeny.

shloka_text: पितरं गुरुभूतं मां यस्मात्त्वमवमन्यसे । राक्षसान्यातुधानांस्त्वं जनयिष्यसि दारुणान् ।। 7.59.15 ।।
transliteration: pitaraṃ gurubhūtaṃ māṃ yasmāttvamavamanyase | rākṣasānyātudhānāṃstvaṃ janayiṣyasi dāruṇān || 7.59.15 ||
translation: पितरं father, गुरुभूतं who is like a preceptor, मां me, यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, अवमन्यसे disrespect, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, यातुधानान् Yatudhanas, त्वम् you, जनयिष्यसि will give birth to, दारुणान् terrible.
explanation: Because you disrespect me, your father and preceptor, you will give birth to terrible Rakshasas and Yatudhanas.

shloka_text: न तु सोमकुलोत्पन्ने वंशे स्थास्यति दुर्मतेः । वंशो ऽपि भवतस्तुल्यो दुर्विनीतो भविष्यति ।। 7.59.16 ।।
transliteration: na tu somakulotpanne vaṃśe sthāsyati durmateḥ | vaṃśo 'pi bhavatastulyo durvinīto bhaviṣyati || 7.59.16 ||
translation: न not, तु indeed, सोमकुलोत्पन्ने born in the Lunar dynasty, वंशे in the lineage, स्थास्यति will remain, दुर्मतेः of the evil-minded one, वंशो lineage, अपि also, भवतः your, तुल्यः similar, दुर्विनीतः ill-behaved, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: The lineage of that evil-minded one (Yati) will not endure in the Lunar dynasty, and your own progeny will also be ill-behaved like you.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिः पूरुं राज्यविवर्धनम् । अभिषेकेण सम्पूज्य आश्रमं प्रविवेश ह ।। 7.59.17 ।।
transliteration: tamevamuktvā rājarṣiḥ pūruṃ rājyavivardhanam | abhiṣekeṇa sampūjya āśramaṃ praviveśa ha || 7.59.17 ||
translation: तम् him, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having said, राजर्षिः the royal sage, पूरुं Puru, राज्यविवर्धनम् who would expand the kingdom, अभिषेकेण with coronation, सम्पूज्य having honored, आश्रमं hermitage, प्रविवेश entered, ह indeed.
explanation: Having thus spoken, the royal sage Yayati honored Puru, who was destined to expand the kingdom, with a coronation and then entered his hermitage.

shloka_text: ततः कालेन महता दिष्टान्तमुपजग्मिवान् । त्रिदिवं सङ्गतो राजा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः ।। 7.59.18 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kālena mahatā diṣṭāntamupajagmivān | tridivaṃ saṅgato rājā yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ || 7.59.18 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, कालेन by time, महता great, दिष्टान्तम् end of destiny, उपजग्मिवान् reached, त्रिदिवं heaven, सङ्गतः went to, राजा king, ययातिः Yayati, नहुषात्मजः son of Nahusha.
explanation: After a long time, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha, reached the end of his life and ascended to heaven.

shloka_text: पूरुश्चकार तद्राज्यं धर्मेण महता वृतः । प्रतिष्ठाने पुरवरे काशिराज्ये महायशाः ।। 7.59.19 ।।
transliteration: pūruścakāra tadrājyaṃ dharmeṇa mahatā vṛtaḥ | pratiṣṭhāne puravare kāśirājye mahāyaśāḥ || 7.59.19 ||
translation: पूरुः Puru, चकार ruled, तद्राज्यं that kingdom, धर्मेण with righteousness, महता great, वृतः endowed with, प्रतिष्ठाने in Pratishthana, पुरवरे in the excellent city, काशिराज्ये in the kingdom of Kashi, महायशाः greatly renowned.
explanation: The greatly renowned Puru, endowed with great righteousness, ruled that kingdom from the excellent city of Pratishthana in the Kashi region.

shloka_text: यदुस्तु जनयामास यातुधानान्सहस्रशः । पुरे क्रौञ्चवने दुर्गे राजवंशबहिष्कृतः ।। 7.59.20 ।।
transliteration: yadustu janayāmāsa yātudhānānsahasraśaḥ | pure krauñcavane durge rājavaṃśabahiṣkṛtaḥ || 7.59.20 ||
translation: यदुस्तु Yadu, however, जनयामास begot, यातुधानान् Rākṣasas, सहस्रशः by thousands, पुरे in the region, क्रौञ्चवने of Krauñcavana, दुर्गे in a difficult-to-access place, राजवंशबहिष्कृतः excluded from the royal lineage.
explanation: King Yadu, having been excluded from the royal lineage, begot thousands of Rākṣasas in the inaccessible region of Krauñcavana.

shloka_text: एष तूशनसा मुक्तः शापोत्सर्गो ययातिना । धारितः क्षत्रधर्मेण यन्निमिश्च न चक्षमे ।। 7.59.21 ।।
transliteration: eṣa tūśanasā muktaḥ śāpotsargo yayātinā | dhāritaḥ kṣatradharmeṇa yannimiśca na cakṣame || 7.59.21 ||
translation: एषः this, तु indeed, उशनसा by Uśanas, मुक्तः given, शापोत्सर्गः the curse, ययातिना by Yayāti, धारितः was borne, क्षत्रधर्मेण by the duty of a Kṣatriya, यत् which, निमिश्च and Nimi, न not, चक्षमे tolerated.
explanation: This curse, given by Uśanas, was indeed borne by Yayāti due to his Kṣatriya duty, a burden which even Nimi could not tolerate.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं दर्शनं सर्वकारिणाम् । अनुवर्तामहे सौम्य दोषो न स्याद्यथा नृगे ।। 7.59.22 ।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ darśanaṃ sarvakāriṇām | anuvartāmahe saumya doṣo na syādyathā nṛge || 7.59.22 ||
translation: एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातम् has been narrated, दर्शनम् the lesson, सर्वकारिणाम् for all actions, अनुवर्तामहे we shall follow, सौम्य O gentle one, दोषः fault, न स्यात् may not be, यथा as, नृगे in Nṛga.
explanation: O gentle one, all this has been narrated to you as a lesson for all actions, so that we may follow it and avoid a fault like that of Nṛga.

shloka_text: इति कथयति रामे चन्द्रतुल्यानने च प्रविरलतरतारं व्योम जज्ञे तदानीम् । अरुणकिरणरक्ता दिग्बभौ चैव पूर्वा कुसुमरसविमुक्तं वस्त्रमाकुण्ठितेव ।। 7.59.23 ।।
transliteration: iti kathayati rāme candratulyānane ca praviralataratāraṃ vyoma jajñe tadānīm | aruṇakiraṇaraktā digbabhau caiva pūrvā kusumarasavimuktaṃ vastramākuṇṭhiteva || 7.59.23 ||
translation: इति thus, कथयति while speaking, रामे Rāma, चन्द्रतुल्यानने whose face was like the moon, च and, प्रविरलतरतारम् with stars becoming very sparse, व्योम the sky, जज्ञे became, तदानीम् at that time, अरुणकिरणरक्ता reddened by the rays of dawn, दिक् the direction, बभौ shone, चैव and indeed, पूर्वा the eastern, कुसुमरसविमुक्तम् a garment released from flower juice (faded), वस्त्रम् garment, आकुण्ठितेव as if rolled up.
explanation: As Rāma, whose face was like the moon, spoke thus, the sky at that time became very sparse with stars, and the eastern direction shone, reddened by the rays of dawn, like a faded garment being rolled up. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 59 ।। Thus ends the fifty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तयोः संवदतोरेवं रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तदा । वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च घर्मदा ।। 7.60.1 ।।
transliteration: tayoḥ saṃvadatorevaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇayostadā | vāsantikī niśā prāptā na śītā na ca gharmadā || 7.60.1 ||
translation: तयोः of those two, संवदतोः while conversing, एवम् thus, रामलक्ष्मणयोः of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, तदा then, वासन्तिकी of spring, निशा night, प्राप्ता arrived, न शीता not cold, न च nor, घर्मदा hot.
explanation: As Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa thus conversed, the spring night arrived, which was neither cold nor hot.
comments: At dawn Rama admits with honour the ascetics of the Yamuna bank, led by Chyavana, who bring offerings -- pledging his kingdom and his very life for the brahmins' sake, he asks their purpose -- the sages applaud a vow that earlier kings had shunned and beg his protection from a great fear that oppresses them.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपौर्वाह्णिकक्रियः । अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थो दर्शनं पौरकार्यवित् ।। 7.60.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtapaurvāhṇikakriyaḥ | abhicakrāma kākutstho darśanaṃ paurakāryavit || 7.60.2 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रभाते in the morning, विमले clear, कृतपौर्वाह्णिकक्रियः having performed the morning rituals, अभिचक्राम approached, काकुत्स्थो Kakutstha (Rama), दर्शनं the audience hall, पौरकार्यवित् knowing the affairs of the citizens.
explanation: Then, in the clear morning, Rama, having completed his morning rituals and being knowledgeable about the citizens' affairs, proceeded to the audience hall.

shloka_text: ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । एते प्रतिहता राजन्द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति तापसाः ।। 7.60.3 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sumantrastvāgamya rāghavaṃ vākyamabravīt | ete pratihatā rājandvāri tiṣṭhanti tāpasāḥ || 7.60.3 ||
translation: ततः then, सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य Sumantra having come, राघवं to Rama, वाक्यमब्रवीत् spoke words, एते these, प्रतिहता stopped, राजन् O King, द्वारि at the door, तिष्ठन्ति are standing, तापसाः ascetics.
explanation: Then Sumantra approached Rama and informed him, "O King, these ascetics are standing at the door, having been stopped."

shloka_text: भार्गवच्यवनं चैव पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । दर्शनं ते महाराज्ञश्चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः । प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः ।। 7.60.4 ।।
transliteration: bhārgavacyavanaṃ caiva puraskṛtya maharṣayaḥ | darśanaṃ te mahārājñaścodayanti kṛtatvarāḥ | prīyamāṇā naravyāghra yamunātīravāsinaḥ || 7.60.4 ||
translation: भार्गवच्यवनं Bhrigu's son Chyavana, चैव and indeed, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front, महर्षयः great sages, दर्शनं audience, ते your, महाराज्ञश्चोदयन्ति are urging (of the great king), कृतत्वराः eagerly, प्रीयमाणा pleased, नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, यमुनातीरवासिनः residents of the Yamuna bank.
explanation: These great sages, residents of the Yamuna bank and pleased to see you, O tiger among men, are eagerly requesting an audience with you, led by Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित् । प्रवेश्यन्तां महाभागा भार्गवप्रमुखा द्विजाः ।। 7.60.5 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ provāca dharmavit | praveśyantāṃ mahābhāgā bhārgavapramukhā dvijāḥ || 7.60.5 ||
translation: तस्य his, तद्वचनं those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामः Rama, प्रोवाच said, धर्मवित् knower of dharma, प्रवेश्यन्तां let them be admitted, महाभागा highly fortunate ones, भार्गवप्रमुखा led by Bhrigu's son, द्विजाः Brahmins.
explanation: Hearing those words, Rama, the knower of dharma, commanded that the revered Brahmins, led by Chyavana, be admitted.

shloka_text: राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । प्रवेशयामास तदा तापसान्सुदुरासदान् ।। 7.60.6 ।।
transliteration: rājñastvājñāṃ puraskṛtya dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ | praveśayāmāsa tadā tāpasānsudurāsadān || 7.60.6 ||
translation: राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां the king's command, पुरस्कृत्य honoring, द्वाःस्थो the doorkeeper, मूर्ध्नि on his head, कृताञ्जलिः having folded hands, प्रवेशयामास caused to enter, तदा then, तापसान्सुदुरासदान् the ascetics who were very difficult to approach.
explanation: Then, the doorkeeper, honoring the king's command by placing it on his head and with folded hands, admitted those ascetics who were otherwise very difficult to approach.

shloka_text: शतं समधिकं तत्र दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । प्रविष्टं राजभवनं तापसानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.60.7 ।।
transliteration: śataṃ samadhikaṃ tatra dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā | praviṣṭaṃ rājabhavanaṃ tāpasānāṃ mahātmanām || 7.60.7 ||
translation: शतं a hundred, समधिकं more than, तत्र there, दीप्यमानं shining, स्वतेजसा with their own splendor, प्रविष्टं entered, राजभवनं the royal palace, तापसानां of ascetics, महात्मनाम् of great souls.
explanation: More than a hundred great-souled ascetics, shining with their own spiritual radiance, entered the royal palace.

shloka_text: ते द्विजाः पूर्णकलशैः सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतैः । गृहीत्वा फलमूलं च रामस्याभ्याहरन्बहु ।। 7.60.8 ।।
transliteration: te dvijāḥ pūrṇakalaśaiḥ sarvatīrthāmbusatkṛtaiḥ | gṛhītvā phalamūlaṃ ca rāmasyābhyāharanbahu || 7.60.8 ||
translation: ते those, द्विजाः Brahmins, पूर्णकलशैः with full pitchers, सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतैः honored with waters from all sacred fords, गृहीत्वा having taken, फलमूलं fruits and roots, च and, रामस्य for Rama, अभ्याहरन् brought, बहु much.
explanation: Those Brahmins brought many offerings for Rama, including full pitchers honored with waters from all sacred pilgrimage sites, and various fruits and roots.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः । तीर्थोदकानि सर्वाणि फलानि विविधानि च ।। 7.60.9 ।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tu tatsarvaṃ rāmaḥ prītipuraskṛtaḥ | tīrthodakāni sarvāṇi phalāni vividhāni ca || 7.60.9 ||
translation: प्रतिगृह्य having received, तु indeed, तत्सर्वं all that, रामः Rama, प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः honored with affection, तीर्थोदकानि sacred waters, सर्वाणि all, फलानि fruits, विविधानि various, च and.
explanation: Rama, showing great affection, received all those offerings, including all the sacred waters and various fruits.

shloka_text: उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन् । इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम् ।। 7.60.10 ।।
transliteration: uvāca ca mahābāhuḥ sarvāneva mahāmunīn | imānyāsanamukhyāni yathārhamupaviśyatām || 7.60.10 ||
translation: उवाच said, च and, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed (Rama), सर्वानेव all indeed, महामुनीन् to the great sages, इमानि these, आसनमुख्यानि excellent seats, यथार्हं as appropriate, उपविश्यताम् may be sat upon.
explanation: The mighty-armed Rama then addressed all the great sages, inviting them to take these excellent seats as was appropriate for their stature.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः । बृसीषु रुचिराख्यासु निषेदुः काञ्चनीषु ते ।। 7.60.11 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ | bṛsīṣu rucirākhyāsu niṣeduḥ kāñcanīṣu te || 7.60.11 ||
translation: रामस्य Rama's, भाषितं words, श्रुत्वा having heard, सर्व all, एव indeed, महर्षयः great sages, बृसीषु on the seats, रुचिराख्यासु beautiful, निषेदुः sat down, काञ्चनीषु golden, ते they.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, all the great sages sat down on the beautiful, well-known golden seats.

shloka_text: उपविष्टानृषींस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरञ्जयः । प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.60.12 ।।
transliteration: upaviṣṭānṛṣīṃstatra dṛṣṭvā parapurañjayaḥ | prayataḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā rāghavo vākyamabravīt || 7.60.12 ||
translation: उपविष्टान् seated, ऋषीन् sages, तत्र there, दृष्ट्वा having seen, परपुरञ्जयः the conqueror of enemy cities, प्रयतः reverent, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, राघवः Rama, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having seen the sages seated there, Rama, the conqueror of enemy cities, reverently and with folded hands, spoke these words.

shloka_text: किमागमनकार्यं वः किं करोमि समाहितः । आज्ञाप्यो ऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम् ।। 7.60.13 ।।
transliteration: kimāgamanakāryaṃ vaḥ kiṃ karomi samāhitaḥ | ājñāpyo 'haṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sarvakāmakaraḥ sukham || 7.60.13 ||
translation: किम् what, आगमनकार्यम् purpose of coming, वः your, किम् what, करोमि shall I do, समाहितः attentively, आज्ञाप्यः to be commanded, अहम् I, महर्षीणाम् of the great sages, सर्वकामकरः one who fulfills all desires, सुखम् easily.
explanation: He asked what the purpose of their visit was and what he could do for them attentively, declaring himself to be at the command of the great sages, ready to fulfill all their desires easily.

shloka_text: इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम् । सर्वमेतद्द्विदार्थं मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि वः ।। 7.60.14 ।।
transliteration: idaṃ rājyaṃ ca sakalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca hṛdi sthitam | sarvametaddvidārthaṃ me satyametadbravīmi vaḥ || 7.60.14 ||
translation: इदम् this, राज्यम् kingdom, च and, सकलम् entire, जीवितम् life, च and, हृदि in the heart, स्थितम् situated, सर्वम् all, एतत् this, द्विदार्थम् for the sake of the Brahmins, मे my, सत्यम् truth, एतत् this, ब्रवीमि I speak, वः to you.
explanation: Rama declared that his entire kingdom, his very life, and everything he possessed was for the sake of the Brahmins, and he spoke this truth to them.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम् ।। 7.60.15 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sādhukāro mahānabhūt | ṛṣīṇāmugratapasāṃ yamunātīravāsinām || 7.60.15 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, साधुकारः applause, महान् great, अभूत् occurred, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, उग्रतपसाम् of severe austerities, यमुनातीरवासिनाम् residing on the banks of Yamuna.
explanation: Having heard his words, a great applause arose from the sages of severe austerities who resided on the banks of the Yamuna.

shloka_text: ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः ।। 7.60.16 ।।
transliteration: ūcuśca te mahātmāno harṣeṇa mahatā vṛtāḥ | upapannaṃ naraśreṣṭha tavaiva bhuvi nānyataḥ || 7.60.16 ||
translation: ऊचुः they said, च and, ते those, महात्मानः great souls, हर्षेण with joy, महता great, वृताः filled, उपपन्नम् fitting, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, तव your, एव only, भुवि on earth, न not, अन्यतः from anyone else.
explanation: And those great souls, filled with great joy, said, "O best among men, such a statement is fitting only for you on earth, and for no one else."

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नतिक्रान्ता महाबलाः । कार्यस्य गौरवं मत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन् ।। 7.60.17 ।।
transliteration: bahavaḥ pārthivā rājannatikrāntā mahābalāḥ | kāryasya gauravaṃ matvā pratijñāṃ nābhyarocayan || 7.60.17 ||
translation: बहवः many, पार्थिवाः kings, राजन् O King, अतिक्रान्ताः who came before, महाबलाः very powerful, कार्यस्य of the task, गौरवम् gravity, मत्वा having considered, प्रतिज्ञाम् the vow, न not, अभ्यरोचयन् undertook.
explanation: Many powerful kings who came before you, O King, considered the gravity of this task and did not undertake the vow.

shloka_text: त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम् । ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो महाभयात्ऺत्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि ।। 7.60.18 ।।
transliteration: tvayā punarbrāhmaṇagauravādiyaṃ kṛtā pratijñā hyanavekṣya kāraṇam | tataśca kartā hyasi nātra saṃśayo mahābhayātऺtrātumṛṣīṃstvamarhasi || 7.60.18 ||
translation: त्वया by you, पुनर् but, ब्राह्मणगौरवात् out of respect for Brahmins, इयम् this, कृता made, प्रतिज्ञा vow, हि indeed, अनवेक्ष्य without considering, कारणम् the reason, ततश्च therefore, कर्ता the doer, हि indeed, असि you are, न not, अत्र here, संशयः doubt, महाभयात् from great fear, त्रातुम् to protect, ऋषीन् the sages, त्वम् you, अर्हसि ought.
explanation: But you, out of respect for Brahmins, made this vow without considering the difficulty, and therefore you are indeed the one who will accomplish it, without a doubt, and you ought to protect the sages from great fear. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 60 ।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवद्भिर्ऋषिभिः काकुत्स्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । किं कार्यं ब्रूत मुनयो भयं तावदपैतु वः ।। 7.61.1 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvadbhirṛṣibhiḥ kākutstho vākyamabravīt | kiṃ kāryaṃ brūta munayo bhayaṃ tāvadapaitu vaḥ || 7.61.1 ||
translation: एवम् thus, ब्रुवद्भिः by those speaking, ऋषिभिः by the sages, काकुत्स्थः Kakutstha (Rama), वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, किम् what, कार्यम् task, ब्रूत tell, मुनयः O sages, भयम् fear, तावत् first of all, अपैतु let it depart, वः from you.
explanation: When the sages spoke thus, Rama replied, "O sages, tell me what the task is; first of all, let your fear depart."
comments: Chyavana tells the origin of their fear: the devout demon Madhu won from Rudra a mighty trident that reduces any challenger to ashes, to pass to one of his sons -- Madhu's son Lavana, born of Kumbhinasi, wields it to torment the three worlds and the ascetics -- and, since Ravana is slain, they implore Rama to deliver them from Lavana.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे भार्गवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । भयानां शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर ।। 7.61.2 ।।
transliteration: tathā bruvati kākutsthe bhārgavo vākyamabravīt | bhayānāṃ śṛṇu yanmūlaṃ deśasya ca nareśvara || 7.61.2 ||
translation: तथा thus, ब्रुवति when speaking, काकुत्स्थे Kakutstha (Rama), भार्गवः Bhargava (Chyavana), वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, भयानाम् of the fears, शृणु listen, यत् which, मूलम् origin, देशस्य of the region, च and, नरेश्वर O lord of men.
explanation: When Rama spoke thus, Bhargava (Chyavana) replied, "O King, listen to the origin of our fears and of this region."

shloka_text: पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन्दैतेयः सुमहाबलः । लोलापुत्रो ऽभवज्ज्येष्ठो मधुर्नाम महासुरः ।। 7.61.3 ।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge rājandaiteyaḥ sumahābalaḥ | lolāputro 'bhavajjyeṣṭho madhurnāma mahāsuraḥ || 7.61.3 ||
translation: पूर्वम् formerly, कृतयुगे in the Krita Yuga, राजन् O King, दैतेयः a Daitya, सुमहाबलः exceedingly powerful, लोलापुत्रः son of Lola, अभवत् was, ज्येष्ठः the eldest, मधुः Madhu, नाम named, महासुरः a great demon.
explanation: O King, formerly in the Krita Yuga, there was an exceedingly powerful Daitya, the eldest son of Lola, named Madhu, who was a great demon.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः । सुरैश्च परमोदारैः प्रीतिस्तस्यातुला ऽभवत् ।। 7.61.4 ।।
transliteration: brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca buddhyā ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ | suraiśca paramodāraiḥ prītistasyātulā 'bhavat || 7.61.4 ||
translation: ब्रह्मण्यश्च one devoted to Brahmins and, शरण्यश्च one who offers refuge and, बुद्ध्या by intellect, च and, परिनिष्ठितः firmly established, सुरैश्च with gods and, परमोदारैः exceedingly generous, प्रीतिः affection, तस्य for him, अतुला unequalled, अभवत् was
explanation: He was devoted to Brahmins, a protector, and firmly resolved in his wisdom, and he had an unequalled affection for the exceedingly generous gods.

shloka_text: स मधुर्वीर्यसम्पन्नो धर्मे च सुसमाहितः । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि रुद्रप्रीत्या ऽकरोत्तपः ।। 7.61.5 ।।
transliteration: sa madhurvīryasampanno dharme ca susamāhitaḥ | bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi rudraprītyā 'karottapaḥ || 7.61.5 ||
translation: सः he, मधुः Madhu, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, धर्मे in righteousness, च and, सुसमाहितः well-established, बहुवर्षसहस्राणि for many thousands of years, रुद्रप्रीत्या to please Rudra, अकरोत् performed, तपः penance
explanation: That Madhu, endowed with great valor and steadfast in righteousness, performed penance for many thousands of years to please Rudra.

shloka_text: रुद्रः प्रीतो ऽभवत्तस्मै वरं दातुं ययौ च सः । बहुमानाच्च रुद्रेण दत्तस्तस्याद्भुतो वरः ।। 7.61.6 ।।
transliteration: rudraḥ prīto 'bhavattasmai varaṃ dātuṃ yayau ca saḥ | bahumānācca rudreṇa dattastasyādbhuto varaḥ || 7.61.6 ||
translation: रुद्रः Rudra, प्रीतः pleased, अभवत् became, तस्मै for him, वरं boon, दातुम् to give, ययौ went, च and, सः he (Rudra), बहुमानात् with great respect, च and, रुद्रेण by Rudra, दत्तः given, तस्य for him, अद्भुतः wonderful, वरः boon
explanation: Rudra became pleased with him and went to grant a boon, and with great respect, an extraordinary boon was given to him by Rudra.

shloka_text: शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य महावीर्यं महाप्रभम् । ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह ।। 7.61.7 ।।
transliteration: śūlaṃ śūlādviniṣkṛṣya mahāvīryaṃ mahāprabham | dadau mahātmā suprīto vākyaṃ caitaduvāca ha || 7.61.7 ||
translation: शूलं trident, शूलात् from his own trident, विनिष्कृष्य extracting, महावीर्यं of great power, महाप्रभम् of great splendor, ददौ gave, महात्मा the great-souled one, सुप्रीतः very pleased, वाक्यं words, च and, एतत् this, उवाच spoke, ह indeed
explanation: The great-souled Rudra, very pleased, extracted a trident of great power and splendor from his own trident, gave it, and indeed spoke these words.

shloka_text: त्वयायमतुलो धर्मो मत्प्रसादकरः कृतः । प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.61.8 ।।
transliteration: tvayāyamatulo dharmo matprasādakaraḥ kṛtaḥ | prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmyāyudhamuttamam || 7.61.8 ||
translation: त्वया by you, अयम् this, अतुलः unequalled, धर्मः righteousness, मत् my, प्रसादकरः pleasing, कृतः done, प्रीत्या with affection, परमया supreme, युक्तः endowed, ददामि I give, आयुधम् weapon, उत्तमम् excellent
explanation: “This unequalled act of righteousness, which pleases me, has been performed by you; filled with supreme affection, I give you this excellent weapon.”

shloka_text: यावत्सुरैश्च विप्रैश्च न विरुध्येर्महासुर । तावच्छूलं तवेदं स्यादन्यथा नाशमेप्यति ।। 7.61.9 ।।
transliteration: yāvatsuraiśca vipraiśca na virudhyermahāsura | tāvacchūlaṃ tavedaṃ syādanyathā nāśamepyati || 7.61.9 ||
translation: यावत् as long as, सुरैः with gods, च and, विप्रैः with Brahmins, च and, न not, विरुध्येः you contend/oppose, महासुर O great Asura, तावत् so long, शूलं the spear, तव your, इदं this, स्यात् shall be, अन्यथा otherwise, नाशम् destruction, एष्यति it will attain.
explanation: O great Asura, as long as you do not contend with gods and Brahmins, this spear shall remain yours; otherwise, it will meet its destruction.

shloka_text: यश्च त्वामभियुञ्जीत युद्धाय विगतज्वरः । तं शूलो भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम् ।। 7.61.10 ।।
transliteration: yaśca tvāmabhiyuñjīta yuddhāya vigatajvaraḥ | taṃ śūlo bhasmasātkṛtvā punareṣyati te karam || 7.61.10 ||
translation: यः whoever, च and, त्वाम् you, अभियुञ्जीत challenges, युद्धाय for battle, विगतज्वरः free from fear, तम् him, शूलः the spear, भस्मसात्कृत्वा having reduced to ashes, पुनः again, एष्यति it will come, ते your, करम् hand.
explanation: Whoever fearlessly challenges you to battle, the spear will reduce him to ashes and then return to your hand.

shloka_text: एवं रुद्राद्वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः । प्रणिपत्य महादेवं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.61.11 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ rudrādvaraṃ labdhvā bhūya eva mahāsuraḥ | praṇipatya mahādevaṃ vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.61.11 ||
translation: एवम् thus, रुद्रात् from Rudra, वरम् a boon, लब्ध्वा having obtained, भूयः again, एव indeed, महासुरः the great Asura, प्रणिपत्य having bowed down, महादेवं to the great god, वाक्यम् words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Having thus obtained a boon from Rudra, the great Asura bowed down to the great god and spoke these words again.

shloka_text: भगवन्मम वंशस्य शूलमेतदनुत्तमम् । भवेत्तु सततं देव सुराणामीश्वरो ह्यसि ।। 7.61.12 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanmama vaṃśasya śūlametadanuttamam | bhavettu satataṃ deva surāṇāmīśvaro hyasi || 7.61.12 ||
translation: भगवन् O Lord, मम my, वंशस्य of the lineage, शूलम् the spear, एतत् this, अनुत्तमम् excellent, भवेत् may it be, तु indeed, सततम् always, देव O God, सुराणाम् of the gods, ईश्वरः the lord, हि for, असि you are.
explanation: O Lord, may this excellent spear always remain with my lineage, for you are indeed the lord of the gods.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजा नैतदेवं भविष्यति ।। 7.61.13 ।।
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ madhuṃ devaḥ sarvabhūtapatiḥ śivaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejā naitadevaṃ bhaviṣyati || 7.61.13 ||
translation: तम् to him, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, मधुम् to Madhu, देवः the god, सर्वभूतपतिः lord of all beings, शिवः Shiva, प्रत्युवाच replied, महातेजा greatly effulgent, न not, एतत् this, एवम् thus, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: To Madhu, who was speaking thus, the greatly effulgent god Shiva, the lord of all beings, replied, "This will not be so."

shloka_text: मा भूत्ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा । भवतः पुत्रमेकं तु शूलमेतद्भजिष्यते ।। 7.61.14 ।।
transliteration: mā bhūtte viphalā vāṇī matprasādakṛtā śubhā | bhavataḥ putramekaṃ tu śūlametadbhajiṣyate || 7.61.14 ||
translation: मा भूत् let it not be, ते your, विफला fruitless, वाणी word/speech, मत्प्रसादकृता made by my grace, शुभा auspicious, भवतः your, पुत्रम् son, एकम् one, तु indeed, शूलम् trident, एतत् this, भजिष्यते will possess.
explanation: May your auspicious words, granted by my grace, not be in vain; indeed, only one of your sons will possess this trident.

shloka_text: यावत्करस्थः शूलो ऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते । अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां शूलहस्तो भविष्यति ।। 7.61.15 ।।
transliteration: yāvatkarasthaḥ śūlo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati sutasya te | avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śūlahasto bhaviṣyati || 7.61.15 ||
translation: यावत् as long as, करस्थः in hand, शूलः trident, अयम् this, भविष्यति will be, सुतस्य of the son, ते your, अवध्यः unslayable, सर्वभूतानाम् by all beings, शूलहस्तः one with a trident in hand, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: As long as this trident remains in your son's hand, he will be invincible to all beings, being one who wields the trident.

shloka_text: एवं मधुर्वरं लब्ध्वा देवात्सुमहदद्भुतम् । भवनं सो ऽसुरश्रेष्ठः कारयामास सुप्रभम् ।। 7.61.16 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ madhurvaraṃ labdhvā devātsumahadadbhutam | bhavanaṃ so 'suraśreṣṭhaḥ kārayāmāsa suprabham || 7.61.16 ||
translation: एवम् thus, मधुः Madhu, वरम् boon, लब्ध्वा having obtained, देवात् from the god, सुमहत् very great, अद्भुतम् wonderful, भवनम् dwelling/city, सः he, असुरश्रेष्ठः best of demons, कारयामास caused to be built, सुप्रभम् very splendid.
explanation: Thus, having obtained this very great and wonderful boon from the god, Madhu, the best of demons, caused a splendid city to be built.

shloka_text: तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसीति या । विश्वावसोरपत्यं सा ह्यनलायां महाप्रभा ।। 7.61.17 ।।
transliteration: tasya patnī mahābhāgā priyā kumbhīnasīti yā | viśvāvasorapatyaṃ sā hyanalāyāṃ mahāprabhā || 7.61.17 ||
translation: तस्य his, पत्नी wife, महाभागा highly fortunate, प्रिया beloved, कुम्भीनसी Kumbhinasi, इति thus, या who, विश्वावसोः of Vishvavasu, अपत्यम् offspring/daughter, सा she, हि indeed, अनलायाम् in Anala, महाप्रभा very radiant.
explanation: His beloved and highly fortunate wife was Kumbhinasi, who was indeed the very radiant daughter of Vishvavasu by Anala.

shloka_text: तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः । बाल्यात्प्रभृति दुष्टात्मा पापान्येव समाचरत् ।। 7.61.18 ।।
transliteration: tasyāḥ putro mahāvīryo lavaṇo nāma dāruṇaḥ | bālyātprabhṛti duṣṭātmā pāpānyeva samācarat || 7.61.18 ||
translation: तस्याः her, पुत्रः son, महावीर्यः very powerful, लवणः Lavana, नाम named, दारुणः terrible, बाल्यात्प्रभृति from childhood onwards, दुष्टात्मा evil-minded, पापानि sins, एव only, समाचरत् committed.
explanation: Her son was the very powerful and terrible Lavana, who, being evil-minded, committed only sinful deeds from his childhood onwards.

shloka_text: तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः । मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किञ्चिदब्रवीत् ।। 7.61.19 ।।
transliteration: taṃ putraṃ durvinītaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā krodhasamanvitaḥ | madhuḥ sa śokamāpede na cainaṃ kiñcidabravīt || 7.61.19 ||
translation: तं that, पुत्रं son, दुर्विनीतं ill-behaved, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, क्रोधसमन्वितः filled with anger, मधुः Madhu, सः he, शोकम् sorrow, आपेदे attained, न not, च and, एनं him, किञ्चित् anything, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Seeing his ill-behaved son, Madhu was filled with anger and sorrow, yet he did not say anything to him.

shloka_text: स विहाय त्विमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम् । शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ।। 7.61.20 ।।
transliteration: sa vihāya tvimaṃ lokaṃ praviṣṭo varuṇālayam | śūlaṃ niveśya lavaṇe varaṃ tasmai nyavedayat || 7.61.20 ||
translation: सः he (Madhu), विहाय having abandoned, तु indeed, इमं this, लोकं world, प्रविष्टो entered, वरुणालयम् the abode of Varuna, शूलं the trident, निवेश्य having placed, लवणे to Lavana, वरं a boon, तस्मै to him, न्यवेदयत् offered.
explanation: Madhu, having left this world, entered the abode of Varuna, and after placing the trident with Lavana, he offered a boon to him.

shloka_text: स प्रभावेण शूलस्य दौरात्म्येनात्मनस्तथा । सन्तापयति लोकांस्त्रीन्विशेषेण च तापसान् ।। 7.61.21 ।।
transliteration: sa prabhāveṇa śūlasya daurātmyenātmanastathā | santāpayati lokāṃstrīnviśeṣeṇa ca tāpasān || 7.61.21 ||
translation: सः he (Lavana), प्रभावेण by the power, शूलस्य of the trident, दौरात्म्येनात्मनस्तथा and by his own wickedness, सन्तापयति torments, लोकांस्त्रीन् the three worlds, विशेषेण especially, च and, तापसान् ascetics.
explanation: Lavana, by the power of the trident and his own wickedness, torments the three worlds, especially the ascetics.

shloka_text: एवंप्रभावो लवणः शूलं चैव तथाविधम् । श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः ।। 7.61.22 ।।
transliteration: evaṃprabhāvo lavaṇaḥ śūlaṃ caiva tathāvidham | śrutvā pramāṇaṃ kākutstha tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ || 7.61.22 ||
translation: एवंप्रभावो such is the power, लवणः of Lavana, शूलं the trident, च and, एव indeed, तथाविधम् of such a kind, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रमाणं (you are our) authority/refuge, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha (Rama), त्वं you, हि indeed, नः our, परमा ultimate, गतिः refuge.
explanation: Having heard of Lavana's power and the nature of his trident, O Rama, you are our ultimate refuge and authority.

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवा राम भयार्तैर्ऋषिभिः पुरा । अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे ।। 7.61.23 ।।
transliteration: bahavaḥ pārthivā rāma bhayārtairṛṣibhiḥ purā | abhayaṃ yācitā vīra trātāraṃ na ca vidmahe || 7.61.23 ||
translation: बहवः many, पार्थिवा kings, राम O Rama, भयार्तैः by those afflicted with fear, ऋषिभिः by sages, पुरा formerly, अभयं protection, याचिता were implored, वीर O hero, त्रातारं a protector, न not, च and, विद्महे we know.
explanation: O Rama, many kings were formerly implored for protection by fear-stricken sages, but we do not know of any true protector.

shloka_text: ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम् । त्रातारं विद्महे तात नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम् । तत्परित्रातुमिच्छामो लवणाद्भयपीडितान् ।। 7.61.24 ।।
transliteration: te vayaṃ rāvaṇaṃ śrutvā hataṃ sabalavāhanam | trātāraṃ vidmahe tāta nānyaṃ bhuvi narādhipam | tatparitrātumicchāmo lavaṇādbhayapīḍitān || 7.61.24 ||
translation: ते those, वयम् we, रावणम् Ravana, श्रुत्वा having heard, हतम् killed, सबलवाहनम् with his army and vehicles, त्रातारम् protector, विद्महे we know, तात O dear one, न not, अन्यम् another, भुवि on earth, नराधिपम् king, तत् therefore, परित्रातुम् to protect, इच्छामः we wish, लवणात् from Lavana, भयपीडितान् those afflicted by fear.
explanation: Having heard that Ravana, along with his army and vehicles, has been killed, we know no other king on earth as a protector, and therefore, O dear one, we wish for you to protect those afflicted by fear from Lavana.

shloka_text: इति राम निवेदितं तु ते भयजं कारणमुत्थितं च यत् । विनिवारयितुं भवान्क्षमः कुरु तं काममहीनविक्रम ।। 7.61.25 ।।
transliteration: iti rāma niveditaṃ tu te bhayajaṃ kāraṇamutthitaṃ ca yat | vinivārayituṃ bhavānkṣamaḥ kuru taṃ kāmamahīnavikrama || 7.61.25 ||
translation: इति thus, राम O Rama, निवेदितम् reported, तु indeed, ते by them, भयजम् born of fear, कारणम् cause, उत्थितम् arisen, च and, यत् which, विनिवारयितुम् to remove, भवान् you, क्षमः capable, कुरु do, तम् that, कामम् wish, अहीनविक्रम O one of undiminished valor.
explanation: O Rama of undiminished valor, you are capable of removing this cause of fear that has arisen and been reported, so please fulfill that wish. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 61 ।। Thus ends the sixty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथोक्ते तानृषीन्रामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः । किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते ।। 7.62.1 ।।
transliteration: tathokte tānṛṣīnrāmaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ | kimāhāraḥ kimācāro lavaṇaḥ kva ca vartate || 7.62.1 ||
