translation: तथोक्ते when thus spoken, तान् those, ऋषीन् sages, रामः Rama, प्रत्युवाच replied, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, किमाहारः what is his food, किमाचारः what is his conduct, लवणः Lavana, क्व where, च and, वर्तते does he reside.
explanation: When the sages had spoken thus, Rama, with folded hands, replied to them, asking what Lavana's food and conduct were, and where he resided.
comments: Rama asks of Lavana's ways and learns that he devours all beings, especially ascetics, from his seat in Madhuvana -- vowing to slay him, Rama asks which brother shall go; Bharata offers, but Shatrughna pleads that Bharata has suffered enough, and Rama assigns the task to Shatrughna, resolving to install him as king of Madhu's realm and bidding him accept consecration.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते । ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा ।। 7.62.2 ।।
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te | tato nivedayāmāsurlavaṇo vavṛdhe yathā || 7.62.2 ||
translation: राघवस्य of Rama, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, ऋषयः sages, सर्व all, एव indeed, ते those, ततः then, निवेदयामासुः they reported, लवणः Lavana, ववृधे grew, यथा how.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, all those sages then reported how Lavana had grown in power.

shloka_text: आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः । आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा ।। 7.62.3 ।।
transliteration: āhāraḥ sarvasattvāni viśeṣeṇa ca tāpasāḥ | ācāro raudratā nityaṃ vāso madhuvane tathā || 7.62.3 ||
translation: आहारः his food, सर्वसत्त्वानि all beings, विशेषेण especially, च and, तापसाः ascetics, आचारः his conduct, रौद्रता ferocity, नित्यम् always, वासः his dwelling, मधुवने in Madhuvana, तथा also.
explanation: His food consists of all beings, especially ascetics, his conduct is perpetually ferocious, and his dwelling is in the Madhuvana forest.

shloka_text: हत्वा बहुसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विपान् । मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम् ।। 7.62.4 ।।
transliteration: hatvā bahusahasrāṇi siṃhavyāghramṛgadvipān | mānuṣāṃścaiva kurute nityamāhāramāhnikam || 7.62.4 ||
translation: हत्वा having killed, बहुसहस्राणि many thousands, सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विपान् lions, tigers, deer, and elephants, मानुषांश्चैव and humans indeed, कुरुते he makes, नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम् a daily meal.
explanation: Having killed many thousands of lions, tigers, deer, elephants, and humans, he makes them his daily meal.

shloka_text: ततो ऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः । संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः ।। 7.62.5 ।।
transliteration: tato 'ntarāṇi sattvāni khādate sa mahābalaḥ | saṃhāre samanuprāpte vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ || 7.62.5 ||
translation: ततो then, अन्तराणि other, सत्त्वानि beings, खादते he eats, सः that, महाबलः mighty one, संहारे at the time of dissolution, समनुप्राप्ते having arrived, व्यादितास्यः with an open mouth, इव like, अन्तकः Yama.
explanation: Then, that mighty one devours other beings, like Yama with an open mouth at the time of cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन् । घातयिष्यामि तद्रक्षो ह्यपगच्छतु वो भयम् ।। 7.62.6 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rāghavo vākyamuvāca sa mahāmunīn | ghātayiṣyāmi tadrakṣo hyapagacchatu vo bhayam || 7.62.6 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवः Rama, वाक्यम् words, उवाच spoke, सः he, महामुनीन् to the great sages, घातयिष्यामि I shall kill, तद्रक्षो that demon, हि indeed, अपगच्छतु let it go away, वः your, भयम् fear.
explanation: Having heard that, Rama spoke these words to the great sages: "I shall indeed kill that demon; let your fear depart."

shloka_text: प्रतिज्ञाय तथा तेषां मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम् । स भ्रातऽन्सहितान्सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.7 ।।
transliteration: pratijñāya tathā teṣāṃ munīnāmugratejasām | sa bhrāta'nsahitānsarvānuvāca raghunandanaḥ || 7.62.7 ||
translation: प्रतिज्ञाय having promised, तथा thus, तेषां to them, मुनीनाम् to the sages, उग्रतेजसाम् of fierce ascetic power, सः he, भ्रातऽन्सहितान्सर्वान् to all his assembled brothers, उवाच spoke, रघुनन्दनः Rama.
explanation: Having thus promised those sages of fierce ascetic power, Rama then spoke to all his assembled brothers.

shloka_text: को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम् । भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्य च धीमतः ।। 7.62.8 ।।
transliteration: ko hantā lavaṇaṃ vīraḥ kasyāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām | bharatasya mahābāhoḥ śatrughnasya ca dhīmataḥ || 7.62.8 ||
translation: कः who, हन्ता will kill, लवणम् Lavana, वीरः hero, कस्यांशः whose share, सः that, विधीयताम् let it be assigned, भरतस्य of Bharata, महाबाहोः the mighty-armed, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, च and, धीमतः the intelligent.
explanation: "Which hero will kill Lavana? To whom among the mighty-armed Bharata and the intelligent Shatrughna should that task be assigned?"

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम् ।। 7.62.9 ।।
transliteration: rāghaveṇaivamuktastu bharato vākyamabravīt | ahamenaṃ vadhiṣyāmi mamāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām || 7.62.9 ||
translation: राघवेण by Rama, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, तु indeed, भरतः Bharata, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, अहम् I, एनम् him, वधिष्यामि will kill, मम my, अंशः share, सः that, विधीयताम् let it be assigned.
explanation: When Rama thus spoke, Bharata replied, "I will kill him; let that task be assigned to me."

shloka_text: भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम् । लक्ष्मणावरजस्तस्थौ हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम् ।। 7.62.10 ।।
transliteration: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā dhairyaśauryasamanvitam | lakṣmaṇāvarajastasthau hitvā sauvarṇamāsanam || 7.62.10 ||
translation: भरतस्य Bharata's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम् endowed with courage and valor, लक्ष्मणावरजः Lakshmana's younger brother, तस्थौ stood up, हित्वा having left, सौवर्णम् golden, आसनम् seat.
explanation: Having heard Bharata's words, which were full of courage and valor, Shatrughna, Lakshmana's younger brother, stood up, leaving his golden seat.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम् । कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.11 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnastvabravīdvākyaṃ praṇipatya narādhipam | kṛtakarmā mahābāhurmadhyamo raghunandanaḥ || 7.62.11 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, तु indeed, अब्रवीत् spoke, वाक्यम् words, प्रणिपत्य having bowed down, नराधिपम् to the king, कृतकर्मा one who has accomplished deeds, महाबाहुः mighty-armed, मध्यमः the middle one, रघुनन्दनः delight of the Raghu dynasty.
explanation: Shatrughna, having bowed down to the king, then spoke, referring to the mighty-armed Bharata, the delight of the Raghu dynasty, as one who has already accomplished great deeds.

shloka_text: आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता । सन्तापं हृदये कृत्वा आर्यस्यागमनं प्रति ।। 7.62.12 ।।
transliteration: āryeṇa hi purā śūnyā tvayodhyā paripālitā | santāpaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā āryasyāgamanaṃ prati || 7.62.12 ||
translation: आर्येण by the noble one, हि indeed, पुरा formerly, शून्या desolate, अयोध्या Ayodhya, परिपालिता was protected, सन्तापम् sorrow, हृदये in the heart, कृत्वा having kept, आर्यस्य of the noble one, आगमनम् return, प्रति regarding.
explanation: Indeed, Ayodhya, though desolate, was formerly protected by the noble Bharata, who kept sorrow in his heart regarding the return of the noble Rama.

shloka_text: दुःखानि च बहूनीह ह्यनुभूतानि पार्थिव । शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे ऽवसत्पुरा ।। 7.62.13 ।।
transliteration: duḥkhāni ca bahūnīha hyanubhūtāni pārthiva | śayāno duḥkhaśayyāsu nandigrāme 'vasatpurā || 7.62.13 ||
translation: दुःखानि sorrows, च and, बहूनि many, इह here, हि indeed, अनुभूतानि experienced, पार्थिव O King, शयानो lying down, दुःखशय्यासु on beds of sorrow, नन्दिग्रामे in Nandigrama, अवसत् resided, पुरा formerly.
explanation: O King, Bharata indeed experienced many sufferings here, formerly residing in Nandigrama, lying on uncomfortable beds.

shloka_text: फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटी चीरधरस्तथा । अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः । प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात् ।। 7.62.14 ।।
transliteration: phalamūlāśano bhūtvā jaṭī cīradharastathā | anubhūyedṛśaṃ duḥkhameṣa rāghavanandanaḥ | preṣye mayi sthite rājanna bhūyaḥ kleśamāpnuyāt || 7.62.14 ||
translation: फलमूलाशनो one who eats fruits and roots, भूत्वा having become, जटी with matted hair, चीरधरस्तथा and wearing bark garments, अनुभूय having experienced, ईदृशं such, दुःखम् sorrow, एष this, राघवनन्दनः son of Raghu (Bharata), प्रेष्ये while a servant, मयि I (am), स्थिते present, राजन् O King, न not, भूयः again, क्लेशम् trouble, आप्नुयात् should obtain.
explanation: Bharata, having become an ascetic eating fruits and roots, with matted hair and bark garments, and having experienced such sorrow, should not again suffer while I, your servant, am present, O King.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति शत्रुघ्ने राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम् ।। 7.62.15 ।।
transliteration: tathā bruvati śatrughne rāghavaḥ punarabravīt | evaṃ bhavatu kākutstha kriyatāṃ mama śāsanam || 7.62.15 ||
translation: तथा thus, ब्रुवति while speaking, शत्रुघ्ने by Shatrughna, राघवः Rama, पुनः again, अब्रवीत् spoke, एवम् thus, भवतु let it be, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, क्रियतां let it be done, मम my, शासनम् command.
explanation: While Shatrughna was speaking thus, Rama again said, "So be it, O Kakutstha; let my command be carried out."

shloka_text: राज्ये त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मधोस्तु नगरे शुभे । निवेशय महाबाहो भरतं यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.16 ।।
transliteration: rājye tvāmabhiṣekṣyāmi madhostu nagare śubhe | niveśaya mahābāho bharataṃ yadyavekṣase || 7.62.16 ||
translation: राज्ये in the kingdom, त्वाम् you, अभिषेक्ष्यामि I shall anoint, मधोः of Madhu, तु indeed, नगरे in the city, शुभे auspicious, निवेशय establish, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, भरतम् Bharata, यदि if, अवेक्षसे you care for.
explanation: I shall install you in the auspicious city of Madhu's kingdom; O mighty-armed one, establish Bharata there if you care for him.

shloka_text: शूरस्त्वं कृतविद्यश्च समर्थश्च निवेशने ।। 7.62.17 ।।
transliteration: śūrastvaṃ kṛtavidyaśca samarthaśca niveśane || 7.62.17 ||
translation: शूरः brave, त्वम् you, कृतविद्यः learned, च and, समर्थः capable, च and, निवेशने in establishing (a city/kingdom).
explanation: You are brave, learned, and capable in establishing a kingdom.

shloka_text: यो हि शत्रुं समुत्पाट्य पार्थिवस्य पुनः क्षये । न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति ।। 7.62.18 ।।
transliteration: yo hi śatruṃ samutpāṭya pārthivasya punaḥ kṣaye | na vidhatte nṛpaṃ tatra narakaṃ sa hi gacchati || 7.62.18 ||
translation: यः who, हि indeed, शत्रुम् an enemy, समुत्पाट्य having uprooted, पार्थिवस्य of the king, पुनः again, क्षये in the destruction, न not, विधत्ते establishes, नृपम् a king, तत्र there, नरकम् hell, सः he, हि indeed, गच्छति goes.
explanation: Indeed, whoever uproots an enemy and, in the destruction of that king's domain, does not establish a new ruler there, he certainly goes to hell.

shloka_text: स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम् । राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.19 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ hatvā madhusutaṃ lavaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam | rājyaṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa vākyaṃ me yadyavekṣase || 7.62.19 ||
translation: स one who, त्वं you, हत्वा having killed, मधुसुतं the son of Madhu, लवणं Lavana, पापनिश्चयम् one whose resolve is evil, राज्यं the kingdom, प्रशाधि rule, धर्मेण righteously, वाक्यं the word, मे my, यदि if, अवेक्षसे you regard.
explanation: If you respect my words, then you, having killed Lavana, the evil-minded son of Madhu, should rule the kingdom righteously.

shloka_text: उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम । बालेन पूर्वजस्याज्ञा कर्तव्या नात्र संशयः ।। 7.62.20 ।।
transliteration: uttaraṃ ca na vaktavyaṃ śūra vākyāntare mama | bālena pūrvajasyājñā kartavyā nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7.62.20 ||
translation: उत्तरं a reply, च and, न not, वक्तव्यं to be spoken, शूर O hero, वाक्यान्तरे in the midst of my words, मम my, बालेन by a younger one, पूर्वजस्य of an elder brother, आज्ञा the command, कर्तव्या should be done, न not, अत्र here, संशयः doubt.
explanation: O hero, do not speak a reply while I am speaking, for a younger brother must obey the command of an elder, there is no doubt about this.

shloka_text: अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व मयोद्यतम् । वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्विप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् ।। 7.62.21 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣekaṃ ca kākutstha pratīcchasva mayodyatam | vasiṣṭhapramukhairviprairvidhimantrapuraskṛtam || 7.62.21 ||
translation: अभिषेकं the consecration, च and, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, प्रतीच्छस्व accept, मया by me, उद्यतम् prepared, वसिष्ठप्रमुखैः by Vasistha and other prominent ones, विप्रैः by Brahmins, विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् accompanied by rituals and mantras.
explanation: O Kakutstha, accept this consecration prepared by me, which is performed by prominent Brahmins like Vasistha, accompanied by proper rituals and mantras. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 62।। Thus ends the sixty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण परां व्रीडामुपागमत् । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह ।। 7.63.1 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu rāmeṇa parāṃ vrīḍāmupāgamat | śatrughno vīryasampanno mandaṃ mandamuvāca ha || 7.63.1 ||
translation: एवं thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामेण by Rama, परां great, व्रीडां shame, उपागमत् he attained, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, मन्दं slowly, मन्दं slowly, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, the valiant Shatrughna felt extreme embarrassment and spoke very slowly.
comments: Shatrughna, abashed to be consecrated before his elders, nonetheless obeys, and Rama has him anointed amid general joy -- Rama gives him the divine, unfailing arrow with which Vishnu once slew Madhu and Kaitabha, instructing that, since Lavana is invincible while holding Shiva's trident, Shatrughna must challenge him at the gate before he can fetch it.

shloka_text: अधर्मं विद्म काकुत्स्थ ह्यस्मिन्नर्थे नरेश्वर । कथं तिष्ठत्सु ज्येष्ठेषु कनीयानभिषिच्यते ।। 7.63.2 ।।
transliteration: adharmaṃ vidma kākutstha hyasminnarthe nareśvara | kathaṃ tiṣṭhatsu jyeṣṭheṣu kanīyānabhiṣicyate || 7.63.2 ||
translation: अधर्मं unrighteousness, विद्म I know, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, हि indeed, अस्मिन् in this, अर्थे matter, नरेश्वर O lord of men, कथं how, तिष्ठत्सु while being present, ज्येष्ठेषु the elders, कनीयान् a younger one, अभिषिच्यते is consecrated.
explanation: O Kakutstha, O king, I indeed know that this matter is unrighteous; how can a younger brother be consecrated while his elders are present?

shloka_text: अवश्यं करणीयं च शासनं पुरुषर्षभ । तव चैव महाभाग शासनं दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.63.3 ।।
transliteration: avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca śāsanaṃ puruṣarṣabha | tava caiva mahābhāga śāsanaṃ duratikramam || 7.63.3 ||
translation: अवश्यं certainly, करणीयं to be done, च and, शासनं command, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, तव your, च and, एव indeed, महाभाग O illustrious one, शासनं command, दुरतिक्रमम् inviolable.
explanation: O best among men and illustrious one, your command is certainly to be carried out and is indeed inviolable.

shloka_text: त्वत्तो मया श्रुतं वीर श्रुतिभ्यश्च मया श्रुतम् । नोत्तरं हि मया वाच्यं मध्यमे प्रतिजानति ।। 7.63.4 ।।
transliteration: tvatto mayā śrutaṃ vīra śrutibhyaśca mayā śrutam | nottaraṃ hi mayā vācyaṃ madhyame pratijānati || 7.63.4 ||
translation: त्वत्तो from you, मया by me, श्रुतं heard, वीर O hero, श्रुतिभ्यः from the scriptures, च and, मया by me, श्रुतम् heard, न not, उत्तरं a reply, हि indeed, मया by me, वाच्यं to be spoken, मध्यमे when the middle one (Bharata), प्रतिजानति promises.
explanation: O hero, I have heard from you and from the scriptures that when the middle brother undertakes a task, no reply should indeed be given by me.

shloka_text: व्याहृतं दुर्वचो घोरं हन्तास्मि लवणं मृधे । तस्यैवं मे दुरुक्तस्य दुर्गतिः पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.63.5 ।।
transliteration: vyāhṛtaṃ durvaco ghoraṃ hantāsmi lavaṇaṃ mṛdhe | tasyaivaṃ me duruktasya durgatiḥ puruṣarṣabha || 7.63.5 ||
translation: व्याहृतं spoken, दुर्वचो harsh words, घोरं terrible, हन्तास्मि I will kill, लवणं Lavana, मृधे in battle, तस्य of that, एवं thus, मे my, दुरुक्तस्य ill-spoken word, दुर्गतिः misfortune, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O best among men, I have uttered terrible, harsh words, saying "I will kill Lavana in battle," and such an ill-spoken word of mine will lead to misfortune.

shloka_text: उत्तरं नहि वक्तव्यं ज्येष्ठेनाभिहिते पुनः । अधर्मसहितं चैव परलोकविवर्जितम् ।। 7.63.6 ।।
transliteration: uttaraṃ nahi vaktavyaṃ jyeṣṭhenābhihite punaḥ | adharmasahitaṃ caiva paralokavivarjitam || 7.63.6 ||
translation: उत्तरं a reply, न not, हि indeed, वक्तव्यं to be spoken, ज्येष्ठेन by the elder brother, अभिहिते when commanded, पुनः again, अधर्मसहितं unrighteous, च and, एव indeed, परलोकविवर्जितम् devoid of the other world.
explanation: Indeed, a reply should not be spoken again when commanded by the elder brother, as doing so is unrighteous and leads to no good in the afterlife.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं द्वितीयं काकुत्स्थ न वक्ष्यामि तवोत्तरम् । मा द्वितीयेन दण्डो वै निपतेन्मयि मानद ।। 7.63.7 ।।
transliteration: so 'haṃ dvitīyaṃ kākutstha na vakṣyāmi tavottaram | mā dvitīyena daṇḍo vai nipatenmayi mānada || 7.63.7 ||
translation: सः that, अहं I, द्वितीयं a second, काकुत्स्थ O scion of Kakutstha, न not, वक्ष्यामि I will speak, तव your, उत्तरम् a reply, मा let not, द्वितीयेन by a second (word/action), दण्डो punishment, वै indeed, निपतेत् fall, मयि upon me, मानद O giver of honor.
explanation: Therefore, O scion of Kakutstha, I will not speak a second reply to you, lest a second punishment indeed fall upon me, O giver of honor.

shloka_text: कामकारो ह्यहं राजंस्तवास्मि पुरुषर्षभ । अधर्मं जहि काकुत्स्थ मत्कृते रघुनन्दन ।। 7.63.8 ।।
transliteration: kāmakāro hyahaṃ rājaṃstavāsmi puruṣarṣabha | adharmaṃ jahi kākutstha matkṛte raghunandana || 7.63.8 ||
translation: कामकारो one who acts according to his own will, हि indeed, अहं I, राजन् O King, तव your, अस्मि am, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, अधर्मं unrighteousness, जहि destroy, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, मत्कृते for my sake, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus.
explanation: Shatrughna tells Rama that he is at Rama's disposal and implores him to destroy this unrighteousness for his sake.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ते तु शूरेण शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । उवाच रामः संहृष्टो भरतं लक्ष्मणं तथा ।। 7.63.9 ।।
transliteration: evamukte tu śūreṇa śatrughnena mahātmanā | uvāca rāmaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo bharataṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tathā || 7.63.9 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ते having been spoken, तु then, शूरेण by the brave one, शत्रुघ्नेन by Shatrughna, महात्मना by the great-souled one, उवाच spoke, रामः Rama, संहृष्टो greatly delighted, भरतं to Bharata, लक्ष्मणं to Lakshmana, तथा and.
explanation: When the brave and great-souled Shatrughna had thus spoken, Rama, greatly delighted, addressed Bharata and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सम्भारानभिषेकस्य आनयध्वं समाहिताः । अद्यैव पुरुषव्याघ्रमभिषेक्ष्यामि राघवम् ।। 7.63.10 ।।
transliteration: sambhārānabhiṣekasya ānayadhvaṃ samāhitāḥ | adyaiva puruṣavyāghramabhiṣekṣyāmi rāghavam || 7.63.10 ||
translation: सम्भारान् preparations, अभिषेकस्य for the consecration, आनयध्वं bring, समाहिताः attentively, अद्यैव today itself, पुरुषव्याघ्रम् the tiger among men, अभिषेक्ष्यामि I shall consecrate, राघवम् the descendant of Raghu.
explanation: Rama commanded them to carefully bring the materials for the consecration, declaring that he would anoint Bharata, the tiger among men and descendant of Raghu, today itself.

shloka_text: पुरोहितं च काकुत्स्थं नैगमानृत्विजस्तथा । मन्त्रिणश्चैव तान्सर्वानानयध्वं ममाज्ञया ।। 7.63.11 ।।
transliteration: purohitaṃ ca kākutsthaṃ naigamānṛtvijastathā | mantriṇaścaiva tānsarvānānayadhvaṃ mamājñayā || 7.63.11 ||
translation: पुरोहितं the chief priest, च and, काकुत्स्थं O Kakutstha, नैगमान् the citizens, ऋत्विजः the priests, तथा and, मन्त्रिणः the ministers, चैव and also, तान् them, सर्वान् all, आनयध्वं bring, ममाज्ञया by my command.
explanation: Rama further instructed them to bring the chief priest, the citizens, the ritual priests, and all the ministers by his command.

shloka_text: राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तथा ऽकुर्वन्महारथाः । अभिषेकसमारम्भं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोधसम् । प्रविष्टा राजभवनं राजानो ब्राह्मणास्तथा ।। 7.63.12 ।।
transliteration: rājñaḥ śāsanamājñāya tathā 'kurvanmahārathāḥ | abhiṣekasamārambhaṃ puraskṛtya purodhasam | praviṣṭā rājabhavanaṃ rājāno brāhmaṇāstathā || 7.63.12 ||
translation: राज्ञः of the king, शासनम् the command, आज्ञाय having understood, तथा thus, अकुर्वन् they did, महारथाः the great charioteers, अभिषेकसमारम्भं the commencement of the consecration, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front, पुरोधसम् the chief priest, प्रविष्टा entered, राजभवनं the royal palace, राजानो the kings, ब्राह्मणाः the Brahmins, तथा and.
explanation: Having understood the king's command, the great charioteers (Bharata and Lakshmana) acted accordingly, and then the kings and Brahmins, honoring the chief priest, entered the royal palace for the commencement of the consecration.

shloka_text: तथो ऽभिषेको ववृधे शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । सम्प्रहर्षकरः श्रीमान्राघवस्य पुरस्य च ।। 7.63.13 ।।
transliteration: tatho 'bhiṣeko vavṛdhe śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | sampraharṣakaraḥ śrīmānrāghavasya purasya ca || 7.63.13 ||
translation: तथो then, अभिषेको the anointing, ववृधे flourished, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, सम्प्रहर्षकरः causing great joy, श्रीमान् glorious, राघवस्य of Rama, पुरस्य of the city, च and.
explanation: Then, the glorious anointing of the great-souled Shatrughna, which brought immense joy to Rama and the entire city, flourished.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्तस्तु शत्रुघ्नो बभौ चादित्यसन्निभः । अभिषिक्तः पुरा स्कन्दः सेन्द्रैरिव मरुद्गणैः ।। 7.63.14 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣiktastu śatrughno babhau cādityasannibhaḥ | abhiṣiktaḥ purā skandaḥ sendrairiva marudgaṇaiḥ || 7.63.14 ||
translation: अभिषिक्तस्तु but having been consecrated, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, बभौ shone, च and, आदित्यसन्निभः sun-like, अभिषिक्तः consecrated, पुरा formerly, स्कन्दः Skanda, सेन्द्रैरिव as if with Indra, मरुद्गणैः by the Marut hosts.
explanation: Having been consecrated, Shatrughna shone like the sun, just as Skanda had shone in ancient times when consecrated by Indra and the Marut hosts.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु शत्रुघ्ने रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । पौराः प्रमुदिताश्चासन्ब्राह्मणाश्च बहुश्रुताः ।। 7.63.15 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣikte tu śatrughne rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā | paurāḥ pramuditāścāsanbrāhmaṇāśca bahuśrutāḥ || 7.63.15 ||
translation: अभिषिक्ते when consecrated, तु indeed, शत्रुघ्ने Shatrughna, रामेणा by Rama, अक्लिष्टकर्मणा by the one of unwearied deeds, पौराः the citizens, प्रमुदिताश्च and delighted, आसन् were, ब्राह्मणाश्च and the Brahmins, बहुश्रुताः learned.
explanation: When Shatrughna was consecrated by Rama, whose deeds were effortless, the citizens and the highly learned Brahmins were greatly delighted.

shloka_text: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च मङ्गलं केकयी तथा । चक्रुस्ता राजभवने याश्चान्या राजयोषितः ।। 7.63.16 ।।
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca maṅgalaṃ kekayī tathā | cakrustā rājabhavane yāścānyā rājayoṣitaḥ || 7.63.16 ||
translation: कौसल्या Kausalya, च and, सुमित्रा Sumitra, च and, मङ्गलम् auspicious rites, केकयी Kaikeyi, तथा likewise, चक्रुस्ता they performed, राजभवने in the royal palace, याश्च and those, अन्या other, राजयोषितः royal ladies.
explanation: Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi, along with other royal ladies, performed auspicious rites in the royal palace.

shloka_text: ऋषयश्च महात्मानो यमुनातीरवासिनः । हतं लवणमाशंसुः शत्रुघ्नस्याभिषेचनात् ।। 7.63.17 ।।
transliteration: ṛṣayaśca mahātmāno yamunātīravāsinaḥ | hataṃ lavaṇamāśaṃsuḥ śatrughnasyābhiṣecanāt || 7.63.17 ||
translation: ऋषयश्च and the sages, महात्मानो great-souled, यमुनातीरवासिनः dwelling on the banks of Yamuna, हतम् slain, लवणम् Lavana, आशंसुः they predicted, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, अभिषेचनात् from the consecration.
explanation: The great-souled sages dwelling on the banks of the Yamuna predicted that Lavana would be slain as a result of Shatrughna's consecration.

shloka_text: ततो ऽभिषिक्तं शत्रुघ्नमङ्कमारोप्य राघवः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं तेजस्तस्याभिपूरयन् ।। 7.63.18 ।।
transliteration: tato 'bhiṣiktaṃ śatrughnamaṅkamāropya rāghavaḥ | uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ tejastasyābhipūrayan || 7.63.18 ||
translation: ततः then, अभिषिक्तम् consecrated, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, अङ्कम् lap, आरोप्य having placed, राघवः Rama, उवाच spoke, मधुराम् sweet, वाणीम् words, तेजः splendor, तस्य his, अभिपूरयन् enhancing.
explanation: Then, Rama, having placed the consecrated Shatrughna on his lap, spoke sweet words, thereby enhancing his splendor and might.

shloka_text: अयं शरस्त्वमोघस्ते दिव्यः परपुरञ्जयः । अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्ता ऽसि रघुनन्दन ।। 7.63.19 ।।
transliteration: ayaṃ śarastvamoghaste divyaḥ parapurañjayaḥ | anena lavaṇaṃ saumya hantā 'si raghunandana || 7.63.19 ||
translation: अयम् this, शरः arrow, तु indeed, अमोघः unfailing, ते your, दिव्यः divine, परपुरञ्जयः conqueror of enemy cities, अनेन by this, लवणम् Lavana, सौम्य O gentle one, हन्ता असि you will kill, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus.
explanation: O gentle Shatrughna, this divine arrow of yours is unfailing and capable of conquering enemy cities; with this, you will surely kill Lavana.

shloka_text: सृष्टः शरो ऽयं काकुत्स्थ यदा शेते महार्णवे ।। 7.63.20 ।।
transliteration: sṛṣṭaḥ śaro 'yaṃ kākutstha yadā śete mahārṇave || 7.63.20 ||
translation: सृष्टः created, शरः arrow, अयम् this, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, यदा when, शेते rests, महार्णवे in the great ocean.
explanation: O Kakutstha, this arrow was created when (Vishnu) rested in the great cosmic ocean.

shloka_text: स्वयम्भूरजितो देवो यन्नापश्यन्सुरासुराः । अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां तेनायं तु शरोत्तमः ।। 7.63.21 ।।
transliteration: svayambhūrajito devo yannāpaśyansurāsurāḥ | adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tenāyaṃ tu śarottamaḥ || 7.63.21 ||
translation: स्वयम्भूः the self-born, अजितः unconquered, देवः god, यत् which, न not, अपश्यन् saw, सुरासुराः gods and demons, अदृश्यः invisible, सर्वभूतानाम् to all beings, तेन therefore, अयम् this, तु indeed, शरोत्तमः the best of arrows.
explanation: This arrow is indeed the best of arrows because it was created by the self-born, unconquered God (Vishnu) in a form that was invisible to all gods, demons, and other beings.

shloka_text: सृष्टः क्रोधाभिभूतेन विनाशार्थं दुरात्मनोः । मधुकैटभयोर्वीर विघाते वर्तमानयोः । स्रष्टुकामेन लोकांस्त्रींस्तौ चानेन हतौ युधि ।। 7.63.22 ।।
transliteration: sṛṣṭaḥ krodhābhibhūtena vināśārthaṃ durātmanoḥ | madhukaiṭabhayorvīra vighāte vartamānayoḥ | sraṣṭukāmena lokāṃstrīṃstau cānena hatau yudhi || 7.63.22 ||
translation: सृष्टः created, क्रोधाभिभूतेन by one overcome by anger, विनाशार्थम् for the destruction, दुरात्मनोः of the two wicked ones, मधुकैटभयोः Madhu and Kaitabha, वीर O hero, विघाते in obstructing, वर्तमानयोः who were engaged, स्रष्टुकामेन by the one desirous of creating, लोकान् worlds, त्रीन् three, तौ those two, च and, अनेन by this, हतौ were killed, युधि in battle.
explanation: O hero, this arrow was created by the angry (Vishnu) for the destruction of the two wicked demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, who were obstructing the creation of the three worlds, and indeed, those two were killed in battle by this very arrow.

shloka_text: तौ हत्वा जनभोगार्थं कैटभं तु मधुं तथा । अनेन शरमुख्येन ततो लोकांश्चकार सः ।। 7.63.23 ।।
transliteration: tau hatvā janabhogārthaṃ kaiṭabhaṃ tu madhuṃ tathā | anena śaramukhyena tato lokāṃścakāra saḥ || 7.63.23 ||
translation: तौ those two, हत्वा having killed, जनभोगार्थं for the enjoyment of people, कैटभं Kaitabha, तु indeed, मधुं Madhu, तथा and, अनेन by this, शरमुख्येन excellent arrow, ततो then, लोकांश्चकार created the worlds, सः he.
explanation: Having killed Kaitabha and Madhu for the benefit of mankind, he (Vishnu) then created the worlds with this excellent arrow.

shloka_text: नायं मया शरः पूर्वं रावणस्य वधार्थिना । मुक्तः शत्रुघ्न भूतानां महांस्त्रासो भवेदिति ।। 7.63.24 ।।
transliteration: nāyaṃ mayā śaraḥ pūrvaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhārthinā | muktaḥ śatrughna bhūtānāṃ mahāṃstrāso bhavediti || 7.63.24 ||
translation: न not, अयं this, मया by me, शरः arrow, पूर्वं previously, रावणस्य of Ravana, वधार्थिना by one desiring the death, मुक्तः released, शत्रुघ्न O Shatrughna, भूतानां of beings, महांस्त्रासः great terror, भवेत् would occur, इति thinking thus.
explanation: O Shatrughna, I did not release this arrow previously, even when desiring Ravana's death, thinking that it would cause great terror to all beings.

shloka_text: यच्च तस्य महच्छूलं त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना । दत्तं शत्रुविनाशाय मधोरायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.63.25 ।।
transliteration: yacca tasya mahacchūlaṃ tryambakeṇa mahātmanā | dattaṃ śatruvināśāya madhorāyudhamuttamam || 7.63.25 ||
translation: यत् च and which, तस्य his, महच्छूलं great trident, त्र्यम्बकेण by Tryambaka (Shiva), महात्मना by the great-souled one, दत्तं given, शत्रुविनाशाय for the destruction of enemies, मधोः Madhu's, आयुधं weapon, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: And that great trident, Madhu's excellent weapon, was given to him by the great-souled Tryambaka (Shiva) for the destruction of enemies.

shloka_text: स तं निक्षिप्य भवने पूज्यमान पुनः पुनः । दिशः सर्वाः समासाद्य प्राप्नोत्याहारमुत्तमम् ।। 7.63.26 ।।
transliteration: sa taṃ nikṣipya bhavane pūjyamāna punaḥ punaḥ | diśaḥ sarvāḥ samāsādya prāpnotyāhāramuttamam || 7.63.26 ||
translation: सः he, तं that, निक्षिप्य having placed, भवने in his dwelling, पूज्यमानः being worshipped, पुनः पुनः again and again, दिशः directions, सर्वाः all, समासाद्य having traversed, प्राप्नोति obtains, आहारम् food, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: Having placed that (trident) in his dwelling, and being worshipped repeatedly, he (Madhu) would traverse all directions and obtain excellent food.

shloka_text: यदा तु युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन् कश्चिदेनं समाह्वयेत् । तदा शूलं गहीत्वा तं भस्म रक्षः करोति हि ।। 7.63.27 ।।
transliteration: yadā tu yuddhamākāṅkṣan kaścidenaṃ samāhvayet | tadā śūlaṃ gahītvā taṃ bhasma rakṣaḥ karoti hi || 7.63.27 ||
translation: यदा when, तु but, युद्धम् battle, आकाङ्क्षन् desiring, कश्चित् someone, एनं him, समाह्वयेत् challenges, तदा then, शूलं the trident, गहीत्वा having taken, तं him, भस्म to ashes, रक्षः the demon, करोति makes, हि indeed.
explanation: But when someone desiring battle would challenge him, the demon (Madhu) would then take the trident and indeed reduce that challenger to ashes.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमायुधविनाकृतम् । अप्रविष्टं पुरं पूर्वं द्वारि तिष्ठ धृतायुधः ।। 7.63.28 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla tamāyudhavinākṛtam | apraviṣṭaṃ puraṃ pūrvaṃ dvāri tiṣṭha dhṛtāyudhaḥ || 7.63.28 ||
translation: स one who, त्वं you, पुरुषशार्दूल O best among men, तम् him, आयुधविनाकृतम् deprived of weapons, अप्रविष्टम् not having entered, पुरम् the city, पूर्वम् previously, द्वारि at the gate, तिष्ठ stand, धृतायुधः holding weapons.
explanation: O best among men, you should stand at the city gate, armed, and wait for him, who is deprived of weapons and has not yet entered the city.

shloka_text: अप्रविष्टं च भवनं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभ । आह्वयेथा महाबाहो ततो हन्तासि राक्षसम् ।। 7.63.29 ।।
transliteration: apraviṣṭaṃ ca bhavanaṃ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabha | āhvayethā mahābāho tato hantāsi rākṣasam || 7.63.29 ||
translation: अप्रविष्टम् not having entered, च and, भवनम् the dwelling, युद्धाय for battle, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, आह्वयेथाः you should challenge, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, ततः then, हन्तासि you will kill, राक्षसम् the demon.
explanation: O best among men, O mighty-armed one, you should challenge him for battle before he enters his dwelling, and then you will be able to kill the demon.

shloka_text: अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु अवध्यः स भविष्यति । यदि त्वेवं कृते वीर विनाशमुपयास्यति ।। 7.63.30 ।।
transliteration: anyathā kriyamāṇe tu avadhyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati | yadi tvevaṃ kṛte vīra vināśamupayāsyati || 7.63.30 ||
translation: अन्यथा otherwise, क्रियमाणे if done, तु indeed, अवध्यः unkillable, सः he, भविष्यति will become, यदि if, तु indeed, एवम् thus, कृते done, वीर O hero, विनाशम् destruction, उपयास्यति he will attain.
explanation: If this is done otherwise, he will become unkillable, but if you act in this manner, O hero, he will certainly meet his destruction.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शूलस्य च विपर्ययः । श्रीमतः शितिकण्ठस्य कृत्यं हि दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.63.31 ।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ śūlasya ca viparyayaḥ | śrīmataḥ śitikaṇṭhasya kṛtyaṃ hi duratikramam || 7.63.31 ||
translation: एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातम् has been told, शूलस्य of the spear, च and, विपर्ययः the reversal, श्रीमतः glorious, शितिकण्ठस्य of the blue-throated one (Shiva), कृत्यम् the deed, हि indeed, दुरतिक्रमम् difficult to transgress.
explanation: All this has been explained to you, including the reversal of the spear's power, for the deed of the glorious blue-throated Shiva is indeed impossible to transgress. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 63 ।। Thus ends the sixty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा च काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः । पुनरेवापरं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.64.1 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā ca kākutsthaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ | punarevāparaṃ vākyamuvāca raghunandanaḥ || 7.64.1 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, च and, काकुत्स्थम् to Kakutstha (Rama), प्रशस्य having praised, च and, पुनः पुनः again and again, पुनरेव again indeed, अपरम् another, वाक्यम् word/statement, उवाच spoke, रघुनन्दनः the delight of the Raghus (Rama).
explanation: Having spoken thus to Rama and praised him repeatedly, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, then spoke another statement.
comments: Rama equips Shatrughna with horses, chariots, elephants, gold and a retinue, counselling him to win his soldiers' loyalty by kindness, to go ahead alone with his bow lest Lavana suspect him, and to strike when the rains come -- Shatrughna orders his army's camps, salutes the queen-mothers and his brothers, and after a month sets out.

shloka_text: इमान्यश्वसहस्राणि चत्वारि पुरुषर्षभ । रथानां द्वे सहस्रे च गजानां शतमुत्तमम् ।। 7.64.2 ।।
transliteration: imānyaśvasahasrāṇi catvāri puruṣarṣabha | rathānāṃ dve sahasre ca gajānāṃ śatamuttamam || 7.64.2 ||
translation: इमानि these, अश्वसहस्राणि thousands of horses, चत्वारि four, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, रथानाम् of chariots, द्वे two, सहस्रे thousands, च and, गजानाम् of elephants, शतम् a hundred, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: O best among men, take these four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, and a hundred excellent elephants.

shloka_text: अन्तरा पणवीथ्यश्च नानापण्योपशोभिताः । अनुगच्छन्तु काकुत्स्थं तथैव नटनर्तकाः ।। 7.64.3 ।।
transliteration: antarā paṇavīthyaśca nānāpaṇyopaśobhitāḥ | anugacchantu kākutsthaṃ tathaiva naṭanartakāḥ || 7.64.3 ||
translation: अन्तरा in between, पणवीथ्यः market streets, च and, नानापण्योपशोभिताः adorned with various goods, अनुगच्छन्तु let them follow, काकुत्स्थम् Kakutstha, तथैव similarly, नटनर्तकाः actors and dancers.
explanation: Let market streets adorned with various goods, and similarly actors and dancers, follow Kakutstha along the way.

shloka_text: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य नियुतं पुरुषर्षभ । आदाय गच्छ शत्रुघ्न पर्याप्तधनवाहनः ।। 7.64.4 ।।
transliteration: hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya niyutaṃ puruṣarṣabha | ādāya gaccha śatrughna paryāptadhanavāhanaḥ || 7.64.4 ||
translation: हिरण्यस्य of gold, सुवर्णस्य of fine gold, नियुतम् a million, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, आदाय taking, गच्छ go, शत्रुघ्न O Shatrughna, पर्याप्तधनवाहनः having sufficient wealth and conveyances.
explanation: O Shatrughna, best among men, take a million units of gold and fine gold, and go, equipped with ample wealth and conveyances.

shloka_text: बलं च सुभृतं वीर हृष्टपुष्टमनुद्धतम् । सम्भाषासम्प्रदानेन रञ्जयस्व नगेत्तम ।। 7.64.5 ।।
transliteration: balaṃ ca subhṛtaṃ vīra hṛṣṭapuṣṭamanuddhatam | sambhāṣāsampradānena rañjayasva nagettama || 7.64.5 ||
translation: बलम् army, च and, सुभृतम् well-maintained, वीर O hero, हृष्टपुष्टम् cheerful and well-nourished, अनुद्धतम् disciplined, सम्भाषासम्प्रदानेन by good conversation and giving gifts, रञ्जयस्व please, नगेत्तम O best among men.
explanation: O hero, O best among men, please the well-maintained, cheerful, well-nourished, and disciplined army by engaging in good conversation and bestowing gifts.

shloka_text: न ह्यर्थास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः । सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गश्च यत्र तिष्ठसि राघव ।। 7.64.6 ।।
transliteration: na hyarthāstatra tiṣṭhanti na dārā na ca bāndhavāḥ | suprīto bhṛtyavargaśca yatra tiṣṭhasi rāghava || 7.64.6 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, अर्थाः wealth, तत्र there, तिष्ठन्ति remain, न nor, दाराः wives, न nor, च and, बान्धवाः relatives, सुप्रीतः well-pleased, भृत्यवर्गः servant class, च and, यत्र where, तिष्ठसि you stand, राघव O Raghava.
explanation: O Raghava, neither wealth, wives, nor relatives truly endure, but a well-pleased retinue will remain with you wherever you are.

shloka_text: ततो हृष्टजनाकीर्णां प्रस्थाप्य महतीं चमूम् । एक एव धनुष्पाणिर्गच्छ त्वं मधुनो वनम् ।। 7.64.7 ।।
transliteration: tato hṛṣṭajanākīrṇāṃ prasthāpya mahatīṃ camūm | eka eva dhanuṣpāṇirgaccha tvaṃ madhuno vanam || 7.64.7 ||
translation: ततो then, हृष्टजनाकीर्णां filled with joyful people, प्रस्थाप्य having dispatched, महतीं a great, चमूम् army, एक alone, एव indeed, धनुष्पाणिः holding a bow in hand, गच्छ go, त्वं you, मधुनो of Madhu, वनम् to the forest.
explanation: Then, having dispatched a great army filled with joyful people, you alone, holding a bow in hand, should go to the forest of Madhu.

shloka_text: यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम् । लवणस्तु मधोः पुत्रस्तथा गच्छेरशङ्कितम् ।। 7.64.8 ।।
transliteration: yathā tvāṃ na prajānāti gacchantaṃ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam | lavaṇastu madhoḥ putrastathā gaccheraśaṅkitam || 7.64.8 ||
translation: यथा so that, त्वां you, न not, प्रजानाति knows, गच्छन्तं going, युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम् desiring battle, लवणस्तु but Lavana, मधोः of Madhu, पुत्रः the son, तथा thus, गच्छेः you should go, अशङ्कितम् without suspicion.
explanation: You should go without suspicion, so that Lavana, the son of Madhu, does not recognize you as one going and desiring battle.

shloka_text: न तस्य मूत्युरन्यो ऽस्ति कश्चिद्धि पुरुषर्षभ । दर्शनं यो ऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि ।। 7.64.9 ।।
transliteration: na tasya mūtyuranyo 'sti kaściddhi puruṣarṣabha | darśanaṃ yo 'bhigaccheta sa vadhyo lavaṇena hi || 7.64.9 ||
translation: न not, तस्य his, मृत्युः death, अन्यः another, अस्ति is, कश्चित् any, हि indeed, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, दर्शनं sight, यः who, अभिगच्छेत approaches, सः he, वध्यः to be killed, लवणेन by Lavana, हि indeed.
explanation: O best among men, there is no other way to kill him, for anyone who approaches his sight is indeed slain by Lavana.

shloka_text: स हि ग्रीष्मो ऽपयाते तु वर्षारात्र उपागते । हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य सहि कालो ऽस्य दुर्मतेः ।। 7.64.10 ।।
transliteration: sa hi grīṣmo 'payāte tu varṣārātra upāgate | hanyāstvaṃ lavaṇaṃ saumya sahi kālo 'sya durmateḥ || 7.64.10 ||
translation: सः that, हि indeed, ग्रीष्मः summer, अपयाते having departed, तु but, वर्षारात्रे when the rainy season, उपागते has arrived, हन्याः you should kill, त्वं you, लवणं Lavana, सौम्य O gentle one, सः that, हि indeed, कालः time, अस्य for him, दुर्मतेः the wicked one.
explanation: O gentle one, you should kill Lavana when summer has departed and the rainy season has arrived, for that is indeed the opportune time for that wicked one.

shloka_text: महर्षींस्तु पुरत्कृत्य प्रयान्तु तव सौनिकाः । यथा ग्रीष्मावशेषेण तरेयुर्जाह्नवीजलम् ।। 7.64.11 ।।
transliteration: maharṣīṃstu puratkṛtya prayāntu tava saunikāḥ | yathā grīṣmāvaśeṣeṇa tareyurjāhnavījalam || 7.64.11 ||
translation: महर्षींस्तु but the great sages, पुरत्कृत्य having placed in front, प्रयान्तु let them go, तव your, सौनिकाः soldiers, यथा so that, ग्रीष्मावशेषेण with the remaining part of summer, तरेयुः they may cross, जाह्नवीजलम् the waters of the Ganga.
explanation: Let your soldiers proceed, placing the great sages in front, so that they may cross the waters of the Ganga with the remaining part of summer.

shloka_text: तत्र स्थाप्य बलं सर्वं नदीतीरे समाहितः । अग्रतो धनुषा सार्धं गच्छ त्वं लघुविक्रमः ।। 7.64.12 ।।
transliteration: tatra sthāpya balaṃ sarvaṃ nadītīre samāhitaḥ | agrato dhanuṣā sārdhaṃ gaccha tvaṃ laghuvikramaḥ || 7.64.12 ||
translation: तत्र there, स्थाप्य having stationed, बलं army, सर्वं all, नदीतीरे on the river bank, समाहितः having settled, अग्रतः in front, धनुषा with the bow, सार्धं together with, गच्छ go, त्वं you, लघुविक्रमः swift in action.
explanation: Having stationed your entire army on the river bank, you, swift in action, should proceed ahead with your bow.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण शत्रुघ्नस्तान्महाबलान् । सेनामुख्यान्समानीय ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.64.13 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu rāmeṇa śatrughnastānmahābalān | senāmukhyānsamānīya tato vākyamuvāca ha || 7.64.13 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, रामेण by Rama, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, तान् those, महाबलान् mighty, सेनामुख्यान् army chiefs, समानीय having gathered, ततः then, वाक्यम् words, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Shatrughna gathered those mighty army chiefs and then spoke these words.

shloka_text: एते वो गणिता वासा यत्र तत्र निवत्स्यथ । स्थातव्यं चाविरोधेन यथा बाधा न कस्यचित् ।। 7.64.14 ।।
transliteration: ete vo gaṇitā vāsā yatra tatra nivatsyatha | sthātavyaṃ cāvirodhena yathā bādhā na kasyacit || 7.64.14 ||
translation: एते these, वः your, गणिताः assigned, वासाः camps, यत्र where, तत्र there, निवत्स्यथ you shall dwell, स्थातव्यं one should stay, च and, अविरोधेन peacefully, यथा so that, बाधा trouble, न not, कस्यचित् to anyone.
explanation: These are your assigned camps where you shall dwell, and you must stay peacefully so that no one is troubled.

shloka_text: तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य प्रस्थाप्य च महद्बलम् । कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत् ।। 7.64.15 ।।
transliteration: tathā tāṃstu samājñāpya prasthāpya ca mahadbalam | kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat || 7.64.15 ||
translation: तथा thus, तान् them, तु indeed, समाज्ञाप्य having instructed, प्रस्थाप्य having sent forth, च and, महत् great, बलम् army, कौसल्यां Kausalya, च and, सुमित्रां Sumitra, च and, कैकेयीं Kaikeyi, च and, अभ्यवादयत् he saluted.
explanation: Having thus instructed them and sent forth the great army, he then saluted Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: रामं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शिरसा ऽभिप्रणम्य च । रामेण चाभ्यनुज्ञातः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुतापनः ।। 7.64.16 ।।
transliteration: rāmaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śirasā 'bhipraṇamya ca | rāmeṇa cābhyanujñātaḥ śatrughnaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ || 7.64.16 ||
translation: रामं Rama, प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य having circumambulated, शिरसा with his head, अभिप्रणम्य having bowed down, च and, रामेण by Rama, च and, अभ्यनुज्ञातः permitted, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, शत्रुतापनः tormentor of enemies.
explanation: Having circumambulated Rama and bowed down with his head, Shatrughna, the tormentor of enemies, was then given leave by Rama.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः । पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान् । प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा निर्जगाम महाबलः ।। 7.64.17 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ caiva praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ | purohitaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ prayatātmavān | pradakṣiṇamatho kṛtvā nirjagāma mahābalaḥ || 7.64.17 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, भरतं Bharata, चैव and also, प्रणिपत्य having bowed down, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, पुरोहितं to the priest, वसिष्ठं Vasishtha, च and, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, प्रयतात्मवान् with a controlled mind, प्रदक्षिणमथो then circumambulation, कृत्वा having done, निर्जगाम departed, महाबलः the mighty one.
explanation: The mighty and pure-minded Shatrughna, having bowed down with folded hands to Lakshmana, Bharata, and the priest Vasishtha, and having performed circumambulation, then departed.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य सेनामथ सो ऽग्रतस्तदा गजेन्द्रवाजिप्रवरौघसङ्कुलाम् । उपास मासं तु नरेन्द्रपार्श्वतस्त्वथ प्रयातो रघुवंशवर्धनः ।। 7.64.18 ।।
transliteration: prasthāpya senāmatha so 'gratastadā gajendravājipravaraughasaṅkulām | upāsa māsaṃ tu narendrapārśvatastvatha prayāto raghuvaṃśavardhanaḥ || 7.64.18 ||
translation: प्रस्थाप्य having sent forth, सेनाम् the army, अथ then, सः he, अग्रतः in front, तदा then, गजेन्द्रवाजिप्रवरौघसङ्कुलाम् crowded with excellent elephants and horses, उपास stayed, मासं for a month, तु indeed, नरेन्द्रपार्श्वतः by the king's side, त्वथ then, प्रयातः departed, रघुवंशवर्धनः the增ifier of the Raghu dynasty.
explanation: Having first sent forth his army, which was crowded with excellent elephants and horses, Shatrughna, the增ifier of the Raghu dynasty, then stayed by the king's side for a month before departing. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 64 ।। Thus ends the sixty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य च बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि । एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितं तदा ।। 7.65.1 ।।
transliteration: prasthāpya ca balaṃ sarvaṃ māsamātroṣitaḥ pathi | eka evāśu śatrughno jagāma tvaritaṃ tadā || 7.65.1 ||
translation: प्रस्थाप्य having sent forth, च and, बलं the army, सर्वं all, मासमात्रोषितः having stayed for only a month, पथि on the way, एक alone, एव indeed, आशु quickly, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, जगाम went, त्वरितं swiftly, तदा then.
explanation: After sending forth his entire army and staying on the way for only a month, Shatrughna then quickly went forth alone and swiftly.
comments: Going ahead alone, Shatrughna lodges at Valmiki's hermitage, where the sage tells of his ancestor Saudasa (Kalmashapada): how, having slain one of two rakshasas, the king was tricked by the survivor, disguised as Vasishtha, into serving human flesh and was cursed -- his own counter-curse, stayed by his wife, fell on his feet and spotted them, and Vasishtha later limited the curse to twelve years.

shloka_text: द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः । वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद्वासमुत्तमम् ।। 7.65.2 ।।
transliteration: dvirātramantare śūra uṣya rāghavanandanaḥ | vālmīkerāśramaṃ puṇyamagacchadvāsamuttamam || 7.65.2 ||
translation: द्विरात्रम् for two nights, अन्तरे during, शूरः the brave one, उष्य having stayed, राघवनन्दनः the delight of the Raghus, वाल्मीकेः of Valmiki, आश्रमं to the hermitage, पुण्यम् sacred, अगच्छत् went, वासम् dwelling, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: The brave Shatrughna, the delight of the Raghus, having stayed for two nights on the way, then went to the sacred and excellent hermitage of Valmiki.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाल्मीकिं मुनिसत्तमम् । कृताञ्जलिरथो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.65.3 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ vālmīkiṃ munisattamam | kṛtāñjaliratho bhūtvā vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.65.3 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, महात्मानं the great-souled, वाल्मीकिं Valmiki, मुनिसत्तमम् the best of sages, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, अथ then, भूत्वा having become, वाक्यम् words, एतत् these, उवाच spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: Having saluted the great-souled Valmiki, the best of sages, Shatrughna then stood with folded hands and spoke these words.

shloka_text: भगवन्वस्तुमिच्छामि गुरोः कृत्यादिहागतः । श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीचीं वारुणीं दिशम् ।। 7.65.4 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanvastumicchāmi guroḥ kṛtyādihāgataḥ | śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmi pratīcīṃ vāruṇīṃ diśam || 7.65.4 ||
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, वस्तुम् to stay, इच्छामि I wish, गुरोः from the guru's, कृत्यात् task, इह here, आगतः having come. श्वः tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, गमिष्यामि I shall go, प्रतीचीम् western, वारुणीम् of Varuna, दिशम् direction.
explanation: Shatrughna, having arrived there for his guru's task, requested permission to stay for the night, stating his intention to depart westward the next morning.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं स्वागतं ते महायशः ।। 7.65.5 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasya munipuṅgavaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ svāgataṃ te mahāyaśaḥ || 7.65.5 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नस्य Shatrughna's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रहस्य having smiled, मुनिपुङ्गवः the foremost among sages, प्रत्युवाच replied, महात्मानम् to the great-souled one, स्वागतम् welcome, ते to you, महायशः O greatly renowned one.
explanation: Hearing Shatrughna's words, the eminent sage Valmiki smiled and welcomed the great-souled and greatly renowned prince.

shloka_text: स्वमाश्रममिदं सौम्य राघवाणां कुलस्य हि । आसनं पाद्यमर्ध्यं च निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ मे ।। 7.65.6 ।।
transliteration: svamāśramamidaṃ saumya rāghavāṇāṃ kulasya hi | āsanaṃ pādyamardhyaṃ ca nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīccha me || 7.65.6 ||
translation: स्वम् your own, आश्रमम् hermitage, इदम् this, सौम्य O gentle one, राघवाणाम् of the Raghus, कुलस्य of the family, हि indeed. आसनम् seat, पाद्यम् water for feet, अर्ध्यम् water for respectful offering, च and, निर्विशङ्कः without hesitation, प्रतीच्छ accept, मे from me.
explanation: Valmiki assured Shatrughna that this hermitage was indeed like his own, belonging to the Raghu lineage, and urged him to accept the offered seat, water for feet, and respectful offering without any hesitation.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तदा पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम् । भक्षयामास काकुत्स्थस्तृप्तिं च परमां गतः ।। 7.65.7 ।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tadā pūjāṃ phalamūlaṃ ca bhojanam | bhakṣayāmāsa kākutsthastṛptiṃ ca paramāṃ gataḥ || 7.65.7 ||
translation: प्रतिगृह्य having accepted, तदा then, पूजां the hospitality, फलमूलम् fruits and roots, च and, भोजनम् food, भक्षयामास he ate, काकुत्स्थः Kakutstha's descendant, तृप्तिम् satisfaction, च and, परमाम् supreme, गतः attained.
explanation: Shatrughna, the descendant of Kakutstha, then accepted the hospitality, ate the offered fruits and roots, and achieved supreme satisfaction.

shloka_text: स भुक्त्वा फलमूलं च महर्षिं तमुवाच ह । इयं यज्ञविभूतिस्ते कस्याश्रमसमीपतः ।। 7.65.8 ।।
transliteration: sa bhuktvā phalamūlaṃ ca maharṣiṃ tamuvāca ha | iyaṃ yajñavibhūtiste kasyāśramasamīpataḥ || 7.65.8 ||
translation: सः he, भुक्त्वा having eaten, फलमूलम् fruits and roots, च and, महर्षिम् to the great sage, तम् him, उवाच spoke, ह indeed. इयम् this, यज्ञविभूतिः splendor of sacrifice, ते your, कस्य whose, आश्रमसमीपतः near the hermitage.
explanation: After eating the fruits and roots, Shatrughna then asked the great sage about the origin of the sacrificial splendor he observed near the hermitage.

shloka_text: तत्तस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् । शत्रुघ्न शृणु यस्येदं बभूवायतनं पुरा ।। 7.65.9 ।।
transliteration: tattasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā vālmīkirvākyamabravīt | śatrughna śṛṇu yasyedaṃ babhūvāyatanaṃ purā || 7.65.9 ||
translation: तत् that, तस्य his, भाषितं spoken words, श्रुत्वा having heard, वाल्मीकिः Valmiki, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, शत्रुघ्न O Shatrughna, शृणु listen, यस्य whose, इदं this, बभूव was, आयतनं abode, पुरा formerly,
explanation: Having heard his words, Valmiki spoke, saying, "O Shatrughna, listen to whose abode this place formerly was."

shloka_text: युष्माकं पूर्वको राजा सौदासस्तस्य भूपतेः । पुत्रो वीरसहो नाम वीर्यवानतिधार्मिकः ।। 7.65.10 ।।
transliteration: yuṣmākaṃ pūrvako rājā saudāsastasya bhūpateḥ | putro vīrasaho nāma vīryavānatidhārmikaḥ || 7.65.10 ||
translation: युष्माकं your, पूर्वको former, राजा king, सौदासः Saudasa, तस्य his, भूपतेः of the king, पुत्रो son, वीरसहो Virasaha, नाम named, वीर्यवान् valorous, अतिधार्मिकः very righteous,
explanation: Your ancestor was King Saudasa, and his son was named Virasaha, who was mighty and exceedingly righteous.

shloka_text: स बाल एव सौदासो मृगयामुपचक्रमे । चञ्चूर्यमाणं ददृशे स शूरो राक्षसद्वयम् ।। 7.65.11 ।।
transliteration: sa bāla eva saudāso mṛgayāmupacakrame | cañcūryamāṇaṃ dadṛśe sa śūro rākṣasadvayam || 7.65.11 ||
translation: स he, बाल young, एव indeed, सौदासो Saudasa, मृगयाम् hunting, उपचक्रमे undertook, चञ्चूर्यमाणं roaming about, ददृशे saw, स he, शूरो brave, राक्षसद्वयम् two rakshasas,
explanation: When Saudasa was still young, he went hunting and that brave king saw two rakshasas roaming about.

shloka_text: शार्दूलरूपिणौ घोरौ मृगान्बहुसहस्रशः । भक्षमाणावसन्तुष्टौ पर्याप्तिं नैव जग्मतुः ।। 7.65.12 ।।
transliteration: śārdūlarūpiṇau ghorau mṛgānbahusahasraśaḥ | bhakṣamāṇāvasantuṣṭau paryāptiṃ naiva jagmatuḥ || 7.65.12 ||
translation: शार्दूलरूपिणौ in the form of tigers, घोरौ terrible, मृगान् animals, बहुसहस्रशः many thousands, भक्षमाणौ eating, असन्तुष्टौ unsatisfied, पर्याप्तिं satisfaction, नैव never, जग्मतुः reached,
explanation: These two terrible rakshasas, in the form of tigers, were devouring many thousands of animals but remained unsatisfied, never reaching sufficiency.

shloka_text: स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मृगं च वनं कृतम् । क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो जघानैकं महेषुणा ।। 7.65.13 ।।
transliteration: sa tu tau rākṣasau dṛṣṭvā nirmṛgaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtam | krodhena mahatā ' 'viṣṭo jaghānaikaṃ maheṣuṇā || 7.65.13 ||
translation: स he, तु but, तौ those two, राक्षसौ rakshasas, दृष्ट्वा having seen, निर्मृगं devoid of animals, च and, वनं forest, कृतम् made, क्रोधेन by anger, महता great, आविष्टो overcome, जघानैकं killed one, महेषुणा with a great arrow,
explanation: But he, having seen those two rakshasas and the forest made devoid of animals, became overcome with great anger and killed one of them with a mighty arrow.

shloka_text: विनिपात्य तमेकं तु सौदासः पुरुषर्षभः । विज्वरो विगतामार्षो हतं रक्षो ह्युदैक्षत ।। 7.65.14 ।।
transliteration: vinipātya tamekaṃ tu saudāsaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ | vijvaro vigatāmārṣo hataṃ rakṣo hyudaikṣata || 7.65.14 ||
translation: विनिपात्य having struck down, तम् him, एकम् one, तु indeed, सौदासः Saudasa, पुरुषर्षभः best among men, विज्वरः free from distress, विगतामार्षः free from anger, हतम् killed, रक्षः the demon, हि indeed, उदैक्षत he saw.
explanation: King Saudasa, the best among men, having struck down that one demon, looked at the killed demon, now free from distress and anger.

shloka_text: निरीक्षमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा सहायं तस्य रक्षसः । सन्तापमकरोद्घोरं सौदासं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.65.15 ।।
transliteration: nirīkṣamāṇaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahāyaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ | santāpamakarodghoraṃ saudāsaṃ cedamabravīt || 7.65.15 ||
translation: निरीक्षमाणम् looking on, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सहायम् the companion, तस्य of that, रक्षसः demon, सन्तापम् sorrow, अकरोत् he made, घोरम् terrible, सौदासम् to Saudasa, च and, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् he said.
explanation: Having seen Saudasa looking on, the companion of that demon felt terrible sorrow and spoke these words to Saudasa.

shloka_text: यस्मादनपराधं त्वं सहायं मम जघ्निवान् । तस्मात्तवापि पापिष्ठ प्रदास्यामि प्रतिक्रियाम् ।। 7.65.16 ।।
transliteration: yasmādanaparādhaṃ tvaṃ sahāyaṃ mama jaghnivān | tasmāttavāpi pāpiṣṭha pradāsyāmi pratikriyām || 7.65.16 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, अनपराधम् innocent, त्वम् you, सहायम् companion, मम my, जघ्निवान् have killed, तस्मात् therefore, तव to you, अपि also, पापिष्ठ O most sinful one, प्रदास्यामि I will give, प्रतिक्रियाम् retaliation.
explanation: The demon declared, "Because you have killed my innocent companion, O most sinful one, I will therefore give you retaliation."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तद्राक्षस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । कालपर्याययोगेन राजा मित्रसहो ऽभवत् ।। 7.65.17 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu tadrākṣastatraivāntaradhīyata | kālaparyāyayogena rājā mitrasaho 'bhavat || 7.65.17 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तु indeed, तत् that, राक्षसः demon, तत्रैव right there, अन्तरधीयत disappeared, कालपर्याययोगेन by the passage of time, राजा the king, मित्रसहः Mitrasaha, अभवत् became.
explanation: Having spoken thus, that demon indeed disappeared right there, and in due course, the king became known as Mitrasaha.

shloka_text: राजापि यजते यज्ञमस्याश्रमसमीपतः । अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं तं वसिष्ठो ऽभ्यपालयत् ।। 7.65.18 ।।
transliteration: rājāpi yajate yajñamasyāśramasamīpataḥ | aśvamedhaṃ mahāyajñaṃ taṃ vasiṣṭho 'bhyapālayat || 7.65.18 ||
translation: राजा the king, अपि also, यजते performs, यज्ञम् a sacrifice, अस्य of this, आश्रमसमीपतः near the hermitage, अश्वमेधम् Ashwamedha, महायज्ञम् great sacrifice, तम् that, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, अभ्यपालयत् supervised.
explanation: The king also performs a great Ashwamedha sacrifice near this hermitage, and Vasishtha supervised that sacrifice.

shloka_text: तत्र यज्ञो महानासीद्बहुवर्षगणायुतः । समृद्धः परया लक्ष्म्या देवयज्ञसमो ऽभवत् ।। 7.65.19 ।।
transliteration: tatra yajño mahānāsīdbahuvarṣagaṇāyutaḥ | samṛddhaḥ parayā lakṣmyā devayajñasamo 'bhavat || 7.65.19 ||
translation: तत्र there, यज्ञो a sacrifice, महान् great, आसीत् was, बहुवर्षगणायुतः lasting for many years, समृद्धः prosperous, परया with supreme, लक्ष्म्या splendor, देवयज्ञसमः equal to a sacrifice of the gods, अभवत् it became.
explanation: There was a great sacrifice that lasted for many years, which became exceedingly prosperous and splendid, rivaling even the sacrifices performed by the gods.

shloka_text: अथावसाने यज्ञस्य पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् । वसिष्ठरूपी राजानमिति होवाच राक्षसः ।। 7.65.20 ।।
transliteration: athāvasāne yajñasya pūrvavairamanusmaran | vasiṣṭharūpī rājānamiti hovāca rākṣasaḥ || 7.65.20 ||
translation: अथ then, अवसाने at the conclusion, यज्ञस्य of the sacrifice, पूर्ववैरम् the old enmity, अनुस्मरन् remembering, वसिष्ठरूपी in the form of Vasiṣṭha, राजानम् to the king, इति thus, होवाच spoke, राक्षसः the demon.
explanation: Then, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, the demon, remembering his old enmity and disguised as Vasiṣṭha, spoke thus to the king.

shloka_text: अस्य यज्ञस्य जातो ऽन्तः सामिषं भोजनं मम । दीयतामिह शीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।। 7.65.21 ।।
transliteration: asya yajñasya jāto 'ntaḥ sāmiṣaṃ bhojanaṃ mama | dīyatāmiha śīghraṃ vai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 7.65.21 ||
translation: अस्य of this, यज्ञस्य sacrifice, जातः has come, अन्तः the end, सामिषम् with meat, भोजनम् food, मम for me, दीयताम् let it be given, इह here, शीघ्रम् quickly, वै indeed, न not, अत्र here, कार्या should be done, विचारणा deliberation.
explanation: The demon, disguised as Vasiṣṭha, demanded that since the sacrifice had concluded, meat-laden food should be given to him quickly without any further deliberation.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं रक्षसा ब्रह्मरूपिणा । भक्ष्यसंस्कारकुशलमुवाच पृथिवीपतिः ।। 7.65.22 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rakṣasā brahmarūpiṇā | bhakṣyasaṃskārakuśalamuvāca pṛthivīpatiḥ || 7.65.22 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, व्याहृतम् spoken, वाक्यम् word, रक्षसा by the demon, ब्रह्मरूपिणा in the form of a Brahmin, भक्ष्यसंस्कारकुशलम् to one skilled in preparing food, उवाच spoke, पृथिवीपतिः the king.
explanation: Having heard that speech spoken by the demon disguised as a Brahmin, the king then addressed the person skilled in preparing food.

shloka_text: हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम् । तथा कुरुष्व शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद्यथा गुरुः ।। 7.65.23 ।।
transliteration: haviṣyaṃ sāmiṣaṃ svādu yathā bhavati bhojanam | tathā kuruṣva śīghraṃ vai parituṣyedyathā guruḥ || 7.65.23 ||
translation: हविष्यम् sacrificial food, सामिषम् with meat, स्वादु delicious, यथा so that, भवति it becomes, भोजनम् food, तथा thus, कुरुष्व do, शीघ्रम् quickly, वै indeed, परितुष्येत् may be pleased, यथा so that, गुरुः the preceptor.
explanation: The king instructed the cook to quickly prepare the sacrificial food with meat, making it delicious, so that the preceptor (Vasiṣṭha) would be pleased.

shloka_text: शासनात्पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य सूदः सम्भ्रान्तमानसः । स राक्षसः पुनस्तत्र सूदवेषमथाकरोत् ।। 7.65.24 ।।
transliteration: śāsanātpārthivendrasya sūdaḥ sambhrāntamānasaḥ | sa rākṣasaḥ punastatra sūdaveṣamathākarot || 7.65.24 ||
translation: शासनात् from the command, पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य of the king of kings, सूदः the cook, सम्भ्रान्तमानसः with a bewildered mind, सः that, राक्षसः demon, पुनः again, तत्र there, सूदवेषम् the guise of a cook, अथ then, अकरोत् assumed.
explanation: Due to the king's command, the cook was bewildered, and that demon again assumed the guise of a cook there.

shloka_text: स मानुषमथो मांसं पार्थिवाय न्यवेदयत् । इदं स्वादु हविष्यं च सामिषं चान्नमाहृतम् ।। 7.65.25 ।।
transliteration: sa mānuṣamatho māṃsaṃ pārthivāya nyavedayat | idaṃ svādu haviṣyaṃ ca sāmiṣaṃ cānnamāhṛtam || 7.65.25 ||
translation: सः he, मानुषम् human, अथ then, मांसम् flesh, पार्थिवाय to the king, न्यवेदयत् presented, इदम् this, स्वादु delicious, हविष्यम् fit for oblation, च and, सामिषम् with meat, च and, अन्नम् food, आहृतम् brought.
explanation: He then presented human flesh to the king, saying, "This delicious food, fit for oblation and mixed with meat, has been brought."

shloka_text: स भोजनं वसिष्ठाय पत्न्या सार्धमुपाहरत् । मदयन्त्या नरव्याघ्र सामिषं रक्षसा हृतम् ।। 7.65.26 ।।
transliteration: sa bhojanaṃ vasiṣṭhāya patnyā sārdhamupāharat | madayantyā naravyāghra sāmiṣaṃ rakṣasā hṛtam || 7.65.26 ||
translation: सः he, भोजनम् the meal, वसिष्ठाय to Vasistha, पत्न्या with his wife, सार्धम् together, उपाहरत् offered, मदयन्त्या with Madayanti, नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, सामिषम् with meat, रक्षसा by the demon, हृतम् prepared.
explanation: O tiger among men, he (the king) offered that meal, which was prepared with meat by the demon, to Vasistha along with his wife Madayanti.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा तदामिषं विप्रो मानुषं भाजनं गतम् । क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.65.27 ।।
transliteration: jñātvā tadāmiṣaṃ vipro mānuṣaṃ bhājanaṃ gatam | krodhena mahatā ' 'viṣṭo vyāhartumupacakrame || 7.65.27 ||
translation: ज्ञात्वा having known, तत् that, आमिषम् meat, विप्रः the brahmin, मानुषम् human, भाजनम् into the vessel, गतम् gone, क्रोधेन by anger, महता great, आविष्टः overcome, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Realizing that the meat in the vessel was human flesh, the brahmin (Vasistha), overcome by great anger, began to speak (a curse).

shloka_text: यस्मात्त्वं भोजनं राजन्ममैतद्दातुमिच्छसि । तस्माद्भोजनमेतत्ते भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.65.28 ।।
transliteration: yasmāttvaṃ bhojanaṃ rājanmamaitaddātumicchasi | tasmādbhojanametatte bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.65.28 ||
translation: यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, भोजनम् food, राजन् O king, मम to me, एतत् this, दातुम् to give, इच्छसि desire, तस्मात् therefore, भोजनम् food, एतत् this, ते your, भविष्यति will be, न no, संशयः doubt.
explanation: "Because you desire to give me this food, O king, therefore this very food shall be yours, without a doubt," (Vasistha cursed).

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धस्तु सौदासस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना । वसिष्ठं शप्तुमारेभे भार्या चैनमवारयत् ।। 7.65.29 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kruddhastu saudāsastoyaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā | vasiṣṭhaṃ śaptumārebhe bhāryā cainamavārayat || 7.65.29 ||
translation: ततः then, क्रुद्धस्तु enraged, सौदासः Saudasa, तोयम् water, जग्राह took, पाणिना with his hand, वसिष्ठम् Vasistha, शप्तुम् to curse, आरेभे began, भार्या his wife, च and, एनम् him, अवारयत् restrained.
explanation: Then, enraged, King Saudasa took water in his hand and began to curse Vasistha, but his wife restrained him.

shloka_text: राजन्प्रभुर्यतो ऽस्माकं वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः । प्रतिशप्तुं न शक्तस्त्वं देवतुल्यं पुरोधसम् ।। 7.65.30 ।।
transliteration: rājanprabhuryato 'smākaṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ | pratiśaptuṃ na śaktastvaṃ devatulyaṃ purodhasam || 7.65.30 ||
translation: राजन् O King, प्रभुः master, यतः because, अस्माकम् our, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, भगवान् revered, ऋषिः sage, प्रतिशप्तुम् to curse back, न not, शक्तः capable, त्वम् you, देवतुल्यम् god-like, पुरोधसम् priest.
explanation: She said, "O King, because the revered sage Vasistha is our master, you are not capable of cursing back this god-like priest."

shloka_text: ततः क्रोधमयं तोयं तेजोबलसमन्वितम् । व्यसर्जयत धर्मात्मा ततः पादौ सिषेच च ।। 7.65.31 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ krodhamayaṃ toyaṃ tejobalasamanvitam | vyasarjayata dharmātmā tataḥ pādau siṣeca ca || 7.65.31 ||
translation: ततः then, क्रोधमयम् imbued with anger, तोयम् water, तेजोबलसमन्वितम् endowed with power and strength, व्यसर्जयत released, धर्मात्मा the righteous one, ततः then, पादौ feet, सिषेच sprinkled, च and.
explanation: Then, the righteous king, releasing the water imbued with anger, power, and strength, poured it onto his own feet.

shloka_text: तेनास्य राज्ञस्तौ पादौ तदा कल्माषतां गतौ । तदाप्रभृति राजा ऽसौ सौदासः सुमहायशाः । कल्माषपादः संवृत्तः ख्यातश्चैव तथा नृपः ।। 7.65.32 ।।
transliteration: tenāsya rājñastau pādau tadā kalmāṣatāṃ gatau | tadāprabhṛti rājā 'sau saudāsaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ | kalmāṣapādaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ khyātaścaiva tathā nṛpaḥ || 7.65.32 ||
translation: तेन by that, अस्य his, राज्ञः of the king, तौ those, पादौ feet, तदा then, कल्माषताम् spottedness, गतौ attained, तदाप्रभृति from then onwards, राजा king, असौ that, सौदासः Saudasa, सुमहायशाः greatly renowned, कल्माषपादः Kalmashapada, संवृत्तः became, ख्यातः famous, चैव and indeed, तथा thus, नृपः king.
explanation: By that water, the king's feet then became spotted, and from that time onwards, the greatly renowned King Saudasa became known as Kalmashapada, the spotted-footed king.

shloka_text: स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः । पुनर्वसिष्ठं प्रोवाच यदुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणा ।। 7.65.33 ।।
transliteration: sa rājā saha patnyā vai praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ | punarvasiṣṭhaṃ provāca yaduktaṃ brahmarūpiṇā || 7.65.33 ||
translation: सः that, राजा king, सह with, पत्न्या his wife, वै indeed, प्रणिपत्य having bowed down, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, पुनः again, वसिष्ठम् to Vasistha, प्रोवाच spoke, यत् what, उक्तम् was said, ब्रह्मरूपिणा by the one in the form of Brahma.
explanation: That king, along with his wife, having bowed down repeatedly, then spoke again to Vasistha, who was like Brahma in his wisdom.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य रक्षसा विकृतं च तत् । पुनः प्रोवाच राजानं वसिष्ठः पुरुषर्षभम् ।। 7.65.34 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā pārthivendrasya rakṣasā vikṛtaṃ ca tat | punaḥ provāca rājānaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ puruṣarṣabham || 7.65.34 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य of the king of kings, रक्षसा by the Rakshasa, विकृतं transformed, च and, तत् that, पुनः again, प्रोवाच spoke, राजानं to the king, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, पुरुषर्षभम् to the best among men.
explanation: Having heard that the king of kings was transformed by the Rakshasa, Vasistha again spoke to the king, who was the best among men.

shloka_text: मया रोषपरीतेन यदिदं व्याहृतं वचः । नैतच्छक्यं वृथा कर्तुं प्रदास्यामि च ते वरम् ।। 7.65.35 ।।
transliteration: mayā roṣaparītena yadidaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ | naitacchakyaṃ vṛthā kartuṃ pradāsyāmi ca te varam || 7.65.35 ||
translation: मया by me, रोषपरीतेन overcome by anger, यत् which, इदं this, व्याहृतं spoken, वचः word, न not, एतत् this, शक्यं possible, वृथा in vain, कर्तुं to make, प्रदास्यामि I will give, च and, ते to you, वरम् a boon.
explanation: The words I have spoken while overcome by anger cannot be made in vain, but I will grant you a boon.

shloka_text: कालो द्वादश वर्षाणि शापस्यान्तो भविष्यति । मत्प्रासादाच्च राजेन्द्र व्यतीतं न स्मरिष्यसि ।। 7.65.36 ।।
transliteration: kālo dvādaśa varṣāṇi śāpasyānto bhaviṣyati | matprāsādācca rājendra vyatītaṃ na smariṣyasi || 7.65.36 ||
translation: कालः the time, द्वादश twelve, वर्षाणि years, शापस्य of the curse, अन्तः the end, भविष्यति will be, मत्प्रासादात् by my grace, च and, राजेन्द्र O king of kings, व्यतीतं what has passed, न not, स्मरिष्यसि you will remember.
explanation: The duration of the curse will be twelve years, and by my grace, O king of kings, you will not remember what has transpired.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुज्यारिसूदनः । प्रतिलेभे पुना राज्यं प्रजाश्चैवान्वपालयत् ।। 7.65.37 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā taṃ śāpamupabhujyārisūdanaḥ | pratilebhe punā rājyaṃ prajāścaivānvapālayat || 7.65.37 ||
translation: एवं thus, सः that, राजा king, तं that, शापं curse, उपभुज्य having experienced, अरिसूदनः destroyer of enemies, प्रतिलेभे regained, पुनः again, राज्यं kingdom, प्रजाः subjects, च and, एव indeed, अन्वपालयत् protected.
explanation: Thus, that king, the destroyer of enemies, having endured the curse, regained his kingdom and indeed protected his subjects.

shloka_text: तस्य कल्माषपादस्य यज्ञस्यायतनं शुभम् । आश्रमस्य समीपे ऽस्य यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव ।। 7.65.38 ।।
transliteration: tasya kalmāṣapādasya yajñasyāyatanaṃ śubham | āśramasya samīpe 'sya yanmāṃ pṛcchasi rāghava || 7.65.38 ||
translation: तस्य of him, कल्माषपादस्य of Kalmashapada, यज्ञस्य of the sacrifice, आयतनं the place, शुभम् auspicious, आश्रमस्य of the hermitage, समीपे near, अस्य of this, यत् which, मां me, पृच्छसि you ask, राघव O Raghava.
explanation: O Raghava, the auspicious place of sacrifice belonging to Kalmashapada, which you ask me about, is near this hermitage.

shloka_text: तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम् । विवेश पर्णशालायां महर्षिमभिवाद्य च ।। 7.65.39 ।।
transliteration: tasya tāṃ pārthivendrasya kathāṃ śrutvā sudāruṇām | viveśa parṇaśālāyāṃ maharṣimabhivādya ca || 7.65.39 ||
translation: तस्य his, ताम् that, पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य of the king, कथाम् story, श्रुत्वा having heard, सुदारुणाम् very terrible, विवेश entered, पर्णशालायाम् into the hermitage, महर्षिम् the great sage, अभिवाद्य having saluted, च and.
explanation: Having heard that very terrible story of the king, he saluted the great sage and entered the hermitage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 65 ।। Thus ends the sixty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: यामेव रात्रिं शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालामुपाविशत् । तामेव रात्रिं सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् ।। 7.66.1 ।।
transliteration: yāmeva rātriṃ śatrughnaḥ parṇaśālāmupāviśat | tāmeva rātriṃ sītāpi prasūtā dārakadvayam || 7.66.1 ||
translation: यामेव the very same, रात्रिम् night, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, पर्णशालाम् the hermitage, उपाविशत् entered, तामेव the very same, रात्रिम् night, सीतापि Sita also, प्रसूता gave birth, दारकद्वयम् to two sons.
explanation: The very same night that Shatrughna stayed in the hermitage, Sita also gave birth to two sons.
comments: That very night Sita bears twin sons at the hermitage, and Valmiki performs the protective rites, naming the elder Kusha and the younger Lava -- Shatrughna hears the joyful news and congratulates Sita, then at dawn departs westward and reaches the sages' hermitage on the Yamuna.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धरात्रसमये बालका मुनिदारकाः । वाल्मीकेः प्रियमाचख्युः सीतायाः प्रसवं शुभम् ।। 7.66.2 ।।
transliteration: tato 'rdharātrasamaye bālakā munidārakāḥ | vālmīkeḥ priyamācakhyuḥ sītāyāḥ prasavaṃ śubham || 7.66.2 ||
translation: ततो then, अर्धरात्रसमये at midnight, बालकाः boys, मुनिदारकाः hermitage boys, वाल्मीकेः to Valmiki, प्रियम् the pleasing news, आचख्युः announced, सीतायाः of Sita, प्रसवम् the birth, शुभम् auspicious.
explanation: Then, at midnight, the hermitage boys announced the auspicious birth of Sita's children to Valmiki.

shloka_text: भगवन्रामपत्नी सा प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् । ततो रक्षां महातेजः कुरु भूतविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.3 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanrāmapatnī sā prasūtā dārakadvayam | tato rakṣāṃ mahātejaḥ kuru bhūtavināśinīm || 7.66.3 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, रामपत्नी Rama's wife, सा she, प्रसूता has given birth, दारकद्वयम् to two sons, ततो therefore, रक्षाम् protection, महातेजः O greatly effulgent one, कुरु perform, भूतविनाशिनीम् that which destroys evil spirits.
explanation: They informed him, "O revered and greatly effulgent one, Rama's wife has given birth to two sons, so please perform the protective rituals that destroy evil spirits."

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः समुपागमत् । बालचन्द्रप्रतीकाशौ देवपुत्रौ महौजसौ ।। 7.66.4 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā maharṣiḥ samupāgamat | bālacandrapratīkāśau devaputrau mahaujasau || 7.66.4 ||
translation: तेषाम् their, तत् that, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, महर्षिः the great sage, समुपागमत् approached, बालचन्द्रप्रतीकाशौ resembling the young moon, देवपुत्रौ divine sons, महौजसौ greatly powerful.
explanation: Having heard their words, the great sage approached, seeing the two greatly powerful divine sons who resembled the young moon.

shloka_text: जगाम तत्र हृष्टात्मा ददर्श च कुमारकौ । भूतघ्नीं चाकरोत्ताभ्यां रक्षां रक्षोविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.5 ।।
transliteration: jagāma tatra hṛṣṭātmā dadarśa ca kumārakau | bhūtaghnīṃ cākarottābhyāṃ rakṣāṃ rakṣovināśinīm || 7.66.5 ||
translation: जगाम went, तत्र there, हृष्टात्मा joyful-souled, ददर्श saw, च and, कुमारकौ the two boys, भूतघ्नीं demon-destroying, च and, अकरोत् he performed, ताभ्यां for them two, रक्षां protection, रक्षोविनाशिनीम् demon-destroying.
explanation: With a joyful mind, he went there, saw the two boys, and performed for them a protection ritual that destroys demons and malevolent spirits.

shloka_text: कुशमुष्टिमुपादाय लवं चैव तु स द्विजः । वाल्मीकिः प्रददौ ताभ्यां रक्षां भूतविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.6 ।।
transliteration: kuśamuṣṭimupādāya lavaṃ caiva tu sa dvijaḥ | vālmīkiḥ pradadau tābhyāṃ rakṣāṃ bhūtavināśinīm || 7.66.6 ||
translation: कुशमुष्टिम् a handful of Kuśa grass, उपादाय having taken, लवं a piece, च and, एव indeed, तु and, सः that, द्विजः brahmin, वाल्मीकिः Valmiki, प्रददौ gave, ताभ्यां to them two, रक्षां protection, भूतविनाशिनीम् demon-destroying.
explanation: Having taken a handful of Kuśa grass and a piece (of it), that brahmin Valmiki indeed gave to the two boys a protection that destroys demons.

shloka_text: यस्तयोः पूर्वजो जातः स कुशैर्मन्त्रसत्कृतैः । निर्मार्जनीयस्तु तदा कुश इत्यस्य नाम तत् ।। 7.66.7 ।।
transliteration: yastayoḥ pūrvajo jātaḥ sa kuśairmantrasatkṛtaiḥ | nirmārjanīyastu tadā kuśa ityasya nāma tat || 7.66.7 ||
translation: यः who, तयोः of them two, पूर्वजः first-born, जातः was born, सः he, कुशैः with Kuśa grass, मन्त्रसत्कृतैः consecrated with mantras, निर्मार्जनीयः was to be purified, तु and, तदा then, कुशः Kuśa, इति thus, अस्य his, नाम name, तत् that.
explanation: The one who was born first of the two, he was to be purified with Kuśa grass consecrated by mantras, and thus his name became Kuśa.

shloka_text: यश्चावरो भवेत्ताभ्यां लवेन स समाहितः । निर्मार्जनीयो वृद्धाभिर्लव इत्येव नामतः ।। 7.66.8 ।।
transliteration: yaścāvaro bhavettābhyāṃ lavena sa samāhitaḥ | nirmārjanīyo vṛddhābhirlava ityeva nāmataḥ || 7.66.8 ||
translation: यः who, च and, अवरः younger, भवेत् was, ताभ्यां of them two, लवेन with a piece, सः he, समाहितः carefully, निर्मार्जनीयः was to be purified, वृद्धाभिः by old women, लवः Lava, इति thus, एव indeed, नामतः by name.
explanation: And the one who was younger of the two, he was carefully purified with a piece (of Kuśa grass) by the old women, and thus he was named Lava.

shloka_text: एवं कुशलवौ नाम्ना तावुभौ यमजातकौ । मत्कृताभ्यां च नामभ्यां ख्यातियुक्तौ भविष्यतः ।। 7.66.9 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ kuśalavau nāmnā tāvubhau yamajātakau | matkṛtābhyāṃ ca nāmabhyāṃ khyātiyuktau bhaviṣyataḥ || 7.66.9 ||
translation: एवं thus, कुशलवौ Kuśa and Lava, नाम्ना by name, तौ those, उभौ both, यमजातकौ born as twins, मत्कृताभ्यां given by me, च and, नामभ्यां by names, ख्यातिमुक्तौ renowned, भविष्यतः will become.
explanation: Thus, these two, born as twins, will be known by the names Kuśa and Lava, and will become renowned by these names given by me.

shloka_text: तां रक्षां जगृहुस्ताश्च मुनिहस्तात्समाहिताः । अकुर्वंश्च ततो रक्षां तयोर्विगतकल्मषाः ।। 7.66.10 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ rakṣāṃ jagṛhustāśca munihastātsamāhitāḥ | akurvaṃśca tato rakṣāṃ tayorvigatakalmaṣāḥ || 7.66.10 ||
translation: तां that, रक्षां protection, जगृहुः they took, ताः they (the women), च and, मुनिहस्तात् from the hands of the sage, समाहिताः attentive, अकुर्वंश्च and they performed, ततः then, रक्षां protection, तयोः for the two (newborns), विगतकल्मषाः purified.
explanation: The attentive women took the protective charm from the sage's hands and, being purified, then performed the protective rites for the two newborns.

shloka_text: तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्जन्म नाम च । सङ्कीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ ।। 7.66.11 ।।
transliteration: tathā tāṃ kriyamāṇāṃ ca vṛddhābhirjanma nāma ca | saṅkīrtanaṃ ca rāmasya sītāyāḥ prasavau śubhau || 7.66.11 ||
translation: तथा thus, तां that, क्रियमाणां being performed, च and, वृद्धाभिः by the elderly women, जन्म birth, नाम name, च and, सङ्कीर्तनं chanting, च and, रामस्य of Rama, सीतायाः of Sita, प्रसवौ the two births, शुभौ auspicious.
explanation: Thus, while that (protection) was being performed by the elderly women, there was also chanting of Rama's name and glorification of Sita's two auspicious births.

shloka_text: अर्धरात्रे तु शत्रुघ्नः शुश्राव सुमहत्प्रियम् । पर्णशालां ततो गत्वा मातर्दिष्ट्येति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.66.12 ।।
transliteration: ardharātre tu śatrughnaḥ śuśrāva sumahatpriyam | parṇaśālāṃ tato gatvā mātardiṣṭyeti cābravīt || 7.66.12 ||
translation: अर्धरात्रे at midnight, तु indeed, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, शुश्राव heard, सुमहत्प्रियम् very great good news, पर्णशालां to the hermitage, ततः then, गत्वा having gone, मातः O mother, दिष्ट्या fortunately, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् he said.
explanation: At midnight, Shatrughna heard the very great good news, and then, having gone to the hermitage, he said to Sita, "O mother, fortunately!"

shloka_text: तथा तस्य प्रहृष्टस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । व्यतीता वार्षिकी रात्रिः श्रावणी लघुविक्रमः ।। 7.66.13 ।।
transliteration: tathā tasya prahṛṣṭasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | vyatītā vārṣikī rātriḥ śrāvaṇī laghuvikramaḥ || 7.66.13 ||
translation: तथा thus, तस्य his, प्रहृष्टस्य overjoyed, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, व्यतीता passed, वार्षिकी rainy season's, रात्रिः night, श्रावणी of Shravana, लघुविक्रमः swiftly.
explanation: Thus, for the overjoyed, great-souled Shatrughna, the night of Shravana, which marked the rainy season, passed swiftly.

shloka_text: प्रभाते सुमहावीर्यः कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकीं क्रियाम् । मुनिं प्राञ्जलिरामन्त्र्य ययौ पश्चान्मुखः पुनः ।। 7.66.14 ।।
transliteration: prabhāte sumahāvīryaḥ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikīṃ kriyām | muniṃ prāñjalirāmantrya yayau paścānmukhaḥ punaḥ || 7.66.14 ||
translation: प्रभाते in the morning, सुमहावीर्यः the very mighty (Shatrughna), कृत्वा having performed, पौर्वाह्णिकीं morning's, क्रियाम् rites, मुनिं the sage, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, आमन्त्र्य having bid farewell, ययौ he went, पश्चान्मुखः facing west, पुनः again.
explanation: In the morning, the very mighty Shatrughna, having performed his morning rites and having bid farewell to the sage with folded hands, again departed, facing west.

shloka_text: स गत्वा यमुनातीरं सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि । ऋषीणां पुण्यकीर्तीनामाश्रमे वासमभ्ययात् ।। 7.66.15 ।।
transliteration: sa gatvā yamunātīraṃ saptarātroṣitaḥ pathi | ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakīrtīnāmāśrame vāsamabhyayāt || 7.66.15 ||
translation: स he, गत्वा having gone, यमुनातीरं to the bank of Yamuna, सप्तरात्रोषितः having stayed for seven nights, पथि on the way, ऋषीणां of the sages, पुण्यकीर्तीनाम् of pure fame, आश्रमे in the hermitage, वासम residence, अभ्ययात् he obtained.
explanation: Having traveled and stayed for seven nights on the way, he reached the bank of the Yamuna and obtained residence in the hermitage of the sages of pure fame.

shloka_text: स तत्र मुनिभिः सार्धं भार्गवप्रमुखैर्नृपः । कथाभिरभिरूपाभिर्वासं चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.66.16 ।।
transliteration: sa tatra munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhārgavapramukhairnṛpaḥ | kathābhirabhirūpābhirvāsaṃ cakre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.66.16 ||
translation: स he, तत्र there, मुनिभिः with the sages, सार्धं together, भार्गवप्रमुखैः with Bhargava (Chyavana) as the chief, नृपः the king, कथाभिः with stories, अभिरूपाभिः delightful, वासं his stay, चक्रे he made, महायशाः the greatly renowned one.
explanation: There, the greatly renowned king spent his stay with the sages, led by Bhargava, engaging in delightful conversations.

shloka_text: स काञ्चनाद्यैर्मुनिभिः समेतो रघुप्रवीरो रजनीं तदानीम् । कथाप्रकारैर्बहुभिर्महात्मा विरामयामास नरेन्द्रसूनुः ।। 7.66.17 ।।
transliteration: sa kāñcanādyairmunibhiḥ sameto raghupravīro rajanīṃ tadānīm | kathāprakārairbahubhirmahātmā virāmayāmāsa narendrasūnuḥ || 7.66.17 ||
translation: स he, काञ्चनाद्यैः with Kanchana and others, मुनिभिः with the sages, समेतः accompanied by, रघुप्रवीरः the hero of Raghu's lineage, रजनीं the night, तदानीम् then, कथाप्रकारैः with various kinds of stories, बहुभिः many, महात्मा the great-souled one, विरामयामास he passed, नरेन्द्रसूनुः the son of the king.
