explanation: Then, the great-souled Shatrughna, the hero of Raghu's lineage and son of the king, accompanied by sages like Kanchana and others, passed the night with many kinds of stories. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 66 ।। Thus ends the sixty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां प्रवृत्तायां शत्रुघ्नो भृगुनन्दनम् । पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथा बलम् ।। 7.67.1 ।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ śatrughno bhṛgunandanam | papraccha cyavanaṃ vipraṃ lavaṇasya yathā balam || 7.67.1 ||
translation: अथ then, रात्र्यां the night, प्रवृत्तायां having advanced, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, भृगुनन्दनम् the son of Bhrigu, पप्रच्छ he asked, च्यवनं Chyavana, विप्रं the brahmin, लवणस्य of Lavana, यथा how, बलम् the strength.
explanation: Then, as the night advanced, Shatrughna asked the brahmin Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu, about the extent of Lavana's strength.
comments: Shatrughna asks of the trident's power, and Chyavana tells of King Mandhata, who, having conquered the earth, sought heaven, but was told by Indra he must first subdue Lavana -- challenging the demon, Mandhata was burned to ashes with the trident -- Chyavana assures Shatrughna of victory on the morrow if he catches Lavana away from his weapon.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन्के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः । अनेन शूलमुख्येन द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागताः ।। 7.67.2 ।।
transliteration: śūlasya ca balaṃ brahmanke ca pūrvaṃ vināśitāḥ | anena śūlamukhyena dvandvayuddhamupāgatāḥ || 7.67.2 ||
translation: शूलस्य of the trident, च and, बलं the strength, ब्रह्मन् O Brahmana, के who, च and, पूर्वं previously, विनाशिताः were destroyed, अनेन by this, शूलमुख्येन by the chief trident, द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् single combat, उपागताः who engaged in.
explanation: O Brahmana, Shatrughna further inquired about the strength of the trident and who had previously been destroyed by this formidable trident when they engaged in single combat.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजाश्च्यवनो रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.67.3 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejāścyavano raghunandanam || 7.67.3 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् वचनम् that word, श्रुत्वा having heard, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः the great-souled, प्रत्युवाच replied, महातेजाः the greatly effulgent, च्यवनः Chyavana, रघुनन्दनम् to the delight of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: Having heard those words of the great-souled Shatrughna, the greatly effulgent Chyavana replied to the scion of Raghu.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्येयानि कर्माणि यान्यस्य रघुनन्दन । इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणष्व मे ।। 7.67.4 ।।
transliteration: asaṅkhyeyāni karmāṇi yānyasya raghunandana | ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhave yadvṛttaṃ tacchṛṇaṣva me || 7.67.4 ||
translation: असङ्ख्येयानि innumerable, कर्माणि deeds, यानि which, अस्य of him, रघुनन्दन O delight of Raghu's lineage, इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे born in the Ikshvaku lineage, यत् वृत्तम् what happened, तत् that, शृणष्व listen, मे from me.
explanation: O scion of Raghu, listen to me about the innumerable deeds and the story of him who was born in the Ikshvaku lineage.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायां पुरा राजा युवनाश्वसुतो बली । मान्धातेति स विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ।। 7.67.5 ।।
transliteration: ayodhyāyāṃ purā rājā yuvanāśvasuto balī | māndhāteti sa vikhyātastriṣu lokeṣu vīryavān || 7.67.5 ||
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, पुरा formerly, राजा king, युवनाश्वसुतः son of Yuvanashva, बली powerful, मान्धाता इति as Mandhata, सः he, विख्यातः renowned, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds, वीर्यवान् valorous.
explanation: Formerly in Ayodhya, there was a powerful king, the son of Yuvanashva, who was renowned as Mandhata and was valorous in the three worlds.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां शासने पृथिवीपतिः । सुरलोकमितो जेतुमुद्योगमकरोन्नृपः ।। 7.67.6 ।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śāsane pṛthivīpatiḥ | suralokamito jetumudyogamakaronnṛpaḥ || 7.67.6 ||
translation: सः he, कृत्वा having made, पृथिवीम् the earth, कृत्स्नाम् entire, शासने under his rule, पृथिवीपतिः the lord of the earth, सुरलोकम् the world of gods, इतः from here, जेतुम् to conquer, उद्योगम् effort, अकरोत् made, नृपः the king.
explanation: Having brought the entire earth under his rule, that king, the lord of the earth, then made an effort to conquer the world of the gods from here.

shloka_text: इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्रं सुराणां च महात्मनाम् । मान्धातरि कृतोद्योगे देवलोकजिगीषया ।। 7.67.7 ।।
transliteration: indrasya ca bhayaṃ tīvraṃ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām | māndhātari kṛtodyoge devalokajigīṣayā || 7.67.7 ||
translation: इन्द्रस्य of Indra, च and, भयम् fear, तीव्रम् intense, सुराणाम् of the gods, च and, महात्मनाम् the great-souled, मान्धातरि when Mandhata, कृतोद्योगे had made the effort, देवलोकजिगीषया with the desire to conquer the world of gods.
explanation: Intense fear arose in Indra and the great-souled gods when Mandhata made the effort with the desire to conquer the world of the gods.

shloka_text: अर्धासनेन शक्रस्य राज्यार्धेन च पार्थिवः । वन्द्यमानः सुरगणैः प्रतिज्ञामध्यरोहत ।। 7.67.8 ।।
transliteration: ardhāsanena śakrasya rājyārdhena ca pārthivaḥ | vandyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ pratijñāmadhyarohata || 7.67.8 ||
translation: अर्धासनेन by half-seat, शक्रस्य of Indra, राज्यार्धेन by half-kingdom, च and, पार्थिवः the king, वन्द्यमानः being saluted, सुरगणैः by hosts of gods, प्रतिज्ञाम् a vow, अध्यरोहत he undertook.
explanation: The king, Mandhata, who was honored with half of Indra's seat and half of his kingdom, and saluted by the hosts of gods, then undertook a challenge.

shloka_text: तस्य पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाकशासनः । सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच युवनाश्वजम् ।। 7.67.9 ।।
transliteration: tasya pāpamabhiprāyaṃ viditvā pākaśāsanaḥ | sāntvapūrvamidaṃ vākyamuvāca yuvanāśvajam || 7.67.9 ||
translation: तस्य his, पापम् sinful, अभिप्रायम् intention, विदित्वा having known, पाकशासनः Indra, सान्त्वपूर्वम् gentle, इदम् this, वाक्यम् word, उवाच he spoke, युवनाश्वजम् to the son of Yuvanashva.
explanation: Knowing Mandhata's sinful intention, Indra, the slayer of Paka, spoke these conciliatory words to the son of Yuvanashva.

shloka_text: राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत्पुरुषर्षभ । अकृत्वा पृथिवीं वश्यां देवराज्यमिहेच्छसि ।। 7.67.10 ।।
transliteration: rājā tvaṃ mānuṣe loke na tāvatpuruṣarṣabha | akṛtvā pṛthivīṃ vaśyāṃ devarājyamihecchasi || 7.67.10 ||
translation: राजा king, त्वम् you, मानुषे in the human, लोके world, न not, तावत् yet, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, अकृत्वा without making, पृथिवीम् the earth, वश्याम् subservient, देवराज्यम् the kingdom of gods, इह here, इच्छसि you desire.
explanation: O best among men, you are a king in the human world, and you desire the kingdom of the gods here without first bringing the entire earth under your control.

shloka_text: यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे । देवराज्यं कुरुष्वेह सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.67.11 ।।
transliteration: yadi vīra samagrā te medinī nikhilā vaśe | devarājyaṃ kuruṣveha sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ || 7.67.11 ||
translation: यदि if, वीर O hero, समग्रा complete, ते your, मेदिनी earth, निखिला whole, वशे under control, देवराज्यम् kingdom of gods, कुरुष्व do, इह here, सभृत्यबलवाहनः with servants, army, and vehicles.
explanation: O hero, if your entire earth is completely under your control, then you may establish the kingdom of the gods here with your servants, army, and vehicles.

shloka_text: इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मान्धाता वाक्यमब्रवीत् । क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले ।। 7.67.12 ।।
transliteration: indramevaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ māndhātā vākyamabravīt | kva me śakra pratihataṃ śāsanaṃ pṛthivītale || 7.67.12 ||
translation: इन्द्रम् to Indra, एवम् thus, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, तम् to him, मान्धाता Mandhata, वाक्यम् word, अब्रवीत् he spoke, क्व where, मे my, शक्र O Indra, प्रतिहतम् obstructed, शासनम् rule, पृथिवीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: To Indra, who was speaking thus, Mandhata replied, "O Indra, where on the surface of the earth is my rule obstructed?"

shloka_text: तमुवाच सहस्राक्षो लवणो नाम राक्षसः । मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न ते ऽ ऽज्ञां कुरुते ऽनघ ।। 7.67.13 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca sahasrākṣo lavaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ | madhuputro madhuvane na te ' 'jñāṃ kurute 'nagha || 7.67.13 ||
translation: तम् him, उवाच said, सहस्राक्षः Indra, लवणः Lavana, नाम named, राक्षसः demon, मधुपुत्रः son of Madhu, मधुवने in Madhuvana, न not, ते your, आज्ञाम् command, कुरुते obeys, अनघ O sinless one.
explanation: Indra informed (Shatrughna) that a demon named Lavana, son of Madhu, residing in Madhuvana, does not obey his commands, O sinless one.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रियं घोरं सहस्राक्षेण भाषितम् । व्रीडितो ऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।। 7.67.14 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vipriyaṃ ghoraṃ sahasrākṣeṇa bhāṣitam | vrīḍito 'vāṅmukho rājā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha || 7.67.14 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, विप्रियम् unpleasant, घोरम् terrible, सहस्राक्षेण by Indra, भाषितम् spoken, व्रीडितः ashamed, अवाङ्मुखः with downcast face, राजा the king, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, न not, शशाक was able, ह indeed.
explanation: Having heard those terrible and unpleasant words spoken by Indra, the king (Shatrughna) was ashamed and, with a downcast face, was indeed unable to speak.

shloka_text: आमन्त्र्य तु सहस्राक्षं ह्रिया किञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः । पुनरेवागमच्छ्रीमानिमं लोकं नरेश्वरः ।। 7.67.15 ।।
transliteration: āmantrya tu sahasrākṣaṃ hriyā kiñcidavāṅmukhaḥ | punarevāgamacchrīmānimaṃ lokaṃ nareśvaraḥ || 7.67.15 ||
translation: आमन्त्र्य having bid farewell, तु and, सहस्राक्षम् to Indra, ह्रिया with shame, किञ्चित् somewhat, अवाङ्मुखः with downcast face, पुनरेव again indeed, आगमत् came, श्रीमान् glorious, इमम् this, लोकम् world, नरेश्वरः the lord of men.
explanation: And having bid farewell to Indra, the glorious lord of men (Shatrughna), still somewhat ashamed and with a downcast face, returned to this world.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा हृदये ऽमर्षं सभृत्यबलवाहनः । आजगाम मधोः पुत्रं वशे कर्तुमरिन्दमः ।। 7.67.16 ।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā hṛdaye 'marṣaṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ | ājagāma madhoḥ putraṃ vaśe kartumarindamaḥ || 7.67.16 ||
translation: सः he, कृत्वा having placed, हृदये in his heart, अमर्षम् indignation, सभृत्यबलवाहनः with servants, army, and vehicles, आजगाम came, मधोः of Madhu, पुत्रम् the son, वशे under control, कर्तुम् to make, अरिन्दमः the subduer of enemies.
explanation: Holding indignation in his heart, the subduer of enemies (Shatrughna) came with his servants, army, and vehicles to bring Madhu's son (Lavana) under his control.

shloka_text: स काङ्क्षमाणो लवणं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभः । दूतं सम्प्रेषयामास सकाशं लवणस्य हि ।। 7.67.17 ।।
transliteration: sa kāṅkṣamāṇo lavaṇaṃ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabhaḥ | dūtaṃ sampreṣayāmāsa sakāśaṃ lavaṇasya hi || 7.67.17 ||
translation: सः he, काङ्क्षमाणः desiring, लवणम् Lavana, युद्धाय for battle, पुरुषर्षभः the best among men, दूतम् a messenger, सम्प्रेषयामास sent, सकाशम् to the presence, लवणस्य of Lavana, हि indeed.
explanation: Desiring battle with Lavana, the best among men (Shatrughna) indeed sent a messenger to Lavana's presence.

shloka_text: स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम् । वदन्तमेवं तं दूतं भक्षयामास राक्षसः ।। 7.67.18 ।।
transliteration: sa gatvā vipriyāṇyāha bahūni madhunaḥ sutam | vadantamevaṃ taṃ dūtaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ || 7.67.18 ||
translation: सः he, गत्वा having gone, विप्रियाणि unpleasant things, आह said, बहूनि many, मधुनः of Madhu, सुतम् to the son, वदन्तम् speaking, एवम् thus, तम् that, दूतम् messenger, भक्षयामास devoured, राक्षसः the demon.
explanation: Having gone and spoken many unpleasant things to Madhu's son, the demon Lavaṇa devoured that messenger who was speaking thus.

shloka_text: चिरायमाणे दूते तु राजा क्रोधसमन्वितः । अर्दयामास तद्रक्षः शरवृष्ट्या समन्ततः ।। 7.67.19 ।।
transliteration: cirāyamāṇe dūte tu rājā krodhasamanvitaḥ | ardayāmāsa tadrakṣaḥ śaravṛṣṭyā samantataḥ || 7.67.19 ||
translation: चिरायमाणे when delaying, दूते the messenger, तु indeed, राजा the king, क्रोधसमन्वितः filled with anger, अर्दयामास tormented, तद्रक्षः that demon, शरवृष्ट्या with a shower of arrows, समन्ततः from all sides.
explanation: When the messenger delayed, the king, filled with anger, attacked that demon Lavaṇa from all sides with a shower of arrows.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य तद्रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना । वधाय सानुबन्धस्य मुमोचायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.20 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prahasya tadrakṣaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā | vadhāya sānubandhasya mumocāyudhamuttamam || 7.67.20 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रहस्य having laughed loudly, तद्रक्षः that demon, शूलम् the trident, जग्राह took, पाणिना with his hand, वधाय for the killing, सानुबन्धस्य along with his retinue, मुमोच released, आयुधम् the weapon, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: Then, that demon Lavaṇa laughed loudly, took the excellent trident in his hand, and released that supreme weapon to kill the king along with his retinue.

shloka_text: तच्छूलं दीप्यमानं तु सभृत्यबलवाहनम् । भस्मीकृत्वा नृपं भूयो लवणस्यागमत्करम् ।। 7.67.21 ।।
transliteration: tacchūlaṃ dīpyamānaṃ tu sabhṛtyabalavāhanam | bhasmīkṛtvā nṛpaṃ bhūyo lavaṇasyāgamatkaram || 7.67.21 ||
translation: तत् that, शूलम् trident, दीप्यमानम् shining brightly, तु indeed, सभृत्यबलवाहनम् along with servants, army, and vehicles, भस्मीकृत्वा having reduced to ashes, नृपम् the king, भूयः again, लवणस्य of Lavaṇa, आगमत् returned, करम् to the hand.
explanation: That brightly shining trident, having reduced the king along with his servants, army, and vehicles to ashes, then returned to Lavaṇa's hand.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा सुमहान्हतः सबलवाहनः । शूलस्य तु बलं सौम्य अप्रमेयमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.22 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā sumahānhataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ | śūlasya tu balaṃ saumya aprameyamanuttamam || 7.67.22 ||
translation: एवम् thus, सः that, राजा king, सुमहान् very great, हतः was killed, सबलवाहनः along with his army and vehicles, शूलस्य of the trident, तु indeed, बलम् the power, सौम्य O gentle one, अप्रमेयम् immeasurable, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed.
explanation: Thus, that very great king was killed along with his army and vehicles; indeed, O gentle one, the power of that trident is immeasurable and unsurpassed.

shloka_text: श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः । अगृहीतायुधं क्षिप्रं ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव ।। 7.67.23 ।।
transliteration: śvaḥ prabhāte tu lavaṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ | agṛhītāyudhaṃ kṣipraṃ dhruvo hi vijayastava || 7.67.23 ||
translation: श्वः tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, तु indeed, लवणं Lavana, वधिष्यसि you will kill, न not, संशयः doubt, अगृहीतायुधं when he has not taken his weapon, क्षिप्रं swiftly, ध्रुवो certain, हि indeed, विजयस्तव your victory.
explanation: Tomorrow morning, you will certainly kill Lavana, and your victory is assured, especially when he has not taken up his weapon.

shloka_text: लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्यात्कृते कर्मणि च त्वया । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं लवणस्य दुरात्मनः ।। 7.67.24 ।।
transliteration: lokānāṃ svasti caiva syātkṛte karmaṇi ca tvayā | etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ lavaṇasya durātmanaḥ || 7.67.24 ||
translation: लोकानां for the people, स्वस्ति welfare, चैव and indeed, स्यात् will be, कृते when done, कर्मणि the deed, च and, त्वया by you, एतत् this, ते to you, सर्वम् all, आख्यातं has been told, लवणस्य of Lavana, दुरात्मनः the wicked one.
explanation: The welfare of the worlds will be achieved by this deed done by you, and all this about the wicked Lavana has been told to you.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं घोरमप्रमेयं नरर्षभ । विनाशश्चैव मान्धातुर्यत्तेनाभूच्च पार्थिव ।। 7.67.25 ।।
transliteration: śūlasya ca balaṃ ghoramaprameyaṃ nararṣabha | vināśaścaiva māndhāturyattenābhūcca pārthiva || 7.67.25 ||
translation: शूलस्य of the trident, च and, बलं strength, घोरम् terrible, अप्रमेयं immeasurable, नरर्षभ O best among men, विनाशश्चैव and indeed the destruction, मान्धातुः of Mandhata, यत् which, तेन by him, अभूत् happened, च and, पार्थिव O king.
explanation: O best among men, the terrible and immeasurable strength of the trident, and the destruction of Mandhata which was caused by him, has also been recounted, O king.

shloka_text: त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन्वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे । शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र ।। 7.67.26 ।।
transliteration: tvaṃ śvaḥ prabhāte lavaṇaṃ mahātmanvadhiṣyase nātra tu saṃśayo me | śūlaṃ vinā nirgatamāmiṣārthe dhruvo jayaste bhavitā narendra || 7.67.26 ||
translation: त्वं you, श्वः tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, लवणं Lavana, महात्मन् O great-souled one, वधिष्यसे you will kill, न not, अत्र here, तु indeed, संशयः doubt, मे my, शूलं the trident, विना without, निर्गतम् having gone out, आमिषार्थे for the sake of meat, ध्रुवो certain, जयस्ते your victory, भविता will be, नरेन्द्र O king.
explanation: O great-souled one, you will kill Lavana tomorrow morning; there is no doubt in my mind about this, and your victory will be certain, O king, when he has gone out without his trident for the sake of food. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 67 ।। Thus ends the sixty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: कथां कथयतां तेषां जयं चाकाङ्क्षतां शुभम् । व्यतीता रजनी शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.68.1 ।।
transliteration: kathāṃ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ jayaṃ cākāṅkṣatāṃ śubham | vyatītā rajanī śīghraṃ śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.68.1 ||
translation: कथां the talk, कथयतां while speaking, तेषां of them, जयं victory, च and, आकाङ्क्षतां while desiring, शुभम् auspicious, व्यतीता passed, रजनी the night, शीघ्रं quickly, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः the great-souled one.
explanation: While they were conversing and wishing for an auspicious victory, the night quickly passed for the great-souled Shatrughna.
comments: At morning Lavana comes out for food, and Shatrughna, having crossed the Yamuna, stands armed at the gate -- the demon mocks and threatens to devour him, but Shatrughna, weeping with rage, names himself Rama's brother come for his death and demands single combat -- Lavana, boasting of his kinship to Ravana, bids him wait while he fetches a weapon, but Shatrughna refuses to let the seen foe escape.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभाते विमले तस्मिन्काले स राक्षसः । निर्गतस्तु पुराद्धीरो भक्ष्याहारप्रचोदितः ।। 7.68.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prabhāte vimale tasminkāle sa rākṣasaḥ | nirgatastu purāddhīro bhakṣyāhārapracoditaḥ || 7.68.2 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रभाते in the morning, विमले clear, तस्मिन्काले at that time, सः that, राक्षसः demon, निर्गतस्तु indeed came out, पुरात् from the city, धीरः brave, भक्ष्याहारप्रचोदितः impelled by the desire for food.
explanation: Then, in that clear morning, the brave demon, impelled by his hunger for food, came out of the city.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः शत्रुघ्नो यमुनां नदीम् । तीर्त्वा मधुपुरद्वारि धनुष्पाणिरतिष्ठत ।। 7.68.3 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare vīraḥ śatrughno yamunāṃ nadīm | tīrtvā madhupuradvāri dhanuṣpāṇiratiṣṭhata || 7.68.3 ||
translation: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे in the meantime, वीरः the brave, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, यमुनां Yamuna, नदीम् river, तीर्त्वा having crossed, मधुपुरद्वारि at the gate of Madhupura, धनुष्पाणिः with bow in hand, अतिष्ठत stood.
explanation: In the meantime, the brave Shatrughna, having crossed the Yamuna river, stood at the gate of Madhupura with his bow in hand.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते क्रूरकर्मा स राक्षसः । आगच्छद्बहुसाहस्रं प्राणिनां भारमुद्वहन् ।। 7.68.4 ।।
transliteration: tato 'rdhadivase prāpte krūrakarmā sa rākṣasaḥ | āgacchadbahusāhasraṃ prāṇināṃ bhāramudvahan || 7.68.4 ||
translation: ततः then, अर्धदिवसे midday, प्राप्ते having arrived, क्रूरकर्मा cruel-deeded, सः that, राक्षसः demon, आगच्छत् came, बहुसाहस्रं many thousands, प्राणिनां of living beings, भारम् burden, उद्वहन् carrying.
explanation: Then, as midday arrived, that cruel demon came, carrying the burden of many thousands of living beings.

shloka_text: ततो ददर्श शत्रुघ्नं स्थितं द्वारि धृतायुधम् । तमुवाच ततो रक्षः किमनेन करिष्यसि ।। 7.68.5 ।।
transliteration: tato dadarśa śatrughnaṃ sthitaṃ dvāri dhṛtāyudham | tamuvāca tato rakṣaḥ kimanena kariṣyasi || 7.68.5 ||
translation: ततः then, ददर्श he saw, शत्रुघ्नं Shatrughna, स्थितं standing, द्वारि at the gate, धृतायुधम् holding a weapon, तम् to him, उवाच said, ततः then, रक्षः the demon, किम् what, अनेन with this, करिष्यसि will you do.
explanation: Then he saw Shatrughna standing at the gate, holding a weapon, and the demon then asked him, "What will you do with this?"

shloka_text: ईदृशानां सहस्राणि सायुधानां नराधम । भक्षितानि मया रोषात्कालमाकाङ्क्षसे नु किम् ।। 7.68.6 ।।
transliteration: īdṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi sāyudhānāṃ narādhama | bhakṣitāni mayā roṣātkālamākāṅkṣase nu kim || 7.68.6 ||
translation: ईदृशानां of such (like you), सहस्राणि thousands, सायुधानां armed, नराधम O vilest of men, भक्षितानि have been devoured, मया by me, रोषात् out of anger, कालम् death, आकाङ्क्षसे do you desire, नु indeed, किम् what.
explanation: "O vilest of men, I have devoured thousands of armed individuals like you out of anger; do you indeed desire death?"

shloka_text: आहारश्चास्य सम्पूर्णो ममायं पुरुषाधम । स्वयं प्रविष्टो ऽद्य मुखं कथमासाद्य दुर्मते ।। 7.68.7 ।।
transliteration: āhāraścāsya sampūrṇo mamāyaṃ puruṣādhama | svayaṃ praviṣṭo 'dya mukhaṃ kathamāsādya durmate || 7.68.7 ||
translation: आहारश्च food and, अस्य his, सम्पूर्णो complete, ममायं my this, पुरुषाधम O vilest of men, स्वयम् by himself, प्रविष्टो entered, अद्य today, मुखं mouth, कथमासाद्य how having reached, दुर्मते O evil-minded one
explanation: The demon, addressing Shatrughna, exclaims that Shatrughna, the vilest and evil-minded of men, has today entered his mouth by himself, thus becoming his complete meal.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं भाषमाणस्य हसतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो रोषादश्रूण्यवासृजत् ।। 7.68.8 ।।
transliteration: tasyaivaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya hasataśca muhurmuhuḥ | śatrughno vīryasampanno roṣādaśrūṇyavāsṛjat || 7.68.8 ||
translation: तस्य his, एवम् thus, भाषमाणस्य while speaking, हसतश्च while laughing and, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, वीर्यसम्पन्नो endowed with valor, रोषात् from anger, अश्रूण्यवासृजत् shed tears
explanation: As the demon spoke thus and laughed repeatedly, the valiant Shatrughna shed tears out of intense anger.

shloka_text: तस्य रोषाभिभूतस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । तेजोमया मरीच्यस्तु सर्वगात्रैर्विनिष्पतन् ।। 7.68.9 ।।
transliteration: tasya roṣābhibhūtasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | tejomayā marīcyastu sarvagātrairviniṣpatan || 7.68.9 ||
translation: तस्य his, रोषाभिभूतस्य overcome by anger, शत्रुघ्नस्य Shatrughna's, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, तेजोमया radiant, मरीच्यस्तु rays indeed, सर्वगात्रैः from all limbs, विनिष्पतन् burst forth
explanation: From the great-souled Shatrughna, who was overcome by such rage, radiant rays of light emanated from all his limbs.

shloka_text: उवाच च सुसङ्क्रुद्धः शत्रुघ्नस्तं निशाचरम् । योद्धुमिच्छामि दुर्बुद्धे द्वन्द्वयुद्धं त्वया सह ।। 7.68.10 ।।
transliteration: uvāca ca susaṅkruddhaḥ śatrughnastaṃ niśācaram | yoddhumicchāmi durbuddhe dvandvayuddhaṃ tvayā saha || 7.68.10 ||
translation: उवाच spoke, च and, सुसङ्क्रुद्धः very much enraged, शत्रुघ्नस्तं Shatrughna to him, निशाचरम् to the night-wanderer, योद्धुमिच्छामि I wish to fight, दुर्बुद्धे O evil-minded one, द्वन्द्वयुद्धं single combat, त्वया with you, सह together
explanation: And Shatrughna, greatly enraged, spoke to that demon, declaring his wish to engage in single combat with the evil-minded one.

shloka_text: पुत्रो दशरथस्याहं भ्राता रामस्य धीमतः । शत्रुघ्नो नित्यशत्रुघ्नो वधाकाङ्क्षी तवागतः ।। 7.68.11 ।।
transliteration: putro daśarathasyāhaṃ bhrātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ | śatrughno nityaśatrughno vadhākāṅkṣī tavāgataḥ || 7.68.11 ||
translation: पुत्रो son, दशरथस्याहं of Dasharatha I, भ्राता brother, रामस्य of Rama, धीमतः the wise, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, नित्यशत्रुघ्नो the eternal slayer of enemies, वधाकाङ्क्षी desirous of killing, तवागतः your has come
explanation: I am Shatrughna, the son of Dasharatha and brother of the wise Rama, the eternal slayer of enemies, and I have come here desiring your death.

shloka_text: तस्य मे युद्धकामस्य द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदीयताम् । शत्रुस्त्वं सर्वभूतानां न मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि ।। 7.68.12 ।।
transliteration: tasya me yuddhakāmasya dvandvayuddhaṃ pradīyatām | śatrustvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ na me jīvangamiṣyasi || 7.68.12 ||
translation: तस्य मे for me, युद्धकामस्य desirous of battle, द्वन्द्वयुद्धं a single combat, प्रदीयताम् let it be given. शत्रुस्त्वं you are an enemy, सर्वभूतानां of all beings, न not, मे from me, जीवन् alive, गमिष्यसि you will go.
explanation: Grant me, who desires battle, a single combat, for you are an enemy to all beings, and you shall not escape me alive.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु राक्षसः प्रहसन्निव । प्रत्युवाच नरश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो ऽसि दुर्मते ।। 7.68.13 ।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstathā bruvāṇe tu rākṣasaḥ prahasanniva | pratyuvāca naraśreṣṭhaṃ diṣṭyā prāpto 'si durmate || 7.68.13 ||
translation: तस्मिंस्तथा when he thus, ब्रुवाणे was speaking, तु indeed, राक्षसः the demon, प्रहसन्निव as if laughing, प्रत्युवाच replied, नरश्रेष्ठं to the best of men, दिष्ट्या fortunately, प्राप्तो ऽसि you have arrived, दुर्मते O evil-minded one.
explanation: As he spoke thus, the demon, as if laughing, replied to the best of men, "Fortunately, O evil-minded one, you have arrived!"

shloka_text: मम मातृष्वसुर्भ्राता रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । हतो रामेण दुर्बुद्धे स्त्रीहेतोः पुरुषाधम ।। 7.68.14 ।।
transliteration: mama mātṛṣvasurbhrātā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ | hato rāmeṇa durbuddhe strīhetoḥ puruṣādhama || 7.68.14 ||
translation: मम my, मातृष्वसुर्भ्राता mother's sister's brother (maternal uncle), रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of demons, हतो was killed, रामेण by Rama, दुर्बुद्धे O foolish one, स्त्रीहेतोः for the sake of a woman, पुरुषाधम O lowest of men.
explanation: O foolish one, O lowest of men, my maternal uncle Ravana, the lord of demons, was killed by Rama for the sake of a woman.

shloka_text: तच्च सर्वं मया क्षान्तं रावणस्य कुलक्षयम् । अवज्ञां पुरतः कृत्वा मया यूयं विशेषतः ।। 7.68.15 ।।
transliteration: tacca sarvaṃ mayā kṣāntaṃ rāvaṇasya kulakṣayam | avajñāṃ purataḥ kṛtvā mayā yūyaṃ viśeṣataḥ || 7.68.15 ||
translation: तच्च and that, सर्वं all, मया by me, क्षान्तं was tolerated, रावणस्य Ravana's, कुलक्षयम् destruction of the lineage. अवज्ञां disrespect, पुरतः first, कृत्वा having made, मया by me, यूयं you all, विशेषतः especially.
explanation: I tolerated all that, the destruction of Ravana's lineage, but I have especially shown contempt towards you all from the very beginning.

shloka_text: निहताश्च हि मे सर्वे परिभूतास्तृणं यथा । भूताश्चैव भविष्याश्च यूयं च पुरुषाधमाः ।। 7.68.16 ।।
transliteration: nihatāśca hi me sarve paribhūtāstṛṇaṃ yathā | bhūtāścaiva bhaviṣyāśca yūyaṃ ca puruṣādhamāḥ || 7.68.16 ||
translation: निहताश्च and killed, हि indeed, मे by me, सर्वे all, परिभूतास्तृणं insulted like grass, यथा as. भूताश्चैव and those who were (past), भविष्याश्च and those who will be (future), यूयं you all, च and, पुरुषाधमाः O lowest of men.
explanation: Indeed, all of them, past, present, and future, including you, O lowest of men, have been killed and insulted by me as if they were mere grass.

shloka_text: तस्य ते युद्धकामस्य युद्धं दास्यामि दुर्मते । तिष्ठं त्वं च मुहूर्तं तु यावदायुधमानये । ईप्सितं यादृशं तुभ्यं सज्जये यावदायुधम् ।। 7.68.17 ।।
transliteration: tasya te yuddhakāmasya yuddhaṃ dāsyāmi durmate | tiṣṭhaṃ tvaṃ ca muhūrtaṃ tu yāvadāyudhamānaye | īpsitaṃ yādṛśaṃ tubhyaṃ sajjaye yāvadāyudham || 7.68.17 ||
translation: तस्य to that, ते your, युद्धकामस्य one desirous of battle, युद्धं battle, दास्यामि I will give, दुर्मते O evil-minded one, तिष्ठं stand, त्वं you, च and, मुहूर्तं for a moment, तु indeed, यावत् until, आयुधम् weapon, आनये I bring, ईप्सितं desired, यादृशं of what kind, तुभ्यं for you, सज्जये I prepare, यावत् until, आयुधम् weapon
explanation: O evil-minded one, I will give you the battle you desire; just wait for a moment until I bring and prepare the kind of weapon you wish for.

shloka_text: तमुवाचाशु शत्रुघ्नः क्व मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि । शत्रुर्यदृच्छया दृष्टो न मोक्तव्यः कृतात्मना ।। 7.68.18 ।।
transliteration: tamuvācāśu śatrughnaḥ kva me jīvangamiṣyasi | śatruryadṛcchayā dṛṣṭo na moktavyaḥ kṛtātmanā || 7.68.18 ||
translation: तम् to him, उवाच said, आशु quickly, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, क्व where, मे from me, जीवन् alive, गमिष्यसि will you go, शत्रुः an enemy, यदृच्छया by chance, दृष्टः seen, न not, मोक्तव्यः to be released, कृतात्मना by a resolute person
explanation: Shatrughna quickly said to him, "Where will you go alive from me? An enemy, once seen by chance, should not be released by a resolute person."

shloka_text: यो हि विक्लवया बुद्ध्या प्रसरं शत्रवे ददौ । स हतो मन्दबुद्धित्वाद्यथा कापुरुषस्तथा ।। 7.68.19 ।।
transliteration: yo hi viklavayā buddhyā prasaraṃ śatrave dadau | sa hato mandabuddhitvādyathā kāpuruṣastathā || 7.68.19 ||
translation: यः who, हि indeed, विक्लवया confused, बुद्ध्या with intellect, प्रसरं opportunity, शत्रवे to the enemy, ददौ gave, सः he, हतः is killed, मन्दबुद्धित्वात् due to dull-wittedness, यथा just as, कापुरुषः a coward, तथा so
explanation: Indeed, whoever gives an advantage to an enemy with a wavering mind is killed due to his dull-wittedness, just like a coward.

shloka_text: तस्मात्सुदृष्टं कुरु जीवलोकं शरैः शितैस्त्वां विविधैर्नयामि । यमस्य गेहाभिमुखं हि पापं रिपुं त्रिलोकस्य च राघवस्य ।। 7.68.20 ।।
transliteration: tasmātsudṛṣṭaṃ kuru jīvalokaṃ śaraiḥ śitaistvāṃ vividhairnayāmi | yamasya gehābhimukhaṃ hi pāpaṃ ripuṃ trilokasya ca rāghavasya || 7.68.20 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, सुदृष्टं well-seen, कुरु make, जीवलोकं the world of living beings, शरैः with arrows, शितैः sharp, त्वां you, विविधैः various, नयामि I will lead, यमस्य of Yama, गेहाभिमुखं towards the house, हि indeed, पापं sinful, रिपुं enemy, त्रिलोकस्य of the three worlds, च and, राघवस्य of Rama
explanation: Therefore, take a good look at the world of the living, for I shall lead you, a sinful enemy of the three worlds and of Rama, towards Yama's abode with various sharp arrows. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 68 ।। Thus ends the sixty-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । क्रोधामाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.1 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | krodhāmāhārayattīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt || 7.69.1 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, भाषितं speech, तस्य his, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः the great-souled, क्रोधं anger, आहारयत् he felt, तीव्रं intense, तिष्ठ stop, तिष्ठ stop, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् he said
explanation: Having heard that speech of the great-souled Shatrughna, he felt intense anger and exclaimed, "Stop! Stop!"
comments: The battle resumes -- Lavana hurls trees and fells Shatrughna senseless, but, thinking him dead, fails to fetch his trident -- recovering, Shatrughna takes up the divine arrow, whose blazing splendour terrifies all beings until Brahma reveals it to be Vishnu's own form -- Shatrughna looses it into Lavana's chest and slays him, the trident returns to Rudra, and the gods rejoice at the death of the world's terror.

shloka_text: पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च । लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत् ।। 7.69.2 ।।
transliteration: pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantānkaṭakaṭāyya ca | lavaṇo raghuśārdūlamāhvayāmāsa cāsakṛt || 7.69.2 ||
translation: पाणौ in hand, पाणिं hand, विनिष्पिष्य having pressed, दन्तान् teeth, कटकटाय्य having gnashed, च and, लवणो Lavaṇa, रघुशार्दूलम् the tiger among Raghus (Shatrughna), आह्वयामास challenged, च and, असकृत् repeatedly.
explanation: Lavaṇa, pressing his hands together and gnashing his teeth, repeatedly challenged Shatrughna, the foremost of the Raghu dynasty.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम् । शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.3 ।।
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoradarśanam | śatrughno devaśatrughna idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.69.3 ||
translation: तं him, ब्रुवाणं speaking, तथा such, वाक्यं words, लवणं Lavaṇa, घोरदर्शनम् of terrible appearance, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, देवशत्रुघ्न the destroyer of the gods' enemy, इदं this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: To Lavaṇa, who was speaking such words and had a terrible appearance, Shatrughna, the destroyer of the gods' enemy, spoke these words.

shloka_text: न शत्रुघ्नस्तथा जातो यथा ऽन्ये निर्जितास्त्वया । तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम् ।। 7.69.4 ।।
transliteration: na śatrughnastathā jāto yathā 'nye nirjitāstvayā | tadadya bāṇābhihato vraja tvaṃ yamasādanam || 7.69.4 ||
translation: न not, शत्रुघ्नस्तथा Shatrughna is such, जातो born, यथा as, अन्ये others, निर्जितास्त्वया conquered by you, तदद्य therefore today, बाणाभिहतो struck by arrows, व्रज go, त्वं you, यमसादनम् to the abode of Yama.
explanation: Shatrughna declared that he was not like the others Lavaṇa had conquered, and therefore, Lavaṇa would today be struck by his arrows and go to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: ऋषयो ऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे । पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम् ।। 7.69.5 ।।
transliteration: ṛṣayo 'pyadya pāpātmanmayā tvāṃ nihataṃ raṇe | paśyantu viprā vidvāṃsastridaśā iva rāvaṇam || 7.69.5 ||
translation: ऋषयो sages, अप्यद्य also today, पापात्मन् O evil-souled one, मया by me, त्वां you, निहतं slain, रणे in battle, पश्यन्तु let them see, विप्रा Brahmins, विद्वांसः learned ones, त्रिदशाः gods, इव like, रावणम् Ravana.
explanation: Shatrughna wished that the sages, Brahmins, and learned ones, like the gods witnessing Ravana's fall, would today see him slay the evil-souled Lavaṇa in battle.

shloka_text: त्वयि मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे पतिते ऽद्य निशाचर । पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति ।। 7.69.6 ।।
transliteration: tvayi madbāṇanirdagdhe patite 'dya niśācara | pure janapade cāpi kṣemameva bhaviṣyati || 7.69.6 ||
translation: त्वयि you, मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे burnt by my arrows, पतिते fallen, अद्य today, निशाचर O night-wanderer, पुरे in the city, जनपदे in the country, च and, अपि also, क्षेममेव welfare indeed, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Shatrughna declared that with Lavaṇa, the night-wanderer, burnt by his arrows and fallen today, there would indeed be welfare in both the city and the country.

shloka_text: अद्य मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः । प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः ।। 7.69.7 ।।
transliteration: adya madbāhuniṣkrāntaḥ śaro vajranibhānanaḥ | pravekṣyate te hṛdayaṃ padmamaṃśurivārkajaḥ || 7.69.7 ||
translation: अद्य today, मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः issued from my arm, शरः arrow, वज्रनिभाननः having a thunderbolt-like tip, प्रवेक्ष्यते will enter, ते your, हृदयम् heart, पद्मम् a lotus, अंशुः a ray, इव like, अर्कजः of the sun,
explanation: Today, the arrow released from my arm, with its thunderbolt-like tip, will pierce your heart just as a sunbeam penetrates a lotus.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत् ।। 7.69.8 ।।
transliteration: evamukto mahāvṛkṣaṃ lavaṇaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ | śatrughnorasi cikṣepa sa ca taṃ śatadhācchinat || 7.69.8 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः addressed, महावृक्षम् a great tree, लवणः Lavana, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with anger, शत्रुघ्नोरसि on Shatrughna's chest, चिक्षेप threw, सः he, च and, तम् that, शतधा into a hundred pieces, अच्छिनत् cut,
explanation: Thus addressed, Lavana, overcome with rage, hurled a massive tree at Shatrughna's chest, but Shatrughna instantly shattered it into a hundred pieces.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु । पादपान्सुबहून्गृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद्बली ।। 7.69.9 ।।
transliteration: taddṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punareva tu | pādapānsubahūngṛhya śatrughnāyāsṛjadbalī || 7.69.9 ||
translation: तत् that, दृष्ट्वा having seen, विफलम् fruitless, कर्म action, राक्षसः the demon, पुनरेव again indeed, तु and, पादपान् trees, सुबहून् very many, गृह्य seizing, शत्रुघ्नाय at Shatrughna, असृजत् hurled, बली the powerful one,
explanation: Seeing that action prove fruitless, the powerful demon Lavana again seized very many trees and hurled them at Shatrughna.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून् । त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः ।। 7.69.10 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnaścāpi tejasvī vṛkṣānāpatato bahūn | tribhiścaturbhirekaikaṃ ciccheda nataparvabhiḥ || 7.69.10 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, च and, अपि also, तेजस्वी powerful, वृक्षान् trees, आपततः falling, बहून् many, त्रिभिः with three, चतुर्भिः with four, एकैकम् each one, चिच्छेद cut, नतपर्वभिः with bent-jointed arrows,
explanation: And the powerful Shatrughna, with his bent-shafted arrows, cut down each of the many approaching trees with three or four arrows.

shloka_text: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद्राक्षसोरसि । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः ।। 7.69.11 ।।
transliteration: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vyasṛjadrākṣasorasi | śatrughno vīryasampanno vivyathe na sa rākṣasaḥ || 7.69.11 ||
translation: ततः then, बाणमयम् a shower of arrows, वर्षम् rain, व्यसृजत् discharged, राक्षसोरसि on the demon's chest, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, विव्यथे was pained, न not, सः that, राक्षसः demon,
explanation: Then, the valorous Shatrughna unleashed a shower of arrows upon the demon's chest, but that demon was not pained by them.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान् । शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै ।। 7.69.12 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇo vṛkṣamudyamya vīryavān | śirasyabhyahanacchūraṃ srastāṅgaḥ sa mumoha vai || 7.69.12 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रहस्य having laughed, लवणो Lavana, वृक्षम् a tree, उद्यम्य having lifted, वीर्यवान् the mighty one, शिरसि on the head, अभ्यहनत् struck, शूरम् the brave one, स्रस्ताङ्गः with limbs loosened, सः he, मुमोह fainted, वै indeed.
explanation: Then, the mighty Lavana laughed, lifted a tree, and struck the brave Shatrughna on the head, causing him to faint with his limbs loosened.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणां देवसङ्घानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा ।। 7.69.13 ।।
transliteration: tasminnipatite vīre hāhākāro mahānabhūt | ṛṣīṇāṃ devasaṅghānāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā || 7.69.13 ||
translation: तस्मिन् when that, निपतिते fell down, वीरे brave one, हाहाकारो a cry of distress, महान् great, अभूत् arose, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, देवसङ्घानाम् of the hosts of gods, गन्धर्वाप्सरसां of Gandharvas and Apsaras, तथा and also.
explanation: When that brave warrior fell, a great cry of distress arose from the sages, hosts of gods, Gandharvas, and Apsaras.

shloka_text: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम् । रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम् ।। 7.69.14 ।।
transliteration: tamavajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam | rakṣo labdhāntaramapi na viveśa svamālayam || 7.69.14 ||
translation: तम् him, अवज्ञाय disregarding, तु but, हतम् killed, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, भुवि on the ground, पातितम् fallen, रक्षो the demon, लब्धान्तरमपि even though having found an opportunity, न not, विवेश entered, स्वमालयम् his own abode.
explanation: Disregarding Shatrughna, who had fallen to the ground as if killed, the demon, even though he had found an opportunity, did not enter his own abode.

shloka_text: नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम् । ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान्भक्षान्समुदावहत् ।। 7.69.15 ।।
transliteration: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam | tato hata iti jñātvā tānbhakṣānsamudāvahat || 7.69.15 ||
translation: न not, अपि even, शूलम् the trident, प्रजग्राह took up, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, भुवि on the ground, पातितम् fallen, ततः then, हतः killed, इति thus, ज्ञात्वा having known, तान् those, भक्षान् food items, समुदावहत् carried away.
explanation: Even after seeing Shatrughna fallen on the ground, Lavana did not pick up his trident; instead, thinking him dead, he carried away his prey.

shloka_text: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः । शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः सम्प्रपूजितः ।। 7.69.16 ।।
transliteration: muhūrtāllabdhasañjñastu punastasthau dhṛtāyudhaḥ | śatrughno vai puradvāri ṛṣibhiḥ samprapūjitaḥ || 7.69.16 ||
translation: मुहूर्तात् in a moment, लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु having regained consciousness, पुनः again, तस्थौ stood, धृतायुधः holding his weapon, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, वै indeed, पुरद्वारि at the city gate, ऋषिभिः by the sages, सम्प्रपूजितः well-worshipped.
explanation: In a moment, Shatrughna regained consciousness, and, holding his weapon, he stood again at the city gate, honored by the sages.

shloka_text: ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम् । ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश ।। 7.69.17 ।।
transliteration: tato divyamamoghaṃ taṃ jagrāha śaramuttamam | jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa || 7.69.17 ||
translation: ततः then, दिव्यम् divine, अमोघम् unfailing, तम् that, जग्राह he took, शरम् arrow, उत्तमम् excellent, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, तेजसा with splendor, घोरम् dreadful, पूरयन्तम् filling, दिशः directions, दश ten.
explanation: Then he took that excellent, divine, and unfailing arrow, which was blazing with dreadful splendor and filling all ten directions.

shloka_text: वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् । नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम् ।। 7.69.18 ।।
transliteration: vajrānanaṃ vajravegaṃ merumandarasannibham | nataṃ parvasu sarveṣu saṃyugeṣvaparājitam || 7.69.18 ||
translation: वज्राननम् having a tip like a thunderbolt, वज्रवेगम् having the speed of a thunderbolt, मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् resembling Mount Meru and Mandara, नतम् bent, पर्वसु at the joints, सर्वेषु all, संयुगेषु in battles, अपराजितम् unconquered.
explanation: The arrow had a thunderbolt-like tip and speed, resembled Mount Meru and Mandara, was perfectly bent at all its joints, and remained unconquered in all battles.

shloka_text: असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्रिणम् । दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारणम् ।। 7.69.19 ।।
transliteration: asṛkcandanadigdhāṅgaṃ cārupatraṃ patatriṇam | dānavendrācalendrāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca dāraṇam || 7.69.19 ||
translation: असृक् blood, चन्दन sandalwood, दिग्धाङ्गम् smeared on its body, चारुपत्रम् having beautiful feathers, पतत्रिणम् winged, दानवेन्द्र of the lords of Danavas, अचलेन्द्राणाम् of the lords of mountains, असुराणाम् of Asuras, च and, दारणम् a splitter.
explanation: Its body was smeared with blood and sandalwood, it had beautiful feathers, and it was capable of splitting the lords of Danavas, the lords of mountains, and the Asuras.

shloka_text: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते । दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन् ।। 7.69.20 ।।
transliteration: taṃ dīptamiva kālāgniṃ yugānte samupasthite | dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni paritrāsamupāgaman || 7.69.20 ||
translation: तम् that, दीप्तम् blazing, इव like, कालाग्निम् the fire of destruction, युगान्ते at the end of an age, समुपस्थिते having arrived, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सर्वाणि all, भूतानि beings, परित्रासम् great fear, उपागमन् they experienced.
explanation: Seeing that arrow blazing like the fire of destruction at the end of a cosmic age, all beings were struck with great terror.

shloka_text: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम् । जगद्धि सर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.69.21 ।।
transliteration: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ munibhiḥ sāpsarogaṇam | jagaddhi sarvamasvasthaṃ pitāmahamupasthitam || 7.69.21 ||
translation: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वम् with gods, asuras, and gandharvas, मुनिभिः with sages, साप्सरोगणम् with groups of Apsaras, जगत् the world, हि indeed, सर्वम् all, अस्वस्थम् uneasy, पितामहम् to Brahma, उपस्थितम् approached.
explanation: Indeed, the entire world, including gods, asuras, gandharvas, sages, and groups of Apsaras, became uneasy and approached Brahma.

shloka_text: उवाच देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम् । देवानां भयसंमोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.22 ।।
transliteration: uvāca devadeveśaṃ varadaṃ prapitāmaham | devānāṃ bhayasaṃmoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.22 ||
translation: उवाच said, देवदेवेशं to the lord of gods, वरदं the bestower of boons, प्रपितामहम् to the great-grandfather, देवानां of the gods, भयसंमोहो fear and bewilderment, लोकानां of the worlds, सङ्क्षयं destruction, प्रति regarding.
explanation: The gods addressed Brahma, the great-grandfather and bestower of boons, regarding the fear and bewilderment among the gods and the impending destruction of the worlds.

shloka_text: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह । देवानां भयसम्मोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.23 ।।
transliteration: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ ca na śrutaṃ prapitāmaha | devānāṃ bhayasammoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.23 ||
translation: न not, ईदृशं such, दृष्टपूर्वं seen before, च and, न not, श्रुतं heard, प्रपितामह O great-grandfather, देवानां of the gods, भयसम्मोहो fear and bewilderment, लोकानां of the worlds, सङ्क्षयं destruction, प्रति regarding.
explanation: They declared to Brahma that such fear and bewilderment among the gods, concerning the destruction of the worlds, had never been seen or heard of before.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः । भयकारणमाचष्ट लोकानामभयङ्करः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.69.24 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ | bhayakāraṇamācaṣṭa lokānāmabhayaṅkaraḥ | uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ sarvadevatāḥ || 7.69.24 ||
translation: तेषां their, तत् that, वचनं speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, ब्रह्मा Brahma, लोकपितामहः the great-grandfather of the worlds, भयकारणम् the cause of fear, आचष्ट explained, लोकानाम् of the worlds, अभयङ्करः the dispeller of fear, उवाच said, मधुरां sweet, वाणीं words, शृणुध्वं listen, सर्वदेवताः O all gods.
explanation: Having heard their words, Brahma, the great-grandfather and dispeller of fear for the worlds, explained the cause of their fear and spoke sweet words, asking all the gods to listen.

shloka_text: वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नधारितः । तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.69.25 ।।
transliteration: vadhāya lavaṇasyājau śaraḥ śatrughnadhāritaḥ | tejasā tasya sammūḍhāḥ sarve smaḥ surasattamāḥ || 7.69.25 ||
translation: वधाय for the killing, लवणस्य of Lavana, आजौ in battle, शरः the arrow, शत्रुघ्नधारितः held by Shatrughna, तेजसा by the radiance, तस्य of that, सम्मूढाः bewildered, सर्वे all, स्मः we are, सुरसत्तमाः O best of gods.
explanation: Brahma revealed that the gods' bewilderment was caused by the immense radiance of the arrow held by Shatrughna, intended for the killing of Lavana in battle.

shloka_text: एष पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः । शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम् ।। 7.69.26 ।।
transliteration: eṣa pūrvasya devasya lokakartuḥ sanātanaḥ | śarastejomayo vatsā yena vai bhayamāgatam || 7.69.26 ||
translation: एष this, पूर्वस्य of the ancient, देवस्य god, लोककर्तुः the creator of the worlds, सनातनः eternal, शरः arrow, तेजोमयः full of light, वत्सा O dear ones, येन by which, वै indeed, भयम् fear, आगतम् has come.
explanation: Brahma further explained that this radiant arrow, which caused their fear, is the eternal weapon of the ancient god, the creator of the worlds.

shloka_text: एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः । सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः ।। 7.69.27 ।।
transliteration: eṣa vai kaiṭabhasyārthe madhunaśca mahāśaraḥ | sṛṣṭo mahātmanā tena vadhārthe daityayostayoḥ || 7.69.27 ||
translation: एषः this, वै indeed, कैटभस्य of Kaitabha, अर्थे for the sake of, मधुनः of Madhu, च and, महाशरः great arrow, सृष्टः created, महात्मना by the great-souled one, तेन by him, वधार्थे for the purpose of killing, दैत्ययोः of the two demons, तयोः those two,
explanation: This great arrow was indeed created by that great-souled one for the purpose of killing those two demons, Kaitabha and Madhu.

shloka_text: एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम् । एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.69.28 ।।
transliteration: eka eva prajānāti viṣṇustejomayaṃ śaram | eṣā eva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇostasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.69.28 ||
translation: एकः only one, एव indeed, प्रजानाति knows, विष्णुः Vishnu, तेजोमयम् full of splendor, शरम् arrow, एषा this, एव indeed, तनुः body, पूर्वा ancient, विष्णोः of Vishnu, तस्य of that, महात्मनः great-souled one,
explanation: Only Vishnu truly knows this arrow, which is full of splendor, for this is indeed the ancient form of that great-souled Vishnu himself.

shloka_text: इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना । रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम् ।। 7.69.29 ।।
transliteration: ito gacchata paśyadhvaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā | rāmānujena vīreṇa lavaṇaṃ rākṣasottamam || 7.69.29 ||
translation: इतः from here, गच्छत go, पश्यध्वम् see, वध्यमानम् being killed, महात्मना by the great-souled one, रामानुजेन by Rama's younger brother, वीरेण by the hero, लवणम् Lavana, राक्षसोत्तमम् the chief of Rakshasas,
explanation: Go from here and witness Lavana, the chief of Rakshasas, being killed by the great-souled hero, Rama's younger brother.

shloka_text: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः । आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ ।। 7.69.30 ।।
transliteration: tasya te devadevasya niśamya vacanaṃ surāḥ | ājagmuryatra yudhyete śatrughnalavaṇāvubhau || 7.69.30 ||
translation: तस्य his, ते that, देवदेवस्य of the God of gods, निशम्य having heard, वचनम् words, सुराः the gods, आजग्मुः came, यत्र where, युध्येते were fighting, शत्रुघ्नलवणौ Shatrughna and Lavana, उभौ both,
explanation: Having heard the words of that God of gods, the deities arrived at the place where both Shatrughna and Lavana were engaged in battle.

shloka_text: तं शरं दिव्यसङ्काशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम् ।। 7.69.31 ।।
transliteration: taṃ śaraṃ divyasaṅkāśaṃ śatrughnakaradhāritam | dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni yugāntāgnimivotthitam || 7.69.31 ||
translation: तम् that, शरम् arrow, दिव्यसङ्काशम् divine-looking, शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् held in Shatrughna's hand, ददृशुः saw, सर्वभूतानि all beings, युगान्ताग्निम् the fire of the end of an age, इव like, उत्थितम् risen,
explanation: All beings saw that divine-looking arrow, held in Shatrughna's hand, shining like the risen fire of the cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: अकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः । सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लक्षणं पुनः ।। 7.69.32 ।।
transliteration: akāśamāvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devairhi raghunandanaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā dadarśa lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ || 7.69.32 ||
translation: अकाशम् the sky, आवृतम् covered, दृष्ट्वा having seen, देवैः by gods, हि indeed, रघुनन्दनः Shatrughna, सिंहनादम् a lion's roar, भृशम् loudly, कृत्वा having made, ददर्श he saw, लक्षणम् Lakshmana, पुनः again.
explanation: Indeed, having seen the sky covered by gods, Shatrughna, after letting out a loud lion's roar, saw Lakshmana again.

shloka_text: आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः ।। 7.69.33 ।।
transliteration: āhūtaśca punastena śatrughnena mahātmanā | lavaṇaḥ krodhasaṃyukto yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ || 7.69.33 ||
translation: आहूतः called, च and, पुनः again, तेन by him, शत्रुघ्नेन by Shatrughna, महात्मना the great-souled, लवणः Lavana, क्रोधसंयुक्तः filled with anger, युद्धाय for battle, समुपस्थितः stood ready.
explanation: And again, challenged by the great-souled Shatrughna, Lavana, filled with anger, appeared ready for battle.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ तद्धनुर्धन्विनां वरः । तं मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.69.34 ।।
transliteration: ākarṇātsa vikṛṣyātha taddhanurdhanvināṃ varaḥ | taṃ mumoca mahābāṇaṃ lavaṇasya mahorasi || 7.69.34 ||
translation: आकर्णात् up to the ear, सः he, विकृष्य having drawn, अथ then, तत् that, धनुः bow, धन्विनाम् among archers, वरः the best, तम् that, मुमोच he released, महाबाणम् great arrow, लवणस्य of Lavana, महोरसि on the great chest.
explanation: Then, the best among archers, Shatrughna, having drawn that bow up to his ear, released that great arrow onto Lavana's broad chest.

shloka_text: उरस्तस्य विदार्याशु प्रविवेश रसातलम् ।। 7.69.35 ।।
transliteration: urastasya vidāryāśu praviveśa rasātalam || 7.69.35 ||
translation: उरः the chest, तस्य his, विदार्य having pierced, आशु quickly, प्रविवेश it entered, रसातलम् the netherworld.
explanation: Quickly piercing his chest, the arrow entered the netherworld.

shloka_text: गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः । पुनरेवागमत्तूर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् ।। 7.69.36 ।।
transliteration: gatvā rasātalaṃ divyaḥ śaro vibudhapūjitaḥ | punarevāgamattūrṇamikṣvākukulanandanam || 7.69.36 ||
translation: गत्वा having gone, रसातलम् to the netherworld, दिव्यः divine, शरः arrow, विबुधपूजितः worshipped by gods, पुनरेव again indeed, आगमत् it came, तूर्णम् quickly, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् to the delight of the Ikshvaku family.
explanation: Having gone to the netherworld, the divine arrow, worshipped by gods, quickly returned to Shatrughna, the delight of the Ikshvaku family.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः । पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः ।। 7.69.37 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnaśaranirbhinno lavaṇaḥ sa niśācaraḥ | papāta sahasā bhūmau vajrāhata ivācalaḥ || 7.69.37 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो pierced by Shatrughna's arrow, लवणः Lavana, सः that, निशाचरः demon, पपात fell, सहसा suddenly, भूमौ on the ground, वज्राहतः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like, अचलः a mountain.
explanation: That demon Lavana, pierced by Shatrughna's arrow, suddenly fell to the ground like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तच्च शूलं महत्तेन हते लवणराक्षसे । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात् ।। 7.69.38 ।।
transliteration: tacca śūlaṃ mahattena hate lavaṇarākṣase | paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ rudrasya vaśamanvagāt || 7.69.38 ||
translation: तत् that, च and, शूलम् trident, महत् great, तेन by him, हते having been killed, लवणराक्षसे Lavana the demon, पश्यताम् while watching, सर्वदेवानाम् of all the gods, रुद्रस्य of Rudra, वशम् to the control, अन्वगात् returned.
explanation: And that great trident, after the demon Lavana was killed by Shatrughna, returned to the control of Rudra while all the gods watched.

shloka_text: एकेषुपातेन भृशं निपात्य लोकत्रयस्यापि रघुप्रवीरः । विनिर्बभावुत्तमचापबाणस्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः ।। 7.69.39 ।।
transliteration: ekeṣupātena bhṛśaṃ nipātya lokatrayasyāpi raghupravīraḥ | vinirbabhāvuttamacāpabāṇastamaḥ praṇudyeva sahasraraśmiḥ || 7.69.39 ||
translation: एकेषुपातेन by the shot of a single arrow, भृशम् completely, निपात्य having struck down, लोकत्रयस्य of the three worlds, अपि even, रघुप्रवीरः the great hero of the Raghu dynasty, विनिर्बभौ shone forth, उत्तमचापबाणः with an excellent bow and arrow, तमः darkness, प्रणुद्य having dispelled, इव like, सहस्ररश्मिः the sun.
explanation: Having completely struck down the terror of the three worlds with a single arrow, the great hero of the Raghu dynasty, Shatrughna, shone forth with his excellent bow and arrow, just like the sun dispelling darkness.

shloka_text: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः । दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्तस्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः ।। 7.69.40 ।।
transliteration: tato hi devā ṛṣipannagāśca prapūjire hyapsarasaśca sarvāḥ | diṣṭyā jayo dāśaratheravāptastyaktvā bhayaṃ sarpa iva praśāntaḥ || 7.69.40 ||
translation: ततः then, हि indeed, देवाः gods, ऋषि sages, पन्नगाः serpents, च and, प्रपूजिरे worshipped, हि indeed, अप्सरसः Apsaras, च and, सर्वाः all, दिष्ट्या fortunately, जयः victory, दाशरथेः of Dasharatha's son, अवाप्तः obtained, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, भयम् fear, सर्पः a serpent, इव like, प्रशान्तः calmed.
explanation: Then indeed, all the gods, sages, serpents, and Apsaras worshipped him, exclaiming that fortunately, victory had been obtained by Dasharatha's son, and they were now calm, having abandoned fear, like a pacified serpent. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 69 ।। Thus ends the sixty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: हते तु लवणे देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः । ऊचुः सुमधुरां वाणीं शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम् ।। 7.70.1 ।।
transliteration: hate tu lavaṇe devāḥ sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ | ūcuḥ sumadhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śatrughnaṃ śatrutāpanam || 7.70.1 ||
translation: हते having been killed, तु indeed, लवणे Lavana, देवाः the gods, सेन्द्राः with Indra, साग्निपुरोगमाः with Agni at their forefront, ऊचुः spoke, सुमधुराम् very sweet, वाणीम् words, शत्रुघ्नम् to Shatrughna, शत्रुतापनम् the tormentor of enemies.
explanation: Indeed, after Lavana was killed, the gods, led by Indra and with Agni at their forefront, spoke very sweet words to Shatrughna, the tormentor of enemies.
comments: The gods offer Shatrughna a boon, and he asks that Madhu's realm become a populous city -- granting it, they depart, and Shatrughna founds the prosperous city of Mathura in Shurasena, adorning it over the years -- his purpose accomplished, he resolves to go and behold Rama when the twelfth year arrives.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या ते विजयो वत्स दिष्ट्या लवणराक्षसः । हतः पुरुषशार्दूल वरं वरय सुव्रत ।। 7.70.2 ।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā te vijayo vatsa diṣṭyā lavaṇarākṣasaḥ | hataḥ puruṣaśārdūla varaṃ varaya suvrata || 7.70.2 ||
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately, ते your, विजयो victory, वत्स O dear one, दिष्ट्या fortunately, लवणराक्षसः the demon Lavana, हतः is killed, पुरुषशार्दूल O tiger among men, वरं a boon, वरय ask for, सुव्रत O virtuous one.
explanation: O dear and virtuous tiger among men, it is by good fortune that you have achieved victory and the demon Lavana has been killed; now, ask for a boon.

shloka_text: वरदास्तु महाबाहो सर्व एव समागताः । विजयाकाङ्क्षिणस्तुभ्यममोघं दर्शनं हि नः ।। 7.70.3 ।।
transliteration: varadāstu mahābāho sarva eva samāgatāḥ | vijayākāṅkṣiṇastubhyamamoghaṃ darśanaṃ hi naḥ || 7.70.3 ||
translation: वरदास्तु indeed givers of boons, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, सर्व all, एव indeed, समागताः have assembled, विजयाकाङ्क्षिणस्तुभ्यम् desiring victory for you, अमोघं fruitful, दर्शनं sight, हि indeed, नः our.
explanation: O mighty-armed one, all of us who have assembled here are indeed givers of boons, having desired your victory, and our presence here is certainly not in vain.

shloka_text: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा शूरो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुः शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान् ।। 7.70.4 ।।
transliteration: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā śūro mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ | pratyuvāca mahābāhuḥ śatrughnaḥ prayatātmavān || 7.70.4 ||
translation: देवानां of the gods, भाषितं speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, शूरो the brave one, मूर्ध्नि on his head, कृताञ्जलिः having made an anjali, प्रत्युवाच replied, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, प्रयतात्मवान् the self-controlled one.
explanation: Having heard the words of the gods, the brave, mighty-armed, and self-controlled Shatrughna, with folded hands placed on his head, replied.

shloka_text: इयं मधुपुरी रस्या मधुरा देवनिर्मिता । निवेशं प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रमेष मे ऽस्तु वरः परः ।। 7.70.5 ।।
transliteration: iyaṃ madhupurī rasyā madhurā devanirmitā | niveśaṃ prāpnuyācchīghrameṣa me 'stu varaḥ paraḥ || 7.70.5 ||
translation: इयं this, मधुपुरी the city of Madhu, रस्या delightful, मधुरा sweet, देवनिर्मिता created by gods, निवेशं a settlement, प्राप्नुयात् may obtain, शीघ्रम् quickly, एष this, मे my, अस्तु may be, वरः boon, परः supreme.
explanation: Shatrughna requested that this delightful and sweet city of Madhu, which was created by the gods, quickly become a populated settlement, declaring this to be his foremost boon.

shloka_text: तं देवाः प्रीतमनसो बाढमित्येव राघवम् । भविष्यति पुरी रम्या शूरसेना न संशयः ।। 7.70.6 ।।
transliteration: taṃ devāḥ prītamanaso bāḍhamityeva rāghavam | bhaviṣyati purī ramyā śūrasenā na saṃśayaḥ || 7.70.6 ||
translation: तं to him, देवाः the gods, प्रीतमनसो with pleased minds, बाढम् So be it, इति thus, एव indeed, राघवम् to the descendant of Raghu, भविष्यति will be, पुरी city, रम्या beautiful, शूरसेना Shurasena, न no, संशयः doubt.
explanation: With pleased minds, the gods replied to Shatrughna, the descendant of Raghu, saying "So be it," and assured him that the city would indeed become a beautiful one in the region of Shurasena, without a doubt.

shloka_text: ते तथोक्त्वा महात्मानो दिवमारुरुहुस्तदा । शत्रुघ्नो ऽपि महातेजास्तां सेनां समुपानयत् ।। 7.70.7 ।।
transliteration: te tathoktvā mahātmāno divamāruruhustadā | śatrughno 'pi mahātejāstāṃ senāṃ samupānayat || 7.70.7 ||
translation: ते they, तथा thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, महात्मानो the great souls, दिवम् to the sky/heaven, आरुरुहुः ascended, तदा then, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, अपि also, महातेजाः highly effulgent/very powerful, तां that, सेनां army, समुपानयत् brought together/led
explanation: After the great sages spoke, they ascended to the heavens, and then the powerful Shatrughna gathered that army.

shloka_text: सा सेना शीघ्रमागच्छच्छ्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नशासनम् । निवेशनं च शत्रुघ्नः श्रावणेन समारभत् ।। 7.70.8 ।।
transliteration: sā senā śīghramāgacchacchrutvā śatrughnaśāsanam | niveśanaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ śrāvaṇena samārabhat || 7.70.8 ||
translation: सा that, सेना army, शीघ्रम् quickly, आगच्छत् came, श्रुत्वा having heard, शत्रुघ्नशासनम् Shatrughna's command, निवेशनं the establishment/settlement (of the city), च and, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, श्रावणेन in the month of Shravana, समारभत् began
explanation: That army quickly arrived upon hearing Shatrughna's command, and Shatrughna began the establishment of the city in the month of Shravana.

shloka_text: सा पुरा दिव्यसङ्काशा वर्षे द्वादशमे शुभे । निविष्टा शूरसेनानां विषयश्चाकुतोभयः ।। 7.70.9 ।।
transliteration: sā purā divyasaṅkāśā varṣe dvādaśame śubhe | niviṣṭā śūrasenānāṃ viṣayaścākutobhayaḥ || 7.70.9 ||
translation: सा that (city), पुरा city, दिव्यसङ्काशा resembling a divine city, वर्षे in the year, द्वादशमे twelfth, शुभे auspicious, निविष्टा established/settled, शूरसेनानां of the brave warriors (or the region of Shurasena), विषयः region/country, च and, अकुतोभयः free from all fear
explanation: That city, resembling a divine abode, was established in the auspicious twelfth year, becoming a region for brave warriors, free from all fear.

shloka_text: क्षेत्राणि सस्ययुक्तानि काले वर्षति वासवः । अरोगवीरपुरुषा शत्रुघ्नभुजपालिता ।। 7.70.10 ।।
transliteration: kṣetrāṇi sasyayuktāni kāle varṣati vāsavaḥ | arogavīrapuruṣā śatrughnabhujapālitā || 7.70.10 ||
translation: क्षेत्राणि fields, सस्ययुक्तानि full of crops, काले at the proper time, वर्षति rains, वासवः Indra (the rain god), अरोगवीरपुरुषा having healthy and brave men, शत्रुघ्नभुजपालिता protected by Shatrughna's arm
explanation: The fields were full of crops, Indra rained at the proper time, and the region, protected by Shatrughna's arm, had healthy and brave men.

shloka_text: अर्धचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा यमुनातीरशोभिता । शोभिता गृहमुख्यैश्च चत्वरापणवीथिकैः । चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्ता नानावाणिज्यशोभिता ।। 7.70.11 ।।
transliteration: ardhacandrapratīkāśā yamunātīraśobhitā | śobhitā gṛhamukhyaiśca catvarāpaṇavīthikaiḥ | cāturvarṇyasamāyuktā nānāvāṇijyaśobhitā || 7.70.11 ||
translation: अर्धचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा resembling a half-moon, यमुनातीरशोभिता adorned by the banks of Yamuna, शोभिता adorned, गृहमुख्यैः by prominent houses, च and, चत्वरापणवीथिकैः by squares, shops, and streets, चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्ता endowed with the four varnas (social classes), नानावाणिज्यशोभिता adorned with various trades/commerce
explanation: The city, resembling a half-moon and beautified by the Yamuna's banks, was adorned with grand houses, squares, shops, and streets, inhabited by people of all four varnas, and bustling with diverse commerce.

shloka_text: यच्च तेन पुरा शुभ्रं लवणेन कृतं महत् । तच्छोभयति शत्रुघ्नो नानावर्णोपशोभिताम् ।। 7.70.12 ।।
transliteration: yacca tena purā śubhraṃ lavaṇena kṛtaṃ mahat | tacchobhayati śatrughno nānāvarṇopaśobhitām || 7.70.12 ||
translation: यच्च and which, तेन by him, पुरा formerly, शुभ्रं pure, लवणेन by Lavana, कृतं made, महत् great, तत् that, शोभयति beautifies, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, नानावर्णोपशोभिताम् adorned with various colors.
explanation: Shatrughna now beautifies that great and pure city, which was formerly created by Lavana, adorning it with various colors.

shloka_text: आरामैश्च विहारैश्च शोभमानं समन्ततः । शोभितां शोभनीयैश्च तथा ऽन्यैर्दैवमानुषैः ।। 7.70.13 ।।
transliteration: ārāmaiśca vihāraiśca śobhamānaṃ samantataḥ | śobhitāṃ śobhanīyaiśca tathā 'nyairdaivamānuṣaiḥ || 7.70.13 ||
translation: आरामैः with gardens, च and, विहारैः with pleasure-grounds, च and, शोभमानं shining, समन्ततः all around, शोभितां adorned, शोभनीयैः with beautiful things, च and, तथा similarly, अन्यैः with others, दैवमानुषैः divine and human.
explanation: The city was adorned all around with gardens and pleasure-grounds, and beautified by other divine and human elements.

shloka_text: तां पुरीं दिव्यसङ्काशां नानापण्योपशोभिताम् । नानादेशागतैश्चापि वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम् ।। 7.70.14 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ purīṃ divyasaṅkāśāṃ nānāpaṇyopaśobhitām | nānādeśāgataiścāpi vaṇigbhirupaśobhitām || 7.70.14 ||
translation: तां that, पुरीं city, दिव्यसङ्काशां resembling a divine city, नानापण्योपशोभिताम् adorned with various merchandise, नानादेशागतैः arrived from various countries, च and, अपि also, वणिग्भिः by merchants, उपशोभिताम् adorned.
explanation: That city, resembling a divine abode, was adorned with various merchandise and beautified by merchants who had arrived from diverse lands.

shloka_text: तां समृद्धां समृद्धार्थः शत्रुघ्नो भरतानुजः । निरीक्ष्य परमप्रीतः परं हर्षमुपागमत् ।। 7.70.15 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ samṛddhāṃ samṛddhārthaḥ śatrughno bharatānujaḥ | nirīkṣya paramaprītaḥ paraṃ harṣamupāgamat || 7.70.15 ||
translation: तां that, समृद्धां prosperous, समृद्धार्थः one whose purpose is fulfilled, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, भरतानुजः younger brother of Bharata, निरीक्ष्य having seen, परमप्रीतः extremely pleased, परं great, हर्षं joy, उपागमत् attained.
explanation: Shatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, whose purpose was fulfilled, observed that prosperous city and attained supreme joy, being extremely pleased.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य मधुरां पुरीम् । रामपादौ निरीक्षे ऽहं वर्षे द्वादश आगते ।। 7.70.16 ।।
transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya madhurāṃ purīm | rāmapādau nirīkṣe 'haṃ varṣe dvādaśa āgate || 7.70.16 ||
translation: तस्य his, बुद्धिः thought, समुत्पन्ना arose, निवेश्य having established, मधुरां Mathura, पुरीम् city, रामपादौ Rama's feet, निरीक्षे I shall see, अहं I, वर्षे in the year, द्वादश twelfth, आगते having arrived.
explanation: A thought arose in his mind that after establishing the city of Mathura, he would go to see Rama's feet when the twelfth year arrived.

shloka_text: ततः स ताममरपुरोपमां पुरीं निवेश्य वै विविधजनाभिसंवृताम् । नराधिपो रघुपतिपाददर्शने दधे मतिं रघुकुलवंशवर्धनः ।। 7.70.17 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa tāmamarapuropamāṃ purīṃ niveśya vai vividhajanābhisaṃvṛtām | narādhipo raghupatipādadarśane dadhe matiṃ raghukulavaṃśavardhanaḥ || 7.70.17 ||
translation: ततः then, सः he, ताम् that, अमरपुरोपमाम् resembling the city of gods, पुरीम् city, निवेश्य having established, वै indeed, विविधजनाभिसंवृताम् filled with various people, नराधिपः the king, रघुपतिपाददर्शने in seeing the feet of Rama, दधे placed, मतिम् mind, रघुकुलवंशवर्धनः the enhancer of the Raghu family lineage.
explanation: After establishing that city, which resembled the city of gods and was filled with various people, the king Shatrughna, the enhancer of the Raghu lineage, set his mind on seeing the feet of Lord Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 70 ।। Thus ends the seventieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो द्वादशमे वर्षे शत्रघ्नो रामपालिताम् । अयोध्यां चकमे गन्तुमल्पभृत्यबलानुगः ।। 7.71.1 ।।
transliteration: tato dvādaśame varṣe śatraghno rāmapālitām | ayodhyāṃ cakame gantumalpabhṛtyabalānugaḥ || 7.71.1 ||
translation: ततः then, द्वादशमे in the twelfth, वर्षे year, शत्रघ्नः Shatrughna, रामपालिताम् protected by Rama, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, चकमे desired, गन्तुम् to go, अल्पभृत्यबलानुगः accompanied by a small retinue of servants and army.
explanation: Then, in the twelfth year, Shatrughna, accompanied by a small retinue of servants and army, desired to go to Ayodhya, which was protected by Rama.
comments: In the twelfth year Shatrughna sets out for Ayodhya and lodges at Valmiki's hermitage, where the sage praises his slaying of Lavana, which he had witnessed from Indra's assembly -- there Shatrughna hears the singing of Valmiki's composed poem recounting Rama's own deeds, and he and his men are amazed and moved to tears, yet he forbids them to question the sage out of mere curiosity.

shloka_text: ततो मन्त्रिपुरोगांश्च बलमुख्यान्निवर्त्य च । जगाम हयमुख्यैश्च रथानां च शतेन सः ।। 7.71.2 ।।
transliteration: tato mantripurogāṃśca balamukhyānnivartya ca | jagāma hayamukhyaiśca rathānāṃ ca śatena saḥ || 7.71.2 ||
translation: ततः then, मन्त्रिपुरोगांश्च and the chief ministers, बलमुख्यान्निवर्त्य having sent back the chief commanders, च and, जगाम went, हयमुख्यैश्च and with excellent horses, रथानाम् of chariots, च and, शतेन with a hundred, सः he.
explanation: Then, having sent back his chief ministers and military commanders, he proceeded with excellent horses and a hundred chariots.

shloka_text: स गत्वा गणितान्वासान्सप्ताष्टौ रघुनन्दनः । वाल्मीक्याश्रममागत्य वासं चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.71.3 ।।
transliteration: sa gatvā gaṇitānvāsānsaptāṣṭau raghunandanaḥ | vālmīkyāśramamāgatya vāsaṃ cakre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.71.3 ||
translation: सः he, गत्वा having gone, गणितान्वासान् counted days of travel, सप्ताष्टौ seven or eight, रघुनन्दनः the delight of the Raghus, वाल्मीक्याश्रममागत्य having come to Valmiki's hermitage, वासम् stay, चक्रे made, महायशाः the greatly renowned.
explanation: Having traveled for seven or eight counted days, the greatly renowned Shatrughna, the delight of the Raghus, arrived at Valmiki's hermitage and made his stay there.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ वाल्मीकेः पुरुषर्षभः । पाद्यमर्ध्यं तथातिथ्यं जग्राह मुनिहस्ततः ।। 7.71.4 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya tataḥ pādau vālmīkeḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ | pādyamardhyaṃ tathātithyaṃ jagrāha munihastataḥ || 7.71.4 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, ततः then, पादौ feet, वाल्मीकेः of Valmiki, पुरुषर्षभः the best among men, पाद्यम् water for washing feet, अर्ध्यम् water for respectful offering, तथातिथ्यम् and hospitality, जग्राह accepted, मुनिहस्ततः from the hand of the sage.
explanation: Then, the best among men, Shatrughna, having saluted Valmiki's feet, accepted the water for washing feet, the respectful offering, and the hospitality from the sage's hand.

shloka_text: बहुरूपाः सुमधुराः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः । कथयामास स मुनिः शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने ।। 7.71.5 ।।
transliteration: bahurūpāḥ sumadhurāḥ kathāstatra sahasraśaḥ | kathayāmāsa sa muniḥ śatrughnāya mahātmane || 7.71.5 ||
translation: बहुरूपाः of many forms, सुमधुराः very sweet, कथाः stories, तत्र there, सहस्रशः in thousands, कथयामास narrated, सः that, मुनिः sage, शत्रुघ्नाय to Shatrughna, महात्मने to the great-souled one.
explanation: That sage narrated thousands of stories, varied in form and very sweet, to the great-souled Shatrughna.

shloka_text: उवाच च मुनिर्वाक्यं लवणस्य वधाश्रितम् । सुदुष्करं कृतं कर्म लवणं निघ्नता त्वया ।। 7.71.6 ।।
transliteration: uvāca ca munirvākyaṃ lavaṇasya vadhāśritam | suduṣkaraṃ kṛtaṃ karma lavaṇaṃ nighnatā tvayā || 7.71.6 ||
translation: उवाच spoke, च and, मुनिः the sage, वाक्यम् words, लवणस्य of Lavana, वधाश्रितम् related to the killing, सुदुष्करम् very difficult, कृतम् done, कर्म deed, लवणम् Lavana, निघ्नता by one who killed, त्वया by you.
explanation: And the sage spoke words concerning the killing of Lavana, saying that the deed of killing Lavana, which you accomplished, was extremely arduous.

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवाः सौम्य हताः सबलवाहनाः । लवणेन महाबाहो युध्यमाना महाबलाः ।। 7.71.7 ।।
transliteration: bahavaḥ pārthivāḥ saumya hatāḥ sabalavāhanāḥ | lavaṇena mahābāho yudhyamānā mahābalāḥ || 7.71.7 ||
translation: बहवः many, पार्थिवाः kings, सौम्य O gentle one, हताः killed, सबलवाहनाः with their armies and vehicles, लवणेन by Lavana, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, युध्यमानाः fighting, महाबलाः very powerful.
explanation: O gentle and mighty-armed one, many very powerful kings, along with their armies and vehicles, were killed by Lavana while fighting him.

shloka_text: स त्वया निहतः पापो लीलया पुरुषर्षभ । जगतश्च भयं तत्र प्रशान्तं तव तेजसा ।। 7.71.8 ।।
transliteration: sa tvayā nihataḥ pāpo līlayā puruṣarṣabha | jagataśca bhayaṃ tatra praśāntaṃ tava tejasā || 7.71.8 ||
translation: सः that, त्वया by you, निहतः killed, पापः wicked one, लीलया with ease, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, जगतः of the world, च and, भयम् fear, तत्र there, प्रशान्तम् pacified, तव your, तेजसा by valor.
explanation: O best among men, that wicked one was killed by you with ease, and the fear of the world was pacified by your valor.

shloka_text: रावणस्य वधो घोरो यत्नेन महता कृतः । इदं तु सुमहत्कर्म त्वया कृतमयत्नतः ।। 7.71.9 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇasya vadho ghoro yatnena mahatā kṛtaḥ | idaṃ tu sumahatkarma tvayā kṛtamayatnataḥ || 7.71.9 ||
translation: रावणस्य of Ravana, वधः the killing, घोरः terrible, यत्नेन with effort, महता great, कृतः done, इदम् this, तु but, सुमहत्कर्म very great deed, त्वया by you, कृतम् done, अयत्नतः effortlessly.
explanation: The terrible killing of Ravana was accomplished with great effort, but this very great deed was done by you effortlessly.

shloka_text: प्रीतिश्चास्मिन्परा जाता देवानां लवणे हते । भूतानां चैव सर्वेषां जगतश्च प्रियं कृतम् ।। 7.71.10 ।।
transliteration: prītiścāsminparā jātā devānāṃ lavaṇe hate | bhūtānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ jagataśca priyaṃ kṛtam || 7.71.10 ||
translation: प्रीतिः joy, च and, अस्मिन् in this matter, परा great, जाता arose, देवानां of the gods, लवणे Lavana, हते having been killed, भूतानां of beings, च and, एव indeed, सर्वेषां of all, जगतः of the world, च and, प्रियं good, कृतम् was done.
explanation: Upon Lavana's death, great joy arose among the gods and all beings, and good was done for the entire world.

shloka_text: तच्च युद्धं मया दृष्टं यथावत्पुरुषर्षभ । सभायां वासवस्याथ उपविष्टेन राघव ।। 7.71.11 ।।
transliteration: tacca yuddhaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ yathāvatpuruṣarṣabha | sabhāyāṃ vāsavasyātha upaviṣṭena rāghava || 7.71.11 ||
translation: तत् that, च and, युद्धं battle, मया by me, दृष्टं was seen, यथावत् properly, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men, सभायां in the assembly, वासवस्य of Vasava (Indra), अथ then, उपविष्टेन by one seated, राघव O Raghava.
explanation: O best among men, O Raghava, that battle was seen by me exactly as it happened, while I was seated in the assembly of Indra.

shloka_text: ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हृदि शत्रुघ्न वर्तते । उपाघ्रास्यामि ते मूर्ध्नि स्नेहस्यैषा परा गतिः ।। 7.71.12 ।।
transliteration: mamāpi paramā prītirhṛdi śatrughna vartate | upāghrāsyāmi te mūrdhni snehasyaiṣā parā gatiḥ || 7.71.12 ||
translation: मम my, अपि also, परमा supreme, प्रीतिः joy, हृदि in the heart, शत्रुघ्न O Shatrughna, वर्तते exists, उपाघ्रास्यामि I will smell/kiss, ते your, मूर्ध्नि on the head, स्नेहस्य of affection, एषा this, परा supreme, गतिः expression.
explanation: O Shatrughna, supreme joy also resides in my heart, and I will kiss your head, for this is the highest expression of affection.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा मूर्ध्नि शत्रुघ्नमुपाघ्राय महामुनिः । आतिथ्यमकरोत्तस्य ये च तस्य पदानुगाः ।। 7.71.13 ।।
transliteration: ityuktvā mūrdhni śatrughnamupāghrāya mahāmuniḥ | ātithyamakarottasya ye ca tasya padānugāḥ || 7.71.13 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, मूर्ध्नि on the head, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, उपाघ्राय having kissed, महामुनिः the great sage, आतिथ्यम् hospitality, अकरोत् offered, तस्य to him, ये who, च and, तस्य his, पदानुगाः followers.
explanation: Having thus spoken and kissed Shatrughna on the head, the great sage offered hospitality to him and his followers.

shloka_text: स भुक्तवान्नरश्रेष्ठो गीतमाधुर्यमुत्तमम् । शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले यथाकृमम् ।। 7.71.14 ।।
transliteration: sa bhuktavānnaraśreṣṭho gītamādhuryamuttamam | śuśrāva rāmacaritaṃ tasminkāle yathākṛmam || 7.71.14 ||
translation: सः he, भुक्तवान् having eaten, नरश्रेष्ठः the best among men, गीतमाधुर्यम् the sweetness of the song, उत्तमम् excellent, शुश्राव heard, रामचरितं the deeds of Rama, तस्मिन् in that, काले time, यथाकृमम् in due order.
explanation: After eating, the best among men, Shatrughna, heard the excellent sweetness of the song narrating the deeds of Rama, in due order at that time.

shloka_text: तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्तं त्रिस्थानकरणान्वितम् । संस्कृतं लक्षणोपेतं समतालसमन्वितम् । शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले पुरा कृतम् ।। 7.71.15 ।।
transliteration: tantrīlayasamāyuktaṃ tristhānakaraṇānvitam | saṃskṛtaṃ lakṣaṇopetaṃ samatālasamanvitam | śuśrāva rāmacaritaṃ tasminkāle purā kṛtam || 7.71.15 ||
translation: तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्तं endowed with the rhythm of string instruments, त्रिस्थानकरणान्वितम् accompanied by actions in three registers, संस्कृतं refined, लक्षणोपेतं endowed with characteristics, समतालसमन्वितम् endowed with perfect rhythm, शुश्राव he heard, रामचरितं the deeds of Rama, तस्मिन्काले at that time, पुरा previously, कृतम् composed.
explanation: At that time, he heard the previously composed deeds of Rama, which were endowed with the rhythm of string instruments, accompanied by actions in three registers, refined, characterized by rules, and perfectly rhythmic.

shloka_text: तान्यक्षराणि सत्यानि यथावृत्तानि पूर्वशः । श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलो विसञ्ज्ञो बाष्पलोचनः ।। 7.71.16 ।।
transliteration: tānyakṣarāṇi satyāni yathāvṛttāni pūrvaśaḥ | śrutvā puruṣaśārdūlo visañjño bāṣpalocanaḥ || 7.71.16 ||
translation: तानि those, अक्षराणि words, सत्यानि true, यथावृत्तानि as they happened, पूर्वशः formerly, श्रुत्वा having heard, पुरुषशार्दूलो the tiger among men (Rama), विसञ्ज्ञो bewildered, बाष्पलोचनः with tearful eyes.
explanation: Having heard those true words, which recounted events exactly as they had formerly happened, Rama, the tiger among men, became bewildered with tearful eyes.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तमिवासञ्ज्ञो विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः । तस्मिन् गीते यथावृत्तं वर्तमानमिवाशृणोत् ।। 7.71.17 ।।
transliteration: sa muhūrtamivāsañjño viniḥśvasya muhurmuhuḥ | tasmin gīte yathāvṛttaṃ vartamānamivāśṛṇot || 7.71.17 ||
translation: स he, मुहूर्तमिवासञ्ज्ञो as if bewildered for a moment, विनिःश्वस्य having sighed, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, तस्मिन् in that, गीते song, यथावृत्तं as it happened, वर्तमानमिवाशृणोत् he heard as if it were happening in the present.
explanation: For a moment, he remained as if bewildered, sighing repeatedly, and in that song, he heard the past events as if they were unfolding in the present.

shloka_text: पदानुगाश्च ये राज्ञस्तां श्रुत्वा गीतिसम्पदम् । अवाङ्मुखाश्च दीनाश्च ह्याश्चर्यमिति चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.71.18 ।।
transliteration: padānugāśca ye rājñastāṃ śrutvā gītisampadam | avāṅmukhāśca dīnāśca hyāścaryamiti cābruvan || 7.71.18 ||
translation: पदानुगाश्च and the followers, ये who, राज्ञः of the king, तां that, श्रुत्वा having heard, गीतिसम्पदम् excellent song, अवाङ्मुखाश्च and with downcast faces, दीनाश्च and distressed, हि indeed, आश्चर्यमिति "this is a wonder", च and, अब्रुवन् they said.
explanation: And the king's followers, having heard that excellent song, became downcast and distressed, exclaiming, "This is indeed a wonder!"

shloka_text: परस्परं च ये तत्र सैनिकाः सम्बभाषिरे । किमिदं क्व च वर्तामः किमेतत्स्वप्नदर्शनम् ।। 7.71.19 ।।
transliteration: parasparaṃ ca ye tatra sainikāḥ sambabhāṣire | kimidaṃ kva ca vartāmaḥ kimetatsvapnadarśanam || 7.71.19 ||
translation: परस्परं to each other, च and, ये who, तत्र there, सैनिकाः soldiers, सम्बभाषिरे spoke, किमिदं what is this, क्व where, च and, वर्तामः are we, किमेतत्स्वप्नदर्शनम् is this a dream vision.
explanation: And the soldiers present there spoke to each other, wondering, "What is this? Where are we? Is this a dream vision?"

shloka_text: अर्थो यो नः पुरा दृष्टस्तमाश्रमपदे पुनः । शृणुमः किमिदं स्वप्नो गीतबन्धं श्रियो भवेत् ।। 7.71.20 ।।
transliteration: artho yo naḥ purā dṛṣṭastamāśramapade punaḥ | śṛṇumaḥ kimidaṃ svapno gītabandhaṃ śriyo bhavet || 7.71.20 ||
translation: अर्थो a meaning/thing, यो which, नः by us, पुरा previously, दृष्टः was seen, तम् that, आश्रमपदे in the hermitage, पुनः again, शृणुमः we hear, किम् what, इदम् is this, स्वप्नः a dream, गीतबन्धं a song-composition, श्रियः of beauty/fortune, भवेत् it might be.
explanation: They wondered if what they were hearing in the hermitage, which seemed to be a previously seen event, was a dream or a beautiful song.
