transliteration: evaṃ bahuvidhā vāco hyantarikṣagatāḥ surāḥ | vyājahrurhṛṣṭamanaso dṛṣṭvā sītāpraveśanam || 7.97.23 ||
translation: एवम् thus, बहुविधाः various, वाचः words, हि indeed, अन्तरिक्षगताः celestial, सुराः gods, व्याजह्रुः uttered, हृष्टमनसः with joyful minds, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सीताप्रवेशनम् Sita's entry.
explanation: The celestial gods, with joyful minds, uttered various words upon witnessing Sita's entry into the earth.

shloka_text: यज्ञवाटगताश्चापि मुनयः सर्व एव ते । राजानश्च नरव्याघ्रा विस्मयान्नोपरेमिरे ।। 7.97.24 ।।
transliteration: yajñavāṭagatāścāpi munayaḥ sarva eva te | rājānaśca naravyāghrā vismayānnoparemire || 7.97.24 ||
translation: यज्ञवाटगताः those in the sacrificial enclosure, च and, अपि also, मुनयः sages, सर्वे all, एव indeed, ते those, राजानः kings, च and, नरव्याघ्राः best among men, विस्मयात् from astonishment, न not, उपरेमिरे ceased.
explanation: All those sages and kings, who were like tigers among men, present in the sacrificial enclosure, did not cease their astonishment.

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षे च भूमौ च सर्वे स्थावरजङ्गमाः । दानवाश्च महाकायाः पाताले पन्नगाधिपाः ।। 7.97.25 ।।
transliteration: antarikṣe ca bhūmau ca sarve sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ | dānavāśca mahākāyāḥ pātāle pannagādhipāḥ || 7.97.25 ||
translation: अन्तरिक्षे in the sky, च and, भूमौ on the earth, च and, सर्वे all, स्थावरजङ्गमाः stationary and moving beings, दानवाः demons, च and, महाकायाः of huge bodies, पाताले in the netherworld, पन्नगाधिपाः lords of serpents.
explanation: All stationary and moving beings in the sky and on the earth, along with the huge-bodied demons and the lords of serpents in the netherworld, were present.

shloka_text: केचिद्विनेदुः संहृष्टाः केचिद्ध्यानपरायणाः । केचिद्रामं निरीक्षन्ते केचित्सीतामचेतनाः ।। 7.97.26 ।।
transliteration: kecidvineduḥ saṃhṛṣṭāḥ keciddhyānaparāyaṇāḥ | kecidrāmaṃ nirīkṣante kecitsītāmacetanāḥ || 7.97.26 ||
translation: केचित् some, विनेदुः roared, संहृष्टाः greatly delighted, केचित् some, ध्यानपरायणाः absorbed in meditation, केचित् some, रामम् Rama, निरीक्षन्ते gazed at, केचित् some, सीताम् Sita, अचेतनाः stunned.
explanation: Some, greatly delighted, roared; some were absorbed in meditation; some gazed at Rama, while others, stunned, looked at Sita.

shloka_text: सीताप्रवेशनं दृष्ट्वा तेषामासीत्समागमः । तन्मुहूर्तमिवात्यर्थं समं सम्मोहितं जगत् ।। 7.97.27 ।।
transliteration: sītāpraveśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣāmāsītsamāgamaḥ | tanmuhūrtamivātyarthaṃ samaṃ sammohitaṃ jagat || 7.97.27 ||
translation: सीताप्रवेशनम् Sita's entry, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तेषाम् among them, आसीत् there was, समागमः a gathering, तत् that, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, इव as if, अत्यर्थम् exceedingly, समम् entirely, सम्मोहितम् bewildered, जगत् the world.
explanation: Upon witnessing Sita's entry, there was a great gathering of beings, and for a moment, the entire world seemed exceedingly bewildered. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 97 ।। Thus ends the ninety-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रसातलं प्रविष्टायां वैदेह्यां सर्ववानराः । चुक्रुशुः साधु साध्वीति मुनयो रामसन्निधौ ।। 7.98.1 ।।
transliteration: rasātalaṃ praviṣṭāyāṃ vaidehyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ | cukruśuḥ sādhu sādhvīti munayo rāmasannidhau || 7.98.1 ||
translation: रसातलं into the netherworld, प्रविष्टायां having entered, वैदेह्यां when Vaidehi (Sita), सर्ववानराः all the monkeys, चुक्रुशुः cried out, साधु excellent, साध्वीति excellent (feminine), मुनयो the sages, रामसन्निधौ in the presence of Rama.
explanation: When Vaidehi entered the netherworld, all the monkeys and sages present before Rama cried out "Excellent! Excellent!"
comments: Stricken with grief and rage, Rama demands that Earth restore Sita or grant him entry, threatening her destruction -- Brahma appears, bids him not grieve, reminds him of his nature as Vishnu, and promises reunion with the pure Sita in heaven -- extolling Valmiki's poem and bidding Rama hear its remaining Uttara portion, Brahma departs, and the grieving Rama arranges for the rest to be sung on the morrow.

shloka_text: दण्डकाष्ठमवष्टभ्य बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः । अवाक्छिरा दीनमना रामो ह्यासीत्सुदुःखितः ।। 7.98.2 ।।
transliteration: daṇḍakāṣṭhamavaṣṭabhya bāṣpavyākulitekṣaṇaḥ | avākchirā dīnamanā rāmo hyāsītsuduḥkhitaḥ || 7.98.2 ||
translation: दण्डकाष्ठम् a staff, अवष्टभ्य leaning upon, बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः with eyes agitated by tears, अवाक्छिरा with head bowed down, दीनमना with a sorrowful mind, रामो Rama, ह्यासीत् indeed was, सुदुःखितः extremely distressed.
explanation: Leaning upon a staff, with his eyes agitated by tears, his head bowed down, and his mind filled with sorrow, Rama was indeed extremely distressed.

shloka_text: स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं बहुशो बाष्पमुत्सृजन् । क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.3 ।।
transliteration: sa ruditvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bahuśo bāṣpamutsṛjan | krodhaśokasamāviṣṭo rāmo vacanamabravīt || 7.98.3 ||
translation: स He, रुदित्वा having wept, चिरं for a long, कालं time, बहुशो many times, बाष्पम् tears, उत्सृजन् shedding, क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो overcome by anger and sorrow, रामो Rama, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having wept for a long time and shedding many tears, Rama, overcome by both anger and sorrow, then spoke these words.

shloka_text: अभूतपूर्वं शोकं मे मनः स्प्रष्टुमिवेच्छति । पश्यतो मे यथा नष्टा सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी ।। 7.98.4 ।।
transliteration: abhūtapūrvaṃ śokaṃ me manaḥ spraṣṭumivecchati | paśyato me yathā naṣṭā sītā śrīriva rūpiṇī || 7.98.4 ||
translation: अभूतपूर्वं unprecedented, शोकं sorrow, मे my, मनः mind, स्प्रष्टुम् to touch, इवेच्छति seems to desire, पश्यतो while I watched, मे my, यथा just as, नष्टा disappeared, सीता Sita, श्रीरिव like the goddess of fortune, रूपिणी embodied.
explanation: My mind seems to desire an unprecedented sorrow, as Sita, who was like the embodied goddess of fortune, disappeared right before my eyes.

shloka_text: सा ऽदर्शनं पुरा सीता लङ्कापारे महोदधेः । ततश्चापि मयानीता किं पुनर्वसुधातलात् ।। 7.98.5 ।।
transliteration: sā 'darśanaṃ purā sītā laṅkāpāre mahodadheḥ | tataścāpi mayānītā kiṃ punarvasudhātalāt || 7.98.5 ||
translation: सा That, अदर्शनं disappearance, पुरा formerly, सीता Sita, लङ्कापारे on the other side of Lanka, महोदधेः of the great ocean, ततश्चापि and from there, मयानीता brought by me, किं what, पुनर् again, वसुधातलात् from the surface of the earth.
explanation: Formerly, Sita disappeared on the other side of Lanka, beyond the great ocean, and even from there I brought her back; how much more difficult will it be to retrieve her from the surface of the earth now?

shloka_text: वसुधे देवि भवति सीता निर्यात्यतां मम । दर्शयिष्यामि वा रोषं यथा मामवगच्छसि ।। 7.98.6 ।।
transliteration: vasudhe devi bhavati sītā niryātyatāṃ mama | darśayiṣyāmi vā roṣaṃ yathā māmavagacchasi || 7.98.6 ||
translation: वसुधे O Earth, देवि O Goddess, भवति (you) are, सीता Sita, निर्यात्यतां let her be brought forth, मम to me, दर्शयिष्यामि I will show, वा or, रोषं anger, यथा so that, माम् me, अवगच्छसि you understand.
explanation: O Goddess Earth, bring forth Sita to me, or else I will show you my wrath so that you understand who I am.

shloka_text: कामं श्वश्रूर्ममैव त्वं त्वत्सकाशाद्धि मैथिली । कर्षता हलहस्तेन जनकेनोद्धृता पुरा ।। 7.98.7 ।।
transliteration: kāmaṃ śvaśrūrmamaiva tvaṃ tvatsakāśāddhi maithilī | karṣatā halahastena janakenoddhṛtā purā || 7.98.7 ||
translation: कामं indeed, श्वश्रूः mother-in-law, मम my, एव indeed, त्वं you, त्वत्सकाशात् from you, हि indeed, मैथिली Maithili (Sita), कर्षता by one who was ploughing, हलहस्तेन with a plough in hand, जनकेन by Janaka, उद्धृता was taken out, पुरा formerly.
explanation: Indeed, you are my mother-in-law, for Maithili was certainly taken out from you by Janaka, who was ploughing with a plough in hand, long ago.

shloka_text: तस्मान्निर्यात्यतां सीता विवरं वा प्रयच्छ मे । पाताले नाकपृष्ठे वा वसेयं सहितस्तया ।। 7.98.8 ।।
transliteration: tasmānniryātyatāṃ sītā vivaraṃ vā prayaccha me | pātāle nākapṛṣṭhe vā vaseyaṃ sahitastayā || 7.98.8 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, निर्यात्यतां let her be brought forth, सीता Sita, विवरं an opening, वा or, प्रयच्छ give, मे to me, पाताले in the netherworld, नाकपृष्ठे on the surface of heaven, वा or, वसेयं I would dwell, सहितः accompanied, तया by her.
explanation: Therefore, bring forth Sita, or grant me an opening, so that I may dwell with her either in the netherworld or on the surface of heaven.

shloka_text: आनय त्वं हि तां सीतां मत्तो ऽहं मैथिलीकृते । न मे दास्यसि चेत्सीतां यथारूपां महीतले ।। 7.98.9 ।।
transliteration: ānaya tvaṃ hi tāṃ sītāṃ matto 'haṃ maithilīkṛte | na me dāsyasi cetsītāṃ yathārūpāṃ mahītale || 7.98.9 ||
translation: आनय bring, त्वं you, हि indeed, तां her, सीतां Sita, मत्तः maddened, अहं I, मैथिलीकृते for the sake of Maithili, न not, मे to me, दास्यसि you will give, चेत् if, सीतां Sita, यथारूपां in her true form, महीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: You must indeed bring that Sita, as I am maddened for Maithili's sake; if you do not give Sita to me in her true form on the surface of the earth, then...

shloka_text: सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां विधमिष्यामि ते स्थितम् । नाशयिष्याम्यहं भूमिं सर्वमापो भवत्विह ।। 7.98.10 ।।
transliteration: saparvatavanāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vidhamiṣyāmi te sthitam | nāśayiṣyāmyahaṃ bhūmiṃ sarvamāpo bhavatviha || 7.98.10 ||
translation: सपर्वतवनां with mountains and forests, कृत्स्नां entire, विधमिष्यामि I will destroy, ते your, स्थितम् existence, नाशयिष्यामि I will destroy, अहं I, भूमिं the earth, सर्वम् everything, आपः water, भवतु let it become, इह here.
explanation: I will destroy your entire existence, including all mountains and forests, I will annihilate the earth, and let everything here become water.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणे काकुत्स्थे क्रोधशोकसमन्विते । ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.98.11 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇe kākutsthe krodhaśokasamanvite | brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhamuvāca raghunandanam || 7.98.11 ||
translation: एवं thus, ब्रुवाणे while speaking, काकुत्स्थे to Kakutstha (Rama), क्रोधशोकसमन्विते filled with anger and sorrow, ब्रह्मा Brahma, सुरगणैः with the hosts of gods, सार्धम् together, उवाच spoke, रघुनन्दनम् to the delight of the Raghus (Rama).
explanation: While Rama, filled with anger and sorrow, was speaking thus, Brahma, accompanied by the hosts of gods, addressed him.

shloka_text: राम राम न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत । स्मर त्वं पूर्वकं भावं मन्त्रं चामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.98.12 ।।
transliteration: rāma rāma na santāpaṃ kartumarhasi suvrata | smara tvaṃ pūrvakaṃ bhāvaṃ mantraṃ cāmitrakarśana || 7.98.12 ||
translation: राम O Rama, राम O Rama, न not, सन्तापम् sorrow, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought, सुव्रत O virtuous one, स्मर remember, त्वम् you, पूर्वकम् former, भावम् state (of being), मन्त्रम् sacred incantation, च and, अमित्रकर्शन O destroyer of enemies.
explanation: O virtuous Rama, you should not grieve; O destroyer of enemies, remember your ancient divine nature and the sacred incantation.

shloka_text: न खलु त्वां महाबाहो स्मारयेयमनुत्तमम् । इमं मुहूर्तं दुर्धर्ष स्मर त्वं जन्म वैष्णवम् ।। 7.98.13 ।।
transliteration: na khalu tvāṃ mahābāho smārayeyamanuttamam | imaṃ muhūrtaṃ durdharṣa smara tvaṃ janma vaiṣṇavam || 7.98.13 ||
translation: न not, खलु indeed, त्वाम् you, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, स्मारयेयम् I would remind, अनुत्तमम् the unsurpassed (state), इमम् this, मुहूर्तम् moment, दुर्धर्ष O unconquerable one, स्मर remember, त्वम् you, जन्म birth, वैष्णवम् divine (Vishnu's).
explanation: O mighty-armed and unconquerable one, I would indeed remind you of your unsurpassed divine nature; at this very moment, remember your divine birth as Vishnu.

shloka_text: सीता हि विमला साध्वी तव पूर्वपरायणा । नागलोकं सुखं प्रायात्त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात् ।। 7.98.14 ।।
transliteration: sītā hi vimalā sādhvī tava pūrvaparāyaṇā | nāgalokaṃ sukhaṃ prāyāttvadāśrayatapobalāt || 7.98.14 ||
translation: सीता Sita, हि indeed, विमला pure, साध्वी virtuous, तव your, पूर्वपरायणा solely devoted from the beginning, नागलोकम् to the Naga world, सुखम् happily, प्रायात् went, त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात् by the strength of her penance relying on you.
explanation: Indeed, Sita, pure, virtuous, and solely devoted to you from the beginning, happily went to the Naga world by the power of her penance and devotion to you.

shloka_text: स्वर्गे ते सङ्गमो भूयो भविष्यति न संशयः । अस्यास्तु परिषन्मध्ये यद्ब्रवीमि निबोध तत् ।। 7.98.15 ।।
transliteration: svarge te saṅgamo bhūyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ | asyāstu pariṣanmadhye yadbravīmi nibodha tat || 7.98.15 ||
translation: स्वर्गे in heaven, ते your, सङ्गमः union, भूयः again, भविष्यति will be, न no, संशयः doubt, अस्याः of this, तु but, परिषन्मध्ये in the midst of the assembly, यत् what, ब्रवीमि I say, निबोध understand, तत् that.
explanation: There is no doubt that your union with her will happen again in heaven; but understand what I am about to tell you in the midst of this assembly.

shloka_text: एतदेव हि काव्यं ते काव्यानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् । सर्वं विस्तरतो राम व्याख्यास्यति न संशयः ।। 7.98.16 ।।
transliteration: etadeva hi kāvyaṃ te kāvyānāmuttamaṃ śrutam | sarvaṃ vistarato rāma vyākhyāsyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.98.16 ||
translation: एतदेव this alone, हि indeed, काव्यं poem, ते by you, काव्यानाम् among poems, उत्तमं best, श्रुतम् heard. सर्वं all, विस्तरतः in detail, राम O Rama, व्याख्यास्यति will explain, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: This poem, which you have heard, is indeed the best among all poems, and Rama will explain everything in detail without a doubt.

shloka_text: जन्मप्रभृति ते वीर सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् । भविष्यदुत्तरं चेह सर्वं वाल्मीकिना कृतम् ।। 7.98.17 ।।
transliteration: janmaprabhṛti te vīra sukhaduḥkhopasevanam | bhaviṣyaduttaraṃ ceha sarvaṃ vālmīkinā kṛtam || 7.98.17 ||
translation: जन्मप्रभृति from birth onwards, ते your, वीर O hero, सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् experiencing joys and sorrows. भविष्यदुत्तरं and the future, च and, इह here, सर्वं all, वाल्मीकिना by Valmiki, कृतम् composed.
explanation: O hero, Valmiki has composed everything, from your birth and the experiences of joy and sorrow, to the future events that will unfold.

shloka_text: आदिकाव्यमिदं राम त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । नह्यन्यो ऽर्हति काव्यानां यशोभाग्राघवादृते ।। 7.98.18 ।।
transliteration: ādikāvyamidaṃ rāma tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam | nahyanyo 'rhati kāvyānāṃ yaśobhāgrāghavādṛte || 7.98.18 ||
translation: आदिकाव्यम् this first poem, इदं this, राम O Rama, त्वयि in you, सर्वं all, प्रतिष्ठितम् established. न not, हि indeed, अन्यः another, अर्हति deserves, काव्यानां among poems, यशोभाग्राघवादृते the share of glory, except for Rama.
explanation: O Rama, this primeval poem is entirely founded upon you, and indeed, no one else but you, O Raghava, deserves the glory among poems.

shloka_text: श्रुतं ते पूर्वमेतद्धि मया सर्वं सुरैः सह । दिव्यमद्भुतरूपं च सत्यवाक्यमनावृतम् ।। 7.98.19 ।।
transliteration: śrutaṃ te pūrvametaddhi mayā sarvaṃ suraiḥ saha | divyamadbhutarūpaṃ ca satyavākyamanāvṛtam || 7.98.19 ||
translation: श्रुतं heard, ते by you, पूर्वम् previously, एतत् this, हि indeed, मया by me, सर्वं all, सुरैः with gods, सह together. दिव्यम् divine, अद्भुतरूपं of wondrous form, च and, सत्यवाक्यम् truthful words, अनावृतम् unconcealed.
explanation: Indeed, I have previously heard all of this, which is divine, of wondrous form, and contains unconcealed truthful words, along with the gods.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धर्मेण सुसमाहितः । शेषं भविष्यं काकुत्स्थ काव्यं रामायणं शृणु ।। 7.98.20 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla dharmeṇa susamāhitaḥ | śeṣaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ kākutstha kāvyaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ śṛṇu || 7.98.20 ||
translation: स therefore, त्वं you, पुरुषशार्दूल O best among men, धर्मेण with righteousness, सुसमाहितः well-composed/attentive. शेषं the remaining, भविष्यं future, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, काव्यं poem, रामायणं Ramayana, शृणु listen.
explanation: Therefore, O best among men, O Kakutstha, being well-composed and attentive to righteousness, listen to the remaining future events of the Ramayana poem.

shloka_text: उत्तरं नाम काव्यस्य शेषमत्र महायशः । तच्छृणुष्व महातेज ऋषिभिः सार्धमुत्तमम् ।। 7.98.21 ।।
transliteration: uttaraṃ nāma kāvyasya śeṣamatra mahāyaśaḥ | tacchṛṇuṣva mahāteja ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhamuttamam || 7.98.21 ||
translation: उत्तरं Uttaram, नाम named, काव्यस्य of the epic poem, शेषम् the remainder, अत्र here, महायशः O greatly renowned one, तत् that, शृणुष्व listen, महातेज O greatly effulgent one, ऋषिभिः with the sages, सार्धम् together with, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: O greatly renowned and effulgent Rama, listen here to this excellent concluding part of the epic poem, named Uttara, along with the sages.

shloka_text: न खल्वन्येन काकुत्स्थ श्रोतव्यमिदमुत्तमम् । परमम् ऋषिणा वीर त्वयैव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.98.22 ।।
transliteration: na khalvanyena kākutstha śrotavyamidamuttamam | paramam ṛṣiṇā vīra tvayaiva raghunandana || 7.98.22 ||
translation: न not, खलु indeed, अन्येन by another, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, श्रोतव्यम् to be heard, इदम् this, उत्तमम् excellent, परमम् supreme, ऋषिणा by the sage, वीर O hero, त्वया by you, एव only, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus.
explanation: Indeed, O Kakutstha, O hero, O delight of the Raghus, this excellent and supreme work, composed by the sage, is not to be heard by anyone else, but only by you.

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः । जगाम त्रिदिवं देवो देवैः सह सबान्धवैः ।। 7.98.23 ।।
transliteration: etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ brahmā tribhuvaneśvaraḥ | jagāma tridivaṃ devo devaiḥ saha sabāndhavaiḥ || 7.98.23 ||
translation: एतावत् thus much, उक्त्वा having said, वचनम् the word, ब्रह्मा Brahma, त्रिभुवनेश्वरः the lord of the three worlds, जगाम went, त्रिदिवम् to heaven, देवः the god, देवैः with the gods, सह together with, सबान्धवैः with his relatives.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Brahma, the lord of the three worlds, the god, went to heaven along with the other gods and his associates.

shloka_text: ये च तत्र महात्मान ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता न्यवर्तन्त महौजसः । उत्तरं श्रोतुमनसो भविष्यं यच्च राघवे ।। 7.98.24 ।।
transliteration: ye ca tatra mahātmāna ṛṣayo brāhmalaukikāḥ | brahmaṇā samanujñātā nyavartanta mahaujasaḥ | uttaraṃ śrotumanaso bhaviṣyaṃ yacca rāghave || 7.98.24 ||
translation: ये those who, च and, तत्र there, महात्मानः great-souled ones, ऋषयः sages, ब्राह्मलौकिकाः belonging to Brahma's world, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, समनुज्ञाताः permitted, न्यवर्तन्त returned, महौजसः greatly powerful ones, उत्तरम् the Uttara Kanda, श्रोतुमनसः desirous to hear, भविष्यम् the future, यत् which, च and, राघवे regarding Rama.
explanation: And those great-souled, greatly powerful sages from Brahma's world, who were desirous to hear the Uttara Kanda and the future events concerning Rama, returned after being permitted by Brahma.

shloka_text: ततो रामः शुभां वाणीं देवदेवस्य भाषिताम् । श्रुत्वा परमतेजस्वी वाल्मीकिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.25 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ devadevasya bhāṣitām | śrutvā paramatejasvī vālmīkimidamabravīt || 7.98.25 ||
translation: ततः then, रामः Rama, शुभाम् auspicious, वाणीम् speech, देवदेवस्य of the god of gods, भाषिताम् spoken, श्रुत्वा having heard, परमतेजस्वी most effulgent, वाल्मीकिम् to Valmiki, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Then, the most effulgent Rama, having heard the auspicious words spoken by Brahma, the god of gods, said this to Valmiki.

shloka_text: भगवन् श्रोतुमनस ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । भविष्यदुत्तरं यन्मे श्वोभूते सम्प्रवर्तताम् ।। 7.98.26 ।।
transliteration: bhagavan śrotumanasa ṛṣayo brāhmalaukikāḥ | bhaviṣyaduttaraṃ yanme śvobhūte sampravartatām || 7.98.26 ||
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, श्रोतुमनसः desirous of hearing, ऋषयः sages, ब्राह्मलौकिकाः from Brahma's realm, भविष्यत् future, उत्तरम् latter part, यत् which, मे by me, श्वोभूते on the morrow, सम्प्रवर्तताम् let it be commenced.
explanation: Valmiki addresses the venerable sages from Brahma's realm, expressing his desire for the future, latter part of his Ramayana to be commenced on the following day for them to hear.

shloka_text: एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा सम्प्रगृह्य कुशीलवौ । तं जनौघं विसृज्याथ पर्णशालामुपागमत् । तामेव शोचतः सीतां सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी ।। 7.98.27 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā sampragṛhya kuśīlavau | taṃ janaughaṃ visṛjyātha parṇaśālāmupāgamat | tāmeva śocataḥ sītāṃ sā vyatīyāya śarvarī || 7.98.27 ||
translation: एवम् thus, विनिश्चयम् decision, कृत्वा having made, सम्प्रगृह्य having taken, कुशीलवौ Kusha and Lava, तम् that, जनौघम् multitude of people, विसृज्य having dismissed, अथ then, पर्णशालाम् to the hermitage, उपागमत् he went, ताम् that, एव indeed, शोचतः lamenting, सीताम् for Sita, सा that, व्यतीयाय passed away, शर्वरी night.
explanation: Having made this decision and accepted Kusha and Lava, Rama dismissed the crowd and returned to his hermitage, where that night passed as he grieved for Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 98 ।। Thus ends the ninety-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रजन्यां तु प्रभातायां समानीय महामुनीन् । गीयतामविशङ्काभ्यां रामः पुत्रावुवाच ह ।। 7.99.1 ।।
transliteration: rajanyāṃ tu prabhātāyāṃ samānīya mahāmunīn | gīyatāmaviśaṅkābhyāṃ rāmaḥ putrāvuvāca ha || 7.99.1 ||
translation: रजन्याम् in the night, तु and, प्रभातायाम् having dawned, समानीय having assembled, महामुनीन् the great sages, गीयताम् let it be sung, अविशङ्काभ्याम् fearlessly, रामः Rama, पुत्रौ to his sons, उवाच said, ह indeed.
explanation: When the night dawned, Rama assembled the great sages and instructed his sons, Kusha and Lava, to sing the Ramayana fearlessly.
comments: Next day Kusha and Lava sing the future portion of the poem -- bereft of Sita, Rama concludes the sacrifice and returns to Ayodhya, taking no other wife but a golden image of Sita for every rite, and over ten thousand years performs many sacrifices in a reign free of death and disease -- in time his mothers Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi pass to heaven and are reunited with Dasharatha.

shloka_text: ततः समुपविष्टेषु ब्रह्मर्षिषु महात्मसु । भविष्यदुत्तरं काव्यं जगतुस्तौ कुशीलवौ ।। 7.99.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ samupaviṣṭeṣu brahmarṣiṣu mahātmasu | bhaviṣyaduttaraṃ kāvyaṃ jagatustau kuśīlavau || 7.99.2 ||
translation: ततः then, समुपविष्टेषु when they were seated, ब्रह्मर्षिषु the Brahmarishis, महात्मसु the great-souled ones, भविष्यत् future, उत्तरम् latter part, काव्यम् the epic, जगतुः they sang, तौ those two, कुशीलवौ Kusha and Lava.
explanation: Then, as the great-souled Brahmarishis were seated, Kusha and Lava sang the future, latter part of the epic.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टायां तु सीतायां भूतलं सत्यसम्पदा । तस्यावसाने यज्ञस्य रामः परमदुर्मनाः ।। 7.99.3 ।।
transliteration: praviṣṭāyāṃ tu sītāyāṃ bhūtalaṃ satyasampadā | tasyāvasāne yajñasya rāmaḥ paramadurmanāḥ || 7.99.3 ||
translation: प्रविष्टायाम् when she entered, तु and, सीतायाम् Sita, भूतलम् the earth, सत्यसम्पदा by the power of her truth, तस्य of that, अवसाने at the conclusion, यज्ञस्य of the sacrifice, रामः Rama, परमदुर्मनाः extremely distressed.
explanation: And when Sita entered the earth by the power of her truth, at the conclusion of that sacrifice, Rama became extremely distressed.

shloka_text: अपश्यमानो वैदेहीं मेने शून्यमिदं जगत् । शोकेन परमायस्तो न शान्तिं मनसा ऽगमत् ।। 7.99.4 ।।
transliteration: apaśyamāno vaidehīṃ mene śūnyamidaṃ jagat | śokena paramāyasto na śāntiṃ manasā 'gamat || 7.99.4 ||
translation: अपश्यमानो not seeing, वैदेहीं Vaidehi, मेने he considered, शून्यम् empty, इदं this, जगत् world, शोकेन by sorrow, परमायस्तो greatly distressed, न not, शान्तिं peace, मनसा in mind, अगमत् he attained.
explanation: Unable to see Vaidehi, he considered this world empty, and being greatly distressed by sorrow, he could not attain peace of mind.

shloka_text: विसृज्य पार्थिवान्सर्वानृक्षवानरराक्षसान् । जनौघं विप्रमुख्यानां वित्तपूर्वं विसृज्य च ।। 7.99.5 ।।
transliteration: visṛjya pārthivānsarvānṛkṣavānararākṣasān | janaughaṃ vipramukhyānāṃ vittapūrvaṃ visṛjya ca || 7.99.5 ||
translation: विसृज्य having dismissed, पार्थिवान् kings, सर्वान् all, ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान् bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, जनौघं multitude of people, विप्रमुख्यानां of chief Brahmins, वित्तपूर्वं with gifts of wealth, विसृज्य having dismissed, च and.
explanation: Having dismissed all the kings, bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, and also having sent away the multitude of chief Brahmins with gifts of wealth.

shloka_text: एवं समाप्य यज्ञं तु विधिवत्स तु राघवः । ततो विसृज्य तान्सर्वान्रामो राजीवलोचनः ।। 7.99.6 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ samāpya yajñaṃ tu vidhivatsa tu rāghavaḥ | tato visṛjya tānsarvānrāmo rājīvalocanaḥ || 7.99.6 ||
translation: एवं thus, समाप्य having concluded, यज्ञं the sacrifice, तु indeed, विधिवत् according to rites, स he, तु indeed, राघवः Rama, ततो then, विसृज्य having dismissed, तान् them, सर्वान् all, रामः Rama, राजीवलोचनः lotus-eyed.
explanation: Thus, having properly concluded the sacrifice, that Rama, the descendant of Raghu, the lotus-eyed, then dismissed all of them.

shloka_text: हृदि कृत्वा तदा सीतामयोध्यां प्रविवेश ह । इष्टयज्ञो नरपतिः पुत्रद्वयसमन्वितः ।। 7.99.7 ।।
transliteration: hṛdi kṛtvā tadā sītāmayodhyāṃ praviveśa ha | iṣṭayajño narapatiḥ putradvayasamanvitaḥ || 7.99.7 ||
translation: हृदि in his heart, कृत्वा having placed, तदा then, सीताम् Sita, अयोध्यां Ayodhya, प्रविवेश he entered, ह indeed, इष्टयज्ञो one who has performed sacrifices, नरपतिः king, पुत्रद्वयसमन्वितः accompanied by two sons.
explanation: Then, keeping Sita in his heart, that king, who had performed sacrifices and was accompanied by his two sons, entered Ayodhya.

shloka_text: न सीतायाः परां भार्यां वव्रे स रघुनन्दनः । यज्ञे यज्ञे च पत्न्यर्थं जानकी काञ्चनी भवत् ।। 7.99.8 ।।
transliteration: na sītāyāḥ parāṃ bhāryāṃ vavre sa raghunandanaḥ | yajñe yajñe ca patnyarthaṃ jānakī kāñcanī bhavat || 7.99.8 ||
translation: न not, सीतायाः than Sita, परां another, भार्यां wife, वव्रे he chose, स he, रघुनन्दनः Rama, यज्ञे in sacrifice, यज्ञे in sacrifice, च and, पत्न्यर्थं as a wife, जानकी Janaki, काञ्चनी golden, भवत् she was.
explanation: That Rama, the delight of Raghu, did not choose another wife besides Sita, and in every sacrifice, a golden image of Janaki served as his wife.

shloka_text: दशवर्षसहस्राणि वाजिमेघानथाकरोत् । वाजपेयान्दशगुणांस्तथा बहुसुवर्णकान् ।। 7.99.9 ।।
transliteration: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vājimeghānathākarot | vājapeyāndaśaguṇāṃstathā bahusuvarṇakān || 7.99.9 ||
translation: दशवर्षसहस्राणि ten thousand years, वाजिमेघान् Ashwamedha sacrifices, अथ then, अकरोत् he performed, वाजपेयान् Vajapeya sacrifices, दशगुणान् ten times (more), तथा and, बहुसुवर्णकान् with much gold.
explanation: For ten thousand years, he performed Ashwamedha sacrifices, and also Vajapeya sacrifices that were ten times grander and involved abundant gold.

shloka_text: अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां गोसवैश्च महाधनैः । ईजे क्रतुभिरन्यैश्च स श्रीमानाप्तदक्षिणैः ।। 7.99.10 ।।
transliteration: agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ gosavaiśca mahādhanaiḥ | īje kratubhiranyaiśca sa śrīmānāptadakṣiṇaiḥ || 7.99.10 ||
translation: अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्याम् with Agnishtoma and Atiratra (sacrifices), गोसवैः with Gosava sacrifices, च and, महाधनैः with great wealth, ईजे he performed sacrifices, क्रतुभिः with sacrifices, अन्यैः other, च and, सः he, श्रीमान् the glorious one, आप्तदक्षिणैः with ample dakshina.
explanation: The glorious Rama performed other sacrifices like Agnishtoma, Atiratra, and Gosava, which were accompanied by great wealth and ample gifts.

shloka_text: एवं स कालः सुमहान्राज्यस्थस्य महात्मनः । धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य व्यतीयाद्राघवस्य तु ।। 7.99.11 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa kālaḥ sumahānrājyasthasya mahātmanaḥ | dharme prayatamānasya vyatīyādrāghavasya tu || 7.99.11 ||
translation: एवम् thus, सः that, कालः time, सुमहान् very great, राज्यस्थस्य of him ruling the kingdom, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, धर्मे in righteousness, प्रयतमानस्य striving, व्यतीयात् passed away, राघवस्य of Rama, तु indeed.
explanation: Thus, a very long period of time passed for the great-souled Rama, who was established in his kingdom and constantly striving in righteousness.

shloka_text: अनुरञ्जन्ति राजानमहन्यहनि राघवम् । ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि स्थिता रामस्य शासने ।। 7.99.12 ।।
transliteration: anurañjanti rājānamahanyahani rāghavam | ṛkṣavānararakṣāṃsi sthitā rāmasya śāsane || 7.99.12 ||
translation: अनुरञ्जन्ति they pleased, राजानम् the king, अहन्यहनि day by day, राघवम् Rama, ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, स्थिता abiding, रामस्य of Rama, शासने in the command.
explanation: Day by day, the bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, abiding by Rama's command, continued to please King Rama.

shloka_text: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः सुभिक्षं विमला दिशः । हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं पुरं जनपदास्तथा ।। 7.99.13 ।।
transliteration: kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ subhikṣaṃ vimalā diśaḥ | hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇaṃ puraṃ janapadāstathā || 7.99.13 ||
translation: काले at the proper time, वर्षति rains, पर्जन्यः the rain-god, सुभिक्षम् good harvest, विमलाः clear, दिशः directions, हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णम् filled with happy and well-nourished people, पुरम् the city, जनपदाः the districts, तथा and.
explanation: The rain-god rained at the proper time, there was an abundance of food, the directions were clear, and the city and its districts were filled with happy and well-nourished people.

shloka_text: नाकाले म्रियते कश्चिन्न व्याधिः प्राणिनां तथा । नानर्थो विद्यते कश्चिद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ।। 7.99.14 ।।
transliteration: nākāle mriyate kaścinna vyādhiḥ prāṇināṃ tathā | nānartho vidyate kaścidrāme rājyaṃ praśāsati || 7.99.14 ||
translation: नाकाले at an untimely moment, म्रियते dies, कश्चित् anyone, न not, व्याधिः disease, प्राणिनां of living beings, तथा similarly, न not, अनर्थः misfortune, विद्यते exists, कश्चित् any, रामे when Rama, राज्यं the kingdom, प्रशासति was ruling.
explanation: When Rama was ruling the kingdom, no one died an untimely death, nor did any disease afflict living beings, nor did any misfortune exist.

shloka_text: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राममाता यशस्विनी । पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृता कालधर्ममुपागमत् ।। 7.99.15 ।।
transliteration: atha dīrghasya kālasya rāmamātā yaśasvinī | putrapautraiḥ parivṛtā kāladharmamupāgamat || 7.99.15 ||
translation: अथ thereafter, दीर्घस्य of a long, कालस्य period, राममाता Rama's mother (Kausalya), यशस्विनी the illustrious one, पुत्रपौत्रैः by sons and grandsons, परिवृता surrounded, कालधर्मम् the law of time (death), उपागमत् attained.
explanation: After a long period, the illustrious Kausalya, Rama's mother, surrounded by her sons and grandsons, attained the law of time, meaning she passed away.

shloka_text: अन्वियाय सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च यशस्विनी । धर्मं कृत्वा बहुविधं त्रिदिवे पर्यवस्थिता ।। 7.99.16 ।।
transliteration: anviyāya sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca yaśasvinī | dharmaṃ kṛtvā bahuvidhaṃ tridive paryavasthitā || 7.99.16 ||
translation: अन्वियाय followed, सुमित्रा Sumitra, च and, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, च and, यशस्विनी the illustrious one, धर्मं meritorious deeds, कृत्वा having performed, बहुविधं various kinds of, त्रिदिवे in heaven, पर्यवस्थिता resided.
explanation: Sumitra and the illustrious Kaikeyi also followed, and having performed various kinds of meritorious deeds, they resided in heaven.

shloka_text: सर्वाः प्रमुदिताः स्वर्गे राज्ञा दशरथेन च । समागता महाभागाः सर्वधर्मं च लेभिरे ।। 7.99.17 ।।
transliteration: sarvāḥ pramuditāḥ svarge rājñā daśarathena ca | samāgatā mahābhāgāḥ sarvadharmaṃ ca lebhire || 7.99.17 ||
translation: सर्वाः all of them, प्रमुदिताः greatly delighted, स्वर्गे in heaven, राज्ञा with King, दशरथेन Dasharatha, च and, समागताः having reunited, महाभागाः the greatly fortunate ones, सर्वधर्मं all righteousness/merit, च and, लेभिरे obtained.
explanation: All those greatly fortunate queens, reunited with King Dasharatha in heaven, were greatly delighted and obtained all righteousness.

shloka_text: तासां रामो महादानं काले काले प्रयच्छति । मातऽणामविशेषेण ब्राह्मणेषु तपस्विषु ।। 7.99.18 ।।
transliteration: tāsāṃ rāmo mahādānaṃ kāle kāle prayacchati | māta'ṇāmaviśeṣeṇa brāhmaṇeṣu tapasviṣu || 7.99.18 ||
translation: तासां for them, रामः Rama, महादानं great gifts, काले काले from time to time, प्रयच्छति gives, मातॄणाम् for the mothers, अविशेषेण without distinction, ब्राह्मणेषु to Brahmins, तपस्विषु to ascetics.
explanation: Rama regularly gives great gifts for his mothers, without distinction, to Brahmins and ascetics.

shloka_text: पित्र्याणि ब्रह्मरत्नानि यज्ञान्परमदुस्तरान् । चकार रामो धर्मात्मा पितऽन्देवान्विवर्धयन् ।। 7.99.19 ।।
transliteration: pitryāṇi brahmaratnāni yajñānparamadustarān | cakāra rāmo dharmātmā pita'ndevānvivardhayan || 7.99.19 ||
translation: पित्र्याणि ancestral, ब्रह्मरत्नानि excellent Vedic rituals, यज्ञान् sacrifices, परमदुस्तरान् extremely difficult to perform, चकार performed, रामो Rama, धर्मात्मा the righteous-souled, पितऽन् ancestors, देवान् gods, विवर्धयन् causing to prosper.
explanation: The righteous-souled Rama performed ancestral rites, excellent Vedic rituals, and extremely difficult sacrifices, thereby causing his ancestors and the gods to prosper.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि बहून्यथ ययुः सुखम् । यज्ञैर्बहुविधं धर्मं वर्धयानस्य सर्वदा ।। 7.99.20 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi bahūnyatha yayuḥ sukham | yajñairbahuvidhaṃ dharmaṃ vardhayānasya sarvadā || 7.99.20 ||
translation: एवम् thus, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, बहून्यथ many, then, ययुः passed, सुखम् happily, यज्ञैः by sacrifices, बहुविधम् various kinds of, धर्मम् righteousness, वर्धयानस्य of him who was increasing, सर्वदा always.
explanation: Thus, many thousands of years passed happily for him who was always increasing various kinds of righteousness through sacrifices. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनशततमः सर्गः ।। 99 ।। Thus ends the ninety-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य युधाजित्केकयो नृपः । स्वगुरुं प्रेषयामास राघवाय महात्मने । गार्ग्यमङ्गिरसः पुत्रं ब्रह्मर्षिममितप्रभम् ।। 7.100.1 ।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya yudhājitkekayo nṛpaḥ | svaguruṃ preṣayāmāsa rāghavāya mahātmane | gārgyamaṅgirasaḥ putraṃ brahmarṣimamitaprabham || 7.100.1 ||
translation: कस्यचित् some, त्वथ then, कालस्य of time, युधाजित् Yudhājit, केकयो Kekaya, नृपः king, स्वगुरुम् his own preceptor, प्रेषयामास sent, राघवाय to Rama, महात्मने to the great-souled one, गार्ग्यम् Gārgya, अङ्गिरसः of Angiras, पुत्रम् son, ब्रह्मर्षिम् a Brahmarshi, अमितप्रभम् of immeasurable splendor.
explanation: Then, after some time, King Yudhājit of Kekaya sent his own preceptor, Gārgya, the son of Angiras, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, to the great-souled Rama.
comments: King Yudhajit of Kekaya sends his preceptor Gargya with rich gifts, proposing that Rama conquer the beautiful Gandharva land on the banks of the Sindhu, held by three crore Gandharvas, sons of Shailusha -- Rama agrees and sends Bharata with his sons Taksha and Pushkala and an army to subdue them and found two cities, and the host, followed by flesh-eating creatures, marches to Kekaya.

shloka_text: दश चाश्वसहस्राणि प्रीतिदानमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.100.2 ।।
transliteration: daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi prītidānamanuttamam || 7.100.2 ||
translation: दश ten, च and, अश्वसहस्राणि thousands of horses, प्रीतिदानम् a gift of affection, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed.
explanation: And ten thousand horses, an unsurpassed gift of affection, were also sent.

shloka_text: कम्बलानि च रत्नानि चित्रवस्त्रमथोत्तमम् । रामाय प्रददौ राजा शुभान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.100.3 ।।
transliteration: kambalāni ca ratnāni citravastramathottamam | rāmāya pradadau rājā śubhānyābharaṇāni ca || 7.100.3 ||
translation: कम्बलानि blankets, च and, रत्नानि jewels, चित्रवस्त्रम् colorful garments, अथ then, उत्तमम् excellent, रामाय to Rama, प्रददौ gave, राजा the king, शुभानि auspicious, आभरणानि ornaments, च and.
explanation: The king also gave blankets, jewels, excellent colorful garments, and auspicious ornaments to Rama.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवो धीमान्महर्षिं गार्ग्यमागतम् । मातुलस्याश्वपतिनः प्रहितं तन्महाधनम् ।। 7.100.4 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu rāghavo dhīmānmaharṣiṃ gārgyamāgatam | mātulasyāśvapatinaḥ prahitaṃ tanmahādhanam || 7.100.4 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु and, राघवः Rama, धीमान् the intelligent, महर्षिम् the great sage, गार्ग्यम् Gargya, आगतम् who had arrived, मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle, अश्वपतिनः Ashvapati, प्रहितम् sent, तत् that, महाधनम् great wealth.
explanation: The intelligent Rama, having heard that the great sage Gargya, sent by his maternal uncle Ashvapati with great wealth, had arrived.

shloka_text: प्रत्युद्गम्य च काकुत्स्थः क्रोशमात्रं सहानुजः । गार्ग्यं सम्पूजयामास यथा शक्रो बृहस्पतिम् ।। 7.100.5 ।।
transliteration: pratyudgamya ca kākutsthaḥ krośamātraṃ sahānujaḥ | gārgyaṃ sampūjayāmāsa yathā śakro bṛhaspatim || 7.100.5 ||
translation: प्रत्युद्गम्य having gone forth to meet, च and, काकुत्स्थः Rama, क्रोशमात्रम् for a distance of a krosa, सहानुजः with his younger brothers, गार्ग्यम् Gargya, सम्पूजयामास honored greatly, यथा just as, शक्रः Indra, बृहस्पतिम् Brihaspati.
explanation: And Rama, along with his younger brothers, went forth for a krosa to meet Gargya and honored him greatly, just as Indra honors Brihaspati.

shloka_text: तथा सम्पूज्य तमृषिं तद्धनं प्रतिगृह्य च । पृष्ट्वा प्रतिपदं सर्वं कुशलं मातुलस्य च । उपविष्टं महाभागं रामः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.100.6 ।।
transliteration: tathā sampūjya tamṛṣiṃ taddhanaṃ pratigṛhya ca | pṛṣṭvā pratipadaṃ sarvaṃ kuśalaṃ mātulasya ca | upaviṣṭaṃ mahābhāgaṃ rāmaḥ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame || 7.100.6 ||
translation: तथा thus, सम्पूज्य having honored greatly, तम् that, ऋषिम् sage, तत् that, धनम् wealth, प्रतिगृह्य having received, च and, पृष्ट्वा having asked, प्रतिपदम् every detail, सर्वम् all, कुशलम् welfare, मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle, च and, उपविष्टम् seated, महाभागम् the highly fortunate one, रामः Rama, प्रष्टुम् to ask, प्रचक्रमे began.
explanation: Having thus greatly honored that sage, received the wealth, and inquired about every detail of his maternal uncle's welfare, Rama then began to question the highly fortunate sage who was now seated.

shloka_text: किमाह मातुलो वाक्यं यदर्थं भगवानिह । प्राप्तो वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः साक्षादिव बृहस्पतिः ।। 7.100.7 ।।
transliteration: kimāha mātulo vākyaṃ yadarthaṃ bhagavāniha | prāpto vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sākṣādiva bṛhaspatiḥ || 7.100.7 ||
translation: किम् what, आह said, मातुलः the maternal uncle, वाक्यम् message, यदर्थम् for which purpose, भगवान् the revered one, इह here, प्राप्तः arrived, वाक्यविदाम् among those skilled in speech, श्रेष्ठः the best, साक्षात् directly, इव as if, बृहस्पतिः Brihaspati.
explanation: Rama asked what message his maternal uncle had sent, for which purpose the revered sage, who is the best among those skilled in speech, had arrived here, as if Brihaspati himself.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः कार्यविस्तरम् । वक्तुमद्भुतसङ्काशं राघवायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.100.8 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā maharṣiḥ kāryavistaram | vaktumadbhutasaṅkāśaṃ rāghavāyopacakrame || 7.100.8 ||
translation: रामस्य Rama's, भाषितम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, महर्षिः the great sage, कार्यविस्तरम् the detailed matter, वक्तुम् to tell, अद्भुतसङ्काशम् wonderful, राघवाय to Rama, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, the great sage began to narrate the detailed and wonderful matter to Rama.

shloka_text: मातुलस्ते महाबाहो वाक्यमाह नरर्षभः । युधाजित्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रूयतां यदि रोचते ।। 7.100.9 ।।
transliteration: mātulaste mahābāho vākyamāha nararṣabhaḥ | yudhājitprītisaṃyuktaṃ śrūyatāṃ yadi rocate || 7.100.9 ||
translation: मातुलः maternal uncle, ते your, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, वाक्यम् words, आह said, नरर्षभः O best among men, युधाजित् Yudhājit, प्रीतिसंयुक्तम् filled with affection, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, यदि if, रोचते it pleases.
explanation: Yudhājit, your maternal uncle, O mighty-armed Rama, has spoken words filled with affection, which you should hear if they please you.

shloka_text: अयं गन्धर्वविषयः फलमूलोपशोभितः । सिन्धोरुभयतः पार्श्वे देशः परमशोभनः ।। 7.100.10 ।।
transliteration: ayaṃ gandharvaviṣayaḥ phalamūlopaśobhitaḥ | sindhorubhayataḥ pārśve deśaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ || 7.100.10 ||
translation: अयम् this, गन्धर्वविषयः region of Gandharvas, फलमूलोपशोभितः adorned with fruits and roots, सिन्धोः of the Sindhu (river), उभयतः on both sides, पार्श्वे on the banks, देशः region, परमशोभनः exceedingly beautiful.
explanation: This region of the Gandharvas, adorned with fruits and roots, lies on both banks of the Sindhu river and is exceedingly beautiful.

shloka_text: तं च रक्षन्ति गन्धर्वाः सायुधा युद्धकोविदाः । शैलूषस्य सुता वीर त्रिकोट्यो वै महाबलाः ।। 7.100.11 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ca rakṣanti gandharvāḥ sāyudhā yuddhakovidāḥ | śailūṣasya sutā vīra trikoṭyo vai mahābalāḥ || 7.100.11 ||
translation: तम् that, च and, रक्षन्ति protect, गन्धर्वाः Gandharvas, सायुधाः armed, युद्धकोविदाः skilled in warfare, शैलूषस्य of Shailūṣa, सुताः sons, वीर O hero, त्रिकोट्यः three crores, वै indeed, महाबलाः very powerful.
explanation: O hero, that region is protected by three crores of very powerful Gandharvas, the sons of Shailūṣa, who are armed and skilled in warfare.

shloka_text: तान्विनिर्जित्य काकुत्स्थ गन्धर्वनगरं शुभम् । निवेशय महाबोहो स्वे पुरे सुसमाहिते ।। 7.100.12 ।।
transliteration: tānvinirjitya kākutstha gandharvanagaraṃ śubham | niveśaya mahāboho sve pure susamāhite || 7.100.12 ||
translation: तान् them, विनिर्जित्य having conquered, काकुत्स्थ O descendant of Kakutstha, गन्धर्वनगरम् city of Gandharvas, शुभम् auspicious, निवेशय establish, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, स्वे your own, पुरे city, सुसमाहिते well-established.
explanation: O mighty-armed Rama, descendant of Kakutstha, having conquered those Gandharvas, establish your own well-governed and auspicious city in that Gandharva region.

shloka_text: अन्यस्य न गतिस्तत्र देशः परमशोभनः । रोचतां ते महाबाहो नाहं त्वामहितं वदे ।। 7.100.13 ।।
transliteration: anyasya na gatistatra deśaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ | rocatāṃ te mahābāho nāhaṃ tvāmahitaṃ vade || 7.100.13 ||
translation: अन्यस्य for anyone else, न not, गतिः access, तत्र there, देशः region, परमशोभनः exceedingly beautiful, रोचताम् let it please, ते you, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, न not, अहम् I, त्वाम् you, अहितम् harmful, वदे speak.
explanation: No one else has access to that exceedingly beautiful region; O mighty-armed one, may this proposal please you, for I would never speak anything harmful to you.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवः प्रीतो महर्षेर्मातुलस्य च । उवाच बाढमित्येव भरतं चान्ववैक्षत ।। 7.100.14 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rāghavaḥ prīto maharṣermātulasya ca | uvāca bāḍhamityeva bharataṃ cānvavaikṣata || 7.100.14 ||
translation: तत् that (proposal), श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवः Rama, प्रीतः pleased, महर्षेः of the great sage (Valmiki), मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle (Yudhajit), च and, उवाच said, बाढम् certainly, इति एव thus, भरतम् Bharata, च and, अन्ववैक्षत looked at.
explanation: Hearing the proposal from the great sage and his maternal uncle, Rama, pleased, agreed and then looked at Bharata.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीद्राघवः प्रीतः साञ्जलिप्रग्रहो द्विजम् । इमौ कुमारौ तं देशं ब्रह्मर्षे विचरिष्यतः ।। 7.100.15 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravīdrāghavaḥ prītaḥ sāñjalipragraho dvijam | imau kumārau taṃ deśaṃ brahmarṣe vicariṣyataḥ || 7.100.15 ||
translation: सः he, अब्रवीत् said, राघवः Rama, प्रीतः pleased, स-अञ्जलि-प्रग्रहः with folded hands, द्विजम् to the Brahmin (Valmiki), इमौ these two, कुमारौ princes, तम् that, देशम् region, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi (Valmiki), विचरिष्यतः will go forth/will rule.
explanation: Pleased, Rama, with folded hands, said to the Brahmarshi Valmiki, "O Brahmarshi, these two princes will go forth to that region."

shloka_text: भरतस्यात्मजौ वीरौ तक्षः पुष्कल एव च । मातुलेन सुगुप्तौ तु धर्मेण सुसमाहितौ ।। 7.100.16 ।।
transliteration: bharatasyātmajau vīrau takṣaḥ puṣkala eva ca | mātulena suguptau tu dharmeṇa susamāhitau || 7.100.16 ||
translation: भरतस्य of Bharata, आत्मजौ sons, वीरौ valiant, तक्षः Taksha, पुष्कलः Pushkala, एव indeed, च and, मातुलेन by the maternal uncle (Yudhajit), सुगुप्तौ well-protected, तु indeed, धर्मेण with righteousness, सुसमाहितौ well-established/well-trained.
explanation: These are Bharata's valiant sons, Taksha and Pushkala, who are well-protected by their maternal uncle and well-trained in righteousness.

shloka_text: भरतं चाग्रतः कृत्वा कुमारौ सबलानुगौ । निहत्य गन्धर्वसुतान्द्वे पुरे विभजिष्यतः ।। 7.100.17 ।।
transliteration: bharataṃ cāgrataḥ kṛtvā kumārau sabalānugau | nihatya gandharvasutāndve pure vibhajiṣyataḥ || 7.100.17 ||
translation: भरतम् Bharata, च and, अग्रतः in front, कृत्वा having placed/making, कुमारौ the two princes, स-बल-अनुगौ accompanied by an army, निहत्य having killed, गन्धर्व-सुतान् the sons of Gandharvas, द्वे two, पुरे cities, विभजिष्यतः will divide.
explanation: With Bharata leading, the two princes, accompanied by an army, will kill the sons of the Gandharvas and then establish two cities.

shloka_text: निवेश्य ते पुरवरे आत्मजौ सन्निवेश्य च । आगमिष्यति मे भूयः सकाशमतिधार्मिकः ।। 7.100.18 ।।
transliteration: niveśya te puravare ātmajau sanniveśya ca | āgamiṣyati me bhūyaḥ sakāśamatidhārmikaḥ || 7.100.18 ||
translation: निवेश्य having established, ते those, पुरवरे excellent cities, आत्मजौ his sons, सन्निवेश्य having settled, च and, आगमिष्यति will return, मे to me, भूयः again, सकाशम् to the presence, अतिधार्मिकः the very righteous one (Bharata).
explanation: Having established those excellent cities and settled his sons there, the very righteous Bharata will return to my presence again.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मर्षिमेवमुक्त्वा तु भरतं सबलानुगम् । आज्ञापयामास तदा कुमारौ चाभ्यषेचयत् ।। 7.100.19 ।।
transliteration: brahmarṣimevamuktvā tu bharataṃ sabalānugam | ājñāpayāmāsa tadā kumārau cābhyaṣecayat || 7.100.19 ||
translation: ब्रह्मर्षिम् the Brahmarshi, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken to, तु indeed, भरतम् Bharata, सबलानुगम् with his army and followers, आज्ञापयामास commanded, तदा then, कुमारौ the two princes, च and, अभ्यषेचयत् consecrated.
explanation: Having thus spoken to the Brahmarshi Vashistha, Rama then commanded Bharata, who was accompanied by his army and followers, and consecrated the two princes.

shloka_text: नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरस्सुतम् । भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां विनिर्ययौ ।। 7.100.20 ।।
transliteration: nakṣatreṇa ca saumyena puraskṛtyāṅgirassutam | bharataḥ saha sainyena kumārābhyāṃ viniryayau || 7.100.20 ||
translation: नक्षत्रेण by the constellation, च and, सौम्येन auspicious, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front (honoring), अङ्गिरस्सुतम् the son of Angiras (Vashistha), भरतः Bharata, सह with, सैन्येन the army, कुमाराभ्याम् with the two princes, विनिर्ययौ set out.
explanation: Bharata, honoring Vashistha (the son of Angiras) and choosing an auspicious constellation, set out with his army and the two princes.

shloka_text: सा सेना शक्रयुक्तेव नगरान्निर्ययावथ । राघवानुगता दूरं दुराधर्षा सुरैरपि ।। 7.100.21 ।।
transliteration: sā senā śakrayukteva nagarānniryayāvatha | rāghavānugatā dūraṃ durādharṣā surairapi || 7.100.21 ||
translation: सा that, सेना army, शक्रयुक्ता accompanied by Indra, इव as if, नगरान् from the city, निर्ययाव departed, अथ then, राघवानुगता following the Raghava (Bharata), दूरम् far, दुराधर्षा unconquerable, सुरैः by gods, अपि even.
explanation: That army, as if accompanied by Indra, then departed far from the city, following Bharata, and was unconquerable even by the gods.

shloka_text: मांसादानि च सत्त्वानि रक्षांसि सुमहान्ति च । अनुजग्मुर्हि भरतं रुधिरस्य पिपासया ।। 7.100.22 ।।
transliteration: māṃsādāni ca sattvāni rakṣāṃsi sumahānti ca | anujagmurhi bharataṃ rudhirasya pipāsayā || 7.100.22 ||
translation: मांसादानि flesh-eating, च and, सत्त्वानि beings, रक्षांसि Rakshasas, सुमहान्ति very great, च and, अनुजग्मुः followed, हि indeed, भरतम् Bharata, रुधिरस्य of blood, पिपासया with a thirst.
explanation: Indeed, flesh-eating creatures and very great Rakshasas followed Bharata, driven by a thirst for blood.

shloka_text: भूतग्रामाश्च बहवो मांसभक्षाः सुदारुणाः । गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि भोक्तुकामाः सहस्रशः ।। 7.100.23 ।।
transliteration: bhūtagrāmāśca bahavo māṃsabhakṣāḥ sudāruṇāḥ | gandharvaputramāṃsāni bhoktukāmāḥ sahasraśaḥ || 7.100.23 ||
translation: भूतग्रामाः hosts of beings, च and, बहवः many, मांसभक्षाः flesh-eaters, सुदारुणाः very terrible, गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि the flesh of the Gandharva princes, भोक्तुकामाः desirous of eating, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: And many thousands of very terrible flesh-eating spirits, desirous of consuming the flesh of the Gandharva princes, also followed.

shloka_text: सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां खेचराणां च पक्षिणाम् । बहूनि वै सहस्राणि सेनाया ययुरग्रतः ।। 7.100.24 ।।
transliteration: siṃhavyāghravarāhāṇāṃ khecarāṇāṃ ca pakṣiṇām | bahūni vai sahasrāṇi senāyā yayuragrataḥ || 7.100.24 ||
translation: सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां of lions, tigers, and boars, खेचराणां of sky-dwellers, च and, पक्षिणाम् of birds, बहूनि many, वै indeed, सहस्राणि thousands, सेनायाः of the army, ययुः went, अग्रतः in front.
explanation: Many thousands of lions, tigers, boars, and various birds marched in front of the army.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धमासमुषिता पथि सेना निरामया । हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा केकयं समुपागमत् ।। 7.100.25 ।।
transliteration: adhyardhamāsamuṣitā pathi senā nirāmayā | hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā kekayaṃ samupāgamat || 7.100.25 ||
translation: अध्यर्धमासमुषिता having stayed for one and a half months, पथि on the path, सेना the army, निरामया healthy, हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा filled with joyful and well-nourished people, केकयं to Kekaya, समुपागमत् arrived.
explanation: After staying on the road for one and a half months, the army, healthy and filled with joyful and well-nourished people, arrived in Kekaya. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे शततमः सर्गः ।। 100 ।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः । युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत् ।। 7.101.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā senāpatiṃ prāptaṃ bharataṃ kekayādhipaḥ | yudhājidgārgyasahitaṃ parāṃ prītimupāgamat || 7.101.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, सेनापतिं the commander, प्राप्तं arrived, भरतं Bharata, केकयाधिपः the king of Kekaya, युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं accompanied by Yudhajit and Gargya, परां great, प्रीतिम् joy, उपागमत् attained.
explanation: Having heard that Commander Bharata had arrived, the King of Kekaya, accompanied by Yudhajit and Gargya, attained great joy.
comments: Bharata and Yudhajit reach the Gandharva city, and after a seven-night battle Bharata looses the dread Samvarta weapon of Time and slays three crore Gandharvas in an instant -- he founds two cities in Gandhara, Takshashila for Taksha and Pushkalavati for Pushkala, and after five years returns to report to Rama, who is pleased.

shloka_text: स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः । त्वरमाणो ऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान्कामरूपिणः ।। 7.101.2 ।।
transliteration: sa niryayau janaughena mahatā kekayādhipaḥ | tvaramāṇo 'bhicakrāma gandharvānkāmarūpiṇaḥ || 7.101.2 ||
translation: सः he, निर्ययौ went out, जनौघेन with a multitude of people, महता great, केकयाधिपः the king of Kekaya, त्वरमाणो hurrying, अभिचक्राम approached, गन्धर्वान् the Gandharvas, कामरूपिणः who could change their form at will.
explanation: The King of Kekaya went out with a great multitude of people, hurrying to approach the Gandharvas who could change their form at will.

shloka_text: भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमैः । गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ ।। 7.101.3 ।।
transliteration: bharataśca yudhājicca sametau laghuvikramaiḥ | gandharvanagaraṃ prāptau sabalau sapadānugau || 7.101.3 ||
translation: भरतश्च Bharata and, युधाजिच्च Yudhajit and, समेतौ together, लघुविक्रमैः with swift warriors, गन्धर्वनगरं to the city of the Gandharvas, प्राप्तौ arrived, सबलौ with their army, सपदानुगौ with their followers.
explanation: Bharata and Yudhajit, accompanied by swift warriors, arrived together at the city of the Gandharvas with their army and followers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः । योद्धुकामा महावीर्या व्यनदन् वै समन्ततः ।। 7.101.4 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu bharataṃ prāptaṃ gandharvāste samāgatāḥ | yoddhukāmā mahāvīryā vyanadan vai samantataḥ || 7.101.4 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, भरतम् Bharata, प्राप्तम् arrived, गन्धर्वाः the Gandharvas, ते those, समागताः assembled, योद्धुकामाः desirous of fighting, महावीर्याः of great valor, व्यनदन् roared, वै indeed, समन्ततः all around.
explanation: Having heard of Bharata's arrival, those mighty Gandharvas, eager to fight, assembled and roared from all directions.

shloka_text: ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् । सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः ।। 7.101.5 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam | saptarātraṃ mahābhīmaṃ na cānyatarayorjayaḥ || 7.101.5 ||
translation: ततः then, समभवत् occurred, युद्धम् a battle, तुमुलम् tumultuous, रोमहर्षणम् hair-raising, सप्तरात्रम् for seven nights, महाभीमम् exceedingly dreadful, न not, च and, अन्यतरयोः of either of the two, जयः victory.
explanation: Then, a tumultuous, hair-raising, and exceedingly dreadful battle ensued for seven nights, with neither side achieving victory.

shloka_text: खड्गशक्तिधनुर्ग्राहा नद्यः शोणितसंस्रवाः । नृकलेवरवाहिन्यः प्रवृत्ताः सर्वतोदिशम् ।। 7.101.6 ।।
transliteration: khaḍgaśaktidhanurgrāhā nadyaḥ śoṇitasaṃsravāḥ | nṛkalevaravāhinyaḥ pravṛttāḥ sarvatodiśam || 7.101.6 ||
translation: खड्ग swords, शक्ति spears, धनुः bows, ग्राहाः (like) alligators, नद्यः rivers, शोणित blood, संस्रवाः flowing, नृकलेवर human corpses, वाहिन्यः carrying, प्रवृत्ताः flowed, सर्वतोदिशम् in all directions.
explanation: Rivers of flowing blood, carrying human corpses and resembling streams with swords, spears, and bows as their aquatic creatures, flowed in all directions.

shloka_text: ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम् । संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्यचोदयत् ।। 7.101.7 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmānujaḥ kruddhaḥ kālasyāstraṃ sudāruṇam | saṃvartaṃ nāma bharato gandharveṣvabhyacodayat || 7.101.7 ||
translation: ततः then, रामानुजः Rama's younger brother, क्रुद्धः enraged, कालस्य of Time, अस्त्रम् weapon, सुदारुणम् exceedingly terrible, संवर्तम् Samvarta, नाम named, भरतः Bharata, गन्धर्वेषु upon the Gandharvas, अभ्यचोदयत् discharged.
explanation: Then, the enraged Bharata, Rama's younger brother, discharged the exceedingly terrible weapon of Time, named Samvarta, upon the Gandharvas.

shloka_text: ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः । क्षणेनाभिहतास्तेन तिस्रः कोट्यो महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.8 ।।
transliteration: te baddhāḥ kālapāśena saṃvartena vidāritāḥ | kṣaṇenābhihatāstena tisraḥ koṭyo mahātmanām || 7.101.8 ||
translation: ते they, बद्धाः bound, कालपाशेन by the noose of Time, संवर्तेन by Samvarta, विदारिताः torn apart, क्षणेन in a moment, अभिहताः struck down, तेन by him, तिस्रः three, कोट्यः crores, महात्मनाम् of mighty ones.
explanation: Bound by the noose of Time and torn apart by the Samvarta weapon, three crores of those mighty Gandharvas were instantly struck down by Bharata.

shloka_text: तं घातं घोरसङ्काशं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.9 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ghātaṃ ghorasaṅkāśaṃ na smaranti divaukasaḥ | nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tādṛśānāṃ mahātmanām || 7.101.9 ||
translation: तं that, घातं destruction, घोरसङ्काशं terrible-looking, न not, स्मरन्ति remember, दिवौकसः gods, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण within the mere twinkling of an eye, तादृशानाम् of such, महात्मनाम् great souls.
explanation: The gods do not even remember that terrible destruction of those great souls (Gandharvas), as it occurred within the mere twinkling of an eye.

shloka_text: हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु भरतः केकयीसुतः । निवेशयामास तदा समृद्धे द्वे पुरोत्तमे ।। 7.101.10 ।।
transliteration: hateṣu teṣu sarveṣu bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ | niveśayāmāsa tadā samṛddhe dve purottame || 7.101.10 ||
translation: हतेषु having been killed, तेषु those, सर्वेषु all, भरतः Bharata, केकयीसुतः son of Kaikeyi, निवेशयामास established, तदा then, समृद्धे prosperous, द्वे two, पुरोत्तमे excellent cities.
explanation: After all those (Gandharvas) were killed, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, then established two prosperous and excellent cities.

shloka_text: तक्षं तक्षशिलायां तु पुष्कलं पुष्कलावते । गन्धर्वदेशे रुचिरे गान्धारविषये च सः ।। 7.101.11 ।।
transliteration: takṣaṃ takṣaśilāyāṃ tu puṣkalaṃ puṣkalāvate | gandharvadeśe rucire gāndhāraviṣaye ca saḥ || 7.101.11 ||
translation: तक्षं Taksha (son of Bharata), तक्षशिलायां in Takshashila, तु and, पुष्कलम् Pushkala (son of Bharata), पुष्कलावते in Pushkalavati, गन्धर्वदेशे in the land of Gandharvas, रुचिरे beautiful, गान्धारविषये in the region of Gandhara, च and, सः he (Bharata).
explanation: He (Bharata) established Taksha in Takshashila and Pushkala in Pushkalavati, both in the beautiful land of Gandharvas, which is the region of Gandhara.

shloka_text: धनरत्नौघसङ्कीर्णे काननैरुपशोभिते । अन्योन्यसङ्घर्षकृते स्पर्धया गुणविस्तरैः ।। 7.101.12 ।।
transliteration: dhanaratnaughasaṅkīrṇe kānanairupaśobhite | anyonyasaṅgharṣakṛte spardhayā guṇavistaraiḥ || 7.101.12 ||
translation: धनरत्नौघसङ्कीर्णे filled with heaps of wealth and jewels, काननैरुपशोभिते adorned with forests, अन्योन्यसङ्घर्षकृते causing mutual rivalry, स्पर्धया with competition, गुणविस्तरैः with extensive qualities.
explanation: These cities were filled with heaps of wealth and jewels, adorned with forests, and their extensive qualities caused mutual rivalry and competition.

shloka_text: उभे सुरुचिरप्रख्ये व्यवहारैरकिल्बिषैः । उद्यानयानसम्पूर्णे सुविभक्तान्तरापणे ।। 7.101.13 ।।
transliteration: ubhe suruciraprakhye vyavahārairakilbiṣaiḥ | udyānayānasampūrṇe suvibhaktāntarāpaṇe || 7.101.13 ||
translation: उभे both, सुरुचिरप्रख्ये very beautiful in appearance, व्यवहारैरकिल्बिषैः with blameless transactions, उद्यानयानसम्पूर्णे full of gardens and conveyances, सुविभक्तान्तरापणे with well-divided inner markets.
explanation: Both cities were very beautiful in appearance, characterized by blameless transactions, full of gardens and conveyances, and had well-divided inner markets.

shloka_text: उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते । गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानसमवर्णिभिः ।। 7.101.14 ।।
transliteration: ubhe puravare ramye vistarairupaśobhite | gṛhamukhyaiḥ surucirairvimānasamavarṇibhiḥ || 7.101.14 ||
translation: उभे both, पुरवरे excellent cities, रम्ये beautiful, विस्तरैः with extensive areas, उपशोभिते adorned, गृहमुख्यैः with principal houses, सुरुचिरैः very charming, विमानसमवर्णिभिः resembling celestial chariots in appearance.
explanation: Both beautiful and excellent cities were adorned with extensive areas, featuring principal houses that were very charming and resembled celestial chariots.

shloka_text: शोभिते शोभनीयैश्च देवायतनविस्तरैः । तालैस्तमालैस्तिलकैर्वकुलैरुपशोभिते ।। 7.101.15 ।।
transliteration: śobhite śobhanīyaiśca devāyatanavistaraiḥ | tālaistamālaistilakairvakulairupaśobhite || 7.101.15 ||
translation: शोभिते adorned, शोभनीयैः with beautiful ones, च and, देवायतनविस्तरैः with extensive temples, तालैः with palm trees, तमालैः with tamala trees, तिलकैर with tilaka trees, वकुलैः with vakula trees, उपशोभिते adorned.
explanation: The cities were further adorned with beautiful and extensive temples, as well as with palm, tamala, tilaka, and vakula trees.

shloka_text: निवेश्य पञ्चभिर्वर्षैर्भरतो राघवानुजः । पुनरायान्महाबाहुरयोध्यां केकयीसुतः ।। 7.101.16 ।।
transliteration: niveśya pañcabhirvarṣairbharato rāghavānujaḥ | punarāyānmahābāhurayodhyāṃ kekayīsutaḥ || 7.101.16 ||
translation: निवेश्य having established, पञ्चभिः by five, वर्षैः years, भरतः Bharata, राघवानुजः Rama's younger brother, पुनरायात् returned, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, केकयीसुतः Kaikeyi's son.
explanation: After establishing the cities over a period of five years, Bharata, the mighty-armed son of Kaikeyi and younger brother of Rama, returned to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम् । राघवं भरतः श्रीमान्ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः ।। 7.101.17 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ sākṣāddharmamivāparam | rāghavaṃ bharataḥ śrīmānbrahmāṇamiva vāsavaḥ || 7.101.17 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, महात्मानम् the great-souled one, साक्षात् directly, धर्मम् Dharma, इव like, अपरम् another, राघवम् Rama, भरतः Bharata, श्रीमान् the glorious, ब्रह्माणम् Brahma, इव like, वासवः Indra.
explanation: The glorious Bharata, like Indra saluting Brahma, saluted the great-souled Rama, who was like another embodiment of Dharma itself.

shloka_text: शशंस च यथावृत्तं गन्धर्ववधमुत्तमम् । निवेशनं च देशस्य श्रुत्वा प्रीतो ऽस्य राघवः ।। 7.101.18 ।।
transliteration: śaśaṃsa ca yathāvṛttaṃ gandharvavadhamuttamam | niveśanaṃ ca deśasya śrutvā prīto 'sya rāghavaḥ || 7.101.18 ||
translation: शशंस he reported, च and, यथावृत्तम् the full account, गन्धर्ववधम् the slaying of the Gandharvas, उत्तमम् excellent, निवेशनम् the establishment, च and, देशस्य of the region, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रीतः pleased, अस्य his, राघवः Rama.
explanation: Bharata reported the full account of the excellent slaying of the Gandharvas and the establishment of the region, and upon hearing this, Rama was pleased with him. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 101 ।। Thus ends the hundred and first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमापेदे राघवो भ्रातृभिः सह । वाक्यं चाद्भुतसङ्काशं तदा प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणम् ।। 7.102.1 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā harṣamāpede rāghavo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha | vākyaṃ cādbhutasaṅkāśaṃ tadā provāca lakṣmaṇam || 7.102.1 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, हर्षम् joy, आपेदे attained, राघवः Rama, भ्रातृभिः with brothers, सह together, वाक्यम् words, च and, अद्भुतसङ्काशम् wonderful-like, तदा then, प्रोवाच spoke, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana.
explanation: Having heard that, Rama, along with his brothers, felt great joy and then spoke amazing words to Lakshmana.
comments: Rama resolves to give kingdoms to Lakshmana's sons Angada and Chandraketu, settling them at Bharata's counsel in the peaceful Karupatha land -- he founds Angadiya for Angada and Chandrakanta in the Malla country for Chandraketu, whom Lakshmana and Bharata escort to their realms before returning -- and ten thousand years pass, the three brothers shining like three sacred fires.

shloka_text: इमौ कुमारौ सौमित्रे तव धर्मविशारदौ । अङ्गदश्चन्द्रकेतुश्च राज्यार्थे दृढविक्रमौ ।। 7.102.2 ।।
transliteration: imau kumārau saumitre tava dharmaviśāradau | aṅgadaścandraketuśca rājyārthe dṛḍhavikramau || 7.102.2 ||
translation: इमौ these two, कुमारौ sons, सौमित्रे O Lakshmana, तव your, धर्मविशारदौ expert in righteousness, अङ्गदः Angada, चन्द्रकेतुः Chandraketu, च and, राज्यार्थे for the sake of kingdom, दृढविक्रमौ of firm valor.
explanation: O Lakshmana, these two sons of yours, Angada and Chandraketu, are skilled in righteousness and possess firm valor suitable for kingship.

shloka_text: इमौ राज्ये ऽभिषेक्ष्यामि देशः साधु विधीयताम् । रमणीयो ह्यसम्बाधो रमेतां यत्र धन्विनौ ।। 7.102.3 ।।
transliteration: imau rājye 'bhiṣekṣyāmi deśaḥ sādhu vidhīyatām | ramaṇīyo hyasambādho rametāṃ yatra dhanvinau || 7.102.3 ||
translation: इमौ these two, राज्ये in the kingdom, अभिषेक्ष्यामि I shall enthrone, देशः a region, साधु properly, विधीयताम् let it be arranged, रमणीयः charming, हि indeed, असम्बाधः unobstructed, रमेताम् let them dwell happily, यत्र where, धन्विनौ the two archers.
explanation: I shall enthrone these two in a kingdom, so let a suitable, charming, and unobstructed region be prepared where these two archers can happily reside.

shloka_text: न राज्ञो यत्र पीडा स्यान्नाश्रमाणां विनाशनम् । स देशो दृश्यतां सौम्य नापराध्यामहे यथा ।। 7.102.4 ।।
transliteration: na rājño yatra pīḍā syānnāśramāṇāṃ vināśanam | sa deśo dṛśyatāṃ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā || 7.102.4 ||
translation: न not, राज्ञः of the king, यत्र where, पीडा suffering, स्यात् may be, न not, आश्रमाणां of the hermitages, विनाशनम् destruction, सः that, देशः region, दृश्यताम् let it be found, सौम्य O gentle one, न not, अपराध्यामहे we may err, यथा so that.
explanation: O gentle one, let a region be found where there is no oppression of kings or destruction of hermitages, so that we may not commit any fault.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह । अयं कारुपथो देशो रमणीयो निरामयः ।। 7.102.5 ।।
transliteration: tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha | ayaṃ kārupatho deśo ramaṇīyo nirāmayaḥ || 7.102.5 ||
translation: तथा thus, उक्तवति having spoken, रामे when Rama, तु indeed, भरतः Bharata, प्रत्युवाच replied, ह indeed, अयम् this, कारुपथः Karupatha, देशः region, रमणीयः charming, निरामयः peaceful.
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Bharata replied, "This region called Karupatha is charming and peaceful."

shloka_text: निवेश्यतां तत्र पुरमङ्गदस्य महात्मनः । चन्द्रकेतोः सुरुचिरं चन्द्रकान्तं निरामयम् ।। 7.102.6 ।।
transliteration: niveśyatāṃ tatra puramaṅgadasya mahātmanaḥ | candraketoḥ suruciraṃ candrakāntaṃ nirāmayam || 7.102.6 ||
translation: निवेश्यतां let it be established, तत्र there, पुरम् a city, अङ्गदस्य of Angada, महात्मनः the great-souled one, चन्द्रकेतोः of Chandraketu, सुरुचिरम् very beautiful, चन्द्रकान्तम् charming like the moon (or named Chandrakanta), निरामयम् free from disease.
explanation: Let a city be established there for the great-souled Angada and another, very beautiful, moon-charming, and healthy city for Chandraketu.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं भरतेनोक्तं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः । तं च कृत्वा वशे देशमङ्गदस्य न्यवेशयत् ।। 7.102.7 ।।
transliteration: tadvākyaṃ bharatenoktaṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ | taṃ ca kṛtvā vaśe deśamaṅgadasya nyaveśayat || 7.102.7 ||
translation: तत् that, वाक्यम् statement, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, प्रतिजग्राह accepted, राघवः Rama, तम् that, च and, कृत्वा having made, वशे under control, देशम् region, अङ्गदस्य for Angada, न्यवेशयत् he established.
explanation: Rama accepted that statement spoken by Bharata, and having brought that region under control, he established a city for Angada.

shloka_text: अङ्गदीया पुरी रम्याप्यङ्गदस्य निवेशिता । रमणीया सुगुप्ता च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।। 7.102.8 ।।
transliteration: aṅgadīyā purī ramyāpyaṅgadasya niveśitā | ramaṇīyā suguptā ca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā || 7.102.8 ||
translation: अङ्गदीया Angada's, पुरी city, रम्या beautiful, अपि also, अङ्गदस्य for Angada, निवेशिता established, रमणीया delightful, सुगुप्ता well-protected, च and, रामेण by Rama, अक्लिष्टकर्मणा whose deeds are effortless.
explanation: The beautiful city named Angadiya was established for Angada by Rama, whose deeds are effortless, and it was delightful and well-protected.

shloka_text: चन्द्रकेतोश्च मल्लस्य मल्लभूम्यां निवेशिता । चन्द्रकान्तेति विख्याता दिव्या स्वर्गपुरी यथा ।। 7.102.9 ।।
transliteration: candraketośca mallasya mallabhūmyāṃ niveśitā | candrakānteti vikhyātā divyā svargapurī yathā || 7.102.9 ||
translation: चन्द्रकेतोः for Chandraketu, च and, मल्लस्य of Malla, मल्लभूम्याम् in the land of Malla, निवेशिता established, चन्द्रकान्ता Chandrakanta, इति thus, विख्याता renowned, दिव्या divine, स्वर्गपुरी a city of heaven, यथा like.
explanation: And for Chandraketu, a city named Chandrakanta was established in the land of Malla, renowned as divine, just like a city of heaven.

shloka_text: ततो रामः परां प्रीतिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तथा । ययुर्युद्धे दुराधर्षा अभिषेकं च चक्रिरे ।। 7.102.10 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatastathā | yayuryuddhe durādharṣā abhiṣekaṃ ca cakrire || 7.102.10 ||
translation: ततः then, रामः Rama, परां great, प्रीतिम् joy, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, भरतः Bharata, तथा and, ययुः attained, युद्धे in battle, दुराधर्षाः unconquerable, अभिषेकं anointment, च and, चक्रिरे they performed.
explanation: Then Rama, Lakshmana, and Bharata, who were unconquerable in battle, attained great joy and performed the anointment.

shloka_text: अभिषिच्य कुमारौ स प्रस्थापयति राघवः । अङ्गदं पश्चिमां भूमिं चन्द्रकेतुमुदङ्मुखम् ।। 7.102.11 ।।
transliteration: abhiṣicya kumārau sa prasthāpayati rāghavaḥ | aṅgadaṃ paścimāṃ bhūmiṃ candraketumudaṅmukham || 7.102.11 ||
translation: अभिषिच्य having consecrated, कुमारौ the two princes, स he, प्रस्थापयति sends forth, राघवः Rama, अङ्गदं Angada, पश्चिमां to the western, भूमिं land, चन्द्रकेतुं Chandraketu, उदङ्मुखम् to the northern direction.
explanation: Having consecrated the two princes, Rama sent Angada to the western region and Chandraketu to the northern direction.

shloka_text: अङ्गदं चापि सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणो ऽनुजगाम ह । चन्द्रकेतोस्तु भरतः पार्ष्णिग्राहो बभूव ह ।। 7.102.12 ।।
transliteration: aṅgadaṃ cāpi saumitrirlakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha | candraketostu bharataḥ pārṣṇigrāho babhūva ha || 7.102.12 ||
translation: अङ्गदं Angada, च and, अपि also, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, अनुजगाम followed, ह indeed, चन्द्रकेतोस्तु but for Chandraketu, भरतः Bharata, पार्ष्णिग्राहो a supporter, बभूव became, ह indeed.
explanation: Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, followed Angada, and Bharata became Chandraketu's close supporter.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्त्वङ्गदीयायां संवत्सरमथोषितः । पुत्रे स्थिते दुराधर्षे अयोध्यां पुनरागमत् ।। 7.102.13 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇastvaṅgadīyāyāṃ saṃvatsaramathoṣitaḥ | putre sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṃ punarāgamat || 7.102.13 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणस्तु but Lakshmana, अङ्गदीयायां in Angada's territory, संवत्सरम् for a year, अथ then, उषितः having resided, पुत्रे his son, स्थिते having been established, दुराधर्षे unconquerable, अयोध्यां to Ayodhya, पुनः again, आगमत् returned.
explanation: Lakshmana, having resided for a year in Angada's territory until his unconquerable son was established, then returned to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: भरतो ऽपि तथैवोष्य संवत्सरमतो ऽधिकम् । अयोध्यां पुनरागम्य रामपादावुपास्त सः ।। 7.102.14 ।।
transliteration: bharato 'pi tathaivoṣya saṃvatsaramato 'dhikam | ayodhyāṃ punarāgamya rāmapādāvupāsta saḥ || 7.102.14 ||
translation: भरतो Bharata, अपि also, तथैव similarly, उष्य having resided, संवत्सरम् for a year, अतः than that, अधिकम् more, अयोध्यां to Ayodhya, पुनः again, आगम्य having returned, रामपादावुपास्त worshipped Rama's feet, सः he.
explanation: Bharata also, having similarly resided for more than a year, returned to Ayodhya and worshipped Rama's feet.

shloka_text: उभौ सौमित्रिभरतौ रामपादावनुव्रतौ । कालं गतमपि स्नेहान्न जज्ञाते ऽतिधार्मिकौ ।। 7.102.15 ।।
transliteration: ubhau saumitribharatau rāmapādāvanuvratau | kālaṃ gatamapi snehānna jajñāte 'tidhārmikau || 7.102.15 ||
translation: उभौ both, सौमित्रिभरतौ Lakshmana and Bharata, रामपादावनुव्रतौ devoted to Rama's feet, कालं time, गतमपि even passed, स्नेहात् due to affection, न not, जज्ञाते they knew, अतिधार्मिकौ extremely righteous.
explanation: Both Lakshmana and Bharata, being extremely righteous and devoted to Rama's feet, did not even perceive the passage of time due to their profound affection.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तेषां ययुस्तदा । धर्मे प्रयतमानानां पौरकार्येषु नित्यदा ।। 7.102.16 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa teṣāṃ yayustadā | dharme prayatamānānāṃ paurakāryeṣu nityadā || 7.102.16 ||
translation: एवं thus, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, दश ten, तेषां of them, ययुः passed, तदा then, धर्मे in righteousness, प्रयतमानानां of those striving, पौरकार्येषु in civic duties, नित्यदा always.
explanation: Thus, ten thousand years passed for them, who were constantly striving in righteousness and civic duties.

shloka_text: विहृत्य कालं परिपूर्णमानसाः श्रिया वृता धर्मपुरे सुसंस्थिताः । त्रयः समिद्धा इव दीप्ततेजसो महाध्वरे साधु हुतास्त्रयो ऽग्नयः ।। 7.102.17 ।।
transliteration: vihṛtya kālaṃ paripūrṇamānasāḥ śriyā vṛtā dharmapure susaṃsthitāḥ | trayaḥ samiddhā iva dīptatejaso mahādhvare sādhu hutāstrayo 'gnayaḥ || 7.102.17 ||
translation: विहृत्य having spent, कालं time, परिपूर्णमानसाः with minds completely satisfied, श्रिया with prosperity, वृताः endowed, धर्मपुरे in the city of dharma, सुसंस्थिताः well-established, त्रयः the three, समिद्धाः well-kindled, इव like, दीप्ततेजसः of blazing splendor, महाध्वरे in a great sacrifice, साधु properly, हुताः offered, त्रयः three, अग्नयः fires.
explanation: Having spent their time with fulfilled desires, endowed with prosperity, and well-established in the city of dharma, the three brothers shone like three well-kindled fires of blazing splendor, properly offered in a great sacrifice. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे व्द्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 102 ।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य रामे धर्मपरे स्थिते । कालस्तापसरूपेण राजद्वारमुपागमत् ।। 7.103.1 ।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya rāme dharmapare sthite | kālastāpasarūpeṇa rājadvāramupāgamat || 7.103.1 ||
translation: कस्यचित् of some, तु indeed, अथ then, कालस्य of time, रामे while Rama, धर्मपरे devoted to righteousness, स्थिते was abiding, कालः Time, तापसरूपेण in the form of an ascetic, राजद्वारम् to the royal gate, उपागमत् approached.
explanation: Then, after some time, while Rama was abiding devoted to righteousness, Time, in the form of an ascetic, approached the royal gate.
comments: Time himself, in the guise of an ascetic and bearing a message from a great sage, comes to Rama's gate and asks a secret audience on condition that whoever sees or hears it be put to death -- Rama consents, posts Lakshmana at the door under that very charge, and bids the messenger speak.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं धृतिमन्तं यशश्विनम् । मां निवेदय रामाय सम्प्राप्तं कार्यगौरवात् ।। 7.103.2 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravīllakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ dhṛtimantaṃ yaśaśvinam | māṃ nivedaya rāmāya samprāptaṃ kāryagauravāt || 7.103.2 ||
translation: सः he, अब्रवीत् spoke, लक्ष्मणं to Lakshmana, वाक्यं words, धृतिमन्तं resolute, यशश्विनम् glorious, मां me, निवेदय announce, रामाय to Rama, सम्प्राप्तं arrived, कार्यगौरवात् due to the importance of the matter.
explanation: He spoke to the resolute and glorious Lakshmana, saying, "Announce my arrival to Rama, as I have come due to the grave importance of my mission."

shloka_text: दूतो ऽस्म्यतिबलस्याहं महर्षेरमितौजसः । रामं दिदृक्षुरायातः कार्येण हि महाबल ।। 7.103.3 ।।
transliteration: dūto 'smyatibalasyāhaṃ maharṣeramitaujasaḥ | rāmaṃ didṛkṣurāyātaḥ kāryeṇa hi mahābala || 7.103.3 ||
translation: दूतः a messenger, अस्मि I am, अतिबलस्य of the very powerful, अहं I, महर्षेः of the great sage, अमितौजसः of immeasurable energy, रामं Rama, दिदृक्षुः desirous of seeing, आयातः arrived, कार्येण for a purpose, हि indeed, महाबल O mighty one.
explanation: "O mighty one, I am indeed a messenger of a very powerful great sage of immeasurable energy, and I have arrived desirous of seeing Rama for an important purpose."

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिस्त्वरया ऽन्वितः । न्यवेदयत रामाय तापसं तं समागतम् ।। 7.103.4 ।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saumitristvarayā 'nvitaḥ | nyavedayata rāmāya tāpasaṃ taṃ samāgatam || 7.103.4 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, वचनं word, श्रुत्वा having heard, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, त्वरया with haste, अन्वितः endowed, न्यवेदयत informed, रामाय to Rama, तापसं the ascetic, तं him, समागतम् arrived.
explanation: Having heard his words, Lakshmana, filled with haste, informed Rama about the arrival of that ascetic.

shloka_text: जयस्व राम धर्मेण उभौ लोकौ महाद्युते । दूतस्त्वां द्रष्टुमायातस्तपसा भास्करप्रभः ।। 7.103.5 ।।
transliteration: jayasva rāma dharmeṇa ubhau lokau mahādyute | dūtastvāṃ draṣṭumāyātastapasā bhāskaraprabhaḥ || 7.103.5 ||
translation: जयस्व conquer, राम O Rama, धर्मेण by righteousness, उभौ both, लोकौ worlds, महाद्युते O greatly radiant one, दूतः a messenger, त्वां you, द्रष्टुम् to see, आगतः has come, तपसा by penance, भास्करप्रभः radiant like the sun.
explanation: O greatly radiant Rama, conquer both worlds through righteousness; a messenger, radiant like the sun due to his penance, has arrived to see you.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं श्रुत्वा राम उवाच ह । प्रवेश्यतां मुनिस्तात महौजास्तस्य वाक्यधृत् ।। 7.103.6 ।।
transliteration: tadvākyaṃ lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ śrutvā rāma uvāca ha | praveśyatāṃ munistāta mahaujāstasya vākyadhṛt || 7.103.6 ||
translation: तत् that, वाक्यं word, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, उक्तं spoken, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामः Rama, उवाच said, ह indeed, प्रवेश्यतां let him be admitted, मुनिः the sage, तात O dear one, महौजाः greatly powerful, तस्य his, वाक्यधृत् bearer of a message.
explanation: Having heard those words spoken by Lakshmana, Rama indeed said, "O dear one, let that greatly powerful sage, who is a bearer of a message, be admitted."

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रावेशयत तं मुनिम् । ज्वलन्तमेव तेजोभिः प्रदहन्तमिवांशुभिः ।। 7.103.7 ।।
transliteration: saumitristu tathetyuktvā prāveśayata taṃ munim | jvalantameva tejobhiḥ pradahantamivāṃśubhiḥ || 7.103.7 ||
translation: सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, तु and, तथा so be it, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, प्रावेशयत led in, तं that, मुनिम् sage, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, एव indeed, तेजोभिः with splendors, प्रदहन्तम् burning, इव as if, अंशुभिः with rays.
explanation: And Lakshmana, having said "So be it," led in that sage who was blazing with his own splendor, as if burning with rays of light.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिगम्य रघुश्रेष्ठं दीप्यपानं स्वतेजसा । ऋषिर्मधुरया वाचा वर्धस्वेत्याह राघवम् ।। 7.103.8 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhigamya raghuśreṣṭhaṃ dīpyapānaṃ svatejasā | ṛṣirmadhurayā vācā vardhasvetyāha rāghavam || 7.103.8 ||
translation: सः he, अभिगम्य having approached, रघुश्रेष्ठं the best of the Raghus, दीप्यमानं shining, स्वतेजसा with his own splendor, ऋषिः the sage, मधुरया with sweet, वाचा voice, वर्धस्व may you prosper, इति thus, आह said, राघवम् to Rama.
explanation: Having approached Rama, the best of the Raghus, who was shining with his own splendor, the sage said to him with a sweet voice, "May you prosper."

shloka_text: तस्मै रामो महातेजाः पूजामर्घ्यपुरोगमाम् । ददौ कुशलमव्यग्रं प्रष्टुमेवोपचक्रमे ।। 7.103.9 ।।
transliteration: tasmai rāmo mahātejāḥ pūjāmarghyapurogamām | dadau kuśalamavyagraṃ praṣṭumevopacakrame || 7.103.9 ||
translation: तस्मै to him, रामः Rama, महातेजाः the greatly effulgent one, पूजाम् honor, अर्घ्यपुरोगमाम् preceded by arghya, ददौ gave, कुशलम् welfare, अव्यग्रम् calmly, प्रष्टुम् to ask, एव indeed, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: The greatly effulgent Rama offered him honor, preceded by arghya, and calmly began to inquire about his well-being.

shloka_text: पृष्टश्च कुशलं तेन रामेण वदतां वरः । आसने काञ्चने दिव्ये निषसाद महायशाः ।। 7.103.10 ।।
transliteration: pṛṣṭaśca kuśalaṃ tena rāmeṇa vadatāṃ varaḥ | āsane kāñcane divye niṣasāda mahāyaśāḥ || 7.103.10 ||
translation: पृष्टः asked, च and, कुशलम् welfare, तेन by him, रामेण by Rama, वदतां वरः the best among speakers, आसने on the seat, काञ्चने golden, दिव्ये divine, निषसाद sat down, महायशाः the greatly renowned one.
explanation: And being asked about his welfare by Rama, the greatly renowned one, who was the best among speakers, sat down on a divine golden seat.

shloka_text: तमुवाच ततो रामः स्वागतं ते महामुने । प्रापयास्य च वाक्यानि यतो दूतस्त्वमागतः ।। 7.103.11 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca tato rāmaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune | prāpayāsya ca vākyāni yato dūtastvamāgataḥ || 7.103.11 ||
translation: तम् to him, उवाच said, ततः then, रामः Rama, स्वागतम् welcome, ते to you, महामुने O great sage, प्रापय deliver, अस्य his, च and, वाक्यानि words, यतः from whom, दूतः messenger, त्वम् you, आगतः have come.
explanation: Then Rama said to him, "Welcome to you, O great sage; please deliver the messages of him from whom you have come as a messenger."

shloka_text: चोदितो राजसिंहेन मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत । द्वन्द्वमेतत्प्रवक्तव्यं हितं वै यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.12 ।।
transliteration: codito rājasiṃhena munirvākyamabhāṣata | dvandvametatpravaktavyaṃ hitaṃ vai yadyapekṣase || 7.103.12 ||
translation: चोदितः urged, राजसिंहेन by the lion among kings, मुनिः the sage, वाक्यम् words, अभाषत spoke, द्वन्द्वम् a secret, एतत् this, प्रवक्तव्यम् to be spoken, हितम् beneficial, वै indeed, यदि if, अपेक्षसे you desire.
explanation: Urged by the lion among kings, the sage spoke these words: "This secret must be spoken if you indeed desire what is beneficial."

shloka_text: यः शृणोति निरीक्षेद्वा स वध्यो भविता तव । भवेद्वै मुनिमुख्यस्य वचनं यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.13 ।।
